kubernetes_admissionregistration_mutatin.text: The API version used to manage the fields in this managedFields entry.
The type of the fields field. Currently only 'FieldsV1' is supported.

fields_v1 is the Kubernetes fieldsV1 field, which contains a JSON representation of the fields managed by this entry. It stores a set of field paths and their ownership information used for server-side apply conflict detection.
The name of the manager (entity, such as a controller or user) that last applied or updated the managed fields.
Operation is the type of operation that last modified the field, such as 'Update' or 'Apply'.
The subresource of the resource that this managed field entry applies to, such as 'status' or 'scale'.

Indicates whether this version is served by the API server. When true, the version is available for clients to use; when false, it is disabled but may still be stored.
Indicates whether this version is the one used for storing the custom resource in etcd. Only one version can be marked as the storage version.

Specifies subresources for this version of the custom resource, such as status and scale. The status subresource enables the status field, and the scale subresource enables the scale field for autoscaling. Optional in the versions list.
The scale subresource enables horizontal scaling for the custom resource. It specifies the paths to the replicas fields in the spec and status, and optionally a label selector for pod selection.
LabelSelectorPath is the JSON path to the custom field that holds a label selector for the resource. This field is used by the scale subresource to identify the pods belonging to the resource.

The JSON path within the custom resource that points to the field containing the desired number of replicas. This path is used by the scale subresource to read and write the replica count, and must be a simple path under .spec or .status, such as .spec.replicas.

The JSON path within the custom resource's status that identifies the field holding the current number of replicas. This is used by the scale subresource to report the replica count to the HorizontalPodAutoscaler and kubectl scale.
Enables the status subresource for this version of the custom resource.
The last time the condition transitioned from one status to another, in RFC 3339 format.
Human-readable message indicating details about the condition's last transition.
The generation of the CustomResourceDefinition that this condition was last updated for. It indicates the resource version the condition reflects.

Type of the condition, e.g., 'Established' or 'NamesAccepted', indicating the kind of condition this object represents.

Name of the manager that last modified the field. This is usually a client identifier such as a user agent or controller name.
The type of operation used to manage this field set. Allowed values are 'Apply', 'Update', and 'Delete'.
The subresource (e.g., 'status' or 'scale') that this managed field entry applies to. An empty value indicates the entry applies to the main resource itself.
The last time the managed field was updated, in RFC3339 format (e.g., 2023-10-01T12:00:00Z).
The API version (e.g., v1, apps/v1) of the referenced owner resource.
If true, this owner reference blocks deletion of the dependent object until the owner is deleted (when the owner has foregroundDeletion finalizer). Defaults to false.
Controller indicates whether the referenced object is the managing controller for the owning object. A controller reference must be unique; only one owner reference with controller=true is allowed.
The kind of the referenced owner object, such as Deployment or ReplicaSet.
Name of the referent object (the owner).
The UID of the owner object. This field is required in an owner reference and uniquely identifies the owner, enabling Kubernetes garbage collection to correctly manage dependent objects.

lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.
Human-readable message indicating details about the condition's last transition.

ServedVersions holds the versions that the API server can serve for this resource. It is populated by the API server to indicate the supported API versions for the storage version.

kubernetes_apps_controller_revision.meta.text: The API version used by the manager to manage the fields in this ManagedFieldsEntry, such as 'apps/v1'. It identifies the version of the resource that the manager applied.

fieldsV1 stores the set of fields managed by a manager, encoded as a JSON document where each present field indicates that the manager manages that field, with its value reflecting the field's last known state.

The API version of the owner object referenced by this owner reference, e.g., 'apps/v1'.
If true, and the owner is deleted, the object will not be automatically deleted. This prevents garbage collection of the object if the owner is deleted. Defaults to false.

Kind of the referenced owner resource (e.g., 'ReplicaSet', 'DaemonSet', 'StatefulSet').
The name of the owner object referenced by this owner reference entry (matching the kind and apiVersion in the same owner reference).

A node selector term that defines which nodes are preferred for scheduling. It consists of matchExpressions and matchFields fields to constrain the node selection.

A list of label selector requirements that define which node labels must match for a node to be considered for this preferred scheduling preference. Each requirement includes a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optional values.
The label key that the selector applies to. The node must have this label key to satisfy the match expression.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.
The list of values that the node label key must match for the affinity rule. Used only with operators that require values, such as In or NotIn.
A list of node selector requirements that match against node fields (e.g., metadata.name). Each requirement defines a key, operator, and values to constrain node selection based on node fields.
The key (field path) of the node attribute to match, such as 'metadata.name' or a label key in matchFields.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and the set of values. Must be one of In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt.
A list of values that the node field (specified by the key) must match when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'. For 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty.

Weight associated with the corresponding node preference term. The scheduler adds this weight to the sum of all preferences that match the node, and nodes with the highest total weight are preferred. Must be an integer in the range 1-100.

A list of label selector requirements for node affinity. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values. The node must satisfy all match expressions within at least one node selector term to be considered eligible for scheduling.
The label key on the node that this expression matches. The operator and values determine the condition applied to this key.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and the set of values in a node selector requirement. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.
A list of values that the node's label must match for In/NotIn operators. Must be empty for Exists/DoesNotExist operators.
A list of node selector requirements that match on node fields (e.g., metadata.name) to satisfy this node selector term, using a key, operator, and optional values.
The key of the node field to match, such as metadata.name, in this node selector term.
Operator for a field-based node selector requirement. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. The Gt and Lt operators require the value to be an integer.

The list of values that the node's field value must match according to the requirement's operator. For In and NotIn operators, these are the allowed or disallowed values; for Exists and DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.

The pod affinity term for the preferred scheduling rule. It specifies a label selector and topology key to define a group of pods to co-locate with, and optionally restricts the search to specific namespaces.
Labels selector used to identify the set of pods that the affinity term applies to. The affinity will match pods that have the labels specified in this selector.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement contains a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, or DoesNotExist), and, for In and NotIn, a list of values; all requirements must be satisfied for a pod to match the label selector.
The label key that the selector applies to. Must be a valid Kubernetes label key.
The operator to use for the label selector expression. Valid values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'.

A list of label values that the selector matches. When the operator is `In` or `NotIn`, this list must be non-empty and each value must be a valid label value (up to 63 characters, alphanumeric and '-', '_', '.' starting and ending with alphanumeric). For `Exists` and `DoesNotExist`, this field must be empty.

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.
A list of label keys that must be present on the pods for the affinity term to be satisfied. Only the presence of these keys is considered, not their values.

A list of pod label keys. The affinity term applies only to pods that have a value for each key that differs from the value on the pod being scheduled; if the scheduling pod has no value for a key, that key does not select any pods.

A label selector used to select the namespaces in which the target pods exist. If set, the affinity is scoped to pods running in namespaces matching this selector. If empty, it selects all namespaces.

A list of label selector requirements used to select namespaces. Each requirement defines a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. All expressions must be satisfied for a namespace to match.
The label key that the selector operates on. For a namespace selector, this key is matched against labels on namespaces.
The operator defines the relationship between the key and a set of values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values that the selector key must match, per the expression's operator. For In/NotIn operators, values must be non-empty; for Exists/DoesNotExist, values must be empty.
A map of key-value pairs that must be matched by the labels of a namespace for it to be selected by this namespace selector. All specified labels must be present and equal for a namespace to match.
List of namespaces to which this pod affinity term applies. If empty, the term applies to the pod's own namespace.

The node label key that defines the topology domain for the affinity term. For example, 'kubernetes.io/hostname' groups nodes by host name, and the affinity/anti-affinity rule is applied per node group.
The weight associated with a preferred pod affinity term. Must be an integer between 1 and 100. Higher weights increase the preference for scheduling on nodes that match the affinity term.

A label selector is a query over labels on pods to identify the set of pods that the pod affinity rule applies to. It can include matchLabels (exact key-value pairs) and matchExpressions (conditional expressions) to define the selection criteria.

match_expressions is a list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and optionally a list of values. The requirements are ANDed together, and the resulting label selector determines which pods are considered for pod affinity during scheduling.
The label key that this match expression applies to. This is the key in the Kubernetes label selector, e.g., 'app' or 'tier'.
The operator for the label selector requirement, indicating how the key is compared to the values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

The list of values for the label selector match expression. These values are used with the operator (e.g., In or NotIn) to match against the labels of pods or nodes. For operators like Exists or DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.

A map of key-value pairs. The requirements are ANDed: only pods with all specified labels (matching each key-value pair) are selected. A single {key, value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, with key 'key', operator 'In', and values ['value'].

A list of pod label keys used to select pods for this affinity term. Only pods that have the same label values for all specified keys as the incoming pod are considered, in addition to any label selector.

A list of label keys. The scheduler considers only existing pods that have different values for these keys than the pod being scheduled, which helps precisely control pod placement (e.g., anti-affinity among pods with the same replica label).
NamespaceSelector is a label selector for namespaces. If specified, the pod affinity term applies only to pods in namespaces matching this selector; if omitted, it applies to the pod's own namespace.

A list of label selector requirements that constrain which namespaces match. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. All requirements are ANDed together.
The label key that the selector applies to. In this context, it is the key for matching namespace labels in the pod affinity namespace selector.
The operator to apply to the key and value(s) in this namespace selector requirement. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
Values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty.

A map of label keys and values. Namespaces that have all the specified label-value pairs are selected for the pod affinity/anti-affinity rule. This restricts the affinity rule to namespaces matching these labels.
Restricts the pod affinity term to a set of namespaces. If empty or omitted, the term applies to the namespace of the pod that the affinity is defined on.

The topology key defines the node label that groups nodes into topology domains (e.g., kubernetes.io/hostname). It is required for requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution affinity terms, as it determines which nodes are considered for pod placement relative to each other.
Represents a pod affinity term, specifying the label selector, namespaces, and topology key that determine the group of pods and the topology domain for the anti-affinity preference.

A label query over a set of pods for the affinity term. The result of matchLabels and matchExpressions are ANDed. An empty label selector matches all objects, while a null label selector matches no objects.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. The requirements are ANDed, meaning all conditions must be satisfied for a match.
The label key that the selector matches against. This corresponds to a label key defined in the pod's metadata.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

List of values that the label selector matches against. The interpretation depends on the operator: for In and NotIn, these are the required values; for Exists and DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.
A map of label keys and values that must all be present on a pod for the label selector to match. Used to select pods for this pod affinity or anti-affinity term.

List of pod label keys to select which pods should be considered for the pod affinity/anti-affinity term. The keys are matched against the labels of the pod being scheduled and ANDed with any label selector. If empty, all label keys are considered.

A list of pod label keys that must have different values between the current pod and candidate pods for the affinity term to match. This excludes pods with the same label values, preventing self-selection in anti-affinity rules.

A label selector to select namespaces for the pod affinity term. When specified, the affinity/anti-affinity rule applies to pods in the matching namespaces; if omitted, it applies to the pod's own namespace.

A list of label selector requirements that are ANDed. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. The namespace selector matches namespaces whose labels satisfy these expressions.
The label key that the selector matches against. For example, the key of a namespace label.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the specified values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values that the label value must match for the given operator. Required for the 'In' and 'NotIn' operators; must be empty for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist'.
A map of label keys to values used to select namespaces. The pod affinity or anti-affinity rule applies only to pods running in namespaces that match all of the specified label key-value pairs.
A list of namespaces that the pod affinity/anti-affinity term applies to. If empty or omitted, it defaults to the namespace of the pod where the rule is defined.

The key of node labels that defines the topology domain (e.g., kubernetes.io/hostname) used to group nodes for pod anti-affinity. Pods are scheduled to avoid being placed on the same topology domain as other pods that match the label selector.
The weight associated with this preferred scheduling term. It must be an integer between 1 and 100, and higher weights increase the preference for this anti-affinity rule.

A label query over a set of pods. The pods that match this selector are considered as targets for the anti-affinity rule. It is a standard Kubernetes label selector, which can include matchLabels and matchExpressions.

match_expressions is a list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values, used to select pods based on labels for pod anti-affinity rules.
The label key that this match expression applies to. The selector will match resources based on the value of this key on their labels.
The operator used to compare the label key with the values in a match expression. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
values is a list of string values that the key must match according to the operator. For In and NotIn operators, values must be non-empty. For Exists and DoesNotExist, values must be empty.
match_labels is a map of label keys and values used to select pods for the anti-affinity rule. Only pods that have all of the specified labels are considered when determining pod placement.
A list of pod label keys used to select the pods that the anti-affinity rule applies to. Only labels with these keys are considered when matching pods, restricting the scope of the affinity selector.

A list of label keys that, if present on the incoming pod, require existing pods in the selected group to have different values for those keys. This is used to exclude pods that share the same label values from the anti-affinity term.

A label selector that determines which namespaces the pod anti-affinity rule applies to. Only pods running in namespaces matching this selector are considered when evaluating the anti-affinity constraint.
A list of label selector requirements that the namespace labels must satisfy. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values.
The label key that the selector applies to. It must match a label on the namespace.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values that the namespace label key must match for the operator. Required for the In and NotIn operators; must be empty for Exists and DoesNotExist.
A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels of the namespaces to be selected. Only namespaces with all specified labels are considered for the anti-affinity rule.
A list of namespaces that the label selector for this pod anti-affinity term applies to. If unspecified, it defaults to the namespace of the pod.

Specifies the node label key that defines the topology domain for pod anti-affinity. The required anti-affinity rule is evaluated across all nodes sharing this label value, and the pod is scheduled only if the constraint is satisfied.
Arguments to the entrypoint. The container image's CMD is used if this is not provided.

Entrypoint array for the container. This is the command that is run when the container starts, equivalent to Docker's ENTRYPOINT. It overrides the image's ENTRYPOINT. The command is not run inside a shell. If not provided, the image's default entrypoint is used.
List of environment variables to set in the container. Each entry has a name and optionally a value or valueFrom (e.g., configMapKeyRef, secretKeyRef, fieldRef, resourceFieldRef).
The name of the environment variable. Must be a C identifier (alphanumeric, '_', and '-', starting with an alphabetic character or '_').
The value of the environment variable, expressed as a string.
value_from specifies the source for the environment variable's value, such as a reference to a ConfigMap, Secret, or a pod field. It is used when the value is not a literal string.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to populate the value of the environment variable. The ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap whose value is used for this environment variable.
The name of the ConfigMap to select a key from. This must match the name of an existing ConfigMap in the same namespace.

Specifies whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If true, and the key does not exist, the environment variable will be omitted. If false and the key does not exist, the container will fail to start.

Selects a field of the pod. Supports metadata.name, metadata.namespace, metadata.labels['<KEY>'], metadata.annotations['<KEY>'], spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.hostIP, status.podIP, and status.podIPs.
The API version of the referent field (e.g., 'v1') used to interpret the fieldPath in a field reference for environment variable values.
Specifies the path to a field in the pod object (e.g., metadata.name, status.podIP) from which the value is selected.
The key inside the referenced file whose value is used for the environment variable.
Specifies whether the referenced file key is optional. If set to true, the absence of the key is allowed; otherwise, the key is required.
The name of the volume that contains the file referenced by the file key.
ResourceFieldSelector that selects a resource field (such as limits.cpu or requests.memory) from the container to populate the environment variable's value.
Name of the container to select the resource value from. If not specified, defaults to the container where this environment variable is defined.

The divisor for the resource value. The environment variable value is the resource value divided by this divisor. If not specified, it defaults to 1. Must be a valid Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1', '100m').
The name of the container resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
SecretKeyRef selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. This is used to populate an environment variable from a Kubernetes secret.
The key of the secret to select from. Specifies which entry in the Secret's data map to use.
The name of the Secret whose key is referenced. This is the name of the secret in the same namespace as the pod.
Indicates whether the Secret key must be defined. If true, the system will not fail if the key is missing; if false (default), the key must exist.
List of sources to populate environment variables in the container. Each source can be a ConfigMap or a Secret, with optional prefix for variable names.
Reference to a ConfigMap that supplies environment variables to the container, used as one source in the envFrom list.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference. This ConfigMap's data will be used to populate environment variables in the container.

Indicates whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. When true, the ConfigMap may be absent without causing an error, and other envFrom sources are still used. When false (default), the ConfigMap must exist or the pod creation fails.
Optional prefix that is prepended to each environment variable name derived from the referenced ConfigMap or Secret, preventing name collisions when using multiple sources.
The Secret to use as the source of environment variables. The Secret's data keys become environment variable names, and their values become the environment variable values.
The name of the Secret whose data will be exposed as environment variables in the container. It must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Specifies whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If true, and the Secret is not found, the environment variables from this source are skipped and the container can still start.
The container image to run, specified as an image reference like `repository:tag` or `registry/repository:tag`. If the tag is omitted, the `latest` tag is used by default.

Specifies when the kubelet should pull the container image. Allowed values: Always, IfNotPresent, Never. Default is IfNotPresent for images with a tag, Always for images with :latest, and Never for images with :digest.
Defines lifecycle hooks for the container, including postStart and preStop handlers that specify actions to run at container startup or before termination.

postStart is a lifecycle hook that runs immediately after a container is created. It can contain an exec command or an HTTP request to be executed, though the container's main process may start before the hook completes.
The exec action to run a command inside the container as the postStart lifecycle hook. This is an object that defines the command to execute.
The command to run inside the container as the post-start lifecycle hook. It is specified as an array of strings, where the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the post-start lifecycle hook. The request is sent to the container's IP address and port as specified in this action.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Specifies custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each item in the list contains a `name` and `value` string pair.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP request.
The value of the HTTP header entry.
The URL path for the HTTP GET request sent to the container's IP address during the postStart lifecycle hook. If not specified, defaults to '/'.
The port number (1-65535) or IANA service name to access on the container for the HTTP GET request.
The protocol used for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Specifies the scheme (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are "HTTP" and "HTTPS"; defaults to "HTTP".
Defines a sleep action for the post-start lifecycle hook, pausing the container for a specified number of seconds (see the `seconds` field within this object).
Seconds is the number of seconds to sleep during the postStart lifecycle hook.
TCPSocket specifies a TCP action for the postStart lifecycle hook. It attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the given host; the hook succeeds if the connection is established.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket check. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Specifies the TCP port to connect to on the container. Accepts an integer port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports.

pre_stop defines a lifecycle hook that is executed immediately before a container is terminated. It can specify an exec action or an HTTP GET request to trigger a custom action before the container is stopped.
Exec specifies the action to run a command inside the container as the pre-stop lifecycle hook handler. This is mutually exclusive with the HTTP GET handler.

The command to execute in the container during the pre-stop lifecycle hook. The first element is the command, and subsequent elements are arguments. It is exec'd directly, not run in a shell, so shell constructs are not expanded unless a shell is explicitly invoked.
Specifies an HTTP GET request that the container runtime sends to the container as the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This is used to allow the container to gracefully shut down before it is terminated.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each header object specifies a name and value to be sent.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the pre-stop lifecycle hook's HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server.

The TCP port number or named port on the container to which the preStop HTTP GET request is sent. Can be an integer value or a string specifying a named container port; this field is required when using an HTTP GET lifecycle handler.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are `HTTP` and `HTTPS`, with a default of `HTTP`.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Sleep specifies the SleepAction for the pre-stop lifecycle hook, which pauses the container for a defined period to allow graceful shutdown or finalization before termination.
Specifies the duration of the sleep in seconds before the container is terminated.

TCPSocketAction specifies a TCP socket action. In a container lifecycle preStop hook, it connects to a specified port on the container, allowing the container to detect the connection before it is terminated.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket. If not specified, it defaults to the pod IP address.
The TCP port to connect to on the container for the preStop lifecycle hook. This can be an integer port number or a named port that must be defined in the container's ports.
Specifies the signal to be sent to the container when it is being stopped. This is typically a signal name like SIGTERM or SIGKILL.
Configures the liveness probe for the container. The kubelet periodically executes the probe; if it fails, the container is restarted.
Exec specifies a command to execute inside the container. The liveness probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0.

The command to run inside the container for the liveness probe. It is a list of strings where the first element is the command and the rest are arguments. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with a status code of 0.
The number of consecutive failures before the liveness probe is considered failed, causing the container to be restarted. The minimum value is 1; the default is 3.
Configures a gRPC probe for the container. Specifies the port and optional service name to check for liveness.
The port number on which the gRPC server is listening for the liveness probe. This is a required field for gRPC probes and must be a valid TCP port.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is to check the overall server health (no service name).
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform for the liveness probe. This checks container health by making an HTTP GET request to the configured path and port on the container.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.

List of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request sent to the container's liveness probe endpoint. Each header is an object containing a name and a value, allowing the probe to authenticate or pass metadata as required by the application.
The HTTP header name. For example, 'Accept' or 'Content-Type'.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the request to the liveness probe endpoint.
The HTTP path to request when performing the liveness probe.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Can be an integer port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME (a named port defined in the container).
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request, e.g., HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are "HTTP" and "HTTPS". Defaults to "HTTP".
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated.
How often (in seconds) to perform the liveness probe. Must be at least 1; defaults to 10 seconds.
The minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For liveness probes, this value must be 1 (the default).

Defines a TCP socket probe for the liveness check. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the container; if the connection succeeds, the probe is considered successful.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The TCP port to check. This can be a numeric port number or a named port defined in the container's ports. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to this port on the container's IP address.

The number of seconds to wait for the pod to terminate gracefully after receiving a termination signal; after this period, the pod is forcefully killed. This applies to the pod as a whole, not just the container's liveness probe.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.
The name of the container within the pod.
List of ports to expose from the container. Each port entry typically includes a container port number and protocol, and may optionally specify a name and host port.
The port number that the container exposes on the pod's IP address. Must be a valid port number (1-65535).
The host IP address to bind the container port to. If not specified, the port is bound to all host interfaces (0.0.0.0).

The port number on the host node to which the container port is exposed. This enables external access to the container via the host's IP address. If omitted, the container port is not mapped to the host.
Optional name for the container port. Must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME (DNS label) and unique among all ports in the container.
The protocol for the container port. One of TCP, UDP, or SCTP. Defaults to TCP.

Defines a probe that determines whether the container is ready to accept traffic. If the probe fails, the container is removed from service endpoints but is not restarted. Supports exec, HTTP GET, and TCP socket probe types along with timing options such as initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, and failureThreshold.
Exec specifies the action to take, which runs a command inside the container. It defines a command to execute to determine the health of the container.
Command to run inside the container for the readiness probe. The first item is the command, and any remaining items are arguments passed to the command.

The number of consecutive failures required for the readiness probe to be considered failed, causing the container to be marked as not ready. Must be an integer greater than or equal to 1; defaults to 3.
Configures the gRPC health check for the readiness probe. It specifies the port to check and an optional service name.
The port number on the container where the gRPC server is listening for the readiness probe. Must be an integer in the range 1 to 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If this field is not set, the default behavior follows the gRPC health checking protocol, typically using an empty service name.
Performs an HTTP GET request against the container to determine its health within the readiness probe. Configures the endpoint, port, and optional HTTP headers for the request.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP request. Defaults to the pod IP. You generally should not set this; instead, set the 'Host' header via httpHeaders.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the probe request. Each header object contains a name and a value.
The name of the HTTP header to be set in the probe request, such as 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header.
The HTTP request path to access on the server. Defaults to '/' if not specified, for example '/healthz'.
The port number or name to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME corresponding to a named port in the container.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS, defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container starts before the readiness probe is initiated.
The frequency in seconds at which the readiness probe is performed. Must be a positive integer.

Specifies the number of consecutive successful probe responses required for the container to be considered ready after a failed probe. The default is 1, and the value must be a positive integer (minimum 1).
Defines a TCP socket probe that checks readiness by attempting to open a TCP connection to a specific port (and optionally host) on the container.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The TCP port number or named port to connect to for the readiness probe.
The number of seconds a pod is allowed to terminate gracefully before it is forcefully terminated.
The number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. If the probe does not respond within this time, the container is considered not ready.

A list of container resize policies, allowing in-place updates of CPU and memory resources. Each policy specifies a resource (cpu or memory) and a restart policy (Always or OnFailure) that determines whether the container needs to restart to apply the resize.
ResourceName is the name of the resource (e.g., 'cpu' or 'memory') to which this resize policy applies.
Specifies the policy for handling container resizes. Valid values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer', where 'RestartContainer' causes the kubelet to restart the container if the resize fails.
Compute resource requirements for the container, specifying requests (minimum guaranteed resources) and limits (maximum allowed resources) for CPU and memory.
Lists the names of resources, defined in the pod's spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this container. This field is alpha and may change in future Kubernetes versions.
The name of the ResourceClaim that this container requires. The claim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the ResourceClaim as defined in the ResourceClaimTemplate that this container requests.

limits specifies the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the container. Each key is a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the value is a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., '500m', '2Gi').
A map of resource names to quantities (e.g., 'cpu', 'memory') specifying the minimum amount of compute resources required for the container.
The comparison operator used to evaluate the container exit code against the specified value in the restart policy rule.
The list of numeric container exit codes to which this restart policy rule applies.
Security context that defines privilege and access control settings for the container, such as user/group ID, Linux capabilities, and SELinux options.
Controls whether a process in the container can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, privilege escalation is disabled, which is a security hardening measure.
AppArmor profile to apply to the container. The profile type must be one of RuntimeDefault, Localhost, or Unconfined; if Localhost, the localhostProfile field names a pre-loaded profile on the node.
The name of the AppArmor profile to use when type is Localhost. This field is only used if the AppArmor profile type is set to Localhost.
Defines the type of AppArmor profile to apply to the container. Valid values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', and 'Unconfined'.

The capabilities field in a security context specifies Linux capabilities that can be added to or dropped from the container's default capability set. It contains an 'add' list for additional capabilities and a 'drop' list for capabilities to remove.
Specifies the Linux capabilities to add to the container's capability set. For example, 'SYS_ADMIN' or 'NET_ADMIN'.
List of capabilities to drop from the container's effective capabilities. Each entry is a capability name (e.g., 'ALL' or 'NET_RAW').
Run container in privileged mode. Processes in privileged containers are essentially equivalent to root on the host. Defaults to false.
The type of proc mount to use for the container. It defaults to 'Default', which uses the runtime default; set to 'Unmasked' to bypass the default masking of /proc.
Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only. When set to true, the root filesystem becomes read-only, preventing processes from writing to it.
The GID to run the entrypoint of the container process. If not specified, the container runs with the group ID specified in the image or the runtime default.
If true, the container will run as a non-root user, preventing it from running with root privileges. This is a Kubernetes security context setting.
The numeric UID to run the container process as. Must be a non-negative integer. If unspecified, defaults to the user defined in the container image's metadata.
SELinux options for the container, specifying the SELinux context (user, role, type, and level) applied to the container's processes.
The SELinux level (MLS/MCS) for the container, such as 's0' or 's0:c0'.
The SELinux role label for the container. This label is part of the SELinux context and is used to enforce role-based access control.
The SELinux type label, such as 'spc_t', applied to the container. This is part of the SELinux security context options.
The SELinux user label assigned to the container, such as 'system_u'.

SeccompProfile holds the seccomp profile configuration for the container. The type field specifies the profile type: RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, or Localhost; if Localhost, localhostProfile must name a profile path.
The path to a seccomp profile defined on the node's filesystem. This profile must be preconfigured on the node to be used by the container.
The seccomp profile type. Allowed values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Unconfined', and 'Localhost'.
Windows-specific security context options for the container. These settings are applied only when the container is running on a Windows node.
The GMSA credential spec (as a string) used for Windows container security context. This is the full credential spec content, not the name of a credential spec.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the container's Windows security context. This references a pre-configured Group Managed Service Account credential spec on the Windows node.
Determines if the container should run as a HostProcess container. When true, it grants the container access to the host's process namespace and privileges.
The UserName in Windows to run the container's entrypoint. If not specified, the container runs as the container's default user.

Defines a probe that checks whether the application within the container has started successfully. If the startup probe fails, the container is restarted, and the liveness probe is not started until the startup probe succeeds. Useful for containers with slow startup times.
Exec specifies the exec action for the startup probe. It defines a command to run inside the container to determine if the container is ready.
The command to run inside the container for the startup probe. It is executed directly without a shell; an exit status of 0 indicates success (healthy).
The number of consecutive failures required for the startup probe to be considered failed, after which the container is restarted. Must be a positive integer; the default is 3.
grpc specifies the gRPC action for the startup probe. It contains the port to probe and optionally the service name to check, enabling gRPC-based health checks.
Port number on the container that the gRPC server is listening on, used for the startup probe. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not set, the default is the pod name (lowercased).
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform on the container as part of the startup probe. The probe succeeds if the HTTP response status code is in the 200-399 range.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Custom HTTP headers to send with the probe request. Each item defines a header name and value.
The HTTP header field name to include in the probe request. For example, 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the startup probe's HTTP GET request. For example, if the header name is 'X-Custom-Header', this field holds the corresponding value.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Accepts a numeric port (as a string) or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Must be a non-negative integer.
The interval, in seconds, between successive startup probe checks. If unspecified, Kubernetes defaults this to 10 seconds.
Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For startup probes, this value must be 1. Defaults to 1 if not specified.
Specifies a TCP socket probe handler that checks if a TCP connection can be established to the container on the given port. Used as an alternative to HTTP or command probes in the startup probe.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not set, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to probe. Accepts a numeric port (e.g., '80') or a named port (e.g., 'http') defined in the container.
The number of seconds to allow the pod to terminate gracefully after the startup probe fails. If set, this overrides the pod's default termination grace period.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second; must be at least 1.
Whether this container should allocate a buffer for stdin in the container runtime. If not set, reads from stdin in the container will always result in EOF. Defaults to false.
If true, the container's stdin is expected to be a TTY, and stdin will be redirected to the container only once (on container start). Defaults to false.
The path inside the container where the termination message is written. The kubelet reads this file to retrieve information about the container's termination reason.
Specifies how the container's termination message is read. Valid values are 'File' (default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'.
Indicates whether a TTY (teletypewriter) should be allocated for the container. When true, the container gets an interactive terminal. Defaults to false.

volume_devices is a list of volumeDevice objects that define mappings of raw block devices within the container. Each entry specifies the volume name (name) and the device path inside the container (devicePath).
The path inside the container where the device will be mounted.
The name of the volume to which this device applies. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's volumes list.
List of volume mounts to attach to the container. Each mount specifies the volume name, mount path, and options like read-only.
Path within the container at which the volume will be mounted. Must be an absolute path.
Determines how mounts are propagated from the host to container and vice versa. Allowed values are None, HostToContainer, and Bidirectional. When not specified, None is used.
Name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
Mounts the volume as read-only when true. Defaults to false (read-write).
Controls whether a read-only mount is applied recursively to all volumes under the mount path. Valid values are Enabled, Disabled, and IfPossible.
Mounts a sub-path of the referenced volume instead of its root, allowing you to mount a specific directory or file from a volume.

Specifies a sub-path of the volume to mount, with support for environment variable references using $(VAR_NAME) syntax. The expression is expanded using container environment variables before the volume is mounted.
The working directory inside the container where commands are executed. If not set, the default is the image's WORKDIR or the container's root directory.
The name of the DNS resolver option, as defined in resolv.conf (e.g., 'ndots', 'timeout').
The value of the DNS resolver option. This field is optional; if omitted, the option is treated as a flag or empty string.
A list of arguments to pass to the command for the ephemeral container. If not specified, the image's default arguments are used.
The command to run in the ephemeral container, as a list of strings. This overrides the image's entrypoint; the first element is the executable and the rest are arguments.
List of environment variables to set in the ephemeral container. Each entry specifies a variable name and either a direct value or a value source (e.g., configMapKeyRef, secretKeyRef, fieldRef).
Name of the environment variable. Must be a valid environment variable name consisting of alphanumeric characters, '_', or '.', and must not start with a digit.
The literal value of the environment variable. This field is mutually exclusive with `valueFrom`, which can be used to set the value from a source like a config map or secret.
Specifies a source for the value of the environment variable, such as a reference to a ConfigMap key, Secret key, or other field/resource reference. Cannot be used if 'value' is set.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to populate the environment variable's value. Contains the ConfigMap name, the key to reference, and an optional flag indicating whether the key must exist.
The name of the key in the referenced ConfigMap to select the value from. This field is required.
The name of the ConfigMap to select from.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap key must exist. If set to true, the container can start even if the key is not present in the ConfigMap.
Selects a field of the pod (or container) to use as the value of the environment variable. The fieldPath subfield specifies the field to select, such as metadata.name, status.podIP, or spec.nodeName.
The API version of the schema that fieldPath is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1'.
The path to the field in the referenced object from which to select the value. For example, 'metadata.name' or 'status.podIP'.
The key to select from the referenced file (e.g., ConfigMap or Secret) to obtain the value for the environment variable.

Boolean flag indicating whether the referenced key is optional. If true, a missing key does not prevent the container from starting; the environment variable is simply not set. If false, the key must exist.
The path to the file that contains the key referenced by the fileKeyRef.
The name of the volume that contains the file referenced by this file key reference.
ResourceFieldRef selects a resource field (such as limits.cpu or requests.memory) from the container. The value of that field is used as the value of the environment variable.
Container name: required if the resource is a container resource, ignored if it is a pod resource.
Divisor is the value by which the resource value is divided. Defaults to 1 if not specified.
The name of the resource to select from the container, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'. This is a standard Kubernetes resource quantity name.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace.
The key of the secret to select from. Must be a valid secret key.
The name of the Secret from which to select the key.
Specifies whether the referenced secret key must exist. When set to true, the key is optional and its absence is tolerated; when false (default), the key must exist or an error is raised.
List of sources to populate environment variables in the ephemeral container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret to inject environment variables.

configMapRef specifies the ConfigMap to use as a source for environment variables in the container. The referenced ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace, and its keys become environment variable names.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference for environment variables. The ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must exist. If set to true, the ConfigMap is optional; if false (default), the ConfigMap must exist or the container will not start.
An optional identifier to prepend to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. Must be a valid C identifier.
Selects a Kubernetes Secret whose keys and values are exposed as environment variables. The block contains 'name' (the Secret name) and 'optional' (whether the Secret must exist).
Name of the Secret to reference. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Specify whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If set to true, the Pod will start even if the Secret is missing; if false (default), the Secret must exist before the Pod starts.
The container image to use for the ephemeral container.

Determines when the kubelet pulls the container image for the ephemeral container. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never; if not specified, the default is Always if the image tag is 'latest', otherwise IfNotPresent.

Lifecycle describes actions that the container runtime should take in response to container lifecycle events (postStart and preStop). It defines handlers executed at container startup and before termination.
postStart represents the lifecycle hook that is executed immediately after a container is started. It can specify an exec command or a TCP/HTTP request to perform at container startup.
Exec specifies the action to run a command inside the container as the post-start lifecycle hook. This object contains a 'command' field that is a list of strings to execute.

The command line to execute inside the container. The working directory is '/' and it is not run inside a shell, so shell directives like pipes or redirection won't work unless you explicitly invoke a shell.
HTTPGetAction describes an action based on an HTTP GET request. It configures the HTTP request sent to the container's endpoint to trigger the lifecycle hook.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not set, defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set the 'Host' header in httpHeaders instead.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each item is an object containing a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
Name or number of the port to access on the container. If a number, it must be in the range 1 to 65535. If a name, it must be an IANA_SVC_NAME.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme used for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS', with a default of 'HTTP'.

Configures a sleep action in the postStart lifecycle hook, pausing the container for a specified duration before it continues startup. This field corresponds to the Kubernetes SleepAction, available from v1.29.
The number of seconds the container sleeps when this lifecycle hook is triggered. Must be a non-negative integer.
Defines a TCP socket check to be performed during the postStart lifecycle hook, with fields for host and port.
Optional host name to connect to for the TCP socket. Defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to. Can be a numeric port or a string referencing a named port in the pod.
Configuration for a lifecycle hook that runs before the container is terminated. This can specify an exec command or an HTTP request to perform actions such as graceful shutdown.

Exec specifies the action to take, which is to run a command inside the container as a pre-stop lifecycle hook. It corresponds to a Kubernetes ExecAction and contains the command to be executed before the container is terminated.

The command line to execute inside the ephemeral container as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. The command is run directly without a shell, so shell features like pipes or redirects are not interpreted; the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to run as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It configures the endpoint (host, path, port, scheme) and optional headers for the request.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; can be overridden, e.g., to use a service name.
HTTP headers to send in the HTTP GET request. Each item is an object containing the header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header, such as 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header. In a Kubernetes lifecycle hook's HTTP GET request, each header is a name-value pair, and this field provides the value.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The port number to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or the name of an existing container port.
The protocol to use when making the HTTP GET request, such as HTTP or HTTPS.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP'.
Sleep action for the preStop lifecycle hook. It defines a duration in seconds (via the 'seconds' field) for which the container will sleep before being terminated.
Seconds specifies the duration, in seconds, to sleep before the container is terminated, as part of the preStop lifecycle hook.

Represents a TCP socket action as part of a pre-stop lifecycle hook. This action attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the container's IP address to determine whether the hook succeeds.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port number or named port on the container to send the pre-stop hook request to. The value can be an integer port number or a string naming a port in the container's ports list.
Liveness probe configuration for the ephemeral container. Specifies how to check container health and whether to restart it if unhealthy.

Exec specifies the exec action, which runs a command inside the container to check liveness. It is a list of command arguments where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.
Command to run inside the container for the liveness probe's exec action. A list of strings where the first element is the executable and the rest are arguments.
Minimum consecutive failures for the liveness probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1.
Configuration for a gRPC health check, used in place of an HTTP or TCP probe. Requires a port number, and may specify a service name (as defined by the gRPC Health Checking Protocol).
The port number of the gRPC service that the probe will connect to.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health check protocol.

Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the liveness probe. If the probe receives an HTTP response with a status code between 200 and 399, the container is considered healthy; otherwise, it is considered failed.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request for the probe.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request, such as 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header field. This is combined with the header name to form a header sent in the HTTP GET request for the liveness probe.
Path to access on the HTTP server for this HTTP GET request of the liveness probe.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request from the liveness probe.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the liveness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds; minimum value is 1.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the liveness probe to be considered successful after a failure. For liveness probes, this value must be set to 1.
Specifies a TCP socket probe for the liveness check. This object configures the host and port to attempt a TCP connection, and the probe is considered successful if the connection is established.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket liveness probe. If omitted, the pod IP address is used.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535. Name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME.
The number of seconds the pod is allowed to terminate gracefully after receiving a termination signal before it is forcefully killed. This is a pod-level setting applied to all containers.
Number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out.
The name of the ephemeral container in the pod spec.

List of ports to expose from the ephemeral container. Each item typically includes containerPort, protocol, and optionally hostPort, hostIP, and name, following the Kubernetes container port specification.
Port number that the container listens on. Must be a valid port number between 1 and 65535.
The host IP address to bind the container port to. When set, the port will be exposed only on that specific host IP.
The port on the host node that maps to the container port. This allows the container to be accessed externally via the node's IP and this port.
Optional name for the port. Must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME and unique among container ports. Required when multiple ports are specified in the same container.
The network protocol for the port, such as TCP, UDP, or SCTP. Defaults to TCP if not specified.
The readiness probe for the ephemeral container. Kubernetes does not support readiness probes on ephemeral containers, so this field is rejected by the API server if set.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0.

The command to run inside the container for the readiness probe. It is specified as an array of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. If omitted, the container's entrypoint is used.
Specifies the number of consecutive failures required for the readiness probe to be considered failed. The default is 3.
Specifies the gRPC health check configuration for the probe. It contains the port to connect to and an optional service name.
The port number to connect to for the gRPC health check. Must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not set, the default is empty, meaning no service name is sent.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform for the readiness probe. This block configures parameters such as the path, port, scheme, and headers used to check the health of the ephemeral container.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the probe request. Each header is a name-value pair, with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The value of the HTTP header sent in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET probe. Must be a valid integer port (1-65535) or an IANA service name (e.g., 'http').
The network protocol to use for the HTTP probe: either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated.
Specifies the frequency (in seconds) at which the readiness probe is performed. Defaults to 10 seconds.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For readiness probes, the default is 1; set higher to require multiple consecutive successes.
The TCP socket action for the readiness probe. It checks whether a TCP connection can be established to the specified port on the container, typically defined with a 'port' field.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP address.
The TCP port to connect to. Can be a numeric port or a named port on the container.

Specifies the duration in seconds that a pod is allowed to terminate gracefully before being forcefully killed. If set to 0, the pod is deleted immediately; if unset, the Kubernetes default grace period (30 seconds) is used.
Number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. If the probe does not respond within this time, it is considered failed. Minimum value is 1, and the default is 1 second.
Resize policy for the ephemeral container, specifying how each resource can be resized and the restart policy applied (e.g., NotRequired or RestartContainer).
The name of the resource to which the resize policy applies. In Kubernetes, valid values are 'cpu' and 'memory'.
Specifies the restart behavior for an ephemeral container after a resize operation. Valid values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer'.
Specifies the compute resources required for the ephemeral container, including requests and limits for resources such as CPU and memory.

A list of resource claims that this ephemeral container uses. Each claim references a resource defined in the pod's spec.resourceClaims, enabling the container to request dynamic cluster resources. This field corresponds to the Kubernetes ResourceRequirements `claims` field, which is an alpha feature.
Name must match the name of one entry in pod.spec.resourceClaims of the Pod where this field is used. It makes that resource available inside a container.

Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. The keys of the map are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory), and the values are quantities (e.g., "100m", "1Gi"). More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required for the ephemeral container. It is a map of resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) to quantities; if requests are omitted, they default to limits if limits are explicitly specified, otherwise to an implementation-defined value.
The comparison operator used to evaluate container exit codes against specified rules, determining whether a restart policy applies.
The list of container exit codes that trigger this restart policy rule. The rule applies when the container exits with one of these numeric codes.

SecurityContext defines the security options the ephemeral container should be run with, including user ID, group ID, Linux capabilities, SELinux options, and whether the container is privileged. If set, these settings override the Pod-level security context for this container.
Controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to true, privilege escalation is allowed; when false, it is prevented.
Defines the AppArmor profile for the container, including the profile type (RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and an optional localhost profile path.
Specifies a profile loaded on the node that the pod is running on. This is required when the AppArmor profile type is set to Localhost.

Type of AppArmor profile to use. Valid values are: 'RuntimeDefault' uses the container runtime's default profile, 'Localhost' uses a profile pre-loaded on the node, and 'Unconfined' disables AppArmor enforcement.
The Linux capabilities to add to or drop from the container's process, specified as add and drop lists. Part of the security context for ephemeral containers.
Linux capabilities to add to the ephemeral container's capability set. Each entry is a capability name, such as 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN'.
Drops the specified Linux capabilities from the container's default set. Entries are capability names like 'ALL' or 'CAP_NET_ADMIN'.
Indicates whether the container runs in privileged mode, granting it access to all host devices and capabilities.

The type of proc mount to use for the ephemeral container. Supported values are DefaultProcMount (default) and UnmaskedProcMount. This field is alpha and only honored when the kubelet enables the ProcMountType feature gate.
If true, the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only. This prevents writes to the root filesystem; writes must go to a writable volume.
The GID (group ID) to run the container's entrypoint process as. If not specified, the group ID defaults to the image's primary group.
Indicates whether the ephemeral container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the container will be prevented from running as root and will fail if the image's user is root or unspecified.
The user ID (UID) to run the ephemeral container process as. If unspecified, the pod-level or container-level security context applies.
SELinux options to apply to the ephemeral container's security context. This object defines the SELinux label (user, role, type, and level) for the container.
The SELinux level (also known as sensitivity or MLS/MCS label) that applies to the container.
The SELinux role label for the container. In Kubernetes, seLinuxOptions define the SELinux context, and the role field sets the role portion (e.g., system_u).
The SELinux type label for the context, as defined in SELinuxOptions.
The SELinux user label for the container.
SeccompProfile defines the seccomp profile for the container. It allows specifying the type of seccomp profile (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, Localhost) and optionally a localhost profile path.

The path to a seccomp profile on the node, used when the seccomp_profile type is 'Localhost'. This path is typically relative to the kubelet's seccomp profile root directory (e.g., /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp).
The type of seccomp profile to use. Allowed values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', and 'Unconfined'. When 'Localhost' is used, the 'localhostProfile' field must be specified.
Specifies Windows-specific security options for the container, such as GMSA credentials and the username to run container processes as.
GMSACredentialSpec is where the GMSA admission webhook (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/windows-gmsa) inlines the contents of the GMSA credential spec named by the GMSACredentialSpecName field.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the ephemeral container's Windows security context.

Indicates whether the Windows container should be run as a HostProcess container, granting it access to the host's process and network namespaces. This is only applicable to Windows containers running with containerd.
The Windows username to run the container's processes as. This is part of the Windows security context options for ephemeral containers in a DaemonSet pod spec.

Specifies the startup probe for the container. The startup probe indicates whether the application inside the container has started successfully. If it fails, the kubelet kills the container following the container's restart policy. Supported probe types include HTTP, TCP, and exec, and the probe can be configured with fields such as initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, timeoutSeconds, and successThreshold.
Exec specifies the action for the startup probe by running a command inside the container. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with status 0.

The command to execute for the startup probe's exec action. It is a list of strings: the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments. The command runs directly inside the container without a shell.
The number of consecutive failures of the startup probe that must occur before the container is considered unhealthy and is restarted. The value must be a positive integer.
GRPC specifies an action involving a gRPC port. This can be used to perform a gRPC health check on the container.
Port number for the gRPC health check. Must be between 1 and 65535.
Service is the name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health checking protocol.
Specifies the HTTP GET request used by the startup probe to check container health. Includes configuration like target host, port, HTTP path, and headers for the request.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP request. Defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set 'Host' in httpHeaders instead.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP request. Each header is an object with `name` and `value` fields. Allows specifying multiple headers.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the request.
Path to access on the HTTP server for the probe. Defaults to '/'.
The port to access on the container. This can be a numeric port number (1-65535) or a named port as defined in the container's ports specification.
The network protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values: HTTP, HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. This delays the start of the probe to allow the container to initialize.
The number of seconds between each probe execution. The minimum value is 1 second.
The minimum number of consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after a failure. For startup probes, this value must be 1 and it defaults to 1.
TCP socket probe action for the startup probe. Specifies the host and port to check, performing a TCP connection attempt to determine if the container has started.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The TCP port to connect to. Can be a numeric port (e.g., 8080) or a named port defined in the pod's containers.

Optional duration in seconds that the pod needs to terminate gracefully when a startup probe fails. Overrides the pod-level `termination_grace_period_seconds` for the corresponding container; must be a non-negative integer, where zero means immediate termination.
Number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. If the probe does not finish within this time, it is considered failed. Minimum value is 1.
Specifies whether the standard input stream for the ephemeral container is enabled. When true, the container can read from standard input.

Whether stdin is closed after a single attach. If true, stdin is opened on container start, remains open until the first client attaches, then closes when that client disconnects and stays closed until the container restarts.
The name of the container that this ephemeral container attaches to. If unset, it defaults to the first container in the pod.
The path inside the container where a termination message is written. When the container exits, Kubernetes reads this file to include in the pod's status.

Defines how the termination message of the ephemeral container is read. Valid values are 'File' (default, reads the file specified by terminationMessagePath) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError' (uses the last chunk of container logs if the termination message file is empty).
Indicates whether a TTY should be allocated for the ephemeral container. If true, also requires 'stdin' to be true. Defaults to false.
List of block devices to be used by the ephemeral container. Each item specifies a device path and the name of a volume to mount as a block device.
The path inside the container where the raw block device is mounted. This is used when a volume device is specified for a raw block volume.
Name of the volume device. Must match the name of a volume in the pod.
A list of volume mounts to expose to the ephemeral container, specifying the volume name, mount path, and mount options (e.g., read-only, subPath).
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must not contain ':'.
Controls how volume mounts propagate from the host to the container and vice versa. Valid values are 'None', 'HostToContainer', and 'Bidirectional'. Default is 'None'.
The name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
If true, the volume is mounted as read-only; the container cannot write to it. Defaults to false.

Controls whether the volume mount is recursive read-only. Allowed values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', and 'IfPossible', with 'Disabled' being the default when unset. 'Enabled' requires the volume type to support recursive read-only; 'IfPossible' enables it only if the volume type supports it.

The path within the volume from which to mount, rather than the volume's root. This allows mounting a subdirectory of a volume. Must be a relative path and cannot contain '..' to prevent escaping the volume root.
subPathExpr is an expression to compute the subPath directory to mount, using environment variable references (e.g., $(VAR)) to construct the path. It cannot be used together with subPath.
The working directory for the ephemeral container. If not specified, the container runtime default is used.
The list of hostnames that should be resolved to the IP address specified in the same hostAlias entry.
The IP address to add as an alias for the specified hostnames in the pod's /etc/hosts file. Each entry in host_aliases maps an IP to a list of hostnames.
Name of the image pull secret, as defined in the same namespace.
List of arguments to pass to the init container's entrypoint. If the command field is not set, the image's default entrypoint is used.
Command to run in the init container. This overrides the ENTRYPOINT of the container image. Specified as a list of strings; the first element is the command, and the remaining elements are arguments.
