A list of environment variables for the init container. Each variable can be defined with a name and either a direct value or a source (such as a config map, secret, or field reference) from which the value is derived.
Name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier, e.g., MY_VAR.
The value of the environment variable, provided as a string. This is the direct value that will be assigned to the environment variable in the container's init container.
value_from is an optional field that specifies a source for the environment variable's value. It can reference a ConfigMap, Secret, or a field in the pod spec (e.g., downward API).

ConfigMapKeyRef selects a key from a ConfigMap to populate the environment variable's value. Specify the ConfigMap name and key; the optional field indicates whether the ConfigMap or its key must exist.
The key in the referenced ConfigMap to select the value from.
The name of the ConfigMap from which to pull the value for this environment variable.
Indicates whether the ConfigMap key must exist. If set to true, the container starts even if the key or its ConfigMap is missing; if false (default), a missing key causes an error.

Selects a field of the pod for the environment variable value. Common field paths include metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.hostIP, status.podIP, and label/annotation references via metadata.labels['KEY'] or metadata.annotations['KEY'].
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath refers to. Defaults to 'v1' if not specified.
The path to the field to select, such as 'metadata.name' or 'spec.nodeName'.
Specifies whether the referenced key is optional. If true, the container can start even if the key does not exist; if false or omitted, the key must exist.
The name of the volume to read the file key from.

Specifies a container resource field (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) whose value is used as the environment variable's value. The selector includes the container name, resource, and optional divisor.
The name of the container to which the resource field refers. Defaults to the current container if not specified.
The value by which to divide the selected resource quantity. Defaults to 1 if unset.
The name of the resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory', from the container's resource field reference.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace to use as the value for the environment variable.
The key within the Secret to fetch the value from. This must correspond to a valid key in the referenced Secret.
The name of the Secret resource being referenced. Must be a valid Secret name in the same namespace.

Specify whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If set to true, and the secret or key is not found, the environment variable is not set; if false (default), the pod fails to start when the secret or key is missing.

List of sources to populate environment variables in the init container. Each source can be a ConfigMap or Secret, or a reference to such resources, and variables are added to the container's environment.
ConfigMapRef is a reference to a ConfigMap from which environment variables are populated. It contains the name of the ConfigMap and an optional flag to indicate if the ConfigMap must exist.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference. The ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap is optional. If true, a missing ConfigMap is ignored and no environment variables are injected from it; if false or unset, the pod fails to start if the ConfigMap does not exist.
An optional prefix to apply to the keys of the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. When set, each environment variable name is prefixed with this value.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret. The keys in the Secret's data become environment variables in the container. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the Secret to reference for populating environment variables.

Specify whether the Secret must be defined. If set to true, the Secret is optional and its absence does not prevent pod startup; if false or omitted, the Secret must exist or the container fails to start.
The container image to run for this init container, typically specified as a repository, tag, or digest (e.g., busybox:1.36).
Specifies the image pull policy for the container. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never. Defaults to Always if image tag is 'latest' or omitted, otherwise IfNotPresent.

lifecycle is an object that defines lifecycle hooks for the container, such as postStart and preStop, which allow custom actions to be executed at container startup and before termination, respectively.

The post_start field defines the PostStart lifecycle hook, which is executed immediately after a container is started. It is an object that specifies the handler to run, such as an exec command, HTTP GET request, or TCP socket probe.
Exec specifies the action to be taken as an exec-based lifecycle hook. It runs a command inside the container after it is started (PostStart).
The command to run inside the container for this lifecycle hook. It is represented as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.
HTTPGet specifies the HTTP GET request to perform for the post-start lifecycle hook. It defines the endpoint to check and can include path, port, host, and headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request sent by the postStart lifecycle hook. Each item defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to set in the request.
The value of the HTTP header included in the HTTP GET request to the container's postStart lifecycle hook.
The HTTP path (URL path) to send the GET request to when the lifecycle hook is triggered. If not specified, the path defaults to '/'.
The port number or name of the port on the container to send the HTTP GET request to. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535, or a named port defined for the container.
Specifies the protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS; defaults to HTTP.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Sleep performs a sleep action, pausing the container for a specified number of seconds. It requires a `seconds` field indicating the duration of the pause.
The number of seconds to sleep in the postStart lifecycle hook. This delays subsequent lifecycle actions by the specified duration.
Configuration for a TCP socket probe executed as a post-start lifecycle hook for a container.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.

The TCP port to perform the liveness check on. This can be a numeric port or a named port as defined in the container's ports list. The value must be a valid Kubernetes port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that is called immediately before a container is terminated. It allows the container to perform graceful shutdown tasks, such as draining connections or saving state, before the container is stopped.
Exec specifies the action to execute a command inside the container when the preStop lifecycle hook is triggered. This allows you to run a command immediately before the container is terminated.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It is a list of strings; the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly without a shell, and the working directory is the container's root.
An HTTP GET request that kubelet sends to the container as part of a lifecycle hook, typically used in preStop to trigger a graceful shutdown or health check.
The hostname of the HTTP server to connect to for the pre-stop lifecycle hook's GET request. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header is an object with `name` and `value` fields.
The name of the HTTP header to set in the HTTP GET request for the pre-stop lifecycle hook of an init container in a DaemonSet.
The value of the HTTP header field. This is paired with the header name to form a header entry in the HTTP GET request for the container's preStop lifecycle hook.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server for the pre-stop lifecycle hook's HTTP GET request. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port number or name to send the HTTP GET request to. It can be an integer port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request, defaulting to HTTP.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.

The 'sleep' field specifies a SleepAction handler for the preStop lifecycle hook, which pauses the container for a specified duration in seconds before termination, allowing time for graceful shutdown.
The number of seconds the container sleeps before it is terminated, used in the sleep action of the pre-stop lifecycle hook.

tcp_socket is an object that specifies a TCP socket action to be performed during the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It accepts a required port and an optional host, defining the TCP endpoint to connect to before the container is terminated.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port number to connect to for the pre-stop lifecycle hook's TCP socket check. The value is a string containing a numeric port (e.g., "8080").
Defines a probe that checks whether the container is still alive. If the probe fails, the kubelet restarts the container. This configures the liveness probe for the init container.
Specifies a command to run inside the container. The liveness probe is successful if the command exits with status code 0.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container. The working directory for the command is root ('/') in the container's filesystem. The command is simply exec'd, not run inside a shell. Exit status of 0 indicates success; non-zero is unhealthy.
The number of consecutive failures of the liveness probe before the container is restarted. The minimum value is 1.
grpc configures a gRPC-based liveness probe. It specifies the port to check and optionally the service name for the gRPC health check.
The port number to use for the gRPC health check. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the gRPC service to query for the health check. If not specified, the default is an empty string, which typically refers to the server's default health check service.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform as the liveness probe. It configures the HTTP request details such as path, port, and headers used to determine container health.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.

List of custom HTTP headers to include in the probe request. Each header is defined by a name and value pair, allowing the probe to send authentication or other required headers to the target endpoint.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the liveness probe request. This is the header field name (e.g., 'X-Custom-Header') as defined in the HTTPHeader schema.
The value of the HTTP header sent in the liveness probe request.
Path to access on the HTTP server for the liveness probe. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The TCP port to send the HTTP GET request to. Accepts an integer port number or a named port (string).
The protocol (scheme) used for the HTTP GET request, such as HTTP or HTTPS.
Scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the liveness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds; minimum value is 1.
The minimum number of consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For liveness probes, this must be 1. Minimum value is 1.
TCPSocket specifies the TCP socket probe action for the liveness check. It defines the port (and optionally host) that the kubelet will attempt to connect to in order to determine container health.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The TCP port number to check, either as a numeric value or a name of a port defined in the container. For example, 8080 or 'http'.

The number of seconds to wait for the container to terminate gracefully after sending the termination signal before forcefully killing it. Must be a non-negative integer; 0 means delete immediately. Defaults to 30 seconds if not set.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second, and must be at least 1.
The name of the init container. Must be a valid DNS_LABEL and unique within the pod.
List of ports exposed by the init container. Each port object can specify the container port number, protocol (TCP or UDP), optional name, and host port mapping.
The port number that the container exposes on its network interface.
The host IP address to bind the container port to on the node. If specified, the container port is accessible only on this IP. Defaults to all interfaces (0.0.0.0) when not set.

The port number on the host node to which the container port is bound. When set, the container can be accessed externally via the node's IP at this port; if unset, the container port is only reachable from within the cluster.
The name of the container port. Must be an IANA_SVC_NAME (up to 15 characters, alphanumeric and hyphens) and unique within the pod. This name can be referenced by services to target this port.
The protocol for the port. Must be UDP, TCP, or SCTP. Defaults to TCP.
Specifies how kubelet checks the container's readiness. For init containers, this probe is ignored and has no effect.
Exec specifies the action to take, which involves running a command inside the container. The command is an array of strings, with the first element being the command and the rest being arguments.
The command to run inside the container for the readiness check. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0.
The number of consecutive failures allowed before the container is marked as unready. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.
gRPC specifies the parameters for a gRPC health check used by the readiness probe. It includes the port to check (required) and optionally the service name (defaults to the container's hostname).
The port number of the gRPC service. The probe connects to this port to perform the health check.
The name of the gRPC service to place in the health check request. If empty, the default behavior defined by the gRPC health checking protocol is used.
HTTPGet specifies the HTTP GET request to perform as part of the readiness probe. It defines the request path, port, and optional headers used to check container health.
Host name or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to set in the request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the readiness probe request, paired with the corresponding header name.
The HTTP path to request, e.g., /healthz. Defaults to the root path "/" if not specified.
The TCP port number or named port on the container to which the HTTP GET request should be sent. It must be a valid port number (1-65535) or the name of a port defined in the container.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request in the readiness probe.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Minimum value is 0 (default).
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 10 if not specified.
The minimum number of consecutive successful probe results required for the probe to be considered successful after a failure. For readiness probes, this defaults to 1 and must be at least 1.

Configures a TCP socket probe for the readiness check, which verifies container health by attempting to open a TCP connection to a specified port (and optionally a host). The object defines the port and host for the TCP connection.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to check, specified as a number or a named port defined in the container.
The amount of time in seconds to wait for the container to terminate gracefully after receiving a termination signal, before forcing shutdown. If unset, Kubernetes uses a default of 30 seconds.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Must be at least 1.

A list of resource resize policies for the container. Each policy specifies a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and a restart policy (NotRequired or RestartContainer) that determines whether the container must be restarted when the resource size changes.
The name of the resource (e.g., 'cpu' or 'memory') to which this resize policy applies.

The restart policy for the container when its resources are resized. Valid values are 'NotRequired' (resize can occur without restarting the container) and 'RestartContainer' (the container must be restarted to apply the resize).

Compute resources required by the init container, including requests and limits for CPU and memory. The requests field specifies the minimum resources required, and the limits field specifies the maximum resources allowed.
Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this container. This is an alpha feature and may change in the future.
The name of the ResourceClaim that this container requires. The claim must be created in the same namespace as the pod before it can be used.

The maximum amount of compute resources (such as cpu and memory) that the init container can use. The map keys are resource names (e.g., 'cpu', 'memory') and the values are Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., '100m', '1Gi').

A map of resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) to quantities specifying the minimum amount of compute resources required for the init container. If requests are omitted, they default to the container's limits (if set) or an implementation-defined value, and requests cannot exceed limits.
Specifies the operator used to match the container's exit code against the values in the exit_codes list for the restart policy rule.
The list of container exit codes that this restart policy rule matches. Each value is a numeric exit code.

SecurityContext defines the security options the container should be run with, such as user IDs, SELinux options, capabilities, and read-only root filesystem. If set, the fields of securityContext override the equivalent fields of the PodSecurityContext for this init container.

Controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, the container process is run with the 'no_new_privs' flag, preventing privilege escalation such as setuid or file capabilities.

AppArmorProfile defines the AppArmor profile to be applied to the container. It includes a type (RuntimeDefault, Localhost, or Unconfined) and, when type is Localhost, a localhostProfile field specifying the profile name on the node.
Name of a profile on the node to use. Only relevant when the AppArmor profile type is 'Localhost'.
The type of AppArmor profile to apply. Valid values are `RuntimeDefault`, `Localhost`, and `Unconfined`.
Capabilities to add or drop for the container, given as an object with `add` and `drop` lists of Linux capabilities. This allows fine-grained privilege control for init containers.
Adds the specified Linux capabilities to the container's security context. Each entry is a capability name, e.g., 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME'.
Specifies a list of capabilities to drop from the container's default capability set. Each entry is a Linux capability name (e.g., 'NET_ADMIN').

Indicates whether the init container runs in privileged mode. When true, the container gains elevated permissions, including access to host devices and capabilities, similar to running as root on the host.
Specifies the proc mount type for the container, controlling how the /proc filesystem is exposed within the container.
Indicates whether the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only. When true, the container cannot write to its root filesystem, enhancing security for init containers.
The GID (group ID) to run the entrypoint of the container process. If not set, the default is the group ID specified in the container image.

Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. If true, the kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and will fail to start the container if it does.
The UID to run the entrypoint of the init container process. Defaults to the user specified in the image metadata if not set.
SELinux options for the init container. This object specifies the SELinux label (user, role, type, level) that the container's processes will run with.
The SELinux level (MLS/MCS) to apply to the container, such as 's0' or 's0:c1,c2'.
The SELinux role label that applies to the container. This corresponds to the `role` field in Kubernetes' SELinuxOptions.
The SELinux type label applied to the container, e.g., svirt_apache_t. This field is part of the SELinux security context options for the container.
The SELinux user label assigned to the container, which is the user component of the SELinux context (e.g., 'system_u').
seccomp_profile defines the seccomp profile applied to the init container's security context, specifying how system calls are filtered using supported profile types (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost).
The path to the localhost seccomp profile. Used when the seccomp profile type is set to 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to use. Valid values are: RuntimeDefault, Localhost, and Unconfined. When set to Localhost, the localhostProfile field must also be specified.
WindowsSecurityContextOptions contain Windows-specific options and credentials. This includes settings such as GMSA credentials and runAsUserName for Windows containers.
The path to the GMSA credential spec file. This is used to configure Group Managed Service Accounts (GMSA) for Windows containers in the init container's security context.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container. This field is part of the Windows security context options for the container.
Indicates whether the container runs as a HostProcess container. When true, the container gains access to the Windows host namespace and resources.
The Windows user name (in the form 'user' or 'domain\user') to run the container's entrypoint process as. If not specified, the default user from the container image metadata is used.

startup_probe is a Kubernetes probe that indicates whether the application in the container is started. If configured, it disables liveness and readiness checks until the startup probe succeeds, ensuring those probes do not interfere with application startup.
Exec specifies the action to take, consisting of a command to be executed inside the container. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status code 0.
Command is the command line to execute inside the container. It is specified as a list of strings; the first element is the command, and the remaining elements are arguments.
failureThreshold is the minimum consecutive failures of the startup probe before it is considered failed. The value must be an integer greater than or equal to 1; the default is 3.
Defines a gRPC action for the startup probe, specifying the port and optional service name to check container health via gRPC.
The port number to connect to for the gRPC health check. Must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC server.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform against the container to check its startup status. The probe succeeds if the response status code is between 200 and 399.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not set. Consider setting the Host header via httpHeaders instead for most use cases.
Specifies custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP request sent by the startup probe. Each entry defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header in a list of headers to send with the probe request.
The value of the HTTP header used in a startup probe's HTTP GET request.
The path to access on the HTTP server for the startup probe's HTTP GET request.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid integer port number or a named port (as defined in the container's ports).
The network protocol to use for the HTTP request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container starts before the startup probe is initiated. Minimum value is 0 and defaults to 0.
The interval in seconds between successive startup probe checks. Determines how often the kubelet performs the probe on the container.

The minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1; increasing it requires multiple consecutive successes before the container is marked healthy.
Specifies the TCP socket probe action for the startup probe. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port to determine container health.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP probe. If omitted, the pod IP address is used.
The TCP port to connect to for the socket probe. Accepts a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.

The number of seconds to wait for the container to terminate gracefully after a startup probe failure, before it is forcibly killed. Overrides the pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds for this container.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second; minimum value is 1.
Indicates whether the container runtime should allocate a stdin stream for the container. When true, the container's standard input is kept open and available. Defaults to false.
If true, the container's standard input is closed after the first client attaches, preventing subsequent attaches. This requires 'stdin' to be true.
Path where the container's termination message is written. When the container exits, Kubernetes reads this file to get the termination message. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Determines how the container's termination message is captured. Valid values are 'File' (default), which reads from the file specified by terminationMessagePath, and 'Log', which reads from the container's log output.
Whether this container should allocate a TTY for itself.
VolumeDevices is the list of block devices to be used by the container. It is used to expose a raw block device to the container.
Path inside the container where the block device will be mounted.
Name of the volume device, which must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's volumes list.
A list of volumes to mount into the init container's filesystem. Each item specifies the volume name and the mount path inside the container.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path and must not contain ':'.

Determines how mount propagation works between the host and the container, and between containers sharing the same volume. Allowed values: None (no propagation), HostToContainer (mounts created on the host are visible in the container), and Bidirectional (mounts propagate both ways, requiring privileged containers). Defaults to None.
The name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes.
Whether the volume is mounted as read-only. If set to true, the container can only read from the volume, not write to it. Defaults to false.

Indicates whether the read-only mount option is applied recursively to all nested mounts under this volume mount. Must be one of 'Enabled', 'Disabled', or 'IfPossible'. Only supported for volume types that enable recursive mounts, such as CSI volumes.
Specifies a sub-path inside the referenced volume to mount instead of the volume's root. This allows mounting only a subdirectory or file from the volume.
Specifies an alternative to subPath that supports environment variable expansion using $(VAR_NAME) syntax to define the path within the volume to mount.

The working directory for the init container. If not specified, the container runtime default is used (usually the image's specified working directory). Overrides the image's working directory when set.

Specifies the condition type that must be satisfied for the pod to be considered ready. This corresponds to a condition name in the pod's status.conditions, allowing custom readiness conditions beyond the default pod status.
Name of the resource claim. Must be unique within the pod.

The name of the ResourceClaim object in the same namespace that provides the resource. This references a specific ResourceClaim, and only one of resourceClaimName and resourceClaimTemplateName can be set.
The name of a ResourceClaimTemplate object in the same namespace as the pod. The resource claim is generated from this template, defining the requested resource.
Name of the ResourceClaim object that provides the resources. Must be in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the ResourceClaim object that this claim refers to. The ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the scheduling gate. Pods are not scheduled until all gates with these names are removed from the pod's spec.
The name of the sysctl parameter to set, for example `kernel.shm_rmid_forced`.
The value to assign to the sysctl setting, expressed as a string.
The taint effect to tolerate. Valid values are 'NoSchedule', 'PreferNoSchedule', and 'NoExecute'. If empty, matches all effects.
The taint key that the toleration applies to. An empty key matches all taint keys when the operator is 'Exists'.

The operator represents the relationship between the key and value. Valid values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. When set to 'Exists', the value should be empty. When set to 'Equal', the value must match the taint value.
The number of seconds the pod will tolerate the taint before being evicted, typically used with the NoExecute effect.

The taint value the toleration matches. This is used only when the operator is "Equal"; for "Exists" the value must be empty. In the context of a DaemonSet pod spec, it defines which taint value this toleration can tolerate.
A label selector to identify the set of pods that this topology spread constraint applies to. If omitted, the constraint applies to all pods in the namespace.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. These expressions are combined with matchLabels to define the label selector for the topology spread constraint.
The label key that the match expression applies to. The expression matches pods with this label key based on the operator and values.
The operator specifies the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
List of string values that the label key must match when the operator is In or NotIn. Must be empty for Exists and DoesNotExist operators.
A map of label keys to values that the topology spread constraint applies to. Only pods with all specified labels are considered when spreading across the topology domain.

MatchLabelKeys is a set of pod label keys that identifies the pods over which spreading is calculated. If non-empty, the values of these labels from the pod owning this constraint are used to filter the pods matched by the selector; each key must be unique and exist in the pod's labels.
The maximum difference in the number of matching pods between any two topology domains for the workload. Must be greater than zero.

Specifies the minimum number of eligible topology domains that must be used for pod spreading. If the number of eligible domains is less than this value, the global minimum skew is treated as zero when calculating spread.

Specifies how to treat node affinity when calculating pod topology spread skew. Allowed values are "Honor" and "Ignore". When "Honor", nodes with matching node affinity are included; when "Ignore", node affinity is not considered.

Indicates how to handle nodes with taints when calculating pod spread. Accepts 'Honor' to exclude tainted nodes that do not tolerate the pod's tolerations, or 'Ignore' to include all nodes regardless of taints. Defaults to 'Honor'.

The key of node labels. Nodes that have a label with this key and identical values are considered to be in the same topology domain. This key is required for each topology spread constraint and defines how pods are spread across different domains, such as zones or hosts.

Specifies how to handle pods when the topology spread constraint is not satisfied. Allowed values are 'DoNotSchedule' (default), which prevents scheduling, and 'ScheduleAnyway', which schedules the pod regardless.

Represents an AWS Elastic Block Store volume source that can be mounted into a container within a pod. This field configures the volume to use an AWS EBS volume, allowing persistent storage for the daemon set's pods.
Filesystem type to be used for the AWS EBS volume, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. Defaults to ext4 if unspecified.
The partition number of the AWS EBS volume to mount. If specified, only that partition is mounted; otherwise, the entire volume is used.
Indicates whether the AWS Elastic Block Store volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false; set to true to prevent writes.
The unique ID of the AWS EBS volume to mount.
Configures an Azure Disk volume to be mounted into the pod. This is a volume source that references an Azure Data Disk and contains settings for the disk mount.
Specifies the caching mode for the Azure disk volume. Allowed values are None, ReadOnly, and ReadWrite; defaults to None if not specified.
The name of the Azure data disk to attach to the pod. Must be the name of an existing Azure disk in the same location as the cluster.
The URI of the Azure blob storage disk to mount. Must be specified when using a blob-based disk, in the format https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net/<container>/<vhd-name>.vhd.
Filesystem type to mount (e.g., ext4, xfs). Defaults to ext4.
The kind of Azure Data Disk. Allowed values are 'Shared', 'Dedicated', and 'Managed'. Defaults to 'Shared'.
Mounts the Azure disk as read-only when set to true. Defaults to false (read/write).

Represents an Azure File volume source, which mounts an Azure File share into the pod. This configuration typically requires a secret name with Azure storage credentials and a share name, and optionally supports read-only mounting.
Indicates whether the Azure file share should be mounted read-only. If set to true, the volume is mounted read-only; otherwise it is mounted read-write. Defaults to false.
The name of the secret that contains the Azure Storage account name and key, used to authenticate to the Azure file share.
The name of the Azure File share that should be mounted. This corresponds to the shareName field in the Kubernetes azureFile volume source.
Defines a CephFS volume source, used to mount a Ceph Filesystem into the pod. Contains configuration such as monitors, path, user, and secret references.
List of Ceph monitor addresses (hostnames or IPs) for the CephFS volume. Required to connect to the Ceph cluster.
Path within the CephFS filesystem to mount into the pod.
Specifies whether the CephFS volume is mounted as read-only. If true, the volume is read-only; if false (or omitted), it is read-write.
Path to the Ceph keyring file on the host, used for authentication with the Ceph cluster. Either this or secret_ref is required to provide credentials.

secretRef is an optional reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the Ceph credentials (keyring) for accessing the CephFS filesystem. The secret must be in the same namespace as the pod; if not specified, Ceph uses the default keyring.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that provides the CephFS credentials.
The CephFS user to use when mounting the volume. If unset, defaults to 'admin'.
Represents a Cinder volume in OpenStack. Used to attach a Cinder volume to the pod for persistent storage.
Filesystem type to mount for the Cinder volume. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system, e.g., ext4, xfs, ntfs. If not specified, ext4 is typically inferred.
Specifies whether the Cinder volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read/write). If true, forces the read-only setting in volume mounts.

secret_ref is a reference to a Kubernetes secret that contains the authentication credentials (username and password) for the Cinder volume. It is an object with a 'name' field specifying the name of the secret in the same namespace.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret object that contains authentication credentials for the Cinder volume.
The unique ID of the Cinder volume to be mounted. This is a required field for Cinder volume sources.

config_map configures a volume sourced from a Kubernetes ConfigMap. It specifies the name of the ConfigMap to reference and optionally defines which items (keys) to project as files, including their paths and permissions.
Sets the default file permission mode (in octal) for all files in the ConfigMap volume. When unspecified, the default is 0644.

Maps keys from the ConfigMap to specific file paths and optional mode. If unspecified, all keys are projected as files. If specified, only the listed keys are projected, with custom paths and permissions.
The key to select from the ConfigMap's data. The value corresponding to this key will be exposed at the defined path within the volume.
Mode bits used to set permissions on this file, expressed as an octal integer (e.g., 0644).
The relative path of the file within the volume where the value from the corresponding config map key is written.
Name of the ConfigMap to reference for this volume. The volume will be populated with data from the specified ConfigMap.
Optional specifies whether the ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. If true, the volume will not fail if the ConfigMap is missing or if any of the specified keys are absent.

Represents a volume that is provisioned and mounted using a Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver. This configuration includes the driver's name, the volume handle, filesystem type, read-only setting, and any driver-specific volume attributes.
The name of the CSI driver that manages the volume. This must match the name of a CSI driver installed on the cluster.
Filesystem type to mount for the CSI volume (e.g., ext4, xfs). If omitted, the CSI driver's default filesystem type is used.

A reference to a Secret containing credentials or configuration required by the CSI driver for the node publish (or unpublish) operation. It is optional and typically specified when the driver requires additional secrets at node stage/publish time.
The name of the secret. This secret is referenced for the CSI node publish operation.
Indicates if the CSI volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
volumeAttributes are arbitrary attributes of the volume that are passed to the external CSI volume driver.

Configures a Downward API volume that exposes pod metadata (such as labels, annotations, and other fields) to the container as files. This allows containers to read information about themselves without using the Kubernetes API.
The default permissions mode (in octal) for files created by the downward API volume. Must be a value between 0 and 0777; defaults to 0644. This setting does not affect directories.
items specifies the list of downward API volume files. Each item defines a file path and a field reference (fieldRef or resourceFieldRef) to expose.

Selects a field of the pod to expose via the downward API volume. Supported fields include metadata.name, metadata.namespace, metadata.labels, metadata.annotations, spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.hostIP, status.podIP, and status.podIPs.
Version of the schema the field_path is written in terms of. Typically the Kubernetes API version, e.g., 'v1'.
The path to the pod field whose value is exposed to the container via the downward API volume, e.g., metadata.name or metadata.namespace.
The file permission mode, represented as an octal number (e.g., 0644). If not specified, the default mode is 0644.
Path is the file path within the downward API volume where the field value will be written. It is relative to the volume's mount point and must not contain '..'.
Selects a resource field of a container (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) to expose to the downward API volume item.
The name of the container to which the resource field reference applies, used to expose that container's resource limits or requests via the downward API.
The divisor for the resource value, used to scale the quantity (e.g., CPU time). Must be a Quantity string (e.g., '1m', '1Ki'), defaults to '1'.
The name of the container resource to expose, such as 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory'.

Represents an emptyDir volume, a temporary directory created empty when the pod is assigned to a node and deleted when the pod is removed. It provides scratch space that does not persist across pod restarts and is shared by all containers in the pod.

Specifies the storage medium for the emptyDir volume. An empty string (default) uses the node's default storage (disk), 'Memory' uses a RAM-backed tmpfs filesystem, and 'HugePages' uses the Linux huge pages filesystem.
The maximum size of the emptyDir volume, specified as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1Gi'). If unset, the volume is limited by the node's storage.
Represents an ephemeral volume that is created with the pod and deleted when the pod is removed. This field can be used to define a volume from a generic ephemeral volume or a CSI ephemeral volume.

Defines the PersistentVolumeClaim template that is used to create a PVC for this ephemeral volume. The template specifies the desired characteristics of the PVC, such as storage class, access modes, and resources.
Metadata for the PersistentVolumeClaim created by this ephemeral volume claim template, used to set labels, annotations, and optionally a name for the PVC.

Annotations is a map of string keys and values that attaches arbitrary non-identifying metadata to the volume claim template. This is commonly used to store tooling information or other custom metadata without affecting selection.
The timestamp, in RFC3339 format, indicating when the persistent volume claim generated from this template was created. This field is set by the server and cannot be set by clients.
In Kubernetes ObjectMeta, this field specifies the duration in seconds before the object should be deleted. It is set when a graceful deletion is requested and must be a non-negative integer.

The deletionTimestamp is set when the object is marked for deletion, indicating the time at which it will be (or was) removed, in RFC3339 format. In this context, it applies to the PersistentVolumeClaims generated from the volume claim template.
A list of finalizers for this object. Finalizers are strings that must be removed before the object can be deleted, ensuring pre-delete operations complete.

generateName is an optional prefix used by the API server to generate a unique name if the name field is not provided. The generated name will be the prefix plus a random suffix, and the server handles uniqueness conflicts automatically.
A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state. Populated by the system. Read-only.
Labels to assign to the volume claim template's metadata. These labels are applied to the persistent volume claim created from this template, allowing selection and identification of the claim.

A list of ManagedFieldsEntry objects that track the field management operations affecting this metadata. Each entry records the manager, operation, API version, and managed fields (e.g., for server-side apply).

The API version of the resource that the manager used to manage these fields. This is part of the managedFields metadata entry, indicating which API version the managing controller or agent operated with.
FieldsType is the type of the managed fields entry, indicating the serialization format of the FieldsV1 member. For the Kubernetes API, this is typically set to 'FieldsV1'.
This field contains a JSON representation of the managed fields for this entry, encoding which fields are managed by the manager in the v1 format.

The name of the manager (e.g., kubectl, a controller, or an operator) that last applied or updated this managed field. In Kubernetes, each managedFields entry tracks which component owns the fields it manages, and this string identifies that component.
The operation type of the managed field entry, indicating whether the field was applied or updated. Supported values are 'Apply' and 'Update'.

The name of the subresource used to update the object, or empty string if the update was through the main resource. Distinguishes managers even if they share the same name; for example, 'status' for status subresource updates.
Timestamp of when the operation recorded in this managed fields entry was performed.
The metadata name for the volume claim template. This name is not used for the resulting PersistentVolumeClaim; the system generates the PVC name from the pod name and volume name.
The namespace for the volume claim template. For ephemeral volumes, this field must be empty because the resulting PersistentVolumeClaim is always created in the same namespace as the pod.

List of references to the owning objects. Each entry includes fields such as apiVersion, kind, name, uid, and optionally controller and blockOwnerDeletion to specify ownership relationships for garbage collection.
The API version of the owner (referent) object, e.g. 'apps/v1'. This is used together with kind and name to identify the owning object.

Whether this owner reference blocks deletion of the dependent object. If true, the dependent (the volume claim template's metadata) cannot be deleted by the Kubernetes garbage collector until the owner is deleted.
Indicates whether the referenced owner is the managing controller of the object.
The Kubernetes resource kind of the owner object referenced by this owner reference, such as 'DaemonSet'.
The name of the owner object that this reference points to. This corresponds to the metadata.name of the referenced resource.
The UID of the owner object referenced by this OwnerReference. It uniquely identifies the referenced resource in the Kubernetes API.
The resource version of the object, used for optimistic concurrency. This value is set by the server and should not be modified by clients.
The selfLink attribute contains a URL that identifies the resource. It is deprecated and may not be populated in newer Kubernetes versions.
UID is the unique in time and space value for this object. It is typically generated by the server on successful creation of a resource and is not allowed to change on PUT operations.

The specification of the persistent volume claim to be created for this ephemeral volume. It defines properties such as access modes, resource requests, storage class name, and selector for the underlying persistent volume.
Specifies the access modes for the persistent volume claim, determining how the volume can be mounted. Common values include ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, and ReadWriteMany.

data_source is an object that specifies an existing data source (e.g., a VolumeSnapshot or another PersistentVolumeClaim) from which to provision the volume. It corresponds to the dataSource field in a Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaimSpec and uses a TypedLocalObjectReference.
The API group of the referenced data source. Use an empty string for the core API group, or a specific group such as 'snapshot.storage.k8s.io' for VolumeSnapshot.
Kind of the referenced object (e.g., PersistentVolumeClaim).

The name of the data source object referenced by this volume claim template. This is used with the apiGroup and kind fields to identify a specific PersistentVolumeClaim, VolumeSnapshot, or other supported data source.
Reference to a data source object, such as a VolumeSnapshot or another PersistentVolumeClaim, used to pre-populate the volume. The reference includes the API group, kind, and name of the data source.
The API group of the referenced resource, such as 'snapshot.storage.k8s.io' for a VolumeSnapshot. For core resources, this is empty.
The kind (resource type) of the object referenced by this data source reference. For example, 'PersistentVolumeClaim' or 'VolumeSnapshot'.
The name of the referenced object in the same namespace, such as a PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot.
Namespace of the referenced data source object. If omitted, it is assumed to be in the same namespace as the volume claim template.
Minimum storage resources required by the volume claim, typically specified as a quantity in `requests.storage` (e.g., "5Gi").

Resource limits for the ephemeral volume claim, defined as a map of resource names (like 'storage') to quantity strings (e.g., '1Gi'). These limits cap the amount of storage that can be requested by the volume claim template.
A map of resource names to Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., 'cpu': '500m', 'memory': '1Gi') that specifies the minimum amount of resources required for the ephemeral volume claim.
A label query over volumes to consider for binding. This selector is used to match existing PersistentVolumes to the claim.
A list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values. This selector is used to match the labels of the volume claim template.
The label key that the selector expression operates on. It identifies the specific label whose value is checked against the operator and values.
Represents the logical operator that relates the key and values of a label selector requirement. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
values is a list of string values for the label selector match expression. It must be non-empty for operators 'In' and 'NotIn', and must be empty for operators 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist'.

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.
The name of the StorageClass to use for dynamically provisioned storage. If not specified, the cluster's default StorageClass is used.

Name of the VolumeAttributesClass to use for this persistent volume claim. When specified, it applies a set of customizable attributes (such as IOPS or throughput) to the dynamically provisioned volume.
volumeMode specifies whether the volume is treated as a raw block device (Block) or as a filesystem (Filesystem). The default is Filesystem.
The name of the PersistentVolume to bind to this volume claim. When specified, the claim is bound to that existing PersistentVolume.
Configures a Fibre Channel (FC) volume source, allowing the Pod to mount a Fibre Channel LUN. This is used to define an FC volume with parameters such as target WWNs and filesystem type.
Filesystem type to mount for the Fibre Channel volume, such as ext4 or xfs. If not specified, the filesystem type of the first partition is used.
The logical unit number (LUN) of the Fibre Channel volume.
Indicates whether the fibre channel volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; otherwise it is read-write. Defaults to false if not specified.
List of Fibre Channel target World Wide Names (WWNs) for the FC volume. This specifies the addresses of the storage targets to connect to.
Optional list of Fibre Channel World Wide Identifiers (WWIDs) that specify the target volume. This field can be used instead of targetWWNs and lun to identify the Fibre Channel volume.
FlexVolume represents a generic volume plugin that mounts a volume using a user-specified driver and optional options.
Specifies the FlexVolume driver to use for mounting this volume. This is typically a registered volume plugin name.
Filesystem type to mount on the flex volume, e.g. 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Must be supported by the host operating system.
Optional: Extra command options to pass to the FlexVolume plugin, as a map of string keys and values.
If true, the FlexVolume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Optional reference to a Secret that provides sensitive information to the FlexVolume plugin. The Secret must be in the same namespace as the Pod; only the Secret name is specified.
The name of the Secret in the pod's namespace that provides sensitive information to the FlexVolume plugin. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Defines a Flocker volume to be mounted into the container. Flocker is a deprecated volume source in Kubernetes, used to mount volumes from a Flocker dataset.
The name of the Flocker dataset to use for this volume.
UUID of the Flocker dataset. Either dataset_name or dataset_uuid is required, but not both.
gcePersistentDisk represents a Google Compute Engine Persistent Disk resource. This configures the disk name, filesystem type, partition, and read-only mode for mounting the disk into the pod.
Filesystem type to mount, such as ext4 or xfs. Defaults to ext4 if unset.
The partition number on the GCE persistent disk. If specified, only that partition is mounted; if omitted, the entire disk is used.
The name of the Google Compute Engine persistent disk (PD) to mount as a volume in the pod.
Specifies whether the GCE persistent disk is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Represents a gitRepo volume, which clones a Git repository into a volume. Contains settings such as repository, revision, and directory.

Target directory name for the git repo volume. Must not contain or start with '..'. If omitted, the volume root is the git repository root; if specified, it mounts the named subdirectory of the repository.
Repository is the URL of the Git repository to clone into the volume.
The commit revision (hash, tag, or branch) to check out from the git repository. If omitted, the repository's HEAD revision is used.
GlusterFS volume source configuration. Defines how to mount a GlusterFS volume into the pod, including the GlusterFS cluster endpoint and path.
Name of the Endpoints object that defines the GlusterFS cluster topology. Required when using the GlusterFS volume type, and must reference a valid Endpoints resource in the same namespace.
The GlusterFS volume path (e.g., the exported volume name) that is mounted into the pod. This is the name of the GlusterFS volume as defined on the GlusterFS server, such as 'gv0'.
ReadOnly here will force the Glusterfs volume to be mounted with read-only permissions. Defaults to false (read/write).

hostPath represents a pre-existing file or directory on the host machine that is directly exposed to the container. This volume type mounts a file or directory from the host node's filesystem into the pod.
Path of the directory or file on the host node to mount into the pod. This is the absolute path on the node's filesystem.
Specifies the type of hostPath volume. Allowed values are: DirectoryOrCreate, Directory, FileOrCreate, File, Socket, CharDevice, BlockDevice. If not set, the hostPath is used without any type check.

The image volume source that mounts an OCI image as a volume. This field represents an ImageVolumeSource object, allowing the pod to access the contents of the image without running it as a container.

The Kubernetes image pull policy for an image volume source. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never, controlling whether the image is pulled each time, only if absent locally, or never. Defaults to Always when not set.
Reference is the fully qualified image name and tag to mount as the volume, e.g., 'example.com/foo/bar:1.0'.
Configures an ISCSI volume source, allowing a pod to mount an ISCSI target as a volume. This object defines connection and mounting parameters for the ISCSI disk.
Enable CHAP authentication for iSCSI discovery. When set to true, the initiator performs CHAP authentication with the target during the discovery phase.
Whether to enable CHAP authentication for the iSCSI session.
Filesystem type to mount, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system.
Specifies a custom iSCSI initiator name. If not set, the system uses the default initiator name configured on the kubelet.
The iSCSI Qualified Name (IQN) of the target iSCSI device, used to identify the specific iSCSI target for mounting.
The name of the iSCSI interface. If not specified, defaults to "default".
lun is the iSCSI Target Lun number, specifying the logical unit number of the target.
The list of iSCSI portals to connect to if the targetPortal is not the default. Each portal is typically an IP address or hostname along with a port.
Specifies whether the iSCSI volume is mounted as read-only. When true, the filesystem is read-only; otherwise it is read-write (default false).
Reference to the secret that contains CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI volume.
Name of the Secret object that provides authentication credentials (e.g., CHAP) for the iSCSI volume. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
The iSCSI target portal. The portal is either an IP or ip_addr:port if a different port is needed.
The name of the volume. This must be a DNS_LABEL and unique within the pod. Containers reference this name in their volumeMounts to mount the volume.
NFS volume source configuration, allowing the pod to mount a Network File System share.
Path that is exported by the NFS server.
Indicates whether the NFS volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; otherwise, it is read-write.
Hostname or IP address of the NFS server. This field is required when configuring an NFS volume.
PersistentVolumeClaimVolumeSource. Specifies a PersistentVolumeClaim in the same namespace as the pod that should be mounted as a volume. The claim must exist and be bound before the pod can start.
The name of the PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) in the same namespace to use as the volume source for this volume.
For a volume of type persistentVolumeClaim, if true, mounts the volume as read-only. Defaults to false.
Specifies a volume that uses a Photon Controller persistent disk. This configuration includes the persistent disk's ID and the filesystem type to mount.

Filesystem type to mount for the Photon persistent disk volume. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system (e.g., ext4, xfs). If not specified, the filesystem type is inferred from the volume.
The unique identifier of the Photon Controller persistent disk to mount as a volume.
Configuration for a Portworx volume. When specified, this volume source mounts a Portworx volume into the pod.
Filesystem type to mount for the Portworx volume, such as 'ext4', 'xfs', or 'ntfs'. If unspecified, it is inferred to be 'ext4'.
If true, the volume is mounted as read-only.
The unique identifier of the Portworx volume to mount. This field is required and must correspond to an existing Portworx volume in the cluster.
Projected volumes map several existing volume sources into the same directory. This allows a single volume to combine multiple sources such as secrets, configmaps, and service account tokens.
The default permission mode bits for files in the projected volume, expressed as an octal value (e.g., 0o644). If omitted, the API server applies a default of 0644.
Specifies the list of volume sources to project into the same directory. Each entry can reference a Secret, ConfigMap, DownwardAPI, or ServiceAccountToken.
Configures a ClusterTrustBundle as a projected volume source, allowing the bundle's certificates to be mounted into the container.

label_selector is a Kubernetes label selector that filters the ClusterTrustBundles to be projected. When specified, only ClusterTrustBundles whose labels match this selector are included in the projected volume.
A list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and a list of values.
The label key that this match expression applies to. In a Kubernetes label selector requirement, this is the key used together with the operator to match against pod labels.
Specifies the operator for the label selector match expression. Allowed values: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist.
A list of string values that the label key must match for the In and NotIn operators. For the Exists and DoesNotExist operators, this list must be empty.

match_labels is a map of key-value pairs that selects ClusterTrustBundle resources by their labels. Only ClusterTrustBundles whose labels match all specified key-value pairs are included in the projected volume.

Select a single ClusterTrustBundle by name. If set, this overrides labelSelector to choose a specific cluster trust bundle; if omitted, bundles are selected via labelSelector or all bundles when no selector is specified.

Specifies whether the referenced ClusterTrustBundle is optional. When true, the pod starts even if the bundle is not found, and the projected volume contains no data. When false (default), the pod fails to start if the bundle is missing.
Path is the relative path of the file in the volume where the cluster trust bundle CA bundle will be written. The CA bundle contents are stored at this path.
The name of the certificate signer whose certificates are included in the trust bundle. If empty, the default signer (kubernetes.io/cluster-root) is used.
config_map configures a ConfigMap to be projected into the volume. It specifies the name of the ConfigMap, optional items (key-to-path mappings), and an optional default mode for the files.

A list of key-to-path mappings for projecting selected keys from the referenced ConfigMap into the volume. If unspecified, all key-value pairs are projected as files named by key; if specified, only the listed keys are projected to the given paths, and unlisted keys are not present. Each item includes 'key' and 'path', and optionally 'mode'.
The key in the ConfigMap to project into the volume.
Optional mode bits to set permissions on the file. Must be a valid octal value between 0 and 0777 (or 0 and 511) or -1 to use the default mode.
path is the relative path within the volume to place the file. It must not contain '..' or start with '/'.
The name of the ConfigMap to project into the volume. The ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Indicates whether the referenced ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. When true, the volume can be mounted even if the ConfigMap does not exist; when false or unset, the ConfigMap must exist.

The DownwardAPI projection source for a projected volume. This exposes pod metadata (such as labels, annotations, and resource limits) as files inside the container. Configure the 'items' field to define which fields and file paths to project.

List of downward API volume file definitions. Each item specifies a path within the volume and a field selector (via fieldRef or resourceFieldRef) that exposes the corresponding field's value at that path.
Specifies the Pod field to be projected via the downward API, using a FieldRef that identifies the field path (e.g., metadata.name or spec.nodeName).
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath is written in terms of. For example, 'v1'.

The path to the pod field to expose via the downward API, such as `metadata.name` or `metadata.namespace`. This identifies the specific pod metadata or specification field that will be made available to the container.
Optional file permission mode for the downward API file, expressed as an octal or decimal number (e.g., 0644 or 420). If omitted, defaults to 0644.
Path is the relative path name of the file to be created in the projected volume. It must not be absolute or contain '..'.

Represents a reference to a container resource field (such as CPU or memory limits/requests) to be exposed via the downward API. The value is resolved from the pod's container resources and written to the projected volume at the specified path.

The name of the container whose resource quantity (such as CPU or memory requests/limits) is referenced by this resource field. This field is used to select a container's resource when the downward API exposes container-level resource information.

Specifies the divisor (a Kubernetes quantity) used to divide the referenced resource's value before it is exposed via the downward API. For example, setting divisor to '1Mi' converts a memory value from bytes to mebibytes. Defaults to '1' if unset.
Specifies the resource to expose via the downward API, such as 'cpu' or 'memory', optionally with a request or limit prefix (e.g., 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory').
The path within the projected volume where the pod's certificate chain is mounted, as used in a pod_certificate projected volume source.

The path within the projected volume where the credential bundle (the pod's certificate) is mounted. This is a relative path that determines the filename or directory where the certificate data appears to the container.
The path within the projected volume where the certificate private key is mounted.
Maximum number of seconds for which the pod certificate remains valid. The certificate's lifetime will not exceed this value.
The name of the certificate signer that issues the pod certificate projected into the volume. This must correspond to a signer name known to the cluster.
A map of user-defined annotations to be added to the certificate.

Specifies a Secret to project into the volume. This source makes the contents of a Kubernetes Secret available in the projected volume, with the ability to select specific items and mark the secret as optional.

Optional list of key-to-path mappings for the secret data. Each item maps a specific key in the secret to a relative path within the projected volume. If omitted, all keys in the secret are projected automatically.
The key within the referenced Secret's data to project into the volume.
Mode is the file permission bits (in octal) for the secret file at the given path. If unspecified, the system defaults to 0644.
The relative path of the file within the projected volume to which the secret item is mounted. Corresponds to the path in the secret item mapping.
The name of the Secret to be projected into the volume. This must match the name of a Secret in the pod's namespace.
Specifies whether the referenced Secret must exist. If true, the Secret is optional and its absence does not prevent the volume from being mounted or the pod from starting.
Defines a projected volume source that injects a Kubernetes service account token into the volume. Supports configuration for the token audience, expiration time, and path within the volume.
Audience is the intended audience of the returned token. The recipient of the token must identify itself with this audience. If not set, the token audience defaults to the API server's identifier.

The requested duration of validity for the service account token, in seconds. Defaults to 3600 (1 hour) and must be at least 600 (10 minutes). The kubelet will proactively rotate the token as it approaches expiration.
Specifies the relative path to the token file within the projected volume source. This path determines the file name under which the service account token will be mounted.
Defines a Quobyte volume source, configuring how a Quobyte storage volume is mounted into the pod.
Group to map the volume access to. Default is none.
Mounts the Quobyte volume as read-only when set to true. Defaults to false (read/write).
The Quobyte registry service or list of registries (host:port) to connect to. Required field; multiple entries are comma-separated.
The Quobyte tenant name for the volume. This is used to identify the tenant when accessing the Quobyte storage system.
User to map volume access to. If not provided, defaults to the service account user.
The name of the Quobyte volume to mount.
Represents a Ceph RBD (Rados Block Device) volume source. This allows a pod to mount a Ceph block device as a volume, typically configured via monitors, pool, and image details.
Filesystem type to mount on the RBD volume, e.g., ext4, xfs, ntfs. If unspecified, the system infers ext4 as the default.
The name of the RBD (Ceph block device) image to mount. This field is required when using the RBD volume plugin.
Path to the keyring file used for Ceph authentication. If not specified, defaults to /etc/ceph/keyring.
List of Ceph monitor addresses (e.g., '192.168.1.1:6789') used to connect to the Ceph cluster for this RBD volume.
The Ceph RADOS pool where the RBD image resides. If omitted, Kubernetes defaults this to 'rbd'.
Specifies whether the Ceph RBD volume is mounted read-only. Defaults to false.

secret_ref specifies a reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the Ceph authentication key for the RBD volume. The Secret must be of type 'kubernetes.io/rbd' and include the key in the 'key' data field.
Name of the secret containing the Ceph RBD credentials. Must be in the same namespace as the pod.
The RADOS user name for authentication. Defaults to 'admin' if not specified.
Configuration for a ScaleIO volume source, enabling the pod to mount storage from a ScaleIO (Dell EMC) cluster.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Ex. "ext4", "xfs", "ntfs". Defaults to "ext4" if unspecified.
Host name or IP address of the ScaleIO API Gateway used by the ScaleIO volume.
The name of the ScaleIO Protection Domain for the configured storage.
Specifies whether the ScaleIO volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.

A reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the ScaleIO credentials (access key and secret key). The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod. This field is required when using ScaleIO volumes.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret that contains the credentials needed to access the ScaleIO storage system.
Specifies whether SSL is used for communication with the ScaleIO Gateway. When true, the ScaleIO volume plugin enables SSL for API requests.
The storage mode for the ScaleIO volume. Valid values are 'ThinProvisioned' and 'ThickProvisioned', with 'ThinProvisioned' being the default if unspecified.
Name of the StoragePool in the ScaleIO system where the volume is located.
The name of the ScaleIO system to use for this volume.
The name of the ScaleIO volume to mount from the storage system.

Secret represents a Secret volume source. It configures the volume to consume a Kubernetes Secret, allowing the secret data to be exposed as files in the container. The secret source can specify the secret name, optional key/path items, and default file permissions.
Specifies the permission mode for files within the secret volume, given as an octal integer (e.g., 0644). Defaults to 0644 when not specified.

A list of key-to-path mappings. If specified, only the listed keys from the referenced Secret are mounted as files, each at the specified path. If omitted, all keys in the Secret become files named after the keys.
The key in the Secret's data to project into the volume. This key must exist in the Secret's data map.

Permissions mode for the file. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 (or decimal between 0 and 511). YAML accepts both octal and decimal values; JSON requires decimal. Defaults to the volume's defaultMode.

The relative path of the file within the secret volume where the corresponding secret key's value is mounted. The path must not be absolute, must not contain '..' elements, and must not start with '..'. When `items` is specified, this field is required for each entry.
Indicates whether the referenced Secret must exist. When set to true, the Secret may be missing, and the volume will be created without those files. When false or omitted, the Secret must be present.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret to mount as a volume. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.

Represents a StorageOS volume source in a Kubernetes pod specification. This object defines the parameters for accessing a StorageOS volume, including the volume name, namespace, filesystem type, read-only setting, and optional secret for authentication.
The filesystem type to mount, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system.
Mounts the StorageOS volume with read-only permissions.
A reference to a Secret that contains the API credentials required to access the StorageOS volume.
Name of the Kubernetes Secret that holds the StorageOS API credentials. The Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the StorageOS volume to mount. This is the human-readable name of the volume as defined in StorageOS.
The namespace of the StorageOS volume. Defaults to the namespace of the pod.
Defines a vSphere volume (VMDK) to be attached and mounted to the pod. This block specifies the configuration for the vSphere volume source.
Filesystem type to mount for the vSphere volume (e.g., ext4, xfs). If not specified, defaults to ext4.
The ID of the vSphere Storage Policy Based Management (SPBM) storage policy to apply to the volume.
Name of the vSphere storage policy used to provision storage for the volume.
Path that uniquely identifies the vSphere volume, usually a datastore path like '[datastore1] vm/vm.vmdk'. This field is required for vSphere volumes.

kubernetes_apps_daemon_set.status.condit.text: The last time the condition transitioned from one status to another.
A human-readable message providing details about the condition. This field typically contains information about the reason and any relevant context for the condition's state.
A machine-readable, short, CamelCase string explaining why the condition is in its current state, such as 'MinimumReplicasAvailable' or 'ReplicaFailure'.
The status of the condition, indicating whether the condition is True, False, or Unknown.
The type of the DaemonSet condition, providing a machine-readable identifier such as 'Available' or 'Progressing'.

kubernetes_apps_deployment.metadata.mana.text: The version of the Kubernetes API that the managing controller uses for this managed field entry, typically in the format "apps/v1".
The type of the fields stored in the managed fields entry. In Kubernetes, this is typically "FieldsV1", indicating the structure and version of the fields map.
fields_v1 is a JSON representation (FieldsV1 format) of the set of fields that the manager owns or is responsible for, as recorded in a managedFields entry.

The name of the manager (e.g., a controller, agent, or tool) that owns or last modified this managed field entry in the object's metadata. It identifies which component manages these fields per Kubernetes managedFields semantics.
The type of operation that set the field, e.g., Apply or Update.
The subresource associated with this managed field entry, such as 'status' or 'scale'.
The timestamp of when the managed field operation occurred, represented as a string in RFC3339 format.

kubernetes_apps_deployment.metadata.owne.text: The API version (group/version) of the owner resource, e.g. apps/v1 for a Deployment or v1 for a ConfigMap.
If true, and if the owner has the foregroundDeletion finalizer, the owner cannot be deleted from the key-value store until this reference is removed. Defaults to false.
Indicates whether the owner reference is the controlling owner. If true, this owner is the controller of the dependent object.
The kind of the owner object, such as 'Deployment' or 'ReplicaSet'. This is the Kubernetes API kind of the referenced resource and is required in an owner reference.
The name of the owner object that this reference points to.
The unique identifier (UID) of the owner object referenced by this owner reference. Used to unambiguously identify the owner resource in the cluster.

kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.selector.text: The key of the label to which the selector applies.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values in a label selector requirement. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values. For the In and NotIn operators, this specifies the set of values that the label key must match. For Exists and DoesNotExist, this field must be empty.

kubernetes_apps_deployment.spec.template.text: The API version of the resource to which the managed fields apply, e.g., 'apps/v1'.
The type of the fields in a managed fields entry. In Kubernetes, this is typically 'FieldsV1'.

The set of fields managed by the controller for this object, represented as a JSON structure in the FieldsV1 format. It maps field paths (using keys like 'f:') to their values, indicating exactly which fields are governed by the manager.
Manager is the name of the manager that last applied this field.
The operation that produced this managed field entry. Valid values are 'Apply' and 'Update'.
The subresource that the manager is operating on, such as 'status' or 'scale'. For example, in a Deployment, it could be 'status' for status updates.
The time at which the managed fields entry was last updated, expressed as a string in RFC3339 format.
API version of the referent owner resource.

Indicates whether the dependent object should block the owner's deletion. If true, the owner is prevented from being deleted until this owner reference is removed (requires the owner to have a foregroundDeletion finalizer). Defaults to false.
Indicates whether this owner reference is the managing controller for the resource. When true, the referenced owner is the controller that manages the resource's lifecycle.
The kind of the owner resource (e.g., 'Deployment', 'ReplicaSet'). This must match the kind of the object that owns this resource.
The name of the object that owns this resource, as specified in the owner reference.
The UID of the referenced owner object. This is a unique identifier assigned by the Kubernetes API server to uniquely identify the object.
The node selector term that defines the preference rule. It contains matchExpressions and matchFields constraints used to select nodes that satisfy the preferred scheduling requirement.
A list of node selector requirements. Each requirement contains a key, an operator, and a list of values. All requirements in the list must match the node's labels for the preference to apply.
The label key that the node must have for the affinity rule to match. It is a required field in each match expression.
The operator used to compare the label key to the listed values. Allowed values: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt.
