The list of values for the node selector requirement. When the operator is In or NotIn, this list must contain at least one value; for Exists or DoesNotExist, it must be empty.
A list of node selector requirements that specify field-based constraints for the node, such as metadata.name, to match for this preferred scheduling term.
The key of the node label that the match field expression applies to. This key must exist on the node for the affinity rule to match.
The operator represents the relationship between the node label/field key and the value(s) to match. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.
A list of string values for the field selector. This is required when the operator is In, NotIn, Gt, or Lt, and must be empty for Exists or DoesNotExist.

The weight associated with this node affinity preference. Must be an integer between 1 and 100. During scheduling, each node that satisfies the preference adds this weight to its overall score; nodes with higher total weights are preferred.

A list of node selector requirements. Each requirement defines a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. All requirements in the list must be satisfied for the node to match the selector term.
The key of the node label to match against. This key is used with the specified operator to evaluate node affinity.
The operator used to match node labels in a node affinity match expression. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.
The list of values for the match expression. For operators In, NotIn, Gt, and Lt, this list contains the values to match against the node label. For Exists and DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.
A list of node selector requirements that specify node fields (e.g., metadata.name) to match. Each item includes a key, operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optional values.
The key of the node field that this requirement applies to. For match_fields, common keys include 'metadata.name'.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and value(s). Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.
List of values for the match field constraint. Required when the operator is In or NotIn; must be empty for Exists or DoesNotExist.

Defines a set of pods (via label selectors) and a topology domain (via topologyKey) used to express pod affinity or anti-affinity rules. In this context, it supplies the pod matching criteria for a preferred scheduling term.

A standard Kubernetes label selector (with matchLabels and matchExpressions) that selects the set of pods to which this pod affinity term applies. It determines which pods are considered as affinity targets.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, or DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. Multiple requirements are logically ANDed together with matchLabels.
The label key that the selector applies to. This is the key of a label on the pod that must match the specified operator and values.
Operator represents the key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.

A list of string values that the label selector key must match. Required when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'; ignored when the operator is 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist'. The values act as the set of allowed or disallowed values for the key, depending on the operator.
A map of keys and values that the target pods must have. All labels specified here must be present on the pod for the affinity term to match.

A list of pod label keys used to select which pods should be considered for the affinity term. The values of these keys from the pod being scheduled are combined with the labelSelector to filter candidate pods; all specified keys are ANDed together.

A list of pod label keys. If any of these keys are present on the candidate pod with a value equal to the corresponding label value on the pod being scheduled, the affinity term is considered not matching. This is used to exclude pods from the affinity evaluation in addition to the labelSelector, typically for scenarios like excluding pods from the same release or rollout.
A label selector for namespaces, used to scope the pod affinity term to pods in matching namespaces. If omitted, only the pod's own namespace is considered.

A list of label selector requirements for namespace selection. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally values, used to match Kubernetes namespaces.
The label key that the selector expression matches. In this context, it refers to a label on a namespace, used to select namespaces for pod affinity rules.
The operator to use for the label selector expression. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

The values field is used in a label selector requirement. It holds the list of string values that the key must match when the operator is In or NotIn; it must be empty for Exists and DoesNotExist operators.

A map of key-value pairs that must be present in a namespace's labels for the namespace to be selected. This is used within the namespace selector of a pod affinity term to narrow down the set of namespaces whose pods are considered for affinity/anti-affinity.
Specifies the namespaces that this pod affinity/anti-affinity term applies to. If omitted, it defaults to the namespace of the pod where the affinity is defined.

The key of node labels that defines the topology domain for this pod affinity term. For example, 'kubernetes.io/hostname' groups nodes by host, or a custom label can define a different failure domain.

The weight associated with this preferred pod affinity term. Must be an integer between 1 and 100. Higher weights give the corresponding affinity term more influence when summing preferred scheduling preferences.
A label selector used to identify the set of pods that the affinity rule applies to. It matches pods based on their labels using matchLabels and matchExpressions (if defined).

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. Multiple requirements are logically ANDed together to select matching pods.
The label key that the selector matches against. The pod must have a label with this key and a value satisfying the operator for the affinity rule to apply.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values that the key must match when the operator is In or NotIn. For Exists and DoesNotExist operators, this list must be empty.

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.

A list of pod label keys to filter which pods are considered for the affinity match. The pod affinity term applies to pods that match the label selector and have the same values for these specified label keys, helping to maintain consistency when pod labels change.

A list of label keys. Pods with label values that equal the incoming pod's label values for any of these keys are excluded from the affinity match. This allows expressing 'not equal' constraints on specific labels.
Label selector to select the namespaces whose pods are considered for the pod affinity/anti-affinity rule. When omitted, only the pod's own namespace is evaluated.
A list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values.

The label key that the selector applies to. In a namespace selector match expression, this is the key of the label that must exist (or match according to the operator) on a namespace for the pod to be scheduled in that namespace.

The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. For In/NotIn, the values field must be provided; for Exists/DoesNotExist, values must be empty.
The list of values that correspond to the key in the match expression. Required when the operator is In or NotIn; must be empty for Exists or DoesNotExist.
A map of key-value pairs that must match labels on a namespace. A namespace must have all specified labels to satisfy this selector, and multiple requirements are ANDed together.
Specifies the namespaces to which the pod affinity/anti-affinity rule applies. If empty, the rule applies only to the namespace of the current pod.

The key to the node labels that define the topology domain, such as 'kubernetes.io/hostname' for node-level topology or 'failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone' for zone-level topology. This field is required for pod affinity/anti-affinity terms.
The pod affinity term defines the label selector and topology key used to identify a set of pods for anti-affinity. It specifies which pods to avoid scheduling together in the same topology domain.
A label selector that identifies the set of pods for which the affinity or anti-affinity term applies. It uses matchLabels and matchExpressions constraints to define the selection.
A list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed together; each requirement specifies a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values.
The label key that this match expression applies to. Pods must have this key in their labels for the selector to consider them as a match, subject to the operator and values.
Defines the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a match expression. Valid values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'.
A list of values that the key must match for 'In' or 'NotIn' operators. This field is ignored for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist' operators, where it must be empty.

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs that the pod's labels must match for the affinity term to apply. It selects pods that have all specified label keys and values, equivalent to a set of matchExpressions with operator In and a single value each, ANDed together.

A list of label keys used to select the pods for this affinity term. The values for these keys from the new pod are merged with the label selector to determine the existing pods to which the rule applies. Keys not present in the new pod's labels are ignored.

MismatchLabelKeys is a list of label keys that must not match between the incoming pod and existing pods for the affinity term to apply. If any key in this list exists on both the incoming pod and an existing pod with the same value, that existing pod is excluded from consideration.
A label selector to filter namespaces where the target pods are located. If empty, only the pod's own namespace is considered.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. The namespace selector matches namespaces that satisfy all listed requirements.
The label key that the selector applies to. This key must exist in the namespace's labels for the selector to match, and its value is compared against the 'values' field according to the 'operator'.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and a set of values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
Values for the namespace selector label expression. For operators 'In' or 'NotIn', this list must be non-empty; for 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty.

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.
A list of namespaces that the pod affinity term applies to. If empty or null, the term applies to the namespace of the pod where the affinity is defined.
The key of node labels that defines the topology domain used to match pods. For example, 'kubernetes.io/hostname' to spread pods across nodes, or a zone label for availability zones.
Weight associated with the corresponding pod anti-affinity term, ranging from 1 to 100, used to calculate the preferred scheduling score.

A label selector is a core Kubernetes query over labels on objects. In pod anti-affinity, this selector identifies the group of pods to which the anti-affinity rule applies, using matchLabels and matchExpressions.
List of label selector requirements. Each requirement is an object with key, operator, and values fields, used to match pod labels for pod anti-affinity.
The label key that the selector applies to. For example, if the expression is 'app in (frontend, backend)', the key is 'app'.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.
The list of label values that the match expression selects on. For the In and NotIn operators, at least one value is required; for Exists and DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.

matchLabels is a map of key-value pairs that must match the labels of the pods selected for this anti-affinity rule. Each key-value pair is a requirement: the pod must have that label key set to that value. Multiple requirements are ANDed together.

A list of label keys that should not match between this pod and candidate pods for this anti-affinity rule. If a candidate pod has a label with the same key and value as this pod for any of these keys, that candidate pod is excluded from consideration.

A label selector to identify the namespaces to which this pod anti-affinity rule applies. The rule will only consider pods in namespaces matching this selector. If not set, the rule applies to all namespaces (or the pod's own namespace when no namespaces are specified).
A list of label selector requirements for selecting namespaces. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and optional values, and all requirements are combined with a logical AND.

The label key that the namespace selector matches against. In this pod anti-affinity rule, the match expressions apply to labels on namespaces, and this key is the label key whose value is compared using the operator and values specified in the same expression.
In a namespace selector match expression, the operator defines how the label key is matched against the values. Allowed values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'.
The list of values that the label key must match when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'. Must be empty for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist' operators.
match_labels is a map of label keys and values that must be matched by the namespaces considered for the pod anti-affinity rule. Only namespaces with all specified labels are selected.
A list of namespaces to which this pod affinity/anti-affinity term applies. If empty, it defaults to the namespace of the pod where the rule is defined.

The key of node labels that defines the topology domain. For required anti-affinity, this field is required and must not be empty; pods will be scheduled to avoid multiple pods in the same topology domain as defined by this key.
Arguments to the entrypoint. The container image's CMD is used if this is not provided. Overrides the CMD directive in the image when both the command and args are specified.
The command to run in the container, specified as an array of strings. It overrides the image's default entrypoint. Equivalent to the Docker ENTRYPOINT directive.
List of environment variables to set in the container. Each entry defines a variable name and either a direct value or a source for the value (e.g., config map, secret, or field reference).
The name of the environment variable, as referenced in the container's environment configuration.
The value of the environment variable as a string.

valueFrom is an optional source for the environment variable's value. It can reference a ConfigMap key, Secret key, or a field of the pod (downward API). Only one source may be specified, and it cannot be used when value is also set.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to populate the value of the environment variable.
The key to select from the referenced ConfigMap. This is the name of the entry in the ConfigMap whose value will be used as the value for the environment variable.
The name of the ConfigMap to select from.

Indicates whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If true, the container starts even if the ConfigMap or key is missing. If false or unset, the container fails if the referenced ConfigMap or key does not exist.

Selects a field of the pod as the value for the environment variable. The supported fields include metadata.name, metadata.namespace, metadata.labels['<KEY>'], metadata.annotations['<KEY>'], spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.hostIP, status.podIP, and status.podIPs.
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath refers to. Typically 'v1'.
The path to the desired field of the Pod, relative to the Pod object, from which to select the value. Examples include 'status.podIP', 'metadata.name', and 'metadata.namespace'.

Specifies whether the key referenced by the file key ref is required to exist. If true, the container is created even when the key is absent; if false (default), the container fails to start when the key is missing.
The name of the volume that contains the file referenced by the file key. This volume must be defined in the same pod spec.
Selects a container resource field (for example, limits.cpu or requests.memory) to expose as an environment variable value.
The name of the container to select the resource field from. If not specified, the pod's default container is used.
The divisor to divide the resource value by, specified as a Kubernetes quantity. For example, use '1' for CPU cores or '1m' for millicores. If unset, defaults to '1'.
The resource name to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. The value of the specified key is used as the environment variable's value.
The key name within the referenced Secret to select the value from.
The name of the Secret that contains the key. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Specify whether the referenced Secret key must be defined. If true, the container starts even if the key is missing; if false (default), the container fails to start when the key does not exist.
A list of sources to populate environment variables in the container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret, optionally with a prefix to prepend to variable names.

Refers to a Kubernetes ConfigMap. When specified, all key-value pairs from the referenced ConfigMap are imported as environment variables into the container. The object's 'name' field specifies the ConfigMap name, and 'optional' indicates whether the ConfigMap must exist.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference for environment variables.
Indicates whether the ConfigMap must be defined. If true, the ConfigMap may be absent, and the environment variables from it are ignored. Defaults to false, meaning the ConfigMap must exist.
Optional prefix that is prepended to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret to form the environment variable name.
secret_ref is a reference to a Kubernetes Secret from which all key-value pairs are exported as environment variables. It references the Secret by name in the same namespace.
Name of the Secret to read environment variables from.
Optional specifies whether the Secret must be defined. If true, the Secret may not exist and the container will still start; if false, the container will not start if the Secret is absent.
The container image to run, specified as a name with optional tag or digest (e.g., 'nginx:latest' or 'myregistry.example.com/foo@sha256:...').
Defines when the kubelet should pull the container image. Allowed values: Always, IfNotPresent, Never.

lifecycle defines lifecycle hooks for the container, such as postStart and preStop handlers, which allow executing commands at specific points in the container's lifecycle (e.g., right after container start or before container termination).
Specifies a lifecycle hook that runs after a container is successfully created and started. It can define an exec command or HTTP request to execute at that point.
The exec action executes a command inside the container during the postStart lifecycle hook. It contains a command field, which is an array of strings specifying the command and its arguments to run.

The command and arguments to execute when the postStart lifecycle hook is triggered. This is a list of strings where the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly inside the container without a shell, so shell features like pipes or variables require invoking a shell explicitly.

Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform after the container starts. This is part of the postStart lifecycle hook in Kubernetes, and the object defines the request details such as host, port, and path.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
A list of HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request sent by the postStart lifecycle hook. Each item defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the GET request.
The HTTP path to request on the server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port number on the container to access for the HTTP GET request. Can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol to use for the HTTP request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified.

Specifies a sleep action for the postStart lifecycle hook. The sleep action object contains a 'seconds' field that defines the duration of the sleep in seconds, delaying the completion of the postStart hook.
The duration in seconds that the container should sleep before continuing. This is used in the sleep action of a Kubernetes lifecycle hook.
tcp_socket specifies a TCP socket action to be performed during the container's postStart lifecycle hook. It defines the host and port to connect to.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP address.
The port number (as a string) to which the TCP socket connection is made during the postStart lifecycle hook. Must be a valid port number (1-65535).
pre_stop defines a hook that is executed immediately before a container is terminated. It can specify an exec command or an HTTP GET request to perform a task such as graceful shutdown.

Exec specifies the command to execute as a pre-stop lifecycle hook. It runs inside the container; the command is provided as a list of strings where the first element is the executable and the rest are arguments.

The command to run inside the container during the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This is given as an array of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. If omitted, the container's default command is used.
Configures an HTTP GET request that Kubernetes sends to the container's IP address when the container is being terminated as part of a pre-stop hook.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
A list of HTTP headers to send with the GET request. Each item contains a name and value for the header.
The name of the HTTP header to set in the HTTP request, e.g., 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header field that will be sent in the HTTP GET request during the pre-stop lifecycle hook.
Path to access on the HTTP server, for example /healthz. If empty, defaults to /.
The port number or named port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
Protocol to use for the HTTP GET request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
The URI scheme for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The `sleep` block configures a Sleep action for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It contains a single argument, `seconds`, which specifies the number of seconds to delay the container shutdown.
Specifies the sleep duration in seconds before the container is terminated, used in the preStop lifecycle hook to allow graceful shutdown.
Defines a TCP socket handler for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. The kubelet attempts to open a connection to the container's IP address on the specified port to trigger the hook.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to connect to for the preStop hook. Can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container's ports.
Defines a liveness probe for the container. If the probe fails, the kubelet kills the container and restarts it according to the pod's restart policy.
Exec specifies the action to take in the liveness probe. It defines a command to execute inside the container to check its health.

The command to run inside the container for the exec liveness probe, specified as a list of strings (command and arguments). The container is considered healthy if the command exits with status code 0; otherwise, the probe fails.
The number of consecutive failures required for the liveness probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1.

The gRPC action for the liveness probe. It allows the kubelet to check the health of a container using a gRPC service. The action specifies the port to connect to (required) and an optional service name; if omitted, the container's name is used as the default service.
The port number of the gRPC service to query for the liveness probe.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is empty.
Configures the liveness probe to issue an HTTP GET request to the container. The container is considered healthy if the response status code is between 200 and 399.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP probe. Defaults to the pod IP.
Custom headers to include in the HTTP GET request for the liveness probe. Each object in the list has 'name' and 'value' fields, specified as strings, which are sent as HTTP headers to the server.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the liveness probe HTTP request.
The value of the HTTP header to send with the probe request.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The TCP port to send the HTTP request to. Specify an integer port number or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS', with a default of 'HTTP'.
Scheme to use for connecting to the host. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the liveness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds, minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the liveness probe to be considered successful after a failure. For liveness probes, this value must be 1.
Defines a TCP socket probe for the liveness check, specifying the port to test for an open TCP connection.
The host name or IP address to connect to. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port to probe for liveness. This is the port on the container that the kubelet will attempt to connect to during the probe.
The duration in seconds Kubernetes waits for a pod to terminate gracefully before forcefully terminating it. This field is part of the pod specification, not the liveness probe.
The number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out and is considered failed. This timeout is part of the probe configuration for the container.
Name of the container, specified as a DNS_LABEL. Each container in a pod must have a unique name.
List of ports to expose from the container. Each port definition specifies the container port number and protocol, and may include additional attributes such as name or host port.
The port number that the container exposes. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The host IP address to bind the port to. If not set, the port binds to all host interfaces.
The host port number to map to the container port. If set, the container is accessible from outside the cluster via the host's IP address at this port. Must be a valid TCP port number (0-65535).
The name of the container port. Must be an IANA_SVC_NAME (unique identifier, up to 15 characters) and unique among ports in the same pod.
The protocol used for the container port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, or SCTP. Defaults to TCP.
Defines a probe that determines when the container is ready to accept traffic. If the probe fails, the pod is not added to service endpoints until it succeeds again.
Exec specifies the action to take in the readiness probe by running a command inside the container. The command to execute is defined in the 'command' field of this object.

The command to run inside the container for the exec probe. It is specified as a list of strings; the first element is the command and the rest are arguments. A zero exit code indicates success, any non-zero exit code indicates failure.
The number of consecutive failures of the readiness probe required before the container is marked not ready. Kubernetes will stop retrying after this many failures; default is 3 and minimum is 1.
grpc defines the gRPC health check parameters for this readiness probe. It contains the target port (required) and an optional service name to use in the gRPC request.
The port number to connect to for the gRPC health check. Must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is an empty string, which indicates the overall server health rather than a specific service.
Specifies the parameters for an HTTP GET request that the readiness probe performs to check container health.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request; defaults to the pod IP address.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request. Each item specifies a header with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to set in the request (e.g., X-Custom-Header). Must be a valid HTTP header field name.
The value of the HTTP header included in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request.
The HTTP request path to access on the HTTP server, such as "/healthz".
The port to access on the container for the HTTP readiness probe. Can be a numeric port or the name of a container port.
The protocol used for the HTTP GET request, such as HTTP or HTTPS.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container starts before the readiness probe is initiated. Must be a non-negative integer.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds; minimum value is 1.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For readiness probes, this defaults to 1 and can be set higher.

An optional TCP socket probe action. When set, the kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port to determine readiness. The port field is required; host is optional.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The TCP port number or named port to connect to during the readiness check. Provide a numeric port (e.g., 8080) or the name of a port defined in the container's ports list.
The number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.

A list of resource resize policies for the container. Each item specifies a resource (cpu or memory) and the restart policy (NotRequired or RestartContainer) that determines whether the container must be restarted when its resource limits are changed.
The name of the resource (e.g., 'cpu' or 'memory') that this container resize policy applies to.
Specifies the restart behavior for a container when its resource limits are adjusted in-place. Valid values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer'.
Specifies the compute resource requirements for the container, such as CPU and memory, including limits and requests.
The list of resource claims that this container requires. Each claim is an object containing a name that references a matching ResourceClaim in the same namespace.
Name must match the name of the ResourceClaim that this claim refers to.

The maximum amount of compute resources (e.g., CPU, memory) that the container can use. The key is the resource name (e.g., 'cpu', 'memory') and the value is a quantity string such as '500m' or '1Gi'.

Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if Limits are explicitly specified, otherwise to an implementation-defined value. The map keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory, ephemeral-storage) and values are quantities as strings (e.g., '100m', '1Gi').
Defines the container exit codes that trigger the restart behavior as per the restart policy rules.
The comparison operator used to evaluate container exit codes against configured values in the restart policy rule.
List of container exit codes that this restart policy rule applies to. The rule triggers when the container exits with any of these codes.
Security settings for the container, including user and group IDs, Linux capabilities, SELinux/AppArmor options, and read-only root filesystem configuration.
AllowPrivilegeEscalation controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. Defaults to true.
AppArmor profile configuration for the container. The type field can be 'Localhost' (referencing a local profile via localhostProfile), 'RuntimeDefault', or 'Unconfined'.
The name of an AppArmor profile that is pre-loaded on the node and applied to the container. This is used only when the AppArmor profile type is set to 'Localhost'.
The type of AppArmor profile to apply. Accepts 'Localhost', 'RuntimeDefault', or 'Unconfined'. When 'Localhost' is selected, the 'localhostProfile' field must also be set.
Capabilities configures Linux capabilities for the container. It allows adding or dropping capabilities via the 'add' and 'drop' lists.
Specifies a list of Linux capabilities to add to the container. For example, 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME'.
Specifies capabilities to drop from the container. Each entry is a Linux capability name (e.g., 'ALL', 'NET_ADMIN', 'SYS_TIME').
Indicates whether the container runs in privileged mode, granting it all capabilities and access to host devices as if it were root on the host. Defaults to false.
Specifies the proc mount type for the container. Allowed values are 'Default' (kernel-defined default) and 'Unmasked' (unmasks all /proc entries).
If true, mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only, preventing any writes to the root filesystem and enhancing security.
Specifies the group ID (GID) that the container's main process will run as. When not specified, the default GID from the container image is used.

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0, in which case the container will fail to start.
The user ID (UID) that the container's main process will run as. If unspecified, the default is the user defined in the container image.
The SELinux options for the container's security context, defining the SELinux label (user, role, type, level) applied to the container.
The SELinux level, representing the sensitivity or MLS/MCS category, applied to the container. For example, 's0:c123,c456'.
The SELinux role label applied to the container's security context.
The SELinux type label to apply to the container, such as container_t.
The SELinux user label that applies to the container.

SeccompProfile defines the seccomp profile to apply to the container. The type field must be one of Unconfined, RuntimeDefault, or Localhost; if type is Localhost, localhost_profile specifies the path to the profile on the node.
The path to the seccomp profile on the node, used when the seccomp type is 'Localhost'. The profile must be pre-configured on the node.
The type of seccomp profile to apply to the container.
Windows-specific security context options, such as GMSA credential spec, runAsUserName, and hostProcess settings for containers running on Windows.

The GMSA credential spec as a string, containing the JSON-formatted Group Managed Service Account specification for Windows containers. This is used to configure the container to run with a specific GMSA identity.
The name of a GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container's security context.
When true, runs the container as a Windows HostProcess container, which grants it access to the host's process and network namespaces.
The username to run the container's main process as, used for Windows containers. This is part of the Windows security context options.

startup_probe defines a probe that indicates whether the application within the container is started. It supports exec, HTTP GET, and TCP socket checks, and if the probe fails, the container is restarted according to its restart policy.
Exec specifies the action to take, which is to execute a command inside the container. The command's exit code determines the probe result (0 is success).
The command to run in the container for the startup probe's exec action. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.
Specifies the number of consecutive failures allowed before the startup probe is considered failed. The default is 3; the minimum value is 1.
grpc specifies a gRPC-based health check for the startup probe. It configures a gRPC connection to the container, typically requiring a port and optionally a service name.
The port number of the gRPC service to check. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health checking protocol.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform for the startup probe. The request targets the container's IP address and includes configurable host, port, path, and HTTP headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
List of custom HTTP headers to attach to the probe request. Each item defines a header name and value to send with the GET request.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request, e.g., X-Custom-Header.
The value of the HTTP header. This is the value associated with the header name in the startup probe's HTTP GET request.
The HTTP path to request on the server. Defaults to '/'.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container during the HTTP GET probe. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535, or the name of a container port.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS; defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Defaults to 0 if unspecified.
How often (in seconds) to perform the startup probe. Defaults to 10, and the minimum allowed value is 1.

The number of consecutive successful probe checks required for the startup probe to be considered successful. For startup probes, Kubernetes requires this value to be exactly 1, as a startup probe must succeed on the first check after failure.
The TCP socket check for this startup probe. If the specified port is accepting connections, the probe is considered successful.
Optional host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket health check. If not set, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to for the startup probe. Can be a numeric port (specified as a string) or a named port defined in the container.
The number of seconds the pod is allowed to terminate gracefully before being forcefully killed. Must be a non-negative integer; defaults to 30 seconds.
Number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. If the probe does not finish within this period, it is considered failed.
Indicates whether the container runtime should allocate a stdin stream for the container. If set to true, the container can read from standard input.

If true, the container's standard input is opened on container start, remains empty until the first client attaches, then stays open until the client disconnects, at which point it is closed and remains closed until the container restarts. This field only has effect when stdin is also true.
The path where the container's termination message is written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

termination_message_policy sets how the container's termination message is read by kubelet. Valid values are 'File' (default), which reads the message from the file specified by terminationMessagePath, and 'FallbackToLogsOnError', which falls back to the container logs if the message file is empty.
Indicates whether the container should allocate a pseudo-TTY. Set to true to enable interactive terminal access to the container.
List of volume devices to expose to the container, allowing raw block device access. Each entry specifies a device path and the name of a volume with the 'block' volume mode.
Path within the container where the volume device is mounted.
The name of the volume that this block device mounts, corresponding to a volume defined in the pod's volumes list.
List of volumes to mount into the container's filesystem. Each item specifies a volume name, a mount path within the container, and optionally read-only access and sub-path.
The path inside the container at which the volume will be mounted. This is where the volume's data appears in the container's filesystem.
Controls whether and how mounts are propagated between the host and the container. Allowed values: None, HostToContainer, Bidirectional.
Name of the volume to mount. Must correspond to the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
If true, the volume mount is read-only. If false (default), the volume is mounted read-write.

Sets the recursive read-only mode for the volume mount. Allowed values are 'Enabled' (mount is read-only recursively), 'Disabled' (mount is not read-only recursively), and 'IfInherited' (inherits the recursive read-only setting from the parent mount).
Path within the volume from which the container's volume mount is mounted.

subPathExpr is similar to subPath, but supports environment variable references using $(VAR_NAME) syntax. It allows dynamically selecting a path within the volume based on container environment variables.
The container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime default is used. Must be an absolute path.
The name of the DNS resolver option, such as 'ndots', 'timeout', 'attempts', or other valid resolv.conf options.
The value for the DNS resolver option specified in the name field. This is optional; some options may not require a value.
List of arguments to pass to the container's entrypoint. These override the default arguments provided in the container image.
The command to run in this ephemeral container, overriding the container image's entrypoint. If not provided, the image's default entrypoint is used.
List of environment variables to set in the ephemeral container. Each item defines a variable name and optionally its value or value source (e.g., secret or config map reference).
The name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier (e.g., starts with a letter or underscore, followed by alphanumeric characters or underscores).
Value of the environment variable. This field is optional if 'valueFrom' is specified.
Specifies an optional source for the environment variable's value, such as a ConfigMap, Secret, field reference, or resource field reference. Only one of value or valueFrom may be specified.
Selects a key of a ConfigMap in the pod's namespace.
The key of the ConfigMap entry to select.
Name of the ConfigMap being referenced.
Specifies whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If set to true, a missing ConfigMap or key does not prevent container startup; the value is treated as unset.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, status.podIP) and injects its value into the environment variable.
The API version of the schema that fieldPath is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1' if not specified.
The path of the field to select. For example, metadata.name or metadata.namespace.
Optional specifies whether the referenced key must exist. If true, a missing key is allowed and the environment variable is omitted; if false, the key must exist or the pod will not start.
The name of the volume containing the file from which the environment variable value is read.
Selects a resource field (e.g., limits.cpu, requests.memory) from the container's resource specification to expose as an environment variable.
The name of the container to select the resource field from. If omitted, the pod's default container is used.
Divisor for the resource field value. The resource value is divided by this quantity, which must be a valid Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1', '100m'); defaults to 1.
The name of the resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
Selects a key from a Kubernetes Secret to populate the environment variable's value. The Secret must exist in the same namespace unless the optional flag is set to true.
The key of the secret to select from. Must be a valid key in the referenced Secret.
The name of the Secret from which the key is selected.

Specifies whether the Secret or its key must be defined. When set to true, the reference is optional and the container can start even if the Secret or key is missing; the environment variable is omitted. When false (default), the referenced Secret must exist.
env_from specifies a list of sources (ConfigMap or Secret) whose key-value pairs are injected as environment variables into the ephemeral container.
Reference to a ConfigMap that populates environment variables in the container. The referenced ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference. This ConfigMap's data is used to populate environment variables for the container.
Indicates whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If true, a missing ConfigMap is ignored; if false, the container fails to start when the ConfigMap is absent.

An optional prefix that is prepended to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret when converting it to environment variable names. Keys are uppercased and invalid characters are replaced with underscores before the prefix is applied.
secretRef is a reference to a Secret in the same namespace as the Pod. The data of the referenced Secret is exposed as environment variables via envFrom.
Name of the Secret to use. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Specifies whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If set to true, the Secret is optional and its absence will not prevent the container from starting.
The container image to use for the ephemeral container.
The image pull policy for the ephemeral container. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never. Defaults to Always if the image tag is 'latest', otherwise IfNotPresent.
Lifecycle defines lifecycle hooks for the ephemeral container, including postStart and preStop handlers that execute at container startup and shutdown, respectively.
post_start is a lifecycle hook that runs immediately after the ephemeral container is started. It defines a handler (exec, httpGet, or tcpSocket) to perform actions at container start.
The exec-based lifecycle handler, which defines a command to run inside the ephemeral container after it starts, as part of the post-start hook.
The command to run inside the container for the post-start lifecycle exec hook, specified as a list of strings where the first element is the command and the remaining elements are arguments.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform on the container's lifecycle post-start hook. The hook is considered successful if the request returns an HTTP status code between 200 and 399.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Specifies custom HTTP headers to send with the GET request. Each header object contains 'name' and 'value' fields.
The HTTP header field name, e.g., 'Authorization' or 'Content-Type'.
The value of the HTTP header for the postStart lifecycle hook's HTTP GET request.
The path to access on the HTTP server for the HTTP GET request in the post-start lifecycle hook.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. It can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
Specifies the protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to HTTP.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.

Specifies a sleep action to be executed as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. The sleep action pauses execution for a set number of seconds, allowing the container to delay subsequent hook completion.
The number of seconds to sleep as part of the postStart lifecycle hook's sleep action.
Specifies a TCP socket action to be performed as part of the post-start lifecycle hook. This includes checking that a TCP socket is listening on the given port (with optional host).
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
Specifies the port number to connect to on the container for the TCP socket. Can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The pre_stop block configures the preStop lifecycle hook, which is invoked immediately before a container is terminated, allowing for graceful shutdown or cleanup operations.

Exec specifies the command to be run inside the container as the preStop lifecycle hook handler. It represents the ExecAction, which executes a command to perform cleanup or graceful shutdown before the container is terminated.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, specified as an array of strings. The first element is the command, and remaining elements are arguments. If omitted, the container's default command is used.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the pre-stop lifecycle action. The action succeeds if the request returns a 2xx status code.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header should specify a header name and value.
Specifies the name of an HTTP header to include in the preStop HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'. For example, '/healthz'.
Port number or name to access for the HTTP GET request. Can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol (scheme) used for the HTTP GET request, such as HTTP or HTTPS.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Specifies a sleep action for the pre-stop hook, which delays the container's termination by a specified number of seconds to allow graceful shutdown.
The number of seconds the container sleeps before termination, used by the sleep action in the preStop lifecycle hook.
Represents a TCP socket action, defined by a port and optional host, that Kubernetes performs when the pre-stop lifecycle hook is triggered.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to. Accepts a port number (1-65535) or a named port (IANA_SVC_NAME).
Defines the liveness probe for the ephemeral container. Note: Kubernetes ignores liveness probes for ephemeral containers, as they are not restarted by the kubelet.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container for the liveness probe. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0, and fails on any non-zero exit code.
Command to execute inside the container for the liveness probe. The first element is the command, and any remaining elements are arguments passed to it.
Minimum consecutive failures for the liveness probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.
Specifies the gRPC probe configuration for the liveness probe. This probe performs a gRPC health check on the container, requiring a port and optionally a service name.
The port number to send the gRPC health check request to. Must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the gRPC service to check. If not specified, the default is an empty string, which means the gRPC server's default health check is used.
The HTTP GET action to perform for the liveness probe. It configures a request to a specific port and path to determine container liveness.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP GET request for the liveness probe. Each header object contains a name and a value.
The header field name for the HTTP header sent in the liveness probe's HTTP GET request. For example, 'Accept' or 'Authorization'.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent in the liveness probe request.
The HTTP path to request on the server for the liveness probe. Defaults to '/'.
The port to access on the container. This is a string that can be an integer port number or the name of a port defined in the container's ports. Valid port numbers range from 1 to 65535.
Protocol for the HTTP request. Must be either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Must be a non-negative integer (default 0).
The frequency in seconds at which the liveness probe is performed. A higher value means less frequent checks.
Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For liveness probes, this value must be 1.
Specifies a TCP socket probe action, which checks the container's health by attempting to open a TCP connection to the port defined in the `port` field of this object.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket liveness probe. If not specified, it defaults to the pod IP.

The TCP port number to connect to when performing the liveness probe. This can be a numeric port (e.g., '8080') or a named port defined in the container's ports, and must be in the range 1-65535 if numeric.
The duration in seconds the container is allowed to terminate gracefully after a probe failure before being forcefully stopped. If set, this value overrides the pod-level termination grace period.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.
The name of the ephemeral container. Must be unique within the pod.
List of ports to expose from the container. For ephemeral containers, this field is not allowed and specifying it will be rejected by the API server.
The port number that the container listens on, used to expose the container's service.
The host IP address to bind the port to. Defaults to 0.0.0.0 if not specified.

The port number on the host node that maps to the container port for this ephemeral container. If specified, the container's port is exposed directly on the host's network at this port. Valid range is 1-65535.

The optional name of the container port. Must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME (up to 15 characters, lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen). This name can be used to reference the port in other Kubernetes resources, such as services.
The network protocol for this port. Supported values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP; defaults to TCP.

Defines a readiness probe for the ephemeral container. This probe determines when the container is ready to accept traffic and includes settings such as initial delay, period, timeout, and failure thresholds.
Exec specifies the command to run inside the container for the readiness probe. A successful probe (exit code 0) indicates the container is ready.

The command to run inside the container for the exec readiness probe. It is a list of strings representing the command and its arguments, executed directly without a shell unless the first element is '/bin/sh' or similar. The working directory is root ('/') in the container's filesystem, and the command runs as the container's default user (subject to securityContext overrides).
The number of consecutive failures of the readiness probe before the container is considered not ready. Once the probe fails this many times, the container is removed from service endpoints.
Specifies the gRPC action for the probe, configuring a gRPC health check against the container. It includes parameters such as the port to query (required) and an optional service name.
The port number of the gRPC server to connect to. Required when using a gRPC probe.
Specifies the name of the gRPC service to query for health status. If empty, the health check applies to the entire gRPC server.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to check container readiness. Includes settings such as the path, port, HTTP headers, and scheme.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Optional list of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
Name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request, e.g., 'Authorization'.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the readiness probe request. This is paired with the corresponding header name in the httpHeaders list.
The HTTP path to request when performing the readiness probe. For example, '/healthz'.
The port number or name of the port on the container to connect to for the HTTP GET request. This accepts a numeric value as a string or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol (scheme) used for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds; the minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1. For readiness probes, this value must be 1.
Specifies a TCP socket check for the readiness probe. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port to determine if the container is ready.
Optional host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP socket port to probe on the container. It can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container's ports.
Optional number of seconds the pod will wait after receiving a termination signal before it is forcefully terminated. Defaults to 30 seconds if not specified.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.
List of resource resize policies for the ephemeral container, defining which resources (CPU, memory) can be resized and the restart behavior if a resize fails.
The name of the resource (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies, as part of the Kubernetes ephemeral container resize policy.
Specifies the restart policy when a container's resource is resized. Allowed values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer'.
Resource requirements for the ephemeral container, defining requests and limits for compute resources such as CPU and memory.

Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this ephemeral container. This is an alpha field and requires enabling the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate.
The name of the ResourceClaim this container references. The ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

Limits specifies the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the ephemeral container. Each key is a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the corresponding value is a quantity string (e.g., '100m', '1Gi').

Requests is a map of resource names to quantities, specifying the minimum amount of each resource the ephemeral container needs. For example, 'cpu: 100m' and 'memory: 128Mi'. The keys are standard Kubernetes resource names (cpu, memory, hugepages, etc.) and the values are strings in Kubernetes quantity format.
Specifies the restart policy for the ephemeral container. Allowed values are Always, OnFailure, and Never. Defaults to Always if not set.
Specifies the container exit code(s) that this restart policy rule matches. When the ephemeral container exits with one of these codes, the restart action defined in the rule is triggered.
A list of integer exit codes that define which container terminations this restart policy rule applies to. If a container exits with one of these codes, the restart policy rule is followed.

SecurityContext holds security configuration for the ephemeral container, including parameters like runAsUser, runAsGroup, capabilities, SELinux options, and whether the root filesystem is read-only. It controls the container's access to the host and privileges at runtime.

AllowPrivilegeEscalation controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, the container's processes are prevented from gaining additional privileges (e.g., via setuid or setgid binaries).
Configures AppArmor for the container. Defines the profile type (RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and optionally references a profile on the node.
The name of the AppArmor profile to be loaded from the node's localhost, used only when the profile type is 'Localhost'.

Type of AppArmor profile to use. Allowed values are 'Localhost' (use the profile specified in localhostProfile), 'RuntimeDefault' (use the container runtime's default AppArmor profile), and 'Unconfined' (disable AppArmor enforcement).
Capabilities to add or drop for the ephemeral container's process. The object contains 'add' and 'drop' lists of Linux capabilities.
The list of Linux capabilities to add to the container's security context. Valid entries are Linux capability names like CAP_NET_ADMIN or CAP_SYS_TIME.
The list of capabilities to drop from the container's permitted capabilities. For example, can drop 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME'.
Specifies whether the container runs in privileged mode. When true, the container has access to all devices on the host and essentially runs as root on the host.

Sets the proc mount type for the ephemeral container. Allowed values are 'Default' and 'Unmasked'; 'Unmasked' removes the masking of /proc to expose all host proc information, while 'Default' applies the standard restrictions.
Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only. When set to true, the root filesystem cannot be modified, enhancing security by preventing unauthorized changes to container filesystem content.
The GID (group ID) to run the container's entrypoint process with. If omitted, defaults to the container image's group ID.

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. If true, the kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and will fail to start the container if it does.
The UID (user ID) that the container's entrypoint process will run as. Defaults to the user specified in the container image if not set. Must be a non-negative integer.
SELinux options for the ephemeral container, specifying the level, role, type, and user as part of its security context.
Level is the SELinux level label that applies to the container. For example, s0:c123,c456.
The SELinux role label that applies to the container. It defines the role portion of the SELinux context, such as 'system_r'.
The SELinux type label that applies to the container. This specifies the SELinux type, such as 'container_t'.
The SELinux user label for the container.
SeccompProfile configures the seccomp profile for this ephemeral container. It can specify a runtime default, unconfined, or a localhost profile via its type and localhostProfile fields.

localhostProfile indicates a profile defined in a file on the node should be used. The profile must be preconfigured on the node to work. Must be a descending path, relative to the kubelet's configured seccomp profile location. Must only be set if type is 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to use. Allowed values are RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, and Localhost.
Windows-specific security options for the container. Configures settings such as GMSA credentials, host process, and the Windows user name.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the container, enabling Windows GMSA authentication.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container, as defined in the Kubernetes Windows security context options.
HostProcess determines if a container should be run as a HostProcess container. All containers in the pod must have the same value, and the default is false.
The username in Windows to run the entrypoint of the container process. Defaults to the user specified in image metadata if unspecified.

Configures a startup probe for the ephemeral container. This probe determines when the container has started successfully; until it succeeds, liveness and readiness probes are not activated, and if it fails, the container is restarted according to its restart policy. Useful for slow-starting containers.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container for the startup probe. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with status 0; any other exit code indicates a failure.

Command line to execute inside the container for the startup probe. The working directory is '/' in the container's filesystem. The command is executed directly, not via a shell, so shell constructs like pipes are not supported.
Minimum consecutive failures for the startup probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1.
grpc specifies a gRPC health check to perform against the container. It is an object containing the port to check and, optionally, the service name.
The port number on which the gRPC server is listening. Must be a valid TCP port (1-65535). This field is required for a gRPC probe.
Specifies the name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by gRPC.
Configures an HTTP GET request that the startup probe performs against the container. This is an object containing the host, port, path, and optional HTTP headers for the request.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
List of custom HTTP headers to send with the probe request. Each item specifies a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP request.
The value of the HTTP header. This string is sent as the header's value when the probe performs the HTTP request.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server when performing a GET request. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port to send the HTTP request to. Accepts either a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Must be HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP if not specified.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP, and valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.
The number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Defaults to 0; minimum value is 0.
How often, in seconds, to perform the startup probe. Minimum value is 1; default is 10.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1 and must be 1 for startup probes.
Configures a TCP socket checker for the startup probe. It defines the port (and optionally host) to check for TCP connectivity, indicating the container has started.
Host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. The number must be in the range 1 to 65535, or a name must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME.
The grace period in seconds that Kubernetes allows a pod to run after receiving a termination signal before forcefully killing it. Defaults to 30 seconds if not specified.
The number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.
Whether this ephemeral container should have a stdin stream allocated for it. When true, the container runtime allocates a stdin channel, enabling interactive access. Defaults to false.

If true, the container runtime closes the stdin channel after the first attach session disconnects, and stdin remains closed until the container is restarted. When false, stdin remains open across multiple attach sessions if stdin is enabled. Defaults to false.
The name of the target container within the pod that this ephemeral container shares its process namespace with. If not specified, the last started container is used.
Path at which the container's termination message is written, used to record the reason for container termination. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.
Provides the policy for how the termination message of the ephemeral container is captured—either from the termination message file or through container logs under error conditions.
Indicates whether a TTY (pseudo-TTY) should be allocated for the ephemeral container. When true, the container will have a terminal attached, enabling interactive sessions.
List of block devices to be used by the ephemeral container. Each item defines the name of a volume and the device path inside the container.
The path inside the container where the volume device is mounted. This is required when specifying a volume device for an ephemeral container.
The name of the volume to use. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
List of volume mounts for an ephemeral container. Each item specifies a volume to mount into the container's filesystem, including mount path and read-only options.
Path within the ephemeral container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path, e.g., /data.

mount_propagation controls how volume mounts are propagated from the host to the container and between containers. Valid values are None (default), HostToContainer, and Bidirectional. It affects the visibility of mounts in the container.
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
Specifies whether the volume is mounted as read-only. When true, the container can only read from the volume; default is false (read-write).
Configures recursive read-only mounts for this volume mount. Allowed values: Enabled, IfPossible, Disabled.
Path within the volume from which the container's volume is mounted. Defaults to the volume's root if empty.
Specifies the path within the volume to mount, with support for environment variable expansion using $(VAR_NAME) syntax, similar to subPath but allowing dynamic paths.
The working directory for the ephemeral container. If not specified, the container runtime uses the default working directory defined in the container image.
The list of hostnames that resolve to the IP address specified in this hostAliases entry. Kubernetes adds these hostnames to the /etc/hosts file of the container.
The IP address to which the hostnames in this hostAliases entry should resolve.
The name of the image pull secret. Must correspond to a Secret in the same namespace as the pod.
Arguments to the command that this init container runs. These are passed to the container's entrypoint process.
The entrypoint array for the init container, overriding the image's ENTRYPOINT. This is a list of strings, e.g., ['/bin/sh', '-c'].
List of environment variables to set in the container. Each item defines a variable name and optionally a value or a source for the value (e.g., config map, secret, or field reference).
The name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier (e.g., MY_VAR).
The value to set for the environment variable.

Specifies a source for the environment variable's value. It allows referencing a ConfigMap key, Secret key, a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name), or a resource (e.g., limits.cpu). Only one of configMapKeyRef, secretKeyRef, fieldRef, or resourceFieldRef can be set.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to populate the value of the environment variable. The object contains the ConfigMap name and the key to retrieve.
The key to select from the referenced ConfigMap.
The name of the ConfigMap being referenced. Must match a ConfigMap name in the same namespace.
Optional specifies whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. Defaults to false, meaning the key must exist.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, status.podIP, spec.nodeName) to use as the value of the environment variable. The specific field path is provided in the nested fieldPath property.
Version of the schema the FieldPath is written in terms of, defaults to 'v1'.
Path of the field to select from the pod spec, such as 'metadata.name' or 'spec.nodeName'.
Indicates whether the referenced file key is optional. If true, the container can start even when the key does not exist; if false, the key must be present.

The path to the file that contains the key to be used as the value for the environment variable. This is part of a file-based key reference, where the file is read to extract the value at the specified key.
The name of the volume that contains the file referenced by the file key reference. This volume must be defined in the same pod's volume list.
ResourceFieldRef selects a resource field of the container, such as limits.cpu or requests.memory, for use as the value of the environment variable.
The name of the container for which to select a resource. If omitted, defaults to the container where this environment variable is defined.

Divisor is the divisor for the resource value in a resource field reference. It specifies the scaling factor applied to the selected resource quantity (e.g., '1' yields the raw value, '1k' divides by 1000, '1Mi' divides by 1,048,576). Defaults to '1'.

The resource name to select from the pod's resource specification, such as 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory'. This is used in a resource field ref to populate the environment variable's value from a container resource.

Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. This is a SecretKeySelector object that specifies the Secret name and key to use, and may include an 'optional' flag to control behavior when the Secret or key is missing.
The key name within the referenced Secret to retrieve the value from. Must be a valid secret key.
The name of the Secret to select from.

Specifies whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If true, and the secret or key is missing, the environment variable is omitted and the container can start; if false (default), a missing secret or key causes an error.
envFrom is a list of sources to populate environment variables in the container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret (or all keys), or use a prefix to prepend to variable names.
Reference to a ConfigMap from which to populate environment variables for this container. The ConfigMap is referenced by its name within the same namespace.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference. This ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must exist. If true, a missing ConfigMap is allowed; if false (default), the ConfigMap must exist or the pod will fail to start.
An optional identifier to prepend to each key of the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. Must be a valid C identifier.

Reference to a Kubernetes Secret in the same namespace, used to populate environment variables for the init container. The Secret's data keys become environment variable names and their values become the variable values.
The name of the Secret to populate environment variables from. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
Indicates whether the referenced Secret must be defined. When set to true, the Secret may be absent and the container will still start; when false or unset, the Secret must exist.
The container image to run for the init container.

Specifies when the kubelet should pull the container image for this init container. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never. Defaults to Always if the image tag is :latest, otherwise IfNotPresent.
Lifecycle configuration for the init container, specifying postStart and preStop hooks to execute at container start and shutdown.
post_start defines the postStart hook for the container lifecycle. This hook is executed immediately after the container is started and can be used to run initialization commands or checks.
Exec runs a command inside the container when the postStart lifecycle hook is triggered. The command is specified as a list of strings in the 'command' field.
The command to execute in the container for the postStart lifecycle hook. It is executed directly, not through a shell; the working directory is '/' in the container's filesystem.
Configures an HTTP GET request to be sent to the container as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. The request is sent to a specific endpoint on the container to trigger a post-start action.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request; defaults to the pod IP.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request to the postStart handler. Each header object requires a name and value string.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header field.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The TCP port number or named port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Specify the port number as a string, or use a named container port.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request.
The scheme to use for the connection, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.

Configures a sleep action for the postStart lifecycle hook, pausing container execution for a specified number of seconds before continuing. The nested 'seconds' field defines the duration of the sleep.
The number of seconds to sleep for the sleep lifecycle hook action.
Specifies a TCP socket to connect to as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. The handler attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified host and port.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
