The TCP port to connect to on the container. Accepts a numeric port or a named port defined in the container's ports.
preStop is a lifecycle hook that is called immediately before a container is terminated. It can be used to gracefully stop the container or perform cleanup actions.
Exec specifies the command to run in the container as part of the preStop lifecycle hook. It is an ExecAction object containing the command to execute.

The command to run in the container during the preStop lifecycle hook. It is an array of strings; the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly, not through a shell, and the working directory is root ('/') in the container's filesystem.
Represents an HTTP GET request to perform as the container's preStop lifecycle hook. This object defines the endpoint and headers for the request sent to the container before termination.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
List of HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each header object contains `name` and `value` fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request for this preStop lifecycle hook.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to `/`.
The TCP port to send the HTTP request to. This can be a numeric port number or a named port defined in the container's port list.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS; defaults to HTTP.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS, with HTTP as the default.
Represents a sleep action in the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It specifies a duration in seconds to wait before the container is terminated, allowing for graceful shutdown.
Specifies the number of seconds the container should sleep before it is terminated as part of the preStop hook.

Specifies a TCP socket action for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This action attempts to open a TCP connection to a specified host and port, and the hook is considered successful when the connection is established.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The TCP port number to connect to for the preStop lifecycle hook. Can be specified as a numeric port (e.g., "8080") or a named port defined in the container's ports.
Liveness probe configuration for the init container. In Kubernetes, liveness probes are not supported for init containers and this field is ignored.

Exec is the exec-based action for the liveness probe, specifying a command to run inside the container to determine its health status. The command is defined as a list of arguments, which are executed directly in the container.

The command to run inside the container for the exec probe. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the command path and the rest are arguments. The kubelet executes this command periodically to determine whether the container is healthy.
The number of consecutive failures of the liveness probe before the container is restarted. The minimum value is 1; if not specified, the default is 3.
Specifies a gRPC health check action for the liveness probe. It contains a required port number and an optional service name to check, as defined by Kubernetes' GRPCAction.
The port number of the gRPC service to check. This should be the port on which the gRPC server is listening for health checks.
The name of the gRPC service to check in the health check request. If omitted, the probe checks the overall health of the server.
Defines an HTTP GET request used by the kubelet to perform a liveness check on the container. It specifies the path, port, and optional HTTP headers for the request.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. Defaults to the pod IP.
Specifies custom HTTP headers to include in the request sent by the liveness probe. Each header is an object with `name` and `value` fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the liveness probe's HTTP GET request. For example, `X-Custom-Header`.
The value of the HTTP header. This is the actual string sent as the header's value; for example, for a header 'Authorization: Bearer token', the value is 'Bearer token'.
Path to access on the HTTP server for the probe request. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
Specifies the port to use for the HTTP GET request. Accepts a numeric port (1-65535) or the name of a container port.
Specifies the protocol used for the HTTP GET liveness probe, typically 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not set.
The scheme to use for the connection, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the liveness probe on the init container.
Minimum consecutive successes for the liveness probe to be considered successful after a failure. For liveness probes, this value must be 1.
Specifies the TCP socket action for the liveness probe. The probe will attempt to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port to determine if it is healthy.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.

The port number or named port on the container to probe for liveness. In a tcpSocket probe, it specifies the TCP port to connect to; can be a numeric port or a port name defined in the container's ports.
Number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out. Defaults to 1 second; minimum value is 1.
The name of the init container. Must be a valid DNS label and unique within the pod. Required.
List of ports exposed by the init container. Each port object specifies a name, container port number, protocol, and optionally host IP and host port.
The port number on which the container listens. In Kubernetes, the containerPort field specifies the network port that the container expects to receive traffic on, with a valid range of 1-65535.
The host IP address to bind the port to. Defaults to 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces).
The port on the host node to which the container port is mapped. If specified, this makes the container accessible from outside the node via the node's IP address.

Name of the port, used for referencing the port in the pod spec. Must be an IANA_SVC_NAME (up to 15 characters, lowercase alphanumeric, hyphens, and dots). Must be unique among all ports in the same container.
The network protocol used by the port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP. Defaults to TCP.

Readiness probe configuration for an init container. It defines a health check that determines when the init container is considered ready, though init containers typically run to completion and this probe is rarely used.
Exec specifies the action to take, which is to run a command inside the container. The exit status of the command is used to determine whether the probe succeeded (exit code 0 indicates success).

The command to execute inside the container for this exec readiness probe. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status code 0.
Number of consecutive failures of the readiness probe required before the container is considered not ready. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.
Specifies a gRPC probe action for this readiness check. It defines the port and optional service name used to perform a gRPC health check against the container.
Specifies the port number to use for the gRPC health check in the container's readiness probe. Must be a valid TCP port number (1-65535).
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, defaults to an empty string.
Performs an HTTP GET request against the container to check its readiness. A response with a status code in the 2xx or 3xx range indicates success.
The hostname to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. You can set this to override the Host header or connect to a specific host.
Optional list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each object specifies a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request.
The URL path (e.g., /healthz) that the HTTP probe requests from the container. An empty path results in a request to the server root.
The port number or name to use for the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or an IANA service name; defaults to the container's first allocated port if not specified.
The HTTP protocol (scheme) used for the request, such as 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. This is the initial delay, in seconds, before the first probe runs.
The interval in seconds between each readiness probe execution.

Minimum consecutive successes for the readiness probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1. For readiness probes, can be set higher to require multiple successful checks, but must be 1 for liveness and startup probes.

Configures a TCP socket check for the readiness probe. The probe attempts to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port, optionally using a specified host. The container is considered ready if the connection succeeds.
Host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port to check on the container. Can be a port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container spec.
Number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. If the probe does not complete within this duration, it is considered failed. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 1 second if not specified.

List of resource resize policies for the init container. Each policy specifies a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and a restart policy (NotRequired or RestartContainer) that determines whether the container must be restarted when the resource is resized.
The name of the resource (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies. Valid values are "cpu" and "memory".

The restart policy to apply when a container's resource resize is requested. Valid values are 'NotRequired' (no restart needed) and 'RestartContainer' (restart the container to apply the new resource requirements).
Resource requirements for the init container, including requests and limits for compute resources such as CPU and memory.
List of resource claims that can be referenced by the container. Each item contains a 'name' field that refers to a ResourceClaim object in the same namespace.
Name of the ResourceClaim resource that this container requests. The referenced ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the specific request in the ResourceClaim. If not set, the default request is used.
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the container. Each key is a resource name such as 'cpu' or 'memory', and the value is a quantity string (e.g., '500m', '1Gi').
Map of resource names to quantities, specifying the amount of compute resources requested for the init container (e.g., cpu, memory).
Specifies the restart policy for the init container. In Kubernetes, this field is only supported for sidecar init containers, and must be set to 'Always' if specified.
The comparison operator that determines how the specified exit codes are evaluated for the restart policy rule. Valid values include 'In' and 'NotIn'.
A list of numeric exit codes that this restart policy rule applies to.

SecurityContext defines the security configuration for the init container, including settings like runAsUser, capabilities, and SELinux options, controlling the access and privileges of the container process.

Controls whether the init container's processes can gain more privileges than their parent (e.g., via setuid/setgid binaries). When false, the container runs with no_new_privs, preventing privilege escalation.

The AppArmor profile to apply to the init container. The type must be 'Localhost', 'RuntimeDefault', or 'Unconfined'. If type is 'Localhost', the 'localhostProfile' field must be set to the name of the profile.
Specifies the name of an AppArmor profile that is pre-loaded on the node. This field is used only when the type is 'Localhost'.
Specifies the type of AppArmor profile to apply to the container. Valid values are: Localhost, RuntimeDefault, Unconfined.
Configures Linux capabilities for the container. Allows adding or dropping specific capabilities via the 'add' and 'drop' subfields.
Adds the specified Linux capabilities to the init container's capability set. Each entry is a capability name (e.g., 'CAP_NET_ADMIN') that will be granted in addition to the default capabilities.
List of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's default set. For example, 'ALL' or specific capability names like 'NET_RAW'.
Indicates whether the container runs in privileged mode. Processes in privileged containers are equivalent to root on the host.
Specifies the proc mount type for the container. Valid values are 'Default' (default behavior) and 'Unmasked' (allows viewing all processes).

Indicates whether the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the container cannot write to its root filesystem, which helps prevent modifying system files and improves security.
Specifies the group ID (GID) that the container's main process runs as. If omitted, the default group from the container image is used.
Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. If true, the kubelet will reject the container if it is configured to run as UID 0 (root).
The numerical user ID (UID) that the init container's process will run as. If not specified, the default user in the container image is used.
SELinux options for the container, which specify the SELinux labels (user, role, type, and level) applied to the container's processes.
SELinux level label applied to the container, such as s0 or s0:c1,c2.
SELinux role label for the container. This is part of the SELinux options applied to the init container's security context, used to enforce mandatory access control policies.
The SELinux type label for the container, such as 'spc_t' or 'svirt_lxc_net_t'. This is part of the SELinux security context (user:role:type:level).
The SELinux user label applied to the container process.

Configures the seccomp profile for the container. The profile type can be RuntimeDefault, Localhost, or Unconfined; if Localhost, the localhostProfile field specifies the path to the profile on the node.
Specifies the path to a seccomp profile on the node. This field is used only when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'.
The seccomp profile type. Valid values are RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, and Localhost.
Windows-specific security options for the container. These options are only applicable to containers running on Windows.
Specifies the Group Managed Service Account (GMSA) credential spec to use, provided as a JSON string. This allows the container to access resources with the specified GMSA identity.
The name of the GMSA (Group Managed Service Account) credential spec to use for the Windows container. This is part of the Windows security context options for the init container.
Whether the container should run as a HostProcess container. Defaults to false.
The username in Windows to run the container's entrypoint process. If unspecified, the container uses the default user.

The startup probe configuration for the init container. This object defines the probe that determines when the container has started successfully, using the same probe mechanisms (such as HTTP, TCP, or command execution) as other Kubernetes probes.
Exec specifies the action to perform: running a command inside the container. The command's exit status is used to determine probe success.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container. The exit status of the command is the probe result: 0 indicates success, non-zero indicates failure. The command is executed directly, not through a shell.
The number of consecutive failures of the startup probe that must occur before the container is considered failed and restarted. This value must be an integer.
Specifies a gRPC health check action for this startup probe, allowing the kubelet to verify container health via gRPC according to the gRPC Health Checking Protocol.
The port number on which the gRPC server is listening. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
Specifies the name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is the container name.
Specifies an HTTP GET request performed against the container for the startup probe. The probe is considered successful if the HTTP response code is between 200 and 399.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the startup probe's HTTP GET request. Each item defines a header with a `name` and a `value`.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the startup probe's HTTP request.
The value of the HTTP header that is sent in the startup probe's HTTP GET request. This pairs with the header name to form a key-value pair.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. For example, '/healthz'.
The port number or named port on the container that the HTTP GET request will be sent to. Must be a valid integer port number or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. If not specified, defaults to 0.
Number of seconds between startup probe attempts. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 10.
Number of consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. In Kubernetes, this value must be 1 for startup probes; it defaults to 1.

Specifies the TCP socket action for the startup probe. The probe attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's IP address on a specified port. If the connection succeeds, the probe is considered successful. Contains 'port' (required) and 'host' (optional) fields.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to probe, which can be a numeric port (e.g., 8080) or a named port defined in the container's port list.

The duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully upon deletion. This value may be decreased in delete requests, and defaults to 30 seconds if not specified. It applies to all containers in the pod, including init containers.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.
Indicates whether the container runtime should keep the container's standard input (stdin) open. This allows a process to read from stdin, typically for interactive sessions.

Whether the container runtime should close the stdin channel after it has been opened by a single attach. If true, stdin is opened on container start, remains open until the first client disconnects, and then stays closed until the container restarts. Defaults to false.
Path to a file where the container's termination message is written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Specifies how the termination message is derived. Supported values: 'File' (default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'. When set to 'FallbackToLogsOnError', the termination message is read from the container's log if the message file is empty.
Indicates whether a TTY (teletypewriter) should be allocated to the container, enabling interactive terminal access.

The list of block device volume mounts for the init container. Each item maps a volume name to a device path at which the raw block device is exposed inside the container. Typically used when a volume's volumeMode is 'Block'.
The path inside the container where the block device is mounted, such as /dev/xvda. This is the device path that the container will use to access the volume.
The name of the volume that this device refers to. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
List of volumes to mount into the init container's filesystem. Each volume mount references a volume defined in the pod spec and specifies the mount path.
List of mount options for a bind mount, such as 'ro' (read-only), 'rw' (read-write), 'nosuid', 'nodev', etc. These options control the behavior of the mounted filesystem.
The path inside the container at which the volume should be mounted. This is a required field for each volume mount.
Defines how mount propagation is set for this volume mount. Allowed values are 'None', 'HostToContainer', and 'Bidirectional'. If not specified, 'None' is used.
The name of the volume to mount into the init container. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes.
Specifies whether the volume mount is read-only. When set to true, the container can only read from the mounted volume.
Specifies whether the volume mount is recursive read-only. When enabled, the mount and all of its subpaths are read-only. This corresponds to the Kubernetes `recursiveReadOnly` field.
Specifies a sub-path inside the volume to mount instead of the volume's root. The sub-path must already exist before the container starts, and it is relative to the volume's root directory.
Specifies a sub-path inside the volume to mount, with support for environment variable references using $(VAR_NAME) syntax. This is similar to subPath but expands environment variables at runtime.
Container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime's default is used, which might be configured in the container image. Must be an absolute path.
The condition type that must be satisfied for the pod to be considered ready. This corresponds to a condition in the pod's status.
The name of this resource claim, used to reference the claim from container resource claims (e.g., in `resources.claims`).
The name of the ResourceClaim referenced in the pod. This name must be unique within the pod and is used by containers to bind to the claimed resource via their resource claim references.
The name of a ResourceClaimTemplate that provides the resource claim for this pod. The template is used to dynamically create a ResourceClaim.
The name of the ResourceClaim resource (in the same namespace) that this container requests.
The name of the scheduling gate. The pod will not be scheduled until a matching condition with this name is removed from the pod.
The sysctl parameter name to set, e.g. kernel.shm_rmid_forced.
The value to assign to the sysctl parameter. This is a string, but many sysctls expect numeric-like values (e.g., "0" or "1") depending on the specific parameter.
The effect of the taint that this toleration matches. Allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, and NoExecute. An empty string matches all effects.
The key of the taint that this toleration applies to. If the operator is 'Exists', the key can be empty.
The operator to apply to the key and value. Valid values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. If 'Exists', the toleration matches if the taint key matches; if 'Equal', the value must also match.
The number of seconds a pod tolerates a taint before it is evicted when the toleration effect is NoExecute. If unset, the toleration persists indefinitely.
The taint value that the toleration matches. This is required when the operator is 'Equal' and should be empty when the operator is 'Exists'.
LabelSelector is used to find matching pods to which this topology spread constraint applies. If not set, the constraint applies to all pods in the namespace.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values, enabling complex label selection for the topology spread constraint's label selector.
The label key that the match expression applies to, used to select resources based on their labels.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.

values is a list of string values. When the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn', this list specifies the values the label key must (or must not) match; for 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty (and is typically omitted).
A map of key-value pairs that must match the pod's labels for the pod to be selected by this topology spread constraint. Equivalent to matchLabels in a Kubernetes LabelSelector.
A list of label keys that specifiy which pods to consider for spreading. Pods having any of these label keys (regardless of value) are included in the topology spread calculation.
The maximum difference in the number of matching Pods between the topology domain with the most Pods and the domain with the fewest. Must be greater than zero.
The minimum number of topology domains that must exist for pod spreading to be applied. If specified, the cluster must have at least this many domains; otherwise, pods are not scheduled.

Indicates how to treat node affinity when calculating pod topology spread skew. Allowed values are 'Honor' (default) and 'Ignore'. With 'Honor', only nodes matching the pod's node affinity are considered; with 'Ignore', node affinity is ignored.
Specifies how to treat nodes with taints when calculating pod topology spread skew. Allowed values are 'Honor' and 'Ignore' (default is 'Ignore').
The key of node labels. Nodes that have a label with this key and identical values are considered to be in the same topology domain.

Indicates how to handle a pod when the topology spread constraint is not satisfied. Allowed values are 'DoNotSchedule' (default) and 'ScheduleAnyway'. 'DoNotSchedule' prevents the pod from being scheduled, while 'ScheduleAnyway' allows scheduling while still attempting to honor the constraint as much as possible.
Defines an AWS Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume as a source for a Kubernetes volume. This field provides the configuration to attach an EBS volume to the pod.
Filesystem type to mount on the AWS EBS volume, e.g., 'ext4', 'xfs', or 'ntfs'. Must be supported by the host operating system.
The partition number of the AWS EBS volume to mount. If the volume is partitioned, specify the partition number (e.g., 1 for /dev/sdb1).
Specifies whether the AWS EBS volume is mounted as read-only. If true, the volume is mounted read-only; otherwise it can be read-write.
The unique identifier of the AWS EBS volume to be mounted, typically in the form 'vol-xxxxxxxx'.
Represents an Azure Disk volume source, enabling a pod to mount a Microsoft Azure managed disk as a volume for persistent storage.
CachingMode specifies the caching policy for the Azure disk. Allowed values are None, ReadOnly, and ReadWrite; if not set, the default is None.
The name of the Azure data disk to mount. This must be the name of a disk in the same resource group as the cluster.
The URI of the virtual hard disk (VHD) for unmanaged disks, or the resource ID for managed disks, that the volume should mount. This identifies the Azure disk to attach.
Filesystem type to use when mounting the Azure Disk volume. Defaults to 'ext4' if not specified.
Kind of the Azure disk: Shared (multiple blob disks per storage account), Dedicated (single blob disk per storage account), or Managed (managed disk). Defaults to Shared.
Whether the Azure disk volume is mounted as read-only. If set to true, the volume is mounted with read-only access; otherwise, it is mounted with read-write access.
azureFile represents an Azure File volume source that can be mounted as a volume in a pod, using an Azure Files share.
If set to true, the Azure file share is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that stores the Azure Storage account name and key used to access the Azure file share.
The name of the Azure File share to mount. This must match an existing share in the Azure storage account.
Configures a Ceph Filesystem (CephFS) volume that mounts a Ceph share into the pod. This is one of the supported volume source types in the volumes list.
Ceph monitors are the addresses (hostnames or IPs) of the Ceph monitor nodes. This field specifies a list of endpoints used to connect to the Ceph cluster.
Path within the CephFS volume to mount. If not specified, defaults to the root directory.
If true, the CephFS volume is mounted as read-only, preventing write access from the pod.
Path to the Ceph keyring file used for authentication. Defaults to /etc/ceph/user.secret.
Reference to a Secret that contains the CephFS credentials (e.g., keyring). The Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the Secret that holds the CephFS authentication credentials. The Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
The CephFS user to use for authentication. Defaults to 'admin' if not specified.

Cinder represents a Cinder volume (OpenStack block storage) that is mounted into the pod. It contains configuration for the Cinder volume source, such as the volume ID, filesystem type, and read-only settings.
Filesystem type to mount, such as 'ext4', 'xfs', etc. If not specified, the default filesystem type of the volume is used.
Specifies whether the Cinder volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; otherwise it is read-write.
SecretRef is a reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains authentication credentials for the Cinder volume. This is optional and used to provide credentials when mounting the volume.
Name of the Kubernetes secret containing the Cinder authentication credentials.
The ID of the Cinder volume to attach and mount.

config_map is a volume source that configures a volume to use a Kubernetes ConfigMap as its content. The specified ConfigMap's data is exposed as files in the volume, enabling pods to consume configuration data.
Sets the file permission mode (in octal, as a decimal integer) for all files within the ConfigMap volume. If unset, the default mode is 0644.

A list of key-to-path mappings. If specified, only the listed keys from the ConfigMap are exposed as files at the specified paths. If omitted, all keys are exposed as files using their key names as paths.
The key to select from the ConfigMap data. This is the key within the ConfigMap's data map whose value will be written to the file path specified by the 'path' field.

Optional permission mode bits for the file (octal). Valid values are 0000 to 0777 (decimal 0 to 511). In JSON, the number must be expressed in decimal (e.g., 420 for 0644). If unset, the volume's defaultMode is used.
The relative path within the volume where the file from the corresponding configMap key will be mounted.
The name of the ConfigMap that provides the volume data. This must match the name of a ConfigMap in the same namespace as the pod.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap and its keys must be defined. If set to true, a missing ConfigMap or missing keys are tolerated (resulting in an empty volume or ignored key); if false or omitted, the Pod fails when the ConfigMap or specified keys are absent.

Represents a volume that is provisioned by a CSI (Container Storage Interface) driver. This allows Kubernetes to consume storage from a driver that implements the CSI specification, enabling integration with external storage systems.
Name of the CSI driver to use. This field is required and must match the driver name as registered on the kubelet.
Filesystem type to mount for the CSI volume, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. If not specified, it is typically inferred as 'ext4', though the CSI driver may define its own default.

A local object reference to a Kubernetes secret in the same namespace that provides credentials for the CSI driver when publishing the volume on the node. This corresponds to the nodePublishSecretRef field of the CSI volume source.
The name of the Secret that contains the credentials for publishing the volume to the node. This Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
Specifies whether the CSI volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is exposed as read-only to the pod; defaults to false.
Map of string keys and values specifying volume attributes for the CSI driver. The meaning of each attribute is driver-specific.
Represents a volume that exposes the downward API data, including pod metadata like labels, annotations, and resource limits, to the container as files.

Optional mode bits used to set permissions on created files by default. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 or a decimal value between 0 and 511. YAML accepts both octal and decimal values, JSON requires decimal values for mode bits. Defaults to 0644.

Optional list of files to create in the volume. Each item consists of a relative path and a fieldRef or resourceFieldRef that specifies which pod field or container resource value to expose at that path.

fieldRef is a reference to a field in the pod's metadata or spec to be exposed, defined by a fieldPath (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.labels['key']) and optionally an apiVersion for the field's schema.
The API version of the referent (e.g., 'v1') that the fieldPath is evaluated against.
The path to the field in the pod's object that will be exposed. For example, 'metadata.name' or 'spec.nodeName'.
Mode bits to use on this file, represented as an integer. If not set, the volume's default mode is used.
The relative path of the file within the volume where the downward API value will be written. The path must not start with '..' and can include directory components.

The resource field selector that selects a container resource field (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) to expose via the downward API. It is represented by a ResourceFieldSelector object with fields for resource, containerName, and divisor.
The name of the container for which the resource value is referenced. If not specified, defaults to the first container in the pod.
Divisor is the divisor for the resource quantity, specified as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1m' for CPU, '1Gi' for memory). It defaults to '1' if not provided.
The name of the container resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'. This field specifies which resource (request or limit) is exposed via the downward API volume.

Defines a temporary directory that is created empty when the pod starts and exists for the lifetime of the pod, allowing containers in the pod to share files. This volume is removed when the pod is deleted.
The storage medium for the emptyDir volume. Set to 'Memory' to use a RAM-backed tmpfs, or 'HugePages' to use hugepages. The default (empty string) uses the node's disk.
The total amount of local storage required for this emptyDir volume, specified as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '128Mi'). If not set, the node's default limit applies.

Configures an ephemeral volume for the pod. This volume type is created and removed with the pod, and can be backed by either a PersistentVolumeClaim template (generic ephemeral volume) or a CSI driver (CSI ephemeral volume).

A template for a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) that defines the volume's storage characteristics, such as access modes, resources, and storage class. When specified, Kubernetes creates a PVC from this template for the ephemeral volume's lifetime.

Metadata for the PersistentVolumeClaim generated from this volume claim template, such as labels and annotations. This is standard Kubernetes object metadata (ObjectMeta) applied to the PVC created by the ephemeral volume.

Annotations is a map of string keys to string values that can be used to attach arbitrary non-identifying metadata to the volume claim template created for this ephemeral volume. This metadata is accessible to clients and tooling but does not affect the volume's behavior.
CreationTimestamp is a timestamp representing the server time when this object was created. It is represented in RFC3339 form (UTC) and is set by the system; clients cannot set it.
The duration in seconds before the object is forcibly deleted, used during graceful deletion.
The time at which the resource is marked for deletion, in RFC 3339 format. This is set by the server when a deletion is requested and is not directly settable by clients.
List of finalizers that must be removed before the object can be deleted. Each finalizer is a string identifier for a controller or owner that must clean up before deletion is allowed.

A prefix used by the Kubernetes API server to generate a unique name for this object if the name field is not provided. The generated name consists of the prefix followed by a random alphanumeric suffix.
A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state for the persistent volume claim template. This field is populated by the Kubernetes system and is read-only.
Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize the PersistentVolumeClaim created from this template. These labels will be set on the generated PVC's metadata.

A list of managed fields entries that map the workflow-id and version to the set of fields managed by that workflow. This is mostly for internal housekeeping and typically should not be set or modified by users.
The API version (e.g., 'apps/v1') of the Kubernetes resource that this managed fields entry belongs to.
Specifies the type of the fields managed by this entry. In Kubernetes, the only supported value is 'FieldsV1'.
fieldsV1 stores the fields owned by the manager in a structured format (like a Trie) represented as a JSON object.
The name of the field manager that last applied changes to this managed field.
The operation performed by the manager on this managed field, typically 'Apply' or 'Update'.
Describes which subresource of the object the managing controller acted on, such as the main resource (empty string), 'status', or 'scale'.
The timestamp at which the operation recorded in the managed field entry was performed. This is a string in RFC3339 format (e.g., 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z).

The name of the volumeClaimTemplate. This name is used as a base for the PersistentVolumeClaim name generated for each pod that uses this ephemeral volume (the PVC name is typically <pod-name>-<template-name>).

The namespace for the volume claim template. In an ephemeral volume, the generated PersistentVolumeClaim is created in the same namespace as the pod, so this field must be empty or set to that namespace.

List of references to the resources that own this object. Used for garbage collection and cascading deletion; each item contains apiVersion, kind, name, uid, and optionally controller and blockOwnerDeletion.
The API version of the referenced owner resource, e.g., 'apps/v1'. This field is used in an OwnerReference to identify the version of the owning object.
If true, prevents the owner from being deleted in foreground deletion until this dependent object is removed. Defaults to false.
Indicates whether the referenced owner is the managing controller of the resource. If true, this owner manages the resource and prevents it from being garbage-collected until the owner is deleted.
The kind of the owner object referenced, such as 'Deployment' or 'ReplicaSet'.
Name of the referenced owner object.
The UID of the referenced owner object. This is a unique identifier assigned by Kubernetes to the object, used to unambiguously identify the owner in the cluster.

ResourceVersion is an opaque string that identifies the internal version of an object. It is used for optimistic concurrency control; clients should treat it as an opaque value and not interpret it. For a volume claim template, this field is part of the standard metadata schema but is typically not set in template definitions.
self_link is a string that contains the URL of the volume claim template for this ephemeral volume within the Kubernetes API.
UID is a system-generated unique identifier for the object. It is read-only and typically assigned by the server when the resource is created.

spec is the specification of the persistent volume claim to be created for the ephemeral volume. It defines the desired characteristics of the volume, such as storage class, access modes, and resources.
Specifies the access modes for the ephemeral volume claim. Allowed values are ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteMany, and ReadWriteOncePod.
Specifies the data source for the volume claim, such as a VolumeSnapshot or PersistentVolumeClaim, used to pre-populate the ephemeral volume with data.
apiGroup is the group for the resource being referenced. If apiGroup is not specified, the specified Kind must be in the core API group. For any other third-party types, apiGroup is required.
Kind is the kind of the referenced data source (e.g., VolumeSnapshot or PersistentVolumeClaim).
The name of the data source object referenced by this volume claim template's dataSource.

Specifies a reference to an object that should be used to populate the volume claim, such as a VolumeSnapshot, PersistentVolumeClaim, or any custom resource. Unlike dataSource, dataSourceRef can reference objects in other namespaces and is typically used with volume populator controllers. This field is part of the PVC spec generated for an ephemeral volume.
APIGroup is the group for the resource being referenced. If APIGroup is not specified, the specified Kind must be in the core API group. For any other third-party types, APIGroup is required.
The kind of the referenced data source object. Typical values are 'PersistentVolumeClaim' or 'VolumeSnapshot', matching the resource type of the data source.
The name of the data source object (e.g., VolumeSnapshot, PersistentVolumeClaim) referenced by the dataSourceRef for the ephemeral volume claim.
The namespace of the referenced data source object. When not set, the namespace of the containing PersistentVolumeClaim is used.
Defines the storage resource requirements for the ephemeral volume, such as the requested capacity. Supports requests and limits for storage, e.g., requests: { storage: 1Gi }.

limits specifies the maximum resources for this ephemeral volume claim, as a map of resource names (e.g., 'storage') to quantities (e.g., '1Gi'). In Kubernetes, this is used to cap the volume size or other resource usage for the claim.

Requests describes the minimum resources required. For a volume claim, this typically specifies the desired storage size, e.g., {'storage': '1Gi'}. The keys are resource names like 'storage', and values are Kubernetes quantity strings.
A label query over PersistentVolumes to consider for binding. Only volumes that match the selector are eligible for use by the ephemeral volume claim.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values. This enables complex label selection logic for the volume claim template.
The label key that the selector applies to. This is the key of a label that the match expression evaluates against.
The operator that represents the relationship between the key and the set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values for the label selector expression. When the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn', this list must be non-empty; for 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty.
A map of string keys and values that defines a label selector. The selector matches resources whose labels contain all specified key-value pairs.
The name of the StorageClass to use for this volume claim. If omitted, the default StorageClass is used.
The name of a VolumeAttributesClass to apply to the volume claim. If specified, the class sets additional attributes on the provisioned volume.
The volume mode that the volume will be mounted in. Supported values are 'Filesystem' (default) and 'Block'.
The name of the PersistentVolume to bind to this claim. This binding reference directs the persistent volume claim to use a specific volume.

Defines a Fibre Channel (FC) volume source. This allows mounting a Fibre Channel storage volume into the pod, typically by specifying target World Wide Names (WWNs), a logical unit number (LUN), and filesystem type.
Filesystem type to be mounted on the Fibre Channel volume (e.g., ext4, xfs). If not specified, Kubernetes attempts to detect the filesystem automatically.
The LUN (Logical Unit Number) of the Fibre Channel target to mount. This is a required integer.
Indicates whether the Fibre Channel volume is mounted as read-only. If true, the volume is read-only; if false or omitted, it is read-write.
List of Fibre Channel target World Wide Names (WWNs) that specify the devices to connect to. This field is required for FC volumes.
A list of Fibre Channel WWIDs (World Wide Identifiers) used to identify the target volume. If specified, this replaces the targetWWNs and lun fields.

FlexVolume represents a generic volume plugin that is mounted via an exec-based interface. It enables integration with third-party storage systems that implement the FlexVolume API, using driver-specific options.
The name of the FlexVolume driver to use for mounting this volume. This driver must be installed on each node.
Filesystem type to be mounted by the FlexVolume driver, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. If unspecified, the driver may use its own default.
Extra command options to pass to the FlexVolume driver, as a map of string keys and values.
When set to true, the FlexVolume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read-write).

Optional reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains sensitive information (e.g., credentials) needed by the FlexVolume driver. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod and is referenced by name.
Name of the Secret resource that contains the secret data to pass to the FlexVolume driver.
Volume source that represents a Flocker dataset to be mounted into the pod. Configures the Flocker volume using dataset identifiers or name.
The name of the Flocker dataset to mount as a volume. Should be set if dataset_uuid is not set.
The UUID of the Flocker dataset to mount. Either datasetName or datasetUUID must be specified.

Configuration for a Google Compute Engine Persistent Disk volume. This volume source mounts an existing GCE persistent disk into the pod, identified by its disk name and with optional filesystem type, partition, and read-only settings.
Filesystem type for the GCE Persistent Disk volume, e.g., 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Defaults to 'ext4' if not specified.
The partition number of the GCE Persistent Disk to mount. If omitted, the entire disk is mounted.
pdName is the unique name of the GCE Persistent Disk resource. It identifies the disk to be mounted in the pod.
Mounts the GCE Persistent Disk as read-only. When true, the volume is mounted read-only; when false (default), it is mounted read-write.

gitRepo represents a volume populated from a git repository. This is a deprecated volume source; use an emptyDir with an init container instead. The object allows specifying the repository URL, revision, and target directory.
The target directory name inside the volume where the git repository will be cloned. If omitted, the repository's name is used.
The repository URL for the git repository to clone into the volume.
The commit hash to check out from the specified Git repository. If not provided, the repository's HEAD is used.
Glusterfs represents a Glusterfs volume that can be mounted by the pod. It specifies the Glusterfs endpoints and path, and optionally read-only.
The name of the Endpoints object that defines the Glusterfs server addresses for this volume.
Path to the Glusterfs volume (e.g., /vol1). This field is required when using a glusterfs volume source.
Specifies whether the GlusterFS volume is mounted as read-only.
Defines a hostPath volume that mounts a file or directory from the host node's filesystem into the pod. This allows the pod to access host paths.
The path of the directory or file on the host node that will be mounted into the pod. This field is required when using a hostPath volume.

The type of the host path. Supported values include '', Directory, DirectoryOrCreate, File, FileOrCreate, Socket, CharDevice, and BlockDevice. An empty string means no check is performed before mounting.
Image volume source configuration. Specifies an OCI image to be mounted as a volume, including the image reference and pull policy.

The image pull policy for the image volume source. Allowed values are 'Always', 'IfNotPresent', and 'Never'. Defaults to 'IfNotPresent' unless the image reference uses the ':latest' tag, in which case it defaults to 'Always'.
The image reference (name and tag) of the container image to mount as a volume, for example 'nginx:latest'.
Represents an iSCSI volume source, which allows mounting an iSCSI target (LUN) as a volume in the pod.
Enables CHAP authentication for iSCSI discovery. When true, the initiator authenticates the target during the discovery phase.

Indicates whether CHAP (Challenge Handshake Authentication Protocol) authentication is enabled for the iSCSI session. When true, the iSCSI session uses CHAP authentication with the secret specified in the secretRef field.
The filesystem type to be mounted (e.g., ext4, xfs). If not specified, the filesystem type of the underlying iSCSI volume is used.
The custom iSCSI initiator name. If not set, the default initiator name (derived from the system) is used for iSCSI connections.
The iSCSI Qualified Name (IQN) of the iSCSI target.
Specifies the iSCSI interface name for the iSCSI transport. Defaults to 'default' if not set.
The LUN (Logical Unit Number) of the iSCSI target. This numeric identifier specifies the logical unit to mount from the target.
List of iSCSI target portals for the volume. Each portal is an IP address or IP:port pair when using non-default ports (default TCP ports are 8600 and 3260).
Indicates whether the iSCSI volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read-write).
References a Kubernetes Secret that contains the CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI target. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
The name of the Secret that contains CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI target. The Secret must be in the same namespace as the Pod.
The iSCSI target portal. The portal is either an IP address or ip_addr:port if the port is other than the default (typically TCP ports 860 and 3260).
Name of the volume. Must be a unique DNS_LABEL within the pod. This name is used to reference the volume in container volumeMounts.
Configures an NFS (Network File System) share as a volume. Includes settings for the NFS server, exported path, and read-only flag.
Path of the NFS export on the NFS server. This is the directory on the NFS server that will be mounted into the pod.
Forces the NFS export to be mounted with read-only permissions. Defaults to false (read-write).
The hostname or IP address of the NFS server that exports the volume.
Configures a volume that is backed by a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC). This allows a pod to use persistent storage by referencing a PVC in the same namespace.
The name of the PersistentVolumeClaim in the same namespace to reference as a volume source.
If true, the persistent volume claim is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Defines a volume that uses a Photon Controller persistent disk, allowing the container to access a persistent disk managed by Photon Controller.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Ex. 'ext4', 'xfs', 'ntfs'. Implicitly inferred to be 'ext4' if unspecified.
The unique identifier of the Photon persistent disk. This is the ID that identifies the disk in Photon Controller, and it is required to mount the volume.
Configures a Portworx volume as a pod volume. This block defines a volume backed by a Portworx storage volume.
The filesystem type to mount on the Portworx volume, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. If not specified, defaults to 'ext4'.
Specifies whether the Portworx volume is mounted as read-only. If set to true, the volume is mounted with read-only permissions.
The unique identifier of the Portworx volume to be mounted.
Represents a projected volume source, which can mount multiple volume sources into the same directory. It supports sources such as secret, configMap, downwardAPI, and serviceAccountToken.
Optional mode bits used to set permissions on files created in the projected volume. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 or decimal between 0 and 511. Defaults to 0644.
sources is the list of VolumeProjection objects that are projected into the volume. Each projection can be a configMap, secret, downwardAPI, or serviceAccountToken.
Configures a ClusterTrustBundle as a source for a projected volume, allowing the pod to access the trust bundle (such as a CA bundle) from a named ClusterTrustBundle object in the cluster.
labelSelector is a standard Kubernetes label selector that filters ClusterTrustBundle resources by labels. Only ClusterTrustBundles matching this selector are projected into the volume.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. All requirements must be satisfied for the selector to match.
The label key that the match expression uses to select cluster trust bundles. This key must correspond to a label on the bundle and be a valid Kubernetes label key.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values that the label key must match when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'. For operators 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty.

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.
Name of the referenced ClusterTrustBundle object to project into the volume.
Indicates whether the ClusterTrustBundle can be omitted from the projected volume. If set to true, the projection is skipped when the bundle is absent; if false or unset, the bundle must exist.
The relative path of the file within the projected volume where the cluster trust bundle content is mounted. This path must be a relative path and cannot start with '..'.
The signer name of the cluster trust bundle to project. Selects the trust bundle(s) that match this signer name when multiple bundles exist.
ConfigMap projection to include in the projected volume. Used to project a ConfigMap's data (or specific items) into the volume.

Optional list of key mappings that specify which keys from the referenced ConfigMap to project into the volume, and the paths and file modes for each. If omitted, all key-value pairs are projected as files with key names; if specified, only listed keys are projected.
The key in the ConfigMap to select. This must be a valid key name within the referenced ConfigMap's data.
Optional file mode (permission bits) for the file. If not specified, the default is 0644. Must be a 32-bit integer representing an octal permission value, typically between 0 and 0777.

Path specifies the relative file path (within the volume) where the value of the corresponding key is mounted. It must be a relative path, must not contain '..' or start with '/', and determines the filename as seen in the projected volume.
Name of the ConfigMap to project into the volume. Must be a valid Kubernetes object name.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap is optional. When set to true, the volume will not fail if the ConfigMap does not exist.
The `downward_api` source within a projected volume exposes Pod metadata such as labels and annotations as files to the container.
The list of DownwardAPIVolumeFile items that specify the files to project via the downward API. Each item defines a relative file path and the pod field reference to write to that path.
A reference to a pod field whose value is projected into the volume, such as metadata.name or spec.nodeName.
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath refers to. For example, 'v1'.
The path to the pod spec field to be exposed, such as metadata.name or spec.nodeName. It selects a field of the pod specification.
Optional file permissions for the file, specified in octal (e.g., 0644). If unset, the default file mode is used.
Path within the volume where the field value will be exposed as a file. This is the relative path of the file in the projected volume.
Selects a container resource field (such as requests.cpu or limits.memory) to expose in the downward API volume. Only resource limits and requests are supported.
The name of the container to which the resource field reference applies. Required when the resource field refers to a container resource (e.g., limits or requests).
Divisor is the value to divide the resource value by. Must be a valid Quantity, defaults to 1.
The name of the resource to select, such as "limits.cpu" or "requests.memory". This is a required field in the ResourceFieldSelector for downward API volumes.
Path within the projected volume where the certificate chain is exposed. The file at this path contains the full certificate chain.
Specifies the relative path within the projected volume where the certificate's private key file is placed.
The maximum expiration time in seconds for the pod certificate injected into the projected volume. This bounds the lifetime of the certificate, ensuring it does not exceed the specified duration.
The name of the certificate signer that should issue the pod certificate. This is used to select the appropriate signer when requesting a certificate for the pod.
The numeric UID that will own the certificate file projected from this source. If unset, the file is owned by UID 0 (root).
SecretProjection adapts a secret into a projected volume. The secret's data keys are exposed as files in the volume.

A list of key-to-path mappings that specify which secret keys are projected into the volume and the file paths they are exposed at. If items is not set, all keys from the referenced secret are projected.
The key within the referenced Secret that corresponds to the data to project into the volume. This is the name of the entry in the Secret's data map.
The permissions for the file representing the secret key. Must be a numeric value between 0 and 511 (octal 0000-0777) representing Unix file mode bits.
Relative path within the projected volume to which the secret key is mapped. Must be a relative path and must not contain '..' segments.
The name of the Secret to project into the volume. This must match the name of a Secret in the same namespace as the pod.
If true, the referenced secret is not required to exist; if it is missing, the volume is created without files from that secret. Defaults to false, requiring the secret to be present.
Configures a projected volume source that injects the service account token into the pod. The token can be customized with fields such as audience, expirationSeconds, and path.
The audience (aud) claim for the service account token, specifying the intended recipient. The token is valid only for this audience, such as the Kubernetes API server or a specific service.
The expiration time of the projected service account token, in seconds. Must be between 600 and 86400 (10 minutes to 24 hours), and defaults to 3600 (1 hour).
The relative path within the projected volume at which to mount the service account token.
Configuration for a Quobyte volume source, which mounts a Quobyte distributed storage system into the pod.
Group to map volume access to. Defaults to no group.
Whether to mount the volume as read-only. Defaults to false.
The Quobyte registry to connect to, as a host or host:port, or a comma-separated list of registries.
The tenant name that owns the Quobyte volume in the backend; used with dynamically provisioned Quobyte volumes.
User to map volume access to. Defaults to the volume name if not set.
The name of the Quobyte volume to mount.
rbd represents a Rados Block Device (RBD) volume source, allowing a pod to mount an RBD image into the container.
Filesystem type of the RBD volume that Kubernetes will mount (e.g., ext4, xfs). If not set, the filesystem type is determined by the image's existing filesystem.
The rados image name. This is the name of the RBD image to mount as a volume.
The path to the keyring file for RBD user authentication. Defaults to /etc/ceph/keyring.
Monitors is a list of Ceph monitor addresses (host:port) used to connect to the Ceph cluster for the RBD volume.
The Ceph pool name where the RBD image resides. Defaults to 'rbd' if not specified.
If set to true, the RBD volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Reference to a Kubernetes secret that provides the Ceph authentication key for the RBD volume.
Name of the Kubernetes Secret that holds the Ceph authentication credentials for the RBD volume.
Specifies the RADOS user name used for authentication with the Ceph cluster. Defaults to "admin".
ScaleIO represents a ScaleIO persistent volume source. This block configures the ScaleIO volume to be used as a volume in the pod.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system, e.g., ext4, xfs. Defaults to ext4.
The host address of the ScaleIO API gateway.
The name of the ScaleIO Protection Domain for the configured storage.
Marks the ScaleIO volume as read-only. When set to true, the volume is mounted with read-only permissions.
secret_ref is a reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the ScaleIO admin password. It must be in the same namespace as the Pod, and is required for authentication with the ScaleIO system.
Name of the Secret object that contains authentication credentials for ScaleIO volume access.
Enables or disables SSL communication with the ScaleIO Gateway. When true, the volume plugin connects to the gateway over SSL.
Storage mode for the ScaleIO volume. Allowed values are 'ThinProvisioned' (default) and 'ThickProvisioned'.
The name of the ScaleIO storage pool in which the volume is created or from which it is provisioned.
The name of the ScaleIO storage system.
Name of the ScaleIO volume, as defined in the ScaleIO storage system.
secret is a volume source that references a Kubernetes Secret object, allowing the Secret's data to be mounted as files into the pod.
Specifies the default permission mode (in octal) applied to files within the secret volume. Defaults to 0644 if unspecified.

Optional list of key-to-path mappings for the secret volume. Each item specifies a key from the secret, the file path where that key should be mounted, and an optional permission mode. If omitted, all keys in the secret are mounted as files using their key names.
The key in the secret's data that should be exposed as a file. The file path is specified by the corresponding 'path' field in the same item.
The permission mode for the file, specified as a numeric value in octal (e.g., 420 for 0644). If omitted, the volume's defaultMode is used.
The relative path of the file to which the corresponding secret key is mapped within the volume's mount path. Must not contain '..' or start with '../'.
Specifies whether the referenced Secret must be defined. When true, the volume can still be used even if the Secret does not exist.
The name of the Secret to mount as a volume. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Defines a StorageOS volume source for the pod, providing configuration for mounting a StorageOS volume.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. If not specified, the filesystem type is inferred from the volume.
Indicates whether the StorageOS volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume cannot be written to; default is false.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains StorageOS API credentials. If not set, default credentials will be attempted.
The name of the Secret that contains the StorageOS API credentials.
The name of the StorageOS volume to mount. This must match an existing volume in the StorageOS system.
volumeNamespace specifies the namespace of the StorageOS volume. If not set, it defaults to the Kubernetes namespace of the pod.
vsphereVolume represents a vSphere volume to be mounted into the container. It configures a vSphere datastore volume as a storage source for the pod.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Ex. "ext4", "xfs", "ntfs". Implicitly inferred to be "ext4" if unspecified.
The storage policy ID based on which storage is provisioned for the vSphere volume.
The name of the vSphere storage policy to be applied to the volume. This policy determines storage characteristics such as performance and availability.
The datastore path that identifies the vSphere volume to mount, e.g., '[datastore1] vmdisk'.

kubernetes_apps_deployment.status.condit.text: last_transition_time is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. It is a string representing the timestamp in RFC3339 format, as defined in Kubernetes deployment status conditions.
The last time the condition was updated, as a timestamp in RFC3339 format.
A human-readable message providing details about the current condition, such as the reason for the deployment's state.
A brief, machine-readable reason for the condition's last transition, typically in CamelCase.
The status of the condition, one of True, False, or Unknown.
Type of the condition, e.g., Available, Progressing, or ReplicaFailure, indicating the specific aspect of deployment status being reported.

kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.man.text: The API version of the resource that this manager operates on.
The type of the fields managed in this entry, such as 'FieldsV1'.

A JSON representation of the fields managed by the manager in a Kubernetes ManagedFieldsEntry. Its structure mirrors the resource schema, with keys indicating field paths (e.g., 'spec', 'metadata.labels') and values as nested objects or empty objects, denoting ownership.
The name of the manager (e.g., kubectl, a controller) that owns the managed fields entry.
The method used to apply the managed fields, typically 'Update' or 'Apply'.
The subresource this managed field entry applies to, such as 'status' or empty string for the main resource.
Time is the timestamp of when the ManagedFields entry was last updated. It is represented as an RFC3339-formatted string.

kubernetes_apps_replica_set.metadata.own.text: The API version of the owner resource referenced by this owner reference (e.g., 'apps/v1'). This specifies the group and version of the resource kind.

Determines whether this owner reference blocks deletion of the owner until the dependent object is removed. If true, the owner cannot be deleted until this dependent is deleted or this field is set to false.
Indicates whether the owner reference is the managing controller of this resource.
The kind of the owner object, such as 'ReplicaSet' or 'Deployment'. This is a required field in OwnerReference.
The name of the referenced owner object, as defined in the Kubernetes object's metadata.
The UID of the owner object referenced by this owner reference. This uniquely identifies the owning resource in the cluster.

kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.selecto.text: The label key that the selector expression applies to.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values that the key must match when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'. This field is used in a match expression for the label selector of a ReplicaSet.

kubernetes_apps_replica_set.spec.templat.text: The API version used by the manager to modify the object. This field is part of a managed fields entry that tracks field ownership and management in Kubernetes.
The type of the fields in the managedFields entry, indicating the structure of the fieldsV1 field (e.g., 'FieldsV1').
fields_v1 is a JSON representation of the fields owned by the manager. It contains the exact set of fields managed by this entry, serialized as a JSON object.
The name of the manager (e.g., a controller or user) that last modified the fields managed by this entry. This is part of the Kubernetes managedFields mechanism for tracking field ownership.
Operation is the type of operation which lead to this ManagedFieldsEntry being created. The only valid values for this field are 'Apply' and 'Update'.
Specifies the subresource (e.g., 'status') that this managed fields entry applies to, or an empty string for the top-level resource.
The timestamp of when these managed fields were set, in RFC3339 format. It is always empty if the operation is 'Apply'.
The API version of the owner object referenced by this owner reference (e.g., 'apps/v1'). This identifies the group and version of the referenced resource.
If true, this owner reference prevents the owner object from being deleted until the dependent object is removed, which is used in foreground cascading deletion. Defaults to false.
A boolean indicating whether the owning object is a controller that manages the referenced object, such as a ReplicaSet controlling a Pod.
The kind of the owner resource, such as 'ReplicaSet'.
The name of the owner object referenced by this OwnerReference.
The UID of the owner object. This unique identifier is used to reliably reference the owner even if its name changes.
The node selector term that specifies the preference for node affinity scheduling. It contains matchExpressions and matchFields fields that define the node selection constraints.
A list of node selector requirements that define which nodes are considered preferred. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and a list of values to match against node labels.
The Kubernetes label key that the node affinity match expression applies to. For example, 'disktype' or 'kubernetes.io/os'.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and the set of values. Allowed values: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt.

A list of values that the node's label key must match, depending on the operator. For operators In and NotIn, this list enumerates the allowed or disallowed values; for Exists and DoesNotExist, it must be empty.

A list of node selector requirements that specify node fields (e.g., metadata.name) to match for this node affinity preference. Each requirement defines a field key, operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optional values.
The key that the match requirement applies to, such as a node label or field name used in the node selector term.
The operator represents the relationship between the match label key and a set of values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.

The list of values for the node selector requirement. The allowed values depend on the operator: for In and NotIn, this must be a non-empty list of valid label values; for Exists and DoesNotExist, this must be empty; for Gt and Lt, this must contain exactly one numeric string value.
The weight of the node affinity preference, used to calculate the relative importance of this preference. Must be an integer between 1 and 100, inclusive.

A list of label selector requirements that constrain which nodes match this selector term. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt), and optional values, and all requirements are ANDed together.
The label key that the node selector requirement applies to. The node must have this label key for the requirement to match.
Specifies the operator for the match expression. Allowed values: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt.

A list of string values for a node selector requirement. When the operator is In or NotIn, this list must be non-empty and the label key must match one of these values; when the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.

A list of node selector requirements that match on node fields (e.g., metadata.name). Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and a list of values, similar to matchExpressions but for node fields.
The key is the name of the node field (e.g., metadata.name) that this selector requirement matches against.
Specifies the operator to use when matching a node selector field against values.

The list of values that the node field (identified by 'key') must match. The operator (e.g., In, NotIn) defines how these values are used; for operators like Exists or DoesNotExist, the list must be empty.

Defines a pod affinity term for a preferred scheduling rule. This includes a label selector, optional namespaces, and a topology key that specify which pods the affinity applies to and the scope of the affinity.

A label query over the pods to form the affinity term. It specifies the pods whose labels must match for the affinity rule to apply, using standard label selector semantics (matchLabels and matchExpressions).

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a label key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and, for In/NotIn, a list of string values. Only pods whose labels satisfy all requirements are selected.
The label key that the selector will match against. This is the key part of a label selector match expression, used to select pods by their labels.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
List of values for the label selector match expression. For the In and NotIn operators, this list must be non-empty; for the Exists and DoesNotExist operators, it must be empty.
A map of key-value pairs that the target pod's labels must match. If specified, all specified labels must be present on the pod for this affinity term to be considered.

Specifies a list of label keys whose values from the incoming pod are used to construct a label selector for pod affinity. These keys are combined with the labelSelector to determine which pods are considered for affinity.
A list of pod label keys. When set, the affinity/anti-affinity term will only evaluate candidate pods whose label values for these keys differ from the new pod's label values.
A label selector used to select the namespaces that are considered when matching the pod affinity term. If omitted, only the pod's own namespace is considered.

A list of label selector requirements for matching namespaces. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and, for In/NotIn, a set of values. All requirements must be satisfied for the namespace to be selected.
The label key that the selector operates on. In a match expression, this is the key of the label to match against, such as 'app' or 'environment'.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

values is a list of string values used by the match expression. When the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn', this list must be non-empty and contains the label values to match against. When the operator is 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty.
A map of label keys to values used to select namespaces. For the pod affinity term, only namespaces that have all specified labels will be considered when applying the preferred scheduling rule.
List of namespaces that the pod affinity term applies to. If unspecified, the namespace of the pod where the affinity is defined is used.
The label key that defines the topology domain used to match pods. Nodes must share the same label value for this key to be considered in the same topology domain (e.g., 'kubernetes.io/hostname').
Weight associated with the corresponding pod affinity term, in the range 1-100. Higher weights give the term more influence during scheduling.
Label selector used to identify the set of pods that the required pod affinity term applies to. It uses standard Kubernetes label matching rules to select pods based on their labels.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. The pod affinity rule is satisfied when the target pod's labels match all requirements in this list.
The label key that the selector applies to. It should be a valid Kubernetes label key, matching the key of a label on the pod.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

A list of string values that corresponds to the values in a label selector match expression. If the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn', this list must be non-empty; if the operator is 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty. The values are matched against the value of the specified label key.

matchLabels is a map of key-value pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.

A list of pod label keys. Values from the incoming pod for these keys are merged into the label selector to match existing pods, enabling pod affinity/anti-affinity grouping based on dynamic pod labels.

A label selector to filter the namespaces that the affinity/anti-affinity term applies to. The term will match pods running in namespaces that match the label selector. If not specified, the pod's own namespace is used.

A list of label selector requirements that namespaces must satisfy to be eligible for the affinity rule. Each requirement defines a key, operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optional values. All expressions are ANDed together.
The label key that the selector matches on. In this context, it is used within namespaceSelector.matchExpressions for pod affinity rules, selecting namespaces by their labels.
Operator for the match expression, determining how the key is matched against the values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values that the key must match according to the operator. For 'In' and 'NotIn' operators, this array contains the allowed values; for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty.

match_labels is a map of label keys to values used to select namespaces by their labels. It specifies label requirements that the namespace objects must satisfy to be included in the namespace selector for this pod affinity rule.

A list of namespaces that the labelSelector should match. If not specified, it defaults to the namespace of the pod where the affinity term is defined, restricting pod affinity/anti-affinity to pods running in those namespaces.

The node label key that defines the topology domain for this pod affinity term (e.g., kubernetes.io/hostname). Pods are placed only on nodes that share the same value for this label as the matching pods.

Specifies the pod affinity term used in a preferred anti-affinity rule. It defines the group of pods (via label selector) and the topology key that determines the domains (e.g., nodes) where co-location with those pods should be avoided during scheduling.
