Specifies a TCP socket action for the readiness probe. The probe attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's port, with optional host, to determine readiness.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The TCP port to check for the readiness probe. It can be a port number or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. If the probe does not finish within this duration, it is considered failed. Defaults to 1 second.

Defines the resize policy for container resources, allowing in-place resizing of resource requests/limits. Each object specifies a resource (e.g., cpu, memory) and a restart policy: Always, OnEviction, or Never.
The name of the resource to which the resize policy applies, such as cpu or memory.

restart_policy defines whether the container must be restarted to apply changes from a resize operation. Allowed values are 'NotRequired' (no restart is needed; the change applies live) and 'RestartContainer' (the container must be restarted to apply the new resource allocation).
Resource requirements for the init container, specifying requests and limits for compute resources such as CPU and memory.
List of ResourceClaim requirements for this container. Each entry specifies a ResourceClaim name that the container requires, used with the Dynamic Resource Allocation feature.
The name of the PersistentVolumeClaim to reference. This must match the name of a PersistentVolumeClaim in the same namespace.
Request is the name of the resource request within the ResourceClaimStatus. If omitted, it defaults to the name of the ResourceClaim.
Limits specifies the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the init container. Each key is a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the value is a quantity string such as '100m' or '1Gi'.
Requests specifies the minimum amount of compute resources required for the init container. The map's keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) and values are resource quantities as strings.

Defines the restart policy for this init container. Allowed values are "Always" (runs as a sidecar for the duration of the pod) and "Never" (default, runs to completion exactly once per pod lifecycle). Only valid for init containers.
Defines how the exit codes in this rule are compared to the container's actual exit code to determine if the restart policy applies.
Specifies the list of numeric exit codes that trigger this restart policy rule.

SecurityContext defines the security settings (e.g., user, group, capabilities, SELinux options) for this init container. It controls the privilege and access control settings that apply to the container's processes.

AllowPrivilegeEscalation controls whether the process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, the container runs with the no_new_privs flag, preventing privilege escalation. The default is true, but setting it to false is recommended for security.
AppArmor profile settings for the container. Specifies the AppArmor profile to apply, including the type (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and optionally the localhost profile name.

The name of the AppArmor profile to load when the type is Localhost. This field is used only when the appArmorProfile type is set to Localhost, and it specifies the profile name available on the node.
Specifies the type of AppArmor profile to apply to the container. Valid values are `RuntimeDefault`, `Localhost`, and `Unconfined`.
Linux capabilities to add or drop for the container, defining privileged operations the container is allowed to perform.
Adds the specified Linux capabilities to the container's effective capability set. For example, adding 'NET_ADMIN' grants network administration privileges.
Specifies a list of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's default set. For example, 'ALL' drops all capabilities.

Specifies whether the container should run in privileged mode. When true, the container's processes have nearly all capabilities as processes on the host, essentially disabling isolation and granting extended privileges.
Sets the proc mount type for the container. Allowed values are 'Default' (mask /proc for security) and 'Unmasked' (expose all processes). Defaults to 'Default' if not specified.
Indicates whether the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the container cannot write to its root filesystem, which is a common security hardening measure.
Specifies the group ID (GID) that the container's main process should run as. This is an integer value, typically a Unix group ID.
Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the container will not be allowed to run as root (UID 0), and the Kubernetes runtime will enforce this.
The numeric UID that the init container's process will run as. If set, it overrides the user specified in the container image.
SELinux options specify the SELinux context (label) applied to the container, including user, role, type, and level.
The SELinux level label applied to the container, as part of the SELinux options in the container's security context.
The SELinux role label assigned to the container. Part of the SELinux context used for role-based access control.
The SELinux type label, which defines the type domain for the process. In Kubernetes, it is part of the SELinux security context options.
The SELinux user label for the container. This is part of the SELinux options applied to the container's security context.

Configure the seccomp profile for the init container's security context. This object supports a `type` field (e.g., `RuntimeDefault`, `Localhost`, `Unconfined`) and an optional `localhost_profile` path to a custom seccomp profile.
The path to a seccomp profile in the node's local filesystem. This must be set when the seccomp 'type' is 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to apply. Allowed values are RuntimeDefault, Localhost, and Unconfined. When set to Localhost, the localhostProfile field must also be specified.
WindowsOptions holds Windows-specific security settings for the container, such as GMSA credentials and Windows user name. It is only applicable when the container runtime is Windows.
The name of a GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container. This option is specific to Windows security contexts and references a pre-configured GMSA credential spec resource.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container. This references a GMSA credential spec configured in the cluster.

HostProcess determines if a container should be run as a 'Host Process' container. When set to true, the container runs as a host process container on the Windows node. All containers in a pod must have the same effective HostProcess value.

The username to run the container's entrypoint process as for Windows containers. This is part of the WindowsSecurityContextOptions and is an alternative to the runAsUser field, which is not supported for Windows. The value should be in the format DOMAIN\User or User@Domain.
Defines the startup probe settings for the init container. In Kubernetes, probes are not supported for init containers, so this field is not permitted and will be rejected by the API server.
Exec specifies the action to take by running a command inside the container. A successful command (exit code 0) indicates the probe passes.
The command to execute inside the container for this exec-based startup probe. It is run directly without a shell; a nonzero exit status indicates that the probe failed.
The number of consecutive failures required for the startup probe to be considered failed after which the container will be restarted. Minimum value is 1; default is 3.
gRPC probe configuration. Contains the port and optional service name used to perform a gRPC health check on the container.
Port number that the gRPC probe should connect to. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the default is the pod's name.
Performs an HTTP GET request against the container. The `http_get` configuration defines the endpoint (port and path) and optional headers used by the startup probe to check container health.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request for the startup probe. Each item defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request. This is the header field name, such as 'Authorization' or 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header for the GET request sent by the probe. This is a string and is used along with the header name to set the request header.
Path to access on the HTTP server, e.g., '/healthz'.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. This is a string that can be a numeric TCP port (1-65535) or the name of a port defined in the container's ports list.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS', with a default of 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Defaults to 0, and must be a non-negative integer.
How often (in seconds) to perform the startup probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. For startup probes, this value must be 1; defaults to 1 if not specified.

Defines a TCP socket check used as the handler for the startup probe. The probe attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the container, indicating readiness when the connection succeeds.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to connect to for the probe. Can be a numeric port or a named port.

The number of seconds allowed for a container to terminate gracefully before it is forcibly killed with SIGKILL. Must be a non-negative integer; a value of zero means immediate termination. This is a pod-level setting, not specific to the startup probe.
The number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. The value must be at least 1.
Whether this container should allocate a buffer for stdin in the container runtime. If this is not set, reads from stdin in the container will always result in EOF. Defaults to false.
When true, the container's stdin is closed after the first attach (or immediately if no attach). Defaults to false.
Path where the container's termination message is written. The kubelet reads this file to fetch the termination message when the container exits, and it defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Defines how the termination message of the container is populated. Valid values are 'File' (default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'. When set to 'File', the termination message is read from the file /dev/termination-log; when set to 'FallbackToLogsOnError', the last chunk of container log output is used if the termination message file is empty.
Indicates whether a pseudo-TTY should be allocated for the container. When set to true, the container gets a terminal attached, consistent with Docker's -t flag.

List of block devices to be used by the container, mapping each named volume to a raw block device path inside the container. This enables access to raw block volumes, as opposed to filesystem-mounted volumes.
The path inside the container at which the volume device is mounted.
The name of the volume device, which must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's volumes.

Specifies a list of volumes to mount into the init container's filesystem. Each volume mount must reference a volume defined in the Pod spec, and includes the mount path and mount options such as read-only or subPath.
Path within the container where the volume is mounted. Must be an absolute path, such as /data.
Controls how mount propagation is handled for this volume mount. Allowed values are None, HostToContainer, and Bidirectional.
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
Mounts the volume as read-only when true; defaults to false, allowing read-write access.

Recursive read-only mount flag for the volume mount. Determines whether the read-only setting is applied recursively to all nested mounts. Allowed values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', or 'IfPossible' (case-sensitive).
Path within the volume from which the container will be mounted. If not specified, the volume's root is mounted.

sub_path_expr specifies a sub-path within the volume to mount, with support for environment variable references (e.g., $(VAR_NAME)). It is an alternative to the static subPath field, allowing dynamic paths based on environment variables.
The container's working directory. If not specified, the default is '/'. Must be an absolute path.

The name of a custom condition that must be satisfied for the pod to be considered ready. This is the key of a condition that a controller adds to the pod's status; the pod becomes ready only when all readiness gate conditions are true.
The name of the resource claim, which must be unique within the pod and is referenced by containers to use this claim.
The name of the ResourceClaim resource that this pod requests. Must match the name of a ResourceClaim object in the same namespace.

The name of a ResourceClaimTemplate that is used to generate a ResourceClaim for this pod. When set, the ResourceClaim is created and deleted automatically for the pod's lifetime; mutually exclusive with resource_claim_name.
Name of the ResourceClaim that this container references. The named ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the resource claim to request for the container, as specified in the pod's resource requirements.
The name of the scheduling gate. This name uniquely identifies the gate within the pod spec and must be a valid DNS subdomain name. It is used to reference and remove the gate before scheduling.
The name of the sysctl parameter, such as 'kernel.shm_rmid_forced'.
The value to set for the named sysctl parameter.
The taint effect to match, such as NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, or NoExecute. If omitted, the toleration matches all effects.
The key of the taint that this toleration matches. If empty, matches all taints.
The operator used to match the taint key. Allowed values are 'Equal' and 'Exists'. Defaults to 'Equal'.

The duration in seconds for which the pod will tolerate a taint with a NoExecute effect, after which the pod will be evicted if the taint persists. This field is optional and only applies when the toleration's effect is NoExecute.
The value to match against the taint key when the operator is Equal. Must be left empty when the operator is Exists.
Label selector is used to find matching pods. Pods that match this label selector are counted to determine the number of pods in each topology domain.
A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values.
The label key that the selector requirement applies to. In a match expression, this is the key of the label that must match the operator and values.
The operator represents the key's relationship to a set of values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values that the key must match. Required for operators In and NotIn; must be empty for Exists and DoesNotExist.
Label selector for topology spread constraints, expressed as a map of key/value pairs. All matchLabels requirements are ANDed to select the pods the constraint applies to.

List of pod label keys used to select the group of pods over which spreading is calculated. The topology spread is computed over pods that match these label keys with the labels of the pod being scheduled.

The degree to which Pods may be distributed unevenly. Must be greater than zero. The actual skew is calculated as the difference between the number of matching Pods in the most and least loaded topology domains.

An optional field specifying the minimum number of eligible domains required for the topology spread constraint to take effect. If the number of eligible domains is less than min_domains, the constraint is ignored (treated as having a global minimum of 0).

Indicates how to treat a node's nodeAffinity when computing pod spread. Valid values are 'Honor' (only nodes satisfying nodeAffinity are considered) and 'Ignore' (nodeAffinity is ignored). Defaults to 'Honor'.
Indicates how to treat tainted nodes when considering pod topology spread constraints. Allowed values are 'Honor' and 'Ignore'; if not set, the default is 'Ignore'.

The key of node labels that defines the topology domains for spreading pods. Nodes sharing the same value for this key are considered in the same domain, and pods are spread evenly across these domains.

Indicates how to handle a topology spread constraint when it cannot be satisfied. Valid values are 'DoNotSchedule' (default) and 'ScheduleAnyway'. 'DoNotSchedule' prevents scheduling the pod if the constraint cannot be met, while 'ScheduleAnyway' allows scheduling with best-effort spreading.
Defines an AWS Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume to be mounted into the pod. This volume source references an existing EBS volume by its ID and attaches it to the node.
Filesystem type to use when mounting the AWS EBS volume (e.g., ext4, ext3, xfs). If not specified, defaults to ext4.
The partition in the EBS volume from which to mount the volume. If omitted, the first partition is used by default; if the volume has no partitions, the whole volume is mounted.
If true, the EBS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false if not specified.
The unique identifier of the AWS EBS volume to mount, typically in the format 'vol-xxxxxxxx'.
azureDisk represents an Azure Data Disk mount on the host and bind mount to the pod.
Caching mode for the Azure disk. Allowed values: None, ReadOnly, ReadWrite. If not specified, the default is None.
The name of the Azure data disk to mount. This is the disk name as it appears in the Azure resource, used to identify the VHD blob in storage.
The URI of the Azure disk to mount as a volume, corresponding to the diskURI field in the Kubernetes azureDisk volume source.
Filesystem type to mount, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. Defaults to ext4 if not specified.
Kind of the Azure disk. Possible values are 'Shared', 'Dedicated', or 'Managed'. Defaults to 'Shared'.
Specifies whether the Azure disk volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
azureFile is a volume source that represents an Azure File Service mount, allowing a pod to mount an Azure file share as a volume.
Specifies whether the Azure File share is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume cannot be written to from the pod.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret that contains the Azure Storage Account name and key for authenticating to the Azure file share.
Name of the Azure File share to mount.
CephFS represents a Ceph Filesystem mount that lasts the lifetime of a pod. CephFS volumes do not support ownership management or SELinux relabeling.
Required: A collection of Ceph monitor addresses (host:port) for the CephFS volume.
Path within the CephFS filesystem to mount. If not specified, defaults to the root directory '/'. This is the path on the Ceph cluster that will be exposed as the volume.
If true, the CephFS volume is mounted as read-only. This prevents writes to the volume from the pod.
Path to a secret file on the CephFS filesystem that contains the authentication credentials for accessing the CephFS volume.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret containing CephFS authentication credentials (keyring). The secret is used to authenticate to the Ceph cluster.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that contains the CephFS credentials.
The RADOS user name used for CephFS authentication. Defaults to 'admin'.
Cinder represents a Cinder volume (OpenStack block storage) to be mounted into the pod. This volume is attached to the node and then mounted into the container filesystem.
Filesystem type to mount on the volume, such as ext4 or xfs. If not specified, the system will use the default filesystem type of the underlying Cinder volume.
Makes the Cinder volume read-only when mounted. Defaults to false (read-write).
secret_ref is an optional reference to a Kubernetes secret that holds authentication credentials for the Cinder volume provider. It is used when the Cinder volume requires authentication.
The name of the secret that contains authentication credentials for the Cinder volume.
The ID of the Cinder volume to mount. This is the unique identifier of the volume in OpenStack Cinder.

config_map configures a volume sourced from a Kubernetes ConfigMap. It defines how the ConfigMap's data is exposed as files in the volume, including the ConfigMap name, default file permissions, and optional item mappings.
Optional: mode bits used to set permissions on files created in the config map volume. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 or a decimal value between 0 and 511. Defaults to 0644.

Optional list of key-to-path mappings. Each item specifies a key from the ConfigMap and the corresponding path to expose it at within the volume. When omitted, all keys in the ConfigMap are written as files.
The key in the ConfigMap data to mount as a file. Must be a valid ConfigMap key.
Optional mode bits used to set permissions on this file, as an octal integer (e.g., 0644). If not set, the volume's defaultMode is used.
The relative path of the file to map the key to. Must not start with '/' or contain '..'.
Name of the ConfigMap that supplies the volume data. This must match the name of a ConfigMap in the same namespace as the pod.
If true, the referenced ConfigMap (or its keys) may be absent; the volume will be empty in that case. If false, the ConfigMap and keys must exist; otherwise the pod fails to start.
Specifies a volume that is backed by a CSI (Container Storage Interface) driver. This allows pods to mount storage from a CSI driver, which exposes external storage systems to Kubernetes.
driver specifies the name of the CSI driver that provides the volume. This value must match the name of a CSI driver installed on the cluster.
Filesystem type to mount. If not specified, the volume provider determines the default filesystem.
A reference to a Secret object in the same namespace that contains credentials required by the CSI driver to publish the volume on the node.
The name of the Secret in the pod's namespace that provides sensitive data for the CSI node publish operation.
Specifies whether the CSI volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; otherwise it is read-write. Defaults to false.
Attributes of the volume to be used by the CSI driver. The keys and values are driver-specific and defined by the CSI driver implementation.
Configures a volume that uses the Kubernetes downward API to expose pod metadata, such as labels, annotations, or resource limits, to containers as files.
Optional file mode (permission bits) applied to files in the downward API volume. Defaults to 0644 when not set.
The list of files to project into the volume. Each item maps a field reference to a specific file path, allowing selective inclusion of Downward API data.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName) to expose as a file in the downward API volume.
Specifies the API version of the schema used for the field reference (e.g., 'v1'). If not set, the default is 'v1'.
The path to the field in the Pod spec that is exposed via the downward API. For example, 'metadata.name' or 'spec.nodeName'.
Optional file permission mode for this downward API item. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 (decimal 0-511); if omitted, the volume's defaultMode (usually 0644) is used.
Path is the relative file path within the volume where the downward API field's value will be written. It must be a relative path, not starting with '/' and it should not contain '..' components.

ResourceFieldSelector that references a container resource field (e.g., requests.cpu, limits.memory) to be exposed as a file in the downward API volume. It may specify the container name and an optional divisor for the resource quantity.
Specifies the name of the container whose resource value (e.g., CPU or memory limits/requests) is referenced by this resource field reference. Required for resource fields and must be a DNS_LABEL.

Divisor is the divisor for the resource field value, expressed as a Kubernetes quantity. It specifies the divisor to use when reporting the resource value, e.g., '1m' for milli-units. Defaults to '1'.
Specifies the container resource value to expose, such as requests.cpu, limits.memory, or requests.ephemeral-storage.

Represents an emptyDir volume, a temporary directory that is created when a Pod is assigned to a node and remains for the lifetime of the Pod. It is initially empty and can be used for inter-container communication or scratch space.
The storage medium backing the emptyDir volume. Empty string (default) uses the node's default disk storage; "Memory" uses a tmpfs (RAM-backed) filesystem.

The maximum storage limit for the emptyDir volume. Specify a quantity such as '1Gi' or '512Mi'. If not set, the storage is limited only by the underlying medium (default is the node's disk, or memory if medium is 'Memory').

Ephemeral defines a volume that is created on demand and deleted when the pod is removed. It uses a PersistentVolumeClaim template to provision the volume, and the volume's lifecycle is tied to the pod that uses it.
Defines a template for a PersistentVolumeClaim that backs this ephemeral volume. The claim is created when the pod is provisioned and deleted when the pod is removed.
Standard Kubernetes object metadata for the generated PersistentVolumeClaim, such as labels and annotations.

A map of string keys and values that can be used to store arbitrary non-identifying metadata on the volume claim template. Annotations are not used internally by Kubernetes and are intended for external tooling or for attaching metadata to objects.
The timestamp at which the object was created, in RFC3339 format (e.g., '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z'). This field is set by the server upon object creation and is typically read-only.
Optional duration in seconds before the persistent volume claim should be deleted. Value must be non-negative integer; zero means delete immediately. If nil, the default grace period is used.
The timestamp, in RFC 3339 format, at which the object was marked for deletion by Kubernetes. This field is set by the system only when a deletion request is in progress.

The list of finalizers for the object, which are strings that must be empty before the object can be deleted from the cluster. Finalizers are used to ensure cleanup of related resources or external systems before deletion.

generate_name is an optional prefix used by the API server to generate a unique name for the volume claim template metadata when the name field is not specified. The server appends a random suffix to the provided prefix to ensure uniqueness.
A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state for the volume claim template. Populated by the system and read-only.
Labels are key-value pairs attached to the metadata of the volume claim template. They can be used to organize and select the resulting PersistentVolumeClaim resources through label selectors.

A list of managed fields entries that track which controller, operator, or user manages the fields of this volume claim template metadata, including operation, API version, timestamp, and field ownership details.
API version of the managing client that last modified these fields, in the format group/version (e.g., apps/v1).
The type of the managed fields entry, used to discriminate the fields representation. In practice, this is typically 'FieldsV1'.

fields_v1 is a dynamic object that holds the set of fields managed by the manager, represented in the Kubernetes FieldsV1 JSON format. It contains the list of fields that this manager owns or operates on.
The name of the manager (e.g., a controller or user) that owns or last modified this field in Kubernetes managed fields.
The operation performed by the manager, such as 'Apply' or 'Update'.
The subresource that the management operation applied to, such as 'status' or 'scale'. Empty if the operation was on the resource itself.
Time is the timestamp of when the managed field entry was last updated, formatted as a string in RFC3339 (e.g., '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z').
The name used in the generated PersistentVolumeClaim. It serves as the base name for the PVC created for this ephemeral volume.
The namespace for the generated PersistentVolumeClaim. If omitted, the claim is created in the same namespace as the pod.
List of references to owning objects. If all owners are deleted, the object is garbage collected.
API version of the referent. For example, "v1" for core resources or "apps/v1" for apps groups.
If true, and if the owner has the 'foregroundDeletion' finalizer, the owner cannot be deleted from the key-value store until this reference is removed. Defaults to false.
Indicates whether the referenced owner is the managing controller for the owning object.
The kind (resource type) of the owning object, such as 'ReplicaSet' or 'Deployment'.
The name of the owner object referenced by this owner reference.
UID of the object that this owner reference refers to. This is a unique identifier of the owner object within the cluster.
The resource version of the volume claim template metadata, used by the Kubernetes API for optimistic concurrency control. It changes on every update to the resource.
The selfLink attribute is a read-only URL that identifies the resource and can be used to retrieve it. This field is deprecated and should not be relied upon.
UID is a system-generated unique identifier for this object, assigned by the Kubernetes API server and read-only.
Spec specifies the desired characteristics of the persistent volume claim created for this ephemeral volume, such as access modes, storage class, resources, and volume mode.
A list of access modes for the persistent volume claim. Valid values are ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteMany, and ReadWriteOncePod.

Specifies the source of the data to be populated into the volume claim. This can reference a VolumeSnapshot, a PersistentVolumeClaim, or (if the AnyVolumeDataSource feature gate is enabled) any custom resource.

The API group of the resource being referenced in the data source. For example, 'snapshot.storage.k8s.io' for a VolumeSnapshot. If not specified, the referenced resource is assumed to be in the core group.
The kind (type) of the referenced data source resource. When using an existing PersistentVolumeClaim as the data source, set this to 'PersistentVolumeClaim'.
Name of the data source resource (e.g., VolumeSnapshot or PersistentVolumeClaim) referenced by this volume claim template.
Specifies a data source reference for dynamically provisioning the volume, enabling features like volume cloning or snapshot restore. Contains apiGroup, kind, and name of the source object.
The API group of the resource referenced as the data source. If unspecified, the Kind is assumed to be in the core API group; required for non-core types.
The kind of the data source reference, indicating the Kubernetes resource type (e.g., 'PersistentVolumeClaim' or 'VolumeSnapshot').
The name of the data source object referenced by this volume claim template.
The namespace of the referenced data source object (e.g., VolumeSnapshot). If not set, the namespace of the volume claim is used.

Resource requirements for the ephemeral volume claim, such as storage requests and limits (e.g., requests.storage). Specified under the volume claim template's spec, matching the PersistentVolumeClaim resource requirements schema.
A map of resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) to their maximum allowed quantities, defining the upper bound of resources for the ephemeral volume claim.

A map of resource names to minimum required quantities, such as storage size (e.g., '1Gi'), for the ephemeral volume claim template. This defines the lower bound for resources allocated to the volume.
A label selector to filter persistent volumes for binding. It supports matchLabels and matchExpressions to specify volumes that satisfy the claim's requirements.

A list of label selector requirements for the volume claim template selector. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally values. All requirements are ANDed together.
The key of the label that the selector expression operates on. For example, in a matchExpressions item, the key specifies which Pod label the operator and values apply to.
The operator specifies the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a label selector match expression, used to select resources based on labels.

Values is an array of string values that correspond to the key and operator in a label selector requirement. For operators 'In' or 'NotIn', this array must contain at least one value; for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty.
A map of label keys and values used to define the selector for matching PersistentVolumes. The volume claim will be bound to a PersistentVolume that matches all specified labels.
The name of the StorageClass used for this ephemeral volume claim. If not specified, the default StorageClass is used.

The name of the VolumeAttributesClass to use when provisioning the volume. When specified, the volume will be created with the attributes defined in that class (e.g., for CSI volumes). This field is optional and is part of the PersistentVolumeClaimSpec used in the volumeClaimTemplate for ephemeral volumes.
Defines how the volume is formatted and used. Allowed values are 'Filesystem' (default) and 'Block'.
volume_name is the binding reference to a PersistentVolume. When set, the claim will bind to the PersistentVolume with the same name, bypassing dynamic provisioning or other binding logic.
Represents a Fibre Channel resource that is being attached to a node. This volume source is used to mount a Fibre Channel volume into the pod.
Filesystem type to be mounted on the Fibre Channel volume. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system (e.g., ext4, xfs, ntfs). If not specified, it defaults to ext4.
Logical unit number (LUN) of the Fibre Channel volume. This is a required field that identifies the target LUN for the volume.
Specifies whether the Fibre Channel volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; otherwise, it defaults to read-write.
List of target World Wide Names (WWNs) for the Fibre Channel volume. This field is required and must be specified together with lun.
wwids specifies a list of World Wide Identifiers (WWIDs) for the Fibre Channel volume, used to uniquely identify the volume instead of using targetWWNs and lun.
Represents a volume that is mounted using a FlexVolume plugin, an executable that implements the volume interface for a particular storage backend.
Driver is the name of the driver to use for this volume.
Filesystem type to mount for the flex volume, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'.
Optional: extra command options to pass to the FlexVolume driver.
Mounts the flexVolume as read-only if set to true. Defaults to false (read/write), and forces the ReadOnly setting in VolumeMounts.
A reference to a Secret that provides the flexVolume options. If specified, the Secret is passed to the flexVolume driver via the 'secret' field in the flexVolume options.
Name of the Kubernetes Secret to reference for the flexVolume. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
Represents a Flocker volume source, allowing a Flocker dataset to be mounted as a volume in the pod.
The name of the Flocker dataset to use for this volume.
The UUID of the Flocker dataset to be mounted. This is the unique identifier for the dataset in Flocker.

Configures a Google Compute Engine persistent disk volume source. Defines the disk name, filesystem type, partition, and read-only settings for mounting a pre-existing GCE Persistent Disk into the pod.
Filesystem type to mount on the GCE Persistent Disk, e.g., 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Defaults to 'ext4' if not specified.
The partition number on the GCE persistent disk to mount. If omitted, the entire disk is used.
pd_name is the unique name of the GCE Persistent Disk (PD) resource in Google Compute Engine. This name is used to identify the disk to be mounted into the container.
Whether the GCE persistent disk is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Configuration for a Git repository volume, which populates a volume with the contents of a Git repository. Typically specifies the repository URL, revision, and directory to clone.
Target directory for the git repo checkout. Must not start with '/' or contain '..'.
Repository is the URL of the Git repository to clone from into the volume. It must be a valid Git repository URL.
The commit hash to check out for the git repository. This corresponds to the `revision` field of the gitRepo volume source.

Represents a Glusterfs volume that will be mounted into the container. Specify the endpoints (the GlusterFS endpoints object name), path, and optionally readOnly (defaults to false) to define the volume source.
The endpoints name that identifies the GlusterFS cluster. This must be a valid Endpoints object in the same namespace, and it must contain at least one IP address.
Path to the GlusterFS volume (the volume path on the GlusterFS server).
Indicates whether the GlusterFS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Specifies a hostPath volume, which mounts a file or directory from the host node's filesystem into the pod. Useful for accessing node-level resources, but the pod becomes tied to the specific node.
Path of the directory or file on the host node. This is the location on the host that will be mounted into the pod.
Type of host path. Valid values are '', DirectoryOrCreate, Directory, FileOrCreate, File, Socket, CharDevice, and BlockDevice. An empty string means no type check is performed.
Image represents an image volume source, which mounts an OCI container image as a volume. It includes configuration such as the image reference and pull policy.

Specifies how to pull the image for an image volume source. Allowed values are Always, Never, or IfNotPresent; the default is IfNotPresent, except when the image reference uses the :latest tag, in which case the default is Always.
The image reference (e.g., 'my-registry/my-image:tag' or digest) that defines which container image to mount as a volume.
Configures an iSCSI volume for the pod, using an iSCSI target as the storage backend. Requires specifying the target portal, IQN, and LUN.
Specifies whether CHAP authentication is enabled for iSCSI discovery. Defaults to false.
Enable CHAP authentication for the iSCSI session.
Optional filesystem type to mount the iSCSI volume as, such as "ext4", "xfs", or "ntfs". Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system.
The iSCSI initiator name to use when connecting to the iSCSI target. If omitted, the default initiator name is used.
IQN (iSCSI Qualified Name) of the iSCSI target. Required.
The name of the iSCSI interface. Defaults to 'default' if not specified.
The iSCSI target LUN number. This is a required field for ISCSI volumes.
portals is the list of iSCSI portals to connect to, each in the form ip:port.
Indicates whether the iSCSI volume is mounted as read-only. When true, the volume is read-only.
secretRef is a reference to the secret containing CHAP authentication information for the iSCSI target.
The name of the Secret object that contains the authentication credentials for the iSCSI target.
The iSCSI target portal, either an IP address or IP:port if using a non-default port (typically TCP ports 860 and 3260).
The name of the volume. This name must be unique within the pod's spec and is used to reference the volume in container volumeMount definitions.
Defines a Network File System (NFS) volume source, allowing the pod to mount an NFS share from an NFS server.
The NFS export path on the NFS server. This is the directory that will be mounted into the pod.
Optional. Forces the NFS export to be mounted with read-only permissions. Defaults to false.
The hostname or IP address of the NFS server. This is a required field for NFS volumes.

Specifies a PersistentVolumeClaim as a volume source. The referenced PersistentVolumeClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod. This object includes fields such as claimName (the name of the PersistentVolumeClaim) and readOnly (whether the volume is mounted read-only).
Name of the PersistentVolumeClaim to use as the volume. This is required for a persistentVolumeClaim volume source and must reference a PVC in the same namespace as the pod.
Specifies whether the persistent volume claim volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Represents a Photon Controller persistent disk as a volume source in a Kubernetes pod specification. It contains settings such as the persistent disk ID and filesystem type to mount.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Ex. 'ext4', 'xfs'. Implicitly inferred to be 'ext4' if unspecified.
The unique identifier of the Photon persistent disk that this volume represents.
Portworx volume source that mounts a Portworx block volume. Used to attach a Portworx volume to a pod.
The filesystem type to be used when mounting the Portworx volume, such as ext4 or xfs.
Specifies whether the Portworx volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only and cannot be written to.
volume_id is the unique identifier of the existing Portworx volume to mount.
Projected configures a projected volume source that maps multiple existing volume sources into the same directory.
Optional permission mode for files in the projected volume. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 or decimal 0-511; defaults to 0644 if not set.

List of volume projections that make up the projected volume. Each source can be a ConfigMap, Secret, DownwardAPI, or ServiceAccountToken, and the volume is populated with data from all listed sources.

Configures a ClusterTrustBundle projection in the volume, providing the pod with a set of trust anchors from a designated signer. This source allows pods to consume cluster trust bundles via a projected volume.
LabelSelector filters the ClusterTrustBundles to project based on their labels. Only bundles matching the selector are included in the projected volume.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. All requirements are ANDed together; the selector matches when every requirement is satisfied.
The label key that this match expression applies to. For example, in a selector like 'app = myapp', the key is 'app'.

The operator to use for the label selector match expression. Allowed values are: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist. For example, 'In' matches label values in a set, 'Exists' matches if a label key exists.
values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty.

A map of key-value pairs used as label requirements. All listed labels must be present on the resource for the selector to match; the selector matches resources that have every specified key and value.
The name of the ClusterTrustBundle object to project into the volume.
optional indicates whether the ClusterTrustBundle can be omitted. If false, the ClusterTrustBundle must be present; if true, it may be absent.
The relative path of the file within the projected volume where the cluster trust bundle will be mounted. Defaults to 'bundle' if not set.
Selects ClusterTrustBundle objects by signer name. If empty, all cluster trust bundles are selected.
ConfigMap is a source type for a projected volume. This object defines how a ConfigMap's data is exposed within the projected volume.

List of key-to-path mappings for the ConfigMap. Use this to select specific keys and define the file paths they are mounted to in the projected volume; if omitted, all keys are projected with filenames equal to their key names.
The key to select from the ConfigMap.
Optional file permission mode (in octal, e.g., 0644) for the config map item, overriding the default permissions.
The relative path within the projected volume where the file from the config map key is mounted.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference for the projected volume source.

Optional indicates whether the referenced ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. If true, a missing ConfigMap or key will not cause the volume to fail, and the volume will be populated without that item.
Defines the Downward API source for a projected volume, allowing pod metadata such as labels, annotations, and resource limits to be exposed as files to containers.
List of downward API volume files. Each item specifies a path within the volume and a field reference or resource field reference to expose.
Selects a field of the pod to expose via the downward API volume. The object is an ObjectFieldSelector that specifies the apiVersion and fieldPath, e.g., metadata.name or spec.nodeName.
API version of the schema that fieldPath is written in terms of. Defaults to "v1".
The path to the desired field in the Pod's metadata or spec, such as metadata.name or spec.nodeName.
The file permission mode for the item, specified as an octal integer (e.g., 0644). If omitted, the volume's default mode is used.
The relative path within the projected volume where the downward API value is exposed. This is the destination path for the item.

A reference to a container resource field (such as requests.cpu or limits.memory) to be exposed via the downward API into the volume file. The value of the selected resource is written to the path specified in this item.
The name of the container for which the resource is requested. If not specified, this defaults to the container that defines the volume.
Divisor is optional and specifies the value to divide the resource value by when exposing it via the downward API. It must be a valid quantity (e.g., '1', '100m'), and defaults to 1 if omitted.
The name of the resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
The mount path within the projected volume where the certificate chain from the pod certificate source is exposed.
Specifies the relative path within the projected volume where the pod certificate bundle will be exposed.
Specifies the path within the volume where the pod certificate's private key is mounted.
Specifies the type of key used to generate the certificate. Must be one of 'RSA' or 'ECDSA'.
The maximum duration, in seconds, for which the pod certificate remains valid. This value caps the expiration of the certificate that is projected into the volume.

The name of the certificate signer that will issue the pod certificate. This must correspond to a signer configured in the cluster, and it determines the CA and certificate chain used for the projected certificate.
The user ID (UID) that owns the file created from the projected pod certificate.
Projected source that references a Kubernetes Secret. It configures the Secret name, optional items to expose, and default file permissions within the projected volume.
A list of key-to-path mappings for the secret data. Each item specifies a key in the secret and the path (and optionally mode) to expose it as a file in the projected volume.
The key within the referenced Secret's data to expose as a file in the projected volume. This corresponds to the key in the Secret's data map.
Optional Unix file permission mode (e.g., 0644) for the secret key's file when projected into the volume.
The relative file path within the projected volume where the secret key is written. It must be a relative path, and cannot start with '/' or contain '..' segments.
Name of the Secret to project into the volume.

Specifies whether the referenced Secret or its keys must be defined. When true, a missing Secret or missing keys will not cause the volume to fail; when false or unset, the Secret must exist and contain the referenced keys.

serviceAccountToken is a projected volume source that injects a service account token into the volume. It allows configuration of audience, expirationSeconds, and path for the token, enabling pods to authenticate to the Kubernetes API.
The audience for the projected service account token. It defines the intended recipients of the token. If not specified, the token audience defaults to the API server's identifier.
Specifies the lifetime in seconds for the projected service account token. Once this time elapses, the token expires and is no longer valid.
The relative path to the service account token file within the projected volume. This is the path where the token will be mounted.
Quobyte represents a Quobyte mount on the host that shares the pod's lifetime. It is a volume source used to mount a Quobyte volume into the pod.
Group name to map volume access to for the Quobyte volume. Defaults to no group if not specified.
Specifies whether the Quobyte volume should be mounted as read-only. If true, the volume is mounted with read-only permissions.
The Quobyte registry to connect to. This is a comma-separated list of host:port pairs (e.g., 'host1:port,host2:port') specifying the registries that manage the volume.
The tenant name for the Quobyte volume. This optional field specifies the tenant within the Quobyte storage system.
User to map volume access to. Defaults to root.
The name of the Quobyte volume to mount. This is a required field for the Quobyte volume source.
RBD (Rados Block Device) volume source configuration for mounting a Ceph block device into the pod.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Defaults to ext4.
The name of the RBD image to mount.
The path to the keyring file used for the RBD user. If not specified, defaults to /etc/ceph/keyring.
List of Ceph monitor endpoints (host and port) for the RBD volume, e.g., "192.168.0.1:6789".
The name of the Ceph pool in which the RBD image resides. If not specified, the default pool 'rbd' is used.
Indicates whether the RBD volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
The secret containing the Ceph authentication key. The secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the secret in the pod's namespace that holds the authentication key for the RBD volume.
The Ceph RBD user name used for authentication. Defaults to 'admin'.
ScaleIO volume source, used to mount a ScaleIO storage volume into a pod.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Ex. "ext4", "xfs". Default is "ext4".
The host address of the ScaleIO API Gateway.
The name of the ScaleIO Protection Domain for the configured storage. This identifies the protection domain that contains the storage pool used by this volume.
Specifies whether the ScaleIO volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
secretRef is a reference to a Secret resource that contains the ScaleIO storage system credentials (e.g., username and password). The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that provides the ScaleIO credentials. This secret must exist in the same namespace and contain the username and password for the ScaleIO admin user.
Enable or disable SSL for communication with the ScaleIO API gateway.
Storage mode of the ScaleIO volume, either 'ThickProvisioned' or 'ThinProvisioned'. Defaults to 'ThinProvisioned'.
The ScaleIO storage pool from which the volume is provisioned. This is a required field when using ScaleIO volumes.
The name of the ScaleIO storage system.
The name of the ScaleIO volume to use as the backing store for this volume source.
Defines a volume backed by a Kubernetes Secret, allowing secret data to be exposed to containers as files.
The default permission mode for files in the secret volume, specified in octal (e.g., 0644).

Specifies which secret keys to expose and the paths they map to within the volume. Each item contains a 'key' (the secret key) and a 'path' (the relative file path), and optionally 'mode' for file permissions.
The key name within the Secret's data map that should be exposed as a file in the volume. This key must exist in the referenced Secret.

Mode bits used to set permissions on this secret file. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 or a decimal value between 0 and 511. JSON requires decimal. If omitted, the volume's defaultMode is used.
The relative path within the volume where the secret item will be mounted. If not specified, the key name is used as the path.
Specifies whether the secret or its keys must be defined. If true, the secret does not need to exist; if false or unset, the secret must exist.
Name of the Secret resource in the pod's namespace to mount as a volume.
Represents a StorageOS volume to be mounted into the pod. This allows the pod to use storage provisioned by a StorageOS cluster, with configuration options such as volumeName, namespace, and fsType.
Filesystem type to mount for the StorageOS volume, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. Must be supported by the host operating system; defaults to ext4 if unspecified.
Determines whether the StorageOS volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; defaults to false.
Reference to a Secret that contains credentials for accessing the StorageOS volume. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
Name of the secret object that contains the StorageOS API credentials. The secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the StorageOS volume to mount. This must match the human-readable name of an existing StorageOS volume.
The StorageOS volume namespace. If not set, the Kubernetes pod's namespace is used as the default.
Represents a vSphere volume source. This is used to attach a vSphere volume, which is created and managed by vSphere, to the pod.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host. Defaults to "ext4".
The vSphere Storage Policy ID applied to the volume. If omitted, the default storage policy is used.
The name of the storage policy to use for the vSphere volume.
Path that identifies the vSphere volume. This is typically the datastore path to the vmdk file and is required.

kubernetes_apps_replica_set.status.condi.text: The last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This is a string in RFC3339 format, e.g., '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z'.
A human-readable message providing details about the condition, such as the reason for the current status.
A machine-readable reason for the condition's last transition, typically a short CamelCase token indicating the cause (e.g., 'MinimumReplicasAvailable').
The status of the condition, indicating whether the condition is True, False, or Unknown.
The type of the ReplicaSet condition. The only recognized value is 'ReplicaFailure'.

kubernetes_apps_stateful_set.metadata.ma.text: The version of the Kubernetes API that the manager used to apply the fields, e.g., 'apps/v1'.
The type of the managed fields entry. In Kubernetes, this is always "FieldsV1", indicating the fields are represented using the FieldsV1 format.
A JSON representation of the fields managed by this entry, used by Kubernetes for tracking field ownership in server-side apply.
The name of the manager (e.g., a controller, user, or tool) that last applied changes to this resource, as tracked in the managedFields entry.
The type of operation that created this managed field entry. Valid values are 'Apply' and 'Update', indicating whether the field was set via an apply or an update request.
The subresource this managed field entry applies to, such as 'status'. An empty string indicates the main resource.

Indicates whether the owner reference prevents the object from being deleted until the owner is deleted. If true, the object will be blocked from deletion until the owner is removed, ensuring the owner is deleted first.

Kind of the referenced owner object (e.g., StatefulSet, Deployment).

The list of values that the label selector key must match when the operator is In or NotIn. This field must be empty when the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist.

The type of the fields object in this managed fields entry. Typically 'FieldsV1', indicating that the fields are represented as a Kubernetes FieldsV1 structure.

The managed fields for this manager, stored as a JSON object using Kubernetes FieldsV1 encoding (e.g., keys prefixed with 'f:' for fields and 'k:' for map keys). It represents the exact set of fields owned by the manager at the time of the last operation.
Name of the component (e.g., kubectl, kube-controller-manager) that manages the fields recorded in this entry. It identifies the manager that last modified the field.
The operation performed by the manager that last modified this managed field entry. Valid values are 'Apply', 'Update', and 'Delete'.
Subresource indicates which subresource of the StatefulSet the managed fields apply to. It is an empty string for the main resource, or a subresource name such as 'status' or 'scale'.
Time is the timestamp of when the managed field entry was recorded, in RFC3339 format (e.g., 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z).
The apiVersion of the owner resource (e.g., 'apps/v1') that this owner reference points to. It identifies the API group and version of the referenced object.
If true, and the owner has the 'foregroundDeletion' finalizer, the owner cannot be deleted from the key-value store until this reference is removed. Defaults to false.
Indicates whether the referenced object is the managing controller of the resource. When true, the owner reference points to the controller that manages the resource.
The kind of the referenced owner resource, such as 'ReplicaSet' or 'StatefulSet'.
The name of the owner object to which this resource belongs.
UID of the owner object referenced by this owner reference.
The node selector term that defines the preferred node selection constraints. It contains matchExpressions and matchFields requirements for matching nodes.
A list of node selector requirements by node's labels. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and set of values that a node's labels must match.
The key (label name) on the node that the match expression evaluates. For example, 'kubernetes.io/hostname' or 'topology.kubernetes.io/zone'.

The operator represents the relationship between the key and the values in the match expression. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. In and NotIn require an array of string values, Exists and DoesNotExist do not require values, and Gt and Lt require a single numeric value for the key.

List of values that the node label must match, as defined by the corresponding operator in the same match expression. For In and NotIn operators, this list defines the allowed or disallowed values; for Exists and DoesNotExist, it must be empty.

A list of node selector requirements based on node fields. Each requirement specifies a field key, operator, and values, allowing the node preference to match nodes on field values such as metadata.name.
The key of the node label that the match condition applies to. This is the label key that must match the specified operator and values on the node.
The operator specifies the relationship between the node field key and the values in the match expression. Valid values include In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.

The list of values that the field (specified by 'key') must match for the node affinity matchFields expression. Operators like In and NotIn require this list, while Exists and DoesNotExist expect it to be empty.

Weight associated with the corresponding node selector term, ranging from 1 to 100. The scheduler adds this weight to the sum of weights of node selectors that match the node, to determine preference.

A list of node selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a label key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt), and an optional list of values. All requirements within the term are ANDed together.
The label key that the match expression applies to. This is the key of a node label that the affinity requirement targets, such as 'kubernetes.io/hostname' or a custom label.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values used with the operator to match node labels. For 'In' and 'NotIn' operators, the values must be non-empty; for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', the values must be empty.
A list of node selector requirements that match against node fields (e.g., metadata.name). This allows the node affinity to select nodes based on field values, as opposed to labels.
The key of the node field to match against in the node selector term. For match_fields, this must be a valid Kubernetes field path, such as 'metadata.name'.
Operator represents the relationship between the field value and the values in the values field. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt (for numeric comparisons).
The list of values for the node selector requirement. Used with the operator to match node fields, e.g., for In or NotIn operators.
Represents a pod affinity term defining a set of pods and a topology key, used in a preferred scheduling rule.

Label selector used to identify the group of pods to which the affinity or anti-affinity rule applies. It selects matching pods based on their labels, as defined by the Kubernetes LabelSelector object.
A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and optionally a set of values. All requirements are ANDed together to form the full label selector.
The label key to match against in the selector expression. It identifies the label key whose value the operator checks.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and the set of values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values used by the label selector expression. Required when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'; must be empty when the operator is 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist'.
A map of label keys and values that must match the labels on the target pod for this affinity preference to apply. The requirements are ANDed; each key must be present with the specified value.

A list of pod label keys used to build a label selector for the pod affinity term. The values of these keys from the pod's own labels are extracted and used to match candidate pods in the topology domain.
A list of label keys. For each key, if the incoming pod has a label with that key, the target (node or pod) must not have the same label key and value for the affinity term to be satisfied.
A label selector that identifies the namespaces to which the affinity/anti-affinity term applies. When not set, the pod's own namespace is used.
A list of label selector requirements that are ANDed together to select namespaces. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values that must match.
The label key that the selector applies to.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and a set of values in a label selector requirement. Allowed values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'.
A list of string values that the match expression evaluates against. For the In and NotIn operators, this list must be non-empty; for Exists and DoesNotExist, it must be empty.
A map of key-value pairs used to select namespaces. All key-value pairs are ANDed together; each pair is equivalent to a matchExpressions element with operator In and the given value.
Specifies the list of namespaces to consider for this pod affinity term. If empty, the namespace of the pod where the affinity rule is defined is used.

The key of the node label used to define topology domains for pod affinity/anti-affinity. Nodes with the same label value are considered in the same domain, and this key is required for affinity terms.
Weight of the affinity term, used to compute the sum of weights for preferred pod affinity. Must be an integer between 1 and 100.

A label query over a set of pods. The pods matching this selector are used to determine the group for the required pod affinity rule. It supports matchLabels and matchExpressions to define the selection criteria.

A list of label selector requirements. Each item defines a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values. The requirements are ANDed together with matchLabels to form the full selector.
The label key that the selector requirement applies to, such as 'app' or 'tier'.
The operator for a label selector requirement. In Kubernetes, it must be one of 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', or 'DoesNotExist'.
A list of values that the label key must match. Used with the In and NotIn operators; for Exists and DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.

A list of label keys whose values on the existing pod must differ from the values on the incoming (scheduled) pod for the affinity term to match. Pods with identical values for any of these keys are excluded, which helps ignore transient labels (such as pod-template-hash) during rolling updates.

NamespaceSelector is a label selector used to filter the namespaces from which matching pods are considered for the affinity rule. It works alongside the pod affinity selector to restrict the search to specific namespaces.

A list of label selector requirements that are ANDed together. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a set of values; the namespace selector matches namespaces based on these expressions.
The label key that the selector matches against. The expression applies to namespaces that have this key in their labels.
Operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

Values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty. This field is used in a namespace selector match expression for pod affinity.

match_labels is a map of label keys and values used to select namespaces. The namespace selector uses these labels to match namespaces for pod affinity/anti-affinity rules. If multiple labels are specified, all must match.
Specifies the list of namespaces to which the label selector applies. If omitted, it defaults to the namespace of the pod where the affinity term is defined.

The topology key, typically a node label such as 'kubernetes.io/hostname' or 'failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone', that defines the domain over which the scheduler must distribute pods to satisfy the required pod affinity rule.

The pod affinity term defines the anti-affinity rule for this preferred scheduling term. It contains a label selector that identifies the set of pods to avoid, and a topology key that determines the domain for enforcement.
Label selector used to identify the pods that this affinity/anti-affinity term applies to. It can specify matchLabels and matchExpressions to define the selection criteria.
A list of label selector requirements that are ANDed. Each requirement is an object with `key`, `operator`, and `values` fields, where `operator` can be `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, or `DoesNotExist`.

The label key that the match expression applies to. In a Kubernetes label selector, expressions consist of a key, an operator, and values; this field specifies the label key to match against for pod anti-affinity.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a label selector requirement. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values for the label selector match expression. Required for operators 'In' and 'NotIn' (must be non-empty), and must be empty for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist'.
A map of label keys to values used to select pods. A pod must have all the specified label key-value pairs to be considered a match for this label selector.

MatchLabelKeys is a set of label keys that, when present on the pod being scheduled, restrict the set of pods considered for affinity/anti-affinity to those with the same label value for these keys. This allows expressing more specific matching requirements.
Specifies a set of pod label keys. For each key listed, the value from the pod being scheduled is used to exclude pods that have the same key-value pair from this affinity term's selection.

A label query over the set of namespaces to which the pod affinity term applies. The term is applied to the union of the namespaces selected by this field and the ones listed in the 'namespaces' field. A null selector or a null/empty namespaces list means 'this pod's namespace'; an empty selector ({}) matches all namespaces.
A list of label selector requirements used to match namespaces. Each requirement consists of a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values.
The label key that this match expression applies to. It must match a label on the namespace for the selector to match.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.
Values is the list of values for the key in the match expression. For operators In and NotIn, this list must be non-empty; for Exists and DoesNotExist, it must be empty.

A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels on the namespace for the pod anti-affinity term to be considered. This corresponds to the matchLabels field of a Kubernetes label selector, used here to select namespaces.

Specifies the namespaces from which the pod label selector matches pods. If omitted, the rule applies only to the namespace of the pod that defines this affinity term, restricting the scope of the pod anti-affinity rule.
The node label key that defines the topology domain for this anti-affinity term, determining how pods are spread across nodes.

Weight associated with the corresponding pod anti-affinity preference. Must be an integer from 1 to 100. The weight of each matching preference is summed to compute the overall node score for scheduling.

LabelSelector is a query over labels on pods that the anti-affinity rule applies to. The result of matchLabels and matchExpressions are ANDed. An empty label selector matches all objects, while a null label selector matches no objects.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional set of values, used to select pods by labels for the pod anti-affinity rule.
The label key that this match expression applies to. In Kubernetes label selectors, the key is the name of the label, such as 'app' or 'tier'.
The operator represents the key's relationship to a set of values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values. For operators In or NotIn, this array must be non-empty; for Exists or DoesNotExist, it must be empty. Each value must be a valid Kubernetes label value.

match_labels is a map of key-value pairs that must match the labels of a pod to be selected. A single {key, value} in the map is equivalent to a matchExpressions requirement with key, operator In, and values [value]; all requirements are ANDed together.

List of label keys that must match between the incoming pod and existing pods considered for anti-affinity. The scheduler uses these keys to compare the labels of the new pod with those of existing pods, in addition to the label selector, to determine which pods are relevant for scheduling constraints.

A list of label keys. When evaluating pod anti-affinity, only pods that have a different value for each of these keys compared to the incoming pod are considered matching. This makes the anti-affinity rule more selective by excluding pods with identical label values.

A label selector that identifies the namespaces from which pods are considered for this anti-affinity rule. If set, only pods running in namespaces matching this selector are eligible to satisfy or conflict with the affinity term.

A list of label selector requirements for matching namespaces. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. This selector is used to choose namespaces whose labels satisfy the expression for pod anti-affinity scheduling.
The label key that the selector uses to match namespace labels in the namespace selector.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and a set of values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values that the key must match when the operator is In or NotIn. For other operators (Exists, DoesNotExist), this field must be empty.

A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels on a namespace for the anti-affinity rule to apply. This selector identifies namespaces whose pods are considered when enforcing the required pod anti-affinity constraint.
A list of namespaces to which the label selector applies. If not specified, defaults to the namespace of the pod.

The key of node labels that defines the topology domain for pod anti-affinity. Pods will be spread across distinct topology domains, such as kubernetes.io/hostname or failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone.
Arguments to the container's entrypoint. These override the default args in the container image and are passed directly to the command.
The command to run in the container, which overrides the image's entrypoint. This is an array of strings.
List of environment variables to set in the container. Each entry defines a variable name and optionally a value or value source (e.g., config map, secret, or field reference).
The name of the environment variable. Must be a C_IDENTIFIER.
The value of the environment variable. This is a direct string value; if not set, use valueFrom to source the value from a reference. The value defaults to an empty string.
Specifies a source for the environment variable's value, such as a ConfigMap key, Secret key, pod field, or resource field. Exactly one of these sources must be defined.

Selects a key from a ConfigMap to populate the environment variable. The object should specify the ConfigMap name, the key within it, and whether the key is optional; if the ConfigMap or key does not exist and optional is false, the pod will not start.
The key to select from the ConfigMap.
Name of the ConfigMap to select the key from.
Specifies whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If set to true, the container starts even if the referenced ConfigMap or key does not exist.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, status.podIP) whose value is used for the environment variable. The field_ref object must specify the pod field path via its 'fieldPath' attribute.
The version of the schema the fieldPath is written in terms of, defaults to 'v1'.
The path to the pod field to use as the value, such as metadata.name, metadata.namespace, or status.podIP.
The key within the referenced file (typically a ConfigMap or Secret) that identifies the specific value to use for the environment variable.
Specifies whether the referenced key is required to exist. When true, the container will start even if the key is missing; when false (default), the key must exist or the container will not start.
The name of the volume from which the referenced file (key) is read to set the environment variable's value. This volume must be defined in the pod spec.

Selects a resource field of the container, such as limits.cpu or requests.memory, to use as the value of the environment variable. This is part of the valueFrom source in the container's environment variable definition.
The name of the container to select the resource field from. If not specified, defaults to the container where the environment variable is defined.
The divisor to divide the resource value by, expressed as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1m' for milli units). This is optional; if not specified, the default divisor is 1.
The resource name to select from the container's resources, e.g., `limits.cpu` or `requests.memory`. This field specifies which resource value to expose as the environment variable.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. The environment variable's value is set to the value of the specified secret key.
The key within the referenced Secret that should be used as the value for the environment variable. This key must exist in the specified Secret.
The name of the Secret to select from.

Specifies whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If true, the environment variable is set to an empty string when the Secret or key is missing; if false, a missing Secret or key causes an error.
List of sources to populate environment variables in the container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret, optionally with a prefix to prepend to variable names.

Reference to a ConfigMap to populate environment variables from. The referenced ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod, and each key in the ConfigMap becomes an environment variable in the container.
The name of the ConfigMap to use for populating environment variables in the container.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If set to true, the ConfigMap may be absent; otherwise, the container fails to start if the ConfigMap does not exist.

An optional prefix that is prepended to each key from the ConfigMap or Secret when defining environment variables. For example, if prefix is "FOO_" and the source contains key "bar", the resulting environment variable is "FOO_bar".

Reference to a Kubernetes Secret whose keys and values are added as environment variables to the container. The Secret name is specified in the 'name' field, and the 'optional' field can be set to true to allow the Secret to be absent.
The name of the Secret to use for populating environment variables. Must reference a Secret in the same namespace.
Whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If set to true, the Secret may not exist without causing an error.
The container image to run, specified as a name and tag or digest, e.g., 'nginx:1.25'.

Specifies the image pull policy for the container. Valid values are Always, Never, and IfNotPresent. If unset, Kubernetes defaults to Always when the image tag is :latest or absent, otherwise IfNotPresent.
Lifecycle hooks for the container, allowing management of actions during the container lifecycle, such as postStart and preStop events.
The postStart lifecycle hook is executed immediately after a container is created. This block contains the action to be taken, such as an exec command or HTTP GET request.
