Exec specifies an exec action to be performed after the container starts. This is one of the handlers for the postStart lifecycle hook, defining a command to run inside the container.
The command to run when the postStart lifecycle hook is executed. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the command and the remaining elements are arguments.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the postStart lifecycle hook. This defines an HTTPGetAction, including the target host, port, and path for the request.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Custom headers to include in the HTTP GET request for this post-start lifecycle hook. Each item in the list defines a header with `name` and `value` fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request to the lifecycle post-start probe.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent in the postStart lifecycle HTTP GET request.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.

The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME of a port defined in the container's ports. Used for the HTTP GET request in the postStart lifecycle hook.
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URL scheme (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to HTTP if not specified.
Sleep represents the sleep action for the lifecycle hook, allowing the container to sleep for a specified duration as part of the postStart lifecycle phase.
The number of seconds the container will sleep after starting. This field specifies the duration of the sleep action in the Kubernetes lifecycle postStart hook.
Defines a TCP socket handler for the postStart lifecycle hook. It specifies a host and port to attempt a TCP connection to; the hook is considered successful if the connection succeeds.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, defaults to the pod's IP address.
The TCP port number or named port (IANA_SVC_NAME) to which the lifecycle postStart hook connects. The value must be a valid port number between 1 and 65535 or a recognized service name.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that is invoked immediately before a container is terminated. It can be used to perform graceful shutdown actions, such as running a command or sending an HTTP GET request, and is configured as an object with exec or httpGet fields.
Exec specifies the command to run in the container when the pre-stop lifecycle hook is triggered, allowing the container to perform cleanup before termination.

The command to execute as part of the preStop lifecycle handler. This is a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments, providing the executable and its parameters to run in the container before termination.
HTTPGet specifies the HTTP GET request to perform in the preStop lifecycle hook. It allows executing an action via an HTTP request before the container is terminated.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. You may set 'Host' header in httpHeaders instead.
A list of HTTP headers to send with the GET request. Each header is an object with `name` and `value` fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the preStop HTTP GET request. This is the header key, as defined in the Kubernetes HTTPHeader schema.
The value associated with the header name. This is sent as part of the HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server; defaults to '/' if not specified.
Port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or an IANA service name.
Specifies the network protocol (scheme) for the HTTP GET request, such as HTTP or HTTPS. If omitted, the default is HTTP.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.

Sleep action for a preStop lifecycle hook. It delays container termination by pausing for a specified duration (defined in the nested 'seconds' field), allowing the application to gracefully shut down before receiving SIGTERM.
The number of seconds the container should sleep before being terminated as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook.
Specifies a TCP socket to which the kubelet connects to trigger the preStop hook, used to perform actions before the container is terminated.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to on the container. This can be a numeric port number (1-65535) or the name of an existing container port.
The signal to send to the container when it is being stopped, such as SIGTERM.

Liveness probe for the container. Specifies how to determine if the container is healthy and running. If the probe fails, the kubelet kills the container and restarts it according to the pod's restart policy.
Exec defines the command to execute inside the container as a liveness probe. The container is considered healthy if the command exits with status 0.

The command to run for the exec liveness probe. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly without a shell; a zero exit status indicates healthy.
The number of consecutive failures required to consider the liveness probe failed. The minimum value is 1; the default is 3 if not specified.
Defines a gRPC health check used by the liveness probe, including the port to connect to and optional service name.
The port number on which the gRPC server is running for health checks. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.

The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest (see https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/health-checking.md). If this is not specified, the default behavior is defined by gRPC.
Performs an HTTP GET request against the container's IP address on a specified port and path, used to determine container health.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Custom headers to include in the HTTP GET request for the liveness probe. Each item is an object with `name` and `value` keys.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the liveness probe request.
Path to access on the HTTP server.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET liveness probe. This can be an integer port number or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol used for the HTTP GET request in the liveness probe. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS', with 'HTTP' as the default.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
The number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
Number of seconds between liveness probe executions. The default is 10, and the minimum is 1.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the liveness probe to be considered successful after having failed. For liveness probes, this value must be 1.
Specifies a TCP socket check for the liveness probe. Configures the port (and optionally host) that the kubelet connects to for the probe.
The hostname or IP address to probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod's IP address.
The TCP port to check for the liveness probe. Can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container.
The duration in seconds that the pod needs to terminate gracefully. Must be a non-negative integer; defaults to 30 seconds if not specified.
Number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.
The name of the container. This must be unique within the pod and is used to identify the container in logs, exec, and other Kubernetes operations.
Specifies the list of network ports that the container exposes. Each entry defines a port number, protocol, and optionally a name.
The port number on which the container listens and is exposed.
The host IP address to bind the host port to. When hostPort is specified, this restricts the host interface on which the port is exposed; if omitted, the port binds to all host interfaces.
The port on the host node to which the container's port is mapped. If specified, it must be a valid port number (1-65535).
Optional port name. Must be an IANA_SVC_NAME and unique among all named ports in the pod.
The IP protocol used for this container port. Valid values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP. This field defaults to TCP.

Defines a probe that determines when the container is ready to accept traffic. The readiness probe is used to decide whether the container's endpoints should be added to the service load balancers, and traffic is only routed to the pod when this probe succeeds.
Exec specifies the action to take in the container. It runs a command inside the container; a zero exit status indicates success.
The command to run inside the container for the exec readiness probe. This is executed directly by the container runtime, not via a shell, so shell syntax is not supported.
The number of consecutive failures of the probe before the container is considered not ready. Must be a positive integer. Defaults to 3.
Configures a gRPC health check for the readiness probe. The container must implement the gRPC health checking protocol; the probe targets the specified port and optionally a named service.
The port number on which the container's gRPC server is listening for the readiness probe. This must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the gRPC service to check in the health probe. If not specified, the default behavior is to check the overall server status.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform as the readiness probe. The probe sends an HTTP GET request to the container's IP address and port; a response status code of 200-399 indicates success.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP request. Each item in the list defines a header name and value to include when performing the GET request.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the readiness probe request. For example, 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the readiness probe request.
Path to access on the HTTP server.
The TCP port to send the HTTP request to. Can be a port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports list.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated.
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 10.

The number of consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after it has failed. Must be an integer, with a minimum of 1. For readiness probes, this value must be 1 (the default).
Configures a TCP socket check for the readiness probe. The probe succeeds if a TCP connection to the specified port (and optionally host) is successfully established.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod's IP address.
The TCP port to probe for readiness. Can be a numeric port or a named port from the container's definition.

Optional duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully after the readiness probe fails. If unset, the pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds value is used; set to 0 for immediate termination.
Number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. Must be a positive integer. Defaults to 1.

List of resource resize policies for the container. Each policy specifies a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and a restart policy (NotRequired or RestartContainer) that determines how the container is restarted when the resource is resized.
The name of the resource (e.g., 'cpu' or 'memory') to which this resize policy applies.
Defines whether the container must be restarted when a resize operation is applied to the specified resource. Allowed values are 'NotRequired' or 'RestartContainer'.
Resource requirements for this container, specifying the requested and maximum amounts of compute resources (e.g., CPU, memory) as defined by the Kubernetes API.
Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this container. This is an alpha feature and may change in the future.
The name of the ResourceClaim that this container references. The named ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Request is the name of the resource claim that this container requests. The claim must be defined in the same namespace as the pod.

Limits specifies the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the container. Each key is a resource name such as 'cpu' or 'memory', and the value is a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., '1', '2Gi') representing the maximum amount of that resource.

A map of resource names (e.g., 'cpu', 'memory') to the minimum amount of resources that the container is guaranteed to receive. These values are used for scheduling decisions and are enforced as requests by the container runtime.
The list of container exit codes for which this restart policy rule applies. Each entry is an integer representing a process exit status (e.g., 1, 137).
SecurityContext defines the security options for the container, including user/group IDs, Linux capabilities, SELinux options, and read-only root filesystem settings.

AllowPrivilegeEscalation controls whether a process is allowed to gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, the container runs with the no_new_privs flag, preventing privilege escalation via setuid or setgid binaries.

Defines the AppArmor profile for the container. The object has a required 'type' field (allowed values: LocalHost, RuntimeDefault, Unconfined) and an optional 'localhostProfile' field that specifies the profile name when type is LocalHost.
The name of an AppArmor profile that is already loaded on the node, used when the AppArmor profile type is set to Localhost.
The type of AppArmor profile to apply to the container. Valid values are RuntimeDefault, Localhost, and Unconfined.
Linux capabilities to add or drop for the container. This field allows adjusting the default set of capabilities granted to the container's processes.
List of Linux capabilities to add to the container's default capability set.
List of Linux capabilities to remove from the container's default capability set. Entries may include 'ALL' to drop all capabilities or specific capability names like 'NET_RAW'.
Determines whether the container runs in privileged mode. If true, the container has full access to the host's resources and devices, essentially running with root-like privileges on the host.

proc_mount specifies the proc mount mode for the container's /proc filesystem. It can be set to 'Default' (the standard masked /proc) or 'Unmasked' to expose the full host /proc, which may be necessary for privileged system operations but carries security risks.
When set to true, the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only, preventing writes to it.
The GID (group ID) to run the container's entrypoint process with. This overrides the group specified in the container image.

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0, and will refuse to start the container if it does.

Sets the numeric user ID (UID) used to run the container's entrypoint process, overriding the image's default user. Typically a positive integer, it helps enforce non-root execution or specific user privileges.
SELinux options for the container. This field defines the SELinux context used when the container is started, including settings such as user, role, type, and level.
The SELinux level (MLS) that applies to the container, as defined in the SELinuxOptions for the container's security context.
The SELinux role label for the container.
The SELinux type label to apply to the container. This is part of the SELinux context (user, role, type, level) and specifies the type enforcement type for the container's processes.
The SELinux user label that applies to the container. This is part of the SELinux context.
Configures the seccomp profile for the container. It specifies the seccomp profile type (RuntimeDefault, Localhost, or Unconfined) and optionally the path to a custom profile when type is Localhost.
Path to a seccomp profile on the node, used when the seccomp type is 'Localhost'.
The seccomp profile type, which must be one of Unconfined, RuntimeDefault, or Localhost. If set to Localhost, the localhostProfile field must be specified.
Windows-specific security options for the container. This object allows configuring settings such as GMSA credential specs and the Windows user name when the container runs on Windows nodes.

The GMSA credential spec to use for the container. This is a JSON string that specifies the Group Managed Service Account (GMSA) configuration, allowing the container to run with a specific GMSA identity.
The name of the GMSA (Group Managed Service Account) credential spec to use for the container. This references a pre-configured GMSA credential spec by name.

HostProcess determines whether the container should be run as a HostProcess container on Windows. When set to true, the container has special access to the host and can run in the host's process namespace.
Specifies the Windows username (in the form 'User' or 'DOMAIN\User') that the container's entrypoint process will run as. If unspecified, defaults to the user specified in the image metadata.

startup_probe defines a probe that checks whether the application within the container has started. When configured, other probes are not executed until the startup probe succeeds, allowing for applications that take a long time to initialize.
Defines a probe action that executes a specified command inside the container. A zero exit code indicates the startup probe is successful; any non-zero exit code indicates failure.

Command to run inside the container to perform the probe. The command is executed directly by the container runtime; it is not run through a shell, so shell features like variable expansion are not available.
The number of consecutive failures of the startup probe that must occur before the container is considered failed and restarted. The default value is 3.

Specifies a gRPC-based probe action for the container probe. It requires a port number and optionally a service name; if no service is specified, the check targets the gRPC server's default health service.
The network port number that the gRPC probe will connect to for the health check.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not set, the default is "" (empty string).
Defines an HTTP GET request to be performed against the container as part of the startup probe. Includes options for the request path, port, host, scheme, and custom headers.
The hostname to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. Defaults to the pod IP; to set the Host header, use the httpHeaders field instead.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request used for the startup probe. Each item in the list is an object with `name` and `value` fields specifying the header to send.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the startup probe request.
The value of the HTTP header. This is the value corresponding to the header name specified in the 'name' field of the HTTP header entry.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to /.
The port number or name of the port on the container to access for the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid TCP port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request: either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated.
The number of seconds between each startup probe execution.
Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1 and must be 1 for startup probes.
Specifies a TCP socket check for the startup probe. The probe attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the container.
Host name or IP address to connect to. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to. Accepts a numeric port number or an IANA port name (e.g., 'http' or '80').

Optional duration in seconds for the pod to terminate gracefully after the startup probe fails. Overrides the pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds; if unset, the pod's termination grace period is used. Must be a non-negative integer.
Number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. Defaults to 1 second, minimum value is 1.
Whether this container should allocate a buffer for stdin in the container runtime. If not set, reads from stdin in the container will always result in EOF. Defaults to false.

If true, the container's standard input is opened only once for the first attach session and then closed after that session detaches, rather than remaining open for multiple attaches. Defaults to false.
Specifies the path of a file where the container's termination message is written. The kubelet reads this file to retrieve the message when the container exits. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Defines how the container's termination message is read. Allowed values are 'File' (default) to read from /dev/termination-log, or 'FallbackToLogsOnError' to fall back to container logs when the file is empty and the container exits with an error.
Whether to allocate a pseudo-TTY for the container. When true, the container gets a terminal device.
List of volume devices (block devices) to be used by the container. Each device specifies a volume name and the path inside the container where the device is mounted.
The path inside the container where the device will be mounted.
The name of the volume device, which must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
List of volume mounts for the container. Each mount defines a volume name, a mount path, and optional properties like read-only and subPath.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must not contain ':'.

Determines how volume mounts propagate from the host to the container and between containers. Allowed values are None (no propagation), HostToContainer (mounts from the host are visible in the container), and Bidirectional (mounts propagate both ways).
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes.
If set to true, the volume will be mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Specifies whether read-only mounts should be handled recursively. This field is alpha-level and only honored by servers that enable the RecursiveReadOnlyMounts feature gate.
Path within the volume from which to mount the volume. Defaults to the volume root if not specified.

subPathExpr specifies a sub-path of the volume to mount, similar to subPath but with support for environment variable expansion using the $(VAR_NAME) syntax. It must begin with a '/' when non-empty, and is used for mounting a sub-path that includes environment variables.
The container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime's default is used.
The name of the DNS resolver option to configure. This corresponds to option names accepted by the system's DNS resolver, such as 'ndots' or 'timeout'.
The optional value for the DNS option. This field is not required for all DNS options and can be omitted when the option does not need a value.

List of arguments to the container's entrypoint. These override the image's configured arguments when combined with the 'command' field, or provide arguments to the image's default command if 'command' is not specified.
The command to run in the ephemeral container. This is a list of strings that overrides the default entrypoint of the container image.
List of environment variables to set in the ephemeral container. Each item is an EnvVar object with a name and a value or valueFrom source.
Name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier (e.g., a name consisting of letters, digits, and underscores, not starting with a digit).
The value of the environment variable. This is a string that is assigned to the environment variable named in the corresponding 'name' field within the same env entry.
Source for the environment variable's value, such as a reference to a ConfigMap key, Secret key, field, or resource field. Cannot be used if the 'value' field is set.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to populate the value of an environment variable. This references a specific key in the named ConfigMap, optionally allowing the key or ConfigMap to be optional.
The key in the ConfigMap to select. Must be a valid key within the referenced ConfigMap.
The name of the ConfigMap to select a key from. This must match the name of a ConfigMap in the same namespace as the pod.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap key is optional. If true, a missing key results in an empty value for the environment variable and does not prevent the container from starting. If false or omitted, the key must exist or the container creation fails.

field_ref (fieldRef in Kubernetes) selects a pod field to populate the environment variable's value. It is an ObjectFieldSelector with a required fieldPath property that specifies which pod field to read (e.g., metadata.name, status.podIP).
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath is written in terms of. If omitted, it defaults to 'v1'.
The path to the pod field to select. For example, metadata.name or spec.nodeName. Valid paths are defined by the Kubernetes field reference.
A boolean flag indicating whether the referenced key is optional. If true, the absence of the key in the file will not prevent the container from starting; if false, the key must exist.

Selects a resource field (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) from a container's resource specification to populate the environment variable value. It can be scaled by an optional divisor to adjust the value's units.
The name of the container to select the resource field from. If not specified, the container where the environment variable is defined is used.
The divisor to divide the selected resource quantity by. Must be a valid Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1', '100m'). Defaults to '1'.
The resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace to populate the environment variable with its value.
The key of the secret to select. Must be a valid secret key.
The name of the Secret to select a key from. This must be the name of a Secret in the same namespace as the pod.
Indicates whether the Secret key must be defined. If true and the key does not exist, the environment variable is omitted; if false and the key is missing, the pod fails to start.

env_from is a list of sources to populate environment variables in the ephemeral container. Each item can reference a ConfigMap or Secret to import environment variables from, optionally with a prefix.
Reference to a ConfigMap whose key-value pairs become environment variables for the ephemeral container. It supports specifying the ConfigMap name and an optional flag to tolerate missing ConfigMap.
The name of the ConfigMap from which to import environment variables. This field is required when using a ConfigMap as a source in envFrom.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If set to true, the ConfigMap may be missing; if false or unset, the ConfigMap must exist.

Optional prefix to prepend to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret when generating environment variables. For example, if the prefix is 'FOO_' and the key is 'BAR', the resulting environment variable name is 'FOO_BAR'.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret. The selected secret's data keys and values are exposed as environment variables in the container.
The name of the Secret that provides environment variables to the container. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the StatefulSet.
Indicates whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If set to true, the Secret may be absent and the container will still start.
The container image to use for this ephemeral container, as defined in the ephemeral container spec.

The image pull policy for the ephemeral container. Allowed values: Always, IfNotPresent, Never. Controls when the kubelet pulls the image: Always pulls every time, IfNotPresent pulls only if the image is not already present, Never never pulls and only uses local images.
Lifecycle describes actions that the container runtime performs in response to container lifecycle events, such as PostStart and PreStop hooks.

postStart is a lifecycle hook that runs immediately after an ephemeral container is created. It defines an action to execute, such as an exec command, an HTTP GET request, or a TCP socket check, via a handler object.
Exec specifies the command to run in the container during the postStart lifecycle hook. It contains a command array that overrides the container's default command.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container. The command is executed directly, not through a shell, so shell syntax (e.g., pipes, redirection, environment variable expansion) is not supported.

Specifies an HTTP GET request to be performed when the container is started as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. This handler allows the container to execute an HTTP request before it is considered started, and it can include parameters such as the target host, path, port, and headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP address.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header is defined by a name and a value.
The HTTP header name for the HTTP GET request (e.g., X-Custom-Header).
The value of the HTTP header to send in the GET request. This is the string value paired with the header name, such as the token in an Authorization header.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server for the HTTP GET request.
The port number or name to access for the HTTP request. If a number, it must be between 1 and 65535. If a string, it must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME (e.g., a named port).
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS', defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the connection. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The sleep action for the post-start lifecycle hook, which pauses the hook for a specified duration. The duration is configured in seconds within this object.
Specifies the number of seconds the container should sleep before proceeding, used in the sleep action of a PostStart lifecycle hook.

The tcp_socket block defines the TCP socket handler used by the container's post-start lifecycle hook. It configures a check that attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port, signaling that the container has started successfully.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port number (as a string) or name of a port defined in the container, used for the postStart lifecycle hook's TCP socket action.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that is executed immediately before a container is terminated. It allows the container to perform graceful shutdown operations, such as cleaning up resources or notifying dependent services. This field is an object that can define an exec command, an HTTP GET request, or a TCP socket check.
Exec specifies an action that runs a command inside the ephemeral container when the pre-stop lifecycle hook is triggered. The command to execute is defined in the 'command' field of this object.

The command to execute as part of the preStop lifecycle hook. It is specified as a list of strings, where the first element is the executable and the remaining elements are arguments. The command runs directly inside the container without a shell.
Performs an HTTP GET request to the specified path and port on the container when the pre-stop lifecycle hook is triggered. This action defines the HTTP request details for the pre-stop hook.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; you may want to set the Host header in httpHeaders instead.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP request. Each item in the list must have a 'name' and a 'value' field.
The name of the HTTP header to send with the GET request, such as 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header used in the pre-stop HTTP GET request. This is part of a key-value pair defined in the httpHeaders list.
Path to access on the HTTP server for the HTTP GET request.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Accepts an integer port number (as a string) or a named port that matches a port name defined in the container's ports.
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme for the HTTP GET request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified.
The number of seconds to sleep. Specifies the duration of the preStop sleep action.

Configures a TCP socket check performed as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port to determine if the container is ready to be stopped.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP address.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. The number must be in the range 1 to 65535. If a name is specified, it must match an IANA_SVC_NAME.
Configuration for the liveness probe of the ephemeral container. Kubernetes does not execute probes for ephemeral containers, so this field has no operational effect.
Defines the exec action: the command to run inside the container to check liveness. If the command exits with 0, the probe succeeds.
The command to run inside the container for the liveness probe. The first element is the executable, and the remaining elements are arguments. It is executed directly without a shell.
The number of consecutive probe failures allowed before the container is restarted. For a liveness probe, exceeding this threshold triggers a container restart.
grpc specifies the gRPC action to perform for the probe. It contains configuration such as the gRPC service and port to check for health.
The port number of the gRPC service to connect to for the liveness probe.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health check protocol (often checking the overall server health).
Configures the liveness probe to use an HTTP GET request to check the health of the container. The request is sent to the specified path and port.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Custom headers to send with the HTTP GET request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request, such as "Authorization" or "X-Custom-Header".
The value of the HTTP header to include in the liveness probe request.
Path to access on the HTTP server.
The TCP port to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Accepts a numeric port or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the liveness probe is initiated.
How often (in seconds) to perform the liveness probe. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 10.
The minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after a failure. For liveness probes, this value must be set to 1.
TCP socket probe configuration for the liveness check. Specifies the host and port to connect to; a successful connection indicates the probe is healthy.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port number or named port on the container to probe. Must be a valid TCP port number (1-65535) or a name of an IANA_SVC_NAME container port.
Optional number of seconds the container is allowed to terminate gracefully after this liveness probe fails, overriding the pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds. Must be a non-negative integer.
Number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out. Defaults to 1 second if not specified.
The name of the ephemeral container.

List of network ports to expose from the ephemeral container. Each item specifies a container port, protocol (TCP, UDP, or SCTP), optional name, and optional hostIP, following the same schema as regular container ports.
The port number on which the ephemeral container listens. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The host IP address to bind the external port to. If not set, the port is bound to all host interfaces (0.0.0.0).
The port on the host node to expose the container port. Valid range is 1-65535. If specified, the container is accessible via this port on the host IP.
The name of the port. Must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME and unique within the pod. Named ports can be referenced by services.
The network protocol for the port, such as TCP, UDP, or SCTP. Defaults to TCP if not specified.
Readiness probe for the ephemeral container, determining when the container is ready to accept traffic. If the probe fails, the container is considered not ready.
Exec specifies the action to take, by running a command inside the container. It is an ExecAction object that contains a command array to execute.

The command to run inside the container as a list of arguments. It is executed directly without a shell, so features like pipes and redirection are not available. A zero exit status indicates that the container is healthy.
The number of consecutive failures of the readiness probe that must occur for the container to be marked as not ready. Must be an integer greater than or equal to 1.
Specifies a gRPC-based health check for the probe. The object contains a 'port' (required) and 'service' (optional) field to define the gRPC endpoint.
The port number to connect to for the gRPC health check. This is a required field and must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
Optional name of the gRPC service to place in the HealthCheckRequest. When omitted, the default gRPC health check behavior is used.

Specifies the parameters for an HTTP GET request used as a readiness probe. The kubelet sends an HTTP GET request to the container's IP address using the specified port and path, and if the response status code is between 200 and 399, the container is considered ready.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not set, defaults to the pod IP. To set the HTTP Host header, use httpHeaders instead.
Specifies a list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request made by the readiness probe. Each header is defined as an object containing a name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP GET request of the readiness probe.
The value of the HTTP header to send with the probe request.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to / if not specified.
Port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET probe. If a number, it must be between 1 and 65535. If a name, it must match a container port name.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request, such as HTTP or HTTPS.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0.
The number of seconds between each readiness probe execution. Defaults to 10 seconds if not specified.
Minimum consecutive successes for the readiness probe to be considered successful after a failure. Defaults to 1; may be a positive integer.
Specifies a TCP socket probe that checks whether a TCP connection can be established to a given port on the container.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port number or named port on the container. It can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a string name that matches a container port's name.
Specifies the grace period in seconds for pod termination. After the termination signal is sent, the pod has this many seconds to finish running processes before being forcefully killed.
Number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. Defaults to 1 second; the minimum allowed value is 1.

A list of resize policies for the ephemeral container's resources. Each policy specifies a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the associated restart policy ('NotRequired' or 'RestartContainer') that determines whether the container must be restarted when that resource is resized.
The name of the resource (e.g., 'cpu' or 'memory') to which this resize policy applies.

Defines the restart behavior when the specified resource is resized. Allowed values are 'NotRequired' (resources can be changed without restarting the container) and 'RestartContainer' (the container is restarted to apply the new resource sizing).

Resources defines the compute requirements (CPU, memory, etc.) for the ephemeral container. Note that Kubernetes does not enforce resource requests or limits for ephemeral containers, so this field is optional and may be ignored.

A list of resource claims that the ephemeral container requires. Each claim is an object with a 'name' field referencing a ResourceClaim or ResourceClaimTemplate in the same namespace, used to request specific resources beyond the standard CPU/memory limits.

The name of the resource claim (e.g., a PersistentVolumeClaim) that the ephemeral container requests. The claim must exist in the same namespace as the pod and must match a resource claim defined in the pod spec.
Name of the ResourceClaim object requested by the container. Must match the name of a ResourceClaim defined in the pod spec.

A map of resource name to quantity, specifying the maximum amount of compute resources (such as CPU and memory) that the ephemeral container is allowed to use. Values are Kubernetes quantity strings, e.g., '100m' for CPU and '128Mi' for memory.

Resource requests for this ephemeral container. Keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) and values are Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., 100m, 1Gi) specifying the minimum amount of resources required.
The operator used to compare the container exit code against the specified values. Valid values are 'In' and 'NotIn'.
A list of container exit codes that trigger the restart policy rule. When any of these exit codes is observed, the rule's defined action is applied.
SecurityContext holds security configuration that will be applied to the ephemeral container, such as user and group IDs, Linux capabilities, SELinux options, and privilege settings.
AllowPrivilegeEscalation controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. If set to false, the container process cannot use setuid or gain additional capabilities.
AppArmor profile settings for the ephemeral container. Specifies the profile type (RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, or Localhost) and the optional localhost profile name when type is Localhost.
Specifies the name of the AppArmor profile loaded on the node. This is used when the profile type is 'Localhost' and the profile must be preconfigured on the node.
The type of AppArmor profile to use. Allowed values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', and 'Unconfined'.
Defines the Linux capabilities to add to or drop from the container's processes. The capabilities object typically contains lists of capabilities to add and remove.
Specifies the Linux capabilities to add to the container's security context. For example, 'SYS_ADMIN' or 'NET_BIND_SERVICE'.
List of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's default capability set. Dropping capabilities restricts the container's privileges (e.g., 'ALL' drops all capabilities).
Run the ephemeral container in privileged mode, granting it access to all host devices and elevated capabilities. Defaults to false.
procMount specifies the type of proc mount to use for the container. The default is Default, which masks paths in /proc; the only other allowed value is Unmasked, which does not mask paths in /proc.
Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only. When set to true, the root filesystem becomes read-only.
The group ID (GID) under which the container process runs. If omitted, the container's primary group (from the image) is used.
Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the kubelet will validate that the container does not run as UID 0 (root) and will refuse to start it otherwise.
The user ID (UID) to run the container process as. If unspecified, defaults to the user defined in the container image metadata.
SELinux options for the ephemeral container, specifying the SELinux level, user, role, or type applied to the container's security context.
The SELinux level (MLS sensitivity) applied to the process, often formatted as s0:c1,c2 for categories.
The SELinux role for the container, as part of the SELinux security context options.
The SELinux type label, which is part of the SELinux security context for the container.
The user label for the SELinux context applied to the ephemeral container. Part of the se_linux_options security context.

SeccompProfile configures the seccomp profile for the ephemeral container. It supports types such as RuntimeDefault, Localhost, and Unconfined, with an optional localhostProfile field for custom profiles.
The path to a locally-defined seccomp profile on the node. This is used when the seccomp profile type is set to 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to use. Valid values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', and 'Unconfined'.
Windows-specific security options for the ephemeral container's security context, such as GMSA credentials and host process settings.
The GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container. This is a string containing the credential spec JSON, as defined by the GMSA admission webhook.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the container's Windows security context.

Indicates whether the container should run as a HostProcess container, which gives it access to the Windows host's process and network namespaces. When true, the container runs on the host with elevated privileges.
The Windows user name (formatted as 'DOMAIN\USER') that the container process runs as. If not specified, the default user defined in the container image metadata is used.

Configures a startup probe for the ephemeral container. This probe determines when the container has started successfully; until it succeeds, the container is not considered ready, and failures may restart the container according to its restart policy.
Exec defines a command to execute inside the container for this startup probe. If the command exits with status 0, the probe succeeds; any non-zero exit code indicates failure.

The command to run inside the container for this startup probe. It is a list of strings: the first element is the executable, and the rest are arguments. The command is executed directly, not via a shell, so shell syntax such as '|' will not work.

Specifies the number of consecutive failures allowed for the startup probe before the container is restarted or marked as unhealthy. This helps accommodate slow-starting containers by providing more attempts.
The gRPC health check configuration for the startup probe. This specifies the port and optional service name to use when performing a gRPC health check.
The port number on which the gRPC server is listening. The probe connects to this port on the container's IP address. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If this is not specified, the default behavior is to check the overall health of the pod.
HTTPGet specifies the HTTP GET request to perform on the container. It defines the path, port, and optional HTTP headers used by the probe to determine container health.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Specifies custom HTTP headers to include in the request to the probe endpoint. Each entry in the list defines a header name and its value.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP GET request.
The value for the HTTP header, paired with the corresponding header name in the startup probe's HTTP GET request.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server, e.g., '/healthz'. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
Port number or name of the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Accepts an integer port or a named port defined in the container.
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are "HTTP" and "HTTPS". Defaults to "HTTP".
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request (HTTP or HTTPS). Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. A value of 0 means the probe begins immediately after container startup.
The number of seconds between each probe attempt. For startup probes, this controls how frequently the kubelet checks the container's startup status. Defaults to 10; minimum is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after it has failed. Must be 1 for startup probes.
Performs a TCP socket check by attempting to connect to the specified port on the container's IP address (or the specified host). The probe succeeds if the connection is established.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
The TCP port to check. Provide a numeric port (e.g., '80') or a named port defined in the container's ports. This is the port the kubelet attempts to connect to during the startup probe.

Specifies the duration in seconds that the kubelet waits after a startup probe failure before forcefully terminating the container. Overrides the pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds for this container.
The number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. If not specified, the default is 1 second. This applies to the startup probe for ephemeral containers in the StatefulSet pod template.
Indicates whether a stdin buffer should be allocated for this ephemeral container. If true, the container can read from standard input. Defaults to false.
If true, the ephemeral container's stdin is closed after the first time it is attached to, allowing only a single interactive session. Defaults to false.
The name of the container in the pod that this ephemeral container targets, sharing its process namespace. If omitted, the ephemeral container uses the pod's process namespace.
Path where the container's termination message is written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.
Indicates whether a pseudo-TTY should be allocated for the container. When true, the container is allocated a terminal, allowing interactive sessions.
A list of volume devices that map raw block volumes to the ephemeral container. Each entry specifies a volume name and the device path inside the container where the raw block device will be exposed.
devicePath is the path within the container that the device should be mounted at.
The name of the volume for this device, matching the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
List of volume mounts for the ephemeral container, specifying which pod volumes to mount and their mount paths.
Path within the ephemeral container at which the volume is mounted. Must be an absolute path and must not contain a colon (:).
Defines how mount propagation is handled for this volume mount. Allowed values are 'None', 'HostToContainer', and 'Bidirectional'. If empty, defaults to 'None'.
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes.
Mounts the volume as read-only when set to true; otherwise, the volume is mounted read-write.
RecursiveReadOnly specifies whether the volume mount is recursive read-only. Allowed values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', and 'IfPossible'.
Path within the volume from which to mount instead of the volume's root. Useful for mounting a single file or subdirectory.
Specifies a path within the volume from which to mount, with support for environment variable expansion (e.g., $(VAR)). This is similar to subPath but allows variables to be resolved at runtime.
The working directory for the ephemeral container. If not specified, the container runtime uses the default, which may be defined by the container image.
The list of hostnames to be resolved to the IP address of this host alias entry in the pod's /etc/hosts file.
The IP address to add to the pod's /etc/hosts file for this host alias entry.
The name of the image pull secret to use for pulling container images.
Arguments to the container's entrypoint. These are passed to the command and override any default arguments (CMD) specified in the image.
The command to run as the entrypoint for the init container. If not set, the default entrypoint of the container image is used.
List of environment variables to set in the init container. Each entry defines a variable name and optionally a value or valueFrom source.
The name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier, i.e., start with a letter or underscore, and contain only letters, digits, or underscores.
The value of the environment variable. This string is used as the variable's value when no valueFrom source is specified.

If specified, this optional field defines the source for the environment variable's value. It can reference a ConfigMap, Secret, or a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name), allowing the value to be set dynamically rather than as a string literal.
selects a key from a ConfigMap to populate the environment variable value. It specifies the ConfigMap name and the key to retrieve.
The key within the ConfigMap to select. The value corresponding to this key in the referenced ConfigMap is used as the environment variable's value.
Name of the ConfigMap being referenced.

Optional specifies whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If true, the key may be missing and the value will be treated as unset; if false (default), the key must exist or the pod will fail to start.

Selects a field of the pod to use as the value of the environment variable. The field path must be a valid pod field (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace, metadata.labels, spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.hostIP, or status.podIP). Optionally specifies the API version for the field selector.
The API version of the schema that fieldPath is written in terms of. For example, 'v1'.

The path to the field within the pod that the value is read from. For example, metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, or status.podIP. This is used in a Kubernetes FieldRef to select a field of the pod object.

Specifies whether the referenced file key must exist. If true, the container starts even if the key is absent, and the variable is unset. If false or omitted, the container is blocked until the key exists.
The name of the volume that contains the file whose key is referenced by this environment variable.
Selects a resource field (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) of the container to use as the value for the environment variable in Kubernetes init containers.

The name of the container for which the resource field is selected. If empty, defaults to the first container in the pod. Used to reference a resource (e.g., limits.cpu, requests.memory) from that container's resource specification.
Divisor is the value by which the resource quantity is divided to produce the environment variable value. If not specified, defaults to 1.

The name of the container resource to select, such as 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory'. This field specifies which resource quantity from the container's resource limits or requests should be exposed as the environment variable value.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. Specify the secret name and key, and optionally whether the secret must be defined.
The key of the secret to select from. Must be a valid key in the referenced Secret.
The name of the Secret object to select a key from.

Specify whether the referenced Secret or its key must be defined. When true, the environment variable reference is optional and the container will start even if the secret or key is missing. When false (default), a missing secret or key will prevent the container from starting.
List of sources (such as ConfigMaps and Secrets) from which environment variables are populated in the init container. Each entry can define a prefix and select specific keys to import.
Reference to a ConfigMap from which to populate environment variables. All key-value pairs in the referenced ConfigMap are exposed as environment variables in the container.
Name of the ConfigMap that provides environment variables for the init container.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If set to true, the ConfigMap may be absent; if false or omitted, the ConfigMap must exist.
An optional prefix to prepend to each key in the ConfigMap or Secret when they are exposed as environment variables. Must be a valid C identifier.
A reference to a Kubernetes Secret. The selected Secret's data is used to populate environment variables in the container.
The name of the Secret to reference. This must match the name of a Secret in the same namespace as the pod, and is required when secretRef is used.

Specifies whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If true, a missing Secret is allowed and the environment variables from this source are not set; if false or omitted, a missing Secret causes an error.
The container image to use for this init container, typically specified as a name and tag or digest.
The image pull policy for this init container. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never.
Lifecycle configures lifecycle hooks for the init container, including postStart and preStop handlers that execute commands or HTTP requests at container startup and shutdown.
The postStart lifecycle hook, executed immediately after a container is started. Defines actions (e.g., exec command or HTTP GET request) to run before the container's main process continues.
Exec specifies the post-start lifecycle handler as a command to be executed inside the container. It defines an ExecAction, which runs a command in the container's filesystem.

The command to run inside the container for the post-start lifecycle hook. This is an array of strings representing the command and its arguments, executed using the container's default working directory and environment.
HTTP GET request to perform as the postStart lifecycle hook. It is considered successful only if the response code is in the 200-399 range; otherwise the container is killed.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
List of HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each item defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header (e.g., 'X-Custom-Header'). Header names are case-insensitive.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent in the GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server, relative to the host. This is the URL path segment of the HTTP GET request, for example /healthz.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or the name of a port defined in the container's ports.
Specifies the protocol to use for the HTTP GET request (e.g., HTTP or HTTPS).
Scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The duration in seconds of the sleep action. Specifies how long to pause the container before proceeding with the lifecycle hook.

Specifies a TCP socket check that is executed as part of the postStart lifecycle hook after the container starts. This object configures the TCP endpoint (host and port) to probe, allowing the container to signal readiness or trigger dependent actions.
Optional hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port to connect to. Accepts a numeric port number or a named port from the container's defined ports.

Defines a hook that is executed immediately before a container is terminated. This hook can be used to gracefully stop the container, for example, by sending a SIGTERM or performing cleanup operations. The preStop hook is part of the container lifecycle and runs before the container receives its termination signal.
Specifies the exec action to be run inside the container as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. The command is executed when the container is about to be terminated.
The command to run in the container as part of the preStop lifecycle hook's exec action. It is specified as a list of strings; the first element is the command, and subsequent elements are arguments.

Specifies an HTTP GET request that the kubelet sends to the container as part of the preStop lifecycle hook, allowing custom actions before container termination. The request is defined by parameters such as path, port, host, scheme, and headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the request sent to the container's HTTP GET probe or lifecycle action.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the pre-stop hook request.
The value of the HTTP header being sent in the pre-stop lifecycle HTTP GET request.
The URL path for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to '/'.
The port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Accepts an integer port number or a named port (IANA_SVC_NAME). Required.
The protocol (scheme) used for the HTTP GET request, such as HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP if not specified.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Must be either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.

Sleep action for the lifecycle hook, specifying a duration to pause the container before the hook completes. This object contains a mandatory 'seconds' field that defines the sleep duration (must be positive).
The number of seconds to sleep before the container is terminated.
Specifies a TCP socket action to be performed as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook, allowing the container to connect to a given port (and optionally host) before termination.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
Port number or name of the TCP socket to connect to. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME.
Configures a liveness probe for the container. If the probe fails, the kubelet restarts the container.
Exec specifies the action to take, which is to run a command inside the container. If the command exits with 0, the probe is considered successful; any other exit code is considered failure.

The command to execute inside the container for the liveness probe. It is a list of strings where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. For example, ["cat", "/tmp/healthy"].
The number of consecutive failures required for the liveness probe to be considered failed, causing the container to be restarted. Defaults to 3, minimum value is 1.
grpc is an optional field that configures a gRPC-based health check for the liveness probe. It defines the port to probe and optionally the service name.
The port number on which the gRPC server is listening. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the default behavior is to not send a service name.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform against the container to determine its liveness. Includes parameters like path, port, and headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
A list of custom HTTP headers to send with the GET request. Each header is defined as an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request.
The value of the HTTP header in the liveness probe request.
The path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
Port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports.
Specifies the protocol scheme (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET liveness probe. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the liveness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the liveness probe to be considered successful after a failure. For liveness probes, this must be 1.

Configures a TCP socket check for the liveness probe, where the kubelet attempts to open a connection to the specified port on the container. The object should include a 'port' field (required) and may optionally include a 'host' field to specify the address to connect to.
Optional host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to probe. May be an integer port number or a string referring to a named port in the container's list of ports.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second.
The name of the init container. This name must be unique among all containers in the pod and must be a valid DNS_LABEL (e.g., my-init-container).

List of ports to expose from the container. Exposing a port here gives the system additional information about the network connections a container uses, but is primarily informational. Not specifying a port here does NOT prevent that port from being exposed. Any port which is listening on the default '0.0.0.0' address inside a container will be accessible from the network. Cannot be updated.
The port number that the container listens on.
The host IP address to bind the host port to. If omitted, the port is bound to all interfaces on the host (0.0.0.0).
The port on the host node to expose the container's port. When set, the container is reachable via this port from outside the node; when omitted, no host port is allocated.
An optional port name. If specified, it must be an IANA_SVC_NAME and unique among all ports in the pod; services can reference the port by this name.
The protocol used for the container port. Allowed values are 'TCP', 'UDP', and 'SCTP'. Defaults to 'TCP'.
Configuration for a readiness probe on the init container. Note: Kubernetes does not use readiness probes for init containers, as they run to completion, so this field is typically ignored.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container. The readiness probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0.
The command to execute inside the container. This is a list of strings; the first element is the command and the remaining elements are arguments passed to it.
The number of consecutive failures required for the readiness probe to be considered failed, after which the container is marked not ready. Defaults to 3.
grpc provides the configuration for a gRPC-based readiness probe, specifying how the probe should perform a gRPC health check.
The port number that the gRPC health check will connect to on the container.
The name of the service to include in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the health check is performed without a service name.
Configures the HTTP GET request used by the readiness probe to check container health. Specifies the path, port, and headers for the HTTP request to the container.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP address if not specified.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP request. Each header is a name-value pair, typically with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The HTTP header name to include in the GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the readiness probe request.
Path to access on the HTTP server for the probe request. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port number or name of the container to send the HTTP GET request to. Provide a numeric port (1-65535) as a string, or the name of a container port defined in the container specification.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request, either HTTP or HTTPS.
The HTTP or HTTPS scheme used for the probe request. Defaults to HTTP if not specified.
The number of seconds to wait after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 10 seconds if not specified.

The minimum number of consecutive successful probe checks required for the probe to be considered successful after a failure. For readiness probes, this indicates how many successes are needed to mark the container as ready again.

The tcp_socket block configures the TCP socket probe, which checks the container's readiness by attempting to open a TCP connection to the specified port. It contains a required port and an optional host.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP readiness probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to probe for readiness. Provide a numeric port (1-65535) or a named container port. Required when using tcp_socket.

Optional number of seconds the container is allowed to terminate gracefully when this readiness probe fails, overriding the pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds. If not set, the pod's default is used; zero means immediate termination.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Minimum value is 1 second and defaults to 1 second.

List of policies that determine how to resize container resources. Each policy specifies a resource name (such as cpu or memory) and a restart policy (e.g., NotRequired or RestartContainer) for when a resize is requested.
The resource name (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies for the init container.
The restart policy for the container when its resources are resized. Valid values are 'NotRequired' (no restart needed) and 'RestartContainer' (container must be restarted).

The resources field specifies the compute resources required for the init container, including requests and limits for CPU, memory, and other resource types as defined in the Kubernetes Container Resources spec.

A list of resource claim references used by this container. Each item contains a `name` that matches a resource claim declared in the pod's `spec.resourceClaims` field, enabling the container to use that claim. This is an alpha feature.
Name of the ResourceClaim object that this container requires. The ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the container. It is a map of resource names to quantities, e.g., 'cpu' and 'memory'. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-compute-resources-container/

Specifies the minimum amount of compute resources required for the init container. The map keys are resource names (e.g., 'cpu', 'memory') and values are Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., '100m', '128Mi').
The comparison operator used to evaluate the exit code condition. Allowed values are 'In' and 'NotIn'.
The list of container exit codes that trigger this restart policy rule.

Security settings for the init container, including user/group IDs, Linux capabilities, SELinux options, and privilege escalation controls. This field applies to a specific init container within the pod template of the StatefulSet.

Whether the container's processes are allowed to gain more privileges than the parent process, such as via setuid or setgid binaries. Setting this to false prevents privilege escalation inside the container.
AppArmor profile to apply to the container. The object specifies the profile type (e.g., Localhost or RuntimeDefault) and optionally the localhost profile name when type is Localhost.
The name of a profile on the node.
Capabilities configures Linux capabilities for the container. It includes 'add' and 'drop' lists to grant or remove specific capabilities.
List of Linux capabilities to add to the container's permitted capabilities. For example, ['NET_ADMIN', 'SYS_TIME'].
List of capabilities to drop from the container's permitted capabilities. Each entry is a Linux capability name, e.g., 'ALL', 'NET_ADMIN'.
Indicates whether the container runs in privileged mode, granting it extended capabilities and access to host devices.
procMount defines the proc mount to use for the container. Allowed values are 'Default' and 'Unmasked'. When set to 'Unmasked', the container can access host processes.
When true, mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only.
The GID to run the entrypoint of the container process. If omitted, the group ID is determined by the image's metadata.
Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the kubelet will reject the container if it runs as UID 0 (root).
Specifies the numeric user ID (UID) to run the init container process as. Overrides the user specified in the container image, if any.
SELinux options to apply to the init container's processes, defining the SELinux context via level, role, type, and user fields.
SELinux level that applies to the container, such as s0, s0:c123, etc.
The SELinux role label for the container process, used as part of the SELinux security context.
The SELinux type label to be applied to the container, as part of the SELinux context.
The SELinux user label for the container. This is part of the SELinux context applied to the container's processes.
Defines the seccomp profile applied to this init container. Supports types: Unconfined, RuntimeDefault, and Localhost; when Localhost is used, specify localhostProfile to set the path to the profile.
Path to the seccomp profile on the node's localhost. Must be set when the seccompProfile type is 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to use. Allowed values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', and 'Unconfined'.
Windows-specific security options for the container, such as GMSA credentials and run-as-user settings. This field is only relevant for Windows containers.
The full Group Managed Service Account (gMSA) credential spec as a JSON string used to configure Windows gMSA for the container. This field should not be set together with gmsa_credential_spec_name.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for this Windows container. This configures a Group Managed Service Account for the container.
Specifies whether the container should run as a host process on a Windows node. When set to true, the container runs in the host's process namespace and has access to host resources.

The Windows user name to run the container's entrypoint as. Defaults to the user specified in the image metadata if unspecified, and may also be set in PodSecurityContext; if set in both, the value in SecurityContext takes precedence.
Startup probe that indicates whether the init container has successfully started. If specified, no other probes are executed until this probe succeeds.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container to perform the probe. The probe succeeds if the command exits with a zero status.
Specifies the command to execute in the container as a list of strings. The probe considers the container healthy if the command exits with a zero status.
The number of consecutive failures required for the startup probe to be considered failed. After this many failures, the kubelet restarts the container. Minimum value is 1, and the default is 3.
Specifies the gRPC action for the startup probe, including the port to check and an optional service name. This tells kubelet to perform a gRPC health check on the container.
The port number on which the gRPC health check service is listening.
The name of the service to include in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the default behavior defined by gRPC is used.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform on the container as a startup probe. Use this to define the port, path, and optional HTTP headers used to check container health.
The host name used in the HTTP GET request for the startup probe. If not set, the pod's IP address is used as the host.
List of custom HTTP headers to send with the GET request. Each item is an object containing a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request.
The value of the HTTP header that will be sent in the HTTP GET request from the startup probe.
The HTTP request path to access on the HTTP server. For example, /healthz.
The port number or name of the port on the container to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. Accepts an integer port number (1-65535) or a named port (IANA_SVC_NAME).
The protocol (scheme) used for the HTTP GET request in the startup probe. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use when connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Defaults to 0 if not specified.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1.

Specifies a TCP socket probe action, used to check the health of a container by attempting to open a TCP connection to a specified port on the container. This is one of the probe types available for a startup probe.
host is an optional host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP probe; defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to check. Can be a numeric port number or a named port in the container.
Specifies the number of seconds the pod has to terminate gracefully after receiving a termination signal, before Kubernetes forces it to shut down.
The number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. If the probe does not complete within this time, it is considered failed. Defaults to 1 second if not specified.
Whether to allocate a stdin stream for the container. When true, the container's standard input is kept open.
If true, stdin is closed after the container process starts, provided it was attached to a terminal. This is useful for containers that read from stdin only during initialization.
Path where the container writes termination messages, which the kubelet retrieves to report the container's termination reason. If not set, defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Specifies how the init container's termination message is read. Allowed values are 'File' (default) to read from /dev/termination-log, or 'FallbackToLogsOnError' to use the last container log output if the termination message file is empty and the container exits with an error.
Whether this init container should allocate a TTY for itself, enabling interactive processes. This typically requires 'stdin' to be set to true.
List of block devices to be used by the container. Each item specifies the device path and the name of a persistent volume claim that provides the block device.
