The path inside the container where the block device will be mounted. For example, /dev/sdb.
The name of the volume device. This must match the name of a volume listed in the pod's volumes specification.
List of volume mounts for the init container. Each item specifies a volume to mount and the mount path within the container.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path and cannot contain ':'.
Determines how mount propagation is handled for this volume mount. Allowed values are None, HostToContainer, and Bidirectional. Defaults to None if not specified.
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
Indicates whether the volume is mounted as read-only. If true, the container cannot write to the mount.
Specifies whether the volume mount is recursively read-only. Allowed values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', or 'IfPossible'.
Maps a sub-path inside the referenced volume to the mount path. This allows mounting a specific directory or file from the volume, rather than the volume's root.

Specifies a subPath within a volume, with support for environment variable expansion using $(VAR_NAME) syntax. The expanded path is used as the mount point's subPath, allowing dynamic volume paths based on container environment variables.
Sets the working directory for the init container. If not specified, the container runtime default is used.
conditionType is the name of a condition in the pod's condition list.
Name of the ResourceClaim that this container references. The ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the ResourceClaim object that this pod references. The ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

The name of a ResourceClaimTemplate object that defines the resource claim to be created for the pod. This field references a template in the same namespace, which is instantiated to provide a ResourceClaim for the pod.
Name of the ResourceClaim that this pod references. Must refer to a ResourceClaim object in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the scheduling gate.
The name of the sysctl parameter, for example kernel.shm_rmid_forced.
The value to set for the sysctl parameter specified in the `name` field.
The taint effect to match. Allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, and NoExecute. If empty, matches all effects.
The key of the taint that this toleration matches. If the operator is 'Exists', the value should be empty; otherwise, this is the taint key.
The operator used to match the taint effect. Allowed values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. Use 'Exists' to match all taints without a value, or 'Equal' to match a specific key/value pair.
The number of seconds a pod will tolerate a taint before being evicted. If omitted, the pod tolerates the taint indefinitely.
The value to match the taint key. Required when operator is 'Equal' (or not set), and must be empty when operator is 'Exists'.

A label query over pods that should be spread across the topology domains. This selects the pods to which the topology spread constraint applies; if unspecified, all pods in the namespace are considered.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement defines a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. Used to select the pods to which the topology spread constraint applies.
The label key that this selector requirement applies to. The requirement is satisfied if the pod's label with this key matches the operator and values specified.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a label selector requirement. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values that must match the specified operator. For the operators In and NotIn, this list contains the set of values to match; for Exists and DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.
A map of label keys and values that a pod must have to be selected by this label selector for the topology spread constraint.

matchLabelKeys is a list of pod label keys used to filter the pods over which spreading is calculated. The spread constraint only considers pods that have the same values for these labels as the new pod, which avoids counting stale replicas during rolling updates.

The maximum permitted difference in the number of matching Pods between any two topology domains of a given topology type. A higher value allows more uneven distribution; it must be greater than zero.

The minimum number of eligible domains for the topology spread constraint. If the number of eligible domains is less than this value, the global minimum is treated as 0 and skew is calculated per domain. Must be greater than 0 when specified, and is only supported within a single namespace.
Specifies whether to honor node affinity when calculating pod topology spread skew. Allowed values are 'Honor' (respect nodeAffinity constraints) and 'Ignore' (ignore them).
Indicates how to treat nodes with taints when matching topology spread constraints. Allowed values are 'Honor' (default) and 'Ignore'.
The key of node labels that identifies the topology domain. Pods are spread across domains identified by this key, such as 'kubernetes.io/hostname' or 'topology.kubernetes.io/zone'.

Determines how to handle a pod if it does not satisfy the spread constraint. Valid values are 'DoNotSchedule' (default), which prevents scheduling, and 'ScheduleAnyway', which allows scheduling while still honoring the skew limit as much as possible.
Defines an AWS Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume as a storage source in the pod's volumes. This object specifies the configuration necessary to attach and mount an existing EBS volume to the pod.
Filesystem type to mount for the AWS Elastic Block Store volume, e.g., ext4, xfs. Defaults to ext4 if not specified.
The partition number on the AWS EBS volume to mount. If omitted, Kubernetes mounts the first partition (partition 1). For example, specify '1' for /dev/sda1.
Specifies whether the AWS EBS volume is mounted as read-only within the pod. Defaults to false, meaning the volume is mounted read-write.
The unique ID of the AWS Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume that will be mounted into the pod.
Represents an Azure Disk volume source, used to mount a Microsoft Azure data disk into a pod. It contains configuration for the disk such as the disk name, URI, and caching mode.
The name of the Azure data disk to attach to the pod.
The URI of the Azure disk to be mounted as a volume. For unmanaged disks, this is the URI of the VHD blob; for managed disks, this is the resource ID of the managed disk.
Filesystem type to mount for the Azure disk, e.g., 'ext4' or 'xfs'. If not specified, defaults to 'ext4'.
Kind of the Azure disk. Allowed values are 'Shared', 'Dedicated', and 'Managed'. Defaults to 'Shared' if not specified.
Specifies whether the Azure Disk is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read/write).

Represents an Azure File volume source. When defined, this object configures a mount of an Azure File share into the pod. It typically includes settings such as the share name and a reference to a Kubernetes secret containing the storage account key and name.
Specifies whether the Azure File share is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that stores the Azure Storage account name and key. The secret should contain keys 'azurestorageaccountname' and 'azurestorageaccountkey'.
The name of the Azure file share to mount.
Represents a Ceph Filesystem (CephFS) volume source in Kubernetes. When specified, this volume allows the pod to mount a CephFS share.
List of Ceph monitor addresses (host:port) used to connect to the Ceph cluster for this CephFS volume.
The path within CephFS to mount. Defaults to the root directory '/' if not specified.
Defaults to false (read/write). If set to true, forces the volume to be mounted as read-only.
Path to the Ceph client keyring file; defaults to /etc/ceph/user.secret when unset.
secret_ref is a reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the CephFS authentication keyring. This secret is used to authenticate when mounting the CephFS volume.
Name of the secret containing CephFS credentials.
The CephFS user to use when mounting the volume. Defaults to 'admin' if not specified.
cinder represents a Cinder volume source for OpenStack block storage, allowing the pod to mount a Cinder volume.
Filesystem type to mount, such as ext4 or xfs. If not specified, the default filesystem type of the volume is used.
Indicates whether the Cinder volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
A reference to a Secret that provides the authentication credentials for the Cinder volume.
Name of the Kubernetes secret that contains the authentication credentials for the Cinder volume. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The ID of the OpenStack Cinder volume to mount.
ConfigMap represents a volume source that populates the volume with data from a Kubernetes ConfigMap. This allows exposing configuration data as files inside the container.

Specifies the default permission mode for files in the ConfigMap volume, expressed as an octal or decimal value between 0 and 511 (e.g., 0644 or 420). This applies to files that do not have an explicit mode set.

Maps specific keys from the referenced ConfigMap to file paths within the volume. If items is unspecified, all key-value pairs are projected as files named by the keys; if specified, only listed keys are projected to the given paths, and unlisted keys are omitted.
The key in the ConfigMap data to select for this item. Must correspond to an existing key in the ConfigMap's data map.
Optional file mode (permissions) for the item, specified as an octal integer between 0000 and 0777. Defaults to the volume's default permission if not set.
Path within the volume where the config map key is mounted as a file.
Name of the ConfigMap to be mounted as a volume.
Indicates whether the ConfigMap must be defined. When true, the volume is supplied even if the ConfigMap does not exist; when false (default), the pod fails if the ConfigMap is missing.

Represents a volume backed by a CSI (Container Storage Interface) driver. This object defines the driver name and options such as volume attributes, read-only setting, and node publish secret reference.
Name of the CSI driver that will be used to handle the volume. This is a required field for CSI volumes.

Filesystem type to mount in the CSI volume. Examples include 'ext4' and 'xfs'; if not provided, the empty value is passed to the associated CSI driver, which determines the default filesystem to apply.

node_publish_secret_ref is a reference to a Secret that contains credentials required by the CSI driver to publish the volume on the node. This field is specified in the CSI volume source and must reference a Secret in the same namespace.
The name of the secret that contains the node publish credentials for the CSI volume.
Whether the CSI volume is mounted as read-only. When true, the volume is mounted read-only; when false, it is mounted read-write if supported.
Specifies the attributes of the CSI volume to be mounted, as defined by the CSI driver.

The downward API volume source, which exposes pod metadata (such as labels, annotations, and field references) as files to the container. This allows containers to consume pod information without needing a Kubernetes API client.
Mode bits to use on created files by default. Must be between 0 and 0777 (0-511 in decimal). Defaults to 0644 (420 decimal).

A list of entries that map specific downward API fields (e.g., pod name, annotations, resource limits) to files within the projected volume. Each item defines the file path and the source field reference.
Configures which pod field's value to expose through the Downward API. The referenced field must be a valid downward API field, such as metadata.name or spec.nodeName.
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath is written in terms of. This field is optional; if not specified, defaults to 'v1'.
The path to the pod field to expose, such as metadata.name, spec.nodeName, or metadata.labels['key'].
The file permission mode bits (octal) for the downward API item in the volume; values must be between 0 and 0777. If unspecified, the volume's defaultMode applies.
Path of the file within the downward API volume where the field's value is written. The path is relative to the volume's root directory.
The resource_field_ref block selects a resource field (e.g., CPU or memory requests/limits) from a container to expose as a file via the downward API volume.

Name of the container to which the resource field reference refers. Required when the resource is a container resource such as requests.cpu or limits.memory; may be omitted for pod-level resources like metadata.name.

Divisor is the divisor for the resource field selector. The resource value is divided by this divisor before being reported. Must be a valid quantity string (e.g., '1m', '1Gi'). Defaults to 1 if not specified.
The resource to select from the container's resource limits or requests, e.g., 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.

Represents an emptyDir volume, which is a temporary directory that shares the pod's lifetime, initially empty, and is deleted when the pod is removed. It can be configured with a medium (for example, Memory) and a size limit.
Specifies the storage medium for the emptyDir volume. Defaults to the node's disk; set to 'Memory' to use a tmpfs (RAM-backed) filesystem.
The total amount of local storage required for this emptyDir volume, specified as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1Gi'). Optional.

Configures an ephemeral volume that is created with the pod and deleted when the pod is removed. It typically includes a volumeClaimTemplate that can be used to generate a persistent volume claim for the volume.

Defines the PersistentVolumeClaim template used to create the backing volume for this ephemeral volume. This allows the ephemeral volume to have a dynamically provisioned PVC with the specified metadata and spec.
Standard Kubernetes object metadata (e.g., labels, annotations) applied to the PersistentVolumeClaim generated from this volume claim template when the ephemeral volume is created.

Annotations is a map of arbitrary string key-value pairs to attach to the generated PersistentVolumeClaim for this ephemeral volume. Unlike labels, annotations are not used by Kubernetes for identification or selection; they can store metadata for tools and external systems.
The timestamp when the object was created, automatically set by the server in RFC3339 format (UTC). This field is read-only and cannot be set by clients.
The timestamp when the object was marked for deletion. This field is set only when the object is being deleted and is used for garbage collection. The value is in RFC3339 format.
A list of finalizer names that must be completed before the underlying PersistentVolumeClaim is removed. Finalizers prevent deletion until all associated resources are cleaned up.

generateName is an optional prefix used by the API server to generate a unique name for the object if `name` is not specified. It ensures a unique name by appending a random suffix to the provided value.

Labels are key/value pairs attached to the ephemeral volume claim template metadata. They can be used to organize, categorize, and select the resulting volume claim, and may be referenced by selectors.
ManagedFields is a list of managed fields entries that track the field ownership and the last time the field was updated by the system.
The API version of the resource that this managed field entry applies to, in the format 'group/version' (e.g., 'v1' or 'apps/v1').
The type of fields managed by the system, typically 'FieldsV1'.
The JSON representation of the set of fields managed by the manager, stored as a FieldsV1 object.

The name of the manager (e.g., a controller, operator, or client) that owns or manages the fields tracked in this managedFields entry. It is part of the Kubernetes ObjectMeta managedFields metadata used for field ownership and conflict resolution.
The operation type that produced this managedFields entry. Valid values are 'Apply' and 'Update'.
The name of the subresource used to update the object, or empty if the request applied to the main resource (e.g., 'status' for status subresource).
Time is the timestamp of when this managed field entry was last modified, in RFC3339 format.

The name of the volume claim template. It is used as a prefix for the generated PersistentVolumeClaim name; if omitted, a name is generated from the volume and pod names. Must be a valid DNS subdomain name.
The namespace for the persistent volume claim template. In the context of an ephemeral volume, this field is ignored, and the resulting claim is created in the pod's namespace.
List of references to owning objects. Each entry includes apiVersion, kind, name, uid, and optional controller and blockOwnerDeletion flags.
The API version of the referenced owner resource, such as 'v1' or 'apps/v1'. This is part of the ownerReference metadata that identifies the owning object.
If true, and if the owner has the 'foregroundDeletion' finalizer, then the owner cannot be deleted from the key-value store until this reference is removed. Defaults to false.
Indicates whether the referenced owner is the managing controller. Only the controller owner can set this to true, and it distinguishes the primary controller among multiple owners.
The kind of the owner object in a Kubernetes OwnerReference, such as 'StatefulSet' or 'ReplicaSet'. Must correspond to a valid Kubernetes resource kind.
The name of the owner object referenced by this OwnerReference. This should match the name of an existing object with the same apiVersion and kind fields in the owner reference entry.
The UID of the referenced owner object. In Kubernetes OwnerReference, this field uniquely identifies the owner object within its API group and kind.

The resource version, a string that identifies the server's internal version of the object. It is used for optimistic concurrency and change detection, such as when performing watch operations or updates.
self_link is a read-only URL representing the object, generated by the API server. It is deprecated and may be empty in newer Kubernetes versions.
UID is the unique identifier assigned by the Kubernetes system to the object. It is system-generated and read-only.
The specification of the PersistentVolumeClaim that is created for this ephemeral volume. This includes fields such as access modes, storage class, and resource requests.

Specifies the access modes for the persistent volume claim. Valid values include ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteMany, and ReadWriteOncePod, defining how the volume can be mounted by nodes and pods.

If set, specifies the source to use to populate the volume. This can be a reference to a VolumeSnapshot, a PersistentVolumeClaim, or another object that supports provisioning a volume from existing data.
The API group of the resource referenced as the data source. If omitted, the core API group is assumed.
The kind of the data source resource, e.g., PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot. This must match the kind of the resource referenced by the name field.
The name of the data source object (as defined by kind and api_group) that provides the volume content for this ephemeral volume claim.

dataSourceRef specifies the object (such as a VolumeSnapshot or PersistentVolumeClaim) to use as the data source when dynamically provisioning the volume. It takes precedence over the dataSource field if both are set.
The API group of the referenced data source. An empty string indicates the core API group; otherwise, it holds the group name (e.g., snapshot.storage.k8s.io for VolumeSnapshot).
The kind of the object referenced as the data source, such as PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot.
The name of the data source object (e.g., a PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot) referenced by this data source reference in the volume claim template.
The namespace of the referenced data source object. This is an optional field in a dataSourceRef, allowing the data source to reside in a different namespace than the volume claim template.
Defines the resource requirements (e.g., storage size) for the ephemeral volume claim, including requests and limits.
The maximum amount of resources (such as CPU and memory) that the ephemeral volume can consume. This is a map of resource names to quantities, e.g., 'cpu' to '500m', 'memory' to '1Gi'.

A map of resource names to requested quantities, where the key is a resource name (e.g., 'storage') and the value is a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., '1Gi'). For volume claim templates, this typically specifies the desired storage size.
A label query over persistent volumes to consider for binding. The selector must match the labels on a PersistentVolume for it to be bound to this claim. Can specify matchLabels and matchExpressions.

match_expressions is a list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and for In/NotIn a set of values. All requirements are ANDed together to determine the set of objects that match the selector.
The label key that this match expression applies to. It must correspond to a label key on the target resource for the selector to match.
Operator represents the relationship between the key and a set of values in a label selector match expression. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values that the selector requirement applies to. Required for operators 'In' and 'NotIn'; must be empty for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist'.

Specifies a map of label keys to values that must match a PersistentVolumeClaim's labels for the claim to be selected by this volume claim template. All key-value pairs in the map must be present on the claim.
The name of the StorageClass to use for this volume claim. If omitted, the cluster's default StorageClass will be used.
The name of the VolumeAttributesClass that defines attributes to apply to the volume. This is part of the alpha VolumeAttributesClass feature, enabling dynamic customization like IOPS or throughput.
VolumeMode defines what type of volume is required by the claim. Valid values are 'Filesystem' and 'Block'; if omitted, the default is 'Filesystem'.
The name of the PersistentVolume to bind this volume claim to. When set, the claim is bound to that specific volume.
fc represents a Fibre Channel volume, allowing attachment of a Fibre Channel disk to the pod. Specify targetWWNs, lun, fsType, and readOnly.
Filesystem type to mount for the Fibre Channel volume. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system, e.g., "ext4" or "xfs". If not specified, it is implicitly inferred.
The logical unit number (LUN) of the Fibre Channel target, identifying the specific storage device for the volume.
Indicates whether the Fibre Channel volume is mounted as read-only. When true, the volume cannot be written to.

List of Fibre Channel target World Wide Names (WWNs) that the volume connects to. Each entry is a string representing a WWN in the format 'naa.<hex>' or similar, identifying a target port for the Fibre Channel volume.
The list of Fibre Channel World Wide Identifiers (WWIDs) for the FC volume. Either this field or a combination of targetWWNs and lun must be set.
flexVolume represents a FlexVolume volume source, which mounts a volume backed by an out-of-tree volume driver. It typically includes the driver name, filesystem type, and driver-specific options.
The name of the driver used for this flex volume.
The filesystem type to mount, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Must be supported by the host operating system. Defaults to 'ext4' if unspecified.
Options is a map of additional command-line options to pass to the flexvolume driver. Each key-value pair is passed as -o key=value to the driver.
Specifies whether the flexVolume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is mounted with read-only access; defaults to false.
secretRef is an optional reference to a Secret that contains sensitive parameters (such as credentials) to be passed to the FlexVolume plugin.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret to use as the secret reference for the flex volume.
Configures a Flocker volume source for the pod. This allows a pod to use storage provided by Flocker.
The name of the Flocker dataset to mount. Exactly one of datasetName or datasetUUID must be specified.
The UUID of the Flocker dataset to mount. This uniquely identifies the dataset to be used as the volume source.
Represents a GCE (Google Compute Engine) Persistent Disk volume source. This object configures how a pre-existing GCE persistent disk is mounted into the pod.
Filesystem type to mount for the GCE persistent disk, such as 'ext4', 'xfs', or 'ntfs'. If unspecified, defaults to 'ext4'.
The partition number on the GCE persistent disk. Must be omitted if the disk is not partitioned.
The unique name of the GCE Persistent Disk to attach to the pod. This name must match the disk resource as it exists in the GCE project.
Specifies whether the GCE persistent disk is mounted as read-only. If set to true, the volume is mounted read-only; if false or omitted, it is mounted read-write.
Configures a volume backed by a Git repository. The repository is cloned into the volume when the pod starts, making the files available to the container.

The target directory name for the git repository inside the volume. If set to '.', the repository is placed directly in the volume root; otherwise, it is placed in a subdirectory with the given name. Must not contain or start with '..'.
The Git repository URL to clone from. This is the location of the remote repository that will be used to populate the volume.
The commit hash, branch, or tag of the Git repository to check out. If not specified, the repository's HEAD is used.
Defines a Glusterfs volume as a storage source. In a pod spec, this allows containers to mount a directory from a Glusterfs filesystem.
The name of the Kubernetes Endpoints object that identifies the GlusterFS cluster to mount. Must be a valid endpoint name in the same namespace.
The path to the Glusterfs volume. This is the Glusterfs volume name as defined on the Glusterfs server.
If true, the GlusterFS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Defines a hostPath volume, which mounts a file or directory from the host node's filesystem into the pod.
Path of the directory or file on the host machine. Must be an absolute path.

Specifies the type of the hostPath volume. Determines how the path on the host is checked, created, or what kind of file system object it must be. Allowed values include: DirectoryOrCreate, Directory, FileOrCreate, File, Socket, CharDevice, BlockDevice, or empty string for no check.
The pull policy for the container image used as a volume source. Allowed values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never.

The reference to the container image used for this image-backed volume. This is a container image name with optional tag or digest, such as `my-app:latest` or `registry.example.com/my-app@sha256:...`.
Represents an iSCSI volume configuration. When specified, the volume is sourced from an iSCSI target.
Enables CHAP authentication for iSCSI discovery. When set to true, the initiator authenticates against the target during the discovery phase.
Enable CHAP authentication for the iSCSI session. When true, the initiator uses CHAP credentials to authenticate during session establishment.
Filesystem type to be used when mounting the iSCSI volume (e.g., ext4, xfs).
Custom iSCSI initiator name used for authentication with the iSCSI target. If specified along with an iSCSI interface, the interface handles network operations for the connection.
The iSCSI Qualified Name (IQN) of the iSCSI target to be mounted as a volume. This uniquely identifies the target on the iSCSI network.
The iSCSI interface name that uses an iSCSI transport. Defaults to 'default' if not specified.
The iSCSI target LUN number.
List of additional iSCSI portals to connect to, in the form host:port (e.g., 10.0.0.1:3260). These portals complement the primary targetPortal for iSCSI connectivity.
If set to true, the iSCSI volume is mounted as read-only. If false or omitted, the volume is mounted read-write.
The secret_ref is a reference to a Secret resource that contains CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI target. It is used to authenticate the initiator to the target.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret object that holds the CHAP credentials for the iSCSI target.
The iSCSI target portal. The portal is either an IP or ip_addr:port if the port is other than default (typically TCP ports 860 and 3260).
The name of the volume. Must be a valid DNS label and unique within the pod.
Configures an NFS (Network File System) volume source. Contains fields for the NFS server address, the exported path, and whether the mount is read-only.
The NFS export path that the server exposes.
Forces the NFS export to be mounted with read-only permissions. Defaults to false.
The hostname or IP address of the NFS server that exports the volume.
Defines a volume that uses a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) as its backing storage. This field appears in a pod's volume list; the referenced PVC must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the PersistentVolumeClaim to reference as the volume source for this pod volume.
If true, the volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Represents a Photon Controller persistent disk volume source. This allows a pod to mount a pre-existing Photon persistent disk as a volume.
Filesystem type to mount for the Photon persistent disk. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system, e.g., 'ext4'.
pdID is the unique identifier of the Photon Controller persistent disk that this volume references.

Configures a Portworx volume as a volume source for the container, allowing the pod to mount a Portworx volume by specifying its volume ID and optional settings like filesystem type and read-only access.
Filesystem type to be mounted on the Portworx volume (e.g., ext4, xfs). If not specified, the volume's existing filesystem type is used.
Defaults to false (read/write). When set to true, mounts the volume as read-only, forcing the readonly setting in VolumeMounts.
The volume ID that uniquely identifies a Portworx volume.
Projected is a volume type that projects multiple existing volume sources (such as ConfigMap, Secret, downward API, and ServiceAccountToken) into the same directory.
The default file permission mode for files in the projected volume, expressed as an octal integer (e.g., 420 for 0644). If not specified, defaults to 0644.
List of volume projections to include in the projected volume. Each projection can reference a configMap, secret, downwardAPI, or serviceAccountToken source.
Specifies a ClusterTrustBundle projection source, which exposes the selected trust bundle as a file inside the projected volume. The bundle can be selected via signer name or label selector.
label_selector is a label selector that filters the ClusterTrustBundles to project. If unspecified, all ClusterTrustBundles are selected.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values, used to filter ClusterTrustBundle objects for projection.
The label key that the selector applies to. This must be a valid label key and is used to match resources that have the corresponding label.
The operator for the label selector requirement. Allowed values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'. This determines the matching condition for the label key against the specified values.

The values field specifies the list of values that the label selector expression matches against. It must be provided for operators 'In' and 'NotIn', and must be empty for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist'.

match_labels is a map of {key,value} pairs used to select ClusterTrustBundle resources by labels. A single {key,value} in the map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions with key, operator In, and the value, and all requirements are combined with a logical AND.
Name of the ClusterTrustBundle resource to project into the volume, used when selecting a single bundle by object name. Mutually exclusive with signerName and labelSelector.
If true, the volume will successfully mount even if the referenced ClusterTrustBundle object does not exist. If false (default), the pod will fail to mount the volume when the bundle is missing.
The relative path within the volume where the cluster trust bundle will be exposed as a file. Must not start with '..' (i.e., cannot go above the volume root).
The name of the signer whose trust bundle should be projected. If empty, all signers are included.
Configuration for a ConfigMap projection in a projected volume. Specifies the name of the ConfigMap and optionally a list of items (keys and paths) to include.

If unspecified, each key-value pair in the Data field of the referenced ConfigMap is projected into the volume as a file using the key as the filename. If specified, only the listed keys are projected into the specified paths, and unlisted keys are not present. Each item maps a key in the ConfigMap to a relative path within the volume.
The key in the ConfigMap to project into the volume.
Optional mode bits used to set permissions on this file. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 or a decimal value between 0 and 511. If omitted, the volume's defaultMode is used.
The relative path within the projected volume where the config map key's value is mounted. Must not contain '..' and must be relative to the volume root; defaults to the key name if not specified.
Name of the ConfigMap to project into the volume. Must be a valid ConfigMap name in the same namespace.
Optional specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. If true, missing ConfigMap or keys are allowed; if false (default), the ConfigMap must exist for the volume to mount.

Configuration for the downward API volume source within a projected volume. It defines which pod metadata (such as labels, annotations, and resource fields) should be exposed as files, using items that refer to fieldRef or resourceFieldRef.
List of DownwardAPIVolumeFile items, each defining how to project a specific pod field or container resource into a file within the projected volume.
Specifies a field in the pod (such as metadata.name or status.podIP) whose value is exposed as a file in the downward API volume.
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1' if not specified.
Specifies the path to the Pod field that will be exposed, such as 'metadata.name' or 'spec.nodeName'.
The file permission mode (e.g., 0644) for the DownwardAPI volume item. If not specified, the default mode is 0644. The value is a Unix permission mode expressed as a number.
Relative path within the projected volume where the selected downward API value is exposed.
resourceFieldRef selects a container resource (e.g., requests.cpu, limits.memory) from the container's resource requirements, and the chosen resource's value is exposed as a projected volume file.
The name of the container to which the resource field refers. In a downward API volume, this field must be specified to select a resource from a specific container.
Specifies the divisor to divide the resource value by, allowing the resource quantity to be expressed as a different unit. Defaults to 1 if unset.
The name of the container resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
The relative path within the projected volume where the pod certificate chain will be mounted for the container to consume.
Relative path inside the projected volume where the pod certificate bundle is mounted. This bundle contains the pod's credentials and is exposed at the specified location within the volume.
Specifies the path within the projected volume where the private key of the pod's certificate is mounted.
The type of cryptographic key to generate for the pod certificate, e.g., RSA or ECDSA.
The maximum expiration time, in seconds, for the pod certificate. This value sets an upper limit on the certificate's lifetime when it is projected into the volume.
The name of the certificate signer that will sign the projected certificate. Must be a valid signer name, such as 'kubernetes.io/legacy-unknown'.
Secret projects a Kubernetes Secret into the volume. It allows specifying the secret name, which keys to expose, and whether the secret is optional.
The list of key-to-path mappings for the secret's keys. If specified, only the listed keys are projected; if omitted, all keys are projected.
The key in the Secret's data to expose for this item in the projected volume.
Optional permission mode for the file, specified as an octal value between 0000 and 0777 (or decimal 0-511). Defaults to the volume's default file mode if not set.
Relative path within the projected volume where the secret key's value is exposed as a file. This path is resolved relative to the volume's root directory.
Name of the referenced Secret in the same namespace.
Specifies whether the referenced Secret or its keys must be defined. If true, the Secret may be absent; if false, it must exist.
Projects a service account token into the volume. Configurable fields include audience, expirationSeconds, and path.
The intended audience (aud) of the service account token. If not specified, the audience defaults to the API server's identifier.

expirationSeconds is the requested duration of validity for the projected service account token, in seconds. If unset, the default is 3600 seconds (1 hour). The token issuer may return a token with a different validity duration.
The relative path to the file that will contain the service account token. This path is resolved within the projected volume mount point.
Optional configuration block for a Quobyte volume source, which allows the pod to mount a Quobyte storage volume.
The group to map volume access to. Defaults to no group.
Marks the Quobyte volume as read-only when set to true. Defaults to false, meaning read-write.
Specifies one or more Quobyte registry services as a comma-separated list of host:port pairs (e.g., "registry1:7861,registry2:7861"). This is used to connect to the Quobyte cluster for volume access.
The Quobyte tenant name associated with the volume.
The user to map volume access to for the Quobyte volume. Defaults to the service account user.
The name of the Quobyte volume to mount.
Configures a Ceph RBD (Rados Block Device) volume source, allowing a Ceph block device to be mounted as a volume in the pod.
Filesystem type of the RBD volume to mount, e.g., 'ext4', 'xfs', 'ntfs'. Defaults to 'ext4' if unspecified.
The name of the RBD (Ceph block device) image to mount. This is a required field for the rbd volume source.
Path to the Ceph keyring file used for RBD authentication. If not specified, the default /etc/ceph/keyring is used.
A list of Ceph monitor endpoints (host:port) used to connect to the Ceph cluster for this RBD volume.
The Ceph pool name in which the RBD image resides. This must match the pool configured on the Ceph cluster.
ReadOnly here will force the ReadOnly setting in VolumeMounts. Defaults to false.

A reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the Ceph authentication keyring for the RBD volume. It overrides the 'keyring' field if both are set. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret that contains the authentication key for the RBD volume.
The RADOS user name for the RBD volume. Defaults to 'admin'. Used for authentication with the Ceph cluster.
Defines a ScaleIO volume source, allowing a pod to use a volume from a ScaleIO storage system.
Filesystem type to mount for the ScaleIO volume (e.g., ext4, xfs). If not specified, the default is ext4.
The host address of the ScaleIO API Gateway.
The name of the ScaleIO protection domain that the storage system uses to isolate and manage storage resources.
Specifies whether the ScaleIO volume is mounted as read-only.
Reference to a Secret containing the ScaleIO storage system credentials. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret object that contains the ScaleIO admin password. This secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Indicates whether the ScaleIO gateway communication uses SSL/TLS. When true, the connection is encrypted using SSL.
Indicates whether the storage access mode is ThickProvisioned or ThinProvisioned. Defaults to ThinProvisioned.
The ScaleIO Storage Pool associated with the protection domain for this volume.
The name of the ScaleIO storage system.
The name of the existing ScaleIO volume to mount.
Secret represents a volume that is populated with data from a Kubernetes Secret resource. The secret's data is mounted into the pod as files.

Specifies the permission bits for files created in the secret volume. Accepts an octal value between 0000 and 0777 (or decimal 0-511); defaults to 0644 (read/write for owner, read for group and others).
Optional list of mappings from secret keys to file paths within the volume. Each item specifies a key from the secret and the path (relative to the volume mount) where its value should be written.
The key within the Secret's data that should be exposed as a file in the volume. This must match a key in the referenced Secret's data map.
Optional file permissions for the secret file, specified as an octal value between 0000 and 0777 (or decimal 0-511). Defaults to the default mode of the secret volume.
The relative path within the volume where the secret key's value is mounted as a file. Must not start with '/' or '..'.
Indicates whether the secret or its keys must be defined. If set to true, the volume is populated only if the secret exists; otherwise, it is empty.
Name of the Secret in the pod's namespace to use. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Ex. 'ext4', 'xfs', 'ntfs'. Defaults to 'ext4'.
Whether the StorageOS volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, write operations will fail. Defaults to false.

Reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the credentials (username and password) needed to access the StorageOS API and manage the volume. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the Secret object that contains the StorageOS API credentials. This Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
volumeName is the human-readable name of the StorageOS volume. This field is required and must match an existing StorageOS volume.
The namespace in which the StorageOS volume is located. If not set, the default namespace is used.
Represents a vSphere volume source, allowing a vSphere datastore volume to be mounted into the pod. This is one of the supported volume types for Kubernetes pods.
Filesystem type to mount. If not specified, defaults to ext4.
Identifier of the vSphere Storage Policy to apply to the volume.
Name of the storage policy to use for the vSphere volume.
Path that identifies the vSphere volume VMDK.

kubernetes_apps_stateful_set.spec.volume.text: The Kubernetes API version of the PersistentVolumeClaim template. Typically 'v1'.
The Kubernetes kind for the volume claim template, which is always 'PersistentVolumeClaim'.

Standard Kubernetes object metadata for the PersistentVolumeClaim template. The name specified here is used as the base for generated PVC names (each replica gets '-<ordinal>' appended). Labels and annotations can be assigned to the resulting claims.

A map of string keys and values that can be used to attach arbitrary non-identifying metadata to the volume claim template. Unlike labels, annotations are not used for identification or selection and can store larger or structured data.
The creation timestamp of the object, in RFC3339 format. This is set by the server and should not be set by clients.

The duration in seconds before the object is deleted. A value of 0 indicates immediate deletion; if unset, the system default applies. In Kubernetes, this field is read-only and typically set by the server during delete requests, not by users.

DeletionTimestamp is an RFC 3339 date and time at which this resource will be deleted. It is set by the server when graceful deletion is requested and is not directly settable by a client. The resource is expected to be deleted after this time once the finalizers list is empty.
Finalizers is a list of strings that must be empty before the object can be deleted. They ensure that cleanup actions are performed before the resource is removed.
generateName is an optional string prefix. When a name is not specified, the Kubernetes API server generates a unique name by appending a random suffix to this prefix.
The generation of the PersistentVolumeClaim created from this template. It is a system-assigned sequence number that increments on each change to the claim's desired state.
Labels are key/value pairs attached to the PersistentVolumeClaim template. They are used for organization and selection, for example to match selectors.

ManagedFields maps workflow-id and version to the set of fields that are managed by that workflow. This is mostly for internal housekeeping, and users typically shouldn't need to set or understand this field.
The API version of the resource that the manager last operated on, e.g., 'apps/v1'.
The type of the fields represented in this managedFields entry (for example, 'FieldsV1').
A JSON representation of the fields that are managed by the manager, corresponding to the Kubernetes `FieldsV1` type.
The manager is an identifier of the entity that manages the fields in this entry, such as a component or tool that last modified the object.
The operation performed by the manager on the resource. Allowed values are "Apply", "Update", and "Delete".
The subresource that this managed fields entry applies to, such as 'status', or an empty string for the object itself.
The timestamp at which this managed fields entry was recorded, in RFC3339 format.
The name of the volume claim template. It is used to form the names of the PersistentVolumeClaims created for each replica, along with the StatefulSet name and the replica's ordinal index.
The namespace of the PersistentVolumeClaim template. If not specified, it defaults to the namespace of the StatefulSet. The value must be a valid Kubernetes namespace name.

A list of references to owning objects (e.g., the StatefulSet). Each reference includes apiVersion, kind, name, uid, and optionally controller and blockOwnerDeletion flags. This field is used for garbage collection and cascading deletion of dependent resources.
The API version of the referenced owner object, e.g., 'apps/v1'.

If true, and the owner has the 'foregroundDeletion' finalizer, the owner cannot be deleted from the key-value store until this reference is removed. Defaults to false; setting it requires delete permission on the owner.
Indicates whether the owner reference points to a controller resource. When true, the owner is the managing controller, and only one controller can own a given object.
Kind of the referent. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds
The name of the owner object referenced by this owner reference. Must be a valid Kubernetes object name.
The unique identifier (UID) of the object referenced by this owner reference.
The version of the object as maintained by the Kubernetes API server. This string changes each time the object is modified, enabling optimistic concurrency control and watch operations.
The URL representing the resource, as assigned by the Kubernetes API server. This is computed and read-only.
The system-assigned unique identifier for the volume claim template metadata object. This read-only string (typically a UUID) uniquely identifies the template within the cluster.
The spec of the volume claim template defines the desired characteristics of the PersistentVolumeClaim to be provisioned, including access modes, resource requests/limits, and storage class.
Specifies the access modes requested for the PersistentVolumeClaim, such as ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteMany, or ReadWriteOncePod.

Specifies an existing object (such as a PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot) to use as the data source for the newly provisioned volume. Corresponds to the dataSource field in a Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaimSpec, typically containing apiGroup, kind, and name.
The API group of the resource referenced as the data source. For example, use 'snapshot.storage.k8s.io' for VolumeSnapshot sources.
Specifies the type of the data source. Allowed values are 'PersistentVolumeClaim' and 'VolumeSnapshot' (or 'VolumeSnapshotContent' in Kubernetes 1.20+).
Name of the data source resource (e.g., a VolumeSnapshot) to use as the source for the volume claim. Must correspond to the kind and apiGroup specified in the dataSource.

Specifies a data source reference (e.g., a VolumeSnapshot, PersistentVolumeClaim, or other resource) from which to provision the volume. This references an object by apiGroup, kind, and name, and is used for volume cloning or snapshot restoration.
The API group of the referenced resource, such as 'snapshot.storage.k8s.io' for VolumeSnapshot. If not set, the core API group is assumed.
The kind of the object referenced as the data source for the volume claim template, such as 'PersistentVolumeClaim'.

The name of the data source object referenced by this dataSourceRef. This must be the name of an existing object of the specified kind and API group, such as a PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot.
Namespace of the referenced data source object. This optional field allows the data source to reside in a different namespace from the PersistentVolumeClaim.
Resources specifies the compute resources required by the persistent volume claim. Typically used to request a specific storage size, for example: requests: { storage: 1Gi }.
Resource limits for the volume claim, specifying the maximum amount of compute resources (e.g., cpu, memory) allowed. Each key is a resource name and the value is a Kubernetes quantity string.
Map of resource names to requested quantities, e.g., 'storage': '1Gi'.
A label query to select persistent volumes for binding. Only volumes matching these labels are considered for the claim.

A list of label selector requirements. Each item defines a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. The selector matches resources that satisfy all specified requirements.
The label key that this selector requirement applies to, used to match labels on the persistent volume claim template.

The operator represents the relationship between a label key and a set of values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. For In and NotIn, values must be provided; for Exists and DoesNotExist, values must be omitted.
values is the list of values for the key. It must be set when the operator is In or NotIn, and must be empty when the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist.
A map of label keys and values that PersistentVolumes must have in order to be selected for the PersistentVolumeClaim. All specified labels must match.
Name of the StorageClass to use for this volume claim. If not specified, the cluster's default StorageClass will be used.
The name of the VolumeAttributesClass to use for the persistent volume claim. If specified, the volume attributes defined by that class are applied to the volume.
Defines the volume mode for the persistent volume claim. Can be 'Filesystem' (default) to format with a filesystem, or 'Block' to expose as a raw block device.
The name of the PersistentVolume to bind to this claim. This is used when a specific PersistentVolume is required, and must match an existing PersistentVolume name.
Specifies the access modes for the persistent volume claim. Allowed values include ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteMany, and ReadWriteOncePod.

A map of resource names to their allocation statuses, indicating whether each resource has been allocated and is ready for use by the volume claim. The value is a string representing the status, such as WaitForFirstConsumer, Scheduled, or ControllerResizeInProgress.

Reports the resources allocated to the persistent volume claim, typically storage, as a map of resource names to quantities (e.g., 'storage': '10Gi'). This reflects the actual storage capacity provisioned for the PVC.
The actual storage capacity allocated to the persistent volume claim, represented as a map of resource names to Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., {'storage': '1Gi'}).
The conditions of the PersistentVolumeClaim created from this template, each containing details such as type, status, reason, and message about the claim's current state.
last_probe_time is the last time the condition was probed, represented as an RFC3339 timestamp string.
The timestamp (RFC3339 string) of the last transition of this condition on the PersistentVolumeClaim.
Human-readable message indicating details about the condition's last transition.
A machine-readable, short, camelCase reason for the condition's last transition, providing a concise code that explains why the condition is in its current state.
The status of the condition, indicating whether the condition is currently true, false, or unknown. Allowed values are "True", "False", and "Unknown".
The type of PersistentVolumeClaim condition. Possible values include 'Resizing' and 'FileSystemResizePending'.
The current name of the VolumeAttributesClass the PVC is using. When unset, there is no VolumeAttributeClass applied. Must be of the same kind as the one set in spec.volumeAttributesClassName.
A human-readable message providing details about the health condition.
last_transition_time is the timestamp at which the health status last changed state, represented as a string in RFC3339 format.
Status of the volume modification operation. Possible values are `Pending`, `InProgress`, and `Infeasible`.
The name of the VolumeAttributesClass that the volume is being modified to use, as tracked in the status of a volume modification operation.
The current phase of the persistent volume claim, which can be Pending, Bound, or Lost.

kubernetes_apps_stateful_set.status.cond.text: The last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. The timestamp is represented as a string in RFC3339 format.
Human-readable message indicating details about the condition, such as the reason for the current condition status.
A machine-readable, CamelCase reason for the condition's last transition, providing a short identifier for why the condition is in the given status.
The status of the condition, indicating whether the condition is True, False, or Unknown.
The type of the StatefulSet condition, for example 'ReplicaFailure'.

A node selector term that defines a set of nodes eligible for this preferred scheduling preference. It contains matchExpressions and/or matchFields requirements that must be satisfied for the preference to apply.
A list of node selector requirements by label key, operator, and values. All requirements in this list must be satisfied by a node for it to match this node affinity preference term.
The node label key that the match expression targets, used to determine which nodes satisfy the preferred scheduling preference.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.

values is a list of string values that correspond to the key in a node selector requirement. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty.

List of node selector requirements that match on node fields (such as metadata.name) to define node affinity preferences. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values, with operators including In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.
The node field key that the matchFields requirement selects on, such as 'metadata.name' or 'spec.unschedulable'.
The operator for matching node label values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.

A list of values that the node's field must match, as determined by the operator in the same requirement. For example, when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn', this list contains the allowed values; for 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty.
The weight associated with this preferred scheduling term, in the range 1-100. Nodes with higher weight are preferred more.

A list of node selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a node label key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional set of values. The node must satisfy all expressions in the term for the pod to be scheduled onto it.
The label key that this match expression applies to, used with the operator and values to constrain node selection.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and value(s). Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.

Specifies the values for the node selector requirement. The semantics depend on the operator: for In and NotIn, this must be a non-empty list of string values; for Exists and DoesNotExist, this must be empty.
A list of node selector requirements that specify constraints on node fields (such as metadata.name). Each requirement defines a key, operator, and list of values that must be satisfied.
The node field key that this match condition applies to. In match_fields, this is typically a field such as metadata.name.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and the set of values in the node selector requirement. Possible values include In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.

The 'values' field is a list of string values for the node selector requirement's match_fields. It is used when the operator is set to In or NotIn to define the set of element values; for operators Exists or DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.
The pod affinity term that defines the label selector and topology constraints for a preferred scheduling rule, softly influencing pod placement.
A standard Kubernetes label selector that identifies the set of pods to which this preferred pod affinity term applies. It uses matchLabels and matchExpressions to define the selection criteria.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values. The selector matches if all requirements are satisfied.
The label key that this match expression applies to. In a Kubernetes label selector, this is the key component of the selector requirement, used to match resources by their labels.

Specifies the relationship between the key and the set of values. Allowed operators are `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, `DoesNotExist`, `Gt`, and `Lt`. The `Exists` and `DoesNotExist` operators do not require a values list.

A list of string values that the label key must match, used in a label selector requirement. The operator determines how these values are used (e.g., In, NotIn). For operators like Exists or DoesNotExist, this list should be empty.
match_labels is a map of key-value pairs used to select pods by their labels. A pod must have all specified label keys and values to be selected for this affinity term.

MatchLabelKeys is a set of pod label keys that the scheduler uses to select which pods are considered for the same pod affinity group. The labels selected by these keys are combined with the label selector to determine the pod affinity term.

List of pod label keys used to filter candidate pods for this affinity term. Only pods whose label values for these keys differ from the incoming pod's values are matched, helping to exclude groups that share the same label values.
A label selector used to filter the namespaces that the pod affinity term applies to. Pods in namespaces matching this selector are considered for the affinity preference.
A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values, and all requirements are ANDed together to define the namespace selector.
The label key that the selector matches against. For a namespace selector, this is a label applied to namespaces. Must be a valid Kubernetes label key.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and the values. Allowed values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'.

values is a list of string values. For the In and NotIn operators, the values array must be non-empty. For the Exists and DoesNotExist operators, the values array must be empty. This field is used to match namespace labels in the pod affinity term's namespace selector.
A map of key/value pairs used to select namespaces by labels. The namespace must have all specified labels to match.
Specifies a static list of namespaces that the pod affinity term applies to. If null or empty, the term applies to the namespace of the pod where the affinity is defined.
The key of the node label used to define the topology domain for pod affinity. Pods are grouped into domains based on this label, and the affinity constraint is evaluated per domain.
The weight for each preferred pod affinity term, an integer between 1 and 100. The scheduler adds the sum of weights of all matching terms to the node's score, making higher weights more preferred.
Specifies a label query to select pods for the affinity rule. This is a standard Kubernetes label selector, which can include matchLabels and matchExpressions.
A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement is an object with key, operator, and optionally values. The requirements are ANDed together to form the label selector.
The label key that the selector operates on. This is the key of a label that must match for the pod affinity rule to apply.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.

A list of values that the label selector must match. The values apply to the operator specified in the match expression; for In and NotIn, the label value must be one of the listed values, while for Exists and DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.
A map of key-value pairs that must match the pod's labels. Each key-value pair is equivalent to a label selector requirement with operator In and that single value.

An optional list of pod label keys. When specified, the values of these labels from the new pod are combined with the labelSelector, so only existing pods that have matching values for these keys (and satisfy the rest of the selector) are considered for the affinity rule.

Specifies a list of label keys. When evaluating pod affinity, a candidate pod that contains any of these label keys with a value different from the corresponding label on the pod being scheduled is excluded from consideration.

A label query over a set of namespaces. The pod affinity term will match only if the pod is scheduled in a namespace that satisfies this label selector. If null, the term applies to the pod's own namespace.

A list of label selector requirements used to select namespaces. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. All requirements are ANDed together.
The label key that the selector applies to. In a namespace selector match expression, this is the Kubernetes namespace label key to match.
The operator represents the key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.
A list of values for the label selector expression. Used with operators such as 'In' and 'NotIn' to match a set of values; not used with 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist'.

match_labels is a map of label keys to values that must match the labels of the namespaces to be selected for the pod affinity rule. Only namespaces that have all the specified key-value pairs are considered.
A list of namespaces that the affinity/anti-affinity term applies to. If omitted, it defaults to the namespace of the pod where the rule is defined.

The key of the node label that defines the topology domain (e.g., 'kubernetes.io/hostname', 'failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone'). For requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution, this field is required and must be non-empty. The scheduler uses the node's value for this key to determine which nodes belong to the same topology domain for pod affinity/anti-affinity placement.

This is the pod affinity term used in a preferred anti-affinity rule. It specifies a set of pods, identified by label selector and topology key, which the scheduler will attempt to avoid placing this pod together with (i.e., co-location is discouraged).
A label selector that defines the group of pods to which this affinity/anti-affinity rule applies. It can use matchLabels and matchExpressions to indicate the target pods.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. The requirements are combined with a logical AND to determine which Pods match the label selector for the pod anti-affinity rule.
The label key that the selector applies to. This key must exist on the pod's labels for the match expression to be considered satisfiable.
The operator specifies the relationship between the label key and the values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values for the label selector expression. Must be provided when the operator is In or NotIn, and must be empty when the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist.
A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels on a pod for the label selector to apply. This defines the set of pods that the anti-affinity term applies to.

matchLabelKeys is a list of pod label keys. When specified, the labels with these keys from the incoming pod are extracted and ANDed with the labels in the labelSelector to determine which existing pods belong to the same group for this affinity/anti-affinity term. Keys that do not exist in the incoming pod are ignored.

mismatch_label_keys is a list of label key strings. The label selector for this pod anti-affinity term is built from the incoming pod's labels, but any labels whose keys are in this list are excluded from the selector. This ensures that differences in these specific label keys do not affect anti-affinity matching.

A label selector for namespaces. If specified, the affinity term applies only to pods in the selected namespaces. This is a standard Kubernetes label selector object (e.g., with matchLabels or matchExpressions).

A list of label selector requirements used to select namespaces. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values, following standard Kubernetes label selector semantics.
The key (name) of the namespace label that this match expression applies to. The selector will match namespaces that have this label key with the specified operator and values.
Operator is the operator applied to the key and values in the match expression. Valid values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'.

A list of string values used in a label selector requirement. For operators In or NotIn, this list specifies the values the label key must match or not match; for operators Exists or DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.
match_labels is a map of key-value pairs used to select namespaces by their labels. Only namespaces with all the specified labels are eligible for the affinity/anti-affinity rule.
A list of namespaces to which this pod anti-affinity term applies. If omitted, it applies to the pod's own namespace; if specified, the selector is evaluated against pods in the listed namespaces.

The key of the node label that the scheduler uses to determine the topology domain for grouping pods. For anti-affinity, this defines the domain over which pods are spread, such as 'kubernetes.io/hostname' for node-level spread.
The weight of the pod anti-affinity term, an integer between 1 and 100. A higher weight gives the term a greater preference during scheduling.

A label selector used to identify the set of pods that the anti-affinity rule applies to. It can include matchLabels and matchExpressions to define the selection criteria, and must be specified for each required anti-affinity term.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement defines a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values; requirements are combined with AND semantics to select the pods for anti-affinity.
The label key that the match expression applies to. It must correspond to a label on the pod being evaluated for anti-affinity.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and the values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
values is a list of string values. When the operator is In or NotIn, this list must be non-empty. When the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.
Specifies a map of {key,value} pairs. A pod is selected if it has labels matching all specified keys and values.

A list of pod label keys that define the set of pods considered for the same pod anti-affinity group. Pods are considered in the same group only if they have equal values for all listed keys present on them; pods lacking a key are ignored for that key.

A label selector used to identify the namespaces to which the pod anti-affinity rule applies. When specified, the anti-affinity term only matches pods running in namespaces that meet this selector; if omitted, it applies only to the pod's own namespace.
A list of label selector requirements for the namespace selector. The requirements are ANDed to select the namespaces to which the rule applies.
The label key that the selector applies to.
Specifies the operator for the label selector requirement. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

A list of string values. When the operator is In or NotIn, this list must be non-empty and contains the set of values for the key. When the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.
A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels on a namespace for the namespace to be selected by this selector.
A list of namespaces to which the label selector applies. If empty, the namespace of the pod being scheduled is used.

The topology key specifies the node label that defines the topology domain (e.g., kubernetes.io/hostname) for the pod anti-affinity rule. The scheduler enforces that no two pods with the same label value are scheduled on the same domain, preventing co-location within that scope.
List of arguments to pass to the container's entrypoint. These override the default CMD specified in the container image.
The command to run in the container, which overrides the image's default entrypoint. It corresponds to the Docker ENTRYPOINT and is passed as the command to the container runtime.
List of environment variables to set in the container. Each environment variable has a name and optionally a value or a valueFrom (source) to resolve the value dynamically.
Name of the environment variable.
The value of the environment variable. This field is optional and is ignored if 'valueFrom' is specified.
Specifies a source for the environment variable's value, such as a ConfigMap key, Secret key, field reference, or resource field reference. Mutually exclusive with 'value'.

Selects a key from a ConfigMap to use as the value for the environment variable. This object includes the name of the ConfigMap, the key to select, and an optional flag to indicate if the reference must be defined.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap to select. The value associated with this key is injected as the environment variable value.
The name of the ConfigMap containing the key to reference.
Specifies whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. When set to true, the system does not fail if the referenced key is absent, and the environment variable may not be set.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, status.podIP) as the value of the environment variable, using the field_path attribute.

The path to the field in the pod to select, such as 'metadata.name' or 'status.podIP'.
Specifies whether the key referenced by this file_key_ref is optional. When set to true, the container will start even if the specified key is absent from the referenced file.
Selects a resource field (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) from the containing container, and uses its value as the environment variable's value.
The name of the container whose resource value is exposed to the environment variable. Defaults to the container in which this field is defined when omitted.
The divisor to divide the selected resource value by, specified as a Kubernetes resource quantity (e.g., '1m'). If omitted, defaults to 1 (no division).
The name of the container resource to select (e.g., 'limits.cpu', 'limits.memory').
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. The Secret must exist before the pod is created.
The key of the secret to select from. Must be a valid secret key.
The name of the Secret from which to select a key. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

Specifies whether the referenced Secret or its key must be defined. If set to true, a missing key or secret does not prevent the container from starting; the environment variable is omitted. If false (default), the key must exist, otherwise the pod creation fails.
List of sources to populate environment variables in the container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret, optionally with a prefix for environment variable names.

Reference to an existing ConfigMap in the same namespace. The ConfigMap's data will be added as environment variables, with each key becoming an environment variable name and its value the variable value. Must specify the ConfigMap name in the 'name' field.
Name of the ConfigMap to reference as the source of environment variables.
Indicates whether the referenced ConfigMap must exist. When set to true, the ConfigMap is allowed to be missing; when false (default), the ConfigMap must exist or the container will not start.
An optional prefix to prepend to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. The resulting string becomes the environment variable name.

A reference to a Kubernetes Secret. The secret's key-value pairs are exposed as environment variables in the container. The object contains the 'name' of the Secret, which must exist in the same namespace as the CronJob.
The name of the Secret to reference. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the CronJob and will provide environment variables.
Indicates whether the referenced secret must exist. When true, the container can start even if the secret is not found; when false or unset, the secret is required to exist.
The container image to run for the container, e.g., nginx:latest or myregistry/myimage:v1.
Specifies the image pull policy for the container. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never.

Lifecycle hooks for the container, allowing actions to be run at specific points in the container's lifecycle. It contains postStart and preStop handlers, each of which can specify an exec command, HTTP GET request, or TCP socket probe.

Configures the postStart lifecycle hook, which runs immediately after the container is started. This allows you to execute custom commands or requests to prepare the container before it begins normal operation.
Exec specifies the action to take, which is to execute a command inside the container. This field is used in the PostStart lifecycle hook to run a command after the container is started.
The command to execute in the container's postStart lifecycle hook. Provided as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are its arguments.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the post-start lifecycle hook. This configures the endpoint that the container runtime will contact after the container starts.
The host name to connect to. Defaults to the pod IP.
Specifies a list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header must define a name and value pair.
The header name for the HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header.
The path to request on the HTTP server when performing the HTTP GET action.
The TCP port to send the HTTP request to. Can be an integer port number or the name of a port defined in the container's ports list.
Protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Specifies the duration in seconds for the sleep action in the lifecycle postStart hook. The container will be paused for this many seconds before continuing startup.
The host name or IP address to connect to. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port number or IETF service name to connect to. Provide a numeric port as a string (e.g., '8080') or use a service name (e.g., 'http').
Defines a handler that is called immediately before a container is terminated, allowing for graceful shutdown or cleanup tasks.
Exec specifies the command to be executed by the container when the pre-stop lifecycle hook is triggered.

Command is the command to run and its arguments, expressed as a list of strings. For this preStop lifecycle hook's exec action, it specifies the command executed inside the container before the container is terminated.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform as the pre-stop lifecycle hook. The request is sent to the container before it is terminated.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set 'Host' in httpHeaders instead.

Custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request sent by the preStop hook. Each element in the list defines a header name and value; these headers are sent along with the HTTP GET to the specified endpoint.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the pre-stop hook's HTTP GET request.
The path to access on the HTTP server.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port in the container definition.
The network protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'http' or 'https'. If not specified, defaults to 'http'.
Specifies the number of seconds the container should sleep before termination, used by the preStop lifecycle hook's sleep action.
The TCP socket action to execute as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It connects to the specified port on the container's IP to notify the container that it is about to be terminated.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket pre-stop hook. If not specified, it defaults to the pod IP.
The port number (as a string) or named port to use for the TCP socket in the pre-stop lifecycle hook. For example, '8080' or a port name defined in the container's ports.
Defines a health check for the container to determine if it is alive. If the check fails, the kubelet restarts the container.
