Exec specifies a command to execute inside the container to determine health. A successful exit code of 0 indicates the container is healthy.
The command to run inside the container for the liveness probe. It is specified as a list of strings, with the first element being the command and the rest being arguments.
Number of consecutive failures for the liveness probe to be considered failed. When this threshold is reached, the container is restarted. Defaults to 3.
The grpc field configures a gRPC-based liveness probe. It specifies the port to check and optionally the service name for the gRPC health check.
The numeric port on which the gRPC health check should be performed. If not specified, it defaults to the first port in the container's containerPort list.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is an empty string.
Configures an HTTP GET request to be sent to the container to check its health. The probe sends an HTTP GET to the container's IP address on the specified port and path.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
A list of custom HTTP headers to send with the probe request. Each header object contains a name and a value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request, such as 'Authorization' or 'X-Custom-Header'. Must be a valid HTTP header field name.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the liveness probe request.
Path to access on the HTTP server, e.g., /healthz. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The TCP port to send the HTTP request to. Can be specified as a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request, either HTTP or HTTPS.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the liveness probe is initiated. Must be a non-negative integer.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds, minimum value is 1.
The minimum consecutive successes for the liveness probe to be considered successful after having failed. For liveness probes, this value must be 1.
Configuration for a TCP socket probe, used to check container liveness by attempting to open a TCP connection to a specified port. The object defines the port and optionally the host to connect to.
The host name or IP address to check via TCP. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port (number or named port) that the liveness probe will attempt to connect to, as defined in the container's TCP socket probe.
Optional duration in seconds for the pod to terminate gracefully. Kubernetes will wait this long after sending a termination signal before forcefully killing the pod. Must be a non-negative integer.
The number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out. Defaults to 1 second.
The name of the container. Must be a DNS_LABEL and unique within the pod.
List of ports to expose from the container. Each entry defines a port with properties like containerPort, hostPort, protocol, and name.
The port number that the container listens on. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The host IP address to bind the host port to. If left empty, the port is bound to all interfaces (0.0.0.0), which is the default.
The port on the host to map to the container port. When set, the container is accessible via that host port. Must be a valid TCP port number (1-65535).
The name of the port, which must be unique within the pod and can be used to reference the port in other resources. If specified, it must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME.
The network protocol used by the container port (e.g., TCP, UDP, SCTP).
A readiness probe checks when a container is ready to accept traffic. If the readiness probe fails, the container is removed from service endpoints until it passes again.
Exec specifies the action to take, which is to run a command inside the container as part of the readiness probe.
Command to run inside the container for the readiness probe. The first element is the executable command, and subsequent elements are arguments (e.g., `["echo", "ok"]`).
The minimum number of consecutive failures for the readiness probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Must be at least 1; defaults to 3.

Specifies a gRPC-based readiness probe handler. The probe connects to the container's gRPC server on the given port and optionally checks a named service (if the service field is omitted, the overall health of the gRPC server is checked).
Port number of the gRPC endpoint used for the readiness probe. Must be a TCP port between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the default is the container name.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to use for the readiness probe. The probe is successful if the response status code is between 200 and 399.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each item specifies a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the readiness probe request, e.g., 'Authorization'.
The value of the HTTP header sent in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports list.
The protocol used for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS', with 'HTTP' as the default.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0 seconds. Minimum value is 0.
Specifies how often (in seconds) the kubelet performs the readiness probe. The default is 10 seconds, and the value must be greater than 0.
The minimum number of consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after it has failed. Defaults to 1.
tcp_socket configures a TCP socket check for the readiness probe. It contains a required 'port' and an optional 'host' to connect to.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The port to connect to for the TCP probe. Can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container.
The duration in seconds that the pod is allowed to terminate gracefully after receiving a termination signal before it is forcibly killed. This is a pod-level setting in Kubernetes.
The timeout in seconds for the readiness probe. Defaults to 1 second if not specified.

A list of resource resize policies for the container. Each policy specifies how the kubelet handles resizing for a given resource (e.g., cpu, memory) and includes a restartPolicy that can be 'NotRequired' or 'RestartContainer'.
The name of the resource (e.g., 'cpu' or 'memory') to which the container resize policy applies.
Defines the restart policy applied to the container when its resource allocations are resized.

Resources describes the compute resource requirements (requests and limits) for the container, including CPU, memory, and ephemeral storage. The requirements are specified as Kubernetes Quantity values.

The list of resource claims that this container requires. Each entry specifies the name of a ResourceClaim and optionally a request for a specific resource class, used for dynamic resource allocation.
The name of the resource claim referenced by this container. It must match the name of a ResourceClaim object in the same namespace as the pod.
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the container. Keys are resource names such as 'cpu' and 'memory', and values are Kubernetes quantities (e.g., '500m', '1Gi').

Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required for the container. The map keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) and values are quantities (e.g., '100m', '1Gi'). If omitted, the container may use default values set by the cluster or the limit if specified.
The restart policy for the pod containing this container. Valid values are Always, OnFailure, or Never.
The action to take when the conditions of this restart policy rule are met.
Operator defines how the container's exit code is compared against the values in the exit_codes set to determine if the restart policy rule applies.
The list of numeric exit codes that this restart policy rule matches.
SecurityContext holds security configuration that will be applied to the container, such as user/group IDs, privileges, and SELinux options.
Controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. If false, the container is prevented from privilege escalation, such as through setuid or setgid binaries.
AppArmor profile configuration for the container. The `type` field accepts `Unconfined`, `RuntimeDefault`, or `LocalHost`; `localhost_profile` is required when `type` is `LocalHost`.
The name of an AppArmor profile that is already loaded on the node. Must be specified when the appArmorProfile type is 'Localhost'. The profile must be preconfigured on the node to work.
The type of AppArmor profile to apply to the container. Valid values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', and 'Unconfined'. When 'Localhost' is set, the 'localhostProfile' field must also be specified.
Linux capabilities that can be added to or dropped from the container's process. The object includes `add` and `drop` lists.
A list of Linux capabilities to add to the container's capability set. Each entry is a capability name (e.g., 'NET_ADMIN', 'SYS_TIME').
A list of Linux capabilities to drop from the default set for the container. For example, 'ALL' drops all capabilities.
Indicates whether the container runs in privileged mode, granting it access to host devices and all capabilities.

procMount denotes the type of proc mount to use for the container. Allowed values are 'Default' for the container runtime defaults and 'Unmasked' to bypass kernel default settings for the proc filesystem.
If true, mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only, preventing modifications to the root filesystem.
The GID (group ID) to run the container's main process as. If unspecified, the container runtime uses the image's primary group or a default.
Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the kubelet will validate that the container does not run as UID 0, and if it does, the container will fail to start.
The user ID (UID) that the container's main process runs as. If not specified, the container runs as the user defined in the image or the runtime default.
SELinux options for the container, including level, role, type, and user used to apply SELinux labeling.
SELinux level as defined in the SELinux MLS/MCS policy, such as s0 or s0:c1,c2. This specifies the sensitivity level and optional categories for the container's SELinux label.
The SELinux role label for the container.
The SELinux type label, which specifies the type portion of the SELinux security context (e.g., 'spc_t').
The user portion of the SELinux context, such as 'system_u'. This is part of the SELinux options applied to the container.
The seccomp profile for the container. This object allows setting the seccomp type (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and optionally specifying a localhost profile path.
Specifies the path to a seccomp profile on the node's localhost filesystem. This is used when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to use. Valid values are RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, and Localhost.

Windows-specific security options for the container. This field applies only to Windows containers and allows configuration of settings such as GMSA credential specifications, host process behavior, and runAsUserName.
The full GMSA credential spec in JSON format to use for the Windows container.
The name of a GMSA credential spec to use for the container's Windows security context.
HostProcess determines if a container should be run as a 'Host Process' container. Allowed values are true or false, with default false.
Specifies the Windows user name to run the container's entrypoint as. If not set, the user defined in the container image is used.

Configures a startup probe, which checks whether the application in the container has started. If a startup probe is defined, it runs first and, until it succeeds, disables the liveness and readiness probes, accommodating containers with slow startup times.
Specifies a command to be run inside the container. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0, and fails if it exits with any non-zero status.
The command to run inside the container for the startup probe. It is a list of strings where the first element is the command and the remaining elements are arguments.
The number of consecutive failures allowed for the startup probe before the container is considered failed. Defaults to 3; must be a positive integer.
Specifies the gRPC health check action for the startup probe, including the port and optional service name to check.
The port number of the gRPC service to connect to for the probe.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health checking protocol.
Specifies a handler that performs an HTTP GET request on the container to check its health. The object defines the request path, port, and optional headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Custom HTTP headers to send with the GET request. Each header is an object with `name` and `value` fields.
The name of the HTTP header to be set in the HTTP GET request of the startup probe.
The value of the HTTP header to send with the GET request of the startup probe.
The HTTP request path to access on the container, such as /healthz. Defaults to '/' if not specified.

The port number or name on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. For a numeric port, specify an integer between 1 and 65535; for a named port, use the name defined in the container's ports.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before startup probes are initiated.
Specifies how often (in seconds) the startup probe runs. Defaults to 10 seconds; minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after a failure. Defaults to 1 and must be 1 for startup probes.

Performs a TCP socket check by attempting to open a connection to the container's IP address on a specified port. Part of the startup probe's action; the probe succeeds if the TCP connection is established.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If omitted, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to for the startup probe. Accepts a numeric port or a named port (string) defined in the container.

Optional duration in seconds for the pod to terminate gracefully after receiving a termination signal. Must be a non-negative integer; a value of 0 means immediate termination, and if omitted, the cluster's default grace period is used.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.

Whether this container should have stdin enabled. When true, the container runtime allocates a standard input stream for the container, allowing interactive processes to read input. Defaults to false.

If true, the container's standard input is attached only once at startup and not kept open for subsequent interactions. This is often used with `stdin` and `tty` to provide one-time input to the container.
Path where the container's termination message is written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Specifies how the termination message from the container is read. Allowed values are 'File' (read from /dev/termination-log, default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError' (fall back to container logs if the file is empty).
Flag indicating whether a TTY (pseudo-terminal) should be allocated for the container. Setting this to true enables interactive terminal use, often required alongside stdin.

List of block devices to be used by the container. Each entry specifies the device path inside the container and the name of a volume with a raw block device, used for volumes that provide block devices rather than file systems.
The path inside the container where the volume device is mounted. This is typically a block device path, such as /dev/sdb, for raw block volumes.
The name of the volume that this device refers to, as defined in the pod's volumes list.
List of volume mounts for the container. Each mount specifies a volume name, mount path, and mount options (e.g., read-only).
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path (e.g., /data). Optionally, use subPath to mount a subdirectory of the volume.
Specifies mount propagation behavior for the volume mount. Allowed values are 'None', 'HostToContainer', and 'Bidirectional'.
The name of the volume to mount, matching the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes list.
Specifies whether the volume mount is mounted as read-only. When true, the volume is read-only, and writes are not allowed.
Specifies whether the volume mount is recursive read-only. Allowed values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', and 'IfPossible' (case-insensitive).
Path within the referenced volume to mount instead of the volume's root.
Specifies a sub-path within the volume to mount, supporting environment variable expansion using $(VAR_NAME) syntax. This allows dynamic paths based on pod environment variables.
The container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime's default is used, and the directory must exist in the container image.
Name of the DNS resolver option. This is the key of the option, corresponding to an option name in the resolv.conf configuration.
The value for the DNS resolver option. This can be empty if the option is a boolean flag.
Arguments to the entrypoint of the ephemeral container. Overrides the default arguments (CMD) from the container image.
The command to run in the ephemeral container, specified as a list of string arguments. Overrides the image's default entrypoint.
List of environment variables to set for the ephemeral container. Each item defines a variable name and a value, or a source for the value.
The name of the environment variable in the ephemeral container's environment.
The value of the environment variable. This field is mutually exclusive with valueFrom and defaults to an empty string if not specified.

value_from specifies a source for the environment variable's value, such as a reference to a ConfigMap key, a Secret key, a pod field, or a resource. Only one of 'value' or 'value_from' may be specified.
Selects a specific key from a ConfigMap to provide the value for an environment variable. This object must include the ConfigMap's name and the desired key.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap to select for the environment variable's value. This must correspond to a key present in the ConfigMap data or binaryData.
The name of the ConfigMap to select the key from. This refers to a Kubernetes ConfigMap object in the same namespace as the pod.
Optional indicates whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If set to true, and the key does not exist, the value from the ConfigMap is treated as absent rather than causing an error.

field_ref provides a reference to a pod field, such as metadata.name or status.podIP, whose value is used as the environment variable's value. It is one of the possible sources in a Kubernetes env valueFrom.
Version of the schema the fieldPath is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1'.
The path to the field to select, such as 'metadata.name' or 'status.podIP'.
Whether the referenced file key is optional. If true, the container will start even if the key does not exist; if false, the key must be present for the container to start.
The name of the volume that contains the file from which the environment variable's value is read.
Selects a resource field (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) of the container to use as the value of the environment variable.
The name of the container whose resource value is to be selected. If omitted, the container making the request (the ephemeral container) is used.
The divisor value by which the resource's value is divided to produce the final value for the environment variable. Must be a valid quantity (e.g., '1', '100m'). Defaults to 1 if not specified.
Resource is the name of the container resource to select, such as 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory', whose value is exposed to the environment variable.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. The value of the Secret key is used as the value for the environment variable.
The key in the Secret to use as the value. Must correspond to a key present in the referenced Secret.
The name of the Secret in which the selected key is located. This specifies the Secret resource from which the environment variable's value is pulled.
Specifies whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If true and the Secret or key does not exist, the environment variable is not set and the container can still start. Defaults to false.

envFrom is a list of sources that populate environment variables in the ephemeral container. Each source can reference a ConfigMap, a Secret, or a prefix to apply to those references, following standard Kubernetes container envFrom semantics.
Reference to a ConfigMap used to populate environment variables in the container. The keys in the ConfigMap data become environment variable names.
Name of the ConfigMap to reference as the source of environment variables.
Indicates whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If true, the ConfigMap may be absent; if false or omitted, the ConfigMap must exist and a missing reference causes an error.

An optional prefix that is prepended to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret when populating environment variables. If specified, the resulting environment variable names will be <prefix><key>.
Reference to a Secret in the same namespace. The Secret's data keys become environment variable names, and each key's value becomes the environment variable's value.
Name of the Secret to use as the source for environment variables in the ephemeral container.
Specify whether the Secret must be defined. If set to true, the Secret can be undefined and the environment variables from it are omitted. Defaults to false.
Specifies the container image to use for the ephemeral container, following standard container image naming conventions (e.g., repository/name:tag).

The image pull policy for the ephemeral container. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never. If omitted, Kubernetes defaults based on the image tag: Always for :latest, otherwise IfNotPresent.
Configures container lifecycle hooks. For ephemeral containers, Kubernetes does not support lifecycle hooks, so setting this field is not allowed.

The postStart handler is executed immediately after the container is started. It can be used to perform initialization or to signal that the container is ready. The handler configuration is done via exec, http_get, or tcp_socket sub-blocks.
Exec specifies the action to execute a command inside the container as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. It defines a command to run when the container starts.
Specifies the command to run inside the container. It is a list of strings where the first element is the executable and the rest are arguments, executed directly without a shell.

Configuration for an HTTP GET request to be executed as a lifecycle hook (postStart) on an ephemeral container. It specifies the endpoint, port, and other request parameters according to the Kubernetes HTTPGetAction schema.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
A list of custom HTTP headers to send with the GET request. Each item in the list specifies a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header sent in the HTTPGet request.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server when performing the HTTP GET request. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port number or name to use for the HTTP GET request. This can be a numeric port or a named port, specified as a string.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Sleep represents the sleep action for the postStart lifecycle hook. It pauses the container for a specified duration, with the number of seconds defined in the 'seconds' field.
The number of seconds to sleep in the SleepAction lifecycle handler. Must be a non-negative integer.

Represents a TCP socket action for the lifecycle hook. This action attempts to open a TCP socket to the specified port on the container; the hook succeeds if the connection is established. It contains the port (required) and optionally the host to connect to.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, it defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to for the socket action. Can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The pre_stop lifecycle hook is executed immediately before a container is terminated, allowing for graceful shutdown or cleanup operations.
Exec runs a command inside the container as the pre-stop lifecycle hook action.
The command to run in the container for the preStop lifecycle hook. It is a list of strings, with the first element as the command and subsequent elements as arguments to the command.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as a lifecycle hook. The kubelet sends this request to the container when the preStop hook is triggered.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; you may prefer to set the Host header via httpHeaders instead.

A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each item in the list is an object with `name` and `value` fields, allowing you to set specific headers (e.g., Authorization) for the preStop lifecycle hook request.
The header field name for the HTTP header to send with the request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. This can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the connection: either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Sleep specifies the sleep action for the preStop lifecycle hook. It configures the number of seconds the container should sleep before termination.
The number of seconds to sleep before the container is terminated.

Specifies a TCP socket to connect to as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. Kubernetes attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port; the container is considered successfully stopped after the connection is established.
Host name or IP address to connect to. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to connect to. Can be a numeric port or a named port from the container's ports.

LivenessProbe defines how to probe the ephemeral container to determine if it is healthy and when to restart it if the probe fails. It is a standard Kubernetes probe configuration object with fields like exec, httpGet, tcpSocket, initialDelaySeconds, periodSeconds, etc.
The exec action for the liveness probe, which runs a command inside the container to check its health. This is a Kubernetes ExecAction, specifying the command to execute.
The command to run inside the container as part of the exec-based liveness probe. The first element is the command, and any remaining elements are arguments passed to it.
The number of consecutive failures required for the liveness probe to be considered failed, after which the container is restarted.
When set, configures the liveness probe to use a gRPC health check, specifying the port (and optionally a service name) for the gRPC server.
The port number on the container to which the gRPC health check will connect.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health check protocol.
Defines the HTTP GET request to perform against the container for the liveness probe. Includes settings such as path, port, and HTTP headers.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Custom HTTP headers to send in the HTTP GET request of the liveness probe. Each item in the list represents a header with `name` and `value` fields.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the request. This should be a valid HTTP header name, such as 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the liveness probe request.
The HTTP path to request when performing the HTTP GET on the container's liveness probe.
Port number to access on the container. Must be an integer value or a named port (string) defined in the container's ports, e.g., 8080 or 'http'.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request, either `HTTP` or `HTTPS`. Defaults to `HTTP`.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the liveness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0.
The number of seconds between liveness probe checks. If not set, the Kubernetes default of 10 seconds is used.
Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For liveness probes, this must be 1. Defaults to 1, with a minimum value of 1.
TCP socket probe configuration. Performs a TCP check against the specified port on the container's IP address. Optionally, a host can be specified.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket health check. If not specified, it defaults to the pod's IP address.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535. Name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME.
The duration in seconds that the pod is allowed to terminate gracefully after receiving a termination signal. A value of 0 means immediate termination; the default is 30 seconds.
Specifies the number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out. Defaults to 1; the minimum value is 1.
The name of the ephemeral container.
List of ports to expose from the ephemeral container. Each port specifies a network port that the container listens on, including protocol and container port.
The port number that the container listens on. This is the network port exposed by the container, typically an integer between 1 and 65535.
The host IP address to bind the container port to. If not specified, the port is bound to all interfaces (0.0.0.0).
The port on the host node to map to the container port. If not specified, the container port is not exposed externally and is only reachable within the pod's network.
The name of the port, which must be a valid DNS_LABEL and unique among all named ports in the pod. This name is used to reference the port in other contexts such as services or probes.
The protocol (L4) used for the container port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP; defaults to TCP.
Defines a probe that determines when the ephemeral container is ready to accept traffic. If the probe fails, the container is considered not ready and is removed from service endpoints.
Exec specifies the command to execute inside the container as part of a probe. The container's exit code determines success (0) or failure (non-zero).

The command to execute inside the container. It is exec'd directly, not run in a shell; exit status 0 indicates success (healthy), non-zero indicates failure. The working directory defaults to the container's root filesystem.
The number of consecutive failures required for the readiness probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.
Specifies the gRPC probe configuration, including the port and optional service name to use for the health check.
The port number of the gRPC service to probe. This is a required field for a gRPC probe, specifying the network port on which the container's gRPC server is listening.
Service is the name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is empty string, which checks the overall server status.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform for the readiness probe. This includes the path, port, and optional headers for the HTTP request.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET, defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set "Host" in httpHeaders instead.
Specifies custom HTTP headers to include in the probe's HTTP GET request. Each item in the list defines a header with a name and value.
Name of the HTTP header to include in the request. For example, 'Authorization' for a bearer token.
The value of the HTTP header for the readiness probe.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.

The port number (e.g., '80') or name of the port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Can be a numeric port expressed as a string (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0.
Specifies the number of seconds between consecutive readiness probe executions.
Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after a failure. Defaults to 1; the minimum allowed value is 1.
Configures a TCP socket probe action for the readiness probe, checking that a TCP connection can be established to the container on the specified port (and optionally host).
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to for the readiness probe. This can be a numeric port (as a string) or a named port defined in the container's ports.

The number of seconds a pod is allowed to terminate gracefully before being forcefully killed. If not set, the Kubernetes default of 30 seconds applies. This is a pod-level setting, not specific to any container probe.
The number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. The value must be greater than or equal to 1; if not specified, it defaults to 1 second.

List of resource resize policies for the container. Each policy specifies a resource name (cpu or memory) and a restart policy (NotRequired or RestartContainer) indicating whether the container should be restarted when a resize is requested.
The name of the resource (e.g., CPU or memory) to which this container resize policy applies.
The restart policy for container resize operations. Valid values are 'NotRequired' (resize without restarting the container) and 'RestartContainer' (restart the container to apply the resize).
Resources specifies the compute resource requirements (CPU, memory) for the ephemeral container, including requests and limits.
Claims lists the names of resources defined in the pod's spec.resourceClaims that are used by this container. This is used for dynamic resource allocation.
Name of the resource claim, which must match a claim defined in the pod's resourceClaims field.
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. For example: cpu: "1", memory: "1Gi". More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required for the ephemeral container. Keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) and values are Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., '100m', '1Gi').
A list of numeric exit codes for which this restart policy rule is triggered.

SecurityContext holds security configuration that will be applied to the ephemeral container. It includes fields such as runAsUser, runAsGroup, capabilities, seLinuxOptions, and allowPrivilegeEscalation, among others. If both this and the pod-level security context are set, the container-level settings take precedence.

Controls whether the ephemeral container's processes can gain more privileges than their parent process. When set to false, the no_new_privs flag is set, preventing privilege escalation. When true, privilege escalation is allowed.

AppArmorProfile is a Kubernetes object that specifies the AppArmor profile for the container. It contains a type field (e.g., Localhost, RuntimeDefault, Unconfined) and an optional localhostProfile naming a profile preloaded on the node.
The name of a preconfigured AppArmor profile on the node. The profile must be installed on the node and match the name of a profile available for the container runtime to use.
The type of AppArmor profile to use for the ephemeral container's security context.
Defines the Linux capabilities to add to or drop from the container's process capabilities. The object contains lists of capability names under 'add' and 'drop'.

A list of Linux capabilities to add to the container's security context. Each item is a string representing a capability, e.g., 'NET_ADMIN', 'SYS_TIME'. These capabilities are granted to the container's processes in addition to the default set.
Specifies a list of Linux capabilities to remove from the container's effective capability set. Valid entries are Linux capability names, such as 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN' or 'CAP_NET_RAW'.
Whether the ephemeral container runs in privileged mode, granting it access to all host devices and capabilities equivalent to root on the host. Defaults to false.
The proc mount to use for the container. Allowed values are "Default" and "Unmasked".
When set to true, the root filesystem of the ephemeral container is mounted read-only, preventing writes to the root filesystem.
Sets the group ID (GID) that container processes will run as. Must be a positive integer.
Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. When set to true, the kubelet will refuse to start the container if it would run as UID 0 (root).
The UID to run the container process as. If unspecified, the default user in the container image is used.
SELinuxOptions defines the SELinux context (user, role, type, and level) for the ephemeral container. If omitted, the container inherits the SELinux context of the pod or uses the cluster default.
The SELinux level label for the container, typically expressed as a sensitivity category (e.g., s0 or s0:c123).
SELinux role label applied to the container. This is part of the SELinux options defining the security context.
SELinux type label.
The SELinux user label that the container process will run with. Part of the SELinux context.

Configures the seccomp profile for the container. The profile type must be one of RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, or Localhost; if Localhost, the localhostProfile field must specify the path to the profile on the node.
The path to a locally defined seccomp profile on the node, used when type is Localhost.
The seccomp profile type. Allowed values are RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, and Localhost (when a profile is specified in localhostProfile).
Windows-specific security settings applied to ephemeral containers in the pod's security context.

The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for this Windows container. The credential spec is used to configure the container to run with a specific Group Managed Service Account, enabling domain access.
The name of the Group Managed Service Account (gMSA) credential spec to use for the Windows security context.

Specifies whether the container should be treated as a host process container. When true, the container's processes run directly on the host, with access to the host's process namespace and other resources. Defaults to false.

Specifies the Windows username to run the container's entrypoint process as. Defaults to the user specified in the image metadata if not set, and may also be set at the pod level, with this container-level value taking precedence.

Startup probe that indicates whether the container has started successfully. If configured, the kubelet uses it to disable liveness and readiness checks until it succeeds, useful for slow-starting containers.
Exec configures a probe action that runs a command inside the container. The command is specified as an array of strings, and the probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0.
The command to execute in the container, specified as a list of strings. The first element is the command, and subsequent elements are arguments; it is executed directly without a shell.
Minimum consecutive failures for the startup probe to be considered failed. Once this threshold is reached, the container is restarted. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 3.

Configures a gRPC-based health check for the startup probe. The container must implement the gRPC health checking protocol, and the probe will invoke it to determine when the container has started successfully.
Port number on the container for the gRPC startup probe; the gRPC service must be listening on this port.
Specifies the name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If omitted, the default is to check the overall service status.
Configures an HTTP GET request as the action for the startup probe. This is used to check the health of the ephemeral container by sending an HTTP GET request to the specified endpoint.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; to set the Host header, use httpHeaders instead.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the probe's HTTP GET request. Each header is specified as an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
Name of the HTTP header to send in the request.
The value of the HTTP header field sent in the HTTP GET request of the startup probe.
Path to access on the HTTP server.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535. Name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. This delays the start of the probe to allow the container to initialize.
Specifies the frequency (in seconds) at which the startup probe is performed. Must be greater than 0. Defaults to 10 seconds.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1 and must be 1 for startup probes.
Configures the TCP socket action for the startup probe. Specifies the host and port to check by attempting to open a TCP connection.
The host name to connect to for the TCP probe. Defaults to the pod IP when not specified.
The TCP port to connect to on the container. Can be a port number (1-65535) or a named port (an IANA_SVC_NAME).
Optional duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully. Must be a non-negative integer. A value of zero means delete immediately. If unset, the default grace period is used.
Number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. Defaults to 1 second.
Whether this ephemeral container should allocate a buffer for stdin in the container runtime. When false, reads from stdin in the container always result in EOF. Defaults to false.

If true, the container runtime closes the stdin channel after it has been opened by a single attach. For ephemeral containers, when stdin is true and stdinOnce is true, stdin is opened on container start, remains empty until the first client attaches, then remains open until the client disconnects, after which it is closed and remains closed until the container is restarted.

The name of the container in the Pod that this ephemeral container targets, used to share the process namespace and other debugging resources with that specific container. If not set, it defaults to the first container in the pod.

Path at which the file containing the container's termination message is written. The message is captured by the kubelet when the container terminates and is used to record exit information. Defaults to /dev/termination-log if not set.

Defines how the termination message of the ephemeral container is populated. Allowed values are 'File' (default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'. With 'FallbackToLogsOnError', the container log is used as the termination message if the container exits with an error and the termination message file is empty.
Allocate a pseudo-TTY for the ephemeral container. If true, the container gets an interactive terminal. Defaults to false.

List of volume devices to be mounted as raw block devices inside the container. Each item in the list specifies a devicePath (the path in the container where the device is exposed) and the name of the volume (must match a volume defined in the pod).
The path inside the container where the volume device will be mounted.
Name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod.
List of volume mounts to be attached to the ephemeral container. Each mount specifies a volume and a mount path within the container's filesystem.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path and must not contain ':'.
Determines how mount propagation is handled between the host and the container. Supported values: None, HostToContainer, Bidirectional. When not set, None is used.
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
Specifies whether the volume mount is read-only. If true, the container can only read from the mounted volume.

recursiveReadOnly controls whether the volume mount is recursively read-only. Valid values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', and 'IfPossible'. When set to 'Enabled', the mount and all its subdirectories become read-only; 'Disabled' disables this behavior; 'IfPossible' enables it only if the underlying filesystem supports it.
Specifies a sub-path inside the referenced volume to mount instead of the volume root. Useful for mounting a single file or directory from a volume.
An expression that defines the subpath within the volume to mount, supporting environment variable expansion using $(VAR_NAME) syntax.
The working directory for the ephemeral container. If not set, the container runtime uses the image's default working directory.
The list of hostnames to be included in the pod's /etc/hosts file, associated with the IP address specified in the parent hostAliases entry.
The IP address to which the hostnames in this hostAliases entry resolve.
The name of the image pull secret in the same namespace, used to authenticate with container registries.
Arguments to the entrypoint command. Overrides the image's default arguments (CMD) when specified.

The command to run in the init container. This corresponds to the container's entrypoint, overriding the image's default command. It is specified as a list of strings; the first element is the command, and subsequent elements are arguments.
Environment variables to set for the init container. Typically a list of objects each containing a name and value or value_from source.
Name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier as required by Kubernetes.
The value of the environment variable. This sets the literal value for the env var in the init container's environment.

value_from is an object that specifies the source for the environment variable's value, allowing it to be populated from a ConfigMap, Secret, or other field reference rather than a literal value. Supported sources include configMapKeyRef, secretKeyRef, fieldRef, and resourceFieldRef.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to provide the value for the environment variable in the init container.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap that provides the value for this environment variable. The key must exist in the specified ConfigMap.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference. This specifies which ConfigMap's key is used to populate the environment variable's value.
Indicates whether the config map or its key must be defined. If set to true, the value is optional and missing keys won't cause errors; if false or unset, the config map and key must exist.

field_ref is a reference to a field in the pod's spec or status. It selects one of the supported fields: spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.hostIP, status.podIP, or status.podIPs, using apiVersion (e.g., v1) and fieldPath.
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath is written in terms of. Typically 'v1'.
The path to the field of the pod to select, such as metadata.name, metadata.namespace, or spec.nodeName.
Indicates whether the referenced key must be present. Set to true to allow the key to be missing without causing an error; otherwise the key is required.
Selects a resource field of the container (e.g., limits.cpu or limits.memory) and exposes its value as an environment variable. The resource field is specified using a ResourceFieldSelector object.
The name of the container. Required if the resource is a container resource; if not specified, defaults to the container of the current pod.
The divisor to use when retrieving the value from a resource field. It must be a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1', '1k', '100m') and defaults to '1'.
The resource name to select from the pod's resource fields, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. The referenced Secret and key must exist, and the value is injected as the environment variable's value.
The key within the referenced Kubernetes Secret to select, whose value is used as the environment variable's value.
The name of the Secret in the pod's namespace to select from.
Indicates whether the secret key must be defined. If true, the key is optional and its absence does not prevent the container from starting; if false (default), the referenced key must exist.

envFrom is a list of sources to populate environment variables in the container from ConfigMaps or Secrets. Each entry can specify a configMapRef or secretRef, and an optional prefix for variable names.
config_map_ref is an object that refers to a ConfigMap whose key-value pairs are exported as environment variables. It contains the name of the ConfigMap.
The name of the ConfigMap to use for populating environment variables. This is a required field that references the ConfigMap by its name in the same namespace.
Indicates whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If set to true, the ConfigMap is optional and its absence will not cause an error.
An optional identifier prepended to each key from the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. Must be a valid C identifier.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret to use as a source for environment variables. The Secret must be present in the same namespace as the Pod.
Name of the Secret in the same namespace to use for injecting environment variables. Must be a valid DNS subdomain name.
Indicates whether the referenced Secret must be present. If true, the Secret may be absent and the container still starts; if false, the Secret must exist.
The container image to run for the init container, specified as a name and tag (e.g., 'busybox:1.36') or a digest reference.
The image pull policy for this init container. Allowed values are Always, Never, and IfNotPresent. Defaults to Always if the image tag is :latest, otherwise IfNotPresent.
Defines lifecycle hooks (postStart and preStop) for the init container. These hooks allow you to run custom commands or HTTP requests at container startup and before shutdown.

The postStart lifecycle hook handler, executed immediately after a container is started. This block defines actions (such as exec or httpGet) that run before the container's entrypoint completes, and if the handler fails, the container is killed and restarted according to its restart policy.
Exec specifies the exec handler for the postStart lifecycle hook, which runs a command in the container.
The command to run inside the container as the postStart lifecycle hook. It is an array of strings, where the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to execute as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. Includes details such as path, port, and optional headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include with the HTTP GET request. Each header object contains a `name` and `value` field.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP request.
The value of the HTTP header, used in a postStart lifecycle hook's HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The TCP port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request, typically HTTP or HTTPS. If not specified, the default is HTTP.
Scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'.
The number of seconds the container will sleep after starting before continuing with the postStart hook.

Represents a TCP socket action that Kubernetes executes during the postStart lifecycle hook. It specifies the host and port to connect to, and the hook is considered successful if the TCP connection succeeds.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The port number or name of the TCP socket to connect to. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port on the container.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that defines an action to be run immediately before a container is terminated. It is used to perform graceful shutdown or cleanup operations before the container receives a SIGTERM and stops.
Exec specifies the action to take for the lifecycle hook, which is to execute a command inside the container. The 'command' field within this object defines the command to run.
The command to execute as the pre-stop hook, given as a list of strings representing the command and its arguments. This runs inside the init container before it is stopped.
HTTPGetAction describes an HTTP GET request to be performed by the pre-stop handler. It specifies the endpoint to send the request to, including host, port, path, scheme, and HTTP headers.
The hostname to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
A list of custom HTTP headers to send with the GET request. Each item contains a header name and value.
Name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP request.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent in the GET request.
The path to access on the HTTP server for the pre-stop hook's HTTP GET request.
The port number or name of the port to use for the HTTP GET request in the preStop lifecycle hook. It can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use when issuing the HTTP GET request in the pre-stop lifecycle hook.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Sleep is an optional lifecycle handler that pauses the container for a specified number of seconds before termination. It contains a 'seconds' field indicating the sleep duration.
Specifies the number of seconds the container sleeps during the preStop lifecycle hook before termination continues.
Represents a TCP socket action for the lifecycle pre-stop hook. The container runtime attempts to open the specified socket to trigger the hook.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket pre-stop hook. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port number or a named port. The port can be specified as a numeric value (e.g., 8080) or as a string referencing a named port in the container's definition.
Specifies the liveness probe for the init container. This defines the health check that determines whether the container is alive; if the probe fails, the kubelet restarts the container.
Exec specifies the exec action for the liveness probe, running a command inside the container to check its health.
The command line to execute inside the container for the exec liveness probe. It is an array of strings, executed directly without a shell.
The number of consecutive failures required before the probe is considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1.
Specifies the gRPC health probe parameters for the liveness probe, including the port to query and an optional service name. Used to check container health via gRPC health checking protocol.
The port number to which the gRPC probe will connect. This must be a valid port on the container.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is empty.
Configures an HTTP GET request to perform for the liveness probe. The HTTPGetAction object includes parameters such as host, path, port, scheme, and httpHeaders.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. You may want to set 'Host' in httpHeaders instead.

A list of HTTP headers to send with the HTTP request. Each item in the list is an object with `name` and `value` fields, allowing custom headers such as Authorization or Content-Type to be set for the probe.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request, e.g. 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header used in the HTTP GET request for the liveness probe. This is the value part of the header that is sent with the request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.

The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME. If not specified, defaults to the first listening port of the container.
The protocol scheme to use for the HTTP request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Applies to the liveness probe for an init container.
The frequency in seconds at which the liveness probe is performed. Defaults to 10; must be at least 1.

Minimum consecutive successful probe results required for the liveness probe to be considered successful after it has previously failed. For liveness probes, this value must be set to 1 (the default); larger values are not allowed.
Configuration for a TCP socket liveness probe. It specifies the port to check and optionally the host to connect to, as defined by the Kubernetes TCPSocketAction.
Specifies the host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket liveness probe. If not set, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port to connect to for the liveness probe. Can be a numeric port or a named port as defined in the container's ports.
The number of seconds the container is allowed to terminate gracefully after receiving a termination signal before it is forcibly killed. A value of 0 causes immediate termination.
The number of seconds after which the liveness probe is considered failed if it has not completed. This is a standard Kubernetes probe timeout setting.
Name of the init container. Must be unique within the pod.
List of ports to expose from the container. Each item defines a network port, typically with containerPort (the port number), protocol (TCP or UDP), and optionally name and hostPort.
The port number that the container exposes or listens on.
The host IP address to bind the port to. If not specified, the port is bound to all interfaces (0.0.0.0).
The port on the host node that is mapped to the container port. When specified, the container port is accessible via this host port.

The name of the port, used for referencing the port within the container. Must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME (lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, up to 15 characters), and each named port in a pod must have a unique name.
The protocol for the container port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP. Defaults to TCP.
Configures a readiness probe for the container. A readiness probe determines when the container is considered ready to accept traffic, as defined by the kubelet.
Defines a command-based readiness probe. It is an ExecAction object containing a command (list of strings) to run inside the container; the probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0.

The command to execute inside the container for the readiness probe. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the command and the rest are arguments. This is required when using an exec probe.
The number of times Kubernetes will retry a failed probe before giving up. For a readiness probe, giving up marks the Pod as not ready.
grpc specifies the gRPC-based health check settings for the probe. It defines the port to check and, optionally, the service name for the gRPC health check.
The port number of the gRPC service to probe. Must be between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is an empty string.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform for the readiness probe. Defines the endpoint to check, including host, path, port, and HTTP headers.
The hostname to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; it is often preferable to set the Host header via http_headers instead.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP request. Each header is an object with name and value fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request. For example, "Authorization" or "Content-Type".
The value of the HTTP header used in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request.
The HTTP GET path to access on the container's server for this readiness probe.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET probe. Must be a valid integer port number or a named port in the container's ports list.
The protocol scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated.
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds; minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the readiness probe to be considered successful after having failed. For readiness probes, this defaults to 1 and must be at least 1.
Specifies a TCP socket handler for the readiness probe. The probe attempts to establish a TCP connection to the container on a given port (and optionally a host) to determine readiness.
The host name to connect to for the TCP probe. If not specified, it defaults to the pod IP address.
The port number or name of the port to connect to for the TCP socket check. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535, or a valid IANA_SVC_NAME (port name) defined in the container.
The number of seconds after which the probe times out. If not specified, the default is 1 second, and the value must be a positive integer.

A list of resource resize policies for this container, defining how CPU and memory resource changes are handled. Each item specifies a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the restart policy to apply when that resource is resized.
The name of the resource to which this resize policy applies. Supported values include 'cpu' and 'memory'.

Defines how the container handles a resource resize. Allowed values are 'NotRequired' (resize applied without restarting the container) and 'RestartContainer' (container is restarted to apply the resize).

Resources specifies the compute resources required by the init container, including requests and limits for CPU and memory. For example, it can define the minimum amount of resources the container needs (requests) and the maximum it can use (limits).
Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this container.
Name of the ResourceClaim referenced by this container's resource claim entry.
Limits specifies the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the init container. Each entry maps a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) to a quantity string (e.g., '100m', '1Gi').

Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. The keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) and the values are Kubernetes quantity strings, such as '100m' for 0.1 CPU or '1Gi' for 1 gibibyte of memory.
The exit codes of the init container that are covered by this restart policy rule, presented as an object mapping exit codes to their specific policy settings.
The comparison operator used to match the container's exit code against the specified value in the exit code condition.
A list of numeric exit codes that identify the container termination statuses to which this restart policy rule applies.
Security settings applied to the init container, such as UID/GID, user, and Linux capabilities.
Controls whether a process in the container can gain more privileges than its parent process. If set to false, no_new_privs is set, and setuid/setgid binaries cannot escalate privileges.
AppArmor profile configuration for the container. Specifies the type of AppArmor profile to apply (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and optionally the profile name for Localhost type.
The name of an AppArmor profile already loaded on the node. This field is only valid when the appArmorProfile type is set to Localhost.
The type of AppArmor profile to apply. Allowed values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', and 'Unconfined'.
Specifies the Linux capabilities to add or remove for the init container. The value is an object with 'add' and 'drop' lists to grant or restrict container privileges.
Specifies the Linux capabilities to add to the container's effective capability set. Each entry is a capability name (e.g., 'NET_ADMIN', 'SYS_TIME').
The list of capabilities to remove from the container's default capability set. For example, 'ALL' removes all capabilities, or specific names like 'NET_RAW'.
Indicates whether the container should run in privileged mode, granting it access to all devices on the host and capabilities equivalent to root.
Sets the proc mount mode for the container. Valid values are 'Default' (standard proc filesystem) or 'Unmasked' (full, unmasked view).
If true, the container's root filesystem is mounted read-only, preventing any writes to the root filesystem. This is a security hardening measure that helps reduce the attack surface.
The GID (group ID) to run the container's entrypoint and processes with. When set, it overrides the primary group from the image's user metadata.
Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. If true, the kubelet will validate that the container does not run as root (UID 0) and will fail to start if it would.
The user ID (UID) that the init container's processes will run as. This overrides the default user specified in the container image.
Defines the SELinux labels applied to the container, including the user, role, type, and level.
The SELinux level for the container's security context, such as s0 or s0:c123.
The SELinux role label for the process.
The SELinux type label that applies to the container, part of the SELinux security context.
The SELinux user label for the container, e.g., 'system_u'. It defines the user portion of the SELinux security context.

Defines the seccomp profile to apply to the container, restricting available system calls. Typically includes a type (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, Localhost) and optionally a localhostProfile path when type is Localhost.
localhost_profile specifies the path to a seccomp profile on the node's local filesystem. It is used when the seccomp profile type is set to 'Localhost'.
The type of the seccomp profile. Must be one of 'RuntimeDefault', 'Unconfined', or 'Localhost'.
Windows-specific security options for the container, such as GMSA credentials and run-as-username settings. This field is only applicable to Windows containers.
The GMSA credential spec inlined by the GMSA admission webhook, containing the contents of the GMSA credential spec for the Windows container.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the container.
Determines if the container should be run as a 'Host Process' container on Windows. All containers in a pod must have the same effective HostProcess value. Default is false.

The Windows username to run the container process as. Defaults to the user specified in the image metadata if unspecified. When set, this value overrides any value set in the PodSecurityContext's WindowsOptions for this container.

Startup probe configured for this init container. It determines when the container has started successfully, supporting slow-starting applications by delaying liveness/readiness probes until startup completes. The probe configuration can include HTTP requests, TCP connections, or exec commands, along with settings like initial delay, timeout, and failure threshold.

Exec specifies a command to run inside the container as a health check. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0. The command is an array of strings; the first element is the executable, and the remaining elements are arguments.

The command to run inside the container for the startup probe. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed in the container's working directory.
The number of consecutive failures of the startup probe after which the container is considered failed and will be restarted or terminated. Must be a positive integer.
Configures gRPC-based health checking for the startup probe.
The port number of the gRPC service to probe. This is required and must be a valid TCP port number (1-65535).
Specifies the name of the service to be checked in the gRPC health check request. If omitted, the gRPC health check is performed without a service name, and the behavior depends on the gRPC server.

Specifies the HTTP GET action for the startup probe. The probe sends an HTTP GET request to the container's IP address on the specified port and path; a response with status code 200-399 indicates success.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Optional list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request performed by the probe. Each header is defined by a name and a value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP GET request of the startup probe.
The HTTP request path to access on the server, e.g., /healthz.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid integer port number (1-65535) or a named port (IANA_SVC_NAME).
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request in the startup probe.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated.
Specifies the interval in seconds between startup probe checks. The value must be a positive integer (minimum 1).
The minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after a failure. In Kubernetes, for startup and liveness probes, this value must be set to 1.
Specifies a TCP socket probe action, which attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's IP address on a specified port to determine if the container is healthy.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The name or number of the TCP port to connect to for the startup probe. This can be an integer port number or a named port defined in the container's ports.
Number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. If the probe does not complete within this time, it is considered failed.
Whether the container runtime should allocate a stdin stream for this init container. Defaults to false.

If true, stdin is opened on container start and remains open until the first client attaches, then accepts data until that client disconnects, at which point stdin closes and stays closed until the container restarts. This prevents processes reading from stdin from receiving an EOF before the first attach.
Path where the container writes termination messages, which Kubernetes retrieves when the container terminates. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Sets how the container's termination message is read. Allowed values are 'File' (default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'. With 'File', the termination message is read from the file /dev/termination-log; with 'FallbackToLogsOnError', if the container exits with an error, the last chunk of container logs is used as the termination message.
Indicates whether a pseudo-TTY is allocated for the container. When set to true, standard input is connected to the container's terminal.
List of volume devices to be used by the container, referencing block devices defined in the pod's volumes. Each entry specifies a device path inside the container and the corresponding volume name.
The path inside the container where the volume device is mounted. This is required for each volume device entry and must be a valid absolute path.
The name of the volume that this device refers to, matching a volume defined in the pod's volumes.
List of volume mounts for the init container, specifying which volumes are mounted and at which mount path within the container's filesystem.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path and cannot contain ':' after the drive letter (if any).
Specifies how host mounts are propagated to the container and vice versa. Allowed values are 'None', 'HostToContainer', and 'Bidirectional'.
The name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
Specifies whether the volume mount is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the container cannot write to the mounted volume; when false or omitted, the volume is mounted read-write.
Controls whether recursive read-only mounts are enabled for the volume mount. Allowed values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', and 'IfPossible'.

Specifies a sub-path within the referenced volume that should be mounted into the container at the mount path, instead of the volume's root. This allows mounting only a specific directory or file from the volume.
sub_path_expr is an alternative to sub_path for specifying a subpath within a volume. It supports environment variable expansion using the $(VAR_NAME) syntax, and is mutually exclusive with sub_path.
The container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime's default is used, which may be configured in the container image.
The condition type that must be satisfied for the pod to be considered ready, as specified in a readiness gate. This corresponds to a condition name in the pod's Conditions list.
Name of the resource claim. This name must be unique within the pod and is used to reference the claim from containers.
The name of the ResourceClaim object that provides the resources for this claim.
The name of a ResourceClaimTemplate object in the same namespace that defines the resource claims for this pod. The pod's claim is created from this template.
Name must match the name of a resource claim defined in the pod's `spec.resourceClaims` where the container runs. This binds the resource claim to the container so it can be used.
The name of the scheduling gate. The pod remains unschedulable until all gates listed in schedulingGates are removed.
The name of the sysctl parameter, such as 'kernel.shm_rmid_forced'. It specifies which kernel parameter to set in the pod's security context.
The value to assign to the sysctl parameter. This is a string, e.g., '1' or '0' for boolean-like settings, or other kernel parameter values.
The effect of the taint that this toleration matches. Allowed values: NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, NoExecute. If empty, matches all effects.
The key of the taint that this toleration applies to. An empty key with operator 'Exists' matches all keys.
The operator used to match a taint key against the toleration. Allowed values are "Exists" and "Equal". Defaults to "Equal".
The duration in seconds for which the pod will tolerate the taint when the effect is NoExecute. If omitted, the toleration lasts indefinitely.
The value to match with the taint's value when the operator is 'Equal'. If the operator is 'Exists', this field is ignored.
A label selector used to identify the set of pods to which this topology spread constraint applies. If omitted, the constraint applies to all pods in the namespace.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and for In/NotIn, a list of values. This is used to select pods based on label expressions.
The label key that the selector applies to, used in match expressions for label selection (e.g., 'app' or 'environment').
Specifies the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a match expression. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values that the key must match when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'. For operators 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty.
matchLabels is a map of key-value pairs. The topology spread constraint applies to pods whose labels match all of the specified label keys and values.
A list of pod label keys used to select the pods over which the topology spread constraint is calculated. Only pods that have all the specified label keys are included in the spread calculation.

The maximum skew is the maximum allowed difference in the number of matching pods across topology domains. The scheduler enforces that the spread of pods does not exceed this value when distributing pods according to the specified topology spread constraint.

Minimum number of eligible domains required for Pod topology spread to be applied. If the number of matching domains is below this value, the global minimum is treated as zero, changing skew calculation. Must be greater than 0.
Defines how to handle tainted nodes when spreading pods. Allowed values: 'Honor' and 'Ignore'.
The key of node labels that identifies the topology domain (e.g., 'kubernetes.io/hostname' or 'topology.kubernetes.io/zone') across which pods are spread.

Specifies how to handle a pod that does not satisfy the topology spread constraint. Allowed values: `DoNotSchedule` (default) prevents scheduling, `ScheduleAnyway` still schedules while attempting to minimize skew.
Configures a volume backed by an AWS Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume. This object contains settings such as the volume ID, filesystem type, partition, and whether the volume is read-only.
Filesystem type to mount for the AWS EBS volume. Defaults to ext4 if not specified. Supported values include ext4, ext3, and xfs.
The partition number on the AWS EBS volume to mount. If omitted, the first partition is used.
If true, the AWS Elastic Block Store volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
