The volume ID of the AWS EBS volume to be mounted.
azure_disk configures an Azure Data Disk as a volume in a Kubernetes pod. It specifies the disk name, disk URI, caching mode, filesystem type, and read-only setting.
Caching mode for the Azure data disk. Allowed values: None, ReadOnly, ReadWrite.
The name of the Azure data disk to attach. This is the name of the disk as it appears in Azure blob storage.

The URI of the Azure disk to attach to the pod. This uniquely identifies the disk resource in Azure, typically following the pattern /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/{diskName}.
Filesystem type to mount, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Must be supported by the host operating system.
Kind of the Azure disk to use. Allowed values are 'Shared' (default), 'Dedicated', and 'Managed'.
Specifies whether the Azure disk is mounted as read-only in the container. When true, the volume is read-only and writes are not allowed.
Represents an Azure File Service mount on the host and bind mount to the pod. This volume source allows the pod to mount an Azure file share.
Indicates whether the Azure file share is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that contains the Azure Storage account name and key. This secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the Azure file share to be mounted.
Defines a CephFS volume. This is used to mount a Ceph Filesystem (CephFS) into the pod.
Required. A list of Ceph monitor addresses (host:port) for the CephFS volume.
The CephFS path that is mounted as the mount point. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
Optional: Defaults to false (read/write). When set to true, forces the volume to be mounted as read-only, overriding the ReadOnly setting in VolumeMounts.
Path to the key ring file for the Ceph user. Defaults to /etc/ceph/user.secret.

secretRef is an optional reference to a Kubernetes secret that contains Ceph authentication credentials (e.g., user and keyring) for the CephFS volume. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes/#cephfs.
Name of the Secret object that contains CephFS credentials. This Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
The rados user name used to connect to the CephFS. If not provided, the default user is 'admin'.
Configuration for a Cinder volume (OpenStack block storage) to be mounted into the pod. This volume source allows using a Cinder storage volume.
The filesystem type (e.g., ext4, xfs) to mount on the Cinder volume. If not specified, the default filesystem type of the volume is used.
If true, the Cinder volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read/write). This forces the read-only setting in volume mounts.
Reference to a Secret that contains authentication credentials for the Cinder volume. The Secret must exist in the same Kubernetes namespace as the pod.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret that provides authentication credentials for the Cinder volume.
Volume ID used to identify the Cinder volume in Cinder.

ConfigMap represents a configMap that should populate this volume. This volume source is used to mount data from a Kubernetes ConfigMap into the pod, and the object typically specifies the ConfigMap name and optionally the items to select.

Sets the default file permissions (mode bits) for files in the ConfigMap volume. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 (or decimal 0-511); common values include 0644 (owner read/write, group/others read) and 0600.
Optional list of key-to-path mappings to project specific keys from the ConfigMap into the volume. If omitted, all keys are projected as files with their names as paths.
The key within the ConfigMap data to be used as the source for this volume item. The corresponding value from the ConfigMap will be written to the file specified by 'path'.
The permission bits for the file, in octal (e.g., 0644). If not specified, the default is 0644.
The relative path within the volume where the value from the corresponding ConfigMap key is mounted. This path is relative to the volume's mount point.
The name of the ConfigMap to mount as a volume. It must refer to a ConfigMap in the same namespace as the Pod.
Optional specifies whether the ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. When true, the volume is populated only if the ConfigMap exists; otherwise it is empty.

Specifies a volume backed by a CSI (Container Storage Interface) driver. This allows the pod to use a volume provisioned by an installed CSI driver, with configuration options like driver, fsType, and volumeAttributes.
The name of the CSI driver that provides the volume. This is a required field when using the CSI volume source.
Filesystem type to mount, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. If not specified, the CSI driver determines the filesystem type.
A reference to a Secret in the same namespace containing credentials needed by the CSI driver to complete NodePublishVolume and NodeUnpublishVolume calls.
The name of the Secret object in the same namespace that provides node-publish secrets for the CSI volume.
Specifies whether the CSI volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; when false (default), it is read-write.
Additional parameters for the volume, as defined by the CSI driver. This is a map of string keys to string values that are passed to the CSI driver to configure the volume.
Represents a volume that contains the downward API, which exposes pod and container fields as files to the container.
The default file mode (permission bits) applied to files in the downward API volume. Must be an octal integer (e.g., 0644); defaults to 0644 when omitted.
A list of mappings from downward API fields to files. Each item specifies a file path and the field to project into that path (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace, or resource limits/requests).

Selects a field from the pod (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace) and writes its value into the file. The reference consists of an apiVersion (optional) and a fieldPath that points to the desired field.
The version of the schema that the fieldPath is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1'.
The path to the pod field to expose via the downward API volume, such as metadata.name or metadata.namespace.
Optional file permission mode bits, specified as an octal value between 0000 and 0777 (or decimal between 0 and 511). Overrides the volume's defaultMode for this file.
Path is the relative path of the file within the volume where the downward API field is exposed. It must be a relative path and cannot contain '..' segments.

Specifies a container resource (such as requests.cpu or limits.memory) to be exposed via the downward API volume. This is a ResourceFieldSelector object, defining the resource field and optional divisor.
The name of the container to which the resource field refers. Required when the selected resource is a container resource (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory).
The divisor to scale the resource value by, specified as a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., "1", "100m", "1Gi"). If not set, defaults to "1".
The container resource whose value is exposed through the downward API. Valid values include 'limits.cpu', 'limits.memory', 'requests.cpu', and 'requests.memory'.

Represents an EmptyDir volume, which is a temporary directory that is created when the pod is assigned to a node and persists only as long as the pod is running. It starts empty and can be used for sharing data between containers in the same pod.
Specifies the storage medium for the emptyDir volume. Set to 'Memory' to use a tmpfs (RAM-backed filesystem), or leave empty to use the node's default disk-backed storage.
Specifies the total amount of local storage required for this EmptyDir volume. The value is a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1Gi'), and if not set, the node's default limit applies.
Ephemeral represents an ephemeral volume that is created and deleted along with the pod. It supports volume claim templates and CSI ephemeral volumes.
Specifies a template for a PersistentVolumeClaim that will be created for the pod's ephemeral volume. This allows the ephemeral volume to be backed by a dynamically provisioned persistent volume.

Standard Kubernetes object metadata for the volume claim template. This includes labels and annotations that will be applied to the generated PersistentVolumeClaim. The name field is typically not set here because the PVC name is generated automatically from the pod and volume names.
A map of arbitrary key-value pairs that can be used to attach non-identifying metadata to the volume claim template, such as annotations consumed by tools or libraries.
The creation timestamp of the object, in RFC3339 format (e.g., '2025-01-01T12:00:00Z'). This field is set by the server and is generally read-only.

The grace period in seconds before the underlying PersistentVolumeClaim is deleted. Must be a non-negative integer; zero means delete immediately. If not set, the default grace period for the resource type is used.
The time at which the object is being deleted, set only when graceful deletion is in progress. This field is used to coordinate cleanup and is read-only.
A list of finalizer strings that must be empty before the resource is deleted. Kubernetes uses finalizers to ensure that cleanup actions are performed before an object is removed from the cluster.
If 'name' is not provided, this string is used as a prefix to generate a unique name for the volume claim template's metadata. Kubernetes will append a random suffix to ensure uniqueness.

A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state, set and incremented by the system. This field is read-only and intended for internal use, such as optimistic concurrency tracking.

Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize (scope and select) the volume claim template. These labels are attached to the resulting PersistentVolumeClaim and can be used for selection and grouping.

A list of entries tracking which controller or process manages each field of the object, including operation type, API version, and owned fields. This is used for server-side apply and conflict resolution in Kubernetes.
The API version of the Kubernetes object that this managedFields entry describes.
The type of the fields in the managed field entry. In Kubernetes, this value is always 'FieldsV1'.
fields_v1 is a JSON object (fieldsV1 in Kubernetes) that holds the fields and their values managed by a specific manager, as part of a managedFields entry in the metadata.
The name of the manager (such as a controller or kubectl) that owns or last modified the fields.
The type of operation performed on the managed field, such as Apply, Update, or Delete.
The subresource used by the manager for this managed field entry. For most resources it is empty (the main resource), while values like 'status' or 'scale' indicate the subresource that was modified.
Time is a string in RFC3339 format indicating when the last operation was applied to the managed field entry.

The namespace in which the persistent volume claim is created. Note: Kubernetes volume claim templates only permit labels and annotations in metadata; the namespace field is not allowed and setting it may be rejected by the API server.
List of references to owning objects. If all owners are removed, the object is garbage collected. If a controller manages this object, it includes an entry with controller=true.
The API version of the referent object.

If true, and if the owner has the foregroundDeletion finalizer, the owner cannot be deleted from the key-value store until this reference is removed. Defaults to false. Setting this field requires delete permission on the owner.
Indicates whether this owner reference points to the managing controller. When true, the owner reference is considered the controller managing the object.
The kind of the referenced owner object, such as 'CronJob' or 'ReplicaSet'. Must match the kind of the object that owns this resource.
The name of the owner object that this reference points to.
The UID of the referent object, as returned by the Kubernetes API. This field is required and uniquely identifies the owner.

An opaque value that represents the internal version of the object, used for optimistic concurrency control and change detection. Clients must treat this value as opaque and pass it back unmodified when updating the object.
A read-only URL representing the object's location in the Kubernetes API. This field is deprecated in Kubernetes and may be removed in future versions.
UID is the unique identifier of this object, assigned by the server upon creation. This value is system-generated and read-only.
spec is the specification of the persistent volume claim that will be created for this ephemeral volume. It includes settings like access modes, storage class, and resource requests.
A list of access modes for the ephemeral volume claim, such as ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteMany, or ReadWriteOncePod. This defines how the volume can be mounted by nodes and pods.

Specifies the data source for the persistent volume claim. References a TypedLocalObjectReference (apiGroup, kind, name) that can point to a volume snapshot, another PVC, or a custom resource to populate the new PVC.

The API group of the resource referenced by the data source. For core resources (e.g., PersistentVolumeClaim), this field may be empty; for other types like VolumeSnapshot, it must be set to the appropriate group, such as 'snapshot.storage.k8s.io'.
Kind of the referenced data source object, such as 'PersistentVolumeClaim' or 'VolumeSnapshot'.
Name of the referenced data source object (e.g., a VolumeSnapshot, PersistentVolumeClaim, or other resource) as defined by the kind and apiGroup fields.

Reference to a data source (e.g., a VolumeSnapshot or PersistentVolumeClaim) used to populate the volume when the claim is created. Corresponds to the `dataSourceRef` field in the PersistentVolumeClaim spec.
The API group of the referenced resource. For example, when referencing a VolumeSnapshot, set this to 'snapshot.storage.k8s.io'. If not specified, the resource is assumed to be in the core API group.
Kind is the kind of the referenced data source, such as 'PersistentVolumeClaim' or 'VolumeSnapshot'. It identifies the type of the object referred to by the dataSourceRef.
The name of the referenced object in the data source reference. This is the object name (e.g., a PersistentVolumeClaim) that the volume claim will use as its data source.
The namespace of the referenced data source. If not specified, it defaults to the same namespace as the pod.

Resource requirements for the volume claim, specifying the storage size requested (and optionally limited) via the 'requests' and 'limits' sub-fields. For example, 'resources.requests.storage' defines the desired capacity, such as '1Gi'.

Limits specifies the maximum amount of resources allowed for the volume claim, such as storage size. The map's keys are resource names (e.g., 'storage') and values are quantity strings (e.g., '10Gi').
Requests specifies the minimum amount of compute resources for the volume claim. Keys are resource names (e.g., 'cpu', 'memory'), values are Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., '500m', '1Gi').
A label query over PersistentVolumes to consider for binding this claim. It supports matchLabels and matchExpressions to select volumes by their labels.

A list of label selector requirements for selecting the persistent volume claim referenced by the ephemeral volume. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values, following standard Kubernetes LabelSelector semantics.
The label key that this match expression applies to. The selector matches resources that have a label with this key, subject to the operator and values in the same expression.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and a set of values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty.

A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels on a PersistentVolume for the volume claim to be bound. This is part of the label selector in the PersistentVolumeClaim spec within an ephemeral volume's volume claim template.
Name of the StorageClass to be used for the ephemeral volume's PersistentVolumeClaim. If not specified, the default StorageClass is used.

The name of a VolumeAttributesClass to apply to this ephemeral volume. This field is optional and allows dynamic volume attributes (such as IOPS or throughput) to be set via a VolumeAttributesClass resource in the cluster.
Specifies the volume mode for the ephemeral volume claim. Must be 'Filesystem' (default) or 'Block'.
The name of a specific PersistentVolume to bind to this claim. When set, the system binds to that PV; when left empty, the system dynamically provisions or selects an available PV.
Represents a Fibre Channel volume source. Used to mount a Fibre Channel LUN into the pod.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system (e.g., ext4, xfs, ntfs). If unspecified, it is implicitly inferred to be ext4.
The Logical Unit Number (LUN) of the Fibre Channel volume. Required for Fibre Channel volumes.
Boolean flag indicating whether the Fibre Channel volume should be mounted as read-only. Defaults to false, allowing read-write access.
List of Fibre Channel target World Wide Names (WWNs) that the FC volume will connect to. Each WWN is a string, typically in the format 'naa.<hex>' or 'ieee.<hex>'.
List of Fibre Channel WWIDs (World Wide Identifiers) for the volume. Either wwids or targetWWNs and lun must be specified, but not both.
Configures a FlexVolume volume, which mounts a volume using a user-defined driver. This object specifies the driver name, file system type, mount options, and read-only setting.
The name of the FlexVolume driver to use for this volume.
The filesystem type to use when mounting the flex volume, such as ext4 or xfs. Defaults to ext4 if unspecified.
A map of driver-specific options for the FlexVolume. These are passed as command-line arguments to the FlexVolume driver to configure the volume.
Optional: mount the flex volume as read-only. Defaults to false (read/write).
Optional reference to a Secret in the same namespace, providing secret data to the FlexVolume driver. The object's 'name' field specifies the Secret's name.
The name of the Secret in the pod's namespace that provides the secret data for the flexVolume.
Configures a Flocker volume source, allowing the pod to mount a dataset managed by Flocker.
The name of the Flocker dataset to mount as a volume.
The UUID of the Flocker dataset to use. Mutually exclusive with dataset_name.
gcePersistentDisk represents a GCE Persistent Disk volume that is attached to the kubelet's host machine and then exposed to the pod.
The filesystem type to mount (e.g., ext4, xfs). If not specified, the default is ext4. This applies to the GCE persistent disk volume.
The partition number on the GCE persistent disk. If omitted or 0, the entire disk is used as a single volume.
The name of the GCE persistent disk to mount as a volume in the pod.
Indicates whether the GCE persistent disk is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read-write).
Represents a volume sourced from a Git repository. The volume is populated by cloning the repository into an empty directory, allowing configuration of repository URL, revision, and directory.
Target directory inside the volume where the git repository will be checked out. Defaults to the volume root if not specified.
The URL of the Git repository to clone into the volume.
The commit hash, tag, or branch to check out from the git repository. If not specified, the default is HEAD.
The name of the Kubernetes Endpoints object that identifies the Gluster cluster. This must be a valid endpoints object name in the same namespace.
Path is the Glusterfs volume path within the Glusterfs endpoint. It is a required field.
Mounted read-only if true, read-write otherwise. Defaults to false.

hostPath represents a pre-existing file or directory on the host machine's filesystem that is directly exposed to the container. This volume type is useful for accessing host-level data such as Docker sockets or logs.
Path of the directory on the host. Must be an absolute path.
The type of host path volume. Valid values: '', DirectoryOrCreate, Directory, FileOrCreate, File, Socket, CharDevice, BlockDevice. If not set, the type defaults to '' (no type check).

Configures a volume backed by a container image, which is mounted as a read-only filesystem. This object includes fields such as 'reference' to specify the image and 'pullPolicy' to control image pull behavior.
Specifies when to pull the container image used as a volume source. Allowed values are Always, Never, and IfNotPresent. Defaults to IfNotPresent if not specified.
The container image reference (e.g., 'nginx:latest') that defines the image to mount as a volume.
Configures an iSCSI volume, allowing the pod to mount an external iSCSI target as a volume. The node must have the iSCSI initiator installed.
Indicates whether CHAP authentication is enabled for iSCSI discovery. When true, CHAP authentication will be used during discovery.
Indicates whether to enable CHAP authentication for the iSCSI session.
Filesystem type to mount for the ISCSI volume, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. If not specified, it is typically inferred as ext4; the filesystem type must be supported by the host operating system.
The iSCSI initiator name. If not specified, the default initiator name is used.
The iSCSI Qualified Name (IQN) of the target. This is the unique identifier of the iSCSI target and is required for this volume type.
The iSCSI interface name that uses an iSCSI transport. Defaults to 'default' (tcp).
lun is the iSCSI Target Lun number. It is required and must be an integer.
List of iSCSI target portals. Each portal is either an IP address or ip_addr:port if the port is other than the default (typically TCP ports 860 and 3260).
Mounts the iSCSI volume as read-only. When set to true, the volume is mounted with read-only permissions.
Reference to a Secret that contains CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI target.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that holds the CHAP authentication credentials for the ISCSI target. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The iSCSI target portal, specified as an IP address or hostname, optionally with a port (e.g., 10.0.0.3:3260). This is the endpoint through which the iSCSI volume is accessed.
Name of the volume. Must be a DNS_LABEL and unique within the pod. Used to reference the volume from containers.
Specifies an NFS (Network File System) volume source, defining the NFS server, exported path, and optional read-only mount. This allows the pod to mount a filesystem exported by an NFS server.
Path that is exported by the NFS server. This is the directory on the NFS server to mount.
Whether the NFS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read/write).
The hostname or IP address of the NFS server. This field is required when using an NFS volume.

Configures a volume that references a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC) in the same namespace. The PVC must exist before the pod is created, and the volume is mounted with the storage and access modes defined by the claim.
The name of the PersistentVolumeClaim in the same namespace as the pod. This claim is used as the volume source for the container.
If true, the persistent volume claim is mounted as read-only in the pod.

Represents a Photon Controller persistent disk volume source, used to attach an existing Photon persistent disk to the pod. This object typically contains the required 'pdID' and optional 'fsType' fields.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Ex. 'ext4', 'xfs', 'ntfs'.
pdID is the identifier of the Photon Controller persistent disk to be mounted.

portworx_volume is a volume source that represents a Portworx volume, allowing a Portworx block volume to be mounted into the pod. It typically includes settings such as volumeID, fsType, and readOnly.
Filesystem type to mount, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system; if unset, the filesystem type is inferred from the volume format.
Specifies whether the Portworx volume is mounted read-only. Defaults to false (read-write).
The unique ID of the Portworx volume to mount. This is required to identify the specific volume in the Portworx storage system.
Represents a projected volume source, which can combine multiple volume sources (such as secrets, config maps, downward API, and service account tokens) into a single directory mounted to the pod.

defaultMode is the mode bits used to set permissions on created files by default. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 (or decimal 0 to 511). Directories within the path are not affected by this setting.
List of volume projections to include in the projected volume. Each source can be a configMap, secret, downwardAPI, or serviceAccountToken.

cluster_trust_bundle is an object that configures a projected volume source for a ClusterTrustBundle. It injects the trust bundle (a set of CA certificates) from a specified ClusterTrustBundle object into the volume, allowing pods to trust certificates issued by the cluster.

The label_selector is a standard Kubernetes label selector (with matchLabels and matchExpressions) that determines which ClusterTrustBundle resources are selected for projection into the volume. Only bundles matching this selector will be included.
A list of label selector requirements used to filter resources by label keys and values. Each requirement consists of a key, an operator, and optionally a set of values.
The key of the label that this selector expression matches. This is part of a label selector match expression in a projected volume from a cluster trust bundle.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Must be one of `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, or `DoesNotExist`.
The list of values that the key must match for operators such as In and NotIn. It must be empty for operators Exists and DoesNotExist.

A map of key-value pairs that specifies the label requirements for selecting ClusterTrustBundle resources. Multiple labels are ANDed, meaning all specified label pairs must match for a resource to be selected.
The name of the ClusterTrustBundle resource to project. If empty, all ClusterTrustBundles for the specified signerName are projected.

Indicates whether the referenced ClusterTrustBundle is required to exist. If true, the pod will continue to run even if the ClusterTrustBundle is not found; if false (default), the pod will fail to start when the ClusterTrustBundle is missing.
Path is the relative path of the file to which the cluster trust bundle is written. It must not be an absolute path and must not contain '..' elements.
Select all ClusterTrustBundles that match this signer name. Mutually exclusive with name; if name is empty, signerName must be set.
config_map is the ConfigMap source for the projected volume. It defines which ConfigMap to project into the volume, including optional items to select specific keys and their paths.

Maps keys in the referenced ConfigMap to file paths in the projected volume. If omitted, all ConfigMap data keys become files named by the key; if specified, only the listed keys are projected to their mapped paths.
The key to select from the ConfigMap data. The selected value is exposed as a file in the projected volume.
Optional file permission bits for the item, expressed as an octal integer (e.g., 0644). Must be between 0 and 0777. Defaults to 0644 if unspecified.
The relative path within the projected volume where the corresponding ConfigMap key is mounted as a file.
Name of the referenced ConfigMap.
Optional specifies whether the ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. If set to true, the ConfigMap or its keys may be absent; if false (default), the ConfigMap must exist.
Configures a DownwardAPI source for the projected volume, exposing pod metadata (such as labels, annotations, and resource fields) as files in the volume.
List of DownwardAPIVolumeFile objects that define which fields to expose and the file paths where they are mounted.
Selects a field of the pod to expose as a file, such as metadata.name or status.podIP. The fieldRef structure specifies the API version and field path to read from the pod's information.
The API version of the field being referenced, e.g., 'v1'. If not specified, it defaults to 'v1'.
The path of the pod field to expose via the downward API, e.g., "metadata.name" or "spec.nodeName". This corresponds to the fieldPath in the Kubernetes FieldRef.
The file permission mode for the generated file, specified as an octal value (e.g., 0644) or its decimal equivalent (e.g., 420). If omitted, the volume's defaultMode is applied.
path is the file path (relative to the volume root) where the downward API value will be written.

ResourceFieldSelector that selects a container resource field (e.g., limits.cpu, requests.memory) and exposes its value as a file in the projected volume. Includes the container name, resource name, and an optional divisor.
Name of the container for which to expose the resource (e.g., limits.cpu, requests.memory) via the downward API. This must match a container name in the pod spec.
The divisor to divide the resource value by, as a quantity (e.g., '1m' for CPU). Defaults to 1 if not specified.
The name of the resource field to select, such as `limits.cpu`, `limits.memory`, `requests.cpu`, or `requests.ephemeral-storage`. When set, `container_name` must also be specified.
The user ID (UID) of the file's owner, as configured in the downward API projected volume item.
Relative path within the projected volume where the certificate chain (full chain of trust) is mounted.

The maximum validity period, in seconds, for the certificate projected into the volume. The kubelet will request a certificate that expires within this duration when provisioning the projected pod certificate.
The name of the certificate signer to use for the pod certificate projection. If omitted, the default signer is used.
Specifies a Secret to project into the volume. This object configures the Secret name, an optional list of key-to-path mappings, and whether the Secret is optional.

List of items to project from the Secret into the volume. Each item specifies a key, its path, and optionally its file mode. If unspecified, all secret data keys are projected as files with the same name. If specified, only listed keys are projected, and unlisted keys are omitted. Path must be relative and must not contain '..' or start with '..'.
The key within the referenced Secret whose value is projected into the volume.
The octal file mode, such as 0o644, that will be applied to the file created from the secret item. If not set, the default mode for the secret is used.
path is the relative file path within the projected volume where the secret key's value is mounted. If not specified, the key name is used as the path.
Name of the Secret object to reference in the projected volume source.
Specifies whether the secret or its keys must be defined. If set to true, the secret need not exist, and missing keys are treated as empty files. Defaults to false.

The `service_account_token` block configures a projected volume source that injects the Kubernetes service account token into the container. This allows workloads to authenticate to the Kubernetes API or other services using the pod's service account identity.
The audience of the projected service account token. It specifies the intended recipient, and the token will be valid for that audience. If not set, defaults to the API server's identifier.
expiration_seconds is the expected expiration time of the service account token in seconds. The value must be at least 600 and defaults to 3600 (1 hour) if not specified.
The relative path within the volume where the service account token file will be mounted. Must not start with '/'.
Represents a Quobyte volume source in a Kubernetes pod specification. When specified, the Quobyte volume is mounted into the pod.
Group to map volume access to. Defaults to no group if not specified.
Mounted read-only if true, read-write otherwise.
A comma-separated list of Quobyte registry servers (host:port) used to access the volume.
The tenant owning the given Quobyte volume in the backend. Used with dynamically provisioned Quobyte volumes.
The user to map the Quobyte volume access to. If not specified, defaults to the service account user.
Specifies the Quobyte volume to mount. This is the name of the volume as defined in Quobyte.
RBD represents a Rados Block Device mount on the host that shares a pod's lifetime.
Filesystem type to mount for the RBD volume (e.g., ext4, xfs). If not specified, defaults to ext4.
The RADOS image name to mount as the RBD volume.
Path to the keyring file for the RBD user. Defaults to /etc/ceph/keyring.
List of Ceph monitor addresses (host:port) for the RBD volume.
The Ceph pool name for the RBD image. Defaults to 'rbd' if not specified.
Whether the RBD volume is mounted as read-only. If true, the volume is read-only; otherwise, it is read-write.

Reference to a Kubernetes Secret in the same namespace that contains the Ceph authentication key (keyring) for accessing the RBD image. This is used to authenticate with the Ceph cluster when cephx is enabled.
Name of the Secret that holds the authentication key for the RBD volume. The Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
The RADOS user name used for authentication with Ceph RBD. Defaults to 'admin' if not specified.

ScaleIO is a volume type that mounts a ScaleIO volume into the pod. It contains fields for specifying the ScaleIO gateway, system name, protection domain, storage pool, and secret reference for authentication.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Defaults to 'ext4' if not specified.
The hostname or IP address of the ScaleIO API gateway. Required.
The name of the ScaleIO Protection Domain for the configured storage.
Indicates whether the ScaleIO volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; otherwise it is read-write (default).
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret in the same namespace that contains the ScaleIO storage system credentials (username and password) used to authenticate.
Name of the Kubernetes Secret containing the ScaleIO admin credentials.
Flag indicating whether the storage backend is configured to use SSL.
Optional storage mode for the ScaleIO volume: either 'ThickProvisioned' or 'ThinProvisioned'. Defaults to 'ThinProvisioned'.
The name of the ScaleIO storage pool where the volume is provisioned. This field is required in the ScaleIO volume source.
The name of the ScaleIO system that provides storage for the volume.
The name of the ScaleIO volume that backs this volume. This field is required for a ScaleIO volume source.
Defines a volume backed by a Kubernetes Secret. The Secret's contents are mounted as files in the pod, allowing containers to consume sensitive data like tokens or keys.

Default file permission mode for files in the secret volume, expressed as a decimal number (Unix mode bits). Must be between 0 and 511 (equivalent to octal 0000-0777). Defaults to 0644 (420) if not specified.
Maps specific keys of the Secret to file paths within the volume. If not specified, all keys are presented as files with their key names.
The key within the Secret's data to project into the volume. It identifies which entry from the Secret's data map to mount at the corresponding path.
The permission mode, as an octal number, for the secret key file. Must be between 0000 and 0777.
The relative path within the volume where the secret key is mounted. Must not start with '/' and must not contain '..'.
Optional specifies whether the Secret or its keys must be defined. If set to true, the volume will not fail if the Secret is missing; if omitted or false, the Secret must exist.
The name of the Secret in the pod's namespace to use for this volume.
StorageOS represents a StorageOS volume source. This is used to attach and mount a StorageOS volume into the pod.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Ex. 'ext4', 'xfs'. Defaults to 'ext4'.
Mounts the StorageOS volume as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; otherwise it is read-write.
secret_ref is a local object reference to a Secret that contains credentials for authenticating to the StorageOS API. It is used as a volume source for StorageOS volumes.
Name of the Secret that provides credentials for the StorageOS volume. This references a secret in the same namespace.
The name of the StorageOS volume to mount.
Name of the StorageOS volume namespace to use. This is an optional string that identifies the volume namespace on the StorageOS cluster.

Represents a vSphere volume that is mounted into the pod. This volume source references an existing vSphere datastore volume by its path, and can optionally specify filesystem type and storage policy.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Defaults to 'ext4'.
The vSphere storage policy ID to be used with the volume. If specified, the volume will be bound to the storage policy with this ID.
Name of the storage policy to use with this vSphere volume.
The vSphere volume path, which identifies the volume to mount. This must be a valid vSphere volume path, such as '[datastore1] my-volume'.

kubernetes_batch_cron_job.status.active..text: The API version of the referenced Kubernetes resource (e.g., 'batch/v1').

For a Kubernetes ObjectReference, FieldPath is an optional path to a subfield of the referenced object when the reference points to a specific field within an object. In a CronJob's status.active list, which contains references to Jobs, FieldPath is typically empty.
The kind of the referenced object in the active job list, typically 'Job'.
The name of the Job that is currently active for this CronJob.
The Kubernetes namespace of the active job listed in the CronJob status.
The resource version of the referenced Kubernetes job at the time the reference was recorded. Used for optimistic concurrency.
The UID of the active Job object currently running for this CronJob.

kubernetes_batch_job.metadata.managed_fi.text: The API version of the object that this managed field entry belongs to.
The type of the fields stored in this managedFields entry, typically 'FieldsV1'.

`fields_v1` is a JSON-encoded representation of the managed fields for a given manager, as defined by the Kubernetes `FieldsV1` type. It contains a map of field paths to values, indicating which fields are owned by that manager.
The name of the manager that owns or last modified the field. In Kubernetes managedFields, this is typically the name of the controller, operator, or user agent responsible for the last change.
The operation that was applied to the managed field entry, indicating whether the field was set via an apply or update. Valid values are 'Apply' and 'Update'.
Indicates which subresource of the object the managed fields apply to, such as 'status' or empty for the main resource.
The timestamp at which the management operation was recorded, in RFC3339 UTC format (e.g., 2021-01-01T00:00:00Z).

kubernetes_batch_job.metadata.owner_refe.text: The API version of the owner resource as defined in the Kubernetes OwnerReference, e.g., 'v1' or 'batch/v1'.
If true, and the owner has the foregroundDeletion finalizer, the owner cannot be deleted until this reference is removed. Defaults to false.
Indicates whether the owner reference points to the managing controller. This boolean flag is used to identify the controller that manages the owned object.
The Kubernetes resource kind of the owner object referenced by this owner reference (e.g., 'Job').
The name of the owner object being referenced. This is the name of the Kubernetes resource (e.g., a Deployment or Job) that owns this object.
The UID of the referenced owner object. This uniquely identifies the owner resource and is used to verify the reference.

kubernetes_batch_job.spec.pod_failure_po.text: Specifies the action to take when a pod failure matches the rule. Allowed values are `FailJob`, `Ignore`, and `Count`.

The on_exit_codes block specifies the container exit code condition that triggers the pod failure policy. It includes the container name, an operator (In or NotIn), and the list of exit code values that match the rule.
The name of the container to which the exit code rule applies. If not specified, the rule applies to all containers.

Operator defines the relationship between the container exit code and the values in the list. Valid values are 'In' (match if the exit code is in the list) and 'NotIn' (match if the exit code is not in the list).
List of container exit codes that the rule matches. If any container in the pod exits with one of these codes, the PodFailurePolicy rule applies.

A list of pod conditions that, when matched, cause the pod failure policy rule to apply. Each item specifies a condition type (e.g., DisruptionTarget) and a status (True, False, or Unknown) that the condition must have for the rule to take effect.
The status of the pod condition that must be matched for the policy rule to apply. Possible values are True, False, or Unknown.
The type of the Pod condition to match, such as DisruptionTarget, which indicates the pod was evicted due to a disruption.

kubernetes_batch_job.spec.scheduling.res.text: The name of the ResourceClaim that this job's pod references in its scheduling configuration.
The name of the ResourceClaim object that this entry references. The job's pods will use the resources from this claim when they are scheduled.
The name of the ResourceClaimTemplate in the same namespace that will be used to generate a ResourceClaim for this claim.

kubernetes_batch_job.spec.scheduling.sch.text: The topology key that identifies the domain to spread workloads across, such as 'kubernetes.io/hostname' or 'topology.kubernetes.io/zone'.

kubernetes_batch_job.spec.selector.match.text: The label key that the match expression applies to. This is the key part of a Kubernetes label selector requirement.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of label values that the selector matches. Required for the 'In' and 'NotIn' operators; must be empty for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist'.

kubernetes_batch_job.spec.success_policy.text: The minimum number of pods that must succeed for the job to be considered successful under this success policy rule.

A comma-separated list of index ranges (e.g., '0-2,5') that must have succeeded for this success policy rule to match. This field is used with indexed Jobs, and the rule is satisfied when all indexes in the specified set are in the Succeeded phase. The format supports individual indices and ranges (e.g., '0,2-4').

kubernetes_batch_job.spec.template.metad.text: The version of the Kubernetes API that the manager used to apply these managed fields.
The type of the managed fields entry, indicating the format of the fieldsV1 value. This is typically 'FieldsV1'.
fields_v1 is a JSON object that stores the managed fields for this entry, using a trie-like structure in JSON format.

The name of the component (e.g., a controller or client) that is responsible for managing these fields. This is part of Kubernetes' managed fields tracking, which records which manager last modified the field set.
The operation performed by the manager on the field, such as Apply, Update, or Delete.
The subresource that this managed field entry applies to. For example, an empty string indicates the main resource, while 'status' refers to the status subresource.
The timestamp of when the manager's operation was recorded. Part of a managedFields entry that tracks field ownership.
The API version of the owner resource referenced by this owner reference, e.g., 'v1' or 'apps/v1'.

Indicates whether the owner of this reference may be deleted while this owner reference exists. If true, the owner is protected from deletion until this reference is removed, ensuring the dependent object does not outlive its owner unexpectedly.
Indicates whether the referenced owner is the managing controller for this object. If true, this reference points to the managing controller; at most one owner reference can be the controller.
Kind of the owner resource, such as 'Job' or 'CronJob'.
Name of the referenced owner object. This field is required.
The UID of the owner object referenced by this owner reference.

kubernetes_batch_job.spec.template.spec..text: The node selector term that defines the nodes this preference applies to. It contains matchExpressions and matchFields conditions used to select nodes for this preferred scheduling term.
A list of node selector requirements that the node must satisfy. Each requirement specifies a label key, an operator, and a set of values.
The label key that the selector applies to, such as a Kubernetes well-known label or a custom label.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and the set of values, such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, or Lt.

Values is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty. This array is replaced during a strategic merge patch.
A list of node selector requirements that match against node fields (e.g., metadata.name) to define the node affinity preference.
The key of the node field to match, such as 'metadata.name'. This is used in a match_fields node selector requirement.
The operator used to express the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a match_fields expression. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.
A list of field values that must match the specified key and operator in the node affinity preference. For example, when the operator is In, the field must equal one of these values.
Weight associated with the node selector term, ranging from 1 to 100. The scheduler prefers nodes that satisfy the term according to the relative weight; higher weights increase the preference.

A list of node selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a Kubernetes node label key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt), and optionally a list of values, used to filter nodes for scheduling.
The label key that the selector applies to. This is the Kubernetes node label key that must match for the node selector term to apply.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and its values in the node selector requirement. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.

The values field is an array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must contain at least one value; if the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty.
List of node selector requirements that match on node fields (e.g., metadata.name). Each item defines a key, operator, and values, with operators like In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt.
The key of the node field to match against, as part of a node selector term's match_fields list.

The operator represents the relationship between the field key and the values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. For example, In matches if the field value is in the given list, and Gt matches if the field value is greater than the specified value.

The list of values for the field selector requirement. Behavior depends on the operator: for 'In', 'NotIn', 'Gt', and 'Lt', values must be provided (with 'Gt' and 'Lt' expecting exactly one numeric value); for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', the list must be empty.

The pod affinity term defines the selection of pods that this pod prefers to be scheduled alongside, using label selectors and a topology key to express the required co-location. It is part of a preferred scheduling rule, so the scheduler will try to satisfy it but does not require it.
A label selector used to identify the set of pods that the affinity/anti-affinity rule applies to. It supports matchLabels and matchExpressions fields to filter target pods.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values, used to define the conditions for selecting pods in the affinity term.
The label key that the selector operates on. This must be a valid Kubernetes label key, typically a string with optional prefix/name format (e.g., 'example.com/key' or 'key').
The operator for a label selector requirement, defining how the label key is matched against the set of values. Valid operators include In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

values is an array of string values that corresponds to the key in the match expression. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty.
A map of label keys to values used to select the set of pods that the affinity term applies to. Pods with all specified labels are matched.
A list of pod label keys. The label values for these keys from the incoming pod are merged with the label selector to determine the set of existing pods that this affinity term applies to.
A label selector to filter the namespaces to which the pod affinity term applies. If empty, the affinity term applies to the pod's own namespace.
A list of label selector requirements used to match namespaces by labels. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (one of In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values.
The label key that the selector applies to. For namespace selectors, this is a label on the namespace.

The operator defines the relationship between the label key and its values. Valid operators are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'. 'In' and 'NotIn' require a list of values, while 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist' do not.
A list of string values. For the 'In' and 'NotIn' operators, this specifies the set of values that must (or must not) match the key. For 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty.

A map of label keys to values. The namespace selector matches namespaces that have all the specified label keys and values. This is part of the label selector for selecting namespaces to which the pod affinity term applies.
A list of namespaces used for the pod affinity/anti-affinity evaluation. If empty, the namespace of the pod is used.

The key of the topology domain (e.g., kubernetes.io/hostname, failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone) that defines the scope for this pod affinity/anti-affinity term. Pods are considered to be in the same topology domain if they share the same value for this key, and the affinity rule applies only within that domain.
Weight specifies the relative importance of this preference. It must be an integer between 1 and 100, with higher values indicating greater priority for this rule during scheduling.
A label selector used to identify the set of pods that the affinity constraint applies to. It specifies the pods whose labels must match for the scheduling rule to be enforced.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement contains a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. These requirements are combined with matchLabels to define the label selector for pod affinity.
The label key that the selector evaluates. In a match expression, this key is matched against pod labels using the specified operator and values.
The operator defines the relationship between a label key and a set of values. Must be one of In, NotIn, Exists, or DoesNotExist.
List of values for the label selector expression. Must be non-empty when the operator is In or NotIn, and must be empty for Exists or DoesNotExist.

matchLabels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the matchLabels map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is "key", the operator is "In", and the values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.

A list of label keys from the pod being scheduled. The values of these keys on the pod are used to build a label selector that determines which existing pods match this affinity rule. This allows the rule to dynamically match pods based on the incoming pod's own labels.

The list of label keys used to exclude pods from this affinity term. If any candidate pod has a label matching one of these keys, that pod is not selected. This is used to make the pod affinity more specific by filtering out pods with certain label keys.
A label selector for namespaces. The pod affinity rule will consider pods only from those namespaces that match this selector. If not specified, the rule applies to the namespace of the pod.

A list of label selector requirements used to select namespaces. Each requirement specifies a key, operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optional values. The namespace selector matches namespaces that satisfy all of the specified requirements.
The label key that this match expression applies to. It identifies which label on a namespace the selector will evaluate.
Operator represents the key's relationship to a set of values in a label selector requirement. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
The list of label values that the label selector matches. Required when operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'; ignored for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist'.
A map of label keys to values that must match a namespace's labels for that namespace to be selected by this selector. The namespace must have all specified key-value pairs.
Specifies the namespaces from which pods are matched by the affinity selector. If empty, it defaults to the namespace of the pod where this affinity rule is applied.

The topology domain key (a node label, e.g., kubernetes.io/hostname) that defines the scope of the pod affinity rule. Pods are considered to be in the same topology domain if they have the same value for this key.

The pod affinity term that defines the set of pods (via a label selector, namespaces, and topology key) used by the preferred anti-affinity rule. This term is required within each preferred scheduling term and combines with a weight to express a soft scheduling preference.

A label query over the pods to which the pod affinity/anti-affinity rule applies. It selects the set of pods whose labels match the specified requirements, determining the group considered for this affinity term.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values. The matchExpressions and matchLabels together define the label selector for the pod affinity term.
The key of the label selector requirement. This is the label key that the selector matches against.
The operator defines the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a match expression. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
Values is a list of string values that must match the key when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'. For operators 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty.

A map of label keys and values that a pod must have to match this pod affinity term's label selector. This filter is used by the preferred_during_scheduling_ignored_during_execution pod anti-affinity rule in the Kubernetes batch job.

A list of pod label keys. For each key in the list, the incoming pod's label value must match the corresponding label value on a candidate pod for that candidate to be considered by this (anti-)affinity term. The list is sorted and used together with the label selector to refine which pods are selected.

A list of label keys that are used to refine the affinity/anti-affinity matching by excluding pods with the same value for these keys as the current pod. For each key in the list, only pods with a different value are considered matching.
A label selector to select namespaces. When specified, the pod anti-affinity term applies to pods in the selected namespaces.
A list of label selector requirements that the namespace must match. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional set of values.

The label key that the match expression applies to in the namespace selector. This key is used with the operator to select namespaces. For example, a key of 'environment' with operator 'In' and values ['production'] selects namespaces labeled with environment=production.
The operator defines the relationship between the key and the set of values in the match expression. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

A list of values for the label selector expression. For operators In and NotIn, this field specifies the set of values that must (or must not) match the key. For Exists and DoesNotExist, this field must be empty.
A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels of a namespace for it to be considered in the pod affinity/anti-affinity rule. Only namespaces that have all specified labels are selected.
List of namespaces that the pod affinity/anti-affinity term applies to. If not specified, the term applies to the namespace of the pod where the affinity is defined.

The topology key (e.g., `kubernetes.io/hostname` or `failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone`) that defines the scope of the anti-affinity rule. Pods with matching labels are spread across distinct topology domains based on this key.
Weight relative to other preferred terms, from 1 to 100. Higher weight gives this anti-affinity rule more influence during scheduling.
Selects groups of pods by label to which the anti-affinity rule applies. Supports matchLabels (exact key/value pairs) and matchExpressions (list of label selector requirements).
A list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed to form the label selector for the required pod anti-affinity term.
The label key that this selector requirement applies to. For pod anti-affinity, it refers to a label on pods being considered for scheduling, e.g., 'app' or 'tier'.

The operator represents the relationship between the label key and a set of values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. For example, In requires the key to be one of the specified values, while Exists only requires the key to be present.
values is a list of label values that the selector matches. It must be non-empty for the 'In' and 'NotIn' operators, and must be empty for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist'.
A map of label keys to values. The selector matches pods that have all the specified label key-value pairs as labels.

A list of pod label keys whose values from the incoming pod are used to select which existing pods are considered for the anti-affinity rule. This narrows the set of matching pods to those that share the same label values for these keys, complementing the label selector.

A list of pod label keys. Pods that have a key in this list with the same value as the corresponding label on the new pod are excluded from the anti-affinity consideration, limiting the set of pods matched by the anti-affinity rule.
A label selector to choose the namespaces for the pod anti-affinity rule. If omitted, the rule applies to all namespaces.
A list of label selector requirements applied to namespace labels. Each item contains a key, operator, and values to match namespaces, used for selecting namespaces in this pod anti-affinity rule.
The label key that the selector applies to. This is the key part of a match expression, used to select resources based on label values.
Specifies the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a match expression. Allowed values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'.
The list of values that the key must match according to the operator. This is part of a label selector requirement for selecting namespaces in a pod anti-affinity rule.
A map of label keys and values used to match namespace labels. When specified, the pod anti-affinity rule applies to pods only in namespaces that match all these labels.
Specifies the namespaces that the pod anti-affinity term is scoped to. If not specified, the term applies to pods in the same namespace as the pod.

The topology key that defines the scope of the anti-affinity rule. Pods are not scheduled on nodes (or other topology domains) that have other pods matching the label selector. Common examples include 'kubernetes.io/hostname' and 'failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone'.

A list of arguments to pass to the container's entrypoint. If not provided, the image's default CMD is used. Supports variable references like $(VAR_NAME), which are expanded based on the container's environment.

The entrypoint array for the container. Overrides the image's ENTRYPOINT and is not executed within a shell; if not provided, the image's default entrypoint is used. Variable references like $(VAR_NAME) are expanded using the container's environment.
List of environment variables to set in the container. Each entry contains a name and either a direct value or a source (valueFrom) such as a secret, config map, or field reference.
Name of the environment variable. Must be a C_IDENTIFIER.
The value of the environment variable. This is a literal string value, as opposed to being sourced from a field reference, resource, or secret via valueFrom.
Specifies a source for the environment variable's value, such as a ConfigMap key, Secret key, or a field reference. This is mutually exclusive with setting a literal 'value'.
Reference to a specific key within a ConfigMap, used to populate the value of the environment variable. The ConfigMap must exist in the pod's namespace.
The key of the ConfigMap entry to use as the value of the environment variable.
Name of the ConfigMap to select the key from.

Specify whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If true, a missing key or ConfigMap is allowed and the environment variable will be left unset; if false or omitted, a missing key or ConfigMap will cause the pod to fail.
Selects a field of the pod to inject as the environment variable's value, using the field's JSON path (e.g., metadata.name, status.podIP).
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath references. For example, 'v1' for core Kubernetes resources.
Path to the pod field from which to select the environment variable's value. Examples include metadata.name, metadata.namespace, status.podIP, and spec.nodeName.
Boolean indicating whether the referenced key is optional. When true, the key is not required to exist; when false or omitted, the key must exist. Defaults to false if not specified.
Selects a resource field (such as limits.cpu or requests.memory) from the container, and exposes its value as an environment variable. The value is taken from the container's resource specification.

The name of the container whose resource (e.g., CPU or memory limits/requests) should be used for this environment variable. If omitted, the container where this environment variable is defined is used.
Divisor is the value by which the resource value is divided. Must be a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1', '100m'). Defaults to 1.
The resource to select, e.g., 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
SecretKeyRef selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. Specify the secret name and the key to use as the environment variable value.
The key of the secret to select from. This refers to a key in the data field of the referenced Secret object.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret that contains the key being referenced.

Specifies whether the referenced Secret or its key must be defined. If set to true, the reference is optional and the container can start even if the secret or key is missing. If false (default), the secret and key must exist.

List of sources to populate environment variables in the container. Each source can be a ConfigMap or Secret reference, optionally with a prefix. When multiple sources define the same key, the last source takes precedence, and explicit env entries take precedence over envFrom.

config_map_ref selects a ConfigMap as a source for environment variables. It contains fields for the ConfigMap name (`name`) and an optional flag (`optional`) indicating whether the ConfigMap must be defined.
Name of the ConfigMap to reference for populating environment variables.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If set to true, a missing ConfigMap is allowed and the reference is ignored. Defaults to false.
An optional string that, if specified, is prepended to the keys of the referenced ConfigMap or Secret when they are exposed as environment variables.
Reference to a Secret whose attributes (e.g., data keys) are used to populate environment variables in the container. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Job.
Name of the Secret to reference. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Specify whether the referenced secret must be defined. If set to true, the secret may be absent and the environment variables are set only if the secret exists.
Specifies the container image to run for this container, typically in the format `name:tag` or a full image URI (e.g., 'nginx:latest').

Specifies when the kubelet should pull a container image. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never; if omitted, the default is Always for images with the :latest tag or no tag, and IfNotPresent otherwise.
Defines lifecycle hooks for the container, specifying actions to run at container start (postStart) and before container termination (preStop).

The postStart lifecycle hook is executed immediately after a container is created. It can contain an exec action (running a command) or an httpGet action (sending an HTTP request) to perform initialization tasks.
Exec defines a command to be run inside the container when the postStart lifecycle hook fires. The command is specified as a list of strings in the 'command' attribute of this action.
The command to execute inside the container when the post-start lifecycle hook fires. It is given as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.

In the postStart lifecycle hook, http_get defines an HTTP GET request that the kubelet sends to the container after it starts. This object specifies parameters such as host, port, path, scheme, and HTTP headers for the request.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; you can override it or use the Host header in httpHeaders instead.
List of custom HTTP headers to send with the HTTP GET request. Each list item defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request. In Kubernetes, this is a required field when defining HTTP headers for a lifecycle postStart HTTP GET handler.
The value of the HTTP header field. This is used in conjunction with the header name to send custom headers in the HTTP GET request.
The path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port number or named port on the container that the HTTP GET request is sent to. Accepts a numeric port (1-65535) or a port name defined in the container's ports.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request.
The URI scheme for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The sleep action for the postStart lifecycle hook. It specifies a sleep duration (in seconds) that the container must wait before it is considered started. The nested `seconds` attribute is required.
The number of seconds to sleep during the postStart lifecycle hook.

Specifies the tcpSocket action to perform during the postStart lifecycle hook. This includes the host and port to attempt a TCP connection to, indicating successful container startup when the connection is established.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket postStart hook. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
The port number (as a string, e.g., "8080") or named port on which the TCP socket lifecycle handler connects. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a name matching a container port.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that is called immediately before a container is terminated due to an API request or management event such as a liveness probe failure, preemption, resource contention, or other. The hook can be used to gracefully stop the container and can define either an exec command or an HTTP request to perform the pre-stop behavior.
ExecAction defines a command to be executed in the container as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook.
List of strings that specify the command and arguments to execute for the preStop lifecycle hook when using the exec handler. This command runs inside the container before it is terminated.
Specifies an HTTP GET request that the kubelet sends to the container's IP address before the container is stopped. This is used as the preStop lifecycle hook action.
The host name or IP address to which the HTTP GET request is sent. If omitted, the pod's IP address is used.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP GET request. Each header is an object with name and value fields, and repeated headers are allowed.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request.
The value of the HTTP header that will be sent in the HTTP GET request to the pre-stop lifecycle hook endpoint.
The path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The TCP port to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Accepts an integer port number or a named port (as a string). Defaults to 80 if not specified.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS; defaults to HTTP.
Sleep action for the preStop lifecycle hook. This specifies a delay (in seconds via the `seconds` field) before the container is terminated, allowing graceful shutdown tasks to complete.
Specifies the number of seconds to sleep before the container is terminated. Must be a positive integer.

TCP socket action for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. Specifies a port (and optionally host) to connect to; Kubernetes will attempt to open a TCP socket to the given host:port as part of the pre-stop hook.
The host (IP address or hostname) to connect to for the TCP socket action in the preStop lifecycle hook. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The port number (as a string) or name of the port on the container to connect to for the pre-stop lifecycle hook.
Defines a liveness probe for the container. The kubelet periodically executes the probe and restarts the container if the probe fails, ensuring that an unhealthy container is detected and replaced.
Exec specifies the action to take in the container. The command is run inside the container and the probe succeeds if the exit code is 0.

The command to execute inside the container, specified as a list of strings (the executable and its arguments). It is run directly without a shell, so shell features like pipes or wildcards are not interpreted.
Minimum consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3. Minimum value is 1.
Specifies an optional gRPC probe configuration. Contains required 'port' and optional 'service' fields for the gRPC health check request.
The port number of the gRPC service. Must be between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is empty string.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform on the container for the liveness probe. This includes the path, port, and optional HTTP headers used to check container health.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used. This is part of the HTTPGetAction configuration for a liveness probe.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request made by the liveness probe. Each object in the list specifies a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the liveness probe HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP GET request for the liveness probe.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. For example, /healthz. Defaults to /.
The TCP port number or named port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. If not specified, it defaults to the first container port.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request to the liveness probe endpoint. Supported values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
Number of seconds between liveness probe executions. Defaults to 10 seconds; must be greater than 0.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the liveness probe to be considered successful after a failure. For liveness probes, this value must be 1 (default); minimum value is 1.
Specifies a TCP socket check for the liveness probe. The probe will attempt to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port to determine if it is alive.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod's IP address.
The TCP port number or named port that the probe will connect to. It can be an integer port number or a named port defined in the container.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second.
The name of the container within the pod. It must be a valid DNS_LABEL and unique among all containers in the same pod.
List of ports to expose from the container. Each entry can specify containerPort, hostPort, protocol (TCP or UDP), hostIP, and name.
The port number that the container exposes on the pod's IP address. Must be a valid port number between 1 and 65535.
The host IP address to bind the external port to. If not specified, the port is bound to all interfaces (0.0.0.0).

The port number on the host node to which the container port is mapped. This is used to expose the container port directly on the host's network interface; it is optional and when set, the container is reachable on the host's IP at this port.
The name of this port, which must be an IANA_SVC_NAME (up to 15 characters). This name can be used to reference the port in a Service.
The protocol for this container port. Must be TCP, UDP, or SCTP. Defaults to TCP.

The readiness probe configuration for the container. It defines a health check that determines when the container is considered ready to accept traffic; the probe is executed periodically and the container is ready if the probe succeeds.

Exec specifies the action to take, running a command inside the container. For a readiness probe, the command's exit status is used to determine success: 0 indicates healthy, non-zero indicates failure.
The command to execute in the container for the readiness probe. The first element is the executable path, and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is run directly without a shell.
The number of consecutive probe failures required for the container to be considered not ready. Must be a positive integer (minimum 1); the default is 3.
Configures a gRPC-based readiness probe. This object specifies the gRPC service port to check and can optionally define a service name.
Port number of the gRPC service to probe. Must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, defaults to the container name.
Specifies the parameters for an HTTP GET request used to probe the container's readiness. This includes the path, port, and optional headers for the request.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request, defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set 'Host' in httpHeaders instead.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request to the container. Each object in the list defines a header with a name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request, e.g., 'Content-Type'.
The value of the HTTP header in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server when performing the readiness probe. For example, /healthz.
The TCP port or port name for the HTTP GET request. Accepts a numeric port or a named port on the container.
The network protocol used for the HTTP GET probe request, such as 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. This determines whether the connection is unencrypted or uses TLS.
The HTTP or HTTPS scheme to use for the probe request. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0, meaning the probe begins immediately after container start.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1.

Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after it has failed. Defaults to 1. For readiness probes, this value can be greater than 1, but for liveness and startup probes it must be 1.

The tcp_socket block configures a TCP-based probe for the readiness probe. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the container; a successful connection indicates the container is ready.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port number or named port (if defined in the container's ports) that the readiness probe should connect to.
Timeout in seconds after which the probe is considered failed. Defaults to 1 second and must be at least 1.

List of container resize policies. Each item defines how a specific resource (e.g., CPU or memory) can be resized and whether the container must be restarted. Allowed `resourceName` values: `cpu`, `memory`. Allowed `restartPolicy` values: `NotRequired`, `RestartContainer`.
The name of the resource to which the resize policy applies.
Defines the compute resource requirements for the container, including resource requests (minimum resources to reserve) and limits (maximum resources allowed), such as CPU and memory.
Lists the names of resource claims (defined in the pod's spec.resourceClaims) that this container uses. Each item references a ResourceClaim by name.
The name of the ResourceClaim that the container references. This must correspond to a ResourceClaim object in the same namespace.
Limits specifies the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. Each key is a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the value is a quantity string (e.g., '500m', '1Gi').

A map of resource names to quantities, specifying the minimum amount of compute resources required by the container (e.g., cpu: '250m', memory: '128Mi'). Each value is a Kubernetes resource quantity string.
The operator used to match container exit codes against the defined values. Valid values are `In` and `NotIn`.
A list of integer container exit codes that this restart policy rule matches. For example, exit code 137 indicates the container was terminated by SIGKILL.
