Defines the security context for the container, specifying security settings such as runAsUser, runAsGroup, Linux capabilities, and SELinux options, which override the pod-level security context if set.
Controls whether a container process can gain more privileges than its parent process. Set to false to disable privilege escalation (e.g., setuid) for the container.

Configures the AppArmor profile for the container, specifying the profile type (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost) and, for Localhost, the profile name. This field allows setting AppArmor security restrictions on the container's processes.
The name of a profile that is loaded on the node to use for the container. Only used when the type is Localhost.
Specifies the type of AppArmor profile to use. Valid values are 'Localhost', 'RuntimeDefault', and 'Unconfined'. 'Localhost' requires a corresponding localhostProfile to be specified.
Configures Linux capabilities for the container. Use `add` to grant additional capabilities, and `drop` to remove them from the default set.
Specifies a list of Linux capabilities to add to the container's capability set. For example, CAP_NET_ADMIN.

Specifies a list of Linux capabilities to remove from the container's default set. For example, dropping CAP_NET_RAW can prevent the container from performing raw socket operations. This is part of the security context capabilities configuration for the container.
Indicates whether the container runs in privileged mode, granting it access to all host devices and capabilities. Defaults to false.
procMount sets the proc mount to be used for the container. Allowed values are 'Default' (default) and 'Unmasked' to allow visibility of all processes.
Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only. When set to true, processes cannot write to the root filesystem, enhancing security by preventing unauthorized modifications.
Specifies the group ID (GID) that the container's main process runs as. When unset, the default group from the container image is used.

When set to true, the container must run as a non-root user (UID not 0). The kubelet will verify that the container image does not run as root before starting the container, and will fail to start it if it does.
The numeric user ID (UID) that the container's processes will run as. If set, it overrides the user specified in the container image; the value must be a valid integer UID.

SELinux options to be applied to the container. This object specifies the SELinux user, role, type, and level labels for the container's processes. If unspecified, the container runtime will allocate a random SELinux context if SELinux is enabled on the node.
The SELinux level label to apply to the container (e.g., s0, s0:c123).
The SELinux role label for the container, used as part of the SELinux security context.
The SELinux type label that applies to the container.
The SELinux user label that applies to the container, part of the SELinux context.

SeccompProfile configures the seccomp profile for the container's security context. It allows specifying the seccomp mode, such as RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, or Localhost, to apply to the container's processes.
Name of a seccomp profile on the node, relative to the kubelet's seccomp profile directory (e.g., /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp). This is used when the seccompProfile type is 'Localhost'.
The seccomp profile type. Allowed values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Unconfined', and 'Localhost'. When set to 'Localhost', the 'localhostProfile' field must also be specified.
Windows-specific security options for the container, such as GMSA credentials, host process containers, and run as user name. Applied when the container runs on Windows nodes.
The path to the GMSA credential spec file, which defines the identity and permissions for the container when using Group Managed Service Accounts in Windows.
Name of the GMSA credential spec to use for Windows containers. This references a pre-defined GMSA credential spec resource in the cluster.

Indicates whether the container should run as a HostProcess container on Windows nodes. When true, the container has access to host resources, and all containers in the pod must have the same HostProcess setting.

The UserName in Windows to run the entrypoint of the container process. Defaults to the user specified in image metadata if unspecified. May also be set in PodSecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.

startup_probe defines a probe that checks whether the application in the container has started successfully. If the probe fails, the container is restarted, and liveness/readiness probes are not started until it succeeds.
Exec specifies the action to take as a command to run inside the container. The probe is successful if the command exits with status 0.

Command to execute in the container for the startup probe. It is a list of strings, with the first element being the command and the rest being arguments. The command is exec'd directly, not run through a shell.
Specifies the number of consecutive failures required for the startup probe to be considered failed. Defaults to 3, with a minimum value of 1.
Configures a gRPC health check within the probe, specifying the port to check and an optional service name.
The port number to use for the gRPC probe. Must be a valid TCP port number (1-65535).
Name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If omitted, defaults to the container name.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform on the container as part of the startup probe. The probe is considered successful if the container returns an HTTP response code in the 200-399 range.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. If not specified, it defaults to the pod IP.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the probe request. Each item has a name and value, allowing the probe to send extra headers to the endpoint.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the startup probe's HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header. This is the value corresponding to the header name specified in the same http_headers list item.
Path to access on the HTTP server.
The TCP port to use for the HTTP GET request to the container. Can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container. This port is used by the startup probe to check container health.
Specifies the protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request, such as HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP when not specified.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Must be a non-negative integer; defaults to 0 if unset.
The number of seconds between each startup probe execution.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after it has failed. For startup probes, this must be set to 1 (the default); the minimum value is 1.

Configures a TCP socket probe that checks the container's health by attempting to open a TCP connection to a specified port (and optionally host). This is used in the startup probe to determine when the container has successfully started.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket startup probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to. Accepts a port number or a named port from the container.

Optional duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully after the probe has failed. The grace period is the duration after processes receive a termination signal and before they are forcibly halted. Overrides the pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds if set; must be a non-negative integer. A value of 0 indicates immediate termination.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. If the probe does not complete within this time, the probe is considered failed. Defaults to 1 second if not specified.

Whether this container should have a stdin stream allocated for it. When true, the container runtime allocates a stdin channel for the container, allowing interactive processes to read from standard input.

When true, the container runtime closes the container's stdin channel after the first attach session, preventing further input. This is typically used with stdin enabled for one-shot interactive tasks.
Path where the container's termination message is written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log. The message is captured by kubelet and can be retrieved via pod status.

Defines how the container's termination message is read. Allowed values are 'File' (default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'. When set to 'File', the termination message is read from the file /dev/termination-log; when set to 'FallbackToLogsOnError', the message is read from the file unless the container exits with a non-zero exit code, in which case the last portion of container logs are used.
Whether to allocate a pseudo-TTY for this container. When enabled, the container gets a terminal device, typically used for interactive processes.
List of raw block devices to be used by the container. Each item maps a volume name to a device path inside the container, enabling direct access to block storage.
The path inside the container where the block device will be exposed (e.g., /dev/sdb). This is used in the volume_devices list to mount a raw block device.
Name of the volume. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.

A list of volumes to mount into the container. Each entry must specify a name that matches a volume defined in the pod spec and a mountPath, and can optionally set readOnly, subPath, and other mount options.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must not contain ':'.
Defines how mount propagation is handled for this volume mount. Allowed values: None, HostToContainer, Bidirectional. If not specified, None is used.
The name of the volume to mount, which must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes.
If true, the volume is mounted as read-only. If false or omitted, the volume is mounted read-write.

Specifies whether the volume mount is set as read-only recursively, meaning the read-only setting applies to all sub-mounts and directories within the volume. The string value allows for different modes of recursive read-only behavior.
Path within the volume from which to mount the volume into the container, instead of the volume's root.
Path within the volume from which the container will mount, allowing environment variable expansion using $(VAR) syntax. Unlike subPath, this supports dynamic paths based on environment variables.
The working directory inside the container. If not specified, the container runtime's default (often set by the image) is used.
The name of the DNS resolver option, such as 'ndots' or 'timeout'.
The value for the DNS resolver option. In Kubernetes DNS config, an option can have an optional value; if omitted, the option is set without a value (e.g., ndots:5).
Arguments to the container's entrypoint. The container's entrypoint is invoked with these arguments. This corresponds to the `args` field in the Kubernetes container spec.
The command to run inside the ephemeral container. It overrides the image's entrypoint and is specified as a list of strings.
List of environment variables to set in the ephemeral container. Each item typically contains a name and either a value or a valueFrom source.
Name of the environment variable. Must be a C_IDENTIFIER.
The value to assign to the environment variable. This is a plain string value; if you need to source the value from a field or secret, use valueFrom instead.
Source for the environment variable's value. Cannot be used if 'value' is not empty.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap. This field references a specific key within a ConfigMap to populate the value of the environment variable.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap to fetch the value for this environment variable.
The name of the ConfigMap to select the key from.

Optional indicates whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If set to true, the container will start even if the referenced ConfigMap or key does not exist; if false (default), the container will not start until the key is present.

field_ref selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name or status.podIP) to populate the environment variable. It contains sub-fields api_version and field_path, where field_path specifies the exact pod field to reference.
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath is written in terms of. For example, 'v1'.
The path to the desired field of the Pod, such as `metadata.name`, `metadata.namespace`, or `spec.nodeName`, used to populate the environment variable's value from that field.
Specifies whether the referenced key is mandatory. When set to true, a missing key is tolerated; when false (default), the key must exist or the container fails.
The resource_field_ref block selects a resource field (e.g., requests.cpu, limits.memory) from the container's resource specification, and its value becomes the environment variable's value.
The name of the container whose resource value is referenced. If not specified, defaults to the container where this environment variable is defined.
The divisor for the resource field value. The resource value is divided by this quantity before being used, allowing expression in different units (e.g., '1m' for milli-units). Defaults to 1.
The name of the container resource field to reference, such as 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory'. This selects a specific resource value from the container's resource specification.
secretKeyRef selects a key of a Secret to use as the value for an environment variable. It references the Secret name and the key within that Secret; the Secret must exist in the pod's namespace.
The key of the secret to select. Must be a valid secret key.
The name of the Secret to select from. This Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

Specifies whether the referenced Secret or its key must be defined. If true, the reference is optional and the container can start even if the Secret or key is missing; if false or omitted, the Secret and key must exist.
List of sources to populate environment variables in the ephemeral container. Each source can reference a ConfigMap or Secret, and an optional prefix can be applied to the keys.
Selects a ConfigMap to populate environment variables from. The ConfigMap's data key becomes the environment variable name, and the value becomes the environment variable's value.
Name of the ConfigMap to be used for populating environment variables. This must refer to a ConfigMap in the same namespace as the pod.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must exist. If true, the container starts even if the ConfigMap is missing; if false or omitted, the ConfigMap must exist.
An optional identifier prepended to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. Must be a C_IDENTIFIER (e.g., start with a letter or underscore, followed by letters, digits, or underscores).
SecretEnvSource to select a Secret. The selected Secret's data will be exposed as environment variables in the ephemeral container. The Secret must exist in the pod's namespace.
The name of the Secret resource to use for populating environment variables in the ephemeral container.
Specify whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If true, the Secret may be absent; if false or not set, the Secret must exist.
The container image (e.g., Docker image) to use for this ephemeral container.
Image pull policy for this ephemeral container. Valid values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never. If unset, defaults to Always if the image tag is :latest, otherwise IfNotPresent.
Lifecycle hooks configuration for this ephemeral container. Note that Kubernetes does not support lifecycle hooks for ephemeral containers, so this field is generally ignored by the API.
Post-start lifecycle hook for the ephemeral container. Defines a handler that is executed immediately after the container starts.
Exec specifies the command to execute inside the container when the postStart lifecycle hook is triggered. It allows running custom commands immediately after the container starts.

The command to execute inside the container for this lifecycle hook. It is provided as a list of strings (argv) and is run directly, not via a shell, so shell constructs like pipes or redirections will not work unless you explicitly invoke a shell (e.g., ['/bin/sh', '-c', '...']).

Defines an HTTP GET request performed by kubelet after the container starts, as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. It specifies the endpoint to query, including host, port, path, scheme, and headers.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
List of custom HTTP headers to send with the GET request. Each header is defined by a name and value pair.
The HTTP header name.
The value of the HTTP header, as a string. This header is sent as part of the HTTP GET request in the postStart lifecycle handler.
Path to access on the HTTP server.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. For a numeric port, must be in the range 1–65535. For a named port, use the name defined in the container's ports.
The HTTP protocol to use for the request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'.
Sleep is a lifecycle handler action that pauses the container for a specified number of seconds. For postStart, it configures a sleep action via the 'seconds' field.
The number of seconds to sleep for the postStart lifecycle hook. This is a required field for the SleepAction.
Configures a TCP socket handler for this lifecycle event. It specifies the host and port to connect to, and the hook succeeds if the connection is successful.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to connect to, specified as a numeric port (e.g., "8080") or a named port defined in the container.

Defines a lifecycle hook that runs immediately before a container is terminated. This can include an exec command, HTTP GET request, or TCP socket probe (using the `exec`, `http_get`, or `tcp_socket` sub-fields).
Specifies a command to run inside the container as the pre-stop action. This is an ExecAction, part of the Kubernetes lifecycle hook.
The command to execute inside the container when the pre-stop lifecycle hook runs. It is executed directly without a shell, with the container's root ('/') as the working directory.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform against the container's endpoint as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. The request is sent to the configured port and path on the container.
The hostname to connect to for the HTTP request. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each entry defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the request.
The path to access on the HTTP server for the HTTP GET request.
The port number or named port on the container to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Accepts a numeric port (e.g., 8080) or a name defined in the container's ports.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The protocol scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS; if omitted, HTTP is used.
Sleep specifies a lifecycle hook action that pauses the container for a specified duration. This object contains a 'seconds' field indicating the number of seconds to sleep.
Seconds specifies the number of seconds to sleep during the pre-stop hook before the container is terminated. This is a required field for the sleep action and must be a non-negative integer.
Defines a TCP socket handler for the pre-stop lifecycle hook, which opens a TCP connection to the specified port (and optionally a host) to trigger graceful shutdown of the container.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If unspecified, defaults to the pod IP.
Port name or number for the TCP socket. Accepts an integer port number or a named port (string) defined in the container.
Liveness probe configuration for the ephemeral container. Kubernetes does not support liveness probes on ephemeral containers, so this field is typically unused or ignored.
Exec specifies an exec action for the liveness probe, defining the command(s) to run inside the container to check its health.
The command to run inside the container as part of the exec probe. This is a list of strings; the first element is the executable, and subsequent elements are arguments.
The number of consecutive failures of the liveness probe after which the container is restarted. The minimum value is 1, and the default is 3.
Configures a gRPC-based health check for the liveness probe. Includes the port to connect to and optionally the service name, used by the kubelet to perform the gRPC health check.
The port number of the gRPC service to connect to for the probe. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If empty, the probe defaults to the container name.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform as part of the liveness probe. This allows the kubelet to check container health by sending an HTTP GET to the configured path, port, and optional headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request used by the liveness probe. Each header is specified as a name/value pair.
Name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request.
The value of the HTTP header entry in the liveness probe's HTTP GET request. This is the string value sent as the header's value.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to `/` if not specified.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET liveness probe. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
The URI scheme to use for the probe request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS', with 'HTTP' as the default.
The number of seconds after the container has started before the liveness probe is initiated. This delay allows the container to initialize before probing begins.
Specifies the frequency (in seconds) at which the liveness probe is executed. Must be greater than 0; default is 10 seconds if not specified.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For liveness probes, this value must be 1.
Specifies a TCP socket check for the liveness probe. The object allows configuring the port to connect to, and optionally the host.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP check. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The port number or name to use for the TCP socket liveness probe. This can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container.
The duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully. The kubelet sends SIGTERM and waits this long before sending SIGKILL, allowing running processes to finish.
Specifies the number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out. The default is 1 second, and the value must be greater than or equal to 1.
List of ports exposed by the ephemeral container. Each object specifies a container port number, protocol (TCP/UDP), and optionally a host port and host IP.
The port number to expose on the container's IP address. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.

The host IP address to bind the container port to. When set, the port is exposed only on that specific host IP; otherwise, it binds to all host interfaces (0.0.0.0). This field is typically used in conjunction with host_port to map container ports to host ports.
The port on the host node to map to the container port. If specified, this port must be available on the host; if omitted, the container port is not exposed on the host.
Optional name of the port. Must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME and unique among all ports in the pod.
The protocol (L4) for the port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP (if supported by the cluster). Defaults to TCP if not specified.

Defines the readiness probe for the ephemeral container. This probe determines when the container is considered ready to start accepting traffic; it can be configured with handlers such as exec, httpGet, or tcpSocket, along with timing parameters like initialDelaySeconds and periodSeconds.
Defines the exec action, which runs a specified command in the container. The command's exit code determines probe success (0) or failure (non-zero).

The command to run inside the container for this exec probe. It is not run inside a shell, so shell features like pipes or variables require explicitly invoking a shell. A zero exit status indicates success (healthy/ready), while non-zero indicates failure.
The number of consecutive failures required for the readiness probe to be considered failed after a success. The minimum value is 1; if not specified, the default is 3.
Specifies a gRPC action for the readiness probe. The probe checks the health of a gRPC server by connecting to the specified port and optionally the service name.
The port number to connect to for the gRPC health check. Must be between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If this is not specified, the default behavior is to check the health of the container's overall status.
Specifies the HTTP GET request used by the readiness probe to check container health.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified; set the Host header via httpHeaders instead for HTTP/1.1 virtual hosting.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request for the probe. Each item in the list is an object containing a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The port number (1-65535) or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid port number or an IANA_SVC_NAME.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP request. Accepts 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container starts before the readiness probe is initiated. Must be a non-negative integer; defaults to 0 if not specified.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the readiness probe to be considered successful after it has failed. Must be a positive integer; defaults to 1.
Represents a TCP socket probe action. It checks the container's TCP port for a successful connection to determine readiness.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. Defaults to the pod IP.
The port number (e.g., "80") or a named port (a container port's name) to connect to for the TCP socket readiness probe.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.

List of resource resize policies for the ephemeral container. Each policy specifies a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and a restart policy, which can be either 'NotRequired' (changes take effect without restart) or 'RestartContainer' (container must restart to apply the new resource values).
The name of the resource (e.g., 'cpu' or 'memory') to which this resize policy applies. This field must be one of the allowed resource names for container resize policies.
Defines the restart policy for container resize operations. Allowed values are 'Notify' and 'RestartContainer'.
Resources specifies the compute resources (e.g., CPU, memory) required and allowed for the ephemeral container, including requests and limits as defined by the Kubernetes ResourceRequirements object.

A list of resource claims requested for the ephemeral container. Each claim references a ResourceClaim object by name in the same namespace, enabling the container to use resources such as hardware devices defined by a ResourceClass.
The name of the resource claim that this container will use. The referenced ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

The name chosen for a request in the referenced ResourceClaim. If empty, all resources from the claim are made available; otherwise, only the result of this request is made available to the ephemeral container.
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the ephemeral container. Keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) and values are quantities.
Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required for the ephemeral container. The keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) and the values are quantities as strings.
A list of numeric exit codes for the ephemeral container. The container is restarted according to the restart policy rule when it exits with any of the codes in this list.
SecurityContext defines security settings for the ephemeral container, including user/group IDs, capabilities, SELinux settings, and other access controls.

Controls whether a process in the ephemeral container can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, the container is prevented from gaining additional privileges (no effective UID change, no file capability gain, and no additional privilege escalation). This maps to the Kubernetes `allowPrivilegeEscalation` field in the security context.
The name of an AppArmor profile loaded on the node. This is used when the `type` field is set to 'Localhost'.
The type of AppArmor profile to use. Allowed values are 'Localhost' (requires a localhostProfile), 'RuntimeDefault', and 'Unconfined'.
Linux capabilities to add to or drop from the container's process. The object contains 'add' and 'drop' lists of capability names.
The list of Linux capabilities to add to the ephemeral container's security context, such as 'SYS_ADMIN' or 'NET_ADMIN'.
Specifies a list of capabilities to remove from the container's default capability set. For example, 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME'.
Specifies whether to run the container in privileged mode. Privileged containers are granted additional capabilities and are not subjected to standard security isolation.
Specifies the proc mount type for the container. Allowed values are 'Default' (masks /proc paths) and 'Unmasked' (exposes all /proc paths).
Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only for the ephemeral container.
Sets the group ID (GID) under which the container's entrypoint process runs. If unset, the runtime default is used; this value overrides any group set in the pod-level security context.
Indicates whether the ephemeral container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the kubelet will reject the container if it attempts to run as UID 0 (root).
The user ID (UID) under which the container's processes run. Setting this value overrides the user specified in the container image.
SeLinuxOptions specifies the SELinux context to be applied to the container. It contains user, role, type, and level fields that define the SELinux label.
The SELinux level label applied to the container, typically in the format 's0' or with category suffixes like 's0:c123,c789'.
SELinux role label that applies to the container.
The SELinux type label, such as 'container_t' or 'spc_t', applied to the ephemeral container's security context.
The SELinux user label for the container's security context, as defined in the se_linux_options of the ephemeral container's security context.

seccomp_profile is an object that configures the seccomp profile for the container, with fields for type (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, Localhost) and an optional localhostProfile path when type is Localhost.
Specifies the node-local path to the seccomp profile. This field is honored only when the seccomp profile type is set to 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to apply. Valid values are 'Localhost', 'RuntimeDefault', and 'Unconfined'.
The windows options of the security context.

The inline GMSA (Group Managed Service Account) credential spec to apply to the container. This is a string containing the credential spec JSON, typically populated by the GMSA admission webhook for Windows containers.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows security context.
Specifies whether the container should be run as a HostProcess container on Windows. When set to true, the container runs in the host process namespace.
Specifies the Windows user name (or user SID) to run the container's entrypoint with. If empty, the container runs as the default user.
startupProbe indicates that the Container has successfully initialized. If specified, no other probes are executed until this completes successfully. If this probe fails, the container is restarted.
Exec specifies the command to execute inside the container to determine probe success. A command exit status of 0 indicates success; non-zero indicates failure.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container for this exec probe. It is an array of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is run directly, not through a shell, and the working directory is the container's working directory.
The number of consecutive failures allowed for the startup probe before the container is considered failed. This value sets the maximum tolerated failures during the startup phase.
Specifies the gRPC health check parameters for this probe. When configured, the probe performs a gRPC health check to determine if the container has started successfully.
The port number on which the gRPC health check is performed. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by gRPC.
Defines an HTTP GET request used by the probe. It specifies the path, port, and optional HTTP headers to use when checking container health.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the request. Each header object typically contains 'name' and 'value' fields, as defined by the Kubernetes API.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request.
The value of the HTTP header sent with the startup probe's HTTP GET request. This is a string and can be any valid HTTP header value.
The path to access on the HTTP server when performing the HTTP GET probe. Defaults to '/' if not specified.

The port number or name of the container port to which the HTTP GET request is sent. For a numeric port, it can be given as an integer or string; for a named port, it must be a string matching the name of a container port defined in the pod spec.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request performed by the startup probe.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Defaults to 0.
The number of seconds between each attempt of the startup probe.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after a failure. Typically set to 1.
Configuration for a TCP socket probe. Specifies the port (and optionally host) to perform a TCP check against for the startup probe.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
The TCP port to connect to. Can be a numeric port or a named port on the container.
The duration in seconds that the pod is given to terminate gracefully before being forcefully killed, with a default of 30 seconds when not specified.
timeout_seconds is the number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. If not specified, it defaults to 1 second. The value must be at least 1.
Whether this container should have a stdin open. If true, stdin remains open for the container's process. Defaults to false.
If true, the container runtime closes the stdin channel after a single attach has been opened. This is useful for ephemeral containers that need one-time interactive input.
The name of the container in the Pod to which the ephemeral container should attach. This identifies the target container for the ephemeral container's namespace sharing and debugging.
Path where the container's termination message is written. When the container exits, this file is read to retrieve the termination message. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Sets the policy for reading the termination message. Accepts 'File' (default) to read from the file specified by terminationMessagePath, or 'FallbackToLogsOnError' to use the last chunk of container logs if the file is empty.
When true, allocates a pseudo-TTY for the ephemeral container, enabling interactive terminal sessions.
List of block device mappings for the ephemeral container, defining which volume devices are exposed and their paths inside the container.
The path inside the container where the block device will be mounted (e.g., /dev/sdb).
The name of the volume that this device refers to. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes field.
List of volume mounts for the ephemeral container. Each entry specifies a volume name, the mount path within the container, and options like read-only.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path and cannot contain ':'.
Controls how mounts are propagated from the host to the container and vice versa. Allowed values are None, HostToContainer, and Bidirectional, with None as the default.
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes.
If set to true, the volume mount is read-only, so the ephemeral container cannot write to the mounted volume.
Specifies the recursive read-only mode for the volume mount. Must be one of 'Enabled', 'Disabled', or 'IfPossible'.
Path within the volume from which to mount the volume. Defaults to the volume's root.

The subPath expression to use for the volume mount. Unlike sub_path, this supports environment variable expansion using $(VAR_NAME) syntax. The expanded path is used to mount a subdirectory of the volume into the container.
Working directory for the ephemeral container. Defaults to the image's default working directory if not specified. Must be an absolute path if provided.
List of hostnames for this host alias entry; these names will be resolved to the specified IP address.
The IP address for the host alias entry. This is the address that the specified hostnames will resolve to within the pod.
The name of the image pull secret to use. This secret must exist in the same namespace as the job.
Arguments to the entrypoint. The container image's CMD is used if this is not provided.
The command to run in the init container, equivalent to the container's entrypoint. This overrides the image's ENTRYPOINT instruction, and is provided as a list of strings.
Specifies a list of environment variables to set in the init container. Each item defines a variable name and optionally a value or a source (valueFrom) for the value.
The name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier (e.g., MY_VAR).
The string value to assign to the environment variable.

Specifies a source for the environment variable's value, such as a config map key, secret key, field reference, or resource field reference. If set, the value is taken from the referenced source instead of the 'value' field.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to populate the environment variable's value. Specify the ConfigMap name and the key, with an optional flag to indicate whether the key is required.
The key within the ConfigMap to select. This is required and must correspond to a key present in the referenced ConfigMap's data.
Name of the ConfigMap to select from.
Specifies whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If set to true, the reference is optional and the container can start even if the ConfigMap or key does not exist.
FieldRef selects a field of the Pod. Supported field paths include metadata.name, metadata.namespace, metadata.uid, spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.podIP, and status.hostIP.
The API version of the referent field. For pod field references, this is typically 'v1'. If not specified, the default is 'v1'.
Path to the pod field from which to select a value, such as metadata.name or spec.nodeName.
Whether the referenced key is optional. If set to true, the environment variable is set only if the key exists; if false (default), a missing key causes an error.

Reference to a resource field of the container (e.g., requests.cpu, limits.memory) to be exposed as an environment variable. This object specifies the resource name and optionally a divisor for scaling the value.

The name of the container whose resource (e.g., CPU or memory limits/requests) this field references. In a ResourceFieldSelector, this selects a resource value from a specific container in the pod, such as an init container or a regular container.

A quantity string that specifies the divisor for the resource value in the resource field selector. The resource value is divided by this quantity to produce the environment variable's value, allowing unit conversion (e.g., '1m' for milli-CPU, '1Mi' for mebibytes). If not set, the default divisor is 1 for CPU and 1Mi for memory.
Resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'. Specifies the resource name for the container's resource field reference.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace to populate the environment variable value. This references a specific key within a named Secret, and the Secret must exist before the pod is created.
The key of the secret to select from. Must be a valid secret key.
The name of the Secret to select the key from.
Optional indicates whether the Secret or its key must be defined. Defaults to false, meaning the secret and key must exist.
List of sources to populate environment variables in the container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret, optionally with a prefix to prepend to variable names.
Reference to a ConfigMap from which to populate environment variables in the init container. The ConfigMap's data keys become environment variable names and values become their values.
Name of the referenced ConfigMap. This is the name of the ConfigMap whose key-value pairs are used to populate environment variables in the container.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If set to true, the ConfigMap may be absent and missing keys will be ignored. Defaults to false.
An optional prefix that is prepended to each key from the referenced ConfigMap or Secret when creating environment variable names. Must be a valid C identifier.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret whose data will be exposed as environment variables in the container.
The name of the Secret resource to reference. This Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod, and its data will be used to populate environment variables as specified.

Specify whether the Secret must be defined. If optional is true, the Secret may be absent, allowing the container to start without it; if false or unset, the referenced Secret must exist, otherwise the container creation fails.
The container image to use for this init container.
The image pull policy for this init container. Allowed values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never, controlling when Kubernetes pulls the container image.
Lifecycle defines handlers that run during the container's lifecycle, specifically `postStart` and `preStop`, allowing custom actions after container startup and before container shutdown.
post_start defines the postStart lifecycle hook, which is executed immediately after a container is started. It can specify an exec command or an HTTP GET request to perform.
Exec specifies a command to be executed in the container as part of the post-start lifecycle hook. It uses an ExecAction, which runs the defined command immediately after the container starts.

The command line to execute in the container, specified as a list of arguments where the first element is the command. It is executed directly without a shell, with the working directory set to root ('/').
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as part of the lifecycle hook. This action contacts the container on the given port and path, allowing the container to react to lifecycle events.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; you may prefer to set the Host header via httpHeaders instead.
List of HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request. For example, 'Authorization' or 'Content-Type'.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the GET request.
The HTTP URL path to request in the GET request. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
Port number or named port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Accepts an integer port number (e.g., 8080) or a string port name (e.g., 'http') defined in the container's ports.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Sleep action for a postStart lifecycle hook. The object specifies a sleep duration in seconds via its `seconds` field.
Specifies the duration in seconds for the sleep action. The value must be a non-negative integer.
Defines a TCP socket action that is executed after the container starts as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. The action attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified host and port.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port number or name of the socket to connect to. Can be an integer port number or a named port (e.g., 'http').
The preStop hook is executed immediately before a container is terminated. It defines an action (exec command or HTTP request) to perform during termination.
Exec specifies an action to execute a command inside the container as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This object defines the command(s) to run before the container is terminated.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, where the working directory is root ('/') in the container's filesystem. It is exec'd directly, not run in a shell, so shell operators such as pipes or variable expansion are not processed.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to be executed as the pre-stop lifecycle hook. The container will receive this request before termination.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Optional list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request sent to the endpoint. Each item defines a header name and value to be sent as part of the HTTP request.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the GET request, such as 'Content-Type'.
The value of the HTTP header. This value is sent as part of the HTTP GET request in the pre-stop lifecycle hook.
Path to access on the HTTP server when performing the HTTP GET request in the pre-stop lifecycle hook.
The port number (1-65535) or name of the port to access on the container. If a name is used, it must match a container port name.
The protocol used for the HTTP GET request: `HTTP` or `HTTPS`. Defaults to `HTTP`.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.

Sleep represents a lifecycle hook action that pauses the container for a specified duration. This is a SleepAction object, which contains a 'seconds' field indicating the number of seconds to sleep before the container is terminated.
The number of seconds to sleep before the container is terminated. This is the duration of the sleep action in the preStop lifecycle hook.
Specifies a TCP socket handler for the pre-stop lifecycle hook of an init container, used to make a TCP connection to a configured port when the container is terminated.
The host to connect to for the TCP socket pre-stop hook. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.

The port number or name of the port on the container to connect to for the TCP socket lifecycle hook. Must be a valid TCP port number (1-65535) or the name of a container port, specified as a string (e.g., '8080' or 'http').
liveness_probe is a block that defines a probe to check if the container is alive. In init containers, probes are not supported because init containers run to completion, so this field is ignored.

Exec defines an exec-based liveness probe action. It contains the command to be executed inside the container; a zero exit code indicates a healthy container, while any non-zero exit code indicates failure.

The command to execute in the container for the exec liveness probe. It is a list of strings, with the first element being the command and subsequent elements being arguments. The command is run directly without a shell, so shell features like pipes or environment variable expansion are not available unless you invoke a shell explicitly.
Minimum consecutive failures for the liveness probe to be considered failed after a successful probe. Defaults to 3; must be at least 1.
The gRPC health check configuration for the liveness probe. When specified, the probe uses gRPC to perform a health check on the given port, optionally with a service name.
The port number to connect to for the gRPC health check on the init container. This should be the port on which the container's gRPC health server is listening.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is to check the overall server status.
Performs an HTTP GET request against the container to determine liveness. Configure the request path, port, host, scheme, and any custom HTTP headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request in the liveness probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
List of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The header field name, such as 'X-Custom-Header', to include in the HTTP request for the liveness probe.
The value of the HTTP header.
The HTTP path to access on the server; defaults to `/`.
The port number or name of the port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. The port can be specified as a numeric value or as a named port defined in the container.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request (HTTP or HTTPS). Defaults to HTTP.
The HTTP scheme to use for the liveness probe request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the liveness probe begins running. This is the initialDelaySeconds field of a Kubernetes probe.
How often (in seconds) to perform the liveness probe. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 10 seconds.
Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For liveness probes, this value must be 1 and the minimum value is 1.

Configures a TCP socket check for the liveness probe. The probe attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's IP address on the specified port; failure to connect indicates the container is not healthy.
Specifies the hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP check. If not set, defaults to the pod's IP address.
The TCP port to connect to for the liveness probe. This can be a numeric port number or a named port on the container.
The timeout in seconds for the liveness probe. If the probe does not complete within this time, it is considered failed.
Name of the init container. Must be a valid DNS_LABEL and unique within the pod.
A list of ports to expose from the container. Each port object typically includes a containerPort (integer), protocol (TCP/UDP/SCTP), and optional name, hostPort, and hostIP fields.
The port that the container exposes. Must be a valid TCP or UDP port number between 1 and 65535.
The host IP address to bind the port to. If omitted, the port is bound to all host interfaces.
The port on the host node to which the container port is mapped. If not specified, the container port is not accessible from outside the node.
Name of the port. Must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME and unique within the pod. Optional.
The network protocol used by the port. Valid values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP. Defaults to TCP.

Defines the readiness probe for the init container. In Kubernetes, readiness probes are not used for init containers because these containers run to completion and do not serve traffic; the probe configuration is accepted but has no operational effect.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with a status code of 0.
Command to run inside the container for the readiness probe. This is an array of strings that forms the command line, executed directly without a shell.
The minimum consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3 for readiness probes.
Specifies the gRPC action for the readiness probe. It contains the port to check and optionally the service name, allowing a gRPC health check to be performed on the container.
The port number on which the gRPC health check should be performed. Must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the service to include in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the default gRPC health check behavior is used.
Specifies the HTTP GET request parameters used by the readiness probe to check container health, such as the path, port, and HTTP scheme.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each header defines a name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the probe's HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the request for the readiness probe's HTTP get action.
The HTTP path to request for the probe. For example, `/healthz`.
The port number or name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
Specifies the protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' (the default) and 'HTTPS'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Minimum value is 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1.

Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after a failure. Must be a positive integer (>=1); default is 1. For readiness probes, this can be set higher, but for liveness and startup probes it must be 1.

Specifies the TCP socket probe configuration for the readiness probe. It defines how the kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to a specific port (and optionally host) on the container to determine if it is ready to serve traffic.
The host name to connect to. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The port number or name of the port to connect to during the TCP readiness probe. Can be an integer port number or a named port defined in the container's ports.

The grace period in seconds allowed for a pod to terminate gracefully. During this time, Kubernetes waits for the pod to shut down after sending a termination signal; if the pod does not exit within this period, it is forcefully terminated with SIGKILL. Defaults to 30 seconds if not specified.
Number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. Defaults to 1 if not specified.

This is a list of resize policies for the init container's resources. Each policy specifies a resource name (such as 'cpu' or 'memory') and a restart policy ('NotRequired' or 'RestartContainer') controlling how the kubelet handles resource resizing for that resource.
Name of the Kubernetes resource to which the resize policy applies, such as 'cpu' or 'memory'.

Specifies whether the init container should be restarted when its requested resources are adjusted. Allowed values are `NotRequired` (no restart needed) and `RestartContainer` (restart the container). This field is part of the container resize policy in Kubernetes.
Resource requirements for the init container, including requests and limits for compute resources such as CPU and memory.
Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this init container. This is an alpha feature and may change in the future.
Name of the ResourceClaim that this container requests. This must match the name of a ResourceClaim object in the same namespace as the pod.
Map of resource type to maximum amount allowed for the init container (e.g., cpu, memory). Each value is a Kubernetes quantity string, such as '500m' for CPU or '128Mi' for memory.
Map of resource requirements for the init container, specifying the minimum amount of CPU and memory (e.g., cpu=100m, memory=1Gi). Values are Kubernetes quantity strings.
Specifies the operator used to match the container exit code against the exit_codes list. Allowed values are 'In' and 'NotIn'.
Specifies the list of numeric exit codes for which this restart policy rule applies. If the container exits with any of these codes, the corresponding restart policy action is triggered.
Security settings for the init container, such as user ID, group ID, Linux capabilities, and SELinux options. This field defines the security context that applies only to this init container.

Indicates whether the container process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, the no_new_privs flag is enabled, preventing privilege escalation; it defaults to true unless the container is privileged or has CAP_SYS_ADMIN.
AppArmor profile to apply to the container. Can specify a runtime default, unconfined, or a localhost profile reference.
Name of the AppArmor profile to apply if type is set to 'Localhost'. This refers to a profile pre-loaded on the node.
Type of AppArmor profile. Allowed values are RuntimeDefault, Localhost, and Unconfined. If using Localhost, a localhostProfile must also be specified.
Configures Linux capabilities for the init container. Allows adding or dropping specific capabilities via the 'add' and 'drop' lists.
Specifies Linux capabilities to add to the container's capability set. Each item is a capability name, such as 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME'.
List of capabilities to drop from the container's default capability set. Each element is a capability name (e.g., 'ALL' or 'NET_ADMIN').
If true, runs the init container in privileged mode, granting it elevated permissions and access to host devices.
The proc mount type for the container. The default is 'Default' which masks the /proc filesystem for security, while 'Unmasked' removes those restrictions.
If true, the container's root filesystem is mounted read-only.
The group ID (GID) to run the container entrypoint process as. Overrides the group ID specified in the container image if set. Must be a non-negative integer.

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the kubelet will validate that the container does not run as UID 0 (root) and will refuse to start the container if it does. This field is part of the container's security context.
The user ID that the container's process will run as. If specified, it overrides the user defined in the container image.
SELinux options applied to the container, allowing specification of level, role, type, and user. If omitted, the container inherits SELinux settings from the pod or node.
The SELinux level (MLS/MCS) for the container, such as 's0' or 's0:c123'.
The SELinux role label assigned to the container. This is part of the SELinux context, for example 'system_r', and is used in the se_linux_options of the security context.
The SELinux type label for the container.
The SELinux user label for the container, as part of the SELinux context.

Optional. Defines the seccomp profile for the init container. It contains a `type` field with allowed values `RuntimeDefault`, `Unconfined`, or `Localhost`, and a `localhostProfile` field specifying the node-local profile path when `type` is `Localhost`.
Specifies the path to a locally-defined seccomp profile on the node. This field is required when the seccomp profile type is set to 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to apply. Valid values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', and 'Unconfined'.
Windows-specific security settings for the container, such as GMSA credential spec and run-as-user. Only applicable to Windows containers.

The inline contents of the GMSA credential spec, populated by the GMSA admission webhook when the `gmsa_credential_spec_name` field references a pre-defined GMSA credential spec. This provides the security configuration for Windows containers without needing to reference a separate file.
The name of the GMSA (Group Managed Service Account) credential spec to use for the container. This is used in the Windows security context to provide an Active Directory identity to the container.

Specifies whether the container should run as a Windows HostProcess container. When true, the container is given access to the host's process namespace and can run with elevated privileges, which is useful for cluster-level operations.

The username to run the container's entrypoint as for Windows containers. If specified, it must match a valid user in the container image. This field is part of the Windows security context options and is used only for Windows containers.
A block that configures the startup probe for the container. It determines whether the container has started successfully, and if it fails, the container is restarted.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container. The probe considers the container started successfully if the command exits with a zero exit code.

The command to execute inside the container as part of the startup probe's exec action. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. If not specified, the container's default entrypoint is used.
The number of consecutive failures allowed before the startup probe gives up. In Kubernetes, once this threshold is exceeded, the container is restarted.

The grpc block configures a gRPC health check for the startup probe. It specifies the port to connect to (required) and optionally the service name to check, allowing the probe to verify container readiness via gRPC.
The port number of the gRPC service. Must be a valid port number between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the empty string is used, which means the gRPC server's default service is checked.

Configures the HTTP GET action used by the startup probe to check the container's health. The probe sends an HTTP GET request to the container's IP address on the specified port and path; a response code in the 200-399 range indicates success.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. Defaults to the pod IP.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request performed by the startup probe. Each object defines a single header with a name and value.
The header field name for the HTTP header to set in the HTTP request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The HTTP request path to access on the server. Defaults to the root path (/).
The port number to access on the container for the HTTP GET probe. Must be a valid integer port number (1-65535) or the name of an IANA_SVC_NAME port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' (default) and 'HTTPS'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'.
Number of seconds after the container starts before the startup probe is initiated. Defaults to 0.
The number of seconds between each probe attempt. Defaults to 10 seconds.
The minimum number of consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful. For startup probes, this is typically set to 1.
Defines the TCP socket check for the startup probe. The probe attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's port to determine if it has started successfully.
Optional host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe; defaults to the pod IP.
Number or name of the TCP port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME.

The duration in seconds that Kubernetes waits for the container to terminate gracefully before forcibly stopping it. If this value is 0, the pod is killed immediately; a positive value gives the container time to shut down cleanly.
Number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Must be a positive integer.
Whether the container should have stdin enabled. If true, the container runtime will allocate a stdin stream for the container. Defaults to false.
If true, the container's standard input is opened once and then closed, rather than being kept open for the container's lifetime. Typically used together with 'stdin' to provide one-shot input.
Path to the file where the container's termination message is written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Specifies how the container's termination message is sourced. Allowed values are 'File' (default) to read the termination message from a file (e.g., /dev/termination-log), or 'FallbackToLogsOnError' to fall back to writing the last part of container logs if the message file is empty.
Indicates whether the container should allocate a TTY. When true, the container is provided with a pseudo-terminal. Defaults to false.
List of raw block device mappings for the container. Each entry specifies the volume name and the device path inside the container.
The path inside the container at which the raw block device is exposed.
Name of the volume (as defined in the pod's volumes) that this volume device refers to. Must match the name of a volume in the pod.
A list of volume mounts for the init container. Each volume mount specifies a volume name and a mount path within the container.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path and must not contain ':'.

Specifies the mount propagation behavior for this volume mount, controlling whether mount points are propagated between the container and the host or between containers. Valid values are 'None' (no propagation), 'HostToContainer' (host mounts are visible in the container), and 'Bidirectional' (mounts propagate both ways).
Name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's volumes list.
Boolean flag indicating whether the volume is mounted read-only. Defaults to false, meaning the mount is read-write.
recursive_read_only controls whether recursive read-only mounts are enabled. Allowed values are 'Enabled', 'IfPossible', and 'Disabled'.
Specifies a sub-path inside the referenced volume to mount instead of its root, allowing you to mount a specific directory or file from the volume.
Path within the volume from which the container's volume is mounted, with support for environment variable expansion using $(VAR_NAME) syntax, similar to subPath but allowing templated paths.
The container's working directory. Defaults to the image's default. Must be an absolute path.

The name of the condition that must be satisfied (status 'True') for the pod to be considered ready. This condition must be set and maintained by some controller or external system; if absent or false, the pod is not ready.
Name of the resource claim, unique within the pod. It is used to reference the claim from containers and in the pod's resource claim status.

The name of the ResourceClaim object that this pod references. This must match the name of a ResourceClaim in the same namespace as the pod. In the Kubernetes API, this corresponds to the `resourceClaimName` field of the PodResourceClaim.
The name of a ResourceClaimTemplate resource that should be used to create a ResourceClaim for this pod. The ResourceClaim is created in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the ResourceClaim object that this container's claim refers to.
The name of the scheduling gate. Must be unique among all scheduling gates on the pod.
The name of the sysctl parameter to set, e.g., kernel.shm_rmid_forced.
The value of the sysctl setting. For example, in a sysctl entry like 'kernel.shm_rmid_forced=1', this field holds the string '1'.
The taint effect to match. Allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, NoExecute, or an empty string to match all effects.
The key of the taint that this toleration matches. When the operator is 'Equal', the key must be specified; when the operator is 'Exists', the key can be omitted.
The operator to apply to the value. Allowed values are 'Equal' and 'Exists'. Defaults to 'Equal'.

toleration_seconds specifies the duration in seconds for which the pod will tolerate a taint with the NoExecute effect. After this period, the pod is evicted if the taint still exists. It is applicable only when the operator is 'Exists' and the effect is 'NoExecute'.
The value to match the taint's value. This field is required when the operator is 'Equal'; it must be empty when the operator is 'Exists'.
Label selector used to identify the set of pods that the topology spread constraint applies to. Must match the pods' labels for the constraint to be selected.
A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values (for operators that require them).
The label key that the selector applies to. This key must exist in the object's labels for the requirement to match (depending on the operator).
Operator defines the relationship between the label key and the values in the match expression. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
List of values for the label selector match expression. Required when the operator is In or NotIn; must be empty for Exists or DoesNotExist.

match_labels is a map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the map is equivalent to a matchExpressions element whose key field is "key", operator is "In", and values array contains only "value". The requirements are ANDed.

A list of pod label keys used in topology spread constraints. The values of these keys from the pod being scheduled are combined with the constraint's labelSelector to determine the set of pods for spreading calculations.

Maximum degree of skew allowed between topology domains for matching pods. This is the maximum difference in number of matching pods between the most and least populated topology domains. Must be a positive integer.

The minimum number of domains (e.g., regions, zones, nodes) the cluster must have for the topology spread constraint to be enforced. If the number of eligible domains is less than minDomains, pods are scheduled as if the constraint were not specified.
Indicates how to treat node affinity when calculating pod spread. Allowed values are 'Honor' (default) and 'Ignore'.
Determines how tainted nodes are treated when spreading pods across topology domains. Valid values are 'Honor' (respect node taints) and 'Ignore' (disregard node taints).
The key of node labels. Nodes that have a label with this key and identical values are considered to be in the same topology, which is used to spread pods across different failure domains.
Specifies how to handle a pod that does not satisfy the spread constraint. Valid values are 'DoNotSchedule' (hard constraint, default) and 'ScheduleAnyway' (soft constraint).
Represents an AWS Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume that can be mounted as a volume in the pod. This is a volume source configuration for using an existing EBS volume as storage.
Filesystem type to mount for the AWS Elastic Block Store volume. Defaults to ext4 if not specified.
Partition number of the AWS EBS volume to mount. If omitted, the volume is mounted by its name; specify a partition (e.g., 1 for /dev/sda1) when the volume has multiple partitions.
Specify whether the AWS EBS volume should be mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
The unique identifier of the AWS EBS volume to mount into the pod.
This volume represents an Azure Disk resource attached to the pod. It enables the pod to access persistent storage from Azure.
The caching mode for the Azure data disk. Valid values are None, ReadOnly, and ReadWrite. Defaults to None.
The name of the Azure data disk that should be mounted as a volume.
The URI of the Azure virtual hard disk (VHD) blob. Must be a valid Azure blob URI, e.g., https://someaccount.blob.core.windows.net/vhds/somedisk.vhd.
Filesystem type to mount for the Azure disk (e.g., ext4, xfs). Defaults to ext4 if not specified.
The kind of Azure disk mounted as a volume. Allowed values are 'Shared', 'Dedicated', and 'Managed'; defaults to 'Managed'.
Whether the Azure disk is mounted as read-only. Set to true to make the disk read-only.
Configures a volume backed by an Azure File share. This block defines the connection details (like share name and storage account secret) required to mount an Azure Files share into the pod.
Specifies whether the Azure File volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that contains the Azure Storage account name and key used to access the Azure file share. This secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the Azure file share that should be mounted.
cephfs defines a CephFS volume source, allowing a pod to mount a Ceph Filesystem into the container. This is one of the supported volume types in the volumes list.
A list of Ceph monitor addresses (host:port) for the CephFS volume. This is a required field for CephFS volumes, specifying the Ceph cluster monitors.
Path within CephFS to mount. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
Indicates whether the CephFS filesystem should be mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
The path to the secret file containing the CephFS authentication keyring, e.g. /etc/ceph/user.secret.
secret_ref is a local object reference to a Kubernetes secret that provides the keyring for CephFS authentication. It must reference a secret in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the Kubernetes secret that provides CephFS credentials. This secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The RADOS user name used for authentication with the Ceph cluster. Defaults to 'admin' if not specified.
Represents an OpenStack Cinder volume source for mounting a Cinder volume into the pod.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Ex. 'ext4', 'xfs', 'ntfs'. Implicitly inferred to be 'ext4' if unspecified.
Marks the Cinder volume as read-only. When true, the volume is mounted read-only.
Optional reference to a secret in the same namespace that provides OpenStack authentication credentials for the Cinder volume. If omitted, the node's default OpenStack credentials are used.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that holds the authentication credentials for the Cinder volume.
The ID of the Cinder volume to mount into the pod.
Configuration for a volume sourced from a Kubernetes ConfigMap, allowing Pods to consume ConfigMap data as files.
Optional file mode (in octal) applied to all files in the ConfigMap volume. Defaults to 0644 when unset.

Optional list of key-to-path mappings for the ConfigMap volume. If unspecified, all keys in the referenced ConfigMap are projected as files named by key. If specified, only the listed keys are projected, each to the path given in the item's 'path' field.
The key in the referenced ConfigMap whose data value is projected into the volume at the specified path.
Mode is the file permission bits, specified as an octal number (e.g., 0644), applied to the file created from this ConfigMap volume item.
The relative path for the config map item within the volume. This is the file name or path where the key's value will be written, relative to the volume mount point.
Name of the ConfigMap to use as the volume source. This must match the name of a ConfigMap in the same namespace.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. If set to true, the volume will not fail if the ConfigMap or specific keys are missing. Defaults to false (must exist).
Defines a volume backed by a Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver, enabling the pod to mount storage provided by an external CSI plugin.
The name of the CSI driver to use for this volume. This must match the name of a CSI driver registered on the cluster.
Filesystem type to mount, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. If not specified, the CSI driver determines the filesystem type.
References a Kubernetes Secret containing credentials required for the CSI driver's NodePublishVolume operation. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the secret containing the credentials needed for the CSI node publish operation. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Indicates whether the CSI volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
A map of key-value pairs passed as volume attributes to the CSI driver.
Configuration for a volume that uses the Downward API to expose pod metadata (such as labels and annotations) to the container via files.
Optional file mode (permissions) used for all files created in the downward API volume when not overridden per path. Defaults to 0644.

Items is a list of downward API volume file definitions. Each item specifies a file path and a field reference (fieldRef) or resource field reference (resourceFieldRef) that populates the file with the corresponding value.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, spec.nodeName) to expose as the value of the downward API item.
The API version of the schema that field_path uses, typically 'v1'.
The relative file path inside the volume where the field value is exposed. The path must not contain '..' and must not start with '/'.
Optional file permission mode bits for the file, specified as an octal integer (e.g., 0644). Defaults to 0644 if not set.
Path within the volume where the value from the selected field is exposed. This must be a relative path and cannot contain '..' to escape the volume.
Selects a resource field of the container, such as limits.cpu or requests.memory, for the downward API volume item.

The name of the container to which the resource field refers. This is required when referencing container-level resources like CPU or memory limits/requests in the downward API. If omitted, the field refers to the pod's own resources.

The divisor for the resource quantity, used to scale the value of a container resource (e.g., cpu or memory) in a downward API field. It must be a valid Kubernetes quantity, such as '1m' for millicores or '1Gi' for gibibytes, and defaults to '1' if unspecified.
The name of the resource to expose via the downward API, such as 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory'.
