Configures an emptyDir volume, which is a temporary directory created on the node's filesystem and shared by containers in the pod. It is initially empty and is removed when the pod is deleted, useful for inter-container communication or temporary data.
The storage medium for the emptyDir volume. Supported values: "Memory" (uses tmpfs, RAM-backed), "HugePages" (uses node hugepages), or unset (default, uses disk-backed storage).
Maximum size of the emptyDir volume, specified as a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., "1Gi"). This field is optional and enforces a limit on the storage used by the volume.

Configures an ephemeral volume that is created and deleted with the pod. This volume type is defined in Kubernetes and typically uses a VolumeAttributesClass or a template to create a volume with the same lifecycle as the pod.

volumeClaimTemplate is a template for a PersistentVolumeClaim that will be created for this ephemeral volume. The claim is created in the same namespace as the pod and is deleted when the pod is deleted, and it defines the metadata and spec of the resulting PersistentVolumeClaim.
Standard Kubernetes object metadata (labels, annotations, name, etc.) for the PersistentVolumeClaim created by this ephemeral volume.

Annotations is a map of string keys and values used to store arbitrary non-identifying metadata with the volume claim template. This metadata is not used for querying and should be preserved by clients when updating the object.
The creation timestamp of the generated PersistentVolumeClaim, assigned by the server in RFC3339 format. This field is read-only and managed by the Kubernetes API.

The duration in seconds before the volume claim created from this template is deleted after a deletion request. Must be a non-negative integer; 0 means delete immediately, and if unset the default grace period for the PVC type is used.
The time at which this object is marked for deletion, in RFC 3339 format. This field is set by the server when graceful deletion is requested, and is not directly settable by a client.
Must be empty before the object can be deleted from the registry. Each entry is an identifier for a finalizer that ensures cleanup of dependent resources or external systems.

An optional prefix used by the Kubernetes server to generate a unique name for this volume claim template if the 'name' field is not provided. The server appends a random suffix to this prefix to create the actual name.
A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state. Populated by the system when changes are made to the object's spec.
Labels are key-value pairs attached to the volume claim template metadata. They can be used for organization and selection, such as by a persistent volume claim selector.

Managed fields is a list of entries that track which fields were set by which manager (e.g., a user, controller, or apply path). It is used by Kubernetes server-side apply to determine ownership and resolve conflicts, and is typically maintained automatically by the system.
The API version of the resource that this managed field entry applies to.
Represents the type of the managed fields entry. In Kubernetes, the only valid value is 'FieldsV1', indicating the fields are in the FieldsV1 format.
fields_v1 stores a set of managed fields in a Trie-like data structure, serialized as JSON. It represents the parsed JSON of the fields that a manager applied.
The name of the manager that last applied the fields in this managed fields entry.
The operation that was performed on the field, such as Apply, Update, or Delete (as defined by Kubernetes managed fields).
The subresource (e.g., 'status') of the resource to which the managed fields apply.
The time at which the managed field entry was applied, in RFC3339 format.

The Kubernetes namespace in which the PersistentVolumeClaim generated from this template will be created. Since the claim is always created in the same namespace as the pod, this field is typically omitted.

A list of references to the owning objects, used to establish owner dependencies for garbage collection and cascading deletion. Each entry includes apiVersion, kind, name, uid, and optionally controller and blockOwnerDeletion flags.
The API version of the referent object.
If true, AND if the owner has the 'foregroundDeletion' finalizer, the owner cannot be deleted from the key-value store until this reference is removed. Defaults to false.
If true, this reference points to the managing controller of the resource.
Kind of the owner object referenced by this owner reference, such as ReplicaSet or StatefulSet.
The name of the owner object that this reference points to. This field is part of the owner reference metadata used to identify the owning resource for garbage collection and dependents.
The UID of the owner object that this reference points to. It uniquely identifies the owner alongside apiVersion and kind.
The resource version, as maintained by the server, used to detect concurrent modifications to the object. It is returned in responses and can be used in update requests for optimistic concurrency.
The self-link URL for the volume claim template metadata. This is a system-generated field used to identify the object in the Kubernetes API.
UID is a system-generated unique identifier for the object, assigned by the server on creation. It is read-only and cannot be set by the user.
Specification of the persistent volume claim template. Defines the desired characteristics of the PVC, such as storage class, access modes, and resource requests, used for the ephemeral volume.
The desired access modes the volume should have. Valid values include ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteMany, and ReadWriteOncePod.
Specifies the data source for the volume claim, such as a VolumeSnapshot or an existing PersistentVolumeClaim. This field is optional.
The API group of the referenced data source resource (e.g., 'snapshot.storage.k8s.io' for VolumeSnapshot). If empty, the resource is assumed to be in the core API group.

The kind (type) of the data source resource being referenced, such as PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot. This is part of the TypedLocalObjectReference that identifies an object to use as the data source for the volume claim.
The name of the data source resource (e.g., a PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot) referenced by this claim's dataSource, used as the source for the volume claim.

data_source_ref is an object that references a data source (such as a VolumeSnapshot or PersistentVolumeClaim) used to populate the ephemeral volume. It supports specifying the exact API group, kind, and name of the source, enabling advanced volume provisioning scenarios.
The API group of the referenced resource. For example, a VolumeSnapshot would use 'snapshot.storage.k8s.io'. Leave empty to refer to a resource in the core API group.
The resource kind of the data source reference. For example, 'PersistentVolumeClaim'.

The name of the referenced object that serves as the data source for the ephemeral volume's persistent volume claim. This is the name of the object (e.g., a VolumeSnapshot or PersistentVolumeClaim) in the same namespace.
The namespace of the referenced data source object. If not provided, the data source is assumed to be in the same namespace as the volume claim.

Specifies the minimum resources required for the ephemeral volume claim. This object supports 'requests' and 'limits', with 'requests.storage' being the field commonly used to request a specific storage size.
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. Each key is a resource name (e.g., 'storage') and each value is a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., '10Gi').
The minimum amount of resources required for the ephemeral volume claim. Keys are resource names (e.g., `storage`, `cpu`, `memory`) and values are Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., `5Gi`, `100m`).
A label selector used to filter PersistentVolumes that are eligible for binding to this volume claim. Only PersistentVolumes with labels matching this selector will be considered.
A list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed.
The label key that this selector requirement applies to. The match expression evaluates labels on the resource against this key.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and the set of values in a label selector requirement. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values that the label key must match when the operator is `In` or `NotIn`. For `Exists` and `DoesNotExist`, this field must be empty.

A map of key-value pairs that must be matched by the labels of a resource. All specified labels must be present for the selector to match. This is equivalent to an 'In' matchExpression for each key with a single value.
Specifies the name of the StorageClass to use for the persistent volume claim. If not set, the cluster's default StorageClass is used.
The name of the VolumeAttributesClass to use for the volume claim template. This specifies the class that defines additional volume attributes for the persistent volume claim.
Specifies the volume mode for the PersistentVolumeClaim, either 'Filesystem' (default) or 'Block'. This indicates whether the volume is formatted with a filesystem or exposed as a raw block device.
The name of the PersistentVolume to bind to this claim. If specified, the claim will bind to that volume instead of dynamically provisioning one.
Defines a Fibre Channel (FC) volume source, allowing a pod to mount a Fibre Channel storage device.
Filesystem type to mount, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system.
The logical unit number (LUN) for the Fibre Channel volume, specifying the storage device's LUN ID.
If true, the Fibre Channel volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read/write).
Specifies the list of Fibre Channel target World Wide Names (WWNs) for the volume. Each entry is a WWN string identifying a Fibre Channel target device.
List of Fibre Channel WWIDs (World Wide Identifiers) that identify the volumes to be mounted. Used for multipath configurations instead of specifying a target WWN and LUN.

Represents a FlexVolume volume source in a Kubernetes pod spec. FlexVolume is a generic volume plugin that mounts a volume using an executable driver, with driver-specific options provided in this object.
The name of the FlexVolume driver to use for this volume. This is a required field for a flexVolume volume source.

Specifies the filesystem type to mount (e.g., ext4, xfs). Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Defaults to the first filesystem type listed in the FlexVolume options, or the default filesystem type.
A map of driver-specific options to pass to the flexVolume driver. Keys and values are strings, and the map can be empty.
Whether the flexVolume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read-write).
Optional reference to a Kubernetes Secret in the same namespace, used by the FlexVolume driver to obtain sensitive data such as credentials. The reference must contain the name of the Secret.
The name of the secret that provides the credentials or data for the FlexVolume.
Represents a Flocker volume source, used to mount a dataset managed by Flocker into the pod.
The name of the Flocker dataset to mount as a volume. Must be the name of an existing dataset in Flocker.
The UUID of the Flocker dataset to mount. This uniquely identifies the dataset in Flocker.
Represents a GCE (Google Compute Engine) persistent disk as a volume source. Used to mount a GCE Persistent Disk into the pod.
Filesystem type to mount for the GCE persistent disk, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Defaults to ext4 if not specified.
The partition number on the GCE persistent disk to mount. If omitted, the entire disk is mounted.
The name of the GCE Persistent Disk to mount. This must match the name of the disk in the GCE project.
Mounts the GCE persistent disk as read-only when set to true. Defaults to false, meaning read-write access.

Configures a volume backed by a Git repository. The volume is populated by cloning the specified repository, optionally at a particular revision or subdirectory. Note: This volume type is deprecated; consider using alternative volume sources.
The target directory name in the volume where the git repository will be checked out. If not specified, the repository is cloned to the volume's root. Must not contain or start with '..'.
The URL of the Git repository to clone into the volume.
Specifies the commit hash to be checked out for the git repository.
Specifies a Glusterfs volume as the storage source for the volume. The volume is mounted from a Glusterfs filesystem.
Name of the Endpoints object that defines the GlusterFS cluster endpoints (IPs and ports). This is required for a GlusterFS volume and must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The path to the GlusterFS volume that should be mounted. This is the path of the volume as defined on the GlusterFS server, not a local filesystem path.
Mounted read-only if true. Forces the GlusterFS volume to be mounted with read-only permissions. Defaults to false.

Specifies a hostPath volume, which mounts a file or directory from the host node's filesystem into the pod. The host_path object contains configuration such as the path on the host and the type of mount.
Specifies the path on the host node to mount into the pod. This is the directory or file on the host that is exposed to the container via the hostPath volume.

Type of the hostPath volume. Determines how the referenced path is checked and created before the pod starts. Allowed values: '', Directory, DirectoryOrCreate, File, FileOrCreate, Socket, CharDevice, BlockDevice.
Volume source that mounts an OCI image as a volume, with options for the image reference and pull policy.
The pull policy for the image volume. Allowed values are Always, Never, and IfNotPresent. Defaults to IfNotPresent.
The image reference to use for the image volume, in the format <image>:<tag> or <image>@<digest>.
Represents an iSCSI volume source. This configures an iSCSI volume to be attached to the pod, including settings for the target portal, IQN, LUN, filesystem type, and read-only mode.
Indicates whether CHAP authentication is enabled for iSCSI discovery of the volume.
Indicates whether CHAP authentication is enabled for the iSCSI session. When set to true, CHAP session authentication is used.
Filesystem type of the iSCSI volume to mount, such as 'ext4', 'xfs', or 'ntfs'. If unspecified, Kubernetes may infer a default (commonly ext4). Must be supported by the host OS.
Custom iSCSI initiator name. If specified together with iscsi_interface, a new iSCSI interface <target portal>:<volume name> will be created for the connection.
The iSCSI Qualified Name (IQN) of the target. This uniquely identifies the iSCSI target on the network.
The iSCSI interface name used for the volume connection. Defaults to 'default' (iSCSI over TCP).
The iSCSI Target Lun number. Specifies the logical unit number on the iSCSI target.
List of additional iSCSI portals to connect to, formatted as `ip:port`. Used when the iSCSI target has multiple portals.
If true, the ISCSI volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
secret_ref is a reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the CHAP secrets used for iSCSI authentication. This is an optional field; when set, it points to a Secret in the same namespace.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that contains the CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI target.
targetPortal is iSCSI Target Portal. The Portal is either an IP or ip_addr:port if the port is other than default (typically TCP ports 860 and 3260).
The name of the volume. Must be a DNS_LABEL and unique within the pod.
nfs represents an NFS (Network File System) volume that is mounted into the pod. It configures the volume to use an NFS server as the storage source.
The path that is exported by the NFS server. Must be an absolute path.
Specifies whether the NFS volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; when false, it is read-write.
Server is the hostname or IP address of the NFS server.
Represents a PersistentVolumeClaim volume source, which mounts a PersistentVolumeClaim into the pod. The referenced claim must exist in the same namespace.
claimName is the name of a PersistentVolumeClaim in the same namespace as the pod using this volume.
If true, the persistent volume claim is mounted as read-only. This forces the read-only setting in the corresponding volume mount. Defaults to false.
Configuration for a Photon Controller persistent disk volume. This volume type mounts a persistent disk created on a Photon Controller into the pod.
Filesystem type to mount for the Photon persistent disk volume, such as ext4. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system.
pd_id is the ID that identifies the Photon Controller persistent disk.
Defines a Portworx volume source for a pod. Specify the Portworx volume ID to mount, along with optional filesystem type and read-only flag.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Ex. 'ext4', 'xfs'. Implicitly inferred to be 'ext4' if unspecified.
Mounted read-only if true; otherwise read-write. When set, the Portworx volume is mounted as read-only in the container.
The ID of the Portworx volume to use. This is the unique identifier assigned to the volume in the Portworx cluster.

A projected volume source that combines multiple existing volume sources (e.g., config maps, secrets, downward API, service account tokens) into the same directory. It contains a sources list and an optional defaultMode for permissions.
Sets the default permissions mode (octal) for files in the projected volume. For example, 0644 gives read/write for owner and read-only for others. If not specified, Kubernetes defaults to 0644.
A list of sources to project into the volume. Each source can be a secret, config map, downward API, or service account token. Supported source types are defined in the Kubernetes API.

Configures a projected volume source that exposes a ClusterTrustBundle as a file. It allows specifying the trust bundle by name, signer name, or label selector, and includes an optional flag and output path.
Optional label selector that filters which ClusterTrustBundle objects are projected into the volume. When unset, all bundles matching the signer name are included.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and optional values. Allowed operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. The requirements are ANDed together to select the set of ClusterTrustBundles matched by the label selector.
The label key that the selector requirement applies to. This is the key used in the match expression for selecting cluster trust bundle resources based on their labels.
The operator that represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
The list of values used with the label selector's operator. For operators 'In' and 'NotIn', values must be non-empty; for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', values must be empty.
A map of key-value pairs used as label selectors to identify the ClusterTrustBundle resource to project. Only the ClusterTrustBundle whose labels match all specified key-value pairs will be selected.
The name of the ClusterTrustBundle resource to project into the volume. If set, this selects a specific ClusterTrustBundle by name.

Indicates whether the ClusterTrustBundle projection is optional. If set to true, the projection is omitted when the referenced ClusterTrustBundle does not exist; if false (default), the volume requires the resource to be present.
The relative path from the volume root to the file where the cluster trust bundle data is written. This path must not begin with '/' and must not contain '..' segments.
Name of the signer whose trust bundle is to be projected into the volume.
ConfigMap projection to include in the projected volume source. This allows exposing a ConfigMap's data as files in the volume, with optional item-level selection.

Optional list of key-to-path mappings to project from the ConfigMap. If specified, only these keys are projected onto the volume at their given relative paths; if omitted, all keys in the ConfigMap are projected.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap that selects the value to expose at the given path in the projected volume.
The permission mode (in octal) for the file created from the config map item. If not specified, the default is 0644.
The relative file path within the projected volume where the value of the corresponding config map key is written. This path is relative to the volume's root and must not contain '..' segments.
Name of the ConfigMap to reference as a projected volume source.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. If true, the ConfigMap and its keys may be absent, and the volume will still mount successfully. If false, the ConfigMap must exist and all referenced keys must be present.
downwardAPI represents a source of a projected volume that populates the volume with information about the pod, such as labels, annotations, and resource limits, using the Downward API.

The list of files to project into the volume. Each item maps a Kubernetes field or resource field (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace, limits.cpu) to a file path, with optional permissions and formatting settings.
field_ref specifies the Pod field to project into the volume. It contains the fieldPath (and optionally the apiVersion) to select the specific field value.
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath is written against, such as 'v1'. It determines how the fieldPath is interpreted.
The path to the field to select from the pod's metadata or status, e.g., 'metadata.name' or 'status.podIP'.
The file permission mode (e.g., 0644) for the projected file. Must be an integer between 0 and 0777. If not specified, the volume's default mode is used.
The relative path (within the projected volume) to the file where the downward API value is written. The path must not contain '..' segments.

resource_field_ref selects a container resource field, such as limits.cpu, limits.memory, requests.cpu, or requests.memory, to expose in the downward API projected volume. The corresponding resource value is written to the volume file. Supported fields include limits and requests for CPU, memory, and ephemeral-storage.
Name of the container to which the resource field applies. Required when the resource field references a container resource such as limits.cpu or requests.memory.
Divisor is the value by which the resource quantity is divided to produce the output value. If not specified, it defaults to 1.
The name of the container resource (e.g., `limits.cpu` or `requests.memory`) whose value is exposed via the downward API.
Specifies the file path inside the projected volume where the certificate key will be mounted. If not set, a default file name is used based on the certificate type.
The name of the certificate signer that will issue the pod's certificate. This corresponds to the `signerName` field in the Kubernetes API for projected pod certificates.
A map of user-defined annotations to apply to the pod certificate.
secret projects a Kubernetes Secret into the projected volume. It specifies the secret name and optional items (keys) and file permissions to include.

A list of key-to-path mappings that specifies which keys from the referenced Secret are projected and the file paths to which they are mounted. If omitted, all keys from the Secret are projected with their key names as paths.
The key within the secret's data map to project into the volume. This identifies which entry from the secret's data is used for this item.
The permission mode bits for the file, specified as an octal number between 0 and 0777. If omitted, the default mode (0644) or the volume's defaultMode applies.
The relative path within the projected volume where the secret key is mounted.
The numeric user ID (UID) that will own the file created from this secret item. When unset, the file's owner defaults to the pod's fsGroup (if set) or root (UID 0).
The name of the secret to project into the volume. The secret must exist in the pod's namespace.
Optional field specifies whether the referenced Secret or its keys must be defined. If true, the volume mounts successfully even if the Secret or some keys are missing.
A projected volume source that injects a service account token into the volume.
The audience (aud) claim for the projected service account token. This overrides the default audience of the API server and specifies the intended recipients that will validate the token.
The desired duration of validity for the service account token in seconds. It must be at least 600 (10 minutes). Defaults to 3600 (1 hour) if not specified.
The relative path within the projected volume where the service account token file is mounted.
Quobyte represents a Quobyte volume source, enabling the pod to mount a volume backed by a Quobyte storage system.
The group to map volume access to. Defaults to the group of the mapped user.
Forces the Quobyte volume to be mounted with read-only permissions. Defaults to false.
The Quobyte registry to connect to, specified as a single host:port or a comma-separated list of host:port pairs.
The Quobyte tenant name for the volume. If not specified, the volume is assumed to be in the default tenant.
User to map volume access to for the Quobyte volume. Defaults to the service account user.
The name of the Quobyte volume to mount. This field is required and specifies which volume in the Quobyte registry to attach to the pod.
Configuration for a Rados Block Device (RBD) volume to be mounted, used to attach a Ceph block device.
The filesystem type of the RBD volume, e.g., ext4, xfs, that will be used when mounting the volume.
The name of the RADOS image to mount as an RBD volume. This identifies the block device within the Ceph cluster.
Path to the keyring file for the Ceph user. Defaults to /etc/ceph/keyring.
Monitors is a list of Ceph monitor endpoints for the RBD volume, typically formatted as host:port.
The name of the Ceph pool where the RBD image is located.
Whether the RBD volume is mounted as read-only. If true, the volume cannot be written to.
Reference to a Kubernetes secret that contains the Ceph authentication key (keyring) for accessing the RBD image. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the Secret in the same namespace that contains the Ceph RBD authentication key.
RADOS user name used for authentication with the Ceph cluster. Defaults to 'admin'.
Defines a ScaleIO volume source, representing a persistent volume backed by a Dell EMC ScaleIO storage system. This object configures the connection and access parameters for the ScaleIO volume.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. Defaults to ext4.
The host address of the ScaleIO API Gateway.
The name of the ScaleIO Protection Domain for the configured storage. If not specified, the default protection domain is used.
If true, the volume is mounted as read-only.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the ScaleIO credentials (e.g., username and password). The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret that contains the ScaleIO credentials.
SSLEnabled specifies whether to enable SSL for communication with the ScaleIO REST API. Defaults to false.
Indicates whether the storage for the volume is 'ThickProvisioned' or 'ThinProvisioned'. Default is 'ThinProvisioned'.
The ScaleIO storage pool where the volume is provisioned. Defaults to 'default' if not specified.
The name of the ScaleIO storage system to use for the volume.
The name of a volume already created in the ScaleIO system. This volume is associated with the ScaleIO storage backend and is mounted into the pod.
Secret represents a secret that should populate this volume. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes#secret
Specifies the permission mode bits for files created in the secret volume. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 (or decimal 0-511); defaults to 0644.
A list of mappings from secret keys to file paths within the volume. Each item defines a key and the path to write its value; if omitted, all keys are mounted.
The key within the Secret to use as the source for this item. The corresponding Secret value is exposed at the given path.

Mode is a numeric value indicating the file permissions (in octal) for the secret item when mounted into the pod. For example, 0644 grants read/write to owner and read to group/others. If not set, the default mode from the secret volume is used.
The relative path of the file within the volume where the secret key is mounted. Must not contain '..' and must be relative (cannot start with '/').
Specifies whether the secret or its referenced keys must be defined. When true, the volume can be mounted even if the secret or some keys are missing.
Name of the Secret in the pod's namespace to use. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Configures a StorageOS volume source to mount a StorageOS volume into the pod. This block specifies the parameters for using a StorageOS volume as a pod volume.
Filesystem type to mount for the StorageOS volume. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host OS (e.g., 'ext4', 'xfs', 'ntfs'). Defaults to 'ext4' if unspecified.
Whether the StorageOS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
secret_ref is a reference to a Kubernetes secret that contains the StorageOS API credentials. It specifies the name of the secret in the same namespace to use for authentication with StorageOS.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret object that stores the StorageOS API key. This Secret is used to authenticate to the StorageOS volume provider.
The name of the StorageOS volume to attach and mount into the pod. This is required when using a StorageOS volume source.
Specifies the namespace of the StorageOS volume. If not set, the namespace of the pod is used.
Represents a vSphere volume source, which mounts a vSphere storage volume (e.g., a VMDK) into the pod.
Filesystem type to mount for the vSphere volume. Defaults to ext4 if not specified.
The vSphere Storage Policy Based Management (SPBM) policy ID to apply to the volume. If not specified, the default storage policy is used.
Name of the vSphere storage policy that governs the volume placement and characteristics. Optional; if not set, the default storage policy is used.
Path that identifies the vSphere volume, typically the vmdk path such as '[datastore1] vmdisk1'.

Specifies a list of node selector requirements that constrain eligible nodes by labels. Each requirement defines a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt), and optionally value(s) that must be matched.
The Kubernetes label key that the match expression applies to.
The operator to apply when matching the key against the listed values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.
A list of values for the node selector expression. Required when the operator is In or NotIn; must be empty for Exists or DoesNotExist.
A list of node selector requirements that match against node fields (e.g., metadata.name, spec.unschedulable) rather than node labels. Each requirement contains a key, operator, and optional values.
The key of the node field (e.g., metadata.name) that the match_fields requirement applies to.
Operator is the logical operator applied when matching the field. Valid values: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt.
A list of field values that must match the node's corresponding field value for the node to be selected. At least one value must match.
The weight (1-100) assigned to this preferred node affinity term, used to calculate the overall preference score for nodes that match the associated selector term.

A list of node selector requirements that must be satisfied for a pod to be eligible to run on a node. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values used with the operator.
The label key that the node must have in order to match the selector expression. This corresponds to a specific node label key that the expression is evaluated against.

The operator defines the relationship between the label key and the specified values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt, controlling how the node's labels are matched against the selector terms.

A list of string values for the match expression. For operators In and NotIn, this list is required and contains the values that must match the key. For operators Exists and DoesNotExist, this list must be empty.

A list of node selector requirements that match against node fields (e.g., metadata.name) rather than labels. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values, and is used to constrain pod scheduling to nodes.
The key of a node field used in a matchFields expression, such as 'metadata.name'. It identifies which node field to match against in the node selector term.

Defines the relationship between the field key and the specified values. Allowed operators include In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt. For example, In requires the field value to be one of the specified values, while Exists requires the field to be present.
A list of values that must be matched for the node selector requirement. For operators such as In or NotIn, these are the values the node's label or field must (or must not) have.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.affinity.pod_af.text: The pod affinity term defines the set of pods to which the preferred scheduling applies, including a label selector to identify the target pods and a topology key to specify the domain for co-location.
Label selector used to identify the set of pods that the affinity term applies to. It typically includes matchLabels and matchExpressions to select pods based on their labels.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a set of values, enabling more expressive label matching than exact matchLabels.
The label key that the selector expression applies to. This key must match a label on the target resource for the expression to match.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
The list of values for the label selector expression. Must be non-empty for the 'In' and 'NotIn' operators, and must be empty for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist' operators.
A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels of the target pod. Each key-value in the map is equivalent to an In operator matchExpression with the given key and value.

Specifies a list of label keys. The values for these keys are extracted from the pod being scheduled and used to select the set of existing pods that this affinity term applies to, enabling dynamic matching based on the incoming pod's labels.

A list of pod label keys used to filter candidate pods for the affinity rule. A pod is considered a match only if its value for any of these keys differs from the incoming pod's value for that key. The keys must not overlap with those in match_label_keys.
A label selector for namespaces. When specified, the pod affinity term applies only to pods running in namespaces that match this selector. If omitted, the affinity term applies to all namespaces.

A list of label selector requirements used to match namespaces. Each requirement defines a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values. The pod affinity term applies only to pods in namespaces that satisfy these expressions.
The label key that the selector applies to. Must be a valid label key, such as 'app' or 'example.com/key'.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a match expression. For Kubernetes label selectors, allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

A list of values that the label key must match, as dictated by the operator. For the In and NotIn operators, this contains the actual values to match against; for Exists and DoesNotExist, this list must be empty (or omitted).
match_labels is a map of label keys to values used to select namespaces. Only namespaces with all specified labels are matched for this pod affinity term.
A list of namespaces to which the label selector for this affinity term applies. If empty or unset, only the namespace of the pod is considered.

The key of node labels used to define topology domains (e.g., kubernetes.io/hostname) for evaluating pod affinity/anti-affinity. The scheduler uses these domains to group nodes and determine preferred scheduling behavior.
Weight associated with the pod affinity term, ranging from 1 to 100. Higher weights give the term higher precedence during scheduling.
A label selector used to identify the set of pods that the affinity term applies to. Supports matchLabels and matchExpressions to define the selection criteria.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. The selector matches pods whose labels satisfy all requirements.
The label key that the match expression evaluates. This is the key of a label on pods that the affinity selector matches against, used together with the operator and values fields.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a label selector requirement. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
The list of values that the label selector key must match, depending on the operator. For operators In and NotIn, this list must be non-empty; for Exists and DoesNotExist, it must be empty.
A map of label keys and values used to select pods that match all specified labels. This selector is used by pod affinity to identify the set of pods that the affinity rule applies to.

A list of label keys that the incoming pod must not have matching values for in the candidate pods. If the incoming pod has a label with a key in this list, candidate pods sharing the same label value are excluded from the affinity selection.
Label selector to filter namespaces to which the pod affinity term applies. Only namespaces matching this selector are considered when determining pod affinity.

A list of label selector requirements that define which namespaces are considered for the pod affinity match. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values according to Kubernetes label selector semantics.
The label key that the selector requirement applies to. Must be a valid Kubernetes label key.
The operator to use for the match expression. Allowed values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'. For 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', the values list must be empty.
List of values that the label selector matches for the given key. When the operator is `In` or `NotIn`, this list must be non-empty; when the operator is `Exists` or `DoesNotExist`, it must be empty.
A map of label keys and values that must match the labels of a namespace for it to be selected. The selector requires that all specified labels are present on the target namespace.
A list of namespace names that restricts the set of pods evaluated for this affinity term. If not set, the term applies only to pods in the pod's own namespace.

The node label key that defines the failure domain for pod affinity/anti-affinity. For example, 'kubernetes.io/hostname' or 'topology.kubernetes.io/zone'. Required for required_during_scheduling_ignored_during_execution.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.affinity.pod_an.text: Configures a pod affinity term, which defines the target pods (via a label selector) and the topology domain (topology key) for the anti-affinity rule. Optionally, a list of namespaces can scope the selector.
A label query over pods to select the group of pods to which the affinity term applies. Uses standard Kubernetes label matching semantics.
A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement defines a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optional values, used to match pods for this anti-affinity term.
The label key that this match expression applies to, used to select pods based on their labels in the pod anti-affinity term.

The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the set of values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist. For In/NotIn, the values field must be non-empty; for Exists/DoesNotExist, the values field must be empty.
A list of string values that the key must match when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'. For 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty.
A map of label keys and values that must match a resource's labels for the label selector to be satisfied. All specified labels must be present for the selector to match.
List of label keys used to filter candidate pods for the affinity/anti-affinity term. Only pods that have the same value for each of these keys as the current pod are considered for the rule.
Label query over the set of namespaces to which the pod affinity term applies. The term applies to the union of namespaces selected by this field and the namespaces listed in the namespaces field.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement defines a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values. The requirements are used to select namespaces based on their labels for this pod anti-affinity term.
The key of the label selector requirement. Identifies the label that the match expression applies to within the namespace selector.
The operator to use for the label selector requirement. Allowed values are `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, and `DoesNotExist`.
The list of values that the label selector's key must match. For the 'In' and 'NotIn' operators, this list must be non-empty; for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty.

match_labels is a map of key/value pairs that must match the labels on a namespace for it to be selected by this namespace selector. Each key-value pair in the map corresponds to an exact match requirement on the namespace's labels.
Specifies the list of namespaces to which the pod affinity/anti-affinity term applies. If not set, the term applies to the pod's own namespace.
topology_key is the key for node labels that the system uses to denote the topology domain. It defines the scope of the affinity/anti-affinity, such as kubernetes.io/hostname for node-level topology.
Weight associated with the pod anti-affinity term, ranging from 1 to 100. Higher weights give the term more influence during scheduling.

A label selector that identifies the group of pods that the pod must not be co-located with during scheduling. The selector supports matchLabels and matchExpressions to define the selection criteria, matching the standard Kubernetes LabelSelector object.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and a set of values. Operators include In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist; values are only used with In and NotIn.
The label key that the match expression applies to. This key is used to select pods based on the value of the specified label.
Operator represents the key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.
An array of string values. If the operator is In or NotIn, the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, the values array must be empty.
A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels of pods to be selected as targets for the anti-affinity rule. Only pods with all specified labels are considered.

A list of label keys that should not match the labels of existing pods in the same topology domain. Pods with labels matching any of these keys are excluded from the anti-affinity rule, allowing more fine-grained control over which pods are considered for scheduling.

A label selector over namespaces that restricts the scope of the pod anti-affinity rule. If specified, the rule only applies to pods in the selected namespaces; if omitted, all namespaces are considered.

A list of label selector requirements for selecting namespaces. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. The selector matches namespaces that satisfy all specified requirements.
The label key that the selector requirement matches against. It specifies which label on a namespace to evaluate for pod anti-affinity.
The operator applied to the key and values in the match expression. Valid values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'.

The values field in a namespace selector match expression is a list of strings that the expression matches against. It is required for the In and NotIn operators, and must be empty for Exists and DoesNotExist.
A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels on the namespaces. All specified labels must be present and have matching values for a namespace to be selected.
A list of namespaces to which this pod anti-affinity term applies. If empty, the namespace of the current pod is used.

The key of a node label that defines the topology domain for this anti-affinity rule. Pods are scheduled such that no two pods from the same topology domain are placed on the same node, based on the label value.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.args.text: Arguments to pass to the container's entrypoint command. These override the image's default arguments (CMD) when specified. Each string is passed as a separate argument to the command.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.comm.text: Entrypoint array. This is the container's command, equivalent to the Docker ENTRYPOINT. It overrides the image's default entrypoint and is not executed within a shell.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.env.text: List of environment variables to set in the container. Each item specifies a variable name and optionally its value or a value source (such as a config map, secret, or field reference).

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.env..text: The name of the environment variable.

The value of the environment variable. Provide a static string to set the environment variable to this value in the container. To dynamically source the value from a Kubernetes resource, use the separate valueFrom block instead.
Defines a source for the environment variable's value, such as a ConfigMap key, Secret key, or field reference. This field is mutually exclusive with 'value'.

Selects a key from a ConfigMap in the pod's namespace to populate the environment variable's value. This object includes the ConfigMap's name, the key to select, and an optional flag to specify if the ConfigMap must exist.
The key within the ConfigMap's data to select the value from for this environment variable.
Name of the ConfigMap to reference. Must match an existing ConfigMap in the pod's namespace or the pod will fail to start if the field is required.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap key is optional. If false (default), the key must exist and the pod will fail to start if it is missing. If true, the key may be absent, and the environment variable will be omitted.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName) to use as the value of the environment variable.
API version of the referent. Defaults to v1 if not specified.
The path to the pod field to select, such as 'metadata.name' or 'status.podIP'. In a FieldRef, this specifies which field of the pod to reference for the environment variable value.

A boolean flag that indicates whether the referenced key is optional. If set to true, the pod will start even if the key does not exist; if false (default), the key must exist for the container to start.
Selects a resource field (e.g., requests.cpu or limits.memory) of the running container and exposes it as an environment variable value.
The name of the container whose resource value is referenced. If empty, defaults to the container where this environment variable is defined.

Specifies the divisor to divide the resource value by before assigning it to the environment variable. This allows adjusting the value's unit (for example, using '1m' to get millicores). The value is a Kubernetes quantity, such as '1k' or '1Gi', and defaults to '1' if not set.
The name of the resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'. This refers to a container's resource request or limit value to be exposed as an environment variable.
Selects a key from a Secret in the pod's namespace. Typically contains 'name' (the Secret name) and 'key' (the key to retrieve) to expose the secret value as an environment variable.
The key within the referenced Secret to select. This key must exist in the Secret's data.
Name of the Secret in the same namespace from which to fetch the key. This field is required when using a secret key reference.
Specify whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If true, the pod will start even if the referenced secret key is missing.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.env_.text: List of sources to populate environment variables in the container. Each source can reference a Kubernetes ConfigMap or Secret, allowing environment variables to be set from those objects, with optional prefix support.
Reference to a ConfigMap whose key-value pairs are used to populate environment variables in the container.
The name of the ConfigMap to source environment variables from. This ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must exist. When set to true, a missing ConfigMap is allowed and the environment variables are not set; when false or unset, the ConfigMap must exist before the pod can start.
An optional identifier that is prepended to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. Must be a valid C identifier.
SecretRef is a reference to a Secret to use for populating environment variables. It contains the name of the Secret and an optional flag indicating whether the Secret must be defined.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret to reference for injecting environment variables.
Specifies whether the Secret referenced by this envFrom source must be defined. When set to true, a missing Secret does not cause an error.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.imag.text: The container image to run, including the registry, repository, and tag or digest (e.g., nginx:latest).

Specifies the pull policy for the container image, controlling when the kubelet should pull the image. Allowed values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never; if unset, the default depends on the image tag (Always for latest or omitted, IfNotPresent otherwise).

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.life.text: Specifies lifecycle hooks for the container. Hooks are executed by the container runtime at specific events: postStart (immediately after the container is started) and preStop (immediately before the container is terminated). Each hook can define an exec command or an HTTP request.
postStart represents a lifecycle hook that is executed immediately after a container is created. It contains either an exec action or an HTTP GET request to be performed.
Specifies a command to execute inside the container as the postStart lifecycle handler.
The command to run in the container as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. It is a list of strings where the first element is the command path and the remaining elements are arguments passed to it.
An HTTP GET request to perform when the container is started, as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. This is a Kubernetes HTTPGetAction object.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.

A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields, allowing you to set specific headers such as Authorization or Content-Type for the lifecycle HTTP GET action.
The name of an HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request for the post-start lifecycle hook.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP GET request for the post-start lifecycle hook.
The HTTP path to request when executing the HTTP GET on the container's postStart lifecycle hook. For example, '/health'.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.

Defines a sleep action for the postStart lifecycle hook, which pauses container startup for a specified number of seconds. The object contains a 'seconds' field (integer) that determines the delay duration.
The number of seconds the container should sleep when the postStart lifecycle hook is triggered. It specifies the duration of the sleep action.

A TCP socket handler that the kubelet attempts to open on the container's port to determine when the postStart lifecycle hook has succeeded. The hook is considered complete when the TCP connection to the specified port succeeds.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If omitted, the pod's IP address is used.
The port number or name of the port to connect to for the TCP socket lifecycle hook. This can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container spec.
Defines a handler that Kubernetes executes immediately before a container is stopped, allowing for graceful shutdown (e.g., sending a signal or running a cleanup script).
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It is an ExecAction that defines the command to execute.

The command to run in the container during the preStop lifecycle hook. It is specified as an array of strings and is executed directly without a shell, so shell features like pipes or variables are not available.

Specifies an HTTP GET request to be executed when the container is about to be terminated as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This request is sent to the given host and port with optional path and headers, and responses are ignored.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If omitted, it defaults to the pod IP address.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each header is defined by a name and value pair.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request (for example, 'X-Custom-Header').
The value of the HTTP header entry used in the preStop hook's HTTP GET request.
The path to access on the HTTP server when performing the pre-stop lifecycle HTTP GET request.
Port number or name of the port to access on the container. Valid values are numeric (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports block.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) used for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to HTTP.
The URL scheme (protocol) to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The sleep action for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It configures a delay (in seconds) to allow the container to terminate gracefully before it is stopped.
Specifies the number of seconds the sleep action should last. For a preStop lifecycle hook, this is the duration the container pauses before termination.
Specifies a TCP socket action for the pre-stop lifecycle hook, which opens a connection to a specified port on the container to signal graceful termination.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP address.
The TCP port to send the pre-stop request to. This can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container. Required.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.live.text: Configuration for the liveness probe of the container. It defines the method and parameters used by Kubernetes to determine if the container is alive, restarting it if the probe fails.
The exec action runs a specified command inside the container. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with a status code of 0.

The command to execute inside the container as part of the exec-based liveness probe. It is a list of strings where the first item is the command and the remaining items are arguments to that command.
The number of consecutive failures before the container is restarted.
The gRPC probe configuration. When set, the kubelet performs a gRPC health check on the specified port to determine container liveness.
The port number of the gRPC service that the probe will check. Must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the gRPC service to check in the health probe. If omitted, the gRPC health check is performed against the whole service, as defined by the gRPC Health Checking Protocol.
Specifies the HTTP GET request parameters used for the liveness probe to check container health. This object configures the path, port, headers, and other HTTP request details.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the request. Each item contains a header name and value, allowing addition of headers such as Host or authentication tokens.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the liveness probe's HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header used in the liveness probe's HTTP GET request.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server when performing the health check. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port number or name to access on the container. Accepts a numeric port between 1 and 65535, or an IANA_SVC_NAME for a named port.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the liveness probe is initiated. The probe will wait this long before running its first check.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after a failure. Must be 1 for a liveness probe.

Specifies the TCP socket action for the liveness probe, including the port (and optionally the host) that the kubelet will attempt to connect to. If the connection succeeds, the probe is considered successful.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to for the liveness probe. Accepts a numeric port number or a named port defined in the container.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.name.text: Name of the container. Must be a valid DNS_LABEL and unique within the pod.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.port.text: A list of network ports exposed by the container. Each entry specifies a container port (and optionally a host port, IP, protocol, and name) as defined by the Kubernetes container spec.
The port number that the container exposes on the pod's network. Valid port numbers range from 1 to 65535.
The host IP address to bind the host port to. Defaults to 0.0.0.0 if not specified.

The host port number to which the container port is mapped, allowing external access to the container. If omitted, the port is only accessible from within the cluster. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) when specified.
The name of the port. If specified, this must be an IANA_SVC_NAME and unique within the pod. Each named port in a pod must have a unique name. This name can be referenced by services.
The protocol for the container port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP. Defaults to TCP if not specified.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.read.text: Configuration for the readiness probe, which checks whether the container is ready to serve traffic. The container is considered ready when the probe succeeds, and only then will it receive traffic from services.
Exec specifies an exec action to perform within the container as part of the readiness probe. It runs a command and uses its exit status to determine container readiness.

The command to run inside the container, as a list of strings where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. It is executed directly (not via a shell) in the container's root filesystem; for probes, an exit status of 0 indicates success.
The number of consecutive failures required for the readiness probe to be considered failed, after which the container is marked as not ready. Defaults to 3.
Defines the gRPC action for the readiness probe, including the port to check and optionally the service name.
The port number of the gRPC service to check. This is required for gRPC probes and must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the gRPC service to query in the health check. If not specified, the default health check service is used.

Defines the parameters for an HTTP GET request used as a readiness probe. The kubelet sends an HTTP GET to the specified path and port on the container's IP address to determine if the container is ready.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Optional list of custom HTTP headers to send with the probe request. Each item is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent in the readiness probe request.
Path to access on the HTTP server.
The port to access on the container. Accepts a port number (as a string) or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are "HTTP" and "HTTPS". Defaults to "HTTP".
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0; minimum value is 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1.

The minimum number of consecutive successful probes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. Must be 1 for liveness and startup probes. Defaults to 1, with a minimum value of 1.

Specifies a TCP socket probe for the container readiness probe. The probe checks whether a TCP connection to the given port can be established, and the container is considered ready if the connection succeeds.
The host name or IP to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The port to check for the TCP readiness probe. This can be a numeric port (as a string) or a named port defined in the container's ports list.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.resi.text: A list of policies defining how the container's resources (e.g., CPU, memory) are resized when the pod's resource requests or limits change. Each policy specifies a resource name and a restart policy.
The name of the resource (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies.
Specifies whether a container must be restarted for a resource resize to take effect. Valid values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer'.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.reso.text: Defines the compute resources (CPU, memory, and ephemeral storage) for the container, specifying resource requests and limits.
A list of resource claims that the container requires. Each claim references a ResourceClaim by name to request specific resources.
Name must match the name of a ResourceClaim in the same namespace.
The maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the container. Keys are resource names like 'cpu' and 'memory', and values are quantities such as '500m' for CPU cores or '128Mi' for memory.

Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. If requests are omitted for a container, it defaults to limits if those are explicitly specified, or to an implementation-defined value. The map keys are resource names like cpu and memory, and values are quantities like '100m' or '1Gi'.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.rest.text: Specifies the restart policy for the pod's containers. Allowed values are Always, OnFailure, and Never. In standard Kubernetes, this is a pod-level field, not a container-level field.

The logical operator used to compare the container exit code against the list of exit_codes in the restart policy rule. It defines the condition for matching, such as whether the exit code must be in the list.
A list of container exit codes that match this rule. If the container exits with any of these codes, the restart policy rule is applied.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.secu.text: Security settings for the container, such as user IDs, capabilities, SELinux options, read-only root filesystem, and privilege escalation control.

Controls whether a process in the container can gain more privileges than its parent process. When false, the container runs with the no_new_privs flag set, preventing privilege escalation via setuid or other mechanisms.

Object that specifies the AppArmor profile to apply to the container. It includes the profile type (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and may include a localhost profile name when type is Localhost.
The name of a pre-loaded AppArmor profile on the node, used when the AppArmor profile type is set to Localhost.

The type of AppArmor profile to apply to the container. Valid values are "Localhost" (use a profile specified in localhostProfile), "RuntimeDefault" (use the container runtime's default profile), or "Unconfined" (disable AppArmor).
Defines the Linux capabilities to add to or drop from the container. This field contains 'add' and 'drop' lists to grant or remove specific capabilities from the container's default set.
Adds the specified Linux capabilities to the container's permitted set.

A list of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's security context. Each entry is a capability name (e.g., 'ALL', 'NET_ADMIN'), and the container will have those capabilities removed from its allowed set.
Run the container in privileged mode, granting all capabilities and access to host devices.
Sets the proc mount mode for the container. Allowed values are 'Default' (use container runtime's default proc mounts) and 'Unmasked' (unmask the proc mount for visibility).
When set to true, the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only, preventing writes to the root filesystem. This is a common security hardening practice.
The GID (group ID) to run the container's entrypoint process with. If omitted, the runtime default group is used.

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the Kubernetes kubelet will validate the container image at runtime to ensure it does not run as UID 0, and will refuse to start the container if it does.
The user ID (UID) that the container's main process runs as. If not set, the container runs as the user specified in the container image, defaulting to root (UID 0) if the image does not specify one.
Specifies the SELinux context for the container, including the user, role, type, and level to be applied.
The SELinux level (e.g., 's0', 's0:c1') for the SELinux label, forming part of the se_linux_options configuration.
The SELinux role label that applies to the container.
The SELinux type label applied to the container's security context, such as 'svirt_sandbox_file_t'.
SELinux user label assigned to the container.
Defines the seccomp profile applied to the container. Contains settings for the seccomp profile type (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined) and, for Localhost, the path to the profile file.

Path to a seccomp profile on the node's local filesystem. Must be a descending path relative to the kubelet's configured seccomp profile location, and should only be set when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to apply to the container. Valid values are RuntimeDefault, Localhost, and Unconfined.
Windows-specific security context options for the container, including GMSA credentials and host process settings.

The GMSA credential spec content for the container's Windows security context. This is the raw JSON string of the credential spec, typically injected by the GMSA admission webhook, either from a referenced credential spec name or provided directly.
Specifies the name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container. This credential spec defines the Group Managed Service Account to be used by the container for authentication.
Indicates whether the container should be run as a 'Host Process' container. All containers in the pod must have the same effective value, and this cannot be set with hostNetwork or runAsUserName.

The Windows user name to run the container's entrypoint process as. Defaults to the user specified in the image metadata if not set; if set in both this security context and the pod security context, the value here takes precedence.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.star.text: The startup probe checks whether the application in the container has started successfully. It is useful for containers with slow startup times; after the startup probe succeeds, the liveness and readiness probes take over. This field is an object representing the probe configuration, such as HTTP GET, TCP socket, or command.
Specifies the command to execute inside the container as part of the startup probe. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0; any non-zero exit indicates a failure.
The command to run inside the container to perform the startup probe. It is specified as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.
The number of consecutive failures of the startup probe that are allowed before the container is considered failed and is restarted. Must be set to a positive integer.
Specifies the gRPC health check parameters for the startup probe. This block defines the port to connect to and, optionally, the service name to query.
The port number that the gRPC server is listening on. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, defaults to the empty string, which checks the server's overall health status.

Performs an HTTP GET request on the container for the startup probe. This action checks container health by requiring an HTTP response with a status code between 200 and 399 from the specified port, path, and optional host, headers, and scheme.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not set, the pod IP is used. This is the host for the TCP connection, not the Host header; use http_headers to set the Host header instead.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request for the startup probe. Each header is defined by a name and a value, and repeated headers are allowed.
The name of the HTTP header to be sent in the startup probe request. For example, 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the GET request sent by the startup probe.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. If not set, defaults to '/'.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535. Name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME.
Specifies the protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Scheme to use for connecting to the host in the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container starts before the startup probe is initiated. Must be a non-negative integer.
Number of seconds between each startup probe attempt.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1 and must be 1 for startup probes (identical to liveness probe semantics).
Defines a TCP socket probe action, used by the startup probe to check if a TCP connection can be established to the container's IP address on a specified port.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port to connect to for the probe. Can be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port in the container.

Specifies the duration in seconds that Kubernetes waits for a pod to terminate gracefully after sending a termination signal. Note: this field is not a part of a startup probe; it is a pod-level setting.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Must be greater than 0.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.stdi.text: Whether to allocate a stdin for the container. Defaults to false.
If true, the container's stdin is closed after the first attach session, so subsequent attach sessions will not receive stdin. Defaults to false.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.term.text: The path inside the container where the termination message is written. This message is captured by kubelet and can be used to report the reason for container termination. Defaults to `/dev/termination-log`.

Indicates how the container's termination message is read. Allowed values are 'File' (read from /dev/termination-log) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError' (read from a file if container exits with error, otherwise use container logs). Defaults to 'File'.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.tty.text: Indicates whether a pseudo-TTY is allocated for the container, enabling interactive shell sessions.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.volu.text: A list of block device mappings for the container. Each item specifies the name of a volume that references a block device and the devicePath where the device appears inside the container.
Path inside the container where the raw block volume device is mounted (e.g., /dev/sdb).
The name of the volume that this device refers to. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
A list of volume mounts for the container. Each item defines a volume to mount and the mount path inside the container, along with options like read-only and sub-path.
The path within the container at which the volume should be mounted.

Controls how mount propagation is handled for this volume mount. Valid values are 'None', 'HostToContainer', and 'Bidirectional'. This determines whether mounts from the host are visible in the container and vice versa.
The name of the volume to mount, which must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
Indicates whether the volume mount is mounted as read-only. If set to true, the container can only read from the mounted volume.

Indicates whether the volume mount uses recursive read-only semantics. Allowed values are 'Enabled' or 'Disabled'; if unset, the default behavior for the volume type applies. Only supported for volumes that support recursive read-only mounts and only when read_only is true.
Path within the volume to mount instead of the volume's root. Used to mount a subdirectory or file from the volume into the container's mount path.

sub_path_expr is an alternative to sub_path that supports environment variable expansion. It specifies a subpath within the volume to mount, with references like $(VAR_NAME) expanded using container environment variables.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.containers.work.text: The container's working directory. If not specified, the default is the root directory (/).

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.dns_config.opti.text: The name of the DNS resolver option, such as 'ndots' or 'timeout'.
The value for a DNS resolver option, as a string. If omitted, the option is treated as a flag. For example, for the 'ndots' option, set value to '2'.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.ephemeral_conta.text: Arguments to the entrypoint. The container image's CMD is used if this is not provided.

The command to run in the ephemeral container, as an entrypoint array. It overrides the image's default ENTRYPOINT. The command is not executed within a shell, and variable references like $(VAR_NAME) are expanded using the container's environment.
List of environment variables for the ephemeral container. Each entry defines a variable name and optionally a value or a valueFrom source (e.g., config map, secret, or field reference).
The name of the environment variable, used to reference it within the container. Must be a valid Kubernetes environment variable name, typically a C identifier (e.g., MY_VAR).
The value of the environment variable. This is the string value assigned to the environment variable named in the 'name' field of the same env entry.
Defines a source for the environment variable's value, such as a reference to a ConfigMap, Secret, or pod field. It is mutually exclusive with the 'value' field.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to use as the value of the environment variable.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap to select the value from for this environment variable.
The name of the ConfigMap to select the key from.
Specify whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If false, the referenced key must exist; if true, the pod will still start even if the key is absent.

Represents a reference to a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName) whose value is used as the environment variable's value. It contains apiVersion and fieldPath attributes.
The API version of the schema that fieldPath is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1'.
The path to the pod field whose value should be used for the environment variable. For example, metadata.name or spec.nodeName.
The key name to retrieve from the referenced file, providing the environment variable's value.
Specifies whether the referenced key is optional. If true, the key does not need to exist; if false, its absence causes an error.
The name of the volume from which the file is read for the environment variable.
Represents a reference to a resource field of the container, such as CPU or memory limits/requests, allowing the environment variable to be set to that resource value.

The name of the container from which to select the resource field. When referring to container-specific resource fields (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory), this is required; if omitted, defaults to the container where the field reference is defined.
The divisor to apply when reading the selected resource quantity, expressed as a Kubernetes quantity. The resource value is divided by this amount; defaults to 1 if not specified.
The name of the container resource to select, such as 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory'.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace to provide the value for the environment variable. The referenced Secret must exist before the pod is created.
The key within the Secret to select the value from.
The name of the Secret from which to select the key.
Specifies whether the secret key must be defined. When set to true, the key is optional and its absence will not cause the container to fail.
A list of sources to populate environment variables in the ephemeral container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret, optionally with a prefix to apply to variable names.
