config_map_ref is a reference to a ConfigMap in the same namespace that provides environment variables to the container. When specified, the keys from the ConfigMap become environment variable names and their values become the environment variable values.
The name of the ConfigMap to use as a source of environment variables for the ephemeral container.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must exist. If true, the ConfigMap may be absent and the pod will still start; if false (default), a missing ConfigMap causes an error. Defaults to false.
Optional string that, if specified, is prepended to each key name of the referenced ConfigMap or Secret when generating environment variables for the ephemeral container.
Specifies a reference to a Secret in the same namespace as the Pod. The Secret's data is used to populate environment variables when this object appears in an envFrom list.
Name of the Secret to use for populating environment variables from the referenced secret.
Specifies whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If true, the Secret may be absent; if false or omitted, the Secret must exist.
The container image to use for the ephemeral container (e.g., nginx:latest).

Specifies when the kubelet should pull the image for this ephemeral container. Allowed values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never. Defaults to Always if the image tag is 'latest' or if the image name is not specified, otherwise IfNotPresent.
Lifecycle configuration for the ephemeral container, defining hooks such as postStart and preStop that execute commands or HTTP/TCP requests at specific container lifecycle events.

The postStart lifecycle hook is executed immediately after the container is started. It can contain exec or httpGet actions to run commands or make HTTP requests before the container is marked as ready.
Exec specifies the action to run when the postStart lifecycle hook is triggered for the ephemeral container. It contains the command to execute inside the container.

Performs an HTTP GET request against a specified endpoint when the postStart lifecycle hook is triggered. This action is configured with host, port, path, and headers to run a custom request after the container starts.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set 'Host' in http_headers instead.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each item should contain a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP GET request.
The header field value sent in the HTTP request.
The HTTP request path to access on the HTTP server. For example, /healthz.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. The port must be a valid port number (1-65535) or the name of a port defined in the container.
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Must be either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified.
The scheme (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to HTTP.
Sleep defines a lifecycle hook action that pauses for a specified number of seconds before the hook completes. The object contains a required 'seconds' field.
The number of seconds to sleep. This value specifies the duration for the sleep lifecycle hook action.
Specifies a TCP socket action for the postStart lifecycle hook. Kubernetes opens a TCP connection to the container's address and the specified port to trigger the lifecycle callback.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
The TCP port to connect to for the postStart lifecycle hook. Accepts a numeric port or a named port defined in the container.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that is called immediately before a container is terminated. This object defines the action to take, such as an exec command, an HTTP GET request, or a TCP socket check, allowing the container to gracefully shut down before being stopped.
Exec specifies the action to run a command inside the container as part of the preStop lifecycle hook. It is represented by an ExecAction object containing a command array.
Command to execute inside the ephemeral container when the preStop lifecycle hook is triggered. It is an array of strings, where the first element is the executable and the rest are arguments.

Defines an HTTP GET request that the kubelet sends to the container's IP address to trigger the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This configuration is part of the lifecycle preStop handler for an ephemeral container.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set 'Host' in httpHeaders instead.
Specifies custom HTTP headers to send with the HTTP GET request. Each item in the list defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the pre-stop hook GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535. Name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME.
The protocol used for the HTTP GET request: either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Sleep represents the sleep action for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It specifies how long the container should sleep before termination.
Specifies the duration in seconds to sleep before the container is terminated. This is used in the lifecycle pre-stop hook to delay termination.
Specifies a TCP socket action to be performed during the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified host and port, signaling the container to begin shutdown.
Host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
The TCP port number (as a string) or named port to connect to when performing the TCP socket check. For example, '8080' or a port name defined in the container.

Liveness probe configuration for the ephemeral container, used to determine if the container is healthy and running. If the probe fails, the container is considered unhealthy, though ephemeral containers are not automatically restarted.
Exec specifies the command to execute inside the container. The command runs directly within the container; a non-zero exit code indicates failure for the probe.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, with the working directory set to '/' in the container's filesystem. Since the command is not run inside a shell, traditional shell instructions such as '|' won't work; invoke a shell explicitly if needed.
The number of consecutive failures allowed before the liveness probe is considered failed and the container is restarted. Minimum value is 1, default is 3.
Specifies the gRPC health check configuration for the liveness probe. This includes the service name and port to use for the gRPC probe.
The port number on which the gRPC service is listening. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
Name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health checking protocol.
Configure the HTTP GET request used by the liveness probe, including the path, port, and custom HTTP headers.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. You may want to set the Host header in httpHeaders instead.
Custom HTTP headers to send in the HTTP GET request. Each item in the list is an object containing a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request.
The value of the HTTP header as a string. This is used in the headers of the HTTP GET request sent by the liveness probe.
Path to access on the HTTP server.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the liveness probe is initiated. This corresponds to the Kubernetes probe field initialDelaySeconds.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For liveness probes, this value must be 1 and defaults to 1.
Configuration for a TCP socket probe, used to check container liveness by attempting to establish a TCP connection. It specifies the port to probe and optionally the host.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to. Accepts a numeric port number as a string, or a named port defined on the container.
Duration in seconds the pod needs to terminate gracefully. Must be a non-negative integer. A value of 0 indicates delete immediately. This is a pod-level setting, not a probe parameter.
Timeout in seconds after which the liveness probe is considered failed. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 1 if not specified.
List of ports to expose from the ephemeral container. Each entry can specify a container port, protocol, and optional host port and name.
The port number the container listens on.
The host IP address to bind the external port to. If not specified, the port is bound to all interfaces.

The port on the host node to which the container port is mapped. If specified, this must be a valid port number between 1 and 65535; if omitted, the container port is not accessible externally via a host port.
The name of this port within the container. Optional, but if specified must be a valid DNS label and unique among all ports in the container.
The network protocol used by the container port, such as TCP, UDP, or SCTP.
Specifies the readiness probe for the ephemeral container, which indicates when the container is ready to serve requests. The probe can be defined with an HTTP GET, TCP socket, or an exec command.

Exec specifies the action to take, which is to run a command inside the container. The command is a list of strings, where the first element is the executable and the rest are arguments. This is used by the readiness probe to check container health.
The command to execute in the container as part of the exec readiness probe. It is a list of command arguments. A zero exit status indicates success; non-zero indicates failure.
The number of consecutive failures required for the readiness probe to be considered failed. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.
Defines a gRPC-based health check for the ephemeral container's readiness probe. Includes the port to connect to and an optional service name.
The port number on which the gRPC health check is performed. This field is required and must be a valid TCP port number (1-65535).
Specifies the name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If omitted, the gRPC health check is performed against the overall container status.
Configures an HTTP GET request that the kubelet executes against the container to determine readiness.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
A list of custom HTTP headers to send with the HTTP GET request. Each header is an object containing 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request. For example, "Authorization" or "Content-Type".
The value of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The HTTP path to request in the HTTP GET probe, such as '/healthz', specifying the endpoint to check on the server.
Port number or name of the port on the container to access for the HTTP GET readiness probe. Accepts a numeric port (e.g., '8080') or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The network protocol to use for the HTTP probe, either "HTTP" or "HTTPS". Defaults to "HTTP".
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0.
The frequency, in seconds, at which the readiness probe is executed. Must be greater than 0; defaults to 10 if unspecified.

The minimum number of consecutive successful probe results required for the readiness probe to be considered successful after it has failed. Defaults to 1; for readiness probes this value may be greater than 1.
TCPSocket specifies an action involving a TCP port. This block configures a TCP socket check for the readiness probe.
The hostname to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The port number or name of the TCP socket to connect to for the readiness probe. This can be a numeric port (e.g., "8080") or a named port defined in the container.
Timeout in seconds after which the readiness probe is considered failed. Defaults to 1 second; minimum value is 1.

Specifies the resource resize policy for the ephemeral container. Each entry defines a resourceName (e.g., cpu or memory) and a restartPolicy (NotRequired or RestartContainer) that controls how resizing that resource affects the container.
The name of the resource (for example, cpu or memory) to which the resize policy applies.
Specifies the restart policy for the container when its resources are resized. Allowed values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer'.

The resource requirements for the ephemeral container, specifying the minimum and maximum amounts of compute resources (e.g., CPU, memory) the container can use, typically defined via `requests` and `limits`.
List of resource claim references used by the container. Each object contains a name that refers to a ResourceClaim defined in the pod's spec.resourceClaims field.
Name of the resource claim (e.g., a ResourceClaim object) that this container's resource requirements reference. The claim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of a specific request within the referenced ResourceClaim to use. If omitted, all resources from the claim are made available.

Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the ephemeral container. Keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) and values are quantities (e.g., '100m', '1Gi'). More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is explicitly specified, or to an implementation-defined value. The map keys are resource names (such as 'cpu' and 'memory') and values are quantities.
The restart policy for the ephemeral container, controlling whether it is restarted after it exits.
The comparison operator used to determine if an exit code matches the specified values.
A list of numeric container exit codes. If the ephemeral container terminates with one of these codes, the associated restart policy rule is applied.

SecurityContext holds security configuration that will be applied to the ephemeral container, such as user and group IDs, Linux capabilities, SELinux options, and seccomp profiles. It allows specifying security settings distinct from the pod-level security context.

AllowPrivilegeEscalation controls whether the ephemeral container's process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When false, it prevents privilege escalation via mechanisms like setuid binaries or file capabilities; when true or omitted, privilege escalation is permitted.

The AppArmor profile settings for the container. This object specifies the type of AppArmor profile to apply (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Localhost, Unconfined), and when type is Localhost, the localhostProfile field provides the name of a profile preloaded on the node.
The name of the AppArmor profile to use when the AppArmorProfile type is set to 'Localhost'. This profile must already be loaded on the node.
Type of AppArmor profile to apply. Valid values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', and 'Unconfined'. If set to 'Localhost', the 'localhost_profile' field must also be specified.
Defines the Linux capabilities to add to or drop from the container's default set. The object contains 'add' and 'drop' lists of capability names.
List of Linux capabilities to add to the container's capability set. Each entry is a capability name such as 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME' that grants additional privileges beyond the default set.
A list of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's default capability set for the ephemeral container.
Indicates whether the ephemeral container runs in privileged mode, granting it access to all devices on the host and bypassing many security restrictions.
Specifies the proc mount behavior for the ephemeral container, controlling how the /proc filesystem is exposed to the container.
Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only, preventing writes to the root filesystem.
Specifies the group ID (GID) to run the container's entrypoint process as. If set, it overrides the image's default group and any pod-level security context. Must be a valid integer GID.
If true, the container must run as a non-root user (UID not 0). The kubelet will validate the image at runtime and fail to start the container if it is configured to run as root.
Specifies the user ID (UID) that the ephemeral container process will run as. This overrides the runAsUser setting from the pod or container security context.
Configures the SELinux context for the ephemeral container, specifying the user, role, type, and level options.
The SELinux level (e.g., s0, s1:c123) applied to the container. This defines the sensitivity level and optional categories for the SELinux policy.
The SELinux role label for the container process.
Type is a SELinux type label that applies to the container.
The SELinux user label for the container's security context. This is part of the SELinux context definition, specifying the user identity used for mandatory access control.

The seccomp profile configuration for the ephemeral container. This object specifies the seccomp profile type (e.g., Unconfined, RuntimeDefault, Localhost) and optionally the path to a localhost profile.
The path to a seccomp profile on the node's local filesystem, used when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'.
Type of seccomp profile to be applied to the container. Allowed values are: Localhost, RuntimeDefault, Unconfined.
Windows-specific security context options for the ephemeral container, such as GMSA credential specs and run-as-user settings.
GMSACredentialSpec is where the GMSA admission webhook (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/windows-gmsa) inlines the contents of the GMSA credential spec named by the GMSACredentialSpecName field.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container. This is used to configure Group Managed Service Accounts (GMSA) for Windows pods.
HostProcess determines whether the container runs as a HostProcess container on Windows nodes. This field is honored only when the WindowsHostProcessContainers feature gate is enabled.

The Windows user name to run the container process as. If unspecified, defaults to the user specified in the image metadata. May also be set in the pod's security context, but this value takes precedence if set.

Exec specifies the action to take within the container, typically running a command to determine if the container is healthy. The command is provided as a list of strings in the 'command' field of this object.
The command to execute in the container for the startup probe. It is provided as a list of strings, and the probe succeeds if the command exits with a status code of 0.
The minimum consecutive number of failures of the startup probe that will cause the container to be terminated and restarted. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.
Specifies a gRPC-based health check for the startup probe. The object defines the port to check and optionally the service name.
The port number on which the gRPC health check will be performed.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the gRPC default behavior is used.
Specifies the HTTP GET request used by the startup probe to check container health. This action makes an HTTP GET request to the container's IP address on a given port and path.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; setting this is generally discouraged in favor of using the 'Host' header in httpHeaders.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP request. Each header is defined by a name and value, allowing you to set headers such as Authorization or Content-Type for the probe request.
The HTTP header name to be sent in the request.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the startup probe request.
The URL path to request when performing the HTTP GET probe. For example, /healthz.
Name or number of the port to access on the container. Number must be in the range 1 to 65535. Name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME.
Protocol for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'.
Number of seconds after the container starts before the startup probe is initiated. Minimum value is 0.
The frequency in seconds at which the startup probe is performed. It determines how often the kubelet checks the container's health during the startup period.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after a failure. For startup probes, this value must be 1.

Specifies a TCP socket probe action for the startup probe. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's IP address on the specified port; a successful connection indicates the container is ready.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port to probe. Can be a port number (e.g., "8080") or a named port defined in the container.

The time in seconds that Kubernetes waits after a startup probe failure before forcefully terminating the container. This value overrides the pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds for this container's probe.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.
Whether this ephemeral container should have stdin open. When true, the container's standard input is connected, allowing interactive processes to read from it.
When set to true and stdin is also true, the ephemeral container's standard input is closed after the first attach, so subsequent attaches cannot write to stdin.

The name of the container within the pod that this ephemeral container targets. When specified, the ephemeral container shares the process namespace of that target container; otherwise it shares the pod's process namespace if one is defined.
The path where the container's termination message is written. This message is used for debugging and can be retrieved after termination.
Specifies how the termination message is read. Valid values are 'File' (default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'.
Whether to allocate a pseudo-TTY (teletype) for the container, enabling interactive terminal sessions. Defaults to false.
List of block device mappings for the ephemeral container. Each item specifies the volume name and the device path inside the container.
The path inside the container where the block device is mounted. This field is required for each volume device.
The name of the volume in the pod that this device references.

List of volume mounts for the ephemeral container, specifying how volumes are mounted into the container's filesystem. Each item defines a volume name and mount path, with optional mount options like read-only and subPath.
A list of strings that specify options for a bind mount, such as 'ro', 'noexec', or 'nosuid'. These options are passed to the mount operation when the volume is mounted in an ephemeral container.
Path within the ephemeral container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path.
Defines how mounts are propagated from the host to the container and between containers. Valid values are None, HostToContainer, and Bidirectional.
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
Indicates whether the volume mount is mounted as read-only. If set to true, the volume is read-only; otherwise it is read-write. Defaults to false.
RecursiveReadOnly specifies whether read-only mounts should be handled recursively. This field is only supported on Linux. Allowed values are 'Enabled', 'IfPossible', and 'Disabled'.
Specifies a sub-path inside the referenced volume that should be mounted instead of the volume's root, allowing selective mounting of a directory or file from the volume.

subPathExpr is an alternative to subPath that allows the sub-path to be defined using environment variable references (e.g., $(VAR_NAME)). It is resolved at container startup and used to mount a sub-path of the volume.
Container's working directory for the ephemeral container. If not specified, the container runtime's default is used.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.host_aliases.ho.text: A list of hostnames that are mapped to the IP address specified in the hostAliases entry. These hostnames are added to the Pod's /etc/hosts file.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.host_aliases.ip.text: The IP address for the host alias entry. This IP is associated with the specified hostnames and added to the pod's /etc/hosts file.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.image_pull_secr.text: Name of the image pull secret. Must reference a Secret in the same namespace.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.init_containers.text: Arguments to the container's entrypoint. This corresponds to the CMD directive in the container image and overrides the image's default command arguments.

The command to run in the init container, corresponding to the entrypoint in Docker. This is not executed by a shell; if shell behavior is desired, explicitly invoke the shell (e.g., ["sh", "-c", "echo hi"]). If omitted, the container image's default entrypoint is used.
List of environment variables to set in the init container. Each entry defines a variable name and either a direct value or a value source (e.g., secret, config map, field ref).
Name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier.
The literal value of the environment variable as a string. This field is optional; if not set, use valueFrom to source the value from a config map, secret, or field reference.

Specifies a source for the environment variable's value, such as a reference to a ConfigMap, Secret, or a field in the pod spec. This is used when the value is not directly set but pulled from another resource.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap. This can be used to populate an environment variable with the value of a specific key in a ConfigMap.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap to select the value from.
The name of the ConfigMap from which to select a key.
Specifies whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If true and the ConfigMap or key does not exist, the environment variable is not set and the container can start. Defaults to false.
Selects a field from the pod definition and uses its value as the environment variable's value.
The API version of the schema that the field path is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1'.
The path of the field to select from the pod's object, such as metadata.name or status.podIP.
Specifies whether the referenced file key must exist. When set to true, the container starts even if the key is absent; when false (default), the pod fails if the key is missing.

ResourceFieldRef selects a resource field of the container (such as requests.cpu, limits.memory) and exposes its value as an environment variable in the init container. It is used in the valueFrom source of an environment variable.
Name of the container to select the resource field from. If not specified, the pod's container is used.
The divisor to divide the resource value by. Must be a valid quantity string (e.g., '1', '100m'). If unspecified, the default divisor is 1.
The name of the resource field to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
secret_key_ref selects a specific key from a Secret in the pod's namespace to supply the value for the environment variable.
The key of the secret to select. This must be a valid key name within the referenced Secret.
The name of the Secret to select the key from.

Specifies whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If set to true, the reference is optional and the container can start even if the secret does not exist or the key is missing. Defaults to false, meaning the secret and key must exist.

A list of sources to populate environment variables in the init container. Each source can reference a ConfigMap or Secret (via config_map_ref or secret_ref) and optionally define a prefix for the variable names.
Reference to a ConfigMap whose data is exposed as environment variables in the container.
The name of the ConfigMap from which to inject environment variables. This must match the name of a ConfigMap in the same namespace as the pod.

Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must exist. If true, a missing ConfigMap is allowed and no environment variables from it are set; if false or omitted, the ConfigMap must exist or the pod will fail to start.
An optional prefix to prepend to each key in the ConfigMap or Secret when populating environment variables. Must be a valid C identifier.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret. The key-value pairs of the referenced secret are exposed as environment variables in the container.
Name of the Secret to reference. This Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Indicates whether the referenced Secret must exist. Defaults to false (the Secret must be present); if true, the Secret is optional and its absence is allowed.
The container image to run, e.g., 'nginx:latest'.

The image pull policy for this init container. Valid values are 'Always', 'IfNotPresent', and 'Never'. 'Always' pulls the image every time the container starts; 'IfNotPresent' pulls only if the image is not already present on the node; 'Never' never pulls the image and fails if it is not already present locally.
Lifecycle defines handlers for container lifecycle events (postStart and preStop). For init containers, Kubernetes does not execute lifecycle hooks, so this field is ignored for them.
Represents the post-start lifecycle hook that runs immediately after a container is created. It can contain an exec command or an HTTP GET request.
Exec specifies the action to take in the form of a command to be executed inside the container.

The command line to execute inside the container during the postStart hook. Specified as a list of strings; the first item is the command and subsequent items are arguments. The command is executed directly without a shell.
http_get specifies an HTTP GET request to perform in the postStart lifecycle hook. It defines the endpoint, port, headers, and other request parameters for the probe.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
A list of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each header is an object with `name` and `value` fields.

The name (key) of the HTTP header to send in the GET request of the post-start lifecycle hook. This is the header field name, such as 'Authorization' or 'Content-Type', paired with its corresponding value.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the GET request.
The path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port number or named port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Accepts a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol scheme used for the HTTP GET request, such as 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'.
The protocol scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP' if unspecified.
The number of seconds the container should sleep as part of the post-start lifecycle hook's sleep action.

The tcp_socket block defines a TCP socket check to be performed during the postStart lifecycle hook. It attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the container, with an optional host.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
Port number or name of the TCP socket to connect to on the container. Accepts a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port; if omitted, defaults to the container's first port.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that executes a handler immediately before a container is terminated. It allows you to run commands or make HTTP/TCP requests to gracefully stop the container, such as cleaning up resources or saving state.
Exec defines a command to execute inside the container as part of the pre_stop lifecycle hook.
Command to run inside the container. This is an array of strings, executed directly without a shell; shell features like pipes or variables are not supported unless you explicitly invoke a shell.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the pre-stop lifecycle hook. Contains endpoint details such as host, port, path, and headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header is an object with a name and a value field.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request, for example 'Authorization' or 'Content-Type'.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Can be a port number or a named port.
The HTTP protocol to use for the request. Allowed values are `HTTP` and `HTTPS`, with a default of `HTTP`.
Scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Sleep performs a sleep action during the pre-stop hook, pausing the container for a specified number of seconds before termination.
Number of seconds for the sleep action in the preStop lifecycle hook. Delays container termination by the specified duration.
Defines the TCP socket handler for the preStop lifecycle hook, specifying the port (and optionally host) to connect to when the container is about to be terminated.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket. If not specified, it defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to. Can be a numeric port number (e.g., 8080) or the name of a port defined in the container (e.g., "http"). This field is required.
Periodic probe of container liveness. The container will be restarted if the probe fails. Cannot be updated.
Specifies the command to execute in the container to perform the liveness probe. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with status 0.
The command to execute inside the container to perform the liveness probe. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status code 0, otherwise the container is restarted.
The minimum consecutive failures for the liveness probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.

grpc specifies an action that involves a gRPC request for the liveness probe. It includes the port to check and optionally the service name to resolve, allowing the kubelet to perform a gRPC health check on the container.
The port number on which the gRPC endpoint is exposed. Must be between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If empty (default), the gRPC server's overall health status is checked.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform on the container as part of the liveness probe to check container health.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
A list of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each object must contain 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request for this liveness probe.
The value of the HTTP header.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Provide a numeric port (1-65535) or the name of a port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request in the liveness probe.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated.
The frequency, in seconds, at which the liveness probe is performed. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 10 if not specified.
The minimum consecutive successes for the liveness probe to be considered successful. For liveness probes, this value must be 1.

Configures the liveness probe to perform a TCP socket check by attempting to open a connection to the container's IP address on the specified port. The port is required, and an optional host can be specified to override the connection target.
The host name to connect to for the TCP probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port number or named port to probe for the liveness check. Accepts an integer port or a name that refers to a port of the container.
The number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out and is considered failed. Defaults to 1 second if not specified.
The name of the init container. Must be a valid DNS label and unique within the pod.
List of ports to expose from the container. Each port defines a container port number and protocol, and optionally a name and host port.
The port number that the container exposes. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The host IP address to bind the port to. If not set, the port is bound to all host interfaces (0.0.0.0).
The port number on the host node to expose this container port. Must be a valid port number between 1 and 65535.
A name for this container port. Must be an IANA_SVC_NAME (e.g., a DNS label) and unique within the pod. This name can be used to reference the port from services or other configurations.
The protocol used for the port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, or SCTP. Defaults to TCP.

Defines a probe that checks whether the container is ready to accept traffic. In Kubernetes, this field is part of the container spec, though for init containers it is generally not used since they run to completion.
Exec specifies a command to run in the container as part of the readiness probe. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with a status code of 0.

The command to run inside the container for the readiness probe. It is specified as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. The probe succeeds if the command exits with exit code 0.
Minimum number of consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.
Specifies a gRPC-based readiness probe. The object includes a required port (integer) and an optional service name (string) to include in the gRPC health check request.
The port number of the gRPC service to probe. In a gRPC readiness probe, this specifies the port on the container that the probe will connect to.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not set, the gRPC server's default service is used.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform against the container as a readiness check. A response with an HTTP status code between 200 and 399 indicates the container is ready.
Host name to connect to, defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set "Host" in httpHeaders instead.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the request sent by the HTTP GET probe. Each item must contain a name and a value, representing a header to be added to the probe's request.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request, e.g., 'Authorization' or 'Content-Type'.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request. It is paired with the header name (the 'name' field) to form the HTTP header entry.
Path to access on the HTTP server.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) to use when making the HTTP request to the readiness probe endpoint.
Specifies the scheme to use for the HTTP request: HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Defaults to 0 seconds.
The number of seconds between each readiness probe execution. Defaults to 10 seconds if not set.

The minimum number of consecutive successful probe results required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. This defaults to 1 for readiness probes. Must be 1 for liveness and startup probes, and the minimum value is 1.

Configures a TCP socket probe. Kubernetes attempts to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port to determine readiness. This is one of the allowed probe types within a readiness probe.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to connect to. Accepts a numeric port string (e.g., '80') or a named port defined in the container.
The number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 1 second.

A list of resource resize policies for the init container. Each policy specifies a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the restart policy (NotRequired or RestartContainer) when that resource is resized, controlling whether the container needs to be restarted for the resize to take effect.
The name of the resource (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies.
Specifies the restart behavior of the container when the assigned resource is resized. Valid values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer'.
Resources defines the compute resource requirements (requests and limits) for the init container, such as CPU and memory.
List of resource claims that must be satisfied for this container. Each item references a ResourceClaim by name, enabling access to resources like persistent volumes or specialized hardware.
Name of the ResourceClaim that this container requires.
Specifies the maximum amount of compute resources that the container is allowed to use. Maps resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) to their quantities.

A map of Kubernetes resource names to quantity strings, specifying the minimum amount of compute resources (e.g., cpu, memory) required for the container. Example values: '100m' for CPU, '128Mi' for memory.

Specifies the restart policy for this init container. The only supported value is 'Always', which runs the container as a sidecar. When omitted, the default behavior is to run the init container to completion.
exit_codes is an object that defines which container exit codes this restart policy rule applies to for restart decisions.
The comparison operator used to match the container's exit code against the values in `exit_codes`. Examples include `In` and `NotIn`.
A list of integer exit codes that trigger this restart policy rule for the init container.
SecurityContext defines the security options the init container should be run with. If set, the fields of SecurityContext override the equivalent fields of PodSecurityContext.
Controls whether the process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, the container will have the no_new_privs bit set, preventing privilege escalation.

The AppArmor profile to apply to the container. This can be a predefined profile (RuntimeDefault or Unconfined) or a custom profile defined on the node (Localhost), optionally specifying the localhost profile name.
The name of the AppArmor profile to load on the local node when the type is 'Localhost'. This profile must exist on the node's local profile store.
The AppArmor profile type. Must be one of `RuntimeDefault`, `Localhost`, or `Unconfined`. If set to `Localhost`, the `localhostProfile` field must also be specified.
Configures Linux capabilities for the container, allowing specific capabilities to be added or dropped via the add and drop lists.
Specifies additional capabilities to grant to the container process. For example, 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME'.
The list of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's default capability set. Each entry is a capability name such as 'NET_ADMIN' or 'SYS_TIME'.
Indicates whether the container runs in privileged mode. Privileged containers have access to all host devices and run with extended capabilities beyond the default.

ProcMount denotes the type of proc mount to use for the container. Allowed values are 'DefaultProcMount' and 'UnmaskedProcMount'. Defaults to 'DefaultProcMount', which masks paths in /proc for security; 'UnmaskedProcMount' provides the full /proc without masking.
Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only, preventing writes to the root filesystem.
The GID to run the init container's entrypoint process as. If set, it overrides the group specified in the container image.

Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. If set to true, the kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and will refuse to start the container if it does.
Specifies the numeric user ID (UID) under which the init container's main process will run. Overrides the pod-level runAsUser if both are set.
seLinuxOptions configures the SELinux context for the init container. It allows specifying the user, role, type, and level of the SELinux label.
The SELinux level label applied to the container, typically a Multi-Category Security (MCS) level such as 's0:c123,c456'.
The SELinux role label for the container process.
The SELinux type label for the container, e.g., 'container_t'. This is part of the SELinux security context applied to the container processes.
The SELinux user label for the container.
Seccomp profile applied to the init container. Supports types Unconfined, RuntimeDefault, and Localhost; when Localhost is used, localhostProfile specifies the path to the node-local profile.
Path to the seccomp profile file on the node, used when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to apply. Allowed values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Unconfined', and 'Localhost'. When set to 'Localhost', a 'localhostProfile' must also be provided.
Windows-specific security context options for the init container. This field configures Windows-only security attributes and is applicable only to Windows containers.
The contents of a GMSA credential spec (as a JSON string) used by the Windows container.

Specifies the name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the container. GMSA (Group Managed Service Accounts) allow containers to inherit Active Directory identities; this must reference a credential spec available on the node.
Indicates whether the container should run as a HostProcess container. All containers in the pod must have the same effective HostProcess value. Defaults to false.
The UserName in Windows to run the container's process as. If unspecified, the default is the user specified in the container image.
Configures a probe to check whether the container's startup has completed. In init containers, this field has no effect because init container success is based on exit status.
Exec specifies a command to execute inside the container for the startup probe. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with status 0.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container for the startup probe. It is a list of strings; the first element is the command, and subsequent elements are arguments. Non-zero exit status indicates probe failure.
The number of consecutive failures that must occur for the startup probe to be considered failed, after which the container is marked as unhealthy.
grpc defines the gRPC-based probe handler for the startup probe, specifying the port to check and optionally the service name.
The port number of the gRPC service for the startup probe. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is an empty string, meaning the health check is performed on the overall service.
The HTTP GET action for the startup probe. Specifies how the probe performs an HTTP GET request to check the container's health.

Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET probe, defaults to the pod IP. This value is used as the Host header in the HTTP request, and you typically set the Host header via httpHeaders instead of this field.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP request. Each item specifies a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the startup probe's HTTP GET request (e.g., 'Authorization', 'X-Custom-Header').
The value of the HTTP header to include in the request.
Path to access on the HTTP server, e.g., '/healthz'. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The TCP port number or named port on the container to send the HTTP GET request to. Can be a numeric port (e.g., '8080') or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol (HTTP or HTTPS) used for the HTTP GET probe.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated.
Specifies how often (in seconds) to perform the startup probe. The default is 10 seconds; the minimum allowed value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Must be 1 for startup probes, as higher values are not allowed.
Configures a TCP socket check for the startup probe, which determines if the container has started successfully by attempting to open a TCP connection to the specified port on the container.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to connect to for the startup probe. Accepts a port number or a named port.
The duration in seconds that the pod is allowed to gracefully terminate before being forcefully killed. A value of 0 means immediate termination.
The number of seconds after which the startup probe times out and is considered failed if no response is received. Must be a positive integer.
Whether to allocate a standard input stream for the container, enabling interactive sessions or input to the container process.
If true, the container's stdin is closed after the first attach when stdin is enabled. Defaults to false when not specified.
Path to the file where the container's termination message is written. This message is then exposed to the kubelet and can be retrieved via the pod status. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Determines how the container's termination message is read. Allowed values are 'File' (default), which reads the message from /dev/termination-log, and 'FallbackToLogsOnError', which falls back to the container's log if the termination message file is empty and the container exits with error.
Indicates whether a TTY should be allocated for the container. This requires 'stdin' to be true.
List of volume devices (block storage) to be mounted into the container. Each entry specifies a device name and the path inside the container where the device will appear.
The path inside the container where the block device will be mounted (devicePath). This is required for each volume device entry.
The name of the volume that the device refers to. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod spec.
Specifies volumes to mount into the init container's filesystem. Each item defines a volume mount, typically including the volume name and mount path, along with options such as read-only or subPath.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must not contain ':'.
Mount propagation mode for this volume mount. Allowed values are 'None', 'HostToContainer', and 'Bidirectional'.
The name of the volume to mount. This must correspond to the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes.
Whether the volume mount is read-only. If true, the container has read-only access to the mounted volume.

recursive_read_only controls whether the volume mount is mounted recursively read-only. Possible values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', and 'IfPossible', where 'IfPossible' applies recursive read-only only if the volume driver supports it.
The sub-path within the volume that should be mounted instead of the volume's root. This allows mounting a specific directory of the volume into the container.
Similar to subPath, but can reference environment variables with the syntax $(VAR_NAME); the kubelet resolves the variables. Mutually exclusive with subPath.
The container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime's default is used, which may be configured in the container image.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.readiness_gates.text: The name of the condition that must be satisfied for the pod to be considered ready. This condition is defined outside the pod spec, typically by a custom controller or resource.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.resource_claims.text: The name of the resource claim. Must be unique within the pod.
The name of the ResourceClaim resource that this pod references. Must match an existing ResourceClaim in the same namespace, or be omitted if a template is provided.
Name of a ResourceClaimTemplate in the same namespace that will be used to create a ResourceClaim for this pod.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.resources.claim.text: The name of the ResourceClaim resource that this pod references. This must match the name of an existing ResourceClaim in the same namespace.
The name of the ResourceClaim that this pod requests. The named ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.scheduling_gate.text: The name of the scheduling gate. This name identifies a gate that can block a pod from being scheduled; the pod will not be scheduled until all scheduling gates are removed.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.security_contex.text: The name of the sysctl parameter to set, such as kernel.shm_rmid_forced or net.ipv4.ip_forward.
The value of the sysctl parameter.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.tolerations.eff.text: The pod scheduling effect this toleration matches, such as NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, or NoExecute.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.tolerations.key.text: The taint key that this toleration matches. When omitted with operator 'Exists', the toleration matches all keys.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.tolerations.ope.text: The operator to use when matching taints. Allowed values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. If 'Exists', the toleration matches all taints with the given key; if 'Equal', it matches taints with the given key and value. Defaults to 'Equal'.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.tolerations.tol.text: The duration in seconds that the toleration is effective for, after which the pod may be evicted if the taint persists. If unset, the toleration does not expire.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.tolerations.val.text: The value to match the taint value when using the Equal operator. If the operator is Exists, this field must be empty.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.topology_spread.text: Label selector used to identify the set of pods to which the topology spread constraint applies. Must match the pods whose spread is constrained.
A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement contains a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values.
The label key that the selector applies to. This must match a label on the resource for the match expression to be satisfied.
The operator used to compare the label value against the set of values. Allowed values are `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, and `DoesNotExist`.
A list of string values that the label key must match. Required when the operator is In or NotIn; must be empty when the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist.
A map of label keys and values that must match the pod's labels for the label selector to match.

A list of pod label keys that must exist on pods for them to be considered by this topology spread constraint. Spreading is calculated over the label values associated with these keys, allowing refinement of the pod set used for distribution.
Maximum degree of skew (difference in number of pods) allowed between any two topology domains when distributing pods, as defined in Kubernetes topology spread constraints. Must be greater than zero.

The minimum number of eligible topology domains for spreading. If the number of eligible domains is less than this value, the spread constraint calculation treats the global minimum as zero and evaluates skew across the existing eligible domains.
Indicates how to treat the Pod's nodeAffinity when calculating pod topology spread skew. Allowed values are 'Honor' and 'Ignore', with 'Honor' as the default.
Policy for handling node taints when computing topology spread. Allowed values are 'Honor' (only consider nodes that match taints) and 'Ignore' (default, ignore taints).
The key of node labels used to group nodes into topology domains for spreading pods; defines the failure domain over which pods are spread.

Determines the action taken when a pod does not satisfy the spread constraint. Valid values are 'DoNotSchedule' (the pod is not scheduled) and 'ScheduleAnyway' (the pod is scheduled anyway, potentially violating the constraint).

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.aws_ela.text: Represents an AWS Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume as a volume source in the pod specification, allowing the pod to mount an AWS EBS volume.
Filesystem type to mount for the AWS EBS volume, e.g., 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system.
The partition number of the AWS EBS volume to mount. If omitted, the first partition is used.
Optional: Defaults to false (read/write). If set to true, the volume is mounted as read-only.
The unique identifier of the AWS EBS volume to mount in the pod.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.azure_d.text: Configuration for an Azure Disk volume that can be attached to the pod.
Specifies the caching mode for the Azure disk. Allowed values are None, ReadOnly, and ReadWrite.
The name of the Azure data disk to use as a volume.
The URI of the Azure disk to attach, in the format /subscriptions/{subscription-id}/resourcegroups/{resource-group}/providers/microsoft.compute/disks/{disk-name}.
Filesystem type to mount for the Azure disk volume. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host OS (e.g., 'ext4', 'xfs', 'ntfs'). Defaults to 'ext4' if unset.
Kind of the Azure disk. Allowed values are `Managed` (default), `Shared`, and `Unmanaged`.
Indicates whether the Azure disk volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; when false (default), it is mounted read-write.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.azure_f.text: Represents an Azure File volume source that mounts a Microsoft Azure file share into the pod. Requires a Kubernetes secret containing the Azure storage account name and key, and the share name.
Mount the Azure File share as read-only. Defaults to false.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret that contains the Azure Storage account name and key.
The name of the Azure File share to be mounted as a volume.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.cephfs.text: CephFS represents a Ceph Filesystem volume mount that allows a CephFS share to be mounted into a pod. It contains configuration such as monitors, path, user, and secret references for the CephFS mount.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.cephfs..text: List of Ceph monitor endpoints (hostnames or IP addresses) for the CephFS volume. Required to connect to the Ceph cluster.
The path within the CephFS volume to mount. Defaults to "/" if not specified.
Marks the CephFS volume as read-only. If true, the volume is mounted with read-only permissions; otherwise it is mounted read-write.
Path to the keyring file used for CephFS authentication. Defaults to /etc/ceph/user.secret.
secretRef is a reference to a Kubernetes Secret that provides the CephFS keyring. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod and contains the key material for accessing the CephFS volume.
The name of the Secret that provides the CephFS credentials. This Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
The RADOS user name used for CephFS authentication. If not provided, the default user is 'admin'.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.cinder.text: Cinder represents an OpenStack Cinder volume that is mounted as a volume in the pod. It is one of the supported volume sources in Kubernetes.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.cinder..text: Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system (e.g., ext4, xfs). Defaults to the volume's filesystem type if not specified.
Mounts the Cinder volume as read-only when set to true. Defaults to false, meaning the volume is read-write.

Reference to a Secret containing Cinder authentication credentials (user and password). The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod. If omitted, default Cinder credentials from the cloud provider are used.
Name of the Kubernetes secret that contains the authentication credentials for the Cinder volume.
The unique ID of the Cinder volume to mount, as defined in OpenStack Cinder.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.config_.text: ConfigMap volume source. Specifies the name of a ConfigMap whose data will be exposed as files in the volume, and optionally, a list of keys to project. If no items are specified, all keys from the ConfigMap are exposed.
Specifies the file mode (permission bits) applied to files in the ConfigMap volume. If unset, defaults to 0644.
Optional list of key-to-path mappings that specifies which keys of the referenced ConfigMap to project into the volume as files. Each item maps a ConfigMap key to a file path within the volume.
The key in the ConfigMap to select. The value corresponding to this key will be mounted at the specified path within the volume.
The permission mode for the file, represented as an integer (e.g., 0644 for owner read/write, group/others read). If omitted, the default mode from the volume is used.
The relative path within the volume where the config map key's value is mounted. Must not be an absolute path, must not contain '..', and must not start with '..'.
Name of the ConfigMap to mount as a volume. Must match the name of a ConfigMap in the same namespace as the pod.
Specifies whether the ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. When set to true, the volume can be populated even if the referenced ConfigMap or keys are missing, avoiding pod startup errors.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.csi.text: Configures a volume sourced from a Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver. This block allows mounting a volume provided by an external CSI driver in the pod.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.csi.dri.text: The name of the CSI driver to use for this volume. This must match the driver name registered with the kubelet.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.csi.fs_.text: Filesystem type to mount (e.g., 'ext4' or 'xfs'). If omitted, the CSI driver's default filesystem is used.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.csi.nod.text: Reference to the Kubernetes secret that contains sensitive information needed by the CSI driver to perform the node publish operation. The secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the secret to use for node publish operations. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.csi.rea.text: Marks the CSI volume as read-only. When set to true, the volume is mounted with read-only access.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.csi.vol.text: Map of attributes to pass to the CSI driver for this volume. These correspond to the volumeAttributes field in the CSI volume source.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.downwar.text: Defines a downward API volume that injects pod metadata (such as labels, annotations, and resource limits) into the pod as files accessible to containers.
The permissions, in octal, to set on files in the downward API volume. Defaults to 0644.

List of files to expose via the downward API volume, where each item specifies a file path and the corresponding pod or container field (such as metadata or resource limits) to project into that file.
The fieldRef is an ObjectFieldSelector that selects a field of the pod (for example, metadata.name or spec.nodeName) whose value is written to the downward API volume file.
The API version of the schema that the field_path refers to. For example, 'v1'.
The path to the field in the Pod specification to expose. For example, `metadata.name` or `metadata.labels`.
The Unix file permission bits to set on the projected file, expressed as an octal number (e.g., 0644). If not specified, the default is 0644.
Relative path within the volume where the file is created. Must not be absolute and must not contain '..' segments.

Reference to a container resource field (like requests.cpu, limits.memory) to be projected into the Downward API volume item. It includes the target container, the resource name, and an optional divisor to scale the value.
Name of the container to which the resource field reference applies. Required when using resourceFieldRef to select a container resource (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory).
Specifies the divisor for the resource quantity. The resource field value is divided by this divisor before being exposed. Defaults to 1 if not specified.
Resource is the name of the container resource to expose, such as 'cpu' or 'memory' for requests/limits.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.empty_d.text: Configures a volume of type emptyDir. An emptyDir volume is created empty when the pod is assigned to a node and persists as long as the pod exists. It is commonly used to share data between containers in the same pod.
Specifies the storage medium for the emptyDir volume. Use 'Memory' to back the volume with tmpfs (RAM-backed storage); an empty string or no value uses the default disk-backed storage.
Specifies a storage size limit for the emptyDir volume as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., "1Gi"). If not set, the volume is limited only by the node's available storage.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.ephemer.text: Configures an ephemeral volume that is created with the pod and deleted when the pod is removed. This is typically used for generic ephemeral volumes (via a PersistentVolumeClaim template) or CSI ephemeral volumes.
Template for a PersistentVolumeClaim that will be created for this pod. The claimed volume is ephemeral, with the PVC created when the pod starts and deleted when the pod is removed.
Standard Kubernetes object metadata for the PersistentVolumeClaim generated from this volume claim template. Includes fields such as labels, annotations, and name.
Annotations is a map of string keys and values that can be used to attach arbitrary non-identifying metadata to the ephemeral volume claim template's metadata.
The server-generated timestamp (RFC3339, UTC) indicating when the PersistentVolumeClaim is created. This field is read-only and cannot be set by clients.
The timestamp (in RFC3339 format) at which the object was marked for deletion. This field is set when deletion has been requested and the object is still being terminated.
A list of finalizer names. Finalizers prevent the deletion of the object until all finalizers are removed, enabling cleanup before deletion.

generate_name is an optional prefix for generating a unique name for the volume claim template when name is not specified. The Kubernetes API server appends a random string to this prefix to create a unique name.

A sequence number representing a specific generation of the desired state. This field is set by the system and is read-only. It monotonically increases each time the desired state of the object is changed.
Labels to attach to the PersistentVolumeClaim created from this template. These labels help select and organize the generated PVCs.
managedFields is a list of managed fields entries. Each entry records the manager, operation, and the fields that the manager owns, used for field management and conflict resolution.
The Kubernetes API version against which the managed fields in this entry were recorded.
The type of the fields in this managed field set, typically 'FieldsV1'.
The set of fields managed by the manager, represented as a JSON object mapping field paths to their values. This is part of the Kubernetes ManagedFieldsEntry and allows tracking of field ownership.
The name of the manager (e.g., kubectl, a controller) that last applied this managed field set.
The type of operation that created this managed fields entry. Allowed values are 'Apply' and 'Update'.

The name of the subresource that the operation was performed on, if any. For example, 'status' when the field manager updated the status subresource. Empty when the operation was on the main resource.
The timestamp of when the managed field entry was last updated, in RFC3339 format.
The namespace in which the volume claim template should be created. If omitted, it defaults to the namespace of the pod.
List of references to owning objects. If all owners are deleted, this object may be garbage collected, subject to the owner reference policy (e.g., blockOwnerDeletion and controller flags).
The API version of the referenced owner object (e.g., 'v1', 'apps/v1').
If true, the owner reference blocks deletion of the dependent object until the owner is deleted, as defined by Kubernetes OwnerReference semantics.
A boolean flag indicating whether this owner reference is the controlling owner. If true, the referenced object is the controller of the dependent resource, and only one controller can exist.
The kind of the owner object (e.g., ReplicaSet, DaemonSet). Must match the kind of the referenced object.
The name of the referenced owner object. This is required when creating an owner reference.
The unique identifier (UID) of the owner object referenced by this owner reference.
The version of the resource as maintained by the server. This value is used for optimistic concurrency and changes on every write.
A URL referencing the object itself, used for API navigation. In Kubernetes, this field is deprecated and may be empty.
The unique identifier assigned by the Kubernetes API server to the persistent volume claim created from this template. This value is generated by the server and is not user-configurable.
spec defines the desired characteristics of the persistent volume claim to be created, such as access modes, resource requests, storage class, and volume mode.
Specifies the access modes for the volume claim, such as ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteMany, or ReadWriteOncePod. This determines how the volume can be mounted by nodes and pods.
Specifies the data source for the volume claim, such as a PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot, allowing pre-population from an existing resource.
APIGroup is the group for the resource being referenced. If APIGroup is not specified, the specified Kind must be in the core API group.
The kind (type) of the data source object referenced by this volume claim template. Common values include 'PersistentVolumeClaim' and 'VolumeSnapshot'.
Name of the source resource (e.g., VolumeSnapshot or PersistentVolumeClaim) referenced by the dataSource for the ephemeral volume's claim template.

dataSourceRef specifies an object (e.g., a VolumeSnapshot, PersistentVolumeClaim, or custom resource) to use as the data source for this volume. It supports cross-namespace references, unlike data_source.
apiGroup is the group of the referenced resource. When empty, the core API group is assumed.
The kind of the referenced data source resource (e.g., PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot). This is part of the DataSourceRef that specifies the source to populate the volume claim.
Name of the data source resource referenced by the volume claim template.
The Kubernetes namespace of the referenced data source object. This field is used to refer to an object (e.g., a VolumeSnapshot) that may reside in a different namespace than the pod.
Resource requirements for the volume claim, expressed as an object with 'requests' and 'limits' maps, commonly used to specify the desired storage size (e.g., 'requests.storage: 10Gi').

Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. This is a map of resource names (e.g., cpu, memory, storage) to quantities. For ephemeral volume claim templates, this can specify the maximum storage size or other resource limits. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/

A map defining the minimum resources required for the ephemeral volume claim, such as storage size. Keys are resource names (e.g., 'storage'), and values are Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., '1Gi').
A label selector used to query PersistentVolumes that satisfy the claim's requirements. Only volumes whose labels match this selector are considered for binding to the claim.
A list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed together, and each requirement consists of a key, an operator, and a list of values.
The label key that the selector expression applies to. In Kubernetes, this is the key of a label that must match for the persistent volume to be considered eligible.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Allowed operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values that correspond to the key and operator. For 'In' and 'NotIn' operators, these are the values to match against. For 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', this list must be empty.

A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels of a PersistentVolumeClaim for the selector to apply. All specified labels must be present and match exactly for the volume claim template to select the claim.
The name of the StorageClass to use for the persistent volume claim. If not specified, the default StorageClass is used.
The name of the VolumeAttributesClass to apply to this volume claim. If not specified, the default VolumeAttributesClass from the StorageClass is used.
Volume mode for the ephemeral volume claim, specifying whether the volume is presented as a filesystem or a raw block device. Allowed values are 'Filesystem' (default) and 'Block'.
The name of an existing PersistentVolume to bind to. When set, the resulting PersistentVolumeClaim is bound to the specified volume.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.fc.text: Represents a Fibre Channel volume source, allowing the Pod to mount a Fibre Channel storage device.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.fc.fs_t.text: Filesystem type to mount, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. If not specified, the default filesystem type of the underlying volume is used.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.fc.lun.text: An integer representing the logical unit number (LUN) of the Fibre Channel target volume.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.fc.read.text: If true, the Fibre Channel volume is mounted as read-only.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.fc.targ.text: The list of Fibre Channel target World Wide Names (WWNs) that the volume will connect to.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.fc.wwid.text: List of Fibre Channel World Wide Identifiers (WWIDs) used to identify the volume. Either wwids or targetWWNs must be set, but not both.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.flex_vo.text: Configuration block for a FlexVolume volume source. This allows a Pod to mount a volume using a FlexVolume driver.
Specifies the name of the FlexVolume driver to use for this volume. This driver must be installed on the host and is responsible for mounting and unmounting the volume.
The filesystem type to be mounted by the FlexVolume, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. If unspecified, it defaults to ext4.
Options is a map of additional command-line arguments to pass to the flexvolume plugin.
If true, the FlexVolume is mounted as read-only, preventing write operations to the volume.

secret_ref is an optional reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains sensitive information, such as credentials, to be used by the FlexVolume driver. It references a Secret object in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the secret. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.flocker.text: Defines a Flocker volume source for a Kubernetes pod volume, which mounts a Flocker dataset into the pod. This is a supported volume type in the pod's spec.
The name of the Flocker dataset to be used for this volume.
The UUID of the Flocker dataset to mount. This uniquely identifies the dataset, as an alternative to datasetName.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.gce_per.text: Configures a Google Compute Engine Persistent Disk as a volume source for the pod. This allows the pod to mount a GCE Persistent Disk that exists in the same GCP project, with options for filesystem type, partition, and read-only access.
The filesystem type to mount on the Google Compute Engine persistent disk, such as ext4 or xfs. Defaults to ext4 if not specified.
The partition number on the GCE persistent disk to mount. If omitted, the entire disk is used.
Name of the GCE persistent disk to mount. This corresponds to the `pdName` field in the Kubernetes GCEPersistentDiskVolumeSource.
Marks the GCE persistent disk volume as read-only, preventing writes from the pod to the volume. Defaults to false (read-write).

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.git_rep.text: Represents a Git repository volume source. It specifies the repository URL, revision, and optional directory to mount; this volume source is deprecated in favor of using an init container to clone the repository.

Target directory name for the git repo volume. Must not contain or start with '..'. If '.' is supplied, the volume directory will be the git repository; otherwise, the volume will contain the git repository in the subdirectory with the given name.
The URL of the git repository to clone into the volume.
The commit hash (revision) of the Git repository to checkout for this volume. This selects a specific commit, tag, or branch from the repository.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.gluster.text: Glusterfs represents a Glusterfs mount that lasts the lifetime of a pod. It configures a volume sourced from a GlusterFS cluster.
The name of the Kubernetes Endpoints object that represents the GlusterFS cluster. This field is required.
The path to the GlusterFS volume, identifying the specific volume within the GlusterFS cluster.
Specifies whether the GlusterFS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.host_pa.text: Configures a hostPath volume, which mounts a file or directory from the host node's filesystem into the pod. The object specifies the path on the host and the type of mount.
The path on the host node to mount into the pod for a hostPath volume.

The type of the hostPath volume, controlling how the host path is checked or created. Possible values include: '', Directory, DirectoryOrCreate, File, FileOrCreate, Socket. For example, 'Directory' ensures the path exists and is a directory.

kubernetes_core_pod.spec.volumes.image.text: Image represents an OCI image volume source. This volume is backed by an OCI image, and its content is mounted read-only into the pod.
