The SELinux role for the container's security context, such as 'system_r' or 'user_r'.
The SELinux type label for the container, used to define the type domain for processes and files.
The SELinux user label for the container, part of the SELinux options in the security context.
Configures the seccomp profile for the container. The profile type can be one of RuntimeDefault, Localhost, or Unconfined, with an optional localhost profile path for the Localhost type.
The path to a seccomp profile on the node's local filesystem. This field is only used when the seccomp type is 'Localhost'.
The seccomp profile type determines which seccomp profile is used for the container, controlling system-call filtering.
Windows-specific security options for the container, such as GMSA credential spec and run-as username. Only applicable when running on Windows nodes.
The full contents of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container, provided as a JSON string.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the container's Windows security context.
Whether the container should be run as a HostProcess container. HostProcess containers allow access to the Windows host, and default to false if not set.

The UserName in Windows to run the entrypoint of the container process. Defaults to the user specified in image metadata if unspecified. May also be set in PodSecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.
Defines a probe that checks whether the application in the container is started. If configured, other probes (liveness and readiness) are not activated until the startup probe succeeds.
Exec specifies the command to run inside the container to perform the startup probe. The probe is successful if the command exits with a status code of 0.
The command to execute inside the container as part of the exec startup probe. A list of strings where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.
Minimum consecutive failures for the startup probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.
Configures a gRPC action for the startup probe, which requires a port number and may include a service name.
The port number of the gRPC service to connect to for the probe. Must be between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the gRPC health check is performed against the entire server.
http_get defines an HTTP GET request used by the startup probe to check container health. It includes configuration for host, port, path, scheme, and HTTP headers to perform the request.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET probe. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request for the startup probe. Each header object contains a `name` and `value` field.
The name of the HTTP header to send as part of the HTTP GET request performed by the startup probe.
The value of the HTTP header field.
HTTP request path to access on the container. Defaults to '/' if not specified.

The port number to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. This can be an integer port number or a named port (string) defined in the container's ports. Port numbers must be in the range 1 to 65535.
Specifies the network protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated.
The number of seconds between each probe execution. Minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1.
Configures the startup probe to check a TCP socket. The probe succeeds if a TCP connection to the specified port can be established.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The port number or name of the TCP socket to probe on the container. Can be an integer port number or a named port.

The duration in seconds the container is given to terminate gracefully after this probe fails, overriding the pod-level terminationGracePeriodSeconds. Must be a non-negative integer; the value zero means delete immediately, and if not set, the pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds is used.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.
Whether to enable stdin for the container, allowing the container to receive input from the standard input stream. Defaults to false.
When true, the container's stdin is closed after the first attach session, rather than remaining open for subsequent attaches. This field only has effect when stdin is also true.
Path where the container's termination message is written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Sets how the kubelet handles the container's termination message. Valid values are 'File' (default, reads from the file specified by terminationMessagePath) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError' (uses the last chunk of container logs if the message file is empty).
Indicates whether to allocate a pseudo-TTY for the container. When set to true, the container gets an interactive terminal.
List of block devices that the container can access, each defining a device name and the device path inside the container.
The path inside the container where the block device will be exposed. This is the device path (e.g., /dev/sdb) where the volume device is made available to the container.
The name of a volume defined in the pod spec. The volume device references this volume to attach as a block device.
Defines volumes to mount into the container's filesystem, including the volume name, mount path, and additional options such as read-only or subPath.
Path within the container at which the volume will be mounted. Must be an absolute path and must not contain ':'.

Controls how mounts propagate from the host to the container and vice versa. Valid values are 'None' (no propagation), 'HostToContainer' (mounts from the host are visible in the container), and 'Bidirectional' (mounts propagate both ways).
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
Mounts the volume as read-only if set to true. If false or omitted, the volume is mounted with read-write access.

Controls whether the volume mount is recursively read-only. Valid values are 'Enabled', 'Disabled', or 'IfPossible'. 'Enabled' makes the mount and all its subdirectories read-only; 'Disabled' disables recursive read-only; 'IfPossible' enables it only if the underlying volume supports it.
Specifies a sub-path within the referenced volume to mount instead of the volume's root. This allows mounting a specific directory from a volume into the container.

subPathExpr specifies a sub-path of the volume to mount, using environment variable references like $(VAR_NAME). It allows the sub-path to be computed dynamically based on the pod's environment variables.
The container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime's default working directory is used (usually the image's WORKDIR or /).
The name of the DNS resolver option, such as 'ndots' or 'timeout'. This field is required in each DNS configuration option.
The value of the DNS resolver option named in the associated `name` field. For example, `ndots:5` sets the ndots threshold.
Arguments to the entrypoint for the ephemeral container. This list is passed to the container's command as arguments, analogous to the args field for regular containers.
The command to run in the ephemeral container, represented as a list of string arguments. This is the container's entrypoint, overriding any default command in the image.
List of environment variables to set in the ephemeral container. Each entry defines a variable name and value or value source.
The name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier.
The value of the environment variable. This sets the literal string value assigned to the environment variable in the container.
valueFrom is an object that defines a source for the environment variable's value, allowing the value to be dynamically populated from a ConfigMap, Secret, pod field, or resource field.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to provide the value for the environment variable. It specifies the ConfigMap name and the key to use.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap to select the value for this environment variable.
Name of the ConfigMap from which to select the key for the environment variable value.
Specifies whether the referenced key or its containing ConfigMap must be defined. If true, a missing key or ConfigMap does not prevent the container from starting.
Selects a field of the pod as the value of the environment variable. Supported fields include metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, and status.podIP.
The API version of the schema that the field path refers to in the field reference (e.g., v1).
The path to the field in the Pod spec to select, such as 'metadata.name' or 'spec.nodeName'.

Boolean flag indicating whether the referenced key must be present. If false, the key is required and must exist in the referenced file; if true, the key is optional and its absence will not prevent the container from starting.
Selects a resource field of the container (e.g. limits.cpu or requests.memory) and exposes its value as an environment variable.
The name of the container whose resource value is referenced. If omitted, defaults to the container that defines the environment variable.
Divisor is the value by which the resource value is divided. Must be a valid Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1Gi', '500m'). Defaults to '1' if not specified.
The name of the resource to select from the container's resource requirements, e.g., 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
SecretKeyRef selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. This can be used to expose a secret value as an environment variable.
The key within the referenced Secret's data map to select. This specifies which key's value should be used as the value for the environment variable.
The name of the Secret to retrieve the key from.

Indicates whether the referenced secret key must exist. Set to true to allow the container to start even if the secret key or its containing secret is not defined, in which case the environment variable is omitted.
A list of sources to populate environment variables in the ephemeral container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret, and the keys within the source become environment variable names.
Reference to a ConfigMap from which to pull environment variables. This object specifies the name of the ConfigMap and whether it is optional.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference. This is the name of the ConfigMap resource defined in the cluster.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If set to true, the ConfigMap may be absent and missing keys are allowed; if false or omitted, the ConfigMap must exist.
An optional prefix that is prepended to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret. For example, if prefix is 'MY_', each key name becomes MY_<key>.
SecretRef is a reference to a Kubernetes Secret whose data will be exposed as environment variables in the container.
The name of the Secret that supplies the environment variables. This must match an existing Secret in the same namespace.

Specifies whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If true, the container can start even if the Secret does not exist; if false or unset, the Secret is required and the container fails if it is missing.
The container image to use for the ephemeral container.
Image pull policy for the ephemeral container. Allowed values are Always, IfNotPresent, and Never. If omitted, the policy defaults to Always if the image tag is 'latest' or IfNotPresent otherwise.
This block configures lifecycle hooks for the ephemeral container, defining actions to take at container startup (postStart) and before shutdown (preStop).
Configures a handler that runs immediately after the ephemeral container is started. Supports exec, httpGet, or tcpSocket actions within the handler.
The exec action to run when the post-start lifecycle hook is triggered. This block defines a command to execute inside the container, typically specified as a list of command and arguments.

The command to run in the container for this exec lifecycle hook. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly, without a shell.
Specifies the HTTP GET request that the kubelet sends to trigger the postStart lifecycle hook.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP address.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request for the postStart lifecycle handler. Each header is defined by a name-value pair.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
The HTTP path that will be requested by the HTTP GET action.
The port to access for the HTTP GET request. Accepts a numeric port or a named port (string) defined in the container's ports.
The URI scheme for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.

Sleep is an optional configuration that specifies a sleep action for the lifecycle hook. It defines the duration (in seconds) the container should sleep, delaying the post-start hook continuation until the sleep completes.
The number of seconds for the sleep action in the postStart lifecycle hook. The container sleeps for this duration after starting before continuing.
Represents a TCP socket action that Kubernetes runs as part of the postStart lifecycle hook, which attempts to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Port number for the TCP socket connection. Accepts a numeric port or a named port (as a string).

PreStop is called immediately before a container is terminated. It allows the container to perform graceful shutdown operations before it is stopped, and the container is terminated once the handler completes or if it fails.
Exec action to run when the pre-stop hook is triggered. This specifies a command and arguments to be executed inside the container before it is terminated.
The command to execute in the container for the preStop lifecycle hook. It is provided as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.

Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This action is executed before the container is terminated and accepts parameters such as host, port, path, scheme, and HTTP headers.
The host name to use for the HTTP GET request. If not specified, the pod IP is used. To set the HTTP Host header, use httpHeaders instead.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP request. Each header is an object containing name and value fields.
The name of the HTTP header to set in the GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent in the HTTP GET request for the pre-stop lifecycle hook.
The path to access on the HTTP server, defaulting to '/' if not specified.
The port on the container to send the HTTP GET request to. Can be a numeric port (e.g., 8080) or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Sleep specifies the Sleep action to be performed before the container is terminated. It accepts a `seconds` field indicating the duration of the sleep.
Specifies the number of seconds the container sleeps during the preStop lifecycle hook.
TCP socket handler for the pre-stop lifecycle hook of an ephemeral container. It specifies a port (and optionally a host) to check for connectivity before the container is terminated.
Optional host name or IP address to connect to; defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port number to connect to. Can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container.

The liveness probe configuration for the ephemeral container. This object defines how to check whether the container is alive, such as by executing a command, making an HTTP request, or opening a TCP socket, along with timing parameters like initial delay and period.
The exec action for the liveness probe, which runs a command inside the container to check its health.

The command to run inside the container for the exec liveness probe. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the executable and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly, not through a shell; a zero exit status indicates success (healthy), non-zero indicates failure.
Minimum consecutive failures for the liveness probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.
Configures a gRPC-based health check for the liveness probe. It contains the port to connect to and optionally the service name to check.
The port number of the gRPC server to query for the liveness probe. This is required for a gRPC probe.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is the same as the container name.
HTTP GET probe configuration that performs a GET request against the container's IP address to determine liveness.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP address. For setting the HTTP Host header, prefer using httpHeaders instead.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the probe request. Each item defines a header name and value.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the liveness probe's HTTP GET request.
The HTTP request path used by the liveness probe's HTTP GET action.
The port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Accepts a port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME port name.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request, such as HTTP or HTTPS.
The URI scheme used for the HTTP request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not set.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds. Minimum value is 1.
Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For a liveness probe, this value must be 1.

Represents a TCP socket probe action for the liveness probe. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port; success indicates the container is healthy, failure triggers the restart policy.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port to probe. This can be a numeric port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The duration in seconds the pod is allowed to terminate gracefully before being forcefully killed. A value of 0 means delete immediately; if unspecified, a default (typically 30 seconds) is used.
Timeout in seconds after which the liveness probe is considered failed if no response is received. Defaults to 1 and must be at least 1.

List of ports to expose from the container. Exposing a port here gives the system additional information about the network connections a container uses, but is primarily informational. It also enables Kubernetes to give that information to networking components such as the load balancer.
The port number that the container listens on and exposes.
The host IP address to bind the host port to. When not set, the port is bound to all host interfaces (0.0.0.0).
The port on the host node to map to the container port. If omitted, the container port is not exposed on the host.
The name of the port. Must be a valid IANA_SVC_NAME and unique within the pod. Optional.
The network protocol for the port. Allowed values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP. Defaults to TCP if not specified.
Exec specifies the exec action for the readiness probe. It contains a command to run inside the container; the probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0.

The command to execute inside the container as part of the exec readiness probe. It is a list of strings representing the command and its arguments. The command is executed directly without a shell; a zero exit status indicates success, non-zero indicates failure.
The number of consecutive failures required before the probe is considered failed. Defaults to 3, minimum value is 1.

Configures a gRPC health check for the readiness probe. This object specifies the gRPC action used to probe the container, including the port to connect to and optionally the name of the health check service.
The port number of the gRPC service to connect to for this readiness probe. Required, must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC implementation.
Defines the HTTP GET request to perform for the readiness probe, specifying the endpoint to query for container health.
Optional. The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; overrides the Host header and connection target.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP request. Each item contains a header name and value, allowing repeated headers as supported by HTTP.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request.
The value of the HTTP header field in the readiness probe's HTTP GET request.
The path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container during the readiness probe. This may be an integer port number or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme for the HTTP request. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container starts before the readiness probe is initiated.
How often, in seconds, the readiness probe is executed. Must be at least 1 second.
Minimum consecutive successes for the readiness probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1.
Specifies a TCP probe that checks the container's health by attempting to open a connection to a given port. The tcp_socket object configures the port to check and optionally the host to connect to.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to connect to for the readiness probe. Accepts a numeric port number or a named port referenced from the container's ports.
The number of seconds the pod is allowed to terminate gracefully before being forcibly killed. Applies to the pod's shutdown procedure.
Number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. Defaults to 1 second if not specified.
Defines resource resize policies for the ephemeral container. Each policy specifies a resource name and the restart behavior when that resource is resized.
The name of the resource (e.g., 'cpu' or 'memory') for which this resize policy is configured.

Specifies the restart policy for the ephemeral container when a resize operation is applied. Allowed values are 'NotRequired' (apply resize without restart) and 'RestartContainer' (restart the container to apply the resize).
Specifies the compute resources (CPU, memory) required for the ephemeral container. Includes requests and limits for resource usage.

A list of resource claim references that specify additional resource requests for the ephemeral container. Each claim refers to a ResourceClaim by name, enabling the use of resources defined in ResourceClass or ResourceClaim objects.
Name of the resource claim, matching a logical name defined in the pod's spec.resourceClaims. This makes the referenced resource available to the ephemeral container.
The name of the ResourceClaim object in the same namespace as the pod that this container's resource claim references.

A map of resource names to quantities defining the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the ephemeral container. For example: cpu: '500m', memory: '128Mi'. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/
A map of resource names to quantities, specifying the minimum amount of compute resources required for the ephemeral container (e.g., cpu, memory).
Specifies the restart policy for the ephemeral container, controlling whether the container is restarted on exit. Allowed values are 'Always', 'OnFailure', and 'Never'.
A list of container exit codes that this rule applies to. If the container exits with any of these codes, the restart policy action is triggered.
SecurityContext holds security configuration that will be applied to an ephemeral container, such as user IDs, capabilities, and SELinux options.

Controls whether the ephemeral container's processes can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, setuid or setgid binaries are prevented from changing the effective user/group ID, effectively disabling privilege escalation.

app_armor_profile defines the AppArmor profile to apply to the ephemeral container. It contains a required type field (one of Localhost, RuntimeDefault, or Unconfined) and an optional localhostProfile field for the profile name when type is Localhost.
Name of a preconfigured AppArmor profile on the node to use. This profile must already be loaded on the node for the container to run.
The type of AppArmor profile to use. Valid values are 'Localhost', 'RuntimeDefault', and 'Unconfined'. When set to 'Localhost', the 'localhost_profile' field must also be specified.

The capabilities field configures Linux capabilities for the ephemeral container, allowing extra capabilities to be added or default ones to be dropped. It contains 'add' and 'drop' lists of capability names.
List of Linux capabilities to add to the ephemeral container's default capability set (e.g., NET_ADMIN, SYS_TIME). Capabilities are specified without the CAP_ prefix.
List of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's effective and permitted capability sets. For example, 'ALL' drops all capabilities, or specific ones like 'NET_RAW'.
Run the container in privileged mode, giving its processes essentially the same access as root on the host. Defaults to false.
Specifies the proc mount mode for the ephemeral container, controlling how the /proc filesystem is exposed within the security context.
Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only, preventing any writes to it. This is a common security hardening measure to limit the impact of a compromised container.
The GID to run the entrypoint of the container process. Must be a numeric positive integer. If unset, the default is the image's primary group.

Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. When set to true, the kubelet will validate that the container's user and image do not run as UID 0, and will fail to start the container otherwise.
The user ID (UID) to run the container process as. Overrides the user specified in the container image.
The SELinux level label (e.g., 's0' or 's0:c123') for the container. If unspecified, the pod-level SELinux level is inherited.
The SELinux role label for the container process (e.g., system_u). In Kubernetes, this is part of the se_linux_options configuration that specifies the role portion of the SELinux context.
The SELinux type label that applies to the container process.
The SELinux user label for the container's security context, such as 'system_u' or 'unconfined_u'. This field is part of the SELinux options and typically follows the SELinux user naming convention.
Defines the seccomp profile for the ephemeral container. It allows specifying the profile type (e.g., RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, Localhost) and optionally the path to a localhost profile.
The path to the localhost seccomp profile file on the node. This must be set when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to be applied to the container's security context.
Windows-specific security options for the ephemeral container, such as Group Managed Service Account (GMSA) credentials and HostProcess settings.
The GMSA credential spec content to use for the Windows container. This can be provided directly as a JSON string, or it is populated by the GMSA admission webhook when GMSACredentialSpecName is set.

The name of the GMSA (Group Managed Service Account) credential spec to use for the ephemeral container. This is part of the Windows security context options and enables the container to use a specific GMSA configuration.
Whether the container should be run as a HostProcess container. Only applicable to Windows containers. Defaults to false.
The username to run the container's entrypoint process as. For Windows containers only; defaults to the image's user if unspecified.

Configures a startup probe for the ephemeral container, which indicates when the container has started successfully. This probe can be used to gate the start of other probes, ensuring they only run after the application is ready.
Exec defines a command to be executed inside the container for the startup probe. The probe succeeds if the command exits with a status code of 0.

The command to run inside the container for the exec startup probe. It is a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly without a shell; exit status 0 indicates success and non-zero indicates failure.
The number of consecutive failures of the startup probe after which the container is considered failed and restarted. The default is 3, and the minimum value is 1.
Configures a gRPC-based probe for the container. The probe checks the gRPC service by connecting to a specified port, and optionally uses a service name.
Port number of the gRPC service that the probe will connect to. This field is required and must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is an empty string.
Performs an HTTP GET request against the container. Configures the HTTP probe action, including path, port, and optional headers for the startup probe.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. If not set, the pod IP is used. This overrides the default host.
List of HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request sent by the probe. Each object defines a header name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP GET request. Must be a valid HTTP header name.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent in the startup probe's HTTP GET request.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server, e.g., /healthz.
The port number or name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Accepts either a numeric port or a named port on the container.
Protocol to use for the HTTP GET probe request, such as HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP if not specified.
The protocol scheme (HTTP or HTTPS) to use for the HTTP GET request to the probe endpoint.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Defaults to 0 seconds.
How often (in seconds) to perform the startup probe. Defaults to 10; minimum value is 1.
The minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. Must be 1 for startup probes.
Specifies a TCP socket probe, used to check container health by attempting to open a TCP connection to a specific port on the container's IP address.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
The TCP port to check on the container. Accepts a numeric port or a named port (string).
The duration in seconds the pod is given to terminate gracefully before being forcefully killed. Defaults to 30 seconds.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second; minimum value is 1.
Set to true to enable standard input (stdin) for this ephemeral container.
When true, stdin is only attached once, and after the process reads from it, the channel is closed, preventing further input. Defaults to false.
The name of the target container to share the process namespace with. If not specified, the first container in the pod is used.
Path where the container's termination message is read from, typically used to capture the reason for container termination. Default is /dev/termination-log.
Defines how the termination message of the ephemeral container is read. Supported values are 'File' (default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'.
Indicates whether a TTY (teletypewriter) should be allocated for the ephemeral container, allowing interactive use. If true, a TTY is allocated.
List of block devices to be used by the ephemeral container. Each item maps a named volume to a device path inside the container (e.g., for raw block volume mounts).
The path inside the container where the volume device should be exposed (e.g., /dev/sdb).
The name of the volume that this volume device refers to.
Volume mounts for the ephemeral container, specifying which volumes to mount and where. Each mount includes a volume name, a mount path inside the container, and options such as read-only.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must not contain ':' and must be an absolute path.

Controls mount propagation for the volume mount. Valid values are None (no propagation), HostToContainer (host mounts are propagated to the container), and Bidirectional (mounts are propagated both ways, requiring privileged).
Name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
Specifies whether the volume mount is read-only. If true, the mount will be read-only; if false or omitted, it will be read-write.
Indicates whether the volume mount is recursive read-only. This field is supported for certain volume types, such as NFS.
subPath specifies a sub-path inside the referenced volume instead of its root, allowing only a portion of the volume to be mounted.

subPathExpr is an alternative to subPath that allows specifying a path relative to the volume's root using environment variable references. It supports the $(VAR_NAME) syntax for expansion, enabling dynamic subpaths based on container environment variables.
Sets the working directory for the ephemeral container. Commands run from this directory if specified; otherwise, the container runtime default is used.
List of hostnames for this host alias entry. These hostnames will be associated with the specified IP address in the pod's /etc/hosts file.
The IP address to associate with the hostnames listed in this host alias entry. This entry is added to the pod's /etc/hosts file.
Name of the Kubernetes secret to use for pulling container images.
Arguments to the container's entrypoint command. These override the CMD portion of the image's default configuration, if any.

The command to run in the init container. This corresponds to Docker's ENTRYPOINT and overrides the image's default entrypoint. The list of strings specifies the executable and its arguments, with the first element being the command and the rest as arguments.
List of environment variables to set in the init container. Each object defines a variable name and either a value or a valueFrom source.
The name of the environment variable to set in the init container. This is the key for the value defined in the same env entry.
The value of the environment variable.
Source for the environment variable's value. Can reference a config map key, secret key, or pod/resource field via configMapKeyRef, secretKeyRef, fieldRef, or resourceFieldRef.
Selects a key from a ConfigMap in the pod's namespace to provide the value for the environment variable. The value is taken from the referenced ConfigMap key.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap to select the value from.
The name of the ConfigMap to select the key from.

Indicates whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If true, the pod starts even if the referenced ConfigMap or key does not exist, leaving the environment variable unset. If false or omitted, the pod fails if the reference is missing.
Selects a field of the pod (e.g., metadata.name, spec.nodeName) to inject as an environment variable value.
The API version of the Kubernetes object from which the field is selected.

The path to the field to select from the pod, such as metadata.name, metadata.namespace, metadata.uid, metadata.labels['<KEY>'], metadata.annotations['<KEY>'], spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.hostIP, status.podIP, or status.podIPs.
The key in the referenced file to use as the value for the environment variable.
Flag to mark the referenced key as optional. When set to true, the container will start even if the specified key does not exist in the referenced file.
Name of the volume that contains the file from which the environment variable value is read.
Selects a resource field (such as limits.cpu or requests.memory) from the container, and optionally divides its quantity by a divisor, to set the environment variable's value.
The name of the container whose resource field is to be selected. If not specified, defaults to the container where this environment variable is defined.
The divisor for the resource value, used to scale the value. Must be a quantity string (e.g., '1', '1Ki'); defaults to '1'.
The name of the container resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.
Selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. This is a SecretKeySelector object that specifies the name of the Secret and the key to retrieve.
The key within the Secret to select the value from.
Name of the Secret to select a key from.
Indicates whether the secret key reference is optional. If true, the environment variable is omitted when the secret or key is missing; if false (default), the pod fails to start.

The env_from block describes a source of environment variables, such as a ConfigMap or Secret, whose data is injected into the init container's environment. Each element can specify a config_map_ref or secret_ref.
Reference to a ConfigMap from which to populate environment variables in the container. The ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the ConfigMap to reference. The keys of the ConfigMap will become environment variables in the container.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If true, the ConfigMap may be absent; if false (default), it must exist.

An optional identifier that is prepended to each key in the referenced ConfigMap or Secret when populating environment variables. If specified, it must be a valid C identifier (e.g., starts with a letter or underscore, contains no dashes).

secretRef is an object that references a Kubernetes Secret to populate environment variables. It contains the name of the Secret and an optional flag indicating whether the Secret must exist. The keys of the Secret become environment variable names in the container.
Name of the Kubernetes Secret to use as the source for environment variables. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Specifies whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If true, the Secret may be absent and any missing keys are ignored.
The container image to run for this init container.

Specifies the image pull policy for the init container. Valid values are 'Always', 'IfNotPresent', and 'Never'. 'Always' pulls the image every time the container starts, 'IfNotPresent' pulls only if the image is not already present, and 'Never' uses only the local image.
Lifecycle configures hooks that run at specific lifecycle events of the init container, such as postStart and preStop.

The postStart lifecycle hook is triggered immediately after a container is created. It defines a handler (such as exec, HTTP GET, or TCP socket) that runs before the container's primary process starts, commonly used for initialization or setup tasks.
Exec specifies the action to take for the lifecycle hook by running a command inside the container. It is an alternative to the HTTP GET handler.

The command to be executed inside the container as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. It is provided as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.

Specifies an HTTP GET request to be sent by the postStart lifecycle handler. The request details include host, port, path, scheme, and HTTP headers, allowing the container to signal readiness or perform initialization via an HTTP endpoint.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; you can override it with a specific hostname.
List of HTTP headers to send with the HTTP GET request. Each header is defined by a name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP request.
The value of the HTTP header sent in the HTTP GET request.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server for the GET request. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
Port number or name for the HTTP GET request. Can be an integer port number or the name of a container port.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request. Typically 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Supported values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS', with a default of 'HTTP'.
Sleep specifies the sleep action for the post-start lifecycle hook. It contains a duration in seconds for the container to sleep.
Number of seconds to sleep for the postStart lifecycle hook.
Configuration for a lifecycle hook handler that performs a TCP socket check by opening a connection to the specified host and port.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port for the postStart lifecycle hook's TCP socket check. This can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container's ports.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that is executed immediately before a container is terminated. It allows the container to perform graceful shutdown actions, such as draining connections or saving state, via an exec command, HTTP GET request, or TCP socket check.
Exec specifies the action to take in the preStop hook, which runs a command inside the container.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container as part of the preStop lifecycle hook. It is an array of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.
Defines the HTTP GET request to perform against the container. This is one of the handlers for the pre-stop lifecycle hook, executed before the container is terminated.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Specifies a list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each header object typically contains a name and a value.
Name of the HTTP header to include in the GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
Path to access on the HTTP server for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to '/'.
Port number (1-65535) or name of the container port to which the HTTP GET request is sent.
The protocol used for the HTTP GET request. Accepts 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS' (case-insensitive), with a default of 'HTTP' if not specified.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS; defaults to HTTP.
Represents the SleepAction for the pre-stop lifecycle hook, which pauses the container for a specified number of seconds before termination.
The number of seconds the container sleeps during the preStop hook, delaying termination.
Configures a TCP socket check as the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This action opens a TCP connection to the specified port (and optionally host) to trigger the stop signal.
Optional host name or IP address to connect to. If not provided, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port to connect to. This can be a numeric port or a named port from the container's defined ports.
Defines a liveness probe for the container. The kubelet uses this probe to determine when to restart the container based on its health.
Defines a command-based probe. Executes the specified command inside the container; the probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0.

Command is the command line to run inside the container. The first element is the command, and subsequent elements are arguments. A non-zero exit code indicates probe failure, while exit code 0 indicates success.
The number of consecutive failures that must occur for the liveness probe to be considered failed, after which the container is restarted. Defaults to 3 when not specified.
grpc specifies the parameters for a gRPC health check performed by the liveness probe. It includes the port number to query and optionally the service name for the gRPC health check.
The port on which the gRPC server is listening. This field is required and must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the default is the container's name.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform for the liveness probe. This allows the probe to check the health of the container by making an HTTP request.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each object should have a 'name' and a 'value' field.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the liveness probe request.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent with the liveness probe's HTTP request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. For example, /healthz. Defaults to / if not specified.
The port number (1-65535) or name of the port on the container to connect to for the HTTP GET request.
The protocol used for the HTTP GET request, typically either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. When unset, it defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request: either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the probe. Defaults to 10 seconds; minimum value is 1.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the liveness probe to be considered successful after a failure. For liveness probes, this value must be 1.
Specifies the TCP socket action for the liveness probe. It checks that a TCP connection can be established to the specified port on the container.
Host name to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not set, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to for the liveness probe. Can be a numeric port or a named port on the container.
Specifies the number of seconds the pod is allowed to terminate gracefully after a termination signal is sent, before it is forcibly killed. If not set, Kubernetes uses a default of 30 seconds.
Number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 1 if not specified.
The name of the init container. This name must be unique within the pod and is used to identify the container in logs, commands, and other references.
List of ports to expose from the container. Each port specifies the protocol (e.g., TCP or UDP), the container port number, and optionally the host port, host IP, and a name for the port.
The TCP/UDP port number the container listens on and exposes. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
The host IP address to bind the host port to. When specified with host_port, the container port is exposed only on that host IP; if omitted, it binds to all host interfaces.
Number of port to expose on the host. If specified, this must be a valid port number, 0 < x < 65536. If HostNetwork is specified, this must match ContainerPort. Most containers do not need this.
The name of the port. Must be an IANA_SVC_NAME and unique among all ports in the pod's containers.
The network protocol for this port. Valid values are 'TCP', 'UDP', and 'SCTP'; defaults to 'TCP'.
Readiness probe block, which defines a health check that determines when the container is considered ready to accept traffic. If the probe fails, the container is removed from service endpoints.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container for the readiness probe. The probe is successful if the command exits with a status code of 0.

The command to run inside the container for the exec probe. This is a list of strings, where the first element is the executable and the remaining elements are arguments. The command is executed directly without a shell.
Minimum consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3, minimum value is 1.
grpc specifies the gRPC action for the readiness probe. It includes the port to probe (required) and an optional service name for the gRPC health check.
The port number of the gRPC service to probe. Must be between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is empty string, which indicates the health check for the entire service.
An HTTP GET request configuration used as a readiness probe to check container health. It defines the endpoint to request, including path, port, and optional headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each header contains a name and a value, allowing you to set headers such as Authorization or Content-Type for the probe request.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the GET request. This sets a custom header for the readiness probe's HTTP request.
The HTTP path to request when performing the HTTP GET probe. For example, /healthz.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP probe request, either HTTP (default) or HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Must be a non-negative integer.
How often (in seconds) the readiness probe is executed by the kubelet. Minimum value is 1; defaults to 10 seconds per Kubernetes specification.
Minimum consecutive successes for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1; must be an integer greater than or equal to 1.
Specifies the TCP socket check to perform for the readiness probe. Defines the port (and optionally host) to test for a listening TCP socket.
The host name or IP address to connect to. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The TCP port to check for the readiness probe. This can be a numeric port (1-65535) or the name of a port defined in the container's ports.
The number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out and is considered failed. If the probe does not respond within this time, the container is not marked ready.
Defines the resource resize policy for the init container. Each item specifies the resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the restart policy to apply when the container's resources are resized.
The name of the resource (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies.
Defines the restart behavior when a container's requested resource is resized. Valid values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer'.

Resource requirements for the init container, specifying the minimum and maximum amounts of compute resources (e.g., CPU, memory) that the container can use. Typically includes 'requests' for the guaranteed amount and 'limits' for the maximum allowed.
Claims is a list of resource claims that the container requires. Each claim refers to a ResourceClaim object by name.
Name of the ResourceClaim resource that this container requests. The named ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of a ResourceClaimTemplate that is used to create a ResourceClaim for this container. This claim binds the container to the resources allocated from that template.

Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the init container. The map keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory, ephemeral-storage) and values are quantities such as "1" for CPU or "1Gi" for memory.
Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. Each map key is a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the value is the requested quantity as a string (e.g., '250m', '64Mi').
The restart policy for the init container. In Kubernetes, this field is used to configure init containers as sidecar containers, which run for the pod's lifetime.
The comparison operator used to evaluate whether a container's exit code matches the values specified in `exit_codes`. This determines when the associated restart policy rule applies.
The list of container exit codes to which this restart policy rule applies. When an init container exits with one of these codes, the rule's action is triggered.

SecurityContext specifies the security settings for the init container, including user/group IDs, Linux capabilities, SELinux options, and privilege level. These settings override the pod-level security context for this specific init container.

Controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When false, the container runs with the no_new_privs flag, preventing privilege escalation through setuid binaries or other mechanisms.

AppArmor profile to apply to the container. It is an object containing a `type` field (e.g., RuntimeDefault or Localhost) and an optional `localhostProfile` field that specifies the profile path when `type` is Localhost.
The name of the localhost AppArmor profile to use when the AppArmor profile type is 'Localhost'. This must be set if the type is 'Localhost' and ignored otherwise.
The type of AppArmor profile to apply. Accepts 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', or 'Unconfined'; when 'Localhost' is selected, the localhost_profile field must also be set.
Configures Linux capabilities for the container. The capabilities object can specify a list of capabilities to add (add) and a list to drop (drop).
List of Linux capabilities to add to the container's capability set. These augment the default capabilities granted to the container.
List of Linux capabilities to remove from the container's capability set. For example, 'ALL' drops all capabilities, or specify individual ones like 'NET_RAW'.
Run the container in privileged mode, giving it access to all host devices and capabilities. Defaults to false.

procMount sets the mount mode for the container's /proc filesystem. Supported values are 'Default' (the default, which masks certain sensitive kernel parameters) and 'Unmasked' (which exposes all of /proc). When not specified, the cluster default is used.
If true, the container's root filesystem is mounted as read-only, preventing write operations to the filesystem.
The GID (group ID) to run the container's main process as. When set, the container process runs with this group ID. If omitted, the group ID is derived from the container image.
Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. When set to true, the kubelet will refuse to start the container if it runs as UID 0 (root).
Specifies the UID (user ID) that the container process will run as. This overrides the user specified in the image metadata if set.
SELinux options for the init container. This object allows setting the SELinux user, role, type, and level labels applied to the container's process.
The SELinux level for the container, e.g., 's0:c1,c2'. This field is part of the SELinux options applied to the container's security context.
Role is a SELinux role label that applies to the container.
SELinux type label that applies to the container, used as part of the SELinux context.
The SELinux user label for the container's security context. This is one of the SELinux options (user, role, type, level) that define the SELinux context applied to the container.
Defines the seccomp profile for the container, specifying the profile type and optionally a custom localhost profile path.
Path to the seccomp profile on the node's filesystem. Required when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'.
The type of seccomp profile to use. Valid values are RuntimeDefault, Unconfined, and Localhost.
Windows-specific security options for the container, such as GMSACredentialSpecName, RunAsUserName, and HostProcess.

The GMSA (Group Managed Service Account) credential spec for the Windows container. This can be a path to a credential spec file or a JSON string containing the credential spec. Typically populated by the GMSA admission webhook when a credential spec name is provided.
The name of a GMSA credential spec to use for the pod's init container. This is part of Windows security options and must be paired with a corresponding config map.

HostProcess specifies whether the container should be run as a HostProcess container on Windows. When true, the container gains extended privileges to access the host's namespace (e.g., Windows services and registry). Defaults to false if not set.
The UserName in Windows to run the container process as. If unspecified, the default is the container's user.

Defines a probe that verifies whether the container has started properly. The kubelet will not restart the container until this probe succeeds, making it suitable for containers with slow startup times. This probe runs during the startup phase and stops after success.
Exec specifies the command to execute within the container for the startup probe. The probe succeeds if the command exits with status code 0.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container, with the working directory set to root ('/') in the container's filesystem. The command is exec'd directly, not run inside a shell, so shell constructs like pipes or redirects won't work unless you explicitly invoke a shell. An exit status of 0 is considered successful (healthy/ready), while non-zero is considered a failure.
Number of consecutive failures allowed for the startup probe before it gives up and marks the container as failed. The minimum value is 1; if not set, the default is 3.

The `grpc` field specifies the parameters for a gRPC-based health check performed on the container. It contains the `port` (required) on which the gRPC health check is served, and the optional `service` name to be checked.
The port number on the container that the gRPC health check will connect to. Must be between 1 and 65535.
The service name to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the default is the container name of the pod.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as the startup probe. Configures the HTTP request details such as path, port, host, scheme, and headers.
The host name or IP address to use when making the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' string fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request. The header name is case-insensitive.
The header value of the HTTP GET request for the startup probe.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. For example, '/healthz'.
Number or name of the port to access on the container. The number must be between 1 and 65535; the name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME.
The protocol (scheme) used for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are `HTTP` and `HTTPS`, with `HTTP` being the default if unspecified.
The scheme to use when connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. This delays the initial probe to allow the container to initialize before checking its status.
Specifies the number of seconds between each probe attempt. For startup probes, this controls how often the kubelet performs the startup check.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after a failure. For startup probes, this value must be 1.
A TCP socket probe that attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's IP address on a specified port, used to indicate whether the container has started.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for this TCP socket probe. If not set, defaults to the pod IP address.
Number or name of the TCP port to connect to for the probe. A numeric value must be in the range 1 to 65535; a name must be an IANA_SVC_NAME.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Must be greater than or equal to 1. Defaults to 1 second if not specified.
Whether the container runtime should allocate a buffer for standard input (stdin). Defaults to false.
If true, the container's stdin is closed immediately after the container starts, rather than remaining open. Only takes effect when `stdin` is also true.

Path at which the file containing the container's termination message is mounted or written. The message is intended to be a brief final status, such as an assertion failure message, and is exposed to the control plane when the container terminates. Defaults to /dev/termination-log if not set.

Specifies how the termination message from the container is read. Valid values are 'File' (default) to read from the file specified by termination_message_path, and 'FallbackToLogsOnError' to read from the container's log output if the container exits with error and the message file is empty.
Indicates whether to allocate a pseudo-TTY for the container. Defaults to false.
A list of volume devices to be exposed to the container. Each entry specifies a volume name and a device path inside the container, enabling raw block device access.
The path inside the container where the volume device is mounted.
Name of the volume to which this device is attached.
Defines the volume mounts for the init container. Each mount references a volume defined in the pod spec and specifies the mount path and options like read-only.
The path within the container at which the volume is mounted. Must be an absolute path and cannot contain ':'.
Controls how mounts are propagated from the host to the container and vice versa. Specifies whether and how volume mounts are shared between the container and other containers or the host.
Name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.volumes.
Specifies that the volume mount is read-only when true, allowing only read access to the mounted volume.
Specifies whether the read-only setting is applied recursively to all files and directories under the mount path. This differs from standard read_only, which does not propagate to sub-mounts.
Path within the volume from which the container's volume should be mounted. Defaults to the volume's root if not specified.
Similar to sub_path, but supports environment variable expansion using $(VAR_NAME) syntax to set the mount path dynamically.
Sets the working directory for the container's processes. If not specified, the default working directory from the container image is used.
The condition type that the readiness gate references. The pod will be considered ready only when all readiness gates have their corresponding condition set to True.
The name of the resource claim, which must be unique within the pod's resource claims. This name is used to reference the claim from containers in the pod spec.
Name of the ResourceClaim object to use. The referenced ResourceClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.

The name of a ResourceClaimTemplate that is used to dynamically create a ResourceClaim for this pod. This is part of the claim source; only one of resourceClaimName or resourceClaimTemplateName should be set.
Name of the resource claim, which must match an entry in the pod's spec.resourceClaims to make the claimed resource available to this container in the pod template.
Name of the sysctl parameter to set in the pod's security context.
The value to set for the sysctl parameter.
Effect indicates the taint effect to match. Empty means match all taint effects. Allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, and NoExecute.
The key of the taint that this toleration matches. When omitted with the Exists operator, the toleration matches all taints.
The operator used to match the taint key. Valid values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. If 'Equal', the value must also match. Defaults to 'Equal' if not specified.
The number of seconds a pod will tolerate a taint before being evicted, when the effect is NoExecute. If unset, the pod tolerates the taint indefinitely; zero or negative values evict immediately.
The value to match the toleration key. Used only when the operator is 'Equal'; ignored when operator is 'Exists'.
A label selector used to identify the set of pods that this topology spread constraint applies to. The constraint is evaluated only against pods whose labels match this selector.

match_expressions is a list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, or DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values, used to select pods based on their labels.
The label key that the selector operates on. Must be a valid Kubernetes label key, such as 'app' or 'tier'.
The operator represents the relationship between the label key and the values in the match expression. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.

The list of values for the label match expression. For the In and NotIn operators, this specifies the set of values the label key must or must not have. For Exists and DoesNotExist, the list must be empty.
A map of key-value pairs that must be matched by the pod's labels for this topology spread constraint label selector to apply. All specified labels must be present on the pod.

A list of pod label keys to select the pods for spreading calculation. Values from the incoming pod's labels with these keys are ANDed with the labelSelector to determine the group of existing pods over which spreading is calculated for the incoming pod. Keys not present in the incoming pod labels are ignored.
The maximum degree of skew allowed when distributing pods across topology domains. This value must be greater than 0.

The minimum number of eligible domains (e.g., zones) required for the topology spread constraint to consider global minimum. If the number of eligible domains is less than this value, the skew calculation uses a global minimum of 0; otherwise it has no effect.
Indicates how to treat a pod's node affinity when computing spread. Allowed values are 'Honor' (default), which considers node affinity, or 'Ignore', which ignores node affinity.

Indicates how to treat tainted nodes when calculating pod topology spread skew. Valid values are 'Ignore' (default) and 'Honor'. With 'Honor', nodes whose taints are not tolerated by the pod are excluded from topology spread calculations.

The key of node labels. Nodes that have the same value for this label are considered to be in the same topology domain, and the scheduler spreads pods across these domains to achieve balanced distribution.

Indicates how to deal with a pod if it doesn't satisfy the spread constraint. Allowed values are 'DoNotSchedule' (default) which prevents scheduling, and 'ScheduleAnyway' which allows scheduling and gives higher priority to nodes that minimize skew.
Represents an AWS Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume that can be mounted into the container. This configuration includes settings such as volume ID, filesystem type, partition, and read-only flag.
Filesystem type to mount for the AWS EBS volume (e.g., 'ext4'). Defaults to 'ext4' if not specified.
Partition on the AWS EBS volume to mount. If omitted, the first partition is mounted.
Mounts the AWS EBS volume as read-only. If not set, defaults to false (read-write).
The unique ID of the AWS EBS volume to be mounted. This field is required.
Configures an Azure Disk volume source, allowing the pod to mount an Azure data disk.
The Azure Data Disk caching mode. Allowed values: None, ReadOnly, ReadWrite. Defaults to None if not specified.
The name of the Azure data disk to be mounted. This field is required when using the Azure Disk volume type.
The URI of the Azure disk to mount. For unmanaged disks, this is the URI of the VHD blob; for managed disks, this is the resource ID.
Filesystem type to mount on the Azure disk. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host OS, e.g., 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Defaults to 'ext4' if unspecified.
Specifies the kind of Azure disk. Allowed values are 'Shared' (multiple blobs per disk), 'Dedicated' (single blob per disk), and 'Managed' (Azure managed disk). Defaults to 'Shared'.
Specifies whether the Azure Disk volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read-write).
Specifies whether the Azure File volume is mounted as read-only.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that contains the Azure Storage account name and key used to access the Azure file share.
The name of the Azure File share to be mounted.
CephFS volume source configuration. This defines a Ceph Filesystem mount that can be used by the pod.
List of Ceph monitor endpoints (host:port) for the Ceph filesystem. Required when using CephFS volume.
Path within CephFS to mount as the volume's root. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
Indicates whether the CephFS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read/write).
Path to the Ceph secret file (e.g., /etc/ceph/user.secret) containing the keyring for the Ceph user. This file is used for authentication when accessing the CephFS volume.
Reference to a Kubernetes secret that provides the Ceph client keyring for CephFS authentication. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the Kubernetes Secret used for CephFS authentication. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The CephFS user to authenticate as when mounting the volume. Defaults to 'admin' if not specified.
Represents a Cinder volume source in Kubernetes, used to mount an OpenStack block storage volume into the pod. This configuration is part of the pod template's volume definitions.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system, e.g. "ext4", "xfs", "ntfs". If unspecified, it is inferred to be "ext4".
Specifies whether the Cinder volume is mounted as read-only.

The secret_ref references a Kubernetes Secret that contains the authentication credentials (e.g., for OpenStack) required to access the Cinder volume. The referenced secret must be in the same namespace as the pod, and its name is provided in the object's 'name' field.
Name of the Kubernetes secret that holds the authentication credentials for the Cinder volume.
The unique identifier of the Cinder volume in OpenStack that will be mounted into the pod.
Represents a volume that is populated from a Kubernetes ConfigMap, making its data available as files in the pod.
Permissions mode (as octal integer) applied to files in the mounted ConfigMap volume. If not specified, defaults to 0644.

A list of mappings from keys in the referenced ConfigMap to file paths within the volume. When specified, only the listed keys are projected as files at the given paths; when omitted, all keys are projected as files named after the keys.
The key in the ConfigMap to project into the volume.
Mode is the optional Unix file permission bits (octal, e.g. 0400) for the config map item. Defaults to 0644 if omitted.
The relative file path within the volume where the value of the corresponding ConfigMap key is mounted. The path must not contain '..' segments and must not start with '/'.
Name of the ConfigMap to reference in this volume.

Indicates whether the ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. If set to true, the volume will be empty if the ConfigMap or keys are not found. If false (default), the pod will fail if the ConfigMap or keys are missing.

csi (object) configures a Container Storage Interface (CSI) volume source for this volume, allowing you to mount storage provided by a CSI driver. It includes fields such as driver, fsType, readOnly, nodePublishSecretRef, and volumeAttributes.
The name of the CSI driver that will handle the volume. This field is required and must match the name of a CSI driver installed on the cluster.

The filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Examples include 'ext4', 'xfs', and 'ntfs'. If not specified, the default filesystem type of the volume is used.
A reference to a Secret object containing credentials for the CSI driver to use when publishing the volume on the node.
The name of the secret in the pod's namespace that provides credentials for the CSI node publish operation.
Indicates whether the CSI volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is mounted read-only; otherwise it is mounted read-write.
Represents additional attributes as key-value pairs to pass to the CSI driver.
Configures a downwardAPI volume, which exposes pod metadata (such as labels, annotations, and other fields) to the container via files.
Specifies the default file permissions (mode bits) for files created in the downward API volume. This is an optional numeric value (octal, e.g., 0644) that defaults to 0644 if not set.
Items is the list of downward API volume files. Each item defines a path and the field to project into that path.
Selects a field from the pod's metadata or status to expose via the downward API. This object typically contains apiVersion and fieldPath to identify the specific pod field.
The version of the schema that the field path refers to, defaults to 'v1' when not specified.

Path to the pod field whose value should be exposed, such as metadata.name, metadata.labels, metadata.annotations, or spec.serviceAccountName. This selects the specific field from the pod's metadata or spec.
Mode is the file permission bits (in octal) for the file, e.g., 0644. If not specified, the default is 0644.
Path within the volume at which the downward API value is exposed as a file.

Selects a container resource field (e.g., limits.cpu, requests.memory, limits.ephemeral-storage) to expose as a file via the downward API. The object includes an optional containerName and a required resource string; only resource limits and requests are supported.

Name of the container for which the resource field is exposed via the downward API. Required when the field references a container resource (e.g., limits.cpu, requests.memory), and must match a container name in the pod spec.

The divisor for the resource value exposed via the downward API. This is a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1', '1Ki') that the resource value is divided by before being presented. Defaults to '1' if unspecified.
The resource field name to select from the container's requests or limits, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'.

Configures an emptyDir volume, a temporary directory that is created when the Pod is scheduled and exists as long as the Pod runs. This object can specify settings such as the medium (e.g., 'Memory' for tmpfs) and size limits.
The medium specifies the storage medium for the emptyDir volume. If unset, the volume uses the node's default filesystem (disk). Set to 'Memory' to back the volume with RAM instead of disk storage.
The size limit for the emptyDir volume, specified as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1Gi', '512M'). When set, the total storage used by the emptyDir volume is restricted to this amount.
Configures an ephemeral volume source, which is handled by a generic storage driver and features a dynamic provisioner. This field is mutually exclusive with other volume source options.
The volume claim template that will be used to create a PersistentVolumeClaim for this ephemeral volume. The template's spec, such as storage class and size, determines the volume characteristics.
Standard Kubernetes object metadata (e.g., labels, annotations, name) for the dynamically created PersistentVolumeClaim from this ephemeral volume's claim template.

A map of string keys and values that stores arbitrary non-identifying metadata attached to the volume claim template. These annotations are applied to the PersistentVolumeClaim created from this template.
The creation timestamp of the object, in RFC3339 format (e.g., 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z).
Number of seconds allowed for this object to gracefully terminate before it is removed from the system. Only set when deletionTimestamp is also set, and may only be shortened.
The timestamp when the object is being deleted, in RFC3339 format. This is set by Kubernetes when a deletion is requested and is used for garbage collection.
A list of finalizer names. When non-empty, the object will not be deleted until all finalizers are removed. Kubernetes will only remove the object from etcd after all finalizers are cleared.
Specifies a prefix to generate a unique name for the volume claim template when a name is not provided. The server will generate a unique name by appending a random suffix to this prefix.

The generation of the VolumeClaimTemplate metadata. This is a system-generated numeric value representing the object's generation, used for internal reconciliation and optimistic concurrency. It is read-only and cannot be set by the user.

Map of string keys and values that will be attached to the metadata of the PersistentVolumeClaim created from this volume claim template. These labels can be used for selection and organization of the generated resources.

A list of managed fields, as defined by Kubernetes. Each entry tracks a controller's management of the object's fields, including the manager name, operation, api version, and fields involved. This is used for field ownership and conflict detection.
The API version of the resource that this managed field entry applies to.
The type of the managed fields entry, indicating the format of the FieldsV1 field. For example, "FieldsV1".
fields_v1 holds the JSON-serialized set of fields managed by this manager, represented as a FieldsV1 structure encoding field paths and values.
The name of the manager (e.g., a controller or client) that last modified the fields. It identifies the workflow managing these fields.
The operation performed on the managed field, such as 'Apply' or 'Update'.
The subresource of the object that the managed fields entry applies to, such as 'status' for status updates or empty string for the main resource.
The timestamp indicating when the managed field entry was last updated, in RFC3339 format.
The namespace for the volume claim template's metadata. For ephemeral volumes, this is typically empty because the persistent volume claim is created in the same namespace as the pod.

A list of owner references that identify the owning objects of this resource. Each reference contains `api_version`, `kind`, `name`, `uid`, and optional `controller` and `block_owner_deletion` fields, establishing ownership and garbage collection behavior.
The API version of the referent object (e.g., 'v1', 'apps/v1').

If true, the owner of this ownerReference cannot be deleted until this dependent object is removed. This flag is used by the Kubernetes garbage collector to honor the ownerReference as a blocking deletion dependency.
Indicates whether the referenced owner is the managing controller of the owning object. When true, this owner reference points to the primary controller responsible for the object's lifecycle.
The kind of the referenced owner object, such as 'Pod' or 'ReplicaSet'.
