The name of the owner object referenced by this owner reference. In Kubernetes, an OwnerReference contains the name of the owning resource.
The UID of the owner object referenced by this owner reference.
The version of the object used by Kubernetes for optimistic concurrency control. This field is set by the server and changes on every update, enabling clients to detect concurrent modifications.
A system-generated unique identifier for the object, set by the Kubernetes API server. It is read-only and used to distinguish the resource from all others in the cluster.
Spec of the PersistentVolumeClaim template, defining desired characteristics such as access modes, storage class, and resource requirements for the ephemeral volume's underlying PVC.

A list of access modes for the persistent volume claim. Valid values are 'ReadWriteOnce', 'ReadOnlyMany', 'ReadWriteMany', and 'ReadWriteOncePod' (when supported by the cluster). Access modes define how the volume can be mounted on nodes and pods.
data_source specifies the source to populate the volume, such as a PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot reference. It is an object containing the kind, name, and API group of the data source.
The API group of the resource being referenced as the data source for the volume claim template. For example, 'snapshot.storage.k8s.io' for a VolumeSnapshot.
The kind of the data source resource, for example 'PersistentVolumeClaim'.
The name of the data source object referenced by the volume claim template. This identifies the specific resource (e.g., a PersistentVolumeClaim) that provides the data for the ephemeral volume.

data_source_ref is a reference to a data source (such as a PersistentVolumeClaim, VolumeSnapshot, or other custom resource) from which the ephemeral volume's underlying persistent volume claim is populated, as defined in the volumeClaimTemplate spec.
The API group of the referenced resource's kind. For resources in the core API group, this is empty; for others, it must be set (e.g., 'snapshot.storage.k8s.io').
The kind of the referenced data source object, such as 'PersistentVolumeClaim' or a custom resource kind.
The name of the Kubernetes resource (such as a PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot) referenced as the data source for the ephemeral volume claim template.
Namespace of the referenced object in the dataSourceRef. If omitted, it defaults to the namespace of the PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeClaimTemplate using this reference.
Specifies the storage resource requirements (requests and limits) for the ephemeral volume claim, such as storage size.

The maximum amount of compute resources (e.g., CPU, memory) allowed for the ephemeral volume claim. Keys are resource names and values are Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., '500m', '2Gi'). More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/.

Requests describes the minimum amount of resources required for the ephemeral volume's underlying PersistentVolumeClaim. Each key is a resource name (e.g., 'storage') and the value is a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '5Gi').
Selector is a label query over PersistentVolumes that can be bound to this claim. It constrains the set of volumes that may be selected, typically using matchLabels and matchExpressions.
A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and optional values. All requirements are ANDed together to form the selector.
The label key that the selector matches against. This is the key of a label that must be present (or absent, depending on the operator) on the target resource.
The operator to use for the label selector expression. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values for the selector expression. Required when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'; must be empty when the operator is 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist'.
A map of key-value pairs that must be matched by the labels of the resource being selected. Only resources with all specified labels are selected.
The name of the StorageClass used for this volume claim. When specified, the cluster provisions the ephemeral volume using this StorageClass; if omitted, the default StorageClass is used.
Name of the VolumeAttributesClass to use for this persistent volume claim. If not specified, the default VolumeAttributesClass is used.
Defines the volume mode for the ephemeral volume claim. Allowed values are 'Filesystem' (default) and 'Block'.
The name of the PersistentVolume to bind this claim to. Used to pre-bind the claim to a specific volume; if not set, the claim remains unbound until a volume is provisioned.

Defines a Fibre Channel (FC) volume source for a Kubernetes pod, allowing specification of FC-specific parameters such as target worldwide names (WWNs), logical unit number (LUN), filesystem type, and read-only mode.
Filesystem type to mount for the Fibre Channel volume, e.g., ext4 or xfs. Must be supported by the host operating system.
lun is the logical unit number (LUN) of the Fibre Channel target device. This field is required and must be an integer between 0 and 255.
Indicates whether the Fibre Channel volume is mounted as read-only.
The list of Fibre Channel target WWNs (World Wide Names) for this volume. Each WWN is a unique identifier for a Fibre Channel target port.
List of Fibre Channel world wide identifiers (WWIDs) that uniquely identify the target volume. Either this list or a combination of targetWWNs and lun must be provided, but not both.
Configures a volume backed by FlexVolume, an out-of-tree volume plugin that uses a driver to mount storage.
Driver is the name of the flex volume driver to use for this volume.
Filesystem type to be mounted (e.g., ext4, xfs) for this flexVolume volume.
A map of key-value pairs that are passed to the FlexVolume driver. The driver interprets these options according to its own conventions.
readOnly is a boolean flag that indicates whether the flexVolume is mounted read-only. Defaults to false.
Optional reference to a secret in the pod's namespace that provides credentials or other sensitive data to the flexVolume driver. The secret must exist before the pod starts.
Name of the Secret resource that provides additional configuration for the FlexVolume driver. The Secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
Flocker volume source. Configures a Flocker volume to be mounted into the pod, allowing the container to access a Flocker dataset.
The name of the dataset (as stored in Flocker's metadata) to mount. One of dataset_name or dataset_uuid must be specified to identify the Flocker dataset.
The UUID of the Flocker dataset to mount. This cannot be set if dataset_name is specified.
Represents a Google Compute Engine Persistent Disk (GCE PD) volume source. This configures the PD name, filesystem type, partition, and read-only mode for mounting into the pod.
The filesystem type to mount on the GCE persistent disk. If not specified, the filesystem type of the underlying disk is used. Common values include ext4, xfs, and ext3.
The partition number on the GCE persistent disk. If 0, the entire disk is used.
The name of the GCE Persistent Disk (PD) to attach as a volume.
Specifies whether the GCE persistent disk volume is mounted as read-only. When set to true, the volume is read-only; when false (default), it is read-write.
Configures a git repository as a volume source. This object specifies the repository URL, the revision to check out, and the target directory within the volume.

Target directory name within the volume where the git repository will be placed. Must not contain or start with '..'. If set to '.', the volume root becomes the git repository; otherwise, the repository is cloned into the specified subdirectory.
The URL of the Git repository to clone into the volume.
The git revision (commit hash) to check out in the Git repository volume.
Configuration for a GlusterFS volume source, used to mount a GlusterFS volume into the pod. This block defines the details of the GlusterFS mount.
Name of the endpoints object that contains the IP addresses of the GlusterFS nodes. This is required for a GlusterFS volume.
Path is the Glusterfs volume path, identifying the specific volume to mount from the GlusterFS cluster.
If true, the GlusterFS volume is mounted as read-only. If false or omitted, the volume is mounted as read-write.
Configures a hostPath volume, which mounts a file or directory from the host node's filesystem into the pod. This allows the pod to access the host's filesystem.
The path on the host node to mount into the pod. Must be an absolute path.
Type of the host path. Must be one of: '', Directory, DirectoryOrCreate, File, FileOrCreate, Socket, CharDevice, BlockDevice. For more details, refer to the Kubernetes documentation.
The 'image' block defines an image volume source, which mounts an OCI image as an ephemeral volume. This volume type includes configurations such as the image reference and pull policy.
Specifies the image pull policy for the image volume source. Allowed values: Always, Never, IfNotPresent. If unset, defaults to Always.
The image reference for the image volume, e.g., 'nginx:latest'. This is the container image to be mounted as a volume.
Configuration for an iSCSI volume source, used to mount an iSCSI target as a volume in the pod.
Enables CHAP authentication for the iSCSI discovery session. When set to true, CHAP authentication is required for target discovery.
Indicates whether CHAP authentication is enabled for the iSCSI session. When true, CHAP authentication is used for the session.
Filesystem type to mount for the iSCSI volume (e.g., 'ext4', 'xfs', 'ntfs'). If unspecified, it is inferred to be 'ext4'.
The custom iSCSI initiator name. If not specified, the system default initiator name is used.
The iSCSI Qualified Name (IQN) of the target. This uniquely identifies the iSCSI target that the volume connects to.
Name of the iSCSI interface. Defaults to 'default' if not specified.
The iSCSI target LUN (Logical Unit Number) to mount. This is a required field for iSCSI volumes.
A list of additional iSCSI portals (IP addresses or hostnames) to connect to if the primary target portal is unreachable.
Mounts the iSCSI volume as read-only. Defaults to false, meaning the volume is mounted read-write.

Reference to a Kubernetes Secret that provides CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI target. The secret must contain the keys 'node.session.auth.username' and 'node.session.auth.password' (or similar) as required by the iSCSI configuration.
Name of the secret that contains the CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI target. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The IP address or hostname of the iSCSI target portal (e.g., 192.168.0.1:3260). This field is required to connect to the iSCSI target.
NFS (Network File System) volume source configuration. This block defines how an NFS export is mounted into the pod, including the server address, exported path, and read-only access settings.
The NFS export path on the server. It specifies the directory on the NFS server that is mounted into the pod.
Indicates whether the NFS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
The hostname or IP address of the NFS server. This field is required when configuring an NFS volume.

Represents a PersistentVolumeClaim volume source that mounts a Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaim into the pod. This field references an existing PersistentVolumeClaim by name to provide storage to the pod.
The name of the PersistentVolumeClaim to reference as the volume source. This claim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
If true, the persistent volume claim is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Represents a Photon Controller persistent disk volume source, allowing a Photon persistent disk to be mounted into the pod.
Filesystem type to mount for the Photon persistent disk volume, e.g., 'ext4'. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system.
ID that identifies the Photon Controller persistent disk.
Block specifying a Portworx volume to attach to the pod. It defines the volume source configuration for a Portworx persistent volume.
Filesystem type to mount the Portworx volume, e.g. "ext4" or "xfs". Defaults to "ext4" if unspecified.
If true, the volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
The unique ID of the Portworx volume to be mounted.

Projected volume source that maps several existing volume sources (such as secrets, config maps, downward API, and service account tokens) into the same directory. The projected volume is defined by a list of sources along with optional default mode permissions.
Specifies the default file permission mode (in octal) for files within the projected volume. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 or decimal between 0 and 511; defaults to 0644 if unset.
List of projections that populate the projected volume. Each entry can reference a secret, config map, downward API, or service account token.
Configures a projected volume source that supplies a ClusterTrustBundle. This allows pods to consume CA trust bundles from a cluster-scoped trust bundle resource.
A label selector that filters the ClusterTrustBundles to be projected into the pod. Only bundles matching this selector are included.

A list of label selector requirements. Each item defines a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values to filter ClusterTrustBundle resources by their labels.
The label key that this match expression applies to in the label selector.
Operator represents the key's relationship to a set of values or existence. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
List of values that the label key must match according to the operator. For operators 'In' and 'NotIn', this must contain at least one value; for 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty.
A map of key-value pairs used to select ClusterTrustBundle resources. Only bundles whose labels match all specified key-value pairs are included in the projected volume.
The name of the ClusterTrustBundle resource to project into the volume.

Optional specifies whether the projected ClusterTrustBundle is optional. If true, the volume will not fail to mount if the referenced ClusterTrustBundle is unavailable; if false or unset, the mount will fail if the bundle is missing.
Relative path inside the projected volume where the ClusterTrustBundle contents are written.
The name of the signer whose certificates are selected for the projected ClusterTrustBundle.
Specifies a ConfigMap as a source for the projected volume. This object defines the ConfigMap to use and how its data is exposed, including optional item mappings.

Optional list of mappings to select specific keys from the referenced ConfigMap and define the file path for each. When items is specified, only the listed keys are projected; when omitted, all keys are projected as files named after the key.
The key within the referenced ConfigMap's data to project into the volume. This must match an existing key in the ConfigMap's data map.
The file permission mode (in octal) for the config map item when projected into the volume.
Relative path of the file to map the config map key to within the volume.
The name of the ConfigMap that provides the data for this projected volume source. This must match the name of a ConfigMap in the same namespace as the pod.
Specify whether the ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. If set to true, the volume does not fail when the ConfigMap or its keys are missing.

Configuration for a downward API volume source within a projected volume. This allows the downward API to expose pod and container metadata (such as labels, annotations, or resource limits) as files in the volume.
Optional list of items, each defining a file path and a field reference to expose from the Downward API into the projected volume. If omitted, all Downward API fields are exposed.
field_ref is a reference to a field in the pod's metadata or status to be exposed as a file, using the format apiVersion and fieldPath (e.g., metadata.name, status.podIP).
The API version of the schema that the fieldPath refers to, typically 'v1'.
The path to the field on the Pod to select, such as metadata.name or spec.nodeName. This must be a valid Pod field path.
Optional mode bits for the projected file, as an octal permission value (e.g., 0644) or its decimal equivalent (0-511). Defaults to 0644 if not set.
The relative path within the projected volume where the Downward API item's value is mounted. This path is used to create the file that exposes the referenced field or resource.
Selects a resource field (e.g., requests.cpu or limits.memory) from a container, using a ResourceFieldSelector. It defines which resource value to expose and how to format it via the divisor.
The name of the container whose resource (e.g., limits.cpu, requests.memory) is to be referenced. Required when the resource field is a container-level resource, as opposed to a pod-level resource.

The divisor for the resource field value. This is an optional string representing a quantity (e.g., '1m' for millicores, '1Mi' for mebibytes) by which the resource field value is divided. Defaults to '1'.
The name of the container resource to expose via the downward API, such as 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory'.
The numeric user ID (UID) that will own the file generated from this downward API item. If not specified, the file's owner defaults to the process's UID.
The path in the projected volume where the certificate chain file will be mounted.
The relative path within the projected volume where the pod's certificate bundle (including the certificate and private key) will be mounted.
The path within the projected volume where the private key for the pod certificate is mounted.
Maximum validity period of the projected pod certificate, in seconds.
The name of the signer for the certificate request. This field maps to the Kubernetes `signerName` field in the pod certificate projection.
SecretProjection configures a Secret to be projected into the volume. It allows specifying the secret name and optional items (keys) to expose.

A list of key-to-path mappings for the secret data. Each item specifies a key from the secret and the corresponding file path in the projected volume. If unspecified, all keys from the secret are projected.
The key in the secret data to include in the projected volume.
Permission mode bits for the file, specified as an octal number between 0000 and 0777 (0 to 511 decimal). If omitted, the default mode of the projected volume source is used.
The relative path of the file to which the secret key is mapped within the projected volume. Must not be an absolute path, must not contain '..', and must not start with '..'.
The name of the Secret object to reference for this projected volume source.
Specifies whether the secret must be defined. If set to true, the secret may not exist and the volume will still be populated with existing keys; if false (default), the secret must exist.

Specifies a projected service account token source, which injects a Kubernetes service account token into the volume. This is commonly used for workload identity, with configurable audience, expiration, and mount path.
The intended audience for the token. The recipient of the token will verify that the audience matches its own identifier. Defaults to the API server's audience.
The requested duration of validity for the service account token, in seconds. Must be at least 600 and defaults to 3600.
Path is the relative path of the service account token file within the projected volume. The token will be mounted at this path relative to the volume mount point.
A Quobyte volume source, used to mount a Quobyte volume into the pod. The configuration includes details such as the Quobyte registry, volume name, and whether the volume is read-only.
The group to map the volume access to. If not specified, the virtual volume's group is used.
Marks the Quobyte volume as read-only. When true, the volume is mounted without write access.
The host:port (or comma-separated list of host:port pairs) of the Quobyte registry services to contact.
The tenant name for the Quobyte volume. This specifies the tenant in the Quobyte cluster that owns the volume.
User to map volume access to. Defaults to the service account user.
The name of the Quobyte volume to mount.

The rbd volume source configures a Ceph RBD (RADOS Block Device) volume to be mounted into the pod. It contains parameters for connecting to a Ceph cluster, such as monitors, image, pool, and authentication details.
Filesystem type to mount, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. If unspecified, it is implicitly inferred to be ext4.
The RADOS image name used by the RBD volume. This is a required field for RBD volumes and specifies the image to mount.
Path to the keyring file containing the Ceph authentication key for this RBD volume. Defaults to /etc/ceph/keyring if not specified.
A list of Ceph monitor addresses (host:port) for the RBD volume.
The Ceph pool name for the RBD image. If omitted, the default pool 'rbd' is used.
If set to true, the RBD volume is mounted as read-only, so the pod cannot write to it.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret in the same namespace that contains the Ceph keyring for RBD authentication.
Name of the Kubernetes Secret that contains the authentication credentials (e.g., keyring) for the Ceph RBD volume.
The rados user name. If not provided, defaults to admin.
ScaleIO volume source configuration. Defines how to attach and mount a ScaleIO persistent volume to the pod.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Defaults to 'xfs'.
The IP address or hostname of the ScaleIO API gateway. This is a required field for ScaleIO volumes.
The name of the ScaleIO protection domain where the storage pool for this volume is located. This is used to identify the domain from which the volume is provisioned.
Whether the ScaleIO volume is mounted as read-only.

Reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the ScaleIO storage account credentials (username and password) used to authenticate with the ScaleIO gateway. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the Pod.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret that contains the ScaleIO credentials. This is a LocalObjectReference to a secret in the same namespace as the pod.
Enable SSL/TLS for communication with the ScaleIO storage backend.
Indicates whether the storage for a volume should be ThickProvisioned or ThinProvisioned. Defaults to ThinProvisioned.
The Storage Pool associated with the ScaleIO protection domain. This is the name of the storage pool from which the volume is provisioned.
The name of the ScaleIO storage system.
The name of the ScaleIO storage volume to mount. This corresponds to the volumeName field in the ScaleIO volume source.

Configuration block for a Kubernetes Secret volume source. It references a Secret by name and can optionally specify items (key-to-path pairs) to expose, along with default permissions and optional behavior.

defaultMode sets the permissions on files created by the secret volume. It must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 or a decimal value between 0 and 511 (JSON requires decimal), and defaults to 0644.
A list of key-to-path mappings. Each item specifies a key from the secret data and the relative path where the key's value should be mounted as a file in the volume.
The key to project from the Secret. The key must be a valid secret key and must exist in the referenced Secret.
The permissions mode for the secret file, represented as an octal integer (e.g., 0644). If not set, the default is 0644.
The relative path within the volume where the secret's key is exposed as a file. This path is relative to the volume mount point.
If set to true, the secret will be treated as optional, allowing the volume to be mounted even if the secret does not exist. Defaults to false, requiring the secret to exist.
Name of the Secret to mount as a volume. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The storageos block configures a StorageOS volume source. It allows setting parameters such as volume name, namespace, filesystem type, read-only flag, and secret reference.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. For example, ext4, xfs, or ntfs.
Whether the StorageOS volume is mounted as read-only.
A reference to a secret that contains the credentials needed to access the StorageOS API. This is used to authenticate with the StorageOS cluster when mounting the volume.
The name of the Kubernetes Secret that contains the StorageOS API credentials. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The StorageOS volume name. This must be unique within the StorageOS cluster.
The namespace within the StorageOS system where the volume is located. This identifies the StorageOS namespace for the referenced volume.
Defines a vSphere volume source to mount a vSphere datastore volume into the pod. This is a volume configuration for using vSphere storage in the pod template.
Filesystem type to mount for the vSphere volume, such as ext4, xfs, etc. If not specified, the default is 'ext4'.
The vSphere Storage Policy Based Management (SPBM) policy ID applied to the virtual disk. If specified, the volume is created according to this storage policy.
The name of the vSphere storage policy to apply to the volume. When specified, the volume is provisioned according to the named storage policy.
The path of the vSphere volume in the datastore, as used in the Kubernetes vSphereVolumeSource.

kubernetes_core_replication_controller.m.text: The version of the Kubernetes API that the manager used to manage the fields.
The type of fields in the managed fields entry. For Kubernetes managed fields, this is typically 'FieldsV1'.
fields_v1 is a JSON representation of the fields owned by the manager, in the Kubernetes FieldsV1 format.
The name of the manager that last applied changes, identifying the component responsible for the update.
The operation that was performed, which led to this managed fields entry being created. Valid values are 'Apply' and 'Update'.
The subresource of the managed field entry, such as 'status'. It indicates which subresource the managed fields apply to.
Time is the timestamp of the last update to this managed field entry, formatted as a string in RFC3339.
The API version of the referent, e.g., 'v1'.
If true, prevents the owner from being deleted until this dependent object is also deleted, when the owner has the 'foregroundDeletion' finalizer. Defaults to false.
Indicates whether the owner reference is a controller. When true, this reference is the managing controller for the resource.
The kind of the referenced owner object, e.g., 'ReplicaSet' or 'StatefulSet'.
The name of the Kubernetes object that owns this resource, as referenced in the ownerReferences metadata.
The UID of the owner object. This is the unique identifier (UUID) assigned by the Kubernetes API to the referenced object, used to unambiguously identify it.

kubernetes_core_replication_controller.s.text: The API version of the manager that last modified the object's fields.
The type of fields stored in the managed fields entry, indicating the serialization format used for the fields. In the Kubernetes API, this is typically 'FieldsV1'.
A dynamic object containing the raw JSON representation of the fields managed by this manager, stored in Kubernetes' FieldsV1 (Trie-like) format.
The name of the manager (e.g., a controller, operator, or client such as 'kubectl') responsible for the last modification of this managed field entry.
The operation type that this managed field entry represents. Valid values are "Apply", "Update", and "Delete".
The subresource this managed field entry applies to. An empty string indicates the main resource, while values like 'status' or 'scale' identify specific subresources.
Time is the timestamp of the operation that modified the object's fields, represented in RFC3339 format.
The API version of the referenced owner object, as defined in Kubernetes OwnerReference.
If true, the owner of this reference is blocked from deletion until this reference is removed. Defaults to false. Requires delete permission on the owner to set to true.
If true, this owner reference points to the managing controller of the resource.
Kind of the owner object referenced by this owner reference, such as 'ReplicationController' or 'Deployment'.
The name of the owner object being referenced. This field identifies the specific resource that owns the dependent object within the same namespace.
The UID of the owner object referenced by this owner reference, used to uniquely identify the owner in the API.
The node selector term that defines the preferred scheduling preference. It contains matchExpressions and matchFields to specify node selection constraints for this preferred term.

A list of node selector requirements that define label-based constraints for node affinity. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values; all requirements must be satisfied for the node to be selected.
The Kubernetes label key for the node affinity requirement. This key must match a label key on the node for the preference to apply.
The operator used to compare the node label with the specified values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.
A list of string values for a node affinity match expression. These are the label values that must match (depending on the operator, such as In or NotIn) for the preferred scheduling rule to apply.
A list of node selector requirements that match against node fields (e.g., metadata.name). Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values.
The key of the node field that this match expression evaluates, such as a node label or field path.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and the set of values for the match field. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.
The list of values used with the operator for the node field matching condition. For example, with the In operator, the node's field must match one of these values; with NotIn, it must match none.
The weight for the preferred node affinity term. Must be an integer between 1 and 100, with higher values indicating greater preference.

A list of node selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a label key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt), and an optional list of values. These requirements are ANDed together to match nodes during scheduling.
The label key that the node selector term matches against. The match expression is evaluated against the value of this key on the node.

The operator specifies the relationship between the key and the set of values for a node selector requirement. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, and also Gt and Lt for numeric value comparisons.
The list of values that the node selector expression matches against node labels, used together with the operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist) to define the affinity rule.
A list of node selector requirements that match on node fields (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.labels) as opposed to label keys. Used in node affinity terms to restrict nodes by their fields.
The key of the node field to match, such as 'metadata.name' or 'metadata.uid'.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and the set of values. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.
Values is an array of string values. If the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn', the values array must be non-empty. If the operator is 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', the values array must be empty.
A term that defines a set of pods and a topology key for a preferred pod affinity rule, specifying which pods to match and the topology domain to consider for soft scheduling constraints.

A label selector used to identify the set of pods to which the pod affinity/anti-affinity rule applies. It matches pods based on their labels, and supports both matchLabels and matchExpressions as defined in the Kubernetes LabelSelector type.
A list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed, and each requirement defines a key, an operator, and an optional set of values.
The label key that the match expression applies to. This key must be present on the pod's labels for the expression to match.
The operator defines the relationship between the label key and the values. It must be one of 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', or 'DoesNotExist'.
A list of values to match against the key. Must be non-empty for the In and NotIn operators, and must be empty for the Exists and DoesNotExist operators.
A map of key/value pairs used to select target pods by their labels. The affinity term applies only if the target pod has all the specified label keys and their corresponding values match.
A label selector used to select the namespaces that the pod affinity/anti-affinity term applies to. If specified, the term only matches pods in the selected namespaces.

A list of label selector requirements used to match namespaces. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values, and is used to filter namespaces by their labels.
The label key that the selector matches against. Must be a valid Kubernetes label key (e.g., 'app' or 'example.com/role').
The operator used to match the namespace's labels. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist, with In and NotIn requiring the values field and Exists/DoesNotExist requiring empty values.
values is a list of label values that the key must match. For operators In and NotIn, values must be provided; for Exists and DoesNotExist, values must be empty.
Map of label keys and values to select namespaces. Only namespaces with all specified labels match this selector.
Specifies the namespaces that the label selector applies to. If not set, it defaults to the namespace of the pod where the affinity rule is defined.

The node label key that defines the topology domain for pod affinity/anti-affinity, such as 'kubernetes.io/hostname' or 'failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone'. Pods are grouped by the value of this label on nodes.
Weight associated with the corresponding pod affinity term, in the range 1-100. Higher weights give the term greater influence during scheduling when multiple terms are considered.
Label selector used to identify the set of pods that the affinity rule applies to. It supports matchLabels and matchExpressions for selection criteria.

A list of label selector requirements. Each item specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. These expressions form the label selector used to match pods for the affinity rule.
The label key that the selector operates on. For example, in a match expression like 'environment in (production, staging)', 'environment' is the key.
operator specifies the relationship between the label key and the given values. Valid values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'.
A list of string values that the label key must match. Required when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'; must be empty for 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist'.
A map of keys and values used to select pods whose labels match all specified pairs, as part of the label selector for required pod affinity.

A list of label keys to be removed from the incoming pod's labels when evaluating this pod affinity/anti-affinity term. If the incoming pod has any of these keys, those labels are excluded from the label selector, preventing them from affecting the match.
A label selector used to identify namespaces to which the pod affinity/anti-affinity rule applies. It specifies which namespaces' pods are considered for the matching requirement.
A list of label selector requirements for selecting namespaces. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values.
The label key that the selector operates on. This is the key of a label on a namespace that must match according to the operator and values specified in the same match expression.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of values for the namespace label selector. When the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn', this list must be non-empty; when 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist', it must be empty.
A map of label keys to values that the target namespace must have. This label selector is used to select namespaces for the pod affinity rule's namespace selector.
A list of namespaces to which the label selector applies. If omitted, only the namespace of the Pod is considered.

The key of the node label that defines the topology domain for the pod affinity rule. Pods are considered to be in the same topology domain if they are on nodes with the same value for this label (e.g., 'kubernetes.io/hostname').

This block defines the pod affinity term, specifying the set of pods and the topology key used to evaluate the preferred anti-affinity rule. It contains a label selector, namespaces, and topology key.
A label query over the pods that determines which pods the anti-affinity rule applies to. Supports matchLabels (exact key/value pairs) and matchExpressions (set-based requirements).

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement contains a key, an operator (In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values for In and NotIn operators. All requirements are logically ANDed together.
The label key that the selector applies to. The match expression will evaluate the values of this key on the resource's labels.
The operator to apply to the label key and values in the match expression. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist.

A list of values that the label key must match, according to the operator defined in the match expression (e.g., for In or NotIn). Must be empty for operators that do not require values, such as Exists or DoesNotExist.

match_labels is a map of key-value pairs that must be matched by the pod's labels for the label selector to be true. All labels in the map must be present on the pod, and the values must match exactly.

MatchLabelKeys is a list of pod label keys used to select the pods over which affinity matching is performed. These label keys, combined with the labelSelector, determine eligible pods. This field is alpha-level and requires the MatchLabelKeysInPodAffinity feature gate.
A label selector used to select the namespaces to which this pod affinity/anti-affinity term applies. If specified, the affinity term applies to pods running in namespaces that match this selector.
A list of label selector requirements. The requirements are ANDed. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values, used to match namespaces for this pod affinity term.
The label key that the match expression operates on. In a namespace selector, this key is matched against namespace labels using the specified operator and optional values.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.
A list of values that the label key must match when the operator is In or NotIn. Must be empty for Exists or DoesNotExist operators.
A map of key-value pairs that must match the labels on the namespace. All requirements are ANDed together.
A list of namespaces to include in the pod affinity/anti-affinity evaluation. If not specified, the namespace of the current object is used.
The key of node labels that defines the topology domain. The scheduler uses this to group nodes into domains for spreading or co-location of pods.
The weight associated with the pod anti-affinity term, used to calculate the overall preference. Must be an integer between 1 and 100.

Label selector used to identify the set of pods that this pod anti-affinity term applies to. It selects pods whose labels match the specified expressions, and the anti-affinity rule will avoid scheduling on nodes that contain any of those selected pods.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a set of values. This is used to define affinity/anti-affinity pod selection rules.
The label key that the match expression applies to. This key is used to select resources based on the value of the specified label.
The operator that defines the relationship between the label key and the set of values in a match expression. Allowed values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'.
A list of values that the key must match. Required when the operator is In or NotIn; must be empty for Exists or DoesNotExist.
A map of key/value pairs that defines the exact labels that must be present on a pod for the anti-affinity rule to match. All specified labels must match for the selector to apply.
List of pod label keys. When specified, the anti-affinity selector only matches pods that have the same values for these label keys as the pod being scheduled.

A list of label keys. When set, the required pod anti-affinity rule only matches pods whose label values for these keys differ from the incoming pod's label values, preventing co-location with pods that have different values for the specified labels.
A label selector to filter namespaces for the anti-affinity rule. Only pods in namespaces matching this selector are considered when determining scheduling constraints.

A list of label selector requirements used to select namespaces. Each requirement contains a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and an optional list of values. The namespace selector matches if all requirements are satisfied.
The label key that the selector matches on. Used to select namespaces by their labels for pod anti-affinity scheduling.
Specifies the relationship between the key and the set of values. Valid values are 'In', 'NotIn', 'Exists', and 'DoesNotExist'.
A list of string values for the namespace selector match expression. Required when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'; must be empty when the operator is 'Exists' or 'DoesNotExist'.
A map of label keys to values used to select namespaces for the pod anti-affinity rule. Only namespaces matching all specified label values are included in the required anti-affinity scope.
A list of namespaces to which the label selector applies for the pod anti-affinity rule. If empty, the rule applies only to the namespace of the pod where the rule is defined.

The key of a node label that defines the topology domain for the required pod anti-affinity rule. Only nodes with the same value for this label key are considered when determining whether pods are co-located.

Arguments to the entrypoint. The container image's CMD is used if this is not provided. Variable references $(VAR_NAME) are expanded using the container's environment. If a variable cannot be resolved, the reference in the input string will be unchanged. Cannot be updated.
The command to run in the container, represented as a list of strings. This overrides the container image's default entrypoint, analogous to Docker's ENTRYPOINT directive.
List of environment variables to set in the container. Each entry defines a variable name and optionally its value or source.
The name of the environment variable.
The value of the environment variable. If not set, you must provide a valueFrom source instead.
Specifies a source for the environment variable's value (e.g., a field reference, resource field, or config map/secret key). Cannot be used when 'value' is also set.
Selects a key of a ConfigMap in the pod's namespace. The value of that key becomes the value of the environment variable.
The key in the referenced ConfigMap whose value is used for this environment variable.
The name of the ConfigMap to select the key from.

Specifies whether the referenced key in the ConfigMap must exist. If true, a missing key is tolerated and the container can start; if false (default), the container will fail if the key is not present.

Selects a field of the pod, such as metadata.name, metadata.namespace, spec.nodeName, status.podIP, etc., and uses its value as the environment variable value. This is part of the valueFrom for an environment variable in a Kubernetes pod spec.
Version of the schema the field path is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1'.
The path to the pod field to select, such as metadata.name, metadata.namespace, metadata.uid, status.podIP, spec.nodeName, or spec.serviceAccountName.

Indicates whether the referenced key must exist. Set to `true` to allow the container to start even if the referenced key is absent from the source (e.g., ConfigMap or Secret). Defaults to `false`, where a missing key prevents the container from starting.

ResourceFieldRef selects a resource field from the container (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) and exposes its value as the environment variable's value. It is used in the env valueFrom context to reference a container resource.

The name of the container to select the resource value from. In Kubernetes' ResourceFieldSelector, this specifies which container's resource (e.g., limits.cpu) is referenced when used in an environment variable's value_from.
Divisor is the value by which the resource's value is divided. Must be a valid Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1m' for milliCPU or '1Gi' for memory).
Specifies the resource name to select from the container's resource requirements, typically in the form of requests.<resource> or limits.<resource>, e.g., "requests.cpu" or "limits.memory".
secret_key_ref is a reference to a specific key within a Kubernetes Secret. When set, the environment variable's value is populated with the value of that Secret key.
The key of the secret to select from. Must be a valid secret key.
The name of the Secret to select from.

Specifies whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If true, the container starts even if the Secret or key is missing; if false (default), the container will not start when the Secret or key is absent.
List of sources to populate environment variables in the container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or Secret, optionally with a prefix.

Reference to a ConfigMap from which environment variables are populated. The ConfigMap's data keys become environment variable names, and the object may include an 'optional' flag to indicate whether the ConfigMap must exist.
Name of the ConfigMap to reference as the source for environment variables.
Indicates whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. When set to true, the ConfigMap may be absent; when false (default), the ConfigMap must exist.
An optional prefix that is prepended to each key in the ConfigMap or Secret referenced by this envFrom entry.
The secret_ref block specifies a Kubernetes Secret to populate environment variables. Each key in the referenced Secret becomes an environment variable in the container.
The name of the Secret whose key-value pairs are exposed as environment variables in the container.
This flag indicates whether the referenced Secret must exist. If set to true, a missing Secret will not cause the container to fail; if false or unset, the Secret must be defined.
The container image to run, specified as a name and optionally a tag or digest, e.g., 'nginx:1.14.2'. This is a required field defining which image the container should use.
Determines when the kubelet should pull the container image. Allowed values: Always, IfNotPresent, Never.

Lifecycle configuration for the container, defining hooks that run at specific points in the container's lifecycle. Supports `postStart` and `preStop` handlers, each executing an exec command, HTTP request, or TCP socket probe.
Specifies a lifecycle hook that runs immediately after a container is created. Can define an exec command or an HTTP GET request to be executed.
Exec specifies the command to run inside the container as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. This is an alternative to the HTTP GET handler for executing custom actions when the container starts.

The command and arguments to execute in the container as part of the postStart lifecycle hook. This is a list of strings where the first element is the executable and the remaining elements are arguments. The command runs inside the container immediately after it has been started; if it fails (non-zero exit), the container is terminated.
The HTTP GET request to be sent to the container when the postStart lifecycle hook is triggered. This defines the request details such as path, port, host, scheme, and HTTP headers.
Specifies the hostname or IP address to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod's IP if not provided.
HTTP headers to send in the GET request. Each item is an object containing `name` and `value` fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request. This corresponds to the header key in the HTTP GET request sent by the postStart lifecycle handler.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the GET request for the post-start lifecycle hook.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server for the HTTP GET request.
The port number (as a string) or name of the port on the container to which the HTTP GET request should be sent.
Protocol is the network protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Defines a sleep action that delays the container start by a specified number of seconds in the postStart lifecycle hook.
The duration in seconds for the container to sleep during the post-start lifecycle hook.
Represents a TCP socket action to be executed as a postStart lifecycle hook, defining the host and port to connect to; the hook is considered successful if the TCP connection is established.
The hostname or IP address to connect to. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP address.
The TCP port to connect to during the postStart lifecycle hook. Accepts a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the pod's container.

PreStop is a lifecycle hook that runs immediately before a container is terminated. It allows the container to perform graceful shutdown tasks, such as draining connections, before the kubelet sends the termination signal.
Exec specifies the action to run a command inside the container as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook.
The command to execute in the container as part of the preStop hook's exec action. It is given as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to be performed when the preStop lifecycle hook is triggered, allowing the container to execute a HTTP request before termination.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
Custom headers to set in the HTTP request. HTTP allows repeated headers. This is used within the HTTP GET action of a lifecycle pre-stop hook.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request for the preStop lifecycle hook.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
The port number or name of the container port to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Can be an integer port number or a named port.
Specifies the protocol to use for the HTTP GET request, either 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'.
The protocol scheme to use for the HTTP request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.

The 'sleep' lifecycle handler pauses the container for a specified number of seconds (defined in its 'seconds' field) during the pre-stop phase, allowing time for graceful shutdown or connection draining before the container is terminated.
The number of seconds to sleep during the preStop lifecycle hook before the container is terminated.

Configures a TCP socket action to be performed during the pre-stop lifecycle hook. The object defines the port (and optionally host) to which the kubelet attempts a TCP connection as part of the hook handler.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The port number or name of the port on the container to connect to for the TCP socket pre-stop hook.
The signal sent to the container when it is requested to stop. Can be a symbolic name like 'SIGTERM' or a numeric value.
Defines the probe used to check container health. If the probe fails, the container is restarted according to the restart policy.
Exec action for the liveness probe. Runs a specified command inside the container; the probe is considered successful if the command exits with code 0.
Command is the command line to execute inside the container. A non-zero exit code indicates a failed liveness probe.
The number of consecutive failures of the liveness probe after which the container is restarted. Must be set to a positive integer; defaults to 3.
Defines a gRPC-based liveness probe, letting the kubelet verify container health by sending a gRPC request. The object must specify the port to connect to, and may optionally include a service name.

The interpretation mode for the gRPC probe. Allowed values are SERVICE_NAME (default) and METHOD_NAME. When set to METHOD_NAME, the service field is interpreted as a fully-qualified gRPC method name (e.g., /package.Service/Method).
The port number to use for the gRPC liveness probe. It should be the port on which the gRPC server is listening.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by gRPC.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to perform as a liveness probe. This action defines the path, port, and headers used to check if the container is alive.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request for the probe. Each object has 'name' and 'value' fields defining the header.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the probe request.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request for the liveness probe.
The HTTP path to request from the server. Defaults to '/'.
The port number or name of the port on the container that the HTTP GET request for the liveness probe will be sent to. It can be a numeric port or a named port as defined in the container's ports.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme to use for the request: HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
Number of seconds between liveness probe attempts. Defaults to 10 seconds, and the minimum value is 1.
Specifies the number of consecutive successes required for the liveness probe to be considered successful after a failure. For liveness probes, this value must be set to 1.
Configures a TCP socket probe for the liveness check, specifying the port (and optionally host) to test connectivity.
The host name or IP address to connect to. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port to check, specified as a numeric port (e.g., 8080) or a named port defined in the container's ports. The probe opens a TCP connection to this port on the container's IP address.
The number of seconds the pod is given to terminate gracefully when it receives a termination signal. The value must be a non-negative integer.
Number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out. Defaults to 1 second if not specified.
The name of the container. Must be unique within the pod.

List of ports exposed from the container. Each object typically specifies the container port number and protocol (TCP or UDP), and may optionally include a host port, host IP, and a name. This provides information about the container's network connections for Kubernetes services and other features.
The TCP/UDP port number that the container listens on and that is exposed in the pod definition.
The host IP address to bind the container port to. If not specified, the port is bound to all host interfaces.

The port number on the host node to which the container port is mapped. When set, the container is accessible on this port via the host's IP address. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) if specified.
Name of the container port. Must be a DNS_LABEL and unique within the pod's containers.
The network protocol associated with the port. Valid values are TCP, UDP, and SCTP; if unset, TCP is used.
Readiness probe defines a probe that checks whether the container is ready to accept traffic. If the probe fails, the container is removed from service endpoints.
Exec specifies the action to take, which is to execute a command inside the container as part of the probe.
Specifies the command to execute inside the container as part of the readiness probe. It is a list of strings where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.
The number of consecutive failed readiness probes required before the container is marked as unready. Defaults to 3.
Specifies a gRPC action for the readiness probe. It contains the port on which the gRPC server is running, and optionally a service name to be checked.
The port number of the gRPC service to connect to. Must be between 1 and 65535.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the default is to check the health of the overall server.
Specifies an HTTP GET request that the kubelet performs against the container to determine readiness. It defines the HTTP endpoint (path, port, and optional headers) used for the health check.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
List of custom HTTP headers to send with the probe request. Each header object must contain `name` and `value` fields.
The header name to use in the HTTP request.
The value of the HTTP header entry. When combined with the corresponding `name`, this defines a custom header to include with the HTTP GET request from the readiness probe.
Path to access on the HTTP server for the readiness probe's HTTP GET request. If not specified, defaults to the root path '/'.
The TCP port (or named port) on the container to send the HTTP GET request to. Can be an integer port number or a named port as defined in the container's ports.
Protocol to use for the HTTP request in the readiness probe. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the probe is initiated. Defaults to 0, minimum value is 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1.
Specifies a TCP socket check for the readiness probe. The kubelet attempts to open a connection to the container's port; the probe succeeds if the connection can be established.
Host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The port number or name of the port on the container to connect to for the TCP socket probe. This can be a numeric port (e.g., "8080") or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The amount of time in seconds that Kubernetes waits after sending a SIGTERM signal to the container before forcibly terminating it with SIGKILL. The default value is 30 seconds.
The number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second.

A list of resource resize policies for the container. Each policy specifies how a resizable resource (such as CPU or memory) should be handled when its size changes, including whether the change requires a restart.
ResourceName is the name of the resource to which the resize policy applies. Supported values are 'cpu' and 'memory'.
The restart policy for all containers in the pod. Valid values are Always, OnFailure, and Never. Defaults to Always.
Resource requirements for the container, specifying requests and limits for CPU, memory, and other compute resources.
Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this container. This is an alpha feature and may not be supported in all clusters.
The name of the resource claim. This must match the name of a PersistentVolumeClaim (or other resource claim) in the same namespace.
The maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the container. The keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory), and the values are quantities (e.g., "100m", "1Gi") that define the upper bound.
The minimum amount of compute resources required. Keys are resource names (e.g., cpu, memory) and values are quantities (e.g., '500m', '1Gi').
A list of container exit codes that trigger this restart policy rule. The rule applies when the container exits with any of the specified numeric codes.
SecurityContext holds security configuration that will be applied to a container. It includes settings such as runAsUser, runAsGroup, capabilities, SELinux options, and read-only root filesystem.
Indicates whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process. Setting this to false prevents privilege escalation, such as executing setuid binaries. Defaults to true.

Defines the AppArmor profile to apply to the container. The type field specifies the profile type (RuntimeDefault, Localhost, or Unconfined), and localhostProfile specifies the name of a profile to use when type is Localhost.
Specifies the name of an AppArmor profile that is pre-loaded on the node. This is used when the type of AppArmor profile is set to 'Localhost'.
The type of AppArmor profile to apply to the container as defined by the Kubernetes security context.
Security context capabilities define Linux capabilities to add or drop for the container. It typically contains `add` and `drop` lists of capability names.
List of capabilities to add to the container's capability set.

Specifies a list of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's effective and permitted capability sets. For example, 'DROP' or 'SETPCAP'. These capabilities will be removed from the container's default capabilities before the container starts.

Indicates whether the container should run in privileged mode. When set to true, the container gains access to all host devices and capabilities, effectively granting it extended privileges beyond those of the host.
procMount specifies the proc mount to use for the container. Allowed values are 'Default' and 'Unmasked'.
Mounts the container's root filesystem as read-only if set to true.
The GID (group ID) to run the container's processes with. If not set, the primary group of the image's default user (or the user specified by run_as_user) is used.
If true, the container must run as a non-root user. The kubelet will validate that the container does not run as UID 0 and will fail to start if it does.
The user ID (UID) that the container process runs as. If not set, the container runs as the user specified in the image's metadata (or as root if not specified). Must be an integer.
SELinux options applied to the container, defining the SELinux labels including level, role, type, and user.
The SELinux level (MLS/MCS) for the container, applied as part of the SELinux options in the security context. For example, 's0:c123,c456'.
The SELinux role label assigned to the container, such as 'system_r' or 'unconfined_r'.
The SELinux type label to be applied to the container.
The SELinux user label for the container. Part of the SELinux context (user:role:type:level).
Defines the seccomp profile for the container, specifying the profile type and optional localhost profile path to configure container seccomp security.
Specifies the path to a seccomp profile on the node's local filesystem when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'. This profile is used to restrict the container's system calls.
The seccomp profile type. Valid values are RuntimeDefault, Localhost, and Unconfined.
Windows-specific security context options. These options apply only to Windows containers and can include settings such as credential specifications (GMSA) and host process configuration.
GMSA credential spec inlined by the GMSA admission webhook from the credential spec named by `gmsa_credential_spec_name`. Contains the full contents of the GMSA credential spec.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the container's Windows security context. This must correspond to a GMSA credential spec defined in the cluster.

Indicates whether the container should run as a Host Process container on Windows. This field is only valid for Windows containers and is alpha-level; all containers in the pod must have the same effective value.
Specifies the username under which the container's main process runs in Windows containers. Common values include 'ContainerUser' and 'ContainerAdministrator'.

Defines a probe that determines whether the application inside the container has started successfully. The startup probe is used to manage the container's startup sequence and can prevent the container from being restarted unnecessarily during initialization.

Exec defines a command-based probe handler. The command is executed inside the container, and the probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0. The command is specified as a list of strings with the first element being the executable and subsequent elements as arguments.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container for the startup probe. It is specified as an array of strings, where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments.
The number of consecutive failures allowed for the startup probe before the container is considered failed and restarted. The default is 3, and the minimum value is 1.
Specifies the gRPC action used by the probe to check container health. It contains the gRPC service name and port to connect to; if the service name is omitted, the pod's name is used by default.
The port number of the gRPC service that the startup probe checks. Must be a valid TCP port number (1-65535).
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default behavior is defined by the gRPC health checking protocol.
HTTP GET action for the startup probe, specifying the request path, port, and optional headers used to check container health during startup.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified. Consider using the 'Host' header in httpHeaders instead of this field for HTTP/1.1.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the probe request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request, such as 'Authorization' or 'Content-Type'.
The value of the HTTP header to include in the probe request.
The path to access on the HTTP server when performing the HTTP GET request.
The port to use for the HTTP GET request. Can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host, such as HTTP or HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. The probe begins after this delay, allowing the container to initialize.
How often (in seconds) to perform the startup probe. The default is 10 seconds; the minimum value is 1.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. Defaults to 1.
Configuration for the TCP socket probe. Specifies the host and port on which the kubelet attempts a TCP connection to determine if the container has started.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port number or named port to connect to for the probe. Accepts an integer port (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports.
Specifies the duration in seconds that the pod has to terminate gracefully after receiving a termination signal before it is forcibly killed. Defaults to 30 seconds.
The number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second; the value must be at least 1.
If true, the container runtime allocates a buffer for stdin, allowing the container to read from standard input. Defaults to false.

If true, the container's stdin is only used once: it remains open for the first attach session and closes when that client disconnects. Thereafter, stdin remains closed until the container is restarted. This setting is only meaningful when stdin is also true.
Path where the container's termination message will be written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.
Sets the termination message policy for the container. Allowed values are 'File', 'Message', and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'.
If true, allocates a pseudo-TTY for the container, enabling interactive terminal sessions. Defaults to false.
List of block device volumes to expose to the container. Each entry maps a volume name to a device path inside the container, allowing raw block devices to be mounted.
The path inside the container where the raw block device will be mounted (e.g., /dev/xvda). This field is required for each entry in volume_devices.
The name of the volume to use, which must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
A list of volume mounts for the container. Each item defines a volume to be mounted into the container, including the volume name, mount path, and mount options.
The path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path, e.g. /data.
Controls whether and how mounts are propagated from the host to the container. Allowed values: None, HostToContainer, Bidirectional.
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod specification.
If true, the volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read-write).
Path within the volume from which to mount the volume. Defaults to the volume's root. Useful for sharing one volume among multiple containers with different mount paths.
Similar to sub_path, but allows environment variable references like $(VAR) to be expanded in the path. The value is a string that specifies the sub-path within the volume to mount.
Working directory for the container. If not specified, the container runtime default is used (e.g., / for Docker). Must be an absolute path.
The name of the DNS resolver option, such as 'ndots' or 'timeout', as defined in resolv.conf or by the DNS provider.
The value for the DNS option. If omitted, the option is configured as a name-only flag (e.g., ndots).
Arguments to the entrypoint. If not provided, the container image's CMD is used; variable references $(VAR_NAME) are expanded using the container's environment.
The command to run in the ephemeral container. It is an array of strings that overrides the image's default entrypoint.
List of environment variables to set in the ephemeral container.
Name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier.
The value to assign to the environment variable. This is a plain string value.
Source for the environment variable's value, referencing a ConfigMap key, Secret key, or downward API field. Cannot be used if 'value' is set.
The ConfigMapKeySelector to use for populating the environment variable from a ConfigMap key. It specifies the name of the ConfigMap, the key to select, and whether the key is required (optional).
The key to select from the referenced ConfigMap.
The name of the ConfigMap to select the key from.
Specifies whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. When set to true, the container can start even if the referenced ConfigMap or key does not exist.

Provides a reference to a pod field (downward API) to populate the environment variable value. Supports selecting fields such as metadata.name, metadata.namespace, metadata.labels['<KEY>'], metadata.annotations['<KEY>'], spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.hostIP, status.podIP, and status.podIPs (first IP).
The version of the schema the fieldPath is written in terms of. Defaults to 'v1'.
The path to the field to reference, relative to the pod. For example, 'metadata.name' or 'status.podIP'. This selects the value of the specified field to be used as the environment variable value.

Specifies whether the referenced file key must exist. When set to true, the key is optional and the container can start even if it is missing; when set to false (default), the key must exist for the container to properly start.
The name of the volume that contains the file from which the environment variable's value is read.

Selects a resource field (such as 'requests.cpu' or 'limits.memory') from the current container, or from a named container via the 'containerName' subfield, to populate the environment variable's value.
The name of the container to which the resource quantity refers. Required when the resource field is a container resource such as cpu or memory (e.g., limits.cpu).
The quantity by which the resource value is divided before being used as the environment variable's value. Defaults to 1 if not specified.
The resource to select from the container's resource requirements, such as `limits.cpu` or `requests.memory`. The corresponding value is exposed as the environment variable's value.
SecretKeyRef selects a key of a Secret in the pod's namespace. It specifies the name of the Secret and the key to use, with an optional flag to indicate whether the Secret must be defined.
The key of the secret entry to select from the referenced Secret. Must be a valid secret key.
Name of the Secret in the same namespace from which to select the key.
If true, the pod will start even if the referenced key does not exist in the referenced Secret. If false or omitted, the pod will not start if the key is missing.

A list of sources to populate environment variables in the ephemeral container. Each source can reference a ConfigMap or a Secret, and the key-value pairs from those sources are injected as environment variables.
Reference to a ConfigMap to populate environment variables from. The ConfigMap is identified by its name; each key in the ConfigMap becomes an environment variable in the container.
Name of the referenced ConfigMap.
Indicates whether the referenced ConfigMap is optional. If set to true, the ConfigMap may be absent and the container can still start; if false or omitted, the ConfigMap must exist.
An optional identifier to prepend to each key in the ConfigMap. Must be a C_IDENTIFIER.
Reference to a Kubernetes Secret whose key-value pairs are exposed as environment variables in the container.
The name of the Secret to select. This field is required and must be the name of a Secret in the same namespace as the pod.
Specify whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If set to true, the envFrom entry will be ignored if the Secret does not exist; if false or unset, the Secret must exist.
The container image to run for the ephemeral container, specified as a string (e.g., 'nginx:latest').
Image pull policy for the ephemeral container. Allowed values are 'Always', 'IfNotPresent', or 'Never'. Defaults to 'IfNotPresent' if the image tag is not ':latest', and 'Always' if it is ':latest'.
Configures lifecycle hooks for the container, such as postStart and preStop, which are executed at specific points during the container's lifetime.
The postStart lifecycle hook, executed immediately after a container is created. This object defines the handler to run, which can be an exec command, HTTP GET request, TCP socket check, or sleep.
Exec specifies the action to take for the postStart lifecycle hook, running a command inside the container.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container; the first element is the command, and subsequent elements are arguments. The working directory for the command is the container's working directory.
The HTTP GET request to execute as the post-start lifecycle handler for the container. Configures the endpoint, port, path, scheme, and headers for the request.
A list of HTTP headers to send with the HTTP GET request issued by the post-start lifecycle hook of the ephemeral container. Each header is an object with name and value fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the HTTP GET request. It pairs with the corresponding header value in the same list entry.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP request.
The HTTP path to access on the server for this HTTP GET request.
The port number or name to use for the HTTP GET request. If a number, must be in the range 1-65535. If a name, must be an IANA_SVC_NAME.
The protocol (scheme) used to connect to the host for the HTTP GET request, such as 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Sleep defines a lifecycle hook action that pauses the container for a specified duration. It contains a required 'seconds' field that sets the sleep time.
The number of seconds the container should sleep during this postStart lifecycle hook. This field is required for a sleep action and must be a non-negative integer.
Specifies a TCP socket action to be performed after the container starts. It includes a port and an optional host; the handler succeeds if a TCP connection to the specified address is established.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket lifecycle hook. If not specified, the pod IP address is used.
The TCP port to connect to. Accepts a numeric port or a named port from the container's ports.

The pre_stop lifecycle hook is executed immediately before the container is terminated. It allows for graceful shutdown procedures, such as running an exec command or sending an HTTP request, before the container receives the termination signal.
Exec specifies the ExecAction handler for the pre-stop lifecycle hook, which runs a command inside the container. The command is provided in the 'command' field of this object.

A list of strings specifying the command and arguments to run in the container. The first element is the command, and the rest are arguments. The command is executed directly, not through a shell, with the working directory set to the container's root ('/'). Exit status 0 indicates success; non-zero causes the container to be terminated.
Represents an HTTP GET request to be performed by the kubelet as part of the pre-stop lifecycle hook.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the GET request. Each object in the list has a 'name' and 'value', defining a single header.
The name of the HTTP header to send in the request.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP request for this lifecycle hook.
Path to access on the HTTP server, used in the HTTP GET request for the pre-stop lifecycle hook.
The port to access on the container for the HTTP GET request. Accepts a numeric port number or a named port (as a string).
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'; defaults to 'HTTP'.
Scheme to use for connecting to the host. Allowed values are "HTTP" (default) and "HTTPS".
Sleep action for the preStop lifecycle hook. It specifies a delay in seconds to pause the container before it is terminated.
Specifies the number of seconds that the container should sleep before being terminated, used in the preStop lifecycle hook to delay termination.
