Specifies a TCP socket action for the lifecycle hook. It defines a TCP port (and optionally host) to check, and the container is considered healthy if the connection succeeds.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket action. If not specified, the pod IP is used.

The TCP port number or name of the container port. Accepts a valid port number (1-65535) or an IANA_SVC_NAME (a named port defined in the container's ports). This is the target port for the TCP socket connection in the lifecycle hook.
LivenessProbe defines the probe that checks whether the ephemeral container is healthy. This is a standard Kubernetes probe configuration, specifying how to determine if the container is alive.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container for the liveness probe. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with status 0.
The command to run inside the container as the liveness probe. It is a list of strings representing the command and its arguments, passed as an argument vector (argv) to the container's runtime.
The number of consecutive failures required for the liveness probe to be considered failed, causing the container to be restarted. Must be at least 1; defaults to 3.
Configures a gRPC-based health check for the liveness probe. It specifies the port to connect to and optionally the service name to check.
The TCP port number to use for the gRPC health check. This field is required and must be an integer.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not set, the default behavior is to use the container name.
Specifies the HTTP GET action for the liveness probe of an ephemeral container. This defines the HTTP request path, port, and headers used to probe the container's health.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP probe. Defaults to the pod IP if unset. Prefer setting the Host header via httpHeaders for virtual hosting.
A list of custom headers to include in the HTTP request for the probe. Each item is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields, specifying the header name and its value.
The name of the HTTP header, such as 'X-Custom-Header'. This is the header field name used in the HTTP GET request of the probe.
The value of the HTTP header field. This is the value associated with the header name in the HTTP request.
The HTTP path to request on the server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol scheme to use for the HTTP GET request, typically 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP' if not specified.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
Specifies the frequency (in seconds) at which the liveness probe is executed. Must be greater than 0; defaults to 10 if not set.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after a failure. For liveness probes, this must be 1 (the default).
Configures a TCP socket check for the liveness probe. The probe will succeed if a TCP connection can be established to the specified port on the container's host/IP.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket liveness probe. If not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The port number or named port to connect to for the TCP socket liveness probe. This must be a valid port number (e.g., 8080) or the name of a port defined in the container.
Timeout in seconds after which the liveness probe is considered failed. Must be at least 1 second.
The name of the ephemeral container. Must be a valid DNS subdomain and unique among all containers in the pod.
List of network ports to expose from the ephemeral container. Each port object typically specifies protocol, containerPort, and hostPort.
The IP address of the host to bind the container port to. If not set, the port is bound to all available host interfaces.
The host port number to expose the container port on the node. In Kubernetes, this field is not allowed for ephemeral containers and is ignored if set.
Name of the port. Must be an IANA_SVC_NAME and unique within the pod. This name can be referenced by services.
The network protocol for this port. Supported values are 'TCP', 'UDP', and 'SCTP'. Defaults to 'TCP'.

Readiness probe, which determines when the container is considered ready. Ephemeral containers do not support readiness probes; this field is invalid for ephemeral containers and will be rejected by the API.
Exec specifies the action to take: run a command inside the container to check its health. The command to execute is defined in the 'command' field of this object as a list of strings.
The command to execute inside the container for the readiness probe. It is a list of strings, executed directly without a shell; an exit code of 0 indicates success, non-zero indicates failure.
Minimum consecutive failures for the probe to be considered failed after having succeeded. Defaults to 3; minimum value is 1.

Configures a gRPC health check for the probe. The gRPC action sends a gRPC request to the specified port on the container, optionally using a provided service name. The object requires a 'port' field and may include a 'service' field.
The port number on which the gRPC server is serving the health check. This is the port that the kubelet connects to when performing the readiness probe.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is an empty string, which checks the overall health of the server.
Specifies the HTTP GET request to perform as a probe action. Includes parameters such as host, port, path, scheme, and custom headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. You probably want to set 'Host' in httpHeaders instead.
A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the probe request. Each header is defined by a name and value.
The name of the HTTP header to send with the probe request. For example, 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the request.
The HTTP path to request on the container's HTTP server. If not specified, the path defaults to '/'.
The port number or name to use for the HTTP GET request. For a numeric port, valid values are 1-65535. For a named port, it must match a container port name.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for connecting to the host. Defaults to HTTP. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the readiness probe is initiated. Must be greater than or equal to 0.
How often (in seconds) to perform the readiness probe. Defaults to 10; must be at least 1.
The number of consecutive successful probe results required for the readiness probe to be considered successful after a failure. Must be an integer greater than 0; defaults to 1.
Configures a TCP socket check for the readiness probe. It defines the host and port that kubelet will connect to to determine container readiness, with port being required.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket check. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The port number or name of the socket to probe. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or the name of a port defined in the container.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.

Defines the resize policy for the container's resources. Each entry specifies a resource name (e.g., cpu, memory) and the restart policy to apply when that resource is resized, with allowed policies of NotRequired or RestartContainer.
The resource name (e.g., cpu or memory) to which this resize policy applies.
The restart policy to apply when the container's resources are resized. Allowed values are 'NotRequired' (no restart) and 'RestartContainer' (restart to apply the new resource allocation).
Resource requirements for the ephemeral container, specifying requests and limits for compute resources such as CPU and memory.
A list of resource claims (ResourceClaim) that specify which ResourceClaim objects this ephemeral container's resources should use. Each claim entry typically includes a name and optional request.
Name must match the name of an entry in pod.spec.resourceClaims.
Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed (e.g., cpu, memory). The keys are resource names and the values are quantities as strings (e.g., '100m', '1Gi').
A map of resource names to quantities specifying the minimum amount of compute resources required. For example, 'cpu' and 'memory' with string values like '100m' and '1Gi'.
Specifies the comparison operator used to evaluate the container's exit code against the configured values in the restart policy rule.
A list of container exit codes to which the restart policy rule applies. Each entry is an integer exit code.
SecurityContext holds the security configuration for the ephemeral container, including settings such as user/group IDs, SELinux options, Linux capabilities, and privilege flags.

Controls whether the container process can gain more privileges than its parent process. When set to false, the container is prevented from executing setuid/setgid binaries and from gaining additional privileges.
Specifies the name of a profile that is already loaded on the node. This field is only valid when the type is 'Localhost'.
The type of AppArmor profile to use. Allowed values are 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', and 'Unconfined'.
Capabilities configures Linux capabilities for the ephemeral container. It allows adding or removing specific capabilities via the 'add' and 'drop' fields.
List of Linux capabilities to add to the container's permitted capability set.
Specifies a list of Linux capabilities to drop from the container's security context. Capabilities are expressed as capability names without the 'CAP_' prefix, e.g., 'SYS_ADMIN'.
Run the ephemeral container in privileged mode, granting access to all host devices and capabilities.
procMount specifies the proc mount to use for the ephemeral container. Allowed values are 'Default' and 'Unmasked'.
When true, the root filesystem of the ephemeral container is mounted as read-only, preventing write operations to the filesystem.
The group ID (GID) that the container process runs as. If not specified, the runtime default is used.
Indicates that the container must run as a non-root user. If true, the kubelet will validate that the container does not run as UID 0 (root) and will fail to start it otherwise.

The user ID (UID) that the container process will run as. Must be a positive integer. When set, overrides the user specified in the container image. Defaults to the image's user or the pod-level security context value if not set.
Specifies the SELinux options for the ephemeral container's security context, allowing configuration of the SELinux label (user, role, type, and level).
The SELinux level that applies to the container, usually expressed as a sensitivity label (e.g., s0).
The SELinux role label for the container's security context. Corresponds to the 'role' field in the SELinuxOptions of the security context.
The SELinux type label (e.g., svirt_sandbox_file_t) applied to the container.
The SELinux user label for the container, e.g., 'system_u'.
Specifies the seccomp profile configuration for the security context of each ephemeral container in the pod template.
The path to the seccomp profile on the node. This field is only used when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost'.

Type specifies which seccomp profile to apply. Valid values are 'RuntimeDefault' (use the container runtime's default profile), 'Unconfined' (no seccomp profile), and 'Localhost' (use a profile defined on the node).
Windows-specific security options for the ephemeral container, including settings like GMSA credential specification, run-as user name, and host process mode.
The GMSA credential spec as a string, containing the JSON representation of the Windows service account identity. This is typically populated by the GMSA admission webhook.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the Windows container's security context.

Whether the container should run as a HostProcess container, gaining access to the host's process and network namespaces. This is a boolean flag commonly set to true for privileged Windows containers.
The username (optionally in domain\user format) used to run the container's entrypoint process on Windows. Defaults to the user specified in the image metadata if not set.

Defines a probe that checks whether the application inside the container has started successfully. If specified, other probes are disabled until this probe succeeds, and failure triggers a restart of the container.
Exec specifies the action to take for the startup probe. It runs a command inside the container; the probe succeeds if the command exits with status 0.

Command is the command line to execute inside the container. The working directory is root ('/') in the container's filesystem. The command is exec'd, not run inside a shell, so traditional shell instructions ('|', '&', ';', etc.) won't work. To use a shell, you need to explicitly call out to that shell, e.g., ['sh', '-c', 'echo hello'].
The minimum consecutive failures of the startup probe that cause the probe to be considered failed and the container to be restarted. It must be a positive integer.
Configures a gRPC health check for the probe. The probe will connect to a gRPC server and verify its health status, typically using the standard gRPC health checking protocol.
The port number on which the gRPC service is running for the startup probe. The gRPC health check will be sent to this port.
The name of the service to place in the gRPC health check request. If not specified, the default behavior is to check the overall health of the pod.
HTTPGetAction performs an HTTP GET request against the container to check its health. It allows specifying the request path, port, and optional HTTP headers.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP. You may want to set the Host header in httpHeaders instead.
Custom HTTP headers to include in the request sent by the startup probe. Each item defines a header name and value to be sent.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The value of the HTTP header to be sent in the startup probe request. For example, a header named 'Authorization' could have the value 'Bearer token'.
The HTTP path to request when performing the HTTP GET probe. If not set, the probe uses the root path '/'.
Port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URL scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated. Must be a non-negative integer.
Specifies the number of seconds between each startup probe attempt. Minimum value is 1; default is 10.
Minimum consecutive successes for the startup probe to be considered successful after having failed. The value must be 1 for startup probes.
Specifies a TCP socket check for the startup probe. Kubernetes attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's port to determine if the container has started successfully.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod's IP address is used.
The TCP port to connect to. This can be a numeric port or a named port as defined in the container's ports.
Number of seconds after which the probe times out. Defaults to 1 second. Minimum value is 1.
Whether this ephemeral container should allocate a buffer for stdin in the container runtime. If not set, reads from stdin in the container will always result in EOF. Default is false.

If set to true, the standard input of the ephemeral container will be closed after the first attach, making it non-interactive for subsequent attaches. This option requires the stdin field to be true.
The name of the target container that this ephemeral container will attach to, enabling debugging within that container's context.

Path to the file where the container's termination message is written. The kubelet reads this file to retrieve the termination message and exposes it via the API server. Defaults to /dev/termination-log.

Specifies how the termination message of the container is populated. Allowed values are 'File' (default), which reads the message from the file '/dev/termination-log', and 'FallbackToLogsOnError', which uses the last chunk of container logs as the message if the termination message file is empty.
Indicates whether a pseudo-TTY should be allocated for the ephemeral container. When true, the container is allocated a TTY.
List of block device mappings for the ephemeral container. Each item specifies a volume name and the device path inside the container where the volume is exposed.
The path inside the container where the block volume device will be mapped to.
Name of the volume to which this device applies. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
Lists the volumes to mount into the ephemeral container's filesystem, specifying the volume name, mount path, and optional mount properties.
Path within the ephemeral container at which the volume is mounted.
Mount propagation determines how mounts are propagated from the host to the container and vice versa. Valid values are 'None' (default), 'HostToContainer', and 'Bidirectional'.
The name of the volume to mount. This must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
When set to true, the volume mount is made read-only recursively, meaning that the volume and all its sub-mounts are read-only. This requires kernel support.
Path within the volume from which the container will be mounted instead of the volume's root.
Similar to subPath, but supports environment variable expansion using $(VAR_NAME) syntax. Environment variables are evaluated relative to the container. Mutually exclusive with subPath.
The working directory for the ephemeral container. If not specified, defaults to the container image's default working directory. Must be an absolute path.
List of hostnames that resolve to the IP address specified in the hostAlias. These hostnames are added to the pod's /etc/hosts.
The IP address that will be added to the pod's /etc/hosts file for this host alias entry. It maps to the hostnames defined in the same host alias.
Name of the Secret in the same namespace that contains credentials for pulling container images.
Arguments to the entrypoint of the init container. This is a list of strings that overrides the default command arguments defined in the container image.
The command to run in the init container. This is an array of strings that overrides the ENTRYPOINT defined in the container image. If not specified, the image's default entrypoint is used.
List of environment variables to set in the init container. Each item is an EnvVar object with name, value, and optional valueFrom field.
Name of the environment variable. Must be a valid C identifier (e.g., MY_VAR).
The literal value for the environment variable. Provide this or use value_from to source the value from a secret or config map.

value_from is an optional source for the environment variable's value, mutually exclusive with the 'value' field. It allows referencing a ConfigMap key, Secret key, a field of the pod (fieldRef), or a container resource (resourceFieldRef).
Selects a key from a ConfigMap to populate the environment variable value. Typically includes the ConfigMap name and the key within it, with an optional flag to indicate whether the key must exist.
The key within the ConfigMap to select the value from. Must correspond to an existing key in the referenced ConfigMap.
The name of the ConfigMap to select a key from.
Specifies whether the ConfigMap or its key must be defined. If true, and the ConfigMap or key is not found, the environment variable is omitted; if false, a missing ConfigMap or key causes an error.
Selects an APIVersioned field of the pod, such as metadata.name or status.podIP, to be exposed as an environment variable.
The API version of the schema that field_path references. Defaults to 'v1' for core Kubernetes fields.
The path of the field to select, such as `metadata.name` or `spec.nodeName`.
The key to select from the referenced file or config map. This key must exist within the file referenced by the file_key_ref.

Specifies whether the referenced file key must be defined. When set to true, the container will still be created even if the key does not exist, and the environment variable is omitted. When false (default), the container will fail to start if the key is missing.

Selects a resource field (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) from the specified container to set the environment variable's value. This block typically includes fields for the container name and the resource name.
The name of the container to select the resource field from. If not specified, defaults to the container where this environment variable is defined.
The divisor to divide the selected resource's value by, specified as a quantity (e.g., '1', '1m'). The result is made available as an integer. Defaults to '1'.
The name of the resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory'. This specifies which resource quantity to read from the container's resource requirements.

Selects a key of a Secret as the source for the environment variable's value. The object specifies the Secret's name, the key within it, and an optional 'optional' flag to indicate if the reference is optional.
The key of the secret to select. This key must exist in the referenced secret.
The name of the Secret to select from. Must be the name of a Secret in the same namespace as the pod.

Optional indicates whether the Secret or its key must be defined. If true, the environment variable is not set if the referenced secret or key is missing; if false (default), the secret and key must exist or the container will not start.
envFrom is a list of sources to populate environment variables in the container. Each entry can reference a ConfigMap or a Secret, with an optional prefix to apply to variable names.
Specifies a ConfigMap whose key-value pairs are exposed as environment variables in the container. All entries in the referenced ConfigMap become environment variables.
Name of the ConfigMap that should be used as the source of environment variables.
Indicates whether the referenced ConfigMap must be defined. If true, the ConfigMap is optional and its absence does not cause the container to fail. If false (default), the ConfigMap must exist.
Prefix to prepend to each key in the ConfigMap or Secret referenced by envFrom. If specified, the keys are transformed by adding this prefix before being used as environment variable names.

Reference to a Kubernetes Secret whose data entries are exposed as environment variables in the container. The object typically includes 'name' (the Secret name) and 'optional' (whether the Secret must exist).
The name of the Secret to reference. The referenced Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Indicates whether the referenced Secret must be defined. If set to true, the Secret is optional and its absence or missing keys will not cause the container to fail.
The container image to use for the init container, specified as a name with optional tag or digest (e.g., nginx:1.25, busybox@sha256:...).

Specifies when the kubelet should pull the container image. Allowed values are Always (always pull), IfNotPresent (pull only if not present locally), and Never (never pull). If omitted, Kubernetes defaults the policy based on the image tag.
Lifecycle describes actions that the management system should take in response to container lifecycle events. It defines postStart and preStop handlers.

Specifies a lifecycle hook that runs immediately after the container is started. It can define an exec command, HTTP GET request, or TCP socket check, and if the handler fails, the container is terminated and restarted according to its restart policy.

Exec specifies the command to run in the container for the postStart lifecycle hook. The command is provided as a list of strings, with the first element being the executable and the rest being arguments.
Specifies the command to run inside the container as the post-start lifecycle handler. This is a list of strings representing the command and its arguments.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to be performed against the container's endpoint during the post-start lifecycle hook.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP address if not specified.

A list of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request sent to the container's lifecycle postStart hook. Each header is an object with `name` and `value` fields, allowing you to set request headers such as Authorization or Content-Type.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The value of the HTTP header to send in the HTTP request.
Path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/'.
Port number or name of the port on which the container's HTTP GET lifecycle handler will connect. Accepts a numeric port (1-65535) or a port name defined in the container's ports list.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request. Valid values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS', defaulting to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request. Allowed values are `HTTP` and `HTTPS`. Defaults to `HTTP`.
SleepAction configures the postStart lifecycle hook to sleep for a specified number of seconds. It contains a required 'seconds' field that defines the sleep duration.
Seconds is the number of seconds to sleep during the lifecycle hook. Must be a positive integer.
The tcp_socket block specifies a TCP socket handler for the post-start lifecycle event. It attempts to open a TCP connection to the specified host and port as part of the container's post-start hook.
Optional host name or IP address for the TCP socket connection. Defaults to the pod IP address.
The TCP port to connect to for the postStart lifecycle hook. This can be a numeric port (e.g., '8080') or a named port (a string referencing a container port name).
The pre_stop lifecycle hook is executed immediately before a container is terminated. This block can contain an exec or http_get handler that defines the action to run.
The exec action to run as the pre-stop lifecycle hook. This specifies the command to execute inside the container when it is about to be terminated.

The command to execute in the container during the pre-stop lifecycle hook. Specified as a list of strings where the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments, analogous to the exec form in container runtimes.
Specifies an HTTP GET request to be sent to the container when the pre-stop hook is triggered, as part of the container lifecycle.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP.

Custom HTTP headers to include in the request to the HTTP GET probe. Each header is defined by a name and value, and repeated headers are allowed. These are sent to the server when performing the pre-stop lifecycle hook.
The name of the HTTP header.
The value of the HTTP header to send with the GET request. Together with the header name, this defines a single header entry.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.
The port number or name of the port on the container to which the HTTP GET request is sent. Can be a numeric port or a named port defined in the container's ports.
The protocol for the HTTP request. Must be 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The URI scheme to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'.
Sleep represents the Sleep action for the lifecycle hook. It pauses the container for a specified duration, defined by the 'seconds' field within this object.
The number of seconds to sleep during the preStop lifecycle hook's sleep action, delaying container termination.

tcp_socket specifies the TCP socket action handler for the pre-stop lifecycle hook. It defines a TCP connection attempt to a port on the container's host or a specified host, used to notify other systems that the container is being terminated.
Optional host name to connect to for the TCP socket lifecycle handler; if not specified, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to. Accepts a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
Liveness probe configuration for the init container. This object defines a periodic health check; if the probe fails, the container is restarted by the kubelet.
Exec specifies the action to take. It defines a command to execute inside the container; the probe is considered successful if the command exits with status 0.

Command to run in the container for the liveness probe. It is a list of strings; the first element is the command and subsequent elements are arguments. The command is executed directly, not via a shell, and a zero exit status indicates success.
The number of consecutive probe failures after which the container is considered unhealthy. For a liveness probe, reaching this threshold causes the container to be restarted.
grpc specifies the gRPC health check configuration for the liveness probe. It includes the port to connect to and optionally the service name for the gRPC health check.
The port number of the gRPC service to probe. This is a required field for gRPC liveness probes and must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the service to place in the gRPC HealthCheckRequest. If not specified, the default is to check the overall server status (empty service name).

Defines the HTTP GET request used by the liveness probe to check container health. It specifies a path and port on the container; the probe is considered successful if the HTTP response is successful.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; you can also set the Host header explicitly via httpHeaders instead.
Optional list of custom HTTP headers to include in the request. Each header is an object containing a name and a value.
The name of the HTTP header to set in the request. For example, 'X-Custom-Header'.
The value of the HTTP header sent in the liveness probe request.
The path to access on the HTTP server, e.g., /healthz. Defaults to the root path if not specified.
Port number or name of the port to access on the container. The port must be an integer between 1 and 65535 or match a named port in the container's pod specification.
The protocol (scheme) to use for the HTTP GET request, such as HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request. Allowed values are HTTP and HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before liveness probes are initiated.
How often (in seconds) to perform the liveness probe. Defaults to 10 seconds; minimum value is 1.
The minimum consecutive successes required for the liveness probe to be considered successful after a failure. Must be 1 for liveness probes.
Represents a TCP socket probe action. The kubelet attempts to open a TCP connection to the container on the specified port; a successful connection indicates the probe passed.
The host name to connect to for the TCP socket probe. Defaults to the pod IP if not specified.
The TCP port to check. Specify a numeric port (e.g., "80") or a named port defined in the container. Required for a TCP socket liveness probe.
Specifies the duration in seconds a pod has to shut down gracefully before being terminated with SIGKILL.
Specifies the number of seconds after which the liveness probe times out. Must be at least 1 second; defaults to 1 second.
Name of the init container. Must be a DNS_LABEL and unique within the pod.
List of ports to expose from the init container. Each element is a ContainerPort object specifying the container port (required) and optional name, host IP, host port, and protocol (defaults to TCP).
The port number on which the container listens. This is the port that the container exposes.

The host IP address to bind the host port to. This is used when the container port is exposed on the host via hostPort. If not specified, it defaults to 0.0.0.0, meaning the port is bound to all host interfaces.
The port number on the host node where the container port is exposed. If omitted, the container port is not exposed on the host.
The name of the container port. If specified, it must be unique among all ports in the container and can be used to refer to this port in other resources such as services.
The protocol for the container port. Allowed values are 'TCP', 'UDP', and 'SCTP'. Defaults to 'TCP'.

Defines a probe to determine when the init container is ready to accept traffic. It uses the standard Kubernetes Probe specification, allowing checks via exec, HTTP GET, TCP socket, with configurable timing and threshold parameters.
Specifies the exec action for the readiness probe. The probe executes a command inside the container, and the probe succeeds if the command exits with a status of 0.
The command to execute in the container as part of the exec readiness probe. This is a list of strings, where the first element is the executable and the remaining elements are arguments.
The number of consecutive probe failures required before the container is considered unhealthy for this readiness probe. Must be a positive integer.

Configures a gRPC-based probe for checking container health. Contains a 'port' (required) that the probe will connect to and a 'service' (optional) that is included in the gRPC health check request; if omitted, the default service name is the container name.
The TCP port number on which the gRPC server is listening. Must be a valid port number between 1 and 65535, and is required for the gRPC probe.
The name of the gRPC service to place in the HealthCheckRequest. If omitted, the gRPC default (empty string) is used.
Specifies the HTTP GET request used for the readiness probe. It includes fields for the request path, port, HTTP headers, and scheme.
Host name to connect to for the HTTP request. Defaults to the pod IP.
List of HTTP headers to send in the HTTP GET request. Each header is an object with 'name' and 'value' fields.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request.
The value of the HTTP header field to include in the readiness probe request.
The path to access on the HTTP server for the readiness probe.
The port number or name of the port to access on the container. Must be a valid port number (1-65535) or a named port defined in the container.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request. Allowed values are 'HTTP' and 'HTTPS'. Defaults to 'HTTP'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request, either HTTP or HTTPS. Defaults to HTTP.
Number of seconds after the container has started before readiness probes are initiated. Defaults to 0.
The frequency, in seconds, at which the probe is performed. The default is 10 seconds, and the value must be greater than 0.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the probe to be considered successful after having failed. For readiness probes, this value can be greater than 1; the default is 1.
The TCP socket probe configuration for the readiness probe. It specifies the port (and optionally host) on which the container's TCP socket is checked for readiness.
The host name or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not specified, the pod IP is used.
The TCP port to check for the readiness probe. Can be a port number or a named port from the container's ports.
The number of seconds after which the readiness probe times out. Defaults to 1 second if not specified.

List of resource resize policies for this container. Each policy specifies a resource name (e.g., 'cpu' or 'memory') and a policy value: 'NotRequired' or 'RestartContainer'. Used for in-place pod vertical scaling (requires InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature gate).
The name of the resource to which this resize policy applies. Kubernetes supports only 'cpu' and 'memory'.
Specifies the restart policy for the container when its resource requirements change. Allowed values are 'NotRequired' and 'RestartContainer'.

The resources field specifies the compute resource requirements for the init container, including requests and limits for resources such as CPU and memory. It defines the minimum resources the container needs (requests) and the maximum it can use (limits).
A list of resource claims that specify additional resources required by the init container. Each claim references a ResourceClaim object, enabling dynamic resource allocation (e.g., GPUs).
The name of the ResourceClaim that this container requests. This must match the name of a ResourceClaim object in the same namespace as the pod.

Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the container. Each key is a resource name such as 'cpu' or 'memory', and the value is the maximum quantity as a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., '500m', '1Gi').

A map of resource names to the minimum amount of those resources required by the init container. Common keys include cpu and memory, with values expressed as Kubernetes quantity strings (e.g., '100m', '1Gi').
Restart policy for this init container. Allowed values: Always, OnFailure, Never.
The list of numeric exit codes that match this restart policy rule.

Security settings for the init container, such as user/group to run as, Linux capabilities, SELinux options, and privilege settings. When set, these override the pod-level security context for this container.
Controls whether a process can gain more privileges than its parent process, such as through setuid or setgid binaries. When set to false, privilege escalation is prevented.

Configures the AppArmor profile for this init container. The profile type can be 'RuntimeDefault', 'Localhost', or 'Unconfined', with an optional 'localhostProfile' field specifying the profile name when type is 'Localhost'.
Specifies the name of an AppArmor profile that is already loaded on the node when the profile type is 'Localhost'.
Type of the AppArmor profile. Valid values are `RuntimeDefault`, `Localhost`, and `Unconfined`.
Configures Linux capabilities for the container. This allows adding or dropping specific capabilities from the container's default set, using the 'add' and 'drop' lists.
Specifies the capabilities to add to the container's capability set. This allows granting specific Linux capabilities to the container beyond the default set.
Lists capabilities to remove from the container's effective capabilities. Entries are Linux capability names (e.g., 'NET_ADMIN') or 'ALL' to drop all capabilities.
Run the container in privileged mode, giving it capabilities beyond the default and access to host devices. This is equivalent to running as root on the host for most purposes.

Sets the proc mount for the container. Allowed values are 'Default' and 'Unmasked'. 'Default' uses the container runtime defaults and ensures certain procfs paths are masked and read-only; 'Unmasked' bypasses those security settings.
Indicates whether the container's root filesystem should be mounted read-only.
The GID to run the entrypoint of the container process. If set, the container process runs with this group ID.

Indicates whether the container must run as a non-root user. When set to true, the container will be prevented from running as root (UID 0) and will fail to start if the image does not specify a non-root user.
The numeric user ID (UID) that the container's processes will run as. If omitted, the user specified in the container image is used.
The SELinux options for the container, which define the SELinux context (level, role, type, user) applied to the container process.
The SELinux level for the container, such as s0:c123. It defines the SELinux MLS/MCS level.
The SELinux role associated with the container, used as part of the SELinux options in the security context.
The SELinux type label that applies to the container.
The SELinux user label for the container, which is part of the SELinux security context options.
The seccomp profile for the container. Supports types Unconfined, RuntimeDefault, and Localhost; for Localhost, localhostProfile specifies the node profile path.
The path to a seccomp profile on the node. This is used when the seccomp profile type is 'Localhost', and must be a path relative to the kubelet's seccomp profile root.

The seccomp profile type. Allowed values are RuntimeDefault (use the container runtime default seccomp profile), Localhost (use a profile defined in a file on the node), and Unconfined (disable seccomp).
Windows-specific security context options for the container. Allows configuration of GMSA credentials, the user name to run the container, and whether the container is a HostProcess container.
Specifies the full content of a Group Managed Service Account (GMSA) credential spec, used by Windows containers to access Active Directory resources.
The name of the GMSA credential spec to use for the container. This field is part of the Windows security context options and should reference a pre-configured GMSA credential spec in the cluster.
Indicates whether the container should run as a HostProcess container. This setting is only valid for Windows containers.

The UserName in Windows to run the entrypoint of the container process. Defaults to the user specified in image metadata if unspecified. May also be set in PodSecurityContext. If set in both SecurityContext and PodSecurityContext, the value specified in SecurityContext takes precedence.

startup_probe is a Kubernetes probe that indicates whether the container has successfully initialized. If specified, no other probes are executed until this probe succeeds, and failures lead to restart or termination depending on the probe's configuration.
Exec specifies a command to run inside the container as part of the startup probe. The probe is considered successful if the command exits with status 0.
The command to run inside the container for the startup probe's exec action. Specified as a list of strings, where the first element is the command and the rest are arguments.
The number of times the startup probe can fail consecutively before the container is considered failed. Defaults to 3, minimum is 1.
Specifies a gRPC-based action for the startup probe, performing a gRPC health check against the container to determine if it has started.
Port number that the gRPC server is listening on for the health check. This is a required field for a gRPC probe, and must be a valid TCP port (1-65535).
The name of the gRPC service to check. If not specified, the gRPC health check is performed on the overall service status.

Configures a probe to perform an HTTP GET request against the container. The probe is successful if the response status code is between 200 and 399. Parameters such as path, port, and custom headers can be specified within this block.
The host name to connect to for the HTTP GET request. Defaults to the pod IP; override to use a different host.
List of custom HTTP headers to include in the HTTP GET request of the startup probe. Each object in the list specifies a header name and its value.
The name of the HTTP header to include in the request to the container.
The value of the HTTP header sent in the startup probe's HTTP GET request for the init container.
The URL path to access on the HTTP server. Defaults to '/' if not specified.

The port number or name of the port to access on the container for the HTTP GET probe. A numeric port must be an integer between 1 and 65535, or you can use the name of a container port defined in the pod spec.
The protocol to use for the HTTP GET request, typically 'HTTP' or 'HTTPS'.
The scheme to use for the HTTP request. Valid values are HTTP and HTTPS.
Number of seconds after the container has started before the startup probe is initiated.
The frequency, in seconds, at which the startup probe is executed. Must be greater than 0; defaults to 10 if not specified.
Minimum consecutive successes required for the startup probe to be considered successful after a failure. Defaults to 1; for startup probes, this must always be 1.
Configures a TCP socket probe: attempts to open a TCP connection to the container's IP address on a specified port. A successful connection indicates the probe passes.
The hostname or IP address to connect to for the TCP socket probe. If not set, defaults to the pod IP.
The TCP port to connect to for the probe. It can be a numeric port number or a named port (e.g., a port name defined in the container's ports).

The number of seconds after which the startup probe times out. If the probe fails after this duration, the container's startup is considered failed. Minimal value is 1; defaults to 1 second if not specified.
Whether the container runtime should allocate a stdin stream for the container. When true, stdin is kept open for the container to read from.

Whether the container runtime should close the stdin channel after it has been opened once. If true, stdin is attached to the container but then closed after the container's first process runs, allowing for a one-time input like piping data.
The path where the container's termination message is written. Defaults to /dev/termination-log if not specified.
Policy for accessing the termination message from the container's status. Valid values are 'File' (default) and 'FallbackToLogsOnError'.
Indicates whether a pseudo-TTY should be allocated for the container. When set to true, the container gets an interactive terminal.
List of block device mappings for the container. Each item defines a volume name and a device path inside the container, allowing the container to access raw block volumes.
The path inside the container where the raw block device will be mounted (e.g., /dev/sdb). Required for each volume device entry.
Name of the volume that this device accesses, matching an existing volume name in the pod spec.
Specifies volumes to mount into the container's filesystem. Each mount references a volume defined in the pod and a mount path within the container.
Path within the container at which the volume should be mounted. Must be an absolute path and cannot contain ':'.
Defines how mount propagation is handled between the host and the container. Allowed values: None, HostToContainer, Bidirectional.
Name of the volume to mount. Must match the name of a volume defined in the pod's spec.
Whether the volume is mounted as read-only. If true, the volume cannot be written to; if false (default), it is read-write.
Path within the volume from which to mount instead of the volume's root. Used to mount a subdirectory of the volume into the container's filesystem.
Path within the volume from which the container's volume should be mounted, with environment variable references like $(VAR) expanded. Similar to subPath but supports environment variable expansion.
Container's working directory. If not specified, the container runtime's default will be used, which might be configured in the container image.
condition_type refers to a condition in the pod's condition list with matching type. The pod is considered ready only when this condition has a status of True.
The name of the ResourceClaim referenced by the pod. This must match the name of a ResourceClaim object in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the ResourceClaim that this pod references. This must match the name of a ResourceClaim object in the same namespace.
Name of the ResourceClaimTemplate that this resource claim references, from which the claim is created.
Name must match the name of a ResourceClaim in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the scheduling gate. Must be a valid label value (DNS-1123 subdomain) and unique among all gates for the pod.
The name of the sysctl parameter to set on the container's kernel. For example, `kernel.msgmax` or `net.core.somaxconn`.
The value of the sysctl setting, as a string.
The effect to match for the toleration. Valid values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, and NoExecute.
The taint key that the toleration matches. If empty, the toleration matches all taints with the specified effect.
The operator field in a Kubernetes toleration specifies the relationship between the key and the value. Valid values are 'Exists' and 'Equal' (default is 'Equal').
The duration in seconds for which the pod tolerates the taint, used when the toleration effect is 'NoExecute'. If not set, the pod tolerates the taint indefinitely.
The value associated with the toleration key. Required when the operator is Equal, and must be empty when the operator is Exists.
A label selector used to identify the set of pods that this topology spread constraint applies to. If unspecified, the constraint applies to all pods in the namespace.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement contains a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and optionally a list of values. This is used to select resources for topology spread constraints.
The label key that the selector operates on. In match expressions, this specifies which label key the operator applies to.
Operator is the key's relationship to a set of values. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.
The list of values that the label selector key must match when the operator is 'In' or 'NotIn'. Must be empty for operators 'Exists' and 'DoesNotExist'.
Map of label keys to values that pods must have to be selected by this label selector. Used by the topology spread constraint to determine which pods the constraint applies to.

A list of pod label keys used to select the pods over which spreading is calculated. The values of these keys from the incoming pod's labels are combined with the labelSelector to identify the relevant existing pods.

The maximum permitted skew in pod distribution across topology domains. Must be greater than 0; it caps the difference in the number of pods scheduled per domain under this topology spread constraint.
The minimum number of eligible topology domains to which Pods must be spread. If the number of eligible domains is less than this value, the Pod is not scheduled.
Indicates how to treat nodes with taints when calculating pod topology spread skew. Allowed values are 'Honor' (default, includes tainted nodes) and 'Ignore' (excludes tainted nodes).
TopologyKey is the key of node labels. Nodes that have a label with this key and identical values are considered to be in the same topology. It is required for topology spread constraints.
Determines the behavior when a pod cannot satisfy the topology spread constraint. Set to 'DoNotSchedule' (default) to prevent scheduling, or 'ScheduleAnyway' to allow scheduling regardless.
Represents an AWS Elastic Block Store (EBS) volume source in a pod's volume specification, allowing an existing EBS volume to be mounted into the pod.
Filesystem type of the volume that will be mounted. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Defaults to ext4 if not specified.
The partition number of the AWS EBS volume to mount. If omitted, the first partition (partition 1) is used.
Indicates whether the volume is mounted as read-only.
The unique ID of the AWS EBS volume to mount in the pod.
Configuration block for an Azure Disk volume source. Represents an Azure Data Disk mount on the host and bind mount to the pod.
Caching mode for the Azure disk. Allowed values: None, ReadOnly, ReadWrite.
The name of the Azure data disk to be mounted. This must match the name of the disk in the Azure resource group.

The URI of the Azure disk to attach as a volume. For managed disks, this is the Azure resource ID (e.g., /subscriptions/{subscription-id}/resourceGroups/{resource-group}/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/{disk-name}); for unmanaged disks, it is the URI of the VHD blob.
Filesystem type to mount. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host operating system. Examples include 'ext4', 'xfs', 'ntfs'.
Type of Azure disk to use. Allowed values: `Managed` (default), `Dedicated`, or `Shared`.
Specifies whether the Azure Disk volume is mounted as read-only. If set to true, the volume is read-only.
azure_file represents an Azure File volume mount, which allows a pod to mount an Azure File share into the container. This volume uses the Azure File service to provide storage.
Specifies whether the Azure File volume is mounted as read-only. When true, the volume is read-only; when false, it is read-write. Defaults to false.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that stores the Azure Storage account name and key. This secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod and is required for Azure File volume authentication.
The name of the Azure File share to mount. This is a required field for Azure File volumes in Kubernetes.
CephFS volume configuration. Defines a CephFS volume source, including parameters like monitors, path, user, and secret reference.
List of Ceph monitors (host:port) that define the Ceph storage cluster.
The path within CephFS to mount as the volume's root. If omitted, the root of the CephFS filesystem is used.
Forces the CephFS volume to be mounted as read-only.
The path to the secret file that contains the CephFS credentials. This file is used for authentication when mounting the CephFS volume.
This is an optional reference to a Kubernetes Secret that contains the Ceph client keyring. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod, and is used to authenticate to the Ceph cluster.
Name of the Kubernetes Secret that contains the CephFS keyring for this volume.
The CephFS user to authenticate as. Defaults to 'admin'.
The Cinder volume source. Represents an OpenStack Cinder volume that is attached and mounted on the pod. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes/#cinder
Filesystem type to mount for the Cinder volume. If not set, the filesystem type is auto-detected. Examples include 'ext4' and 'xfs'.
Specifies whether the Cinder volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
secret_ref is an optional reference to a Secret that contains credentials for accessing the Cinder volume.
The name of the Kubernetes secret that holds the authentication credentials for the Cinder volume.
The ID of the Cinder volume to mount.
ConfigMap volume source for a Kubernetes pod volume. Configures a volume that mounts a ConfigMap as files, with options like the ConfigMap name, file mode, and item mappings.
Optional mode bits used to set permissions on created files by default. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 (or decimal 0 to 511). Defaults to 0644 (420).
Maps keys from the ConfigMap to specific file paths in the volume. Each item defines a key and its corresponding path, allowing selective projection of ConfigMap data.

The key to select from the ConfigMap's data. This must correspond to an existing key in the ConfigMap. The value of that key is projected into the volume as a file, with the file name determined by the path field in this item.
The file permission mode (as an octal number) for the file created from this config map item. If not specified, the default is 0644.
The relative file path within the volume where this ConfigMap key is exposed. Cannot start with '/' and cannot contain '..' segments.
The name of the ConfigMap to reference as a volume.
Specifies whether the ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. If true and the ConfigMap or keys are missing, the volume is empty; if false (default), a missing ConfigMap causes an error.
csi is an object that specifies a volume using a Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver. It includes parameters such as driver, volumeHandle, and readOnly to define the CSI volume source.
The name of the CSI driver that handles this volume. This name must match the driver registered on the cluster.
The filesystem type to mount for the CSI volume, such as 'ext4', 'xfs', or 'ntfs'. If not specified, the CSI driver determines the default filesystem type.

Reference to a secret that provides credentials or other sensitive information to the CSI driver during the node publish (volume mount) operation. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the Kubernetes Secret in the pod's namespace that contains credentials for the CSI node publish operation.
When true, the CSI volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false (read/write).

Map of string values representing attributes of the volume, passed to the CSI driver to configure the volume. These are driver-specific parameters that define aspects such as volume type, size, or other options.
Defines a downward API volume, which exposes pod metadata (labels, annotations, etc.) to containers as files.
Optional file mode bits for files created by the Downward API volume, specified as an octal integer. Defaults to 0644 (420 decimal).
List of DownwardAPIVolumeFile objects that define how to project pod information into files within the downward API volume.

field_ref is an object that specifies a pod field to project into the downward API volume file. It contains a fieldPath (e.g., metadata.name, metadata.namespace) and an optional apiVersion. This field is used when the downward API item references a pod field.
The API version of the schema that the referenced field belongs to. Typically 'v1' for core fields.
The path (relative to the volume mount) where the field value is exposed as a file.
Mode bits used to set permissions on this file, must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 (i.e. 0 and 511 decimal). If not specified, the volume defaultMode is used.
Path within the volume where the downward API item will be mounted. Must be a relative path, and the resulting file will be created at this location inside the volume.
Represents a reference to a container resource (e.g., limits.cpu or requests.memory) whose value is exposed via the downward API volume.
Name of the container to which the resource field reference applies. If empty, the resource field is for the Pod itself; otherwise, it selects the resource field from the specified container.
The divisor to apply to the resource field value, expressed as a Kubernetes quantity (e.g., '1' or '1k'). The resulting file content is the resource value divided by this divisor.
The name of the resource to select from the container, e.g., `requests.cpu` or `limits.memory`.

Represents an emptyDir volume, a temporary directory that is created when a pod is assigned to a node and deleted when the pod is removed. It can be used for scratch space, caching, or sharing data between containers in the same pod. Configuration options include medium and sizeLimit to control storage backend and size constraints.
Specifies the type of storage medium for the emptyDir volume. Use an empty string (default) for disk-backed storage or 'Memory' for a tmpfs (RAM-backed) filesystem.
The maximum size allowed for the emptyDir volume. The value is a Kubernetes quantity, e.g. '1Gi' or '512M'. If unset, the volume size is limited only by the node's available storage.

ephemeral configures an ephemeral volume that is created and deleted with the pod. It uses a volumeClaimTemplate to dynamically provision storage, and the volume's lifecycle is tied to the pod's lifecycle.
Specifies the template for the PersistentVolumeClaim that is created for this ephemeral volume. The Pod is bound to the claim, and the claim is deleted when the Pod is removed.
Standard Kubernetes object metadata (e.g., labels, annotations) applied to the PersistentVolumeClaim generated from this template.

Annotations is an unstructured key-value map stored with a resource that may be set by external tools to store and retrieve arbitrary metadata. These are not queryable and should be used to hold small amounts of supplemental data.

CreationTimestamp is a timestamp representing the server time when the object was created. It is represented in RFC3339 form (e.g., 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z) and is set by the system; clients cannot set this value.
The timestamp when the object was marked for deletion. This field is set when a deletion is requested and remains until the object is fully removed.
Finalizers are a list of strings that must be completed before the object can be deleted. They are used to ensure that cleanup tasks are performed before the resource is removed.
generate_name is an optional prefix used by the API server to generate a unique name for the volume claim template if 'name' is not specified. The server appends a random string to this prefix.
The generation number of the volume claim template metadata, automatically incremented by the system each time the desired state changes, and used for optimistic concurrency control.
Labels are key/value pairs attached to the volume claim template metadata. They are used to organize and select objects, and are represented as a map of string keys to string values.

managed_fields is a list of managed fields entries that record the operations and field ownership for the metadata. This is used by Kubernetes for field management and conflict resolution, and is typically managed automatically by the system.
The API version of the resource that this managed field entry applies to, as defined in the Kubernetes managed fields metadata.
The type of the managed fields entry. In Kubernetes, this is typically 'FieldsV1'.

The fields_v1 field is a JSON object (FieldsV1) that represents the set of fields managed by this entry in the managedFields list. It encodes the fields and their ownership in the Kubernetes managed fields structure.
The identifier of the controller, user, or system that manages this set of fields. Kubernetes uses this to track which component last modified the fields in this managed fields entry.
The specific operation (e.g., 'Apply' or 'Update') that resulted in this managed fields entry, indicating whether the field set was applied or updated by the manager.
The subresource to which the managed fields entry applies. An empty value indicates the main resource, while values like 'status' refer to a specific subresource.
The timestamp at which the managed field operation was recorded, in RFC3339 format.
The Kubernetes namespace for the created PersistentVolumeClaim. If omitted, the Pod's namespace is used.

List of owner references indicating the objects that own this volume claim template. Each reference includes the API version, kind, name, and UID of an owner, and is used to manage garbage collection and dependent resource lifecycle.
The API version of the referenced owner resource, e.g., 'v1' or 'apps/v1'.
If true, and if the owner has the "foregroundDeletion" finalizer, then the owner cannot be deleted from the key-value store until this reference is removed. Defaults to false.
Indicates whether the referenced owner is the managing controller of this resource. This field is typically set to true for the controller that creates and manages the object.
The kind of the owner object referenced by this owner reference, e.g., 'ReplicationController'.
The name of the referenced Kubernetes object in the owner reference.
UID of the referent (owner) object. It uniquely identifies the object within its namespace.
The current version of the object's metadata, maintained by the server. This value can be used in update requests to ensure the object has not changed since the last read.
selfLink is a URL representing this object, used for identifying the resource. In Kubernetes, this field is deprecated and may not be populated in newer API versions.
UID is a system-generated unique identifier assigned to the object by the Kubernetes cluster.
Spec defines the desired characteristics of the persistent volume claim that will be created from this volume claim template, such as access modes, resources, and storage class.

Specifies the desired access modes for the persistent volume claim. Valid values include ReadWriteOnce, ReadOnlyMany, ReadWriteMany, and ReadWriteOncePod. This determines how the volume can be accessed by nodes (e.g., read-write by a single node, read-only by many nodes, etc.).
Specifies an existing PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot as a data source for the volume claim, allowing the ephemeral volume to be pre-populated from an existing PVC or snapshot.
The API group of the referenced resource. For core resources, this is empty; for example, a VolumeSnapshot would use "snapshot.storage.k8s.io".
The kind of the data source for the volume claim template. Valid values include `PersistentVolumeClaim` and `VolumeSnapshot`.
The name of the data source object. This refers to the specific object (such as a PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot) that provides the data for the ephemeral volume claim template.

Specifies the object from which to populate the volume with data, such as a VolumeSnapshot or StorageClass. Can reference both namespaced and cluster-scoped objects; if both dataSource and dataSourceRef are present, dataSource is ignored.
The API group of the referenced resource. Leave empty to reference a resource in the core API group.
Kind of the referenced data source object (e.g., PersistentVolumeClaim or VolumeSnapshot).
The name of the data source object referenced by the volume claim template, used to populate the ephemeral volume.
The namespace of the referenced data source object. If not specified, the object is assumed to be in the same namespace as the volume claim template (or pod).

Resources represents the minimum resources the volume should have. For a PersistentVolumeClaim, this typically includes a request for storage size (e.g., storage: 1Gi) and optionally limits, defined via the standard Kubernetes ResourceRequirements object.
The maximum amount of compute resources allowed for the ephemeral volume claim. Keys are resource names such as 'cpu' and 'memory', and values are quantities like '500m' or '1Gi'.
A map of resource names to quantities (as strings), specifying the minimum resources required for the volume claim. For persistent volume claims, only 'requests' is honored; 'limits' is ignored.
A label query over volumes to consider for binding. This constrains the set of volumes that can be bound to the persistent volume claim.
A list of label matching requirements. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and a set of values to select the volume claim template based on labels.
The label key that this selector match expression applies to. Part of a Kubernetes label selector match expression, which also includes an operator and values.
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist.
values is a list of string values for the label selector requirement. It must be specified for operators In and NotIn, and must be empty for Exists and DoesNotExist.

A map of {key,value} pairs. A single {key,value} in the map is equivalent to an element of matchExpressions, whose key field is 'key', the operator is 'In', and the values array contains only 'value'. The requirements are ANDed.
Name of the StorageClass required by the claim. When set, the PersistentVolumeClaim will use the specified StorageClass. If empty, the default StorageClass will be used.
The name of the VolumeAttributesClass to use for this volume claim. If not set, no VolumeAttributesClass will be applied.
Defines the volume mode for the ephemeral volume claim. Allowed values are 'Filesystem' (default) and 'Block'.
The name of the PersistentVolume to bind to. This allows pre-binding to a specific PersistentVolume instead of relying on dynamic provisioning.
Represents a Fibre Channel volume to mount into the container. This volume source allows attaching a Fibre Channel LUN by specifying target world wide names (WWNs) and a LUN number.
Filesystem type to mount, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Must be supported by the host operating system. If not specified, the default filesystem type of the underlying device is used.
The LUN (Logical Unit Number) to use for the Fibre Channel volume.
When true, the Fibre Channel volume is mounted read-only. Default is false.
The list of Fibre Channel target World Wide Names (WWNs) that identify the storage targets for the volume.
List of Fibre Channel World Wide Identifiers (WWIDs) that uniquely identify the storage volume in the FC fabric.
Represents a FlexVolume volume in a pod spec. This volume type uses an out-of-tree driver to mount storage, with configurable driver name, options, and read-only settings.
The name of the FlexVolume driver to use for this volume.
Filesystem type to be mounted. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host OS (e.g., ext4, xfs, ntfs). If unspecified, it defaults to ext4.
A map of driver-specific key/value pairs passed as options to the FlexVolume plugin. These options are sent to the flexvolume driver's mount/unmount commands.
Mounted read-only. If true, the volume is mounted as read-only, preventing writes from the pod.
A reference to a secret that provides parameters to be passed to the FlexVolume plugin. The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
The name of the Secret in the pod's namespace that provides the secret data for the FlexVolume.
Volume source that represents a Flocker dataset to be mounted into the pod.
The name of the Flocker dataset to use for the volume.
The UUID of the Flocker dataset to be mounted. Exactly one of `dataset_uuid` or `dataset_name` must be set.
Configures a Google Compute Engine (GCE) persistent disk as the backing store for this volume in the pod specification.
Filesystem type to mount, such as ext4, xfs, or ext3. If not specified, the default is ext4.
The partition number on the GCE persistent disk. If omitted, the entire disk is used.
Name of the GCE persistent disk to mount. This must match the name of the PersistentDisk resource in GCE.
Specifies whether the GCE persistent disk volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
git_repo configures a gitRepo volume, which is a Kubernetes volume populated with the contents of a git repository. When specified, the repository is cloned into the volume before the pod starts.
Directory inside the volume where the git repository is checked out. Defaults to the repository root if omitted.
The URL of the Git repository to clone into the volume. This field is required.
The git revision (commit hash, tag, or branch) of the repository to check out for this gitRepo volume.
The name of the Kubernetes Endpoints object that identifies the GlusterFS cluster nodes. This is required for GlusterFS volumes.
The path to the GlusterFS volume on the GlusterFS server.
If true, the GlusterFS volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Represents a hostPath volume source that mounts a file or directory from the host node's filesystem into the pod. It contains 'path' (required) and 'type' (optional) fields.
Path of the directory on the host. If the path is a symlink, it will be resolved.

Type of the hostPath volume. This determines the behavior of the volume, such as whether the path must exist and whether it is a directory or file. Allowed values are '', DirectoryOrCreate, Directory, FileOrCreate, File, Socket, CharDevice, and BlockDevice.

Configures a volume backed by a container image (OCI artifact). The image is pulled and mounted as a read-only volume. The ImageVolumeSource object supports fields for the image reference and pull policy.
Pull policy for the image volume source. Allowed values are 'Always' and 'IfNotPresent'. Defaults to 'IfNotPresent' if not specified.
The image reference to use for the volume, e.g., 'nginx:latest'. This specifies the container image that populates the volume.
Configures an iSCSI volume to mount as a pod volume. Specifies the iSCSI target portal, IQN, and LUN to attach.
Whether to enable CHAP authentication for iSCSI discovery.
Whether to enable CHAP authentication for the iSCSI session.
Filesystem type to use when mounting the ISCSI volume, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. Must be supported by the host operating system.
Custom iSCSI initiator name. If not set, the default initiator name is used.
The iSCSI Qualified Name (IQN) of the target. This uniquely identifies the iSCSI target, typically in the format iqn.yyyy-mm.example.com:name.
The name of the iSCSI transport interface. If not specified, defaults to 'default'.
The iSCSI target LUN (Logical Unit Number) to use when connecting to the target. Must be an integer between 0 and 16777215.
A list of iSCSI portals (IP addresses or hostnames with optional port) to which the volume is exported. Used to specify multiple portals for the iSCSI target.
When true, forces the ISCSI volume to be mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.

secret_ref is a reference to a Kubernetes secret that contains CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI target and initiator. This allows iSCSI volumes to authenticate with the target using CHAP.
Name of the secret in the same namespace that contains the CHAP authentication credentials for the iSCSI volume.
The iSCSI target portal. This is either an IP address or an IP address with a port (ip_addr:port) if the port is not the default (typically 860 or 3260).
Name of the volume. Must be a DNS_LABEL and unique within the pod.
NFS volume source. This configures a volume that mounts an NFS (Network File System) share from a remote server into the pod.
Path that is exported by the NFS server, i.e., the directory on the NFS server to mount.
Set this to true to mount the NFS volume as read-only. Defaults to false.
Hostname or IP address of the NFS server that exports the volume.
Defines a volume backed by a PersistentVolumeClaim. The claimName subfield specifies the name of an existing PersistentVolumeClaim in the same namespace to mount into the pod.
The name of the PersistentVolumeClaim to reference as the volume source. The PersistentVolumeClaim must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Indicates whether the persistent volume claim volume is mounted as read-only. Defaults to false.
Configuration for a VMware Photon persistent disk volume source, enabling a pod to mount a persistent disk from Photon.
Filesystem type to mount the Photon persistent disk. Defaults to ext4 if not specified.
The unique identifier (ID) of the Photon Controller persistent disk to be mounted as a volume. This field is required when using the photonPersistentDisk volume type.
Represents a Portworx volume source. This configures a volume from a Portworx storage system to be mounted into the pod.
The filesystem type to be used when mounting the Portworx volume, such as 'ext4' or 'xfs'. If not specified, the existing filesystem on the volume is used.
Marks the Portworx volume as read-only. When set to true, the volume cannot be written to.
The unique identifier of the Portworx volume to mount.
Defines a projected volume, which merges multiple volume sources (such as secrets, configmaps, downward API, and service account tokens) into a single directory.
Optional mode bits used to set permissions on created files by default. Must be an octal value between 0000 and 0777 or a decimal value between 0 and 511. Defaults to 0644 for projected volumes.
List of sources to project into the projected volume. Each source can be a configMap, secret, downwardAPI, or serviceAccountToken.
If specified, projects a ClusterTrustBundle from the local cluster as a file in the volume. This allows consuming a CA bundle from a ClusterTrustBundle resource.
Label selector to filter ClusterTrustBundle resources when signerName is set. Mutually exclusive with name. If unset, matches nothing; if empty, matches everything.

A list of label selector requirements. Each requirement contains a key, an operator (such as In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. The label selector selects the ClusterTrustBundle objects to project; all requirements must be satisfied for a match.
The label key for the selector expression. It identifies the label on the resource (e.g., ClusterTrustBundle) that the expression evaluates against.
Operator represents the key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values. Required when the operator is In or NotIn, and must be empty when the operator is Exists or DoesNotExist, as per Kubernetes LabelSelectorRequirement semantics.
A map of key-value pairs used as a label selector to match ClusterTrustBundle resources. Only bundles with all specified labels are selected.
Name of the ClusterTrustBundle resource to project. This selects a specific ClusterTrustBundle object from the cluster.
Boolean flag indicating whether the referenced ClusterTrustBundle is optional. If true, the volume will not fail if the ClusterTrustBundle cannot be found.
Path is the relative path within the volume where the cluster trust bundle is mounted. It must be a relative path, must not start with '/', and must not contain '..' components.
SignerName selects all ClusterTrustBundles that match this signer name; the selected bundles are combined into a single trust bundle. Mutually exclusive with name.
ConfigMap is a source for the projected volume that projects a ConfigMap resource. It contains fields to specify the ConfigMap name, optional flag, and items mapping keys to file paths.
Optional list of key-to-path mappings to select and project specific keys from the ConfigMap. If unspecified, all keys in the ConfigMap are projected.
The key within the ConfigMap's data to project into the volume. Must match a key present in the referenced ConfigMap's data.
Specifies the file permission mode (in octal) for the config map item mounted in the projected volume. The value must be between 0 and 0777 (or 0 and 511 decimal). If omitted, the default is 0644.
Path is the relative path within the volume where the config map item is mounted. It must be a relative path (no leading '/') and cannot contain '..'.
Name of the ConfigMap to reference in the projected volume source. The ConfigMap must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Specifies whether the referenced ConfigMap or its keys must be defined. If true, the volume will still mount even if the ConfigMap or the specified keys are missing.

The downward_api source projects pod and container metadata (such as labels, annotations, and resource limits) as files into the projected volume. It contains an optional items list that specifies which fields to project and the file paths to use.

A list of DownwardAPIVolumeFile objects that define how to project downward API information into the volume. Each item specifies a relative file path and a field reference (fieldRef) or resource field reference (resourceFieldRef) to populate.

Selects a field of the pod for the downward API volume. The fieldPath must be a valid pod field reference, such as metadata.name, metadata.namespace, metadata.labels, metadata.annotations, spec.nodeName, status.hostIP, etc.
The API version of the referenced field. Defaults to 'v1' if not specified.
Path of the pod field to select, such as metadata.name, metadata.namespace, metadata.labels, metadata.annotations, spec.nodeName, spec.serviceAccountName, status.hostIP, or status.podIP.
Mode is the file permission mode (as an octal number) for the downward API file, e.g., 0644. If not specified, the volume's default mode is used.
The path (file name) relative to the volume's root directory where the downward API value is written. This field is required and must be set for each item.
