resource_field_ref specifies a container resource (such as CPU or memory requests/limits) to expose via the downward API volume. It defines which resource field's value is projected into the volume as a file.
Name of the container whose resource (e.g., limits.cpu, requests.memory) is referenced by the downward API resource field. Required when the resource field refers to a container-level resource.
Divisor is the value by which the resource value is divided. Defaults to 1.
The name of the resource to select, such as 'limits.cpu' or 'requests.memory', in the downward API resource field reference.
The relative path within the projected volume where the certificate chain from the pod certificate source will be mounted.
The type of cryptographic key to use for the certificate in the projected volume.
The name of the certificate signer that will sign the pod's certificate. This corresponds to the `signerName` in Kubernetes' certificate signing API.
Configuration for a projected volume source that references a Kubernetes secret, exposing its data as files in the volume.
A list of key-to-path mappings. If specified, only the listed keys are projected into the volume at the specified paths. Keys not listed are omitted.
The key within the Secret's data to select for projection.
Optional file mode bits (permissions) for the item, represented as an octal integer. For example, 0644 gives read-write for owner and read for group/others. Defaults to 0644 if unset.
Path within the projected volume where the secret key's value will be written. It must be a relative path, not starting with '..'.
Name of the Secret to project into the volume.
If true, the referenced Secret does not need to exist; if false (default), the Secret must exist. This allows the projected volume to be created even when the Secret is absent.

The serviceAccountToken source configures a projected volume to include a Kubernetes service account token. It supports settings for token audience, expiration time, and the file path where the token is mounted.
The audience of the service account token. This value is placed in the `aud` claim of the token and identifies the intended recipient for validation.
expiration_seconds is the duration in seconds for which the projected service account token remains valid. The value must be at least 600 and defaults to 3600 (1 hour).
The relative path within the projected volume where the service account token file will be created. Must not be absolute or contain '..', and must be UTF-8 encoded.
Represents a Quobyte volume source. This configures a pod to use a pre-existing Quobyte volume by specifying the registry and volume name.
Group to map volume access to. Default is none.
Marks the Quobyte volume as read-only. When set to true, the volume is mounted read-only.
The host:port address of the Quobyte registry service, which the volume source uses to access the volume.
The Quobyte tenant that owns the specified volume. If unset, the default tenant is used.
User to map to the Quobyte volume.
The name of the Quobyte volume to mount. This references an existing Quobyte volume by name.
RBD represents a Ceph Block Device (Rados Block Device) volume source. This object configures how the block device is mounted, including details like monitors, image, and filesystem options.
Filesystem type to mount (e.g., 'ext4'). If not specified, the filesystem type is determined by the kernel.
The name of the RBD (Ceph block device) image to mount. This field is required.
Path to the key ring for the RBD user. Defaults to /etc/ceph/keyring if not specified.
List of Ceph monitor addresses (hostnames, IPs, or Unix socket paths) used to connect to the Ceph cluster for this RBD volume.
The name of the Ceph pool in which the RBD image resides. This is a required field when using an RBD volume source.
Marks the RBD volume as read-only. When true, the volume is mounted with read-only permissions.
Local reference to a secret that contains the Ceph authentication key. The secret must be in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the Secret object (in the same namespace) that contains the Ceph RBD credentials.
The RADOS user name. Defaults to 'admin' if not specified.
ScaleIO volume source for a Kubernetes pod volume. This object configures a ScaleIO storage volume to be mounted into the pod.
Filesystem type to mount, such as ext4, xfs, or ntfs. Defaults to ext4 if not specified.
The host address of the ScaleIO API gateway.
The name of the ScaleIO Protection Domain for the configured storage.
Whether the ScaleIO volume should be mounted as read-only. Defaults to false, meaning the volume is mounted read-write. This is a common Kubernetes volume option to prevent writes to the volume.
A reference to the secret that contains the ScaleIO credentials (username and password). The secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Name of the Secret resource that contains the ScaleIO credentials. The Secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
Boolean indicating whether to enable SSL (HTTPS) for the ScaleIO gateway connection.
Storage mode for the ScaleIO volume, indicating provisioning type. Allowed values are 'ThickProvisioned' and 'ThinProvisioned'.
The name of the ScaleIO storage pool where the volume is located. This field is required when using ScaleIO volumes.
The name of the storage system as configured in ScaleIO, used to identify the ScaleIO system that provides the volume.
The name of an existing ScaleIO volume that has already been created in the ScaleIO system and will be mounted into the pod.
Secret is a volume source that mounts a Kubernetes Secret into the pod. It references an existing Secret by name and exposes its data as files.
The default permission mode, in octal notation (e.g., 0644), for files created in the secret volume when no specific mode is set on individual items. Defaults to 0644 if not specified.
A list of key-to-path mappings that specify which secret data keys to expose and their file paths within the volume. If omitted, all secret data keys are mounted as files named by the keys.
The key in the Secret to project into the volume path.
Mode bits used to set permissions on the file. Must be an integer between 0 and 511 (octal 0000-0777). Defaults to 420 (octal 0644).
The relative path of the file within the volume where the secret key will be mounted. If not specified, the key name is used as the path.
Specify whether the Secret or its keys must be defined. If set to true, the volume will not fail if the referenced Secret is missing.
The name of the Kubernetes secret to use as the volume source. This secret must exist in the same namespace as the pod.
StorageOS represents a StorageOS volume attached and mounted on Kubernetes nodes. Configure this object to specify a StorageOS volume source.
Filesystem type to mount for the StorageOS volume. Must be a filesystem type supported by the host OS (e.g., ext4, xfs, ntfs). Defaults to ext4 if unspecified.

kubernetes_resource_device_taint_rule.me.text: The API version of the resource that the manager applies, such as 'v1' or 'apps/v1'.
The type of the fields structure in the managed fields entry, typically 'FieldsV1' for the serialized format of managed fields.

fields_v1 holds the JSON representation of the fields managed by the manager for this entry, corresponding to the fieldsV1 field in a Kubernetes ManagedFieldsEntry. It contains the set of fields that the manager has ownership of.
The name of the agent (e.g., kubectl, a controller) that manages this set of fields, as recorded in the Kubernetes managedFields entry.
The operation that was performed on this managed field entry, such as 'Apply' or 'Update'.
The subresource that this managed field entry applies to. For example, an empty string for the resource itself, or 'status' for the status subresource.
The timestamp indicating when the operation that produced this managed field entry was performed.
API version of the resource that owns this object, e.g., 'v1' or 'apps/v1'.

If true, and if the owner has the foregroundDeletion finalizer, the owner cannot be deleted until this reference is removed. Defaults to false. To set this field, a user needs delete permission on the owner.
Indicates whether the referenced object is the managing controller of the owning resource.
Kind of the referenced resource, such as 'Deployment' or 'ReplicaSet'. It must match the 'kind' of the owner object.
The name of the owner object referenced by this owner reference entry.
The unique identifier (UID) of the referenced Kubernetes object.

kubernetes_resource_device_taint_rule.st.text: The last time the condition transitioned from one status to another, expressed as a string in RFC3339 format (e.g., '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z').
A human-readable message providing details about the current condition.
The generation of the resource that was last observed by the controller when this condition was updated, indicating whether the condition reflects the latest desired state.
A machine-readable, CamelCase reason that identifies the cause of the condition's last transition, as defined by the Kubernetes condition convention.
Represents the condition status, typically one of 'True', 'False', or 'Unknown', indicating whether the condition is currently satisfied.

kubernetes_resource_resource_claim.metad.text: The API version that the field was managed under.
FieldsType is the discriminator for the different types of fields managed by this set. The discriminator is used to determine the types of fields managed by this set.
Stores the JSON-encoded set of managed fields for this ManagedFieldsEntry, using a Trie-like structure where keys encode field paths (e.g., 'f:metadata', 'k:{...}').
Manager is an identifier of the workflow managing these fields.
The operation (e.g., Apply, Update, Delete) that was performed on the field, as recorded in the managedFields entry.
The subresource to which this managed field entry applies. An empty string indicates the main resource, while values like 'status' or 'scale' refer to specific subresources.
The timestamp, in RFC3339 format, indicating when the field manager recorded the managed fields entry.
The API version of the referenced owner object.
If true, the owner cannot be deleted from the key-value store until this dependent resource is deleted, provided the owner has the 'foregroundDeletion' finalizer. Defaults to false.
Indicates whether the referenced owner is a controller. If true, the owner is the managing controller for the resource.
Kind is the object kind of the referenced resource, such as 'Pod' or 'Deployment'.
The name of the owner object being referenced. This field is required and must match the name of an existing Kubernetes resource in the cluster.
UID of the referent object. This field uniquely identifies the owner object and is required in an OwnerReference.

kubernetes_resource_resource_claim.spec..text: Opaque carries driver-specific configuration parameters in a raw object, allowing the device driver to interpret the settings without Kubernetes understanding them.
Specifies the name of the driver that interprets the opaque device configuration parameters.
Arbitrary JSON object containing driver-specific parameters. The cluster does not interpret these parameters; they are passed as-is to the device driver.
The name of a device attribute that all devices selected for the request must have different values for, ensuring the devices are distinct with respect to that attribute.
The name of the device attribute this constraint applies to. A device is selected only if it has this attribute with a value matching the constraint's 'value' field.
A list of request names that this constraint applies to. If empty, the constraint applies to all requests in the claim.
Indicates that this request requires administrative access to the device(s). Claims with admin access are expected to be used for monitoring or management purposes. Defaults to false.
A map of resource names (e.g., 'cpu', 'memory') to their requested quantities (e.g., '500m', '1Gi') that must be matched exactly by the device's capacity in this request.
The exact number of devices to allocate, as required by the device request's 'exactly' specification.
A CEL (Common Expression Language) expression that evaluates to a boolean. It is used to match devices by their derived attributes; the expression is true for devices that satisfy the condition.
The name of the device attribute that must be matched exactly. It identifies a specific derived attribute in the request.
The name of the DeviceClass that this request is for. The DeviceClass defines the kinds of devices that can be allocated to satisfy this resource claim.

Configures a CEL (Common Expression Language) selector for matching devices. The object contains a CEL expression that is evaluated against device attributes to determine if a device satisfies the request.
The CEL (Common Expression Language) expression used to select devices in the resource claim. It defines the matching criteria that devices must satisfy.
A list of tolerations for the device request. Each toleration allows the request to match devices that have specified conditions, using key, operator, value, and effect fields.
Effect indicates the taint effect to match. Empty means match all taint effects. When specified, allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule and NoExecute.
The key of the taint that this toleration matches. If empty, it matches all keys when the operator is Exists.
The operator used for matching the toleration key and value. Valid values are 'Exists' (matches on key presence) and 'Equal' (matches on key and value).
The number of seconds the toleration remains effective. If omitted, the toleration applies indefinitely.
The value that the toleration matches against the taint's value. This field is optional and is used when the operator is 'Equal'; it must be empty if the operator is 'Exists'.
An ordered list of DeviceRequest alternatives; the first one that can be satisfied will be allocated.
The allocation mode for the device request. In the Kubernetes DRA API, this can be 'All' (allocate all matching devices) or 'Exact' (allocate the specified number of matching devices).
Number of devices to allocate from the first available devices that match the request's class and selectors.
The Common Expression Language (CEL) expression used to compute the derived attribute value from the device's attributes.
The name of the DeviceClass that the requested device must belong to when using the firstAvailable selector. Only devices from the named class are eligible for allocation.

A list of device selectors used to filter devices from the requested device class. Each selector is a CEL expression evaluated against device attributes; multiple selectors are combined with AND logic. If empty, all devices of the class are considered for allocation.

CEL (Common Expression Language) selector for device allocation. The expression is evaluated against device attributes to determine which devices match the request; a device is selected if the expression evaluates to true. This is an alternative to the serial selector.
The CEL expression used to select devices that satisfy this request. It is evaluated against each device's attributes and must return true for the device to be matched.
List of tolerations that apply to this device request in a Kubernetes ResourceClaim. Tolerations allow scheduling onto nodes with matching taints, similar to pod tolerations.
The effect of the taint to match. Valid values are 'NoSchedule', 'PreferNoSchedule', and 'NoExecute'. An empty value matches all taint effects.
The key of the taint that this toleration matches. When the operator is 'Exists', the value must be empty.

The operator used to match the taint key. Valid values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. Defaults to 'Equal'. When 'Exists' is set, the value must be empty and the toleration matches all taints with the specified key.
The duration in seconds for which the toleration tolerates the taint when the effect is NoExecute. If omitted, the toleration lasts forever.

The value associated with the key of the toleration. This is used with the operator to determine a match, e.g., when operator is Equal, the value must match the taint's value; when operator is Exists, this field is ignored.
Name of the device request. Must be unique within the requests list.

kubernetes_resource_resource_claim.statu.text: Opaque provides driver-specific configuration parameters for the device allocation. It is used when the configuration source is 'FromData'.
Driver is used to determine which kubelet plugin needs to be passed these configuration parameters. The driver must be a valid subdomain name.
Opaque parameters for this device configuration, passed as a raw extension object. The structure is driver-defined and not interpreted by Kubernetes.
Source indicates the origin of the device allocation configuration. Valid values are 'claim' (configuration from the ResourceClaim) and 'driver' (configuration from the driver).
Indicates whether the device was allocated with administrative access.

A list of conditions that describe why the binding of the resource to the claim failed. In the Kubernetes ResourceClaim status, this field is populated with error reasons when the scheduler cannot allocate the requested devices.
The name of the device that was allocated from the pool for this resource claim, as reported by the resource driver.
The name of the device driver that provides the allocated device.
The name of the resource pool from which the device was allocated.
The name of the device request that this allocation result corresponds to.
ShareID is a string that uniquely identifies a shared device across multiple resource claims. If the device is not shared, this field is omitted.

A list of node operations that the driver has indicated should be skipped for this allocated device. These operations are normally performed by the kubelet during device preparation, but are skipped for devices that do not require them.
The effect of the taint that this toleration matches, such as NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, or NoExecute.
The taint key that this toleration applies to. If empty, the toleration matches all taints (requiring operator 'Exists').
The operator represents a key's relationship to the value. Valid operators are Exists and Equal. If Exists, the value must be empty; if Equal, the value must match the specified value.
The duration in seconds for which the toleration is effective. In Kubernetes, this is used with the NoExecute effect to specify how long a pod can remain on a node after a taint is added.

The value associated with the toleration key. When the operator is 'Equal', this matches the value of the key on the node; it is ignored or empty when the operator is 'Exists' or when the key is empty.
A list of node selector requirements by node's labels.
The label key that the selector expression applies to. It must be a valid Kubernetes label key (e.g., 'disktype' or 'kubernetes.io/os').
The operator represents a key's relationship to a set of values. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.
values is the list of strings that correspond to the key. For example, if operator is In or NotIn, the key's value must be in (or not in) this list.
match_fields is a list of node selector requirements that specify the node fields (e.g., metadata.name) that must match for a node to be selected by this node selector term.
The label key that this node selector match field targets, such as 'kubernetes.io/hostname'.
The operator to apply to the key and values in this match field requirement. Valid operators are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.

The list of values that the field must match, as part of a node selector term's match field expression. The operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist) determines how these values are interpreted.
The list of conditions representing the latest observed state of the device. Each condition includes the type, status, reason, and message to indicate the device's health status.
lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This timestamp is typically represented in RFC3339 format.
A human-readable message providing details about the current condition of the device in the resource claim.
observedGeneration is the .metadata.generation of the ResourceClaim that this condition was observed against, indicating the freshness of the condition relative to the latest generation.
Reason is a machine-readable, CamelCase reason for the condition's last transition, providing a stable identifier for the cause of the condition.
The status of the condition, typically 'True', 'False', or 'Unknown'.

Arbitrary driver-specific data about the device allocation, as provided by the resource driver. Kubernetes does not interpret this field and it may be used to pass device-specific configuration or status.
The name of the device that has been allocated for this resource claim.
The name of the device driver that manages this allocated device, matching the driver specified in the corresponding DeviceClass.
Network information for the allocated device, including its interface name, IP addresses, and MAC address.
The MAC address of the network interface allocated for this resource claim.
The name of the network interface on the node where this device is allocated.
List of IP addresses assigned to the network device.
The name of the resource pool (ResourceSlice) from which this device was allocated.
The API group of the resource that reserved this claim. For core resources, this is the empty string; otherwise it is the fully-qualified API group name.
The name of the pod that this resource claim is reserved for.
The name of the resource (e.g., a Pod) that holds a reservation for this resource claim, as recorded in the status.reservedFor list.
The UID of the consumer (e.g., a Pod) that this ResourceClaim is reserved for. This is part of the ResourceClaimConsumerReference in the reservedFor list.

kubernetes_resource_resource_claim_templ.text: The Kubernetes API version used to interpret the fields in this managed fields entry.
The type of the managed fields. Currently the only valid value is FieldsV1.
fields_v1 is the JSON representation of the fields managed by this entry, using the Kubernetes FieldSet format.

The name of the manager that last applied the fields. In Kubernetes, this is typically the client identifier (e.g., kube-controller-manager or a user agent string) that owns the managed field entries.
A string indicating the operation type that resulted in this managed field entry, such as 'Apply', 'Update', or 'Delete'.
The subresource that the managed fields apply to, such as 'status'. Empty when the fields apply to the main resource.
Time is the timestamp of the last modification to this managed field entry, in RFC 3339 format.
The API version of the owner resource referenced by this ownerReference. This is used to identify the exact version of the resource kind, such as 'v1' or 'apps/v1'.
Indicates whether the owner reference prevents deletion of the resource. When true, the resource cannot be deleted until the owner is deleted or the owner reference is removed.
A boolean indicating whether the referenced owner is the managing controller of this resource. Typically set to true for the object that manages the lifecycle of the dependent resource.
Kind is the kind of the referenced object in an owner reference, such as 'Deployment' or 'ReplicaSet'.
The name of the owner object that this reference points to, as part of the Kubernetes ownerReferences metadata.
The UID of the owner object, as defined in the OwnerReference. This is a required field that uniquely identifies the owner resource in the Kubernetes API.
The API version of the Kubernetes resource type that this managed field entry applies to. Example values include 'v1' for core resources or 'apps/v1' for deployments.
Specifies the type of the managed field entry, such as 'FieldsV1'.
The fields_v1 attribute contains the managed fields as a dynamic JSON object, representing the exact set of fields that were modified by the manager.
Manager is an identifier of the workflow managing these fields. It represents the name of the manager that last modified the field, used for field ownership tracking.
The operation performed by the manager on the field set. Supported values are 'Update' and 'Apply' for Kubernetes managed fields.
The subresource that the operation was performed on, such as an empty string for the main resource, or 'status' or 'scale' for operations on those subresources.
Time is the timestamp (RFC3339 format) when the managed field operation was recorded, as part of a managedFields entry.
The API version of the referent (the owner object) in the owner reference.
If true, prevents the owner from being deleted until this dependent object is removed. Defaults to false.
Indicates whether this owner reference is the controller of the resource, meaning it manages the resource's lifecycle.
Kind of the referenced owner object, such as 'Deployment' or 'Pod'.
The name of the referenced owner object. This must match the name of the object in the same namespace as the resource.
The UID of the object referenced by this owner reference. This value uniquely identifies the owner object in the cluster and is required in an ownerReference.
Opaque holds driver-specific configuration for a device. It includes a driver name and arbitrary parameters interpreted by that driver.
The name of the device driver that interprets the opaque parameters.
Arbitrary driver-specific configuration parameters for the opaque device, provided as a map of string keys to JSON values. The interpretation of these parameters depends on the driver.
A list of device request names that this configuration applies to. If empty, the configuration applies to all requests in the device claim.
The name of a device attribute that must be distinct across all devices allocated for this claim, ensuring no two devices share the same value for that attribute.
The name of a device attribute that the device must have for this constraint to be satisfied.
Requests is a list of names of device requests this constraint applies to. If empty, the constraint applies to all requests in the claim.
Indicates whether this device request asks for administrative access to the device. When true, the device is allocated with admin privileges.
The exact number of devices to allocate, as specified under the 'exactly' constraint of a device request.
The CEL expression that computes the value of the derived attribute. The expression is evaluated against the device's attributes and the result becomes the attribute's value.
The name of the derived attribute. This identifies the specific attribute within the device request's derived attributes to be matched.

The name of the DeviceClass that defines the set of devices being requested. This field identifies which class of devices the request applies to, as defined in the Kubernetes dynamic resource allocation API.
List of device selectors that filter eligible devices from the associated device class. A device must satisfy all selectors to be considered for the request.
A CEL (Common Expression Language) expression used to match devices in a Kubernetes ResourceClaim. The expression is evaluated against each device to determine if it satisfies the selector.
The CEL expression used to select devices. It must evaluate to true for a device to be selected by this selector.
A list of tolerations that allow the resource to be scheduled on nodes with matching taints. Each toleration includes key, operator, value, effect, and optional tolerationSeconds.
The effect of the toleration. Allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, and NoExecute. If empty, the toleration matches all effects.
The key of the taint this toleration matches. An empty key with the Exists operator matches all taints.
The operator for the toleration. Valid values are 'Equal' and 'Exists'. Defaults to 'Equal'.
Specifies the duration in seconds that the toleration tolerates the taint. If omitted, the toleration tolerates the taint indefinitely.
The value of the toleration. This is the value that must match the taint's value when the operator is "Equal"; if the operator is "Exists", the value should be empty.

The allocation mode for the device request. Valid values are 'All' (allocate all devices of the class) and 'ExactCount' (allocate the number of devices specified in 'count'). Defaults to 'ExactCount'.

The CEL expression used to compute the derived attribute value from the device's attributes. The expression is evaluated in the context of the requested device and must return a string, integer, boolean, or list of such values.
The name of the device class that this request references. It must match the name of a DeviceClass resource in the cluster.
A list of device selectors that define the criteria for selecting matching devices. When using the first_available strategy, the first device that satisfies all selectors is allocated.
The Common Expression Language (CEL) expression that defines the criteria for selecting devices. This expression is evaluated for each available device to determine if it matches the selector.
The CEL (Common Expression Language) expression used to match devices for this selector in the resource claim template.
The taint effect that this toleration matches. Allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, and NoExecute.
The key of the taint that this toleration matches. If empty, matches all taints with the specified effect.

Specifies the relationship between the toleration key and value. Supported values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. When set to 'Exists', the toleration matches if the key exists; when set to 'Equal', it matches if the key equals the specified value.
The number of seconds for which the pod will tolerate the taint after it is applied. Only used when the effect is NoExecute.
The value associated with the key of the taint that this toleration matches. This is required when the operator is 'Equal' and ignored when the operator is 'Exists'.
Name is unique among all device requests in the resource claim and identifies this request within the claim.

kubernetes_resource_resource_pool_status.text: api_version is the version of the resource that this field set applies to, in the format 'group/version', used to track the version for field management.
The type of the fields structure in a Kubernetes managedFields entry, typically 'FieldsV1'.

A JSON representation of the fields managed by a particular operation, as part of Kubernetes managedFields metadata. It contains a map of field names to values indicating which fields were changed by that operation.
The name of the actor that last applied or mutated the field. In Kubernetes, this is typically the component name (e.g., kube-controller-manager) that owns the field update.
The operation performed on the managed field. Allowed values are 'Apply' and 'Update'.
The subresource that the managed field entry applies to, such as 'status' or 'scale'.
The timestamp (RFC3339 format) at which the operation recorded in this managedFields entry was performed.
The API version of the referenced owner resource, e.g., 'v1' or 'apps/v1'.
If true, and the owner has the 'foregroundDeletion' finalizer, the owner cannot be deleted until this reference is removed. Defaults to false.
Indicates whether this owner reference is the managing controller for the resource.
The kind of the owning Kubernetes resource, as defined in the Kubernetes API.
The name of the Kubernetes object that owns this resource, as referenced in the owner reference.
The UID of the owner object referenced by this owner reference.
The last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. Represented as a string in RFC3339 format (e.g., 2023-01-01T00:00:00Z).
Human-readable message providing details about the condition, such as why the resource pool is in the current state.

The generation of the resource pool status request that was observed by the controller when this condition was last updated. This is used to determine whether the condition reflects the latest desired state.
A machine-readable, CamelCase reason for the condition's last transition.
The status of the condition, typically one of "True", "False", or "Unknown".
The type of the condition, indicating the specific aspect of the resource pool status being reported (e.g., Ready, Error).
The number of devices currently allocated from the resource pool.
The number of devices currently available for use in the resource pool.
The name of the Kubernetes node associated with this resource pool.
The number of resource slices in the resource pool.
The amount of resource capacity currently available for allocation in the shared resource pool, expressed as a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., '10Gi').
The amount of the shareable capacity that has been consumed, expressed as a Kubernetes resource quantity (e.g., '1Gi').
The number of devices in the resource pool's shareable summary that are fully available, meaning the entire device is not in use and can be allocated.
Number of devices in the pool that are partially available, meaning they have some capacity already used but still have free resources to be shared.
The total number of devices (e.g., GPUs, NICs) available in the resource pool.
The number of devices in the resource pool that are currently unavailable.

kubernetes_resource_resource_slice.metad.text: The API version of the object that this managed field entry applies to, as recorded at the time of the operation.
The type of the managed fields entry. In Kubernetes, this is typically 'FieldsV1'.

The fields_v1 field contains the structured representation of the fields managed by the manager, as defined by Kubernetes' FieldsV1 type. It is a JSON object whose keys are field path segments and values are nested objects or empty objects for leaf fields.
The name of the component (e.g., kubectl, a controller) that manages this set of fields in the Kubernetes object's metadata.managedFields entry.
Operation is the type of operation performed by the manager, such as Update or Apply, as recorded in Kubernetes managed fields metadata.
The name of the subresource used to update the object, or an empty string if the request was to the main resource.
Timestamp (RFC3339) of the last update to this managedFields entry, indicating when the manager last modified the resource.
The API version of the referenced owner object (e.g., v1).
If true, the owner reference blocks deletion of the object. The object cannot be deleted until its owner is deleted, enabling foreground cascading deletion.
Indicates whether the referenced owner is the managing controller of the resource. Only one owner reference can be designated as a controller.
Kind of the referent. For example, 'Pod' or 'ReplicaSet'. More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds.
The name of the owner object referenced by this owner reference. In Kubernetes, this is the name of the resource that owns the current object, as specified in the metadata.ownerReferences array.
The UID of the object that owns this object, as assigned by the Kubernetes API server. This is a unique identifier for the owner resource within the cluster.

kubernetes_resource_resource_slice.spec..text: When true, the device may be allocated to multiple ResourceClaims simultaneously; when false or omitted, the device is allocated exclusively to a single claim.

Attributes is a map of device attributes. Each key is the attribute name, and the value is a DeviceAttribute object holding a typed value: one of IntValue (int64), BoolValue (bool), StringValue (string), or VersionValue (string). These attributes describe device properties and are used for device selection in resource claims.
When set, this device attribute has a boolean value. Only one of bool, int, string, or version may be specified for an attribute.
The integer value of this device attribute. This field is set when the attribute is an integer; exactly one of 'int', 'bool', 'string', or 'version' must be present.
The string value of a device attribute. This field is set when the attribute's value is specified as a string.
A list of conditions that indicate why this device cannot be bound to a resource claim. If any condition is met, the device is considered unavailable for allocation.

A map of resource names to resource quantities (e.g., memory, cpu) that describes the capacity provided by this device. Each key is a resource name, and the corresponding value is a quantity string like '1Gi' or '500m'.
Specifies the allowed range of values for a device capacity request. Requests must fall within this range to be considered valid.
The maximum value (inclusive) in the valid range for the device request policy. This sets the upper limit for the number of devices that can be requested, expressed as a string.
The minimum value allowed in the valid range, expressed as a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., '1', '500m').
The step size between allowed values in the valid range, specified as a Kubernetes quantity string. Values within the range must be of the form min + N*step, where N is an integer, up to max.
The quantity of the device capacity, expressed as a Kubernetes resource quantity string (e.g., "1Gi", "500m", "2").
List of counters that this device consumes. Each item represents a counter with a name and a value, indicating the amount of that counter required by the device.
The name of the counter set from which the device consumes counters. This refers to a named set of counters defined by a DRA resource driver.
The value of the consumed counter entry, represented as a string (typically a numeric value). Specifies the amount of the counter that this device consumes.
The name of the device, unique within the resource slice.
The key in the node allocatable resources mapping that identifies a particular resource capacity.
The per-pod overhead resource quantity for this device, expressed as a Kubernetes resource quantity string (e.g., '1', '500m', '1Gi').
The name of the Kubernetes node that this device is associated with. This field may be empty if the device is not node-specific.
The node selector that restricts this ResourceSlice to nodes with matching labels. It uses standard Kubernetes label selector semantics to identify eligible nodes.
List of node selector terms. The terms are ORed, so a node matches the node selector if any one term matches. Each term contains a list of match expressions and optionally a list of match fields.
A list of label selector requirements that constrain which nodes are selected. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and a list of values.
The label key that this match expression applies to. In Kubernetes node selectors, this is the key of the label that is matched against node labels.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and a set of values in a Kubernetes node selector requirement. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values for the node selector match expression. Required when the operator is In or NotIn; must be empty for Exists or DoesNotExist. Each value must be a valid label value.
A list of node selector requirements that match nodes by their fields (e.g., metadata.name). Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and optionally a list of values.
The key of the node field to match. In a matchFields expression, this is a field path such as 'metadata.name' or 'spec.unschedulable'.
The operator defines the relationship between the key and the set of values for the node selector match field. Allowed operators are: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt.
Specifies the list of values that the node selector key must match, depending on the operator. For example, with operator 'In', the node must have the key set to one of these values.
Taints is a list of taints associated with the device. Each taint restricts which nodes can allocate the device, defined by key, value, and effect.
The effect of the taint, indicating how pods that do not tolerate the taint are handled. Allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, and NoExecute.

The key of the taint, identifying the specific attribute or condition being tainted on the device. It follows the standard Kubernetes taint key format, which may include a DNS subdomain prefix and a name.
The time at which the taint was added, in RFC3339 timestamp format (e.g., '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z'). This corresponds to the Kubernetes taint's TimeAdded field.
The value associated with the taint key. This is an optional string that provides additional context for the taint, such as a specific condition or constraint.

A list of label selector requirements for the node. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. The node must satisfy all match expressions to match the selector term.
The label key that this match expression applies to. In a Kubernetes node selector, it identifies the node label that the operator and values are evaluated against.
Specifies the operator for the match expression, defining how the key and values are compared. Allowed values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.
The list of values that the key must match when the operator is In or NotIn. Must be empty for Exists and DoesNotExist operators, matching Kubernetes NodeSelectorRequirement semantics.

A list of node selector requirements that match against node fields (e.g., metadata.name), rather than node labels. Each requirement specifies a key, operator, and values that a node's field must satisfy to be selected.
The node field key, such as metadata.name or metadata.uid, that the match field requirement applies to.
The operator specifies the relationship between the key and value(s) in the match field. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, and Lt.

A list of string values for the match field requirement. The operator determines how these values are used: for In and NotIn, the list must be non-empty; for Exists and DoesNotExist, the list must be empty.

kubernetes_resource_v1alpha3_device_tain.text: The API version used to manage the fields in this managedFields entry.
The type of the fields field. Currently only 'FieldsV1' is supported.

fields_v1 is the Kubernetes fieldsV1 field, which contains a JSON representation of the fields managed by this entry. It stores a set of field paths and their ownership information used for server-side apply conflict detection.
The name of the manager (entity, such as a controller or user) that last applied or updated the managed fields.
Operation is the type of operation that last modified the field, such as 'Update' or 'Apply'.

The effect of the taint to match. Valid values are 'NoSchedule', 'PreferNoSchedule', and 'NoExecute'. An empty value matches all taint effects.
The key of the taint that this toleration matches. When the operator is 'Exists', the value must be empty.

The operator used to match the taint key. Valid values are 'Exists' and 'Equal'. Defaults to 'Equal'. When 'Exists' is set, the value must be empty and the toleration matches all taints with the specified key.
The duration in seconds for which the toleration tolerates the taint when the effect is NoExecute. If omitted, the toleration lasts forever.

The value associated with the key of the toleration. This is used with the operator to determine a match, e.g., when operator is Equal, the value must match the taint's value; when operator is Exists, this field is ignored.
Name of the device request. Must be unique within the requests list.

Driver is used to determine which kubelet plugin needs to be passed these configuration parameters. The driver must be a valid subdomain name.
Opaque parameters for this device configuration, passed as a raw extension object. The structure is driver-defined and not interpreted by Kubernetes.
Which of this claim's own device requests this configuration applies to -- every request, when left empty.

Indicates whether the device was allocated with administrative access.

The value associated with the toleration key. When the operator is 'Equal', this matches the value of the key on the node; it is ignored or empty when the operator is 'Exists' or when the key is empty.

Whether this device is available identically on every node in the cluster, rather than being tied to the one node this ResourceSlice is scoped to.
When true, the device may be allocated to multiple ResourceClaims simultaneously; when false or omitted, the device is allocated exclusively to a single claim.

Attributes is a map of device attributes. Each key is the attribute name, and the value is a DeviceAttribute object holding a typed value: one of IntValue (int64), BoolValue (bool), StringValue (string), or VersionValue (string). These attributes describe device properties and are used for device selection in resource claims.
When set, this device attribute has a boolean value. Only one of bool, int, string, or version may be specified for an attribute.
This device attribute's own real value, when it's a list of booleans.
The integer value of this device attribute. This field is set when the attribute is an integer; exactly one of 'int', 'bool', 'string', or 'version' must be present.
This device attribute's own real value, when it's a list of integers.
The string value of a device attribute. This field is set when the attribute's value is specified as a string.
This device attribute's own real value, when it's a list of strings.
This device attribute's own real value, when it's a single semantic version.
This device attribute's own real value, when it's a list of semantic versions.
Real conditions that must all be true before a claim allocated to this device can actually be used, checked at pod-binding time.
A list of conditions that indicate why this device cannot be bound to a resource claim. If any condition is met, the device is considered unavailable for allocation.
Whether allocating this device also binds the claiming pod to the specific node this ResourceSlice is scoped to.

A map of resource names to resource quantities (e.g., memory, cpu) that describes the capacity provided by this device. Each key is a resource name, and the corresponding value is a quantity string like '1Gi' or '500m'.
Real rules constraining how much of this capacity a single request may actually consume, beyond just its own raw quantity.
The real default amount of this capacity a request consumes when it doesn't specify its own explicit amount.
Specifies the allowed range of values for a device capacity request. Requests must fall within this range to be considered valid.
The maximum value (inclusive) in the valid range for the device request policy. This sets the upper limit for the number of devices that can be requested, expressed as a string.
The minimum value allowed in the valid range, expressed as a Kubernetes quantity string (e.g., '1', '500m').
The step size between allowed values in the valid range, specified as a Kubernetes quantity string. Values within the range must be of the form min + N*step, where N is an integer, up to max.
The real, fixed set of amounts a request's own consumption of this capacity is allowed to be, instead of a continuous range.
The quantity of the device capacity, expressed as a Kubernetes resource quantity string (e.g., "1Gi", "500m", "2").
List of counters that this device consumes. Each item represents a counter with a name and a value, indicating the amount of that counter required by the device.
Groups of counter-consuming devices treated as sharing the same real pool -- devices in the same group can't independently double-consume the same counter.
The name of the counter set from which the device consumes counters. This refers to a named set of counters defined by a DRA resource driver.
The real, named counters within the referenced CounterSet, and how much of each this device consumes.
The value of the consumed counter entry, represented as a string (typically a numeric value). Specifies the amount of the counter that this device consumes.
The name of the device, unique within the resource slice.
Real, computed mappings from this device's own capacity down to the node's own allocatable compute resources, so the kubelet accounts for it correctly alongside ordinary pod resource requests.
Real, per-capacity rules translating this device's own capacity into a real node-allocatable compute resource quantity.
The key in the node allocatable resources mapping that identifies a particular resource capacity.
A real scale factor applied to the device capacity's own quantity before it's counted against the node's own allocatable resources.
A real scale factor applied per allocated device before its capacity counts against the node's own allocatable resources.
A real, fixed additional resource reservation this device requires on the node, on top of whatever a claiming pod's own containers request.
The real, fixed additional resource reservation charged once per container using this device.
The per-pod overhead resource quantity for this device, expressed as a Kubernetes resource quantity string (e.g., '1', '500m', '1Gi').
The name of the Kubernetes node that this device is associated with. This field may be empty if the device is not node-specific.
The node selector that restricts this ResourceSlice to nodes with matching labels. It uses standard Kubernetes label selector semantics to identify eligible nodes.
List of node selector terms. The terms are ORed, so a node matches the node selector if any one term matches. Each term contains a list of match expressions and optionally a list of match fields.
A list of label selector requirements that constrain which nodes are selected. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and a list of values.
The label key that this match expression applies to. In Kubernetes node selectors, this is the key of the label that is matched against node labels.
The operator represents the relationship between the key and a set of values in a Kubernetes node selector requirement. Valid values are In, NotIn, Exists, and DoesNotExist.
A list of string values for the node selector match expression. Required when the operator is In or NotIn; must be empty for Exists or DoesNotExist. Each value must be a valid label value.
A list of node selector requirements that match nodes by their fields (e.g., metadata.name). Each requirement specifies a key, an operator, and optionally a list of values.
The key of the node field to match. In a matchFields expression, this is a field path such as 'metadata.name' or 'spec.unschedulable'.
The operator defines the relationship between the key and the set of values for the node selector match field. Allowed operators are: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt.
Specifies the list of values that the node selector key must match, depending on the operator. For example, with operator 'In', the node must have the key set to one of these values.
Taints is a list of taints associated with the device. Each taint restricts which nodes can allocate the device, defined by key, value, and effect.
The effect of the taint, indicating how pods that do not tolerate the taint are handled. Allowed values are NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule, and NoExecute.

The key of the taint, identifying the specific attribute or condition being tainted on the device. It follows the standard Kubernetes taint key format, which may include a DNS subdomain prefix and a name.
The time at which the taint was added, in RFC3339 timestamp format (e.g., '2023-01-01T00:00:00Z'). This corresponds to the Kubernetes taint's TimeAdded field.
The value associated with the taint key. This is an optional string that provides additional context for the taint, such as a specific condition or constraint.

A list of label selector requirements for the node. Each requirement specifies a key, an operator (e.g., In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist), and a list of values. The node must satisfy all match expressions to match the selector term.
The label key that this match expression applies to. In a Kubernetes node selector, it identifies the node label that the operator and values are evaluated against.
